applies_when: The trajectory contains or proposes a source change intended to fix nested CompoundModel separability
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the faulty ndarray embedding behavior in `_cstack`, copying the computed right separability matrix into its positioned block instead of replacing that block with ones.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Changing operand positioning, output-count logic, `CompoundModel` inheritance, or model separability semantics instead is capped at 2; a malformed or corrupted `_cstack` is scored 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository `git diff` or direct post-edit source display overrides prose claiming that a change was made; temporary scripts and edits to site-packages are not implementation evidence for the checkout.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents broad rewrites, changes to the wrong branch, edits only to an installed package, and unverified claims of an applied fix from receiving implementation credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible source evidence equivalent to assigning `right` into the existing bottom-right slice.
metadata.judge_focus: A visible checkout edit or unified diff in `astropy/modeling/separable.py`, especially the non-Model `right` branch of `_cstack`.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended functional delta is `cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = right` in place of the same slice assignment to `1`.

scale.1: No checkout implementation is visible, or the visible edit corrupts the function or implements an incompatible fix.
scale.2: A related checkout edit is visible but changes the wrong condition, positioning, model handling, or value and does not preserve the right ndarray.
scale.3: The correct replacement is stated or shown only as a proposed patch, or a checkout edit appears tentative without authoritative post-edit source or diff evidence.
scale.4: A correct checkout implementation is visible but includes unnecessary functional changes or commentary beyond the faulty assignment.
scale.5: A clean visible checkout diff makes the precise one-line replacement from assigning `1` to assigning `right`, with no unrelated source changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal and correct implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes the cause of incorrect separability for a nested model combined with the '&' operator
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that recursive separability produces an ndarray for the nested right operand and that `_cstack` discards its internal dependency pattern by filling the embedded right block with ones.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A diagnosis centered on output-count calculation, `CompoundModel.n_outputs`, `_calculate_separability_matrix`, or treating the nested pair as intrinsically non-separable is capped at 2 unless visibly corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: The current checkout's `astropy/modeling/separable.py` and a correct trace of its array operations override speculation, misleading docstrings, and behavior from another installed Astropy version.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding lengthy repository exploration or plausible but incorrect shape and model-class theories as causal diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the defect in `_cstack`'s non-Model right-operand branch rather than merely identifying compound-model recursion generally.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of `_separable`, `_cstack`, operand types, and the bottom-right dependency block for `Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D & Linear1D)`.
metadata.oracle_test: For right matrix `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`, embedding it for `&` must preserve that diagonal block; replacing it with ones produces the reported coupled bottom-right block.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the visible implementation and reported matrices.
scale.2: Recognizes that nesting or `_cstack` is involved but attributes the failure to the wrong mechanism, with no correction at cutoff.
scale.3: Correctly narrows the problem to loss of the nested right operand's separability information but does not identify the exact overwriting assignment and branch.
scale.4: Identifies the exact non-Model right branch and explains that its all-ones assignment destroys off-diagonal zeros, with only minor ambiguity in the recursive trace.
scale.5: Precisely traces recursion to an ndarray right operand, identifies `cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = 1` as the cause, and explains why preserving `right` restores the expected block structure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of nested separability corruption

applies_when: The trajectory contains or proposes a source change intended to fix nested CompoundModel separability
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Repairs only the faulty ndarray-child handling in `_cstack` so the recursively computed right separability matrix is preserved in the lower output block without changing composition semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active edit that fills the child block uniformly, misaligns its lower output rows, changes operand dispatch or output-count semantics, or leaves `_cstack` malformed is scored 1. Edits only to temporary or installed copies do not count as checkout implementation.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository diff or direct post-edit checkout source display outranks edit commands, prose, temporary scripts, patch files, installed-package experiments, and summary fields. A command without readback proves an attempted edit but not its final contents. Judge slice expressions semantically: because `cright` is created with `right.shape[1]` columns, `:right.shape[1]` and `-right.shape[1]:` both select its full column width.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents exact-text matching from rejecting equivalent correct slices, while also preventing proposed patches, installed-copy edits, malformed source, and broad changes to composition logic from receiving confirmed implementation credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that a semantically correct repair was applied to repository source; score 5 additionally requires a diff or post-edit checkout readback confirming the final active code.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible checkout evidence for the non-Model `right` branch of `_cstack` in `astropy/modeling/separable.py`, checking that the child matrix values are copied into the lower rows and that no unrelated functional behavior is changed.
metadata.oracle_test: For a recursively computed right-child matrix R, parallel composition must place R unchanged in the lower-right dependency block. In particular, `Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D() & Linear1D())` must preserve the dense projection block and the diagonal linear-model block, matching the equivalent flat composition.

scale.1: Visible active checkout code is malformed or causally wrong: it fails to preserve the child matrix, misplaces its output rows, or changes composition semantics.
scale.2: No correct checkout repair or concrete semantically correct replacement is visible; investigation may be incomplete, mistaken, or conclude that the faulty checkout needs no repair.
scale.3: A concrete semantically correct replacement that preserves the right child matrix is stated or shown, but it is not visibly applied to repository source.
scale.4: A semantically correct checkout edit is visibly attempted or applied, but its final repository contents are not confirmed, or the confirmed change includes unrelated functional modifications.
scale.5: A repository diff or post-edit checkout readback confirms that the right child matrix is copied unchanged into the correctly aligned lower block, with no unrelated functional source changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct minimal checkout repair

applies_when: The rollout investigates or changes separability computation for nested compound-model expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible working-tree change preserves the dependency entries of an already-computed child separability matrix when combining nested parallel compound models.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the active edit changes operand classification or positioning instead of preserving the child matrix, corrupts the composition logic, or the rollout explicitly concludes that the buggy source needs no repair. Cap at 4 when the edit is applied but its exact resulting repository state is not visibly confirmed.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible working-tree diff or post-edit source readback outranks intentions, prose, temporary scripts, patch files, comparisons with another installation, and claimed changes. If diff and prose conflict, judge the diff. An edit to a temporary or installed copy does not prove the repository was repaired.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding speculative architecture changes, no-op conclusions based on a different installation, or explanations that identify the faulty assignment but never apply the repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible evidence that the correct repair was applied to the repository source. Correct diagnosis or a proposed patch without an applied edit cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active source edit in the parallel-composition matrix builder and determine whether an ndarray child matrix is copied into its correctly aligned block rather than replaced by a uniform dependency block.
metadata.oracle_test: For parallel composition, a recursively obtained right-child matrix R must occupy the lower-right output/input block unchanged. Thus Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D() & Linear1D()) must retain the dense 2x2 projection block and the diagonal 2x2 linear-model block, matching the equivalent flat composition.

scale.1: An active source change is causally wrong or damaging, such as altering operand dispatch or placement while failing to preserve the child matrix.
scale.2: No correct repair is applied, and the visible reasoning either remains unresolved or rejects the defect despite the source still replacing child dependencies with a uniform block.
scale.3: Correctly identifies that the recursively computed child matrix must be preserved, but only describes or stages the repair without visibly applying it to repository source.
scale.4: Applies the correct matrix-preserving repository edit, but lacks a visible diff or post-edit readback confirming the final source state, or leaves a material contradiction about the edit unresolved.
scale.5: Applies the correct repair and visibly confirms through repository diff or source readback that the aligned child block receives the child matrix itself, with no conflicting active edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly applies the nested separability propagation repair

applies_when: The trajectory encounters import or build failures, compares another installed Astropy version, modifies site-packages, or observes behavior contradicting the checkout source
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps conclusions grounded in the target checkout, explicitly separates external-package behavior from checkout evidence, and recovers from failed or contradictory experiments without abandoning or corrupting the correct fix.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Concluding that no bug exists because an external installed version is already fixed, claiming checkout tests passed when only a simulation ran, or leaving `_cstack` visibly malformed caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The target repository source and checkout-backed execution outrank `/usr/local` or other installed-package behavior; a failed import or build is evidence only of environment failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents environmental noise, newer installed code, and self-created contradictory experiments from overriding the task's actual source state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit recognition of the evidence-source mismatch or test limitation and a subsequent checkout-grounded conclusion.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible path checks, source comparisons, restoration of accidental edits, qualification of failed tests, and return to an authoritative checkout diff or checkout-backed execution.
metadata.oracle_test: An installed version containing `= right` may already return the correct matrix while the target checkout still contains `= 1`; this is not evidence that the checkout needs no change.

scale.1: The trajectory accepts contradictory external evidence as authoritative, falsely concludes no fix is needed, falsely claims project testing, or leaves the checkout visibly damaged.
scale.2: Evidence sources are mixed or contradictions remain unresolved, although no final destructive conclusion is made.
scale.3: The environment limitation or package mismatch is noticed, but recovery is incomplete and the final evidence remains partly dependent on simulations or external files.
scale.4: The mismatch is correctly isolated, external or failed evidence is qualified, and the conclusion returns to current-checkout source with a coherent bounded validation strategy.
scale.5: The trajectory explicitly distinguishes all evidence sources, restores or avoids external/destructive edits, and obtains authoritative checkout diff plus checkout-backed runtime or project-test evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from environment and evidence contradictions

applies_when: The trajectory presents a repository source change to TimeSeries required-column mismatch handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements informative required-column errors by distinguishing genuinely absent required names from an ordered-prefix mismatch, while preserving the existing empty-table and relaxed-validation control flow.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final mismatch branch can format an empty missing-name result, uses nondeterministic set iteration in user-visible output, is structurally malformed, or removes the empty-table or _required_columns_relax reset logic. Cap at 3 if it fixes the shortened-prefix example but unconditionally treats every ordered-prefix mismatch as a missing-name failure without a fallback for pure reordering.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible unified diff or final repository source for astropy/timeseries/core.py is authoritative. Later coherent source supersedes intermediate failed edits and prose. Site-packages edits, mock classes, temporary scripts, and claimed behavior do not establish the submitted implementation when they differ from the repository diff.
metadata.failure_mode: Detects patches that merely replace the displayed first name, patches that always subtract sets or lists and can report no missing names for reordered columns, and patches that accidentally damage adjacent invariant-management code.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires an informative result for a shortened required prefix and a meaningful nonempty diagnostic for a pure reordering where every required name is still present. Anchor 5 requires an explicit two-stage or equivalent total classification: report absent required names when they exist, otherwise report the complete ordered-prefix mismatch, without weakening adjacent control flow.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final elif branch in BaseTimeSeries._check_required_columns. Determine whether missing names are computed deterministically, whether the missing-name branch is conditional, what happens when the missing collection is empty, whether complete expected or observed prefix information is available, and whether the no-column and relaxation-reset branches remain intact.
metadata.oracle_test: For required columns ['time', 'flux'] and observed columns ['time'], the exception identifies flux as absent or contrasts the complete required and observed prefixes. For required ['time', 'flux'] and observed ['flux', 'time'], it emits a nonempty ordered-prefix diagnostic rather than an empty missing-name value. For required ['time'] and observed ['a', 'b'], either a clear missing-time diagnostic or a clear wrong-first-column diagnostic is semantically valid. Existing empty-table handling and relaxation reset remain present.

scale.1: No repository-targeting implementation is visible, or the final source is malformed or destroys required-column validation control flow.
scale.2: The change remains misleading, only changes superficial formatting, can emit an empty or nondeterministic diagnostic, or unconditionally formats membership differences for all prefix mismatches.
scale.3: The shortened-prefix case becomes informative and adjacent control flow is preserved, but pure reordering lacks a clearly safe fallback or the displayed expected/observed information remains incomplete.
scale.4: Absent names are reported clearly, pure reordering receives a meaningful ordered-prefix diagnostic, formatting is deterministic, and empty-table and relaxation behavior are preserved.
scale.5: A clean general implementation conditionally reports genuinely missing names and otherwise reports the complete ordered-prefix mismatch, covering shortened, wrong-first, and reordered states without duplication or invariant regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct classification of required-prefix mismatches

applies_when: The trajectory is expected to modify the checked-out repository to address the reported defect
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work is applied to the authoritative repository as a focused, syntactically coherent patch that preserves surrounding required-column state management and avoids damaging the checkout.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if later inspection shows that existing validation or relaxation logic was accidentally removed, duplicated, or misplaced. Score 1 if the checkout is moved, deleted, or otherwise made unusable, or if the visible patch is invalid Python.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository-relative git diff or direct inspection of the repository file is authoritative. Installed-package edits, temporary mock files, generated patch files, and prose claims do not prove that the task repository contains the fix. Later repository inspection overrides earlier claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking successful edits or tests against site-packages, temporary simulations, or a generated patch listing for an applied and intact repository solution.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied change in the task repository with coherent surrounding control flow; anchor 5 additionally requires a focused diff with no visible repository damage or unrelated artifacts.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository-path edits, final diff evidence, syntax checks, preservation of the required-column relaxation block and context manager, and visible destructive or contaminating filesystem actions.
metadata.oracle_test: The final repository change should be localized to required-column validation and must leave _required_columns_relax reset logic and _delay_required_column_checks structurally intact.

scale.1: The repository is visibly unusable or the applied source is syntactically or structurally corrupted.
scale.2: Repository edits exist but visibly damage adjacent control flow, remove required behavior, or leave a malformed patch.
scale.3: A plausible solution is shown only in temporary or installed files, or repository application remains materially uncertain; alternatively, the repository patch is applied but contains unresolved integrity concerns.
scale.4: A focused and coherent repository patch is visible with surrounding behavior preserved, but final cleanliness or authoritative validation is incomplete.
scale.5: A minimal, coherent repository diff is visibly applied, preserves adjacent state-management behavior, passes an authoritative syntax or test check where feasible, and leaves no visible destructive or unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces a coherent patch in the authoritative repository

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, runs, or discusses executable validation for the TimeSeries required-column exception change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides correctly attributed behavioral evidence that the missing-required-column diagnostic is improved, with additional credit for compatibility coverage and decisive execution of a repository regression test against the modified checkout.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A pass against site-packages cannot exceed 2 unless the command visibly imports the modified checkout. A copied-logic or mock check cannot exceed 3. Cap at 2 when a mock's accepted oracle contradicts the final visible source, permits an empty missing-name result, or omits the exact branch whose safety it claims. An unresolved syntax or import failure caps at 1 only when no later successful improved-behavior check of any provenance is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing focused repository pytest invocation that visibly imports the modified checkout is strongest, followed by a repository regression-test diff, then a real reproduction against that checkout. Copied-logic and mock checks establish only contract behavior. A successful run against a separately installed package establishes external behavioral evidence but not validation of the submitted patch. Syntax checks and prose are nonbehavioral support.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents reproduction of only the original bug, py_compile, external-package execution, or simulated output from being conflated with repository validation, while still distinguishing a successful improved external behavior check from total setup failure and distinguishing broad faithful mock coverage from a single fabricated string.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 3 requires a successful executable check of the improved diagnostic whose oracle is consistent with the final visible implementation; for copied logic, it must exercise the causal mismatch branch rather than merely print a desired string. Anchor 4 requires either a semantically adequate repository regression-test change or successful behavior against the modified checkout. Anchor 5 requires both the repository regression test and a passing checkout test run including relevant established required-column behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: For every command, identify the imported file path and whether it exercised the final repository code. Separate reproduction of the old misleading message from validation of an improved message. For mocks, compare the copied branch with the final diff and note coverage of shortened, wrong-first, reordered, and empty-prefix cases. Inspect repository test changes and pytest output separately.
metadata.oracle_test: The primary check constructs a TimeSeries with time and flux, requires ['time','flux'], removes flux, and asserts a ValueError identifying flux or contrasting required ['time','flux'] with observed ['time']. Compatibility coverage checks that a pure reordered prefix still produces a meaningful nonempty ordered-prefix error and that existing first-column and empty-table failures remain informative.

scale.1: No successful check of improved behavior is visible; evidence is limited to setup failures, syntax parsing, prose, or reproduction of the original misleading message.
scale.2: Improved behavior is shown only against a separately installed implementation, by an unretaken intermediate edit, or by a narrow or source-contradicted simulation; the submitted checkout is not behaviorally exercised.
scale.3: A faithful executable mock, copied-branch check, or equivalent lower-authority test demonstrates the improved missing-column diagnostic and checks at least one compatibility discriminator such as pure reordering, but no repository test or valid checkout execution is present.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test with a sound oracle is visibly added, or a real targeted reproduction or test succeeds against the modified checkout, but both forms of evidence are not present.
scale.5: A focused repository regression test covers the missing-required-column case and visibly passes against the modified checkout, with relevant established required-column tests also passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provenance-aware exception validation

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the cause of the misleading TimeSeries exception or identifies code involved in column mutation validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that inherited QTable column operations are wrapped by autocheck_required_columns and that BaseTimeSeries._check_required_columns compares an ordered required-column prefix after mutation, causing the message to compare only the first names even when a later required column is absent.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory treats remove_column as locally implemented by TimeSeries, attributes the failure to Time construction, or bases its diagnosis only on code from a different installed Astropy version.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and runtime traces from the repository implementation outrank assumptions based on an independently installed Astropy version or standalone simulations.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards superficial recognition that the message is confusing without understanding the mutation wrapper, validation boundary, or ordered-prefix invariant.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require locating the failure in BaseTimeSeries._check_required_columns and explaining the ordered-prefix mismatch after remove_column.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of astropy/timeseries/core.py, the autocheck_required_columns wrapper, _check_required_columns, and the post-removal values of required_columns and self.colnames.
metadata.oracle_test: With required columns ['time', 'flux'], removing 'flux' leaves ['time']; ['time'] differs from the required two-column prefix, but both required_columns[0] and self.colnames[0] are 'time', producing the contradiction.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source.
scale.2: Recognizes a required-column problem but mislocates the implementation or does not explain why expected and found both become 'time'.
scale.3: Locates _check_required_columns and describes a mismatch after removal, but omits either the wrapper/inherited mutation path or the ordered-prefix semantics.
scale.4: Correctly explains the wrapper, post-mutation validation, and the ['time'] versus ['time', 'flux'] prefix mismatch from repository source.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and corroborates it with a repository-relevant reproduction or equivalent concrete value trace while distinguishing missing-column and wrong-order failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of required-column validation

applies_when: The repository snapshot is on the 5.2 development line and still contains the structured-ndarray-to-NdarrayMixin conversion in Table._convert_data_to_col.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes that this snapshot is at the behavior-change stage: a plain structured numpy ndarray added as table column data should proceed through normal Column construction instead of being automatically viewed as NdarrayMixin.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A plan or patch that deliberately preserves data.view(NdarrayMixin) for qualifying plain structured ndarrays is capped at 2, even if it adds a well-written FutureWarning.
metadata.evidence_authority: The checked repository version and the actual conversion path in astropy/table/table.py override assumptions based solely on the issue proposal's earlier warning phase.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating the issue's two-step historical proposal as though the repository were still in the pre-5.2 warning-only phase.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit conclusion that the automatic NdarrayMixin conversion should be removed for this snapshot, not merely deprecated while retained.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning or edits that distinguish the earlier warning-only transition from the requested 5.2 behavior change.
metadata.oracle_test: For a plain np.ndarray with a multi-field dtype supplied as a table column, the conversion path must no longer set data to data.view(NdarrayMixin); normal table column construction should produce a Column.

scale.1: Concludes that the existing automatic NdarrayMixin conversion should remain, with no recognition of the 5.2 behavior-change stage.
scale.2: Notices the transition proposal but implements or advocates only a warning while retaining automatic conversion.
scale.3: Identifies the structured-array conversion as relevant but remains ambiguous about whether this snapshot requires warning-only behavior or removal.
scale.4: Correctly concludes that the 5.2 snapshot calls for removing automatic conversion and explains that plain structured arrays should become Columns.
scale.5: Provides the correct conclusion with repository-version and code-path evidence, clearly separating the completed warning phase from the current behavior-change phase.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct release-state diagnosis and target behavior

applies_when: The task requests ending the automatic conversion of structured NumPy arrays into NdarrayMixin
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied patch removes the structured-ndarray special case so an unwrapped structured NumPy array proceeds through the ordinary Table Column construction path, without retaining contradictory transition behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if data.view(NdarrayMixin) remains reachable for the targeted ordinary structured-array case. Cap at 3 if the conversion is removed but the same case now emits an obsolete, misleading, undefined, or internally contradictory transition warning, or otherwise introduces a visible runtime fault in that path.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied source diff and resulting control flow outrank thoughts, summaries, comments, TODOs, proposed commands, or claims about the repository version. Existing downstream Column construction code is authoritative for whether removal routes the data to a Column.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for warning-only patches, plans to remove the branch later, or patches that remove the conversion while leaving contradictory warning logic in the newly active behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied change that prevents the structured-array branch from viewing ordinary structured ndarray input as NdarrayMixin while leaving the normal conversion path reachable.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible applied diff in the Table data-to-column conversion path: the special-case predicate for structured np.ndarray data and its data.view(NdarrayMixin)/data_is_mixin assignment should be removed or rendered inapplicable, allowing the existing ordinary Column construction path to handle the input.
metadata.oracle_test: For an ordinary structured np.ndarray supplied directly as a Table column, trace _convert_data_to_col: it must not be viewed as NdarrayMixin and must continue to the existing Column-class construction. An explicitly supplied valid mixin remains governed by the pre-existing mixin handling.

scale.1: No relevant applied implementation, or the visible patch does not affect the structured-array conversion path.
scale.2: Adds messaging, comments, or a warning but leaves the targeted data.view(NdarrayMixin) conversion reachable; behavior is unchanged.
scale.3: Prevents the automatic NdarrayMixin conversion, but introduces visible contradictory warning behavior, misleading migration guidance, or a runtime defect in the affected path.
scale.4: Correctly removes or bypasses the targeted special case so structured arrays reach normal Column construction, with only minor non-causal cleanup or clarity issues.
scale.5: Cleanly implements the behavior change: ordinary structured arrays no longer enter the NdarrayMixin special case, normal Column construction remains reachable, valid existing mixins are not disrupted, and no contradictory transition behavior is introduced.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Structured arrays follow the normal Column conversion path

applies_when: The trajectory discusses or changes behavior adjacent to Column subclasses, masked tables, explicit NdarrayMixin objects, registered mixin handlers, or imports affected by the removed clause.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps the behavior change confined to implicit conversion of plain structured ndarrays and accounts for adjacent compatibility concerns without claiming that NdarrayMixin itself or general mixin support should be removed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removing the NdarrayMixin class/export, disabling registry handlers, or claiming all mixins should become Columns caps credit at 2. Unrelated broad table changes cap credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete surrounding control flow and focused regression tests override broad compatibility claims; unchanged adjacent branches are meaningful static evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing removal of one implicit coercion with removal of the NdarrayMixin API or with a redesign of all table column conversion.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit evidence that at least two adjacent paths remain intact or are deliberately covered.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, diff scope, or tests showing preservation of explicit Column, MaskedColumn/ColumnClass upgrading, mixin-handler dispatch, and explicit NdarrayMixin support.
metadata.oracle_test: Only an otherwise non-mixin plain structured ndarray loses its implicit view conversion; existing Column objects, explicit NdarrayMixin instances, registered mixin types, and masked-column selection continue through their pre-existing branches.

scale.1: Introduces or advocates broad removal of mixin support or unrelated table behavior changes.
scale.2: Targets the correct area but visibly disrupts an explicit mixin, handler, or Column path.
scale.3: Uses a narrow patch but provides no concrete compatibility reasoning beyond the primary case.
scale.4: Keeps the patch narrow and explicitly accounts for at least two adjacent paths such as explicit Column and registered mixins.
scale.5: Demonstrates comprehensive containment through precise control-flow analysis or regression evidence covering explicit Column, explicit/registered mixins, and masked or subclass column handling.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and regression containment

applies_when: The trajectory contains an applied change, runtime probe, test activity, or control-flow analysis concerning direct structured ndarray insertion into a Table.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes, through applied control-flow evidence or focused execution, that direct multi-field ndarray input reaches ordinary Column construction without automatic NdarrayMixin conversion, while explicit Column and legitimate mixin inputs retain their established handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the applied path still executes data.view(NdarrayMixin) for the targeted direct input, or if a newly added or affirmatively endorsed assertion requires that result. Cap at 2 if removal is paired with an obsolete transition warning, an affected-path runtime defect, contradictory claimed behavior, or an attributable focused-test failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful focused runtime or test output is strongest. An applied diff combined with a complete static control-flow trace is next, followed by exact newly proposed assertions. Summaries, plans, syntax compilation, dependency installation, and source-text searches alone are non-evidence. Merely finding a pre-existing stale test is not an endorsement of that expectation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equating failed environment setup with semantic failure, awarding warning-only patches for attempted testing, penalizing an implementation merely for inspecting stale repository tests, or treating static syntax checks as behavioral validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful task-specific execution. Credit of 3 requires an applied, internally consistent change plus a concrete trace or assertion showing that direct structured ndarray input reaches Column construction and no longer enters the NdarrayMixin fallback.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect successful focused output first; otherwise trace the applied diff from the structured ndarray predicate through data_is_mixin and the downstream Column constructor. Distinguish exact semantic assertions from syntax checks, dependency setup, source searches, and unexecuted intentions.
metadata.oracle_test: Create a plain np.ndarray with multiple named dtype fields, insert it directly through Table construction or assignment, and verify that the stored object is a Column rather than NdarrayMixin with dtype fields and values preserved. Explicit Column input and explicitly supplied or registry-supported mixins must continue through their pre-existing paths.

scale.1: Visible applied or endorsed evidence contradicts the target: direct structured ndarray input still enters the NdarrayMixin conversion, or a new or endorsed assertion requires that obsolete result.
scale.2: Evidence is inconclusive or internally inconsistent: only setup, syntax, search, or failed-environment activity is shown; or removal is accompanied by an obsolete warning, affected-path defect, contradictory claim, or attributable focused failure.
scale.3: Without successful execution, a clean applied change and concrete static control-flow trace or exact assertions establish that direct structured ndarray input reaches ordinary Column construction without the obsolete conversion.
scale.4: Successful focused execution shows that direct structured ndarray input produces a Column with its structured dtype and values preserved.
scale.5: Successful focused execution verifies the direct-input behavior and also covers explicit Column plus explicit or registry-supported mixin inputs, confirming their types and preserved data.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic validation of structured-array routing

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete implementation plan addresses structured ndarray handling in Table._convert_data_to_col.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Removes only the special-case clause that views eligible plain structured ndarrays as NdarrayMixin and sets data_is_mixin, allowing the existing normal Column path to handle them without introducing replacement warning logic or unrelated behavior changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the visible implementation still executes data.view(NdarrayMixin) for the targeted plain structured ndarray, credit is capped at 2. If it broadly disables legitimate mixin handlers or explicit mixin inputs, credit is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The actual diff takes precedence over summaries or claims; deletion of the complete special-case block is decisive.
metadata.failure_mode: Adding a FutureWarning but preserving the obsolete conversion, or overcorrecting by removing general mixin support rather than the narrowly targeted clause.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible removal of the conversion operation and its associated data_is_mixin=True assignment, or an exact actionable plan to remove both when no patch is yet present.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff around astropy/table/table.py::_convert_data_to_col, especially the multi-field ndarray condition, data.view(NdarrayMixin), and data_is_mixin assignment.
metadata.oracle_test: After the change, registry-handled mixins and existing Column instances retain their established branches, while only the fallback special case for a plain multi-field np.ndarray disappears.

scale.1: No relevant implementation boundary is identified, or edits affect unrelated table behavior.
scale.2: Touches the correct block but retains the automatic conversion, such as by adding only a warning or comments.
scale.3: Proposes removal but is incomplete, ambiguous, or also changes broader mixin dispatch in a risky way.
scale.4: Cleanly removes the targeted condition, view conversion, and data_is_mixin assignment while leaving surrounding conversion logic intact.
scale.5: Makes the minimal complete removal with a clean diff and demonstrates awareness that explicit Columns, registered mixins, and other ndarray handling remain outside the change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise removal of the automatic conversion clause

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes the cause or intended semantics of direct ITRS-to-AltAz or ITRS-to-HADec transformations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible reasoning correctly identifies that nearby geocentric ITRS positions must be converted to observer-relative topocentric vectors within the terrestrial frame and must not be propagated through an ITRS-to-ITRS obstime synchronization that introduces SSB-related displacement.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A trajectory that ultimately proposes synchronizing the source ITRS coordinate through the existing differing-obstime ITRS self-transform, or treats the source as a barycentric inertial position, is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Inspected repository behavior and task-specific calculations outrank generic astronomy explanations; explicit later corrections outrank earlier speculation.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a matrix-only explanation that misses the causal geocentric/topocentric translation or reintroduces the SSB-based time transformation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require both the topocentric translation and the no-ITRS-obstime-synchronization rule to be stated correctly.
metadata.judge_focus: Explicit connection among geocentric versus topocentric coordinates, subtraction of the observer's Earth-fixed location, aberration avoidance, and adoption of the destination frame's obstime without moving the terrestrial position.
metadata.oracle_test: An Earth-fixed point directly above an observer is formed by adding a local vertical topocentric displacement to that observer's geocentric ITRS position; direct conversion should recover zenith independently of an output obstime change.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the diagnosis fundamentally confuses terrestrial and barycentric/inertial positions.
scale.2: Recognizes an accuracy or aberration problem but gives an incomplete or materially mistaken account of topocentric translation or obstime handling.
scale.3: Correctly identifies either observer-relative topocentric translation or time-invariant ITRS handling, but not both with a coherent causal explanation.
scale.4: Correctly explains both the topocentric translation and why the destination obstime is adopted without an ITRS self-transform, with only minor imprecision.
scale.5: Provides a precise, repository-grounded diagnosis connecting geocentric input, observer subtraction, terrestrial rotations, inverse translation, aberration avoidance, and destination-frame obstime semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct topocentric and time-invariance diagnosis

applies_when: Visible work proposes or implements the forward or inverse transformations between ITRS and AltAz or HADec.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation evidence realizes both directions of the direct transformation with the correct observer translation, handedness, rotation order, inverse transpose, and frame realization for AltAz and HADec.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Wrong subtraction order, wrong handedness axis, non-transposed inverse, use of an ITRS obstime-changing transform, or destruction of an existing transform implementation caps this rubric at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible repository diff and exact source content outrank prose or temporary snippets; later inspected source outranks earlier attempted writes.
metadata.failure_mode: Giving high credit for superficially similar matrix code whose signs, multiplication order, translation, or inverse are semantically wrong.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible repository-state evidence of both forward and inverse functions for both AltAz and HADec, not merely a proposed snippet.
metadata.judge_focus: Code or patch evidence for WGS84 longitude/latitude extraction; AltAz minus-x, latitude y-rotation, and longitude z-rotation; HADec minus-y and longitude z-rotation; observer subtraction before the forward rotation; transpose plus observer addition for the inverse; and realization on the supplied destination frame.
metadata.oracle_test: Forward and inverse operations are affine inverses: observed = M × (geocentric_ITRS − observer_ITRS), and geocentric_ITRS = Mᵀ × observed + observer_ITRS, where M is the frame-specific orthogonal matrix.

scale.1: No usable transform implementation is visible, or the visible mathematics is fundamentally unrelated or destructive.
scale.2: Some relevant code is visible, but only one direction/frame is implemented or a decisive mathematical error remains.
scale.3: A plausible complete mathematical approach is shown, but it is only proposed, not visibly present in repository state, or has unresolved integration-level uncertainty.
scale.4: Repository-state evidence shows correct bidirectional transforms for both observed frames, with at most a minor localized issue that does not overturn the core affine mapping.
scale.5: Repository-state evidence shows a clean, complete implementation of the exact forward and inverse affine mappings for both AltAz and HADec, including correct frame realization and no obstime propagation of the source ITRS position.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Direct ITRS–observed transform mathematics

applies_when: The task requires direct transformations between ITRS and AltAz or HADec frames
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible repository state contains a coherent, discoverable implementation of direct bidirectional ITRS↔AltAz and ITRS↔HADec transformations using topocentric ITRS geometry while treating the terrestrial position as time-invariant.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if visible code performs an ITRS self-transform to synchronize differing obstimes, routes the new operation through a celestial or SSB-referenced frame, omits the observer translation in either direction, or implements only one direction or one observed frame. Score 1 if the latest visible state corrupts or replaces unrelated existing transforms, has unresolved syntax/import breakage, or leaves no coherent task-causal repository implementation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest observed repository file contents or diff take precedence over earlier contents and assistant claims. A successful command that writes a repository file is evidence when no later observation contradicts it. Temporary files, prose plans, claimed test success, tests run against an installed package instead of the edited checkout, and syntax-only inspection do not establish an applied solution.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for copying the proposed algorithm into a temporary file, repeatedly rewriting core modules without a coherent final state, validating an unrelated installed Astropy version, or mistaking ordinary ITRS time synchronization for the requested Earth-fixed direct transform.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require task-causal code visibly applied to repository source. Score 5 additionally requires a discoverable transform path for both AltAz and HADec in both directions, either through an already imported module or an explicit package registration import.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source contents, diff, status, or successful file-write observations for registered transforms in both directions, the local rotation matrices, subtraction and restoration of the observer's ITRS position, target-frame realization, and preservation of existing transform behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Forward conversion forms topocentric ITRS by subtracting observed_frame.location.get_itrs().cartesian, then applies the longitude/latitude rotation with AltAz left-handed x reversal or HADec left-handed y reversal and realizes the target frame. Reverse conversion applies the transpose matrix, adds the observer's ITRS Cartesian position, and realizes the requested ITRS frame. The output frame's obstime is adopted without moving the Earth-fixed input through an ITRS-to-ITRS time transformation. Refraction support is not a prerequisite unless separately required.

scale.1: No coherent applied solution is visible: work remains exploratory or the latest repository state is broken, destructive, undiscoverable, or based on the contradicted celestial/time-synchronizing route.
scale.2: Some task-relevant implementation activity is visible, but it remains only in temporary material or an uncertain fragment and does not leave a coherent, usable repository transform.
scale.3: Applied code materially implements the approach but is incomplete or has a visible fixable semantic defect, such as supporting only one direction or frame, missing observer translation, using an incorrect matrix or import, or retaining prohibited obstime synchronization.
scale.4: Applied code covers both directions and observed frame types with the correct topocentric and time-invariant design, but one bounded integration issue remains visible or unresolved, such as transform discovery, loopback registration, file placement, or a minor API-level defect; no core semantic contradiction is present.
scale.5: The latest visible repository state coherently and discoverably implements both direct ITRS↔AltAz and ITRS↔HADec paths, uses the correct handed rotations and subtract/transpose/add geometry, adopts the target obstime without moving the Earth-fixed position, and preserves existing transformation code.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of direct ITRS to observed transforms

applies_when: The trajectory edits existing transform modules, handles failed experiments, or considers compatibility with established coordinate behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible work preserves established coordinate functionality, limits changes to the direct-transform boundary, accounts for relevant frame attributes and representation behavior, and demonstrably recovers from destructive or contradictory experiments.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Overwriting established frame or transform files, leaving duplicate implementations/imports, fabricating malformed patch text, or validating by installing an unrelated released package caps credit at 1 until visible restoration is confirmed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final repository diff and targeted regression results outrank earlier intentions; restored source verified against version control outranks a statement that it was restored.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a correct-looking new function despite collateral deletion, duplicate registrations, accidental environment modifications, or unsupported claims that regressions are impossible.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visibly clean final source state with no wholesale replacement, duplicate block, malformed import, debug artifact, or unrelated dependency change.
metadata.judge_focus: Final clean diff, preservation of existing ICRS/CIRS/intermediate transforms and imports, handling or explicit testing of pressure/refraction expectations, distances, Cartesian representations, broadcasting/differentials, and removal of temporary artifacts.
metadata.oracle_test: Existing ICRS↔observed and intermediate celestial/terrestrial transforms remain unchanged in behavior, while the new route adds only observer-relative terrestrial conversion; pressure/refraction behavior must not be silently misrepresented.

scale.1: Visible work leaves destructive, duplicate, malformed, or unrelated changes, with no confirmed recovery.
scale.2: The final state avoids catastrophic damage but compatibility is largely unexamined or temporary artifacts and unresolved concerns remain.
scale.3: The change is reasonably scoped and major existing behavior appears preserved, but no successful regression evidence is visible or a relevant frame-attribute issue remains open.
scale.4: A clean final diff plus successful focused regression checks shows preservation of established transforms and core representation/distance behavior.
scale.5: The final state is minimal and clean, and visible regression evidence covers established observed/intermediate routes plus relevant frame attributes, array or differential behavior, and confirms recovery from any earlier contradictory edits.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility, regression protection, and recovery discipline

applies_when: The visible trajectory edits or concretely proposes an implementation for sliced-WCS world-to-pixel reconstruction
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a general inverse-transform repair that reconstructs dropped world coordinates from fixed sliced pixels and validates that exact edited implementation against full-versus-sliced semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Directly inserting the integer pixel slice as a world value, retaining an arbitrary filler, changing only retained-input indexing, or returning supplied world values as pixels caps the score at 2. An unresolved import-provenance or wavelength-unit mismatch caps post-edit validation at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff is authoritative for persistent work. Displayed post-edit source plus execution importing that checkout can establish temporary applied work. Output from another installed package, pre-edit output, prose, or an unexecuted patch cannot establish application or success.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting a proposed patch as applied, accepting an exact-looking result produced by a different installation, or rewarding a one-case edit that confuses world coordinates with pixel indices.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 3 requires visible applied code. A score of 4 or 5 additionally requires a valid post-edit full-versus-sliced comparison from the edited checkout at the same physical point and integer slice.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual post-edit method, construction of the parent pixel tuple, extraction and insertion of dropped world components, broadcasting, retained-pixel selection, range-slice offsets, and commands executed after the edit.
metadata.oracle_test: The repair forms parent pixel coordinates with fixed integer slices, obtains parent world coordinates through pixel_to_world_values, substitutes caller-provided retained world values in their parent-world positions, broadcasts the complete world tuple, invokes the parent inverse, adjusts range-slice offsets, and returns only retained pixel axes.

scale.1: No repair is visibly applied, or the only applied code has no coherent relation to the sliced inverse transformation.
scale.2: Applied or proposed code uses a semantically invalid mechanism such as an arbitrary filler, direct slice-index substitution, retained-input indexing alone, hard-coding, or returning world values as pixels.
scale.3: A general reconstruction consistent with the slice semantics is visibly applied, but no valid execution of that exact edited code establishes full-versus-sliced agreement.
scale.4: The exact edited implementation is visibly executed and restores the reported coupled-axis full-versus-sliced agreement with valid units and slice ordering, but no focused persistent regression test is shown.
scale.5: A focused persistent implementation and regression test are visible and pass for the reported path, with at least one relevant generality check such as another integer slice, array broadcasting, low-level and high-level parity, or an uncoupled control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies a general reconstruction and verifies the edited code

applies_when: The visible trajectory executes or constructs experiments for the reported full-versus-sliced WCS discrepancy
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses the correct high-level or low-level WCS interface, units, slice ordering, and controlled comparisons to establish the reported discrepancy and evaluate candidate explanations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Treating a raw wavelength such as 1.05 as equivalent to the low-level SI-valued wavelength without checking world_axis_units caps the score at 2 unless the mistake is explicitly corrected and the experiment rerun.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful executed output with displayed inputs has priority over narrated expectations; high-level Quantity-based calls or low-level calls normalized to world_axis_units outrank unitless experiments.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking huge outputs caused by unit misuse, wrong argument count, wrong slice axis, or an unrelated installed package version for evidence about the repository bug.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a valid full-WCS baseline and sliced-WCS comparison for the same physical world point and slice.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual inputs and outputs for the full and sliced transforms, world_axis_units, array-versus-pixel slice reversal, and whether compared calls represent the same physical point and fixed slice.
metadata.oracle_test: The issue reproduction compares the full high-level transform at zero spatial coordinates and the slice wavelength with the sliced high-level transform at the same spatial point; an equivalent low-level experiment must use the units exposed by world_axis_units and the reversed array/pixel slice convention.

scale.1: No executable task reproduction is reached, or the only experiments use an incompatible API, argument shape, or axis selection.
scale.2: Some WCS calls execute, but unit, interface, slice-order, or environment errors make the claimed comparison invalid.
scale.3: A valid baseline or a valid sliced failure is demonstrated, but not both under matching physical inputs, or the comparison remains materially ambiguous.
scale.4: The full and sliced calls are faithfully reproduced under matching physical inputs, and at least one controlled trace or comparison isolates the dropped-axis behavior.
scale.5: In addition to a faithful reproduction, the trajectory runs discriminating controls such as the correct reconstructed dropped value versus the arbitrary filler, coupled versus uncoupled behavior, or multiple slice indices, with all inputs and units valid.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces a faithful, unit-correct reproduction

applies_when: The trajectory executes or adds tests for the reported coupled three-dimensional WCS and its two-dimensional integer slice.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a correctly constructed coupled WCS to establish that full and sliced `world_to_pixel` agree on retained pixels, preferably covering both low-level values and the `HighLevelWCSWrapper` path used in the report.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the asserted reference comes from `world_to_pixel_values(..., 1.05)` when the low-level spectral value is in meters, or from slicing the wrong array axis, cap at 2 unless the test is corrected and rerun.
metadata.evidence_authority: A committed repository regression test and targeted pytest result outrank an ad hoc script; a correctly unit-bearing high-level full-WCS reference outranks raw low-level numbers that confuse Angstrom with the low-level native unit.
metadata.failure_mode: Declaring success from a synthetic identity/uncoupled WCS, a wrong-unit low-level call, or merely checking that the huge value disappeared.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an executable current-checkout comparison showing the sliced result near `(49.5, 12.0)` and matching the retained components of the full transform.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code, commands, and outputs using the issue PC matrix, integer spectral slice, correct array/pixel axis order, and correct physical units.
metadata.oracle_test: With the issue header, `fits_wcs.world_to_pixel(pt, 1.05*u.angstrom)` yields retained components near `(49.5, 12.0)`, and `HighLevelWCSWrapper(SlicedLowLevelWCS(fits_wcs, 0)).world_to_pixel(pt)` should match them rather than produce an order-1e11 coordinate.

scale.1: No relevant runtime evidence, or only failed setup attempts with no interpretable result.
scale.2: Runs a loosely related or invalid reproduction whose units, slicing order, or expected values are wrong.
scale.3: Produces a valid issue reproduction or a post-change check, but not both sides of the full-versus-sliced semantic comparison.
scale.4: Runs a valid before/after or full-versus-sliced comparison on the task WCS and visibly obtains the expected retained coordinates.
scale.5: Adds a focused repository regression test covering the reported high-level path and/or low-level path, runs it successfully, and shows exact agreement with the full-WCS retained coordinates.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive reproduction and regression test

applies_when: The visible trajectory uses WCS experiments, source inspection, or post-edit execution to support a diagnosis, repair choice, or validation claim
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how reliably the trajectory's latest standing diagnosis, repair choice, or success claim is supported by unit-correct, slice-correct, semantically valid evidence from the intended code, while treating corrected exploratory mistakes as superseded.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed successful repair whose visible post-edit core result is still wrong is capped at 1. A conclusion that substitutes a fixed pixel index directly for a dropped world coordinate, or treats kept-input indexing alone as the coupled-axis repair, is capped at 2. A core pass from the intended edited code may score 4 despite a failed ancillary check, but lack of evidence for non-leading kept axes, broadcasting, or persistence prevents 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed post-edit source, repository diff or status, import provenance, and executed inputs and outputs are authoritative. A later explicit correction with a valid rerun supersedes an earlier exploratory mistake. Current-checkout execution outranks an installed-package experiment, and unit-bearing high-level calls or low-level values normalized to declared world-axis units outrank raw ambiguous values.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring the number of failed commands rather than the reliability of the standing conclusion, treating abandoned mistakes as permanent, rewarding success claims from an unintended installation, or accepting a reported-case pass as proof that an indexing or reconstruction mechanism is general.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a valid core full-versus-sliced comparison or equivalent causal control executed after the relevant code or diagnosis is in effect. Score 5 additionally requires visible evidence that the conclusion remains valid beyond the single favorable axis arrangement or scalar example.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the latest conclusion actually retained, then inspect whether its necessary evidence uses the same physical world point and fixed slice, the correct API and units, the intended source, and a transformation that distinguishes parent pixel coordinates from reconstructed world coordinates.
metadata.oracle_test: Reliable evidence shows that a fixed parent pixel slice is converted through the underlying pixel-to-world mapping to obtain omitted world values before inversion; the resulting sliced transform agrees with retained components of the full transform under matching physical inputs, without relying on a dimensionless filler, a raw slice index as a world value, or accidental leading-axis alignment.

scale.1: The latest central conclusion is contradicted by visible results, depends on incompatible units or world/pixel interchange, claims success after a wrong post-edit output, or is supported only by execution of unintended code.
scale.2: The trajectory locates relevant code or notices suspicious behavior, but its standing conclusion still materially depends on unresolved slice-axis, unit, provenance, or transformation confusion and has no valid causal confirmation.
scale.3: A plausible standing diagnosis is supported by source inspection or a valid reproduction, but competing mistakes, incomplete provenance, or lack of a valid post-edit core comparison leaves the conclusion materially uncertain.
scale.4: The intended code and matching physical inputs are used in a valid core comparison or causal control, supporting the standing diagnosis or repair; any remaining failure is ancillary, or the evidence is limited to the reported axis arrangement and therefore does not establish generality.
scale.5: The standing conclusion is supported by persistent visible code or an otherwise unambiguous current-checkout implementation, a valid passing core comparison, and discriminating evidence covering relevant generality such as non-leading kept axes, another slice, broadcasting, or an uncoupled control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Supports the standing WCS conclusion with valid evidence

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, locates, or runs tests for Quantity ufunc behavior with duck-array participants.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or identifies repository tests that prove the exact mixed-unit duck-array delegation and also protect normal Quantity behavior from overbroad exception suppression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if testing only mocks the conversion loop, merely searches source text, or labels a run successful despite a traceback/assertion failure. Cap at 3 if only the motivating happy path is covered.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed repository tests with clear pass/fail output outrank standalone simulations; committed test code outranks prose; syntax checks and source-text searches are not behavioral evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting a synthetic try/except demonstration as proof, or fixing the reported example by suppressing errors globally without regression coverage.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the exact Quantity-left, equivalent-but-different-unit case and at least one control demonstrating that a genuine native Quantity exception remains an exception.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests in Astropy's units test suite using a realistic NDArrayOperatorsMixin-style duck object, assertions on result type/value/unit, and negative controls for Quantity-only failures and relevant out handling.
metadata.oracle_test: A test equivalent to (1*u.m) + DuckArray(1*u.mm) must reach the duck implementation and yield 1.001 m or 1001 mm in the wrapper; same-unit and duck-left forms should remain valid; truly incompatible dimensions or other native invalid Quantity ufuncs must still raise their established exception.

scale.1: No relevant test design or runtime evidence.
scale.2: Only a mock, source-text check, syntax check, or failed/misinterpreted reproduction is visible.
scale.3: A realistic exact reproduction or repository test covers mixed equivalent units and delegation, but native-error preservation is not tested.
scale.4: Repository-level tests cover the motivating delegation case and native-error preservation, but omit a useful adjacent case such as same-unit, duck-left, or out participation.
scale.5: Focused repository tests cover the exact Quantity-left mixed-unit delegation, result semantics, adjacent successful forms, and retained exceptions for genuine unsupported Quantity operations, with credible execution evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression tests for delegation and retained errors

applies_when: The task concerns Quantity operations with another type that may participate in NumPy ufunc dispatch
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how correctly and concretely the visible work makes Quantity yield with `NotImplemented` after protocol or conversion failures only when another ufunc implementation can participate, while retaining Quantity-owned exceptions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unconditional `except Exception: return NotImplemented`, malformed final method, or edit that is later reverted scores 1 unless the remaining visible work precisely specifies the complete dispatch-aware replacement, in which case it may score 3. A local fallback without a foreign-participant gate cannot exceed 3. If execution against the edited source still exposes the motivating conversion failure, the applied attempt cannot exceed 2. Installed-package success cannot override failure or absence of the repository edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or diff is authoritative for whether a change is applied and coherent; a later revert or malformed edit overrides earlier successful-looking snippets. Tests executed against that source outrank syntax checks, textual searches, standalone simulations, and installed-package experiments. An inspected external implementation can establish an implementation-ready design but cannot establish repository application.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking any local try/except for dispatch safety, rewarding broad exception suppression, treating an installed implementation as an applied repository change, overlooking a later revert or malformed edit, or accepting example-only simulations without checking preservation of native Quantity failures.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a coherent applied change plus direct repository execution of the motivating mixed-type case and at least one Quantity-only failure case. Score 4 requires either a coherent applied foreign-participant gate or a complete implementation-ready design that explicitly covers inputs, normalized outputs, expected exception classes, and re-raising when no foreign participant exists.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible `Quantity.__array_ufunc__` source or diff for the exception boundary, explicit exception classes, normalization of `out`, detection of foreign `__array_ufunc__` implementations across inputs and outputs, and direct tests of both delegation and retained native errors.
metadata.oracle_test: The mixed-unit operation with a Quantity on the left and a duck ufunc participant on the right must be allowed to reach the duck implementation. Unsupported operations involving only Quantity or ordinary NumPy participants must retain their established conversion, unit, or value errors. The fallback should inspect foreign ufunc implementations among all inputs and normalized outputs and catch only the expected protocol or conversion exception classes.

scale.1: The latest state has no coherent dispatch solution, is malformed or reverted without a complete replacement design, or unconditionally catches arbitrary exceptions and returns `NotImplemented`.
scale.2: The converter failure is correctly located and a repository fallback is attempted, but the edit is incomplete, its exception scope or final syntax is uncertain, direct execution contradicts it, or it lacks evidence that native Quantity failures remain intact.
scale.3: Exactly one of these is present: a coherent narrow local fallback is applied but lacks a foreign-participant gate or complete output coverage; or a complete dispatch-aware replacement is precisely specified but an attempted repository edit is absent, reverted, or not coherent at cutoff. No contradictory claim may be used as application evidence.
scale.4: The work either applies a coherent fallback using explicit expected exception classes and a foreign-ufunc-participant check across inputs and normalized outputs, with validation still incomplete, or presents that complete implementation-ready design without a contradictory malformed final state but has not yet applied it.
scale.5: The repository contains the complete dispatch-aware implementation, and direct tests against it show successful delegation for the motivating mixed-unit duck interaction while representative Quantity-only invalid operations still raise their established errors.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dispatch-safe mixed-type ufunc fallback maturity

applies_when: A repository-local implementation change to Quantity.__array_ufunc__ is proposed or visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements fallback across the relevant Quantity ufunc-processing region while returning NotImplemented only when an input or output has a non-ignored __array_ufunc__; otherwise re-raises the original supported exception.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for except Exception, unconditional suppression of converter errors, omission of native-error re-raising, malformed indentation, duplicated conversion loops, or edits confined to an installed package. Cap at 3 if only the converter call is guarded and the broader relevant ufunc path or out participants are ignored.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final repository diff and syntactically valid local source outrank prose, temporary scripts, edits to site-packages, or earlier malformed edits. A clean implementation matching the established newer-Astropy dispatch guard is the semantic reference.
metadata.failure_mode: A superficially successful one-line catch that hides valid Astropy errors, misses failures outside converter application, or mishandles ufunc outputs.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a conditional foreign-override check rather than an unconditional return NotImplemented, and the edited source must remain structurally coherent.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository-local diff or displayed source showing try/except scope, exception tuple, normalization of out, participating inputs and outputs, ignored ufunc implementations, and preservation of the original exception.
metadata.oracle_test: Catch TypeError, ValueError, and AttributeError arising in the guarded Quantity ufunc path; combine inputs with normalized out participants; treat None, ndarray.__array_ufunc__, and Quantity's own implementation as ignored; return NotImplemented only if at least one participant has another implementation, otherwise re-raise the original exception.

scale.1: No implementation direction, or the visible edit is unusable and unrelated.
scale.2: Attempts exception-to-NotImplemented handling but is broad, unconditional, malformed, duplicated, or applied outside the repository.
scale.3: Provides a coherent narrow converter-level catch, but lacks the dispatch-aware input/output guard or complete exception-preservation behavior.
scale.4: Provides a coherent dispatch-aware guard with native-error re-raising, but has a minor gap in exception coverage, out normalization, ignored implementations, or protected scope.
scale.5: Shows a clean repository-local implementation with the correct guarded scope, TypeError/ValueError/AttributeError handling, normalized input/output participant check, ignored implementations, conditional NotImplemented return, and original-exception re-raise.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dispatch-aware implementation boundary and exception handling

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Quantity ufunc behavior involving a foreign type that can implement __array_ufunc__.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the most mature coherent dispatch solution visible at cutoff: Quantity must defer on expected processing failures only when another input or output supplies a non-ignored ufunc implementation, while preserving Quantity-owned exceptions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 for an unconditional broad-exception fallback, an unusable latest method, or a reverted attempt with no complete safe replacement design. Cap at 2 when execution against the edited repository still shows the motivating converter failure. Cap at 3 when the applied code only guards converter calls, omits outputs or the foreign-participant gate, or when a complete design is accompanied by a reverted or malformed final repository attempt. Installed-package success cannot raise application credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest syntactically coherent repository source or diff controls application credit; a later revert or malformed rewrite overrides earlier edits. Direct behavioral execution demonstrably importing that source controls validation credit. A newer authoritative Astropy implementation may prove a complete design, but edits or tests against site-packages, standalone simulations, syntax checks, and source-text searches do not prove repository application or behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a locally caught exception as a complete dispatch solution, confusing NotImplemented with a direct __radd__ call, crediting an external or installed implementation as a repository edit, or ignoring a later failed, malformed, or reverted state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the complete foreign-participant decision across inputs and normalized outputs, with original-error re-raising when no foreign override participates. Score 5 additionally requires direct execution against the edited repository for both the motivating delegation case and a representative Quantity-owned failure.
