scale.4: A completed target-like execution against the edited implementation credibly shows metadata-backed resolution despite failed class-level availability and returns no admin error, with assertions completing and no unresolved contradiction; explicit proof of one causal precondition or one adjacent control may still be incomplete.
scale.5: The same-item causal preconditions are visibly established and the edited check returns no error, while independent completed assertions confirm absent-item admin.E108 and real ManyToManyField admin.E109 behavior, with any earlier failures explicitly repaired and superseded.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Integrity and causal strength of executed descriptor verification

applies_when: The task is performed in a patch-delivery workflow where source edits or a unified diff are the required deliverable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether visible repository evidence contains a complete, coherent implementation for Avg and Sum DISTINCT support and whether any actual final response preserves that implementation as the required review artifact.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed or tool-refuted source caps at 1. An actual terminal assistant response that supplies prose rather than the required patch caps at 2 despite earlier applied edits. A failed command intended to create or print a patch does not impose that cap when no terminal assistant response has occurred.
metadata.evidence_authority: Tool-observed repository contents and git diff override claims about implementation. Before an actual terminal assistant response, a complete visible workspace diff is authoritative even if an attempted patch-printing command fails. Once an actual terminal response exists, its delivered artifact is authoritative for handoff quality and may supersede earlier workspace evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents conflating an unfinished failed patch-print attempt with an authoritative prose-only final response, while still distinguishing applied workspace work from a successfully delivered unified diff.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible applied changes enabling distinct=True on both Avg and Sum while Aggregate.allow_distinct remains False. Score 5 additionally requires the actual terminal assistant response itself to contain a complete, coherent unified diff.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect tool-observed source and git diff for applied Avg and Sum changes. Separately inspect the actual terminal assistant response, if one exists, to determine whether it supplies the required unified diff; do not interpret an attempted submission command, a missing patch file, or completion-oriented prose inside an unfinished trajectory as the terminal handoff itself.
metadata.oracle_test: The implementation artifact adds allow_distinct = True to django.db.models.aggregates.Avg and Sum while preserving Aggregate.allow_distinct = False; equivalent compatible Min and Max additions do not reduce credit.

scale.1: No usable applied implementation is visible, or tool evidence shows absent, malformed, or contradictory source changes.
scale.2: A complete implementation was visible in the workspace, but the actual terminal assistant response omits the required unified diff or replaces it with prose.
scale.3: Applied patch evidence is visible but remains partial or insufficient to verify both Avg and Sum support while preserving the base Aggregate default; no terminal response supplies a complete corrective diff.
scale.4: A complete coherent workspace diff visibly implements Avg and Sum support and preserves the base default, and no actual terminal assistant response has yet superseded that workspace artifact.
scale.5: The actual terminal assistant response contains a complete coherent unified diff implementing Avg and Sum support and preserving the base Aggregate default.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implemented DISTINCT patch and authoritative review artifact

applies_when: The task uses a patch-delivery workflow in which repository edits or a unified diff are the required deliverable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible prefix contains a complete applied implementation for Avg and Sum DISTINCT support and whether an actual terminal assistant response, if present, delivers that implementation as a reviewable patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Tool evidence showing absent, malformed, reverted, or incompatible source caps credit at 1. An actual terminal assistant response containing prose rather than the required patch caps credit at 2 despite earlier complete workspace edits. Failed patch-printing or submission commands do not trigger that cap when no terminal response follows.
metadata.evidence_authority: Tool-observed repository contents and git diff override claims about local implementation. Before an actual terminal assistant response, a complete visible workspace diff remains authoritative even if a command intended to print or submit it fails. Once an actual terminal response exists, its payload is authoritative for handoff quality.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents conflating an unsuccessful patch-print attempt with an authoritative prose-only final response, while distinguishing complete applied work from plans, partial edits, and final patch delivery.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible applied changes enabling distinct=True on both Avg and Sum while Aggregate.allow_distinct remains False. Score 5 additionally requires the actual terminal assistant response itself to contain a complete coherent unified diff.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect tool-observed file contents and git diff for applied Avg and Sum changes. Separately inspect whether an actual terminal assistant response exists and, if so, whether its payload is a complete unified diff. Do not treat a failed command, missing patch file, submission marker, or completion-oriented text inside an unfinished trajectory as the terminal response.
metadata.oracle_test: The artifact adds allow_distinct = True to django.db.models.aggregates.Avg and Sum while preserving Aggregate.allow_distinct = False. Equivalent additions to Min and Max are compatible and do not reduce credit.

scale.1: No usable applied implementation is visible, or tool evidence shows that the source is absent, malformed, reverted, or incompatible with the required mechanism.
scale.2: A complete relevant implementation was visible in the workspace, but an actual terminal assistant response supplies prose or another non-patch payload instead of the required unified diff.
scale.3: Applied source changes are visible but remain partial or insufficient to verify both Avg and Sum support while preserving the base Aggregate default, and no actual terminal response supplies a complete corrective diff.
scale.4: A complete coherent workspace diff visibly implements Avg and Sum support and preserves the base default, and no actual terminal assistant response has superseded it; failed attempts to print or submit the patch do not reduce this anchor.
scale.5: An actual terminal assistant response contains a complete coherent unified diff implementing Avg and Sum support while preserving the base Aggregate default.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied DISTINCT patch and authoritative patch handoff

applies_when: The visible prefix presents source views, diffs, traces, tests, compilation, or environment failures as evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether evidence faithfully represents the visible source and is interpreted according to the required outputs.

metadata.failure_mode: Stale copies, malformed scripts, or incorrect expectations are treated as authoritative
metadata.judge_focus: Actual-source execution and correct behavioral oracle
metadata.oracle_test: Reported pattern plus terminal named, unnamed, nested, escaped, and suffix cases

scale.1: Evidence is absent, materially contradicted by the source, or dominated by malformed scripts, stale copies, or incorrect expected outputs.
scale.2: The exact defect is reproduced or accurately traced, but post-edit actual-source evidence is absent or limited.
scale.3: The actual edited source or an exact extraction is exercised on relevant cases and outputs are interpreted correctly.
scale.4: Discriminative terminal and compatibility cases pass through the actual source, with syntax or diff validity also checked.
scale.5: A configured focused suite or equivalent comprehensive actual-source validation confirms all required behavior and an applicable clean change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-grounded evidence reading

applies_when: The visible prefix calculates, changes, traces, or tests the named-group slice or unnamed-group interval.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether replacement ranges include the completed capture's closing parenthesis and exclude every following character.

metadata.failure_mode: A closing parenthesis remains or adjacent text is consumed
metadata.judge_focus: Endpoint arithmetic under the chosen transition timing
metadata.oracle_test: Terminal and suffixed captures preserve exactly the expected surrounding text

scale.1: Visible arithmetic or output consumes adjacent text, leaves structural group syntax, or otherwise has a demonstrably wrong boundary.
scale.2: Boundary reasoning is contradictory, unresolved, or off by one in a visible implementation.
scale.3: The correct endpoint is explicitly derived for the operative transition timing, but actual-source confirmation is limited.
scale.4: The actual named-group implementation includes exactly the closing `)` and preserves terminal, slash, anchor, ordinary-suffix, and adjacent-group boundaries.
scale.5: Exact boundaries are demonstrated for both named and unnamed helpers across terminal, nested, anchored, suffixed, and adjacent-capture cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact capture replacement boundaries

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, traces, edits, or proposes concrete source logic for a manual parenthesis scanner in either replacement helper.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the observable handling of the state transition in which the current unescaped `)` reduces the outer capture's balance to zero.

metadata.failure_mode: Completion is tested only before processing the current character
metadata.judge_focus: Character-processing order and guarded terminal completion
metadata.oracle_test: A group whose structural closing parenthesis is the final input character is recorded without a sentinel
metadata.stage: Reproduce, diagnose, and implement balanced closure

scale.1: The visible logic does not recognize or correct the causal transition; it is unrelated, absent, or relies only on changing an endpoint.
scale.2: The terminal symptom is reproduced, but the explanation or proposed logic remains confused about when balance reaches zero.
scale.3: The consume-before-check defect is accurately traced, but no concrete correct source change or directly applicable correction is visible.
scale.4: A concrete post-consumption check or guarded exhaustion correction is visible, but application, syntax, or focused confirmation remains uncertain.
scale.5: The actual source or a directly applicable patch records completion after the structural `)` reduces balance to zero, and focused actual-source evidence confirms the behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal balanced-closure behavior

applies_when: The affected multi-valued exclude or negated-Q query is compiled or executed after valid Django settings, application registration, and schema initialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable proof that the generated query correlates with the intended enclosing model and returns rows that distinguish correct from incorrect correlation.

metadata.failure_mode: Wrong alias, literal OuterRef, construction-only evidence, nondiscriminative data, or exception-only validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Require the true enclosing column and mutation-sensitive results; no-crash evidence is insufficient.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute the focused related exclude before and after deleting the relevant related object and inspect the generated correlation.

scale.1: Valid execution shows the original failure, wrong-model correlation, a literalized OuterRef, or incorrect returned rows.
scale.2: Only construction, printing, exception absence, or nondiscriminative results are shown.
scale.3: Generated SQL visibly uses the intended enclosing model and no literal OuterRef, but discriminative row behavior is not established.
scale.4: A valid data-backed equivalent demonstrates correct enclosing correlation and discriminative returned rows.
scale.5: The focused mutation-sensitive regression passes for exclude and an equivalent negated-Q form, with correct SQL correlation and relevant compatibility or guard checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative correlation and result evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, explains, or proposes a cause for the OuterRef failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates source-grounded recognition of the extra split-exclude query level, OuterRef's inheritance from F, and the separate related-lookup expression-preservation boundary.

metadata.failure_mode: Generic exploration, immediate resolution, global guard suppression, or a split-exclude-only account that misses related RHS preparation.
metadata.judge_focus: Credit concrete causal links rather than stage position, file discovery, or unsupported confidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace enclosing query -> Exists query -> split-exclude subquery and inspect whether the related lookup RHS retains resolve_expression capability.
metadata.stage: Causal tracing across both failure boundaries

scale.1: The visible explanation is absent, unrelated, or materially wrong, such as resolving against the intermediate query or suppressing ResolvedOuterRef.as_sql().
scale.2: Relevant classes or methods are located, but no concrete causal link explains why exclude or negated Q adds the failing boundary.
scale.3: The prefix explicitly connects split_exclude and OuterRef's F inheritance to premature resolution but does not establish the separate related lookup preparation issue.
scale.4: The prefix correctly explains the additional query level and identifies expression capability, rather than immediate SQL compilability, as the related RHS boundary.
scale.5: The prefix gives a complete source-grounded trace of both boundaries and correctly separates OuterRef preservation, ordinary F conversion, literal preparation, and the unresolved-reference guard.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable causal account of both resolution boundaries

applies_when: A relevant imported production edit, executable repository regression edit, or near-final submission artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates observable regressions to established lookup behavior and defects that make the submitted repository incomplete, contaminated, or unusable.

metadata.failure_mode: Broad preparation bypass, disabled guard, missing core hunk, syntax failure, destructive edit, or execution-affecting contamination.
metadata.judge_focus: Preserve ordinary F excludes, relation-value preparation, invalid-value errors, the top-level OuterRef guard, and artifact validity.
metadata.oracle_test: Run focused related lookup, ordinary F, invalid-value, import, and patch-completeness checks.
metadata.stage: Regression sweep and final artifact review

scale.1: No visible compatibility or artifact defect; the relevant repository state is focused, complete, and importable.
scale.2: Only minor cleanup or optional compatibility evidence is missing.
scale.3: A credible compatibility risk, incomplete regression edit, or notable but recoverable artifact problem is visible.
scale.4: A representative compatibility check fails, a necessary core hunk is missing, or production code has syntax or execution-affecting contamination.
scale.5: The patch broadly disables established validation, removes the unresolved-reference guard, cannot import or apply, or contains destructive production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and evaluator-facing artifact damage

applies_when: The prefix attempts Django initialization, model registration, schema creation, repository test execution, or uses runtime output to support an ORM claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates misuse of runtime output, especially continuing after suppressed initialization or registry failure and treating later behavior as evidence about OuterRef.

metadata.failure_mode: Suppressed initialization, invalid application state, or semantic claims based on setup and schema failures.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish recognized environmental failures from invalid-state output presented as semantic evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Verify that the first settings, registry, import, schema, or lookup failure is surfaced and repaired before interpreting queryset behavior.

scale.1: The prefix uses a valid initialized environment or fails fast and does not misuse environmental output.
scale.2: The prefix encounters recognized dependency, command, settings, registry, schema, or lookup errors without drawing target-behavior conclusions from them.
scale.3: The prefix repeatedly uses an invalid harness or leaves confusing runtime artifacts, but does not suppress the decisive failure or claim a semantic result.
scale.4: The prefix suppresses or obscures initialization failure and continues constructing models or queries in an invalid runtime state.
scale.5: The prefix presents success, failure, or causal conclusions as ORM evidence after suppressed or unresolved settings, registry, import, schema, or lookup failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Runtime evidence integrity

applies_when: A visible edit changes imported ORM production code in split_exclude, related lookup preparation, field preparation, or OuterRef resolution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the production implementation preserves OuterRef through one additional query level and keeps expression-capable related RHS values out of scalar preparation without regressing ordinary behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Missing boundary, unreachable type check, immediate resolution, literalization, broad preparation bypass, or global guard suppression.
metadata.judge_focus: The specialized OuterRef path precedes the ordinary F path, and related RHS classification uses expression capability.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect Query.split_exclude() and RelatedLookupMixin.get_prep_lookup(), then compile the affected nested query.

scale.1: The production edit preserves the defect, resolves against the wrong query, suppresses the guard, or is unrelated to the active path.
scale.2: The edit reaches a relevant location but is malformed, speculative, or does not reliably fix either causal boundary.
scale.3: Exactly one required boundary is plausibly fixed, or both are attempted with a material correctness defect.
scale.4: Both required boundaries are narrowly implemented and ordinary F handling is retained, but focused semantic or compatibility evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: Both boundaries are correctly implemented in imported production code, scalar and model-instance preparation remains intact, and the focused diff is complete and importable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete expression-preserving production implementation

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, creates, or executes validation for the scalar-field-to-cross-app-relation migration behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether validation concretely models a retained scalar field becoming a cross-app ForeignKey and semantically checks both the generated AlterField and the migration dependency on creation of the referenced model.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if every attempted execution fails before valid migration states and autodetection are reached. Cap at 2 for source-text occurrence checks presented as behavioral tests. Cap at 3 if the exact semantic test fails after reaching the changed code or if only pre-fix failure is demonstrated.
metadata.evidence_authority: A completed repository-runner result from the exact semantic regression has highest authority, followed by a complete displayed repository-compatible test body. A failure that reaches the asserted migration behavior outranks environment setup failures. Greps, package installation, syntax-only checks, and prose plans are non-confirmatory.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents generic test discovery, dependency installation, malformed model scripts, and static string checks from being scored as completed regression validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a complete visible executable artifact containing both operation and dependency assertions, or an execution that validly reaches autodetection for the task scenario. Score 4 requires the exact post-change semantic check to pass. Score 5 also requires relevant surrounding autodetector coverage to pass.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual displayed test or reproduction for old and new ModelState fixtures, use of the repository's autodetector helper, an AlterField assertion, an external migration-dependency assertion, and the observed command result.
metadata.oracle_test: A repository-native test compares an old state containing a retained UUIDField with a new state containing a ForeignKey of the same name to a model in another app, then asserts an AlterField operation and a source-app migration dependency on the migration creating the target model.

scale.1: No task-specific validation artifact or execution is visible; activity is limited to generic browsing or assertions that testing is needed.
scale.2: A task-related plan, search, or attempted check is visible, but it lacks the complete semantic assertions or fails before valid autodetection is exercised.
scale.3: A complete repository-compatible regression artifact is visible but not successfully run, or a valid execution reaches the target behavior and exposes the expected missing dependency or an implementation defect.
scale.4: The exact regression runs successfully after the change and verifies both AlterField generation and the cross-app migration dependency.
scale.5: The level-4 regression passes and relevant surrounding migration-autodetector tests also pass without contradictory failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Builds and executes the exact altered-relation dependency regression

applies_when: The trajectory examines or creates evidence for the UUIDField-to-ForeignKey migration dependency behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses Django migration-autodetector tests to model an existing UUIDField becoming a cross-app ForeignKey and checks both the AlterField operation and the resulting migration dependency on the referenced model's app migration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed reproduction, a test that never reaches autodetection, or a failing targeted test caps credit at 3; dependency-installation failures are non-confirmatory rather than passing evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed semantic test output outranks static source searches, ad hoc print scripts, or assertions that tests should pass; failing targeted tests outrank unrelated passing tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats successful parsing, helper occurrence counts, package installation, or generic existing FK tests as proof that this regression is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an executable semantic regression test that asserts the generated migration dependency, not only source-text checks or import/syntax checks.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible ModelState fixtures, get_changes/autodetector usage, dependency assertions, operation assertions, and results from the repository's supported migration test runner.
metadata.oracle_test: Given an old state with a UUIDField and a new state with the same field name as a ForeignKey to a model in another app, changes contain AlterField and the source app migration depends on the migration that provides the target model, preventing 'Related model ... cannot be resolved'.

scale.1: No relevant test investigation or runtime evidence.
scale.2: Only generic test searching, environment setup, or a non-executable reproduction with no precise dependency assertion.
scale.3: Defines a credible task-specific test plan or test code covering old/new states, AlterField, and cross-app dependency, but it is not successfully executed.
scale.4: A task-specific semantic regression test is visibly added and passes, but broader relevant migration-autodetector coverage is absent or inconclusive.
scale.5: The focused regression passes and relevant existing migration-autodetector tests also pass, with output showing the intended AlterField dependency behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression test and runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why converting an existing non-relational field into a relation omits a migration dependency.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly traces the conversion through migration autodetection and identifies that the AlterField path must attach the new relation's model dependency, rather than attributing the problem to migration writing, loading, schema execution, or field-operation serialization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory ultimately locates dependency generation in the writer, loader, graph, schema editor, or AlterField constructor despite visible source showing that autodetector.add_operation() stores auto-dependencies. Cap at 3 if it identifies generate_altered_fields() but never connects the new relation to _get_dependencies_for_foreign_key().
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly inspected source and observed call signatures outrank summaries or unsupported assertions. A later source-backed correction outranks an earlier hypothesis. Merely repeating the issue description is not diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding lengthy repository exploration or generic ForeignKey discussion as equivalent to identifying the exact missing causal edge.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require explicit recognition that UUIDField-to-ForeignKey remains on the non-M2M AlterField path and that this path lacks the relation dependency supplied by the AddField path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source excerpts and reasoning about generate_altered_fields(), _generate_added_field(), _get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(), add_operation(), and operation._auto_deps. Credit causal comparisons between the working AddField path and the deficient AlterField path.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, both UUIDField and ForeignKey are non-many-to-many fields, so generate_altered_fields() emits AlterField. The operation must receive auto-dependencies derived from the new relational field through MigrationAutodetector._get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(), passed to MigrationAutodetector.add_operation().

scale.1: No task-specific causal localization; investigation remains broad, materially misunderstands the migration path, or ends on an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Recognizes that a relation dependency is missing but pursues an incorrect or unsupported mechanism for creating it.
scale.3: Narrows the defect to altered-field autodetection or contrasts AddField with AlterField, but omits either the actual AlterField path condition or the auto-dependency helper/attachment mechanism.
scale.4: Correctly identifies generate_altered_fields() as missing the new relation dependency and connects it to _get_dependencies_for_foreign_key() and add_operation(), with only a minor unresolved detail.
scale.5: Provides a complete source-backed causal account: the non-M2M conversion emits AlterField, AddField already computes the needed dependency, AlterField does not, and add_operation(..., dependencies=...) is the correct attachment point.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precisely localizes the missing dependency in altered-field autodetection

applies_when: The selected trajectory applies or attempts a repository code change for dependency generation when an existing field becomes relational.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates visible implementation progress toward deriving the new relation's dependency before registration and attaching it to a normally constructed AlterField through the autodetector's add_operation() interface.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied edit that passes dependencies to AlterField itself, computes them only after operation registration, leaves them unused, reverses the dependency direction, or visibly corrupts syntax or branch structure cannot score above 2 unless a later visible repair supersedes it. An execution failure that reaches the changed API is evidence of an applied but defective implementation, not evidence that no implementation occurred. Cap at 3 when the relevant edit is executed but the final integrated call structure remains materially unverified.
metadata.evidence_authority: A complete latest diff or post-edit source listing has highest authority for final structure. Focused parser or test output outranks claims of success and can establish that an edit was applied even when it disproves correctness. An unambiguous edit command establishes an attempted change but not a coherent final state. A later displayed repair supersedes earlier malformed edits. Summary fields reporting no changes do not override a visibly executed edit or observed changed-code failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents browsing-only work from tying with applied implementation attempts, while still distinguishing unsupported constructor arguments, post-registration computation, and corrupted substitutions from a coherent add_operation() integration. It also prevents environment failures or source-text checks from being treated as behavioral success.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 2 requires a visible applied task-relevant edit or execution reaching changed code. Score 3 requires evidence that dependency computation and add_operation() attachment are both targeted, though final structural coherence may remain partially unverified. Score 4 requires visible coherent final source or diff with supported argument placement and preserved control flow. Score 5 requires passing task-specific behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible state around generate_altered_fields(). Check whether dependencies are initialized before registration, derived from the effective new relation, supplied to self.add_operation(), excluded from operations.AlterField(), and kept within the AlterField-producing branch without damaging the many-to-many versus concrete-field fallback. Separately record whether execution merely exposed a defect or confirmed correct behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Within the branch that emits AlterField, the implementation derives dependencies from the effective new relational field using _get_dependencies_for_foreign_key() or an equivalent, constructs AlterField only with supported field-operation arguments, and calls self.add_operation(app_label, alter_operation, dependencies=dependencies). A regression scenario then shows the source migration depending on the migration that creates the referenced model.

scale.1: No repository implementation is visibly applied; the work remains at browsing, diagnosis, a proposed patch, or an unrelated edit.
scale.2: A task-relevant code change is visibly attempted, but the applied state is unusable or incomplete because dependencies are attached to AlterField, computed after registration, left unused, structurally corrupted, or otherwise contradicted by observed execution.
scale.3: The applied work targets both dependency extraction from the effective new relation and attachment through add_operation(), but the final source is only partially displayed, a repair remains unverified, or another material integration detail is unresolved.
scale.4: The latest visible source or diff coherently computes dependencies before registration, constructs AlterField with supported arguments, passes dependencies to add_operation(), and preserves the surrounding altered-field and fallback branches; task-specific behavioral success is not yet shown.
scale.5: The coherent level-4 implementation is confirmed by a passing task-specific autodetector regression that checks the generated cross-app dependency, with relevant surrounding migration tests also passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Integrates the altered-field dependency through autodetector registration

applies_when: The selected trajectory explicitly begins validation by inspecting a repository test module or helper for this defect, creating a test or reproduction artifact, or executing a syntax, focused-test, or migration-autodetector command.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how much reliable, task-specific evidence the validation work produces. Distinguish commands that fail before exercising migration logic from repository-aware test design, executions that expose the relevant API or dependency defect, and passing regression coverage. Credit productive learning from a failed test when the failure directly constrains the implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed successful validation is overridden by visible syntax errors, import failures, malformed tool calls, invalid model declarations, or tests that never invoke migration autodetection. Cap at 2 when every execution fails before constructing valid migration states and the trajectory does not convert those failures into a repository-native plan. Cap at 3 when a relevant suite exposes an implementation defect that remains unrepaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from the repository's test runner or a valid MigrationAutodetector scenario has highest authority, followed by a complete displayed repository-compatible test body. A focused failure that reaches the changed API is stronger than package installation or import failures. Test-module inspection and a concrete state-and-assertion plan outrank generic greps and static source-string checks.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents environmental setup, malformed scripts, and text searches from being mistaken for behavioral validation. It also avoids collapsing all unsuccessful runs together by recognizing when execution reaches the target code and reveals a causal implementation error.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires either inspection of the repository's migration-autodetector helpers with a concrete old-state, new-state, operation, and dependency assertion plan, or a correctly targeted project test command. Score 4 requires a complete compatible regression artifact or execution that reaches the relevant migration or operation code. Score 5 requires affirmative post-change behavior and relevant surrounding-test confirmation.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine what the validation actually exercised. Look for use of existing ModelState and get_changes-style helpers, a retained scalar field becoming a cross-app relation, assertions for AlterField and the external migration dependency, use of the repository test runner, and whether failures occur before or after target code is reached. Reward explicit adaptation after errors.
metadata.oracle_test: A strong regression uses the existing migration-autodetector test infrastructure to compare an old model state containing a scalar UUIDField with a new state containing a ForeignKey to a model in another app. It asserts that an AlterField is generated and that the migration depends on creation of the referenced model, then runs the focused test and relevant autodetector tests.

scale.1: Performs only nominal validation activity such as generic searches or commands that do not meaningfully target migration behavior, with no reusable test design.
scale.2: Creates or runs a task-related check, but it is malformed, uses invalid APIs or model declarations, or stops at environment/import setup before migration states or the repository harness are reached.
scale.3: Inspects the repository-native autodetector test machinery and specifies a credible old/new state and assertion plan, or invokes the correct project test target but is blocked by environment setup; no complete behavioral result is available.
scale.4: Shows a complete repository-compatible regression or executes a valid scenario that reaches the target code and checks or exposes the AlterField dependency behavior, including a focused failure that directly reveals incorrect dependency API placement.
scale.5: Shows the focused regression passing after the implementation change and confirms that relevant surrounding migration-autodetector tests pass without a contradictory failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces causally informative validation for generated relation dependencies

applies_when: The visible trajectory inspects migration-autodetector test infrastructure, creates a reproduction or regression artifact, or runs a check for the scalar-field-to-cross-app-relation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the maturity and execution authority of validation that models a retained scalar field becoming a cross-app ForeignKey and checks both AlterField generation and the source migration's dependency on creation of the referenced model.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when every attempted execution fails before valid migration states and autodetection are reached and no repository-native test design is completed. Source-text checks and scripts that only print an expected result cannot exceed 2. Cap at 3 when a displayed artifact omits either the AlterField assertion or the cross-app dependency assertion. A relevant execution failure reaching changed code can score 4 as informative validation but cannot score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from the repository's supported test runner or a valid direct MigrationAutodetector scenario has highest authority, followed by a complete displayed repository-compatible test body. A focused failure after valid states reach autodetection outranks an unexecuted artifact. A complete artifact outranks a prose plan. Import failures, package installation, malformed model declarations, source-text occurrence checks, and success claims without output are non-confirmatory.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents environment setup, invalid ProjectState APIs, print-only scripts, and generic FK tests from tying with a complete semantic regression or an execution that reaches and diagnoses the altered-field dependency path.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires repository-harness inspection plus an explicit old-state, new-state, operation, and dependency assertion design. Score 4 requires either a complete executable artifact containing both semantic assertions or valid execution that reaches and observes the target autodetection behavior. Score 5 requires affirmative post-change semantic success and relevant surrounding-test confirmation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether validation uses repository-compatible ModelState fixtures and the existing autodetector/get_changes-style helper, preserves the same model and field identity across old and new states, targets another app's model, and asserts both the AlterField operation and resulting migration dependency. Record whether execution failed before state construction, reached autodetection, exposed changed-code behavior, or passed.
metadata.oracle_test: A repository-native regression compares an old ProjectState containing a retained UUIDField with a new ProjectState containing a ForeignKey of the same model and field name to a model in another app. It asserts that the source app receives an AlterField and that its migration depends on the migration providing the target model, preventing an unresolved-related-model migration state.

scale.1: No task-specific validation design or execution is visible; activity is limited to generic browsing, unrelated tests, or unsupported claims that testing is needed.
scale.2: A task-related search, environment setup, print-only script, malformed reproduction, or execution attempt is visible, but it neither reaches valid autodetection nor provides a complete repository-native old/new-state and assertion design.
scale.3: The trajectory inspects the repository's autodetector test machinery and specifies a concrete retained-scalar-to-cross-app-ForeignKey scenario with planned AlterField and dependency assertions, but no complete artifact containing both assertions and no valid target-behavior execution is visible.
scale.4: A complete repository-compatible artifact visibly contains both the AlterField and cross-app dependency assertions but is not successfully run, or a valid execution reaches autodetection and observes the target behavior or a directly relevant implementation defect; affirmative post-change success is not established.
scale.5: The exact semantic regression passes after the implementation change and verifies both AlterField generation and the cross-app migration dependency, with relevant surrounding autodetector coverage also passing and no contradictory relevant failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Constructs and exercises a repository-native altered-relation regression

applies_when: The trajectory reaches test design, repository test modification, or broader compatibility checking for the call_command() change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Integrates a focused regression test into Django's existing management-command test fixtures and protects ordinary required options, optional mutually exclusive groups, destination aliases, and existing command behavior without adding disposable artifacts or unrelated production changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If production code is changed without any persistent regression test, credit is capped at 3; if visible artifacts alter Django's command package solely for ad hoc testing or official tests visibly fail because of the change, credit is capped at 2 until cleaned or resolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Committed-style test diffs and successful official targeted tests outrank temporary files and custom scripts; a clean final diff outranks earlier untracked experiments.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents high credit for a locally plausible patch that lacks maintainable test coverage, pollutes production command discovery, or regresses ordinary required arguments and aliases.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a persistent regression test in the repository rather than only temporary scripts. Anchor 5 requires visible successful targeted-suite evidence or comparably authoritative regression execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes under the established management command test area, assertions using existing Django test conventions, targeted suite commands and results, and repository diff/status cleanliness.
metadata.oracle_test: A repository regression should define or reuse a command with a required mutually exclusive group and assert call_command() accepts a supplied destination kwarg while still enforcing missing-required and exclusivity behavior; existing individually required option handling must remain intact.

scale.1: No regression consideration is visible, or the trajectory leaves harmful test artifacts/unresolved official failures.
scale.2: Only disposable scripts or generic searches for tests are visible, with no repository-integrated coverage and material cleanup or compatibility concerns.
scale.3: Relevant compatibility cases are reasoned about or exercised ad hoc, and the production diff appears narrow, but no persistent regression test is added.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test is visibly added in an appropriate existing test area and covers the core kwargs success plus required-group failure semantics; authoritative execution may be incomplete.
scale.5: Repository-quality tests cover the core case and meaningful compatibility cases such as the alternate destination/alias, ordinary required options, CLI behavior, or exclusivity; targeted official tests visibly pass and the final diff is clean and narrowly scoped.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression protection and repository-quality integration

applies_when: A source change or concrete implementation plan is visible for Django's management command option parsing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the call_command() argument-simulation logic needed to pass a supplied member of a required mutually exclusive group through parse_args(), using the action's destination and option spelling while retaining existing handling of individually required options and final kwargs merging.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed helper, invalid indentation, duplicate parse_args entries, unconditional arg_options indexing for unsupplied siblings, destructive checkout that removes the fix, or unrelated module-level monkey-patching caps credit at 2 until visibly repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: A coherent repository diff and executable source outrank prose or temporary simulation scripts; the final visible source state outranks earlier attempted edits.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad rewrites, use of nonexistent action.group/container semantics, accidental KeyError on the unsupplied sibling, or a plan that never reaches the source file.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an applied, syntactically coherent source change that includes only supplied group members and preserves the existing opt.required path.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or exact code in django/core/management/__init__.py around parser_actions, required mutually exclusive groups, parse_args construction, and arg_options.
metadata.oracle_test: The implementation should treat an action as parser-required when action.required is true or when that action is contained in a mutually exclusive group with group.required true, and should serialize it only when its supplied destination exists, producing for example --shop-id=1.

scale.1: No concrete implementation is visible, or the source is left unchanged/restored.
scale.2: A source edit exists but is malformed, targets the wrong boundary, accesses absent sibling values, uses invalid argparse assumptions, or otherwise cannot implement the behavior safely.
scale.3: A plausible applied change recognizes required group actions, but its scope, supplied-option guard, subparser interaction, duplication behavior, or final source coherence remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The applied change is coherent and narrowly extends the existing required-option condition to supplied actions in required mutually exclusive groups while preserving ordinary required options; only minor clarity or coverage concerns remain.
scale.5: The final visible diff is minimal and idiomatic, cleanly derives required-group actions from argparse's group structures, uses destination-normalized arg_options safely, preserves existing call_command() behavior, and contains no unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise call_command implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory investigates call_command() with keyword options belonging to an argparse mutually exclusive group whose group-level required flag is true.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that call_command() validates required options through parse_args(), while each member action of a required mutually exclusive group still has action.required false, so a supplied kwarg is omitted from the simulated argument vector and group validation reports that no member was supplied.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible output disproves the claimed argparse representation, or the trajectory continues relying on a nonexistent/wrong group attribute after that contradiction, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful reproduction plus observed argparse action/group state outranks an unsupported explanation; inspected repository source outranks assumptions about action.container or nonexistent argparse attributes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for vague 'kwargs parsing is broken' claims, searching only base.py, or incorrectly treating each group member as individually required.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit evidence that group.required is true while its member actions have required false and that call_command() filters on the individual action flag.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime introspection connecting call_command()'s opt.required filter with parser._mutually_exclusive_groups, each required group's _group_actions, and the reported CommandError.
metadata.oracle_test: For a command with required=True on a mutually exclusive group containing --shop-id/dest shop_id and --shop/dest shop_name, call_command(..., shop_id=1) fails before the fix because parse_args() receives neither group member, whereas the equivalent CLI-style --shop-id=1 satisfies the group.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis is visible, or the explanation fundamentally misidentifies where call_command() or argparse stores the requirement.
scale.2: The trajectory locates call_command() and suspects opt.required but does not establish the group/action distinction, or retains a contradicted model of argparse groups.
scale.3: The explanation correctly states the individual-required versus group-required mismatch and identifies the relevant call_command() filter, but provides only source reasoning or incomplete introspection.
scale.4: Visible source and argparse introspection establish the mismatch, including required group membership through _mutually_exclusive_groups/_group_actions, but the complete failing call_command() behavior is not cleanly reproduced.
scale.5: A clean before-fix reproduction and source/introspection evidence jointly demonstrate the full causal chain, including kwargs failure, equivalent CLI-style success, and omission of the supplied group member from simulated parse_args().

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of required mutually exclusive kwargs

applies_when: A source edit, rollback, or concrete code-level repair plan is visible for Django's call_command() argument simulation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Advances a safe, persistent repair of call_command() so only supplied actions from required mutually exclusive groups are simulated through parse_args(), while retaining individually required options, normalized destination lookup, and existing option merging.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest visible production state containing invalid syntax or indentation, an undefined helper input, nonexistent argparse relationships, duplicate serialization, unconditional lookup of an unsupplied group sibling, or an observed failure caused by the new logic scores at most 1. An explicit rollback cancels defects from the reverted edit and is judged as a clean implementation-ready state rather than as persistent broken code. A success message without inspectable code or target-path behavior cannot by itself establish an applied repair.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest explicit production diff, source excerpt, or checkout determines repository state. A later rollback outranks an earlier edit. Complete source and repository-path execution outrank edit-script messages, prose, and copied simulations; however, execution cannot excuse a malformed visible implementation, and setup or command-discovery failures provide no behavioral confirmation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding malformed helpers, unsafe sibling indexing, duplicate action lists, destination-only approximations that lose action ownership, speculative subparser traversal, copied simulations presented as repository execution, and reverted defects treated as still present. It also preserves credit for a precise safe plan after a defective edit is deliberately removed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a persistent, syntactically coherent production change whose relevant selection and value guard are inspectable, or a sufficiently complete visible edit corroborated by execution through Django's imported call_command() path. Score 5 additionally requires a minimal final diff showing action membership in the owning parser's required mutually exclusive groups, one supplied-destination guard, and one token-construction path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest state of django/core/management/__init__.py around parser action discovery, parser._mutually_exclusive_groups, group._group_actions, destination-normalized arg_options, and parse_args construction. Distinguish an exact clean-source repair plan from an opaque claimed edit, and distinguish both from a coherent persistent implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: For a required group containing --shop-id with destination shop_id and --shop with destination shop_name, the repair should select the supplied action by membership in a required group, read only its normalized destination value, and emit one corresponding token. Either member should satisfy parsing, neither should retain the required-group error, both should retain exclusivity, and an ordinary action.required option should continue to be simulated.

scale.1: The latest production state is visibly malformed or causally unsafe, duplicates a selected token, reads an absent sibling, uses invalid argparse structure, or is contradicted by a reached target-path failure attributable to the edit.
scale.2: An edit is claimed or partly displayed, but its final selection condition, supplied-value guard, parser ownership, or source coherence cannot be established; diagnosis alone is incomplete or contains unsafe assumptions.
scale.3: A precise implementation-ready repair is visible against a clean or deliberately restored source, or a persistent partial edit clearly preserves the ordinary required-action branch and identifies required-group action membership but still lacks enough final code or execution to establish safe exactly-once construction.
scale.4: A persistent coherent edit extends the existing simulation to supplied members of required mutually exclusive groups, preserves individually required actions, uses normalized destination values safely, and is either fully inspectable or credibly corroborated by repository-path execution; only limited scope or clarity concerns remain.
scale.5: The final visible diff is minimal and idiomatic, derives membership from each owning parser's required mutually exclusive-group action collection, guards every value lookup by the supplied normalized destination, emits each action once, preserves existing parsing and merging, and has no unrelated production changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe and persistent call_command required-group repair

applies_when: The trajectory runs or adds tests for a management command containing a required mutually exclusive option group.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides end-to-end evidence that kwargs for either group member satisfy the required group while omission still fails, and that argparse's exclusivity semantics are not bypassed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the claimed success is actually an Unknown command, import/setup failure, direct reimplementation of the patched condition, or a test that unexpectedly accepts both members, credit is capped at 2 unless later valid evidence resolves it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual call_command() results from a registered command outrank direct parser simulations; repository test-run results outrank ad hoc print-only scripts; failed setup and unknown-command output are non-evidence for task behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating a standalone comprehension test, parser-only experiment, or broken command registration as proof that Django call_command() is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires at least one successful post-change call_command(..., shop_id=...) execution and one expected failure with neither group member. Anchor 5 additionally requires the alternate member and mutual-exclusion/CLI compatibility coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible call_command() executions or repository tests using a discoverable BaseCommand, with assertions on success, parsed values, and expected CommandError cases.
metadata.oracle_test: Expected matrix: shop_id=1 succeeds with shop_id 1 and shop_name None; shop_name='x' succeeds with the converse values; no member raises the required-group CommandError; equivalent CLI-form input remains successful; supplying both through parser-visible inputs remains mutually exclusive.

scale.1: No relevant execution evidence is visible, or all attempted tests fail before reaching the behavior.
scale.2: Only direct argparse/simulated-logic evidence is present, or call_command() tests yield setup, import, registration, or unrelated errors.
scale.3: A valid end-to-end execution demonstrates the original kwargs case succeeding after an applied change, but required failure behavior or the alternate member is untested.
scale.4: Valid end-to-end evidence covers kwargs success for a group member and failure when neither member is supplied, with parsed values shown or asserted.
scale.5: A coherent test matrix covers both destination kwargs, the missing-member failure, existing CLI-style success, and preservation of exclusivity when both parser-visible alternatives are supplied, with all observed results matching expectations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive behavioral validation of mutual-exclusion semantics

applies_when: Runtime checks or test results concerning the form are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates successful checks of the actual affected form while keeping validation subordinate to visible production semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: Pre-fix-only evidence, mock checks, setup failures, field-only assertions, or wrong-type values
metadata.judge_focus: Post-edit raw widget state, rendering, and dynamic branches

scale.1: No successful task-specific runtime observation is visible, or a post-edit check shows the repair remains ineffective.
scale.2: A useful pre-fix actual-form observation or partial check is visible, but no successful post-edit target-form result is established.
scale.3: A post-edit actual-form check shows matching field and raw widget state or corrected rendering for one configuration.
scale.4: Post-edit checks cover the model-defined and fallback configurations with correct raw widget values.
scale.5: Both dynamic branches, raw integer state, stale-value overwrite, rendered HTML, and focused authentication-form regressions visibly pass against the checkout.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative runtime validation

applies_when: Source tracing, reproduction, or diagnosis of the AuthenticationForm maxlength regression is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether checkout evidence localizes the regression to a model-derived maximum assigned after widget construction, leaving the actual AuthenticationForm widget stale and requiring narrow synchronization of the existing widget.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if later visible work applies or explicitly commits to widget_attrs() replay, string conversion, setdefault(), a no-op widget_attrs() call, pre-super/base-field mutation, widget replacement, or shared-infrastructure changes. A failed post-edit target-form check also caps at 3. Rendered output or widget_attrs() return values alone cannot satisfy the hard gate.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible checkout-backed target-form state and current production source outrank narration, history, detached fields, mocks, and generated-attribute dictionaries. A later visible edit or post-edit result that contradicts the stated diagnosis overrides earlier claims of a sound remedy.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding maximal causal credit from rendered symptoms, generic field simulations, or an initially correct explanation despite a later ineffective or wrong-typed synchronization mechanism.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require direct inspection of the checkout's actual AuthenticationForm showing a populated field maximum alongside a missing stored widget maxlength, plus an initialization-order explanation. Score 5 additionally requires a viable instance-level remedy that mutates the existing widget after the active model lookup.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual AuthenticationForm field maximum, its stored widget.attrs mapping, rendered output when available, and the initialization-time CharField.widget_attrs path; distinguish stored state from a dictionary merely returned by widget_attrs().
metadata.oracle_test: Before repair, an actual AuthenticationForm has field.max_length equal to the active USERNAME_FIELD maximum or 254, while widget.attrs lacks maxlength and rendered HTML omits it; the cause is that CharField.widget_attrs() ran before the runtime model lookup, so the existing widget must later receive the same effective integer directly.

scale.1: The mechanism is materially misidentified, or visible evidence consists only of setup failures, unrelated code, or unsupported claims.
scale.2: Checkout source, history, detached-field behavior, or rendered output suggests the late-assignment issue, but the actual AuthenticationForm's stored field/widget mismatch and a viable narrow remedy are not both established.
scale.3: Useful target-form evidence or a substantially correct stale-state diagnosis is visible, but it is incomplete, or later visible work is capped by an ineffective, replay-based, wrong-typed, stale-preserving, reordered, or over-broad repair mechanism.
scale.4: The actual checkout AuthenticationForm visibly has a populated field maximum and missing stored widget maxlength; initialization timing is correctly connected to that mismatch and mutation of the existing widget after lookup is selected, with no later contradiction, but one supporting detail or the exact direct-integer remedy remains unconfirmed.
scale.5: The actual target form's field, stored widget mapping, and initialization path jointly establish the stale-state cause; generated widget attributes are correctly distinguished from stored attrs, and the diagnosis selects direct post-lookup overwrite of the existing widget with the same effective integer, with no contradictory later edit or check.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Checkout-backed stale-state diagnosis

applies_when: A production implementation attempt is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible mechanism uses the active model-derived maximum and fallback to overwrite both the field and existing widget with the same raw integer without collateral behavior changes.

metadata.failure_mode: Fixed value, wrong fallback, string value, replay, setdefault, widget replacement, or shared-infrastructure expansion
metadata.judge_focus: Dynamic dual assignment, integer type, overwrite, and preservation

scale.1: The edit cannot repair the late widget state or introduces a severe unrelated change.
scale.2: The edit reaches the widget but uses a confirmed wrong type or mechanism, permits stale state, or updates only one side.
scale.3: The intended mechanism is direct and dynamic, but visible source context leaves a material ambiguity about type, placement, fallback, or executability.
scale.4: The visible source directly synchronizes both targets with the correct dynamic integer and preserves the existing widget and surrounding behavior.
scale.5: The direct synchronization is unambiguous and visible evidence also confirms overwrite behavior, preserved unrelated attributes, and both dynamic branches.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Synchronization mechanism correctness

applies_when: Investigation or editing of the AuthenticationForm username maxlength behavior is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest production-repair state actually visible by the cutoff, preserving distinctions among no edit, a confirmed defective edit, an executed but incompletely inspected correct-looking mutation, and a coherent correct hunk.

metadata.failure_mode: Flattening an attempted narrow repair into no edit, or treating an announced edit as completed
metadata.judge_focus: Observed repository mutation and exact direct synchronization

scale.1: No task-relevant production mutation is visible, or the only visible edit is ineffective for AuthenticationForm.
scale.2: A production mutation is visible but it is confirmed partial or materially wrong, such as string conversion, replay, setdefault(), one-sided synchronization, or shared-code indirection.
scale.3: An exact narrow direct-assignment mutation is visibly executed or partially shown, but the resulting hunk remains incomplete, truncated, or otherwise ambiguous at the cutoff.
scale.4: A coherent source hunk visibly assigns the dynamic integer to both the field and existing widget while preserving the initializer, but post-edit evidence or final integrity inspection is limited.
scale.5: The coherent correct hunk is visible and its executable repository state is confirmed by source integrity inspection or successful target-form behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible implementation progression

applies_when: A visible patch, edited source excerpt, or concrete implementation proposal changes migration serialization of enum.Enum members.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the migration enum serialization boundary so generated code is a valid imported enum-class lookup by a quoted member name, such as module.Status['GOOD'], rather than constructor lookup by a value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if visible code emits EnumClass('NAME'), EnumClass[NAME] without a quoted/serialized string, omits the enum module import, or otherwise cannot execute as migration Python. Cap at 2 if self.value.value remains the reconstruction key.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source excerpt or final diff overrides earlier experiments, prose claims, and ad hoc output generated from a different implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes changing the data from value to name for a complete fix while leaving constructor syntax, invalid quoting, or missing imports.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible applied code that emits syntactically valid EnumClass['NAME'] and retains the import needed to resolve the enum class.
metadata.judge_focus: The final visible EnumSerializer implementation or diff: use of self.value.name, square-bracket lookup, valid quoting or serialization of the name, and preservation of the enum class module import.
metadata.oracle_test: Evaluating the emitted expression with its reported imports must return the original member; Status['GOOD'] is valid, whereas Status('GOOD') normally raises ValueError and Status[GOOD] normally raises NameError.

scale.1: No relevant implementation is visible, or the change is confined to an unrelated component.
scale.2: Touches EnumSerializer but retains value-based reconstruction or introduces a clearly unrelated or nonfunctional transformation.
scale.3: Attempts name-based serialization but leaves a decisive defect such as constructor syntax, an unquoted member name, a missing module import, or visibly malformed code.
scale.4: Emits valid quoted name lookup with the required module import, but uses avoidably broad edits, fragile formatting, or unnecessary reconstruction logic.
scale.5: Applies a focused, robust EnumSerializer change that obtains the member name, emits valid EnumClass['NAME'] syntax, preserves exactly the necessary imports, and avoids collateral serializer changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Valid name-based EnumSerializer implementation

applies_when: The trajectory contains commands, tests, or runtime output intended to demonstrate enum migration serialization behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces trustworthy runtime evidence that serialized enum defaults use stable name lookup and that the generated expression reconstructs the original member, including the translation-sensitive scenario where relevant.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a claimed passing check visibly raises an exception, tests only a hand-written expression, or the observed output differs from the claimed expected syntax. Cap at 3 if output is checked textually but never shown to reconstruct the enum member.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful command output exercising the repository implementation outranks printed expectations, comments, conceptual demonstrations, or assertions that do not execute the generated expression.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats self-authored print statements, substring checks, or standard Enum bracket behavior as proof that Django's generated migration code is valid.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence from Django's actual serializer or MigrationWriter rather than manually composing the desired string.
metadata.judge_focus: Observed serializer or MigrationWriter output, execution or round-trip of that output with imports, field-level serialization, lazy translated values, and outcomes for representative Enum and IntEnum members.
metadata.oracle_test: Serialization of a field default Status.GOOD should visibly contain Status['GOOD']; evaluating the expression after applying its imports should yield Status.GOOD even when the value is lazy translated text.

scale.1: No relevant runtime or test evidence is visible, or all attempted evidence fails before exercising serialization.
scale.2: Shows only conceptual Enum behavior, manually constructed expected strings, or failed serializer experiments.
scale.3: Successfully exercises the actual enum serializer and observes name-based output, but does not execute or round-trip the generated expression.
scale.4: Shows actual serializer or field-level output and successful reconstruction for multiple representative enum types, but does not cover the exact translation-sensitive case or equivalent locale-independent evidence.
scale.5: Demonstrates the exact lazy-translated default scenario through Django serialization, executes or round-trips the generated code to the original member, and includes successful relevant regression-test execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive semantic and runtime evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes migration serialization of enum instances used in model field definitions or defaults.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied migration serializer emits valid Python that reconstructs an enum member by its stable member name, with every required import, rather than by its potentially translated value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An expression that still uses the enum value, calls the enum constructor with the member name, or subscripts with an unquoted name is capped at 1. A valid quoted name lookup that omits a required module import is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest applied repository source or unified diff wins over earlier edits; observed output from that applied code wins over prose claims. Isolated mock snippets, intended patches, comments, and statements that tests passed are non-evidence when the repository implementation or output contradicts them.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a superficial `.value` to `.name` substitution when the surrounding constructor, quoting, or import behavior still makes the generated migration invalid.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied implementation that emits a syntactically valid name-based enum lookup and supplies the enum class module import required by the generated migration.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest applied serializer code or diff, the exact generated expression, its quoting and lookup syntax, and the returned import set. Credit verification through the migration or field serializer, or an equivalent execution of the generated expression.
metadata.oracle_test: After changing only an enum member's value, evaluating the generated migration expression with its returned imports must still resolve the same member through its unchanged name.

scale.1: Applied behavior remains value-based or emits an invalid/unresolvable name expression, such as `EnumClass('MEMBER')` or `EnumClass[MEMBER]`; alternatively, visible applied code directly contradicts the claimed fix.
scale.2: A relevant partial edit is applied, but the visible prefix does not establish a complete generated expression, so its syntax, lookup mode, or required imports cannot be determined.
scale.3: The applied code emits a syntactically valid quoted name lookup, but visible integration is incomplete, such as omitting the required enum module import.
scale.4: The applied code emits a valid quoted name lookup with required imports, but verification remains isolated and does not visibly establish that the migration/field serialization path or executable reconstruction uses it.
scale.5: The applied code emits a valid quoted name lookup with all required imports, and visible task-directed execution through the migration/field serializer or equivalent reconstruction confirms that it resolves the member by name independently of its value.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Enum migration serialization is stable and executable

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis or source evidence concerning serialization of an Enum member used in a migration value or field default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that Django's migration EnumSerializer reconstructs members through their potentially translated value and that stable migration code must instead look up the member by its name.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the defect primarily to CharField, the migration autodetector, database conversion, or translation machinery despite visible source showing EnumSerializer performs value-based reconstruction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed repository source and reproducible serializer output take precedence over summaries or unsupported assertions about migration generation.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards generic issue paraphrasing or investigation of unrelated migration components without establishing the actual serialization mechanism.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the behavior in EnumSerializer or equivalent direct source evidence, not merely restating the issue report.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of django/db/migrations/serializer.py, especially EnumSerializer, and reasoning connecting self.value.value plus EnumClass(value) to failures after lazy translation changes the effective value.
metadata.oracle_test: For Status.GOOD whose value is gettext_lazy('Good'), value-based Status('Good') is locale-sensitive, while name-based Status['GOOD'] identifies the same member independently of translation.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or the visible diagnosis is incompatible with the source behavior.
scale.2: Recognizes an enum/translation problem but does not establish whether value lookup, name lookup, or migration serialization is causal.
scale.3: Correctly contrasts enum values and names and explains translation instability, but does not tie it to the concrete serializer implementation.
scale.4: Locates EnumSerializer and accurately explains that self.value.value and constructor syntax produce value-based migration code.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain from field default through EnumSerializer to locale-sensitive generated code, and identifies name lookup as the stable semantic remedy while distinguishing it from mere display formatting.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of enum migration instability

applies_when: The visible prefix contains an applied change or concrete generated output for migration serialization of an enum member.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the latest applied migration serializer produces an imported, executable enum lookup using a quoted stable member name in the required `module.EnumClass['MEMBER']` form rather than a value, constructor call, unquoted subscript, or attribute expression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 whenever the latest applied behavior emits value-based reconstruction, `EnumClass('MEMBER')`, `EnumClass[MEMBER]`, `EnumClass.MEMBER`, malformed Python, or another expression outside the required quoted subscript contract. A correct quoted lookup with a missing required enum-module import is exactly score 3 and cannot receive higher credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied repository source or unified diff controls implementation status. Output demonstrably produced by that source controls emitted behavior. Either source or output may expose a defect; prose claims, earlier edits, and self-written expected expressions cannot override it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents executable attribute access, constructor syntax with a name, and unquoted subscripting from being mistaken for the requested migration representation, while preserving partial credit for a correct expression whose import integration is incomplete.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require applied code that emits exactly a quoted square-bracket member-name lookup and returns the import needed to resolve the enum class. Score 5 additionally requires visible execution through Django serialization or evaluation of the emitted expression with its returned imports.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest applied EnumSerializer source or diff, then any output produced from that implementation. Determine the exact lookup syntax, quoting of the member name, and returned enum-module import set.
metadata.non_evidence: Planned edits, comments, hand-written desired expressions, generic demonstrations of Python Enum behavior, test-pass assertions without output, and output generated before the latest applied edit are not evidence of the final serializer behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For an enum member `Status.GOOD`, the expression and imports must evaluate as `Status['GOOD']` and return `Status.GOOD`; changing only the member value must not change the serialized reconstruction key.

scale.1: The latest applied behavior is absent or decisively nonconforming: it remains value-based, calls the enum constructor with a member name, uses an unquoted subscript, uses attribute access instead of the required quoted subscript, emits malformed Python, or is contradicted by visible output.
scale.2: A relevant applied attempt or concrete proposal exists, but the visible prefix does not establish the final emitted expression or required imports, so compliance cannot be determined.
scale.3: The applied behavior emits a syntactically valid quoted lookup such as `module.Status['GOOD']`, but the returned imports omit the module required to resolve the enum class.
scale.4: The applied behavior emits the required quoted lookup and returns the required enum-module import, but no visible execution establishes that Django serialization or evaluation with those imports reconstructs the member.
scale.5: The applied behavior emits the required quoted lookup with all required imports, and visible task-directed execution through Django serialization or evaluation with the returned imports confirms reconstruction of the original member by name.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied EnumSerializer emits the required executable name lookup
