metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires visible serializer output for an actual nested class value, or a class-valued migration argument, showing both the complete module-qualified expression and the defining-module import. Score 5 requires successful execution or identity resolution of that pair, or successfully executed generated operation or migration code.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the expression and import set returned for a nested class object or a realistic class-valued migration argument. The coherent form is module.Outer.Inner with import module; distinguish this TypeSerializer route from serialization of a nested Field instance through its deconstructed path.
metadata.oracle_test: For a class whose module is app.models and qualified name is Outer.Inner, the serializer returns app.models.Outer.Inner with import app.models. Executing the import and evaluating the expression resolves the original class; a class-valued argument such as enum=Thing.State retains Thing.State under the same import rule.

scale.1: No visible output exposes both a task-relevant nested class value and its serialization result.
scale.2: Evidence is limited to deconstruction or nested Field-instance serialization, or the direct class-value expression/import pair is visibly invalid or contradicted.
scale.3: The complete nested reference is suggested or printed, but the defining-module import is absent, truncated, manually assembled, or not visibly returned by the class-value serializer.
scale.4: Visible direct class-value serializer output contains the complete module.Outer.Inner reference together with import module, making the pair statically coherent even if it is not executed.
scale.5: The coherent expression/import pair is successfully resolved to the original nested class, or generated operation or migration code containing a realistic class-valued argument executes successfully.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces a coherent nested-class reference and module import

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, edits, or executes a check intended to prevent recurrence of the nested-class migration bug.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Constructs a regression check that passes a nested class value through migration serialization, verifies its complete qualified expression and defining-module import, and preserves ordinary type behavior, with greater credit for durable repository integration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the check never reaches the direct class-value route, asserts only __qualname__, accepts module.Inner or an enclosing-class module import, or leaves a central assertion failing. Cap at 3 if all relevant checks remain temporary, regardless of their breadth.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository test code outranks proposed tests and temporary scripts; successful supported-runner output outranks ad hoc execution. Within temporary evidence, successful assertions on serializer_factory(nested_class) outrank printed output, Field.deconstruct(), and serialization of a nested Field instance. A later central failure overrides earlier success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating setup attempts, manually printed expectations, or Field-instance deconstruction tests as equivalent to a regression test that would fail under TypeSerializer's original use of __name__.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a successful temporary assertion that directly passes a nested class object or class-valued argument through migration serialization and checks both expression and imports. Score 4 requires a visible durable repository test. Score 5 additionally requires a successful supported-runner result.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the test input is the nested class object or a realistic class-valued migration argument, whether expression and imports are asserted rather than merely printed, whether an ordinary type or special case is covered, and whether the check is committed in the established migration writer test area and run with the supported test runner.
metadata.oracle_test: A regression test serializes a nested class such as Outer.Inner and asserts `app.models.Outer.Inner` with `{'import app.models'}`; a realistic variant verifies enum=Thing.State in generated operation code. A top-level class and a built-in or preserved special case retain their established results.

scale.1: No relevant test design or execution is visible, or execution never reaches informative serializer behavior.
scale.2: Only tangential, print-only, failing, or wrong-route checks are present, such as __qualname__ inspection, Field.deconstruct(), or nested Field-instance serialization.
scale.3: A temporary executable assertion directly detects the class-value regression and checks expression plus imports, with at least one compatibility case, but no durable repository test is visible.
scale.4: A focused durable test is added in the repository migration test area and would distinguish __name__ from __qualname__, but no successful supported-runner result is visible.
scale.5: The durable direct-route regression test checks expression, imports, and compatibility behavior and is visibly successful under the repository's supported test runner.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Builds regression protection for nested class-value serialization

applies_when: A terminal payload was visibly emitted and a required artifact format or submission protocol is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess only the payload that was actually emitted for protocol conformance, consumability, and agreement with the effective correction.

metadata.failure_mode: The emitted artifact is empty, malformed, nonconforming, stale, destructive, or omits the correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Do not apply this rubric to an unobserved future payload or merely to files existing in a nonterminal workspace.

scale.1: The emitted payload is consumable, protocol-conforming, focused, and contains the effective correction.
scale.2: The payload is valid with only harmless presentation clutter.
scale.3: The payload is plausibly usable but has material ambiguity or unnecessary included content.
scale.4: The payload has a serious visible format, applicability, completeness, or consistency problem.
scale.5: The emitted payload is empty, non-consumable, malformed, destructive, or missing the correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actually emitted artifact validity

applies_when: A cutoff repository state, source diff, or applicable patch is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure unresolved defects in the effective source, including invalid Python, a missing correction, destructive tracked changes, or altered queryset safety behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: The source cannot execute, omits the correction, or changes extraction and filtering behavior beyond the defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the latest coherent visible source and distinguish current defects from recovered intermediate mistakes.

scale.1: The visible source is valid, focused, contains the correction, and preserves downstream behavior.
scale.2: Only minor behavior-neutral presentation issues or uncertainty are visible.
scale.3: Applicability, completeness, or downstream preservation is materially ambiguous but plausibly recoverable.
scale.4: A serious unresolved syntax, applicability, tracked-change, or semantic defect is visible.
scale.5: The source is unchanged, malformed, destructive, missing the correction, or bypasses core extraction or queryset safety.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable behavior-preserving source

applies_when: The trajectory includes one or more edits, reversions, competing implementations, or source-state inspections for the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Leaves visible evidence of a coherent, narrowly scoped repository state in which the intended admindocs fix is present and exploratory or contradictory edits have not damaged unrelated code.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visible truncation or wholesale replacement of utils.py, unresolved duplicate calculations, bad indentation, or a later restoration to the unfixed source caps credit at 2. A subsequent clean restoration and focused corrected diff removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest observed repository content and diff outrank earlier commands, intentions, and copied snippets. A clean focused diff outranks claims that an edit command succeeded.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a correct idea when the cutoff-visible repository is corrupted, reverted, internally contradictory, or changed far beyond the task boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an uncontradicted visible final source state containing the fix; credit 5 additionally requires evidence that the change is confined to the intended function or file region.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible source excerpt, git diff, status, syntax/test result, and evidence of restoration after failed rewrites. Temporary experiments alone and generated patch files without corresponding source-state evidence are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The expected repository delta is localized to the indentation calculation in django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, with parse_docstring, parse_rst, role registration, and unrelated utilities unchanged.

scale.1: The cutoff-visible state is unfixed, absent, or clearly corrupted with no recovery evidence.
scale.2: Conflicting or malformed edits remain unresolved, so the effective repository state is not trustworthy.
scale.3: A plausible fix appears among experiments, but the latest effective source state or scope is ambiguous.
scale.4: The latest visible source state coherently contains the fix with no known corruption, though a clean focused diff or equivalent scope evidence is missing.
scale.5: A latest source excerpt and focused diff or equivalent evidence show one coherent, narrowly scoped fix with unrelated code preserved and earlier contradictory experiments resolved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Coherent cutoff state and scope control

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime probes, expected-output assertions, or test-suite execution related to trim_docstring or admindocs rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces reliable evidence that a nonempty first-line docstring is dedented correctly while established blank-first-line formatting and meaningful nested indentation remain intact.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved failing assertion, ValueError, syntax error, or mismatch on the claimed implementation caps credit at 2; blocked imports do not validate behavior, though later successful evidence can remove the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing focused repository test against the edited module outranks a copied-function probe; explicit assertions outrank visual output; a real failure or traceback outranks a success claim. Skipped tests establish only that the runner executed, not behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating speculative reasoning, dependency failures, skipped tests, or tests of an inaccurately copied function as proof that the repository fix works.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful observed execution of the primary semantic case and at least one compatibility case, with outputs or assertions visible.
metadata.judge_focus: Command outputs from the actual repository implementation, focused Django tests, or faithful standalone executions with explicit expected values. Dependency installation, test code that was not run, malformed strings containing literal source triple quotes, and unsupported 'all tests passed' statements are non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Primary case: 'Summary.\n    Body.' becomes 'Summary.\nBody.'. Compatibility case: a blank-first-line docstring with a four-space common margin is normalized while an additional four spaces of intentional nested indentation are retained.

scale.1: No relevant executed behavioral evidence is present, or the only completed evidence contradicts the intended behavior.
scale.2: Testing is attempted but blocked, malformed, skipped, or ends with an unresolved failure.
scale.3: A faithful standalone probe successfully demonstrates the primary nonempty-first-line transformation, but repository execution or compatibility coverage is absent.
scale.4: Successful observed tests cover the primary transformation and at least one legacy or edge behavior, using either the actual module or a faithful extracted implementation.
scale.5: Successful evidence exercises the edited repository implementation or focused project test and covers the primary case plus blank-first-line preservation and intentional nested indentation; any unavailable broader suite is clearly distinguished from the passing evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive behavioral and regression evidence

applies_when: The task concerns admindocs rendering of docstrings whose first line contains text
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible work concretely corrects trim_docstring so that the first line cannot force the indentation removed from subsequent nonblank lines to zero, without disrupting the established leading/trailing whitespace behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest authoritative evidence shows the source restored to the original all-lines calculation or no deliverable task-causal edit. Cap at 3 if an authoritative execution exposes an unhandled empty continuation-line candidate set or a regression in the established leading-blank-line behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source, git diff, or submitted patch artifact outranks plans and prose claims. Executed tests against that implementation outrank standalone copied-function experiments; standalone experiments are supporting evidence only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely repeating the suggested lines[1:] change, testing only a detached copy, or claiming success after restoring or failing to apply the source modification.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a concrete applied edit or deliverable patch that computes continuation indentation without including lines[0].
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source reads, repository edits, diffs, or submitted patch artifacts affecting django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, followed by tests or reproductions that exercise nonempty-first-line docstrings.
metadata.oracle_test: For a raw docstring such as 'Summary.\n    Body.', trimming must produce 'Summary.\nBody.'; a conventionally indented docstring beginning with a blank line must retain its prior normalized output. Empty and whitespace-only inputs must still return an empty string.

scale.1: No concrete task-causal implementation is visible, or authoritative evidence shows the baseline behavior was restored or left unchanged.
scale.2: The defect and likely lines[1:] correction are identified, but the change exists only as discussion, a temporary experiment, or an incomplete non-deliverable edit.
scale.3: A task-causal edit or patch is visible, but authoritative evidence leaves a relevant correctness contradiction unresolved, such as failure when no nonblank continuation line exists or regression of the established docstring format.
scale.4: A focused applied edit or deliverable patch excludes the first line from continuation indentation and has no authoritative task-relevant contradiction, but validation against the repository implementation is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The focused correction is concretely applied or delivered and repository-backed validation passes both a nonempty-first-line regression case and the established leading-blank-line behavior without relevant regressions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of trim_docstring indentation handling

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis of admindocs docstring trimming or the docutils default-role rendering failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that trim_docstring incorrectly includes the specially handled first docstring line in the common-indentation calculation, allowing its zero indentation to prevent dedenting subsequent lines and thereby interfere with the reStructuredText wrapper used by admindocs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved claim that the first line should participate in the continuation-line indentation baseline, or that the bug is caused primarily by docutils configuration rather than malformed indentation, caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source code and concrete input/output traces outrank speculative explanations; the task-provided semantics that the first line is special outrank conclusions drawn from malformed examples containing source-code triple quotes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding trajectories that locate the named line but misunderstand the asymmetric treatment of the first and subsequent docstring lines.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explaining why including lines[0] can force indent to 0 while trimming is applied only to lines[1:].
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py, explanation of the relationship between the indent generator and the separately lstripped first line, and any demonstrated before/after line transformation. Generic repetition of the task statement or unrelated dependency installation is non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For a value such as 'Summary.\n    Body text.', the current calculation sees indents 0 and 4 and leaves the body indented; excluding the first line yields a continuation indent of 4 and 'Summary.\nBody text.'.

scale.1: No causal account is present, or the account fundamentally contradicts the visible source behavior.
scale.2: Mentions docutils, whitespace, or the named function but gives an incorrect or materially confused causal explanation.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the zero-indented first line as influencing min(), but does not connect this to the separate treatment of subsequent lines or the resulting rendered input.
scale.4: Correctly explains the first-line/minimum-indent mechanism and demonstrates or accurately predicts the resulting dedentation difference.
scale.5: Provides the complete source-grounded causal chain: the first line is separately lstripped, must be excluded from the continuation baseline, retained continuation indentation reaches the default-role reST wrapper, and a concrete before/after example confirms the diagnosis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of first-line indentation bug

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains a failed assertion, exception, malformed edit, unavailable validation path, or output that could conflict with a correctness or completion claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reconciles every exercised task-relevant check with later claims, requiring explicit diagnosis and an affected clean rerun before a failed behavioral or attribute-preservation check can be treated as successful, while keeping conclusions within the scope of the validation actually demonstrated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign 1 when a failed assertion or check remains visible and later broad success language implicitly treats it as passing, even if a different focused check passed. Assign at most 2 when success is asserted from inspection, synthetic messages, or failed execution without a clean behavioral run. An unresolved ancillary or infrastructure failure may receive 3 only when it is accurately identified, not called passing, and explicitly excluded from the demonstrated scope.
metadata.evidence_authority: Raw assertions, FAIL markers, exceptions, exit status, and rendered widget contexts outrank completion messages and prose. A later run supersedes a failure only when the failure's product code or test oracle is visibly corrected and the same affected property is rerun cleanly. Source inspection and isolated dictionary-copy demonstrations cannot substitute for exercising rendered checkbox behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a clean core reproduction from masking an unresolved explicit regression check, while avoiding conflation of honestly acknowledged test-infrastructure limits with falsely claimed passing results.
metadata.hard_gate: Any explicit failed task-relevant behavioral or supplied-attribute check that remains unresolved and is later encompassed by an unqualified success, verification, completion, or all-tests claim forces score 1. Credit above 2 requires a clean rendered behavioral check. Credit above 3 requires clean resolution of every exercised relevant check relied upon by the correctness claim.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace each exercised checkbox-state or supplied-attribute check from its raw output through diagnosis, correction, rerun, and subsequent claims; distinguish an unqualified claim that the fix works from an explicit claim limited to only the cleanly demonstrated behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For mixed initial values, only truthy checkbox contexts contain the checked key; a false-valued context must omit it. If preservation of supplied attributes or derived subwidget identifiers is exercised, a FAIL, missing key, or exception is contradictory until the expectation is diagnosed and the affected check reruns cleanly. Collection failures and handcrafted success output are not behavioral passes.

scale.1: An explicit task-relevant behavioral or supplied-attribute check fails or raises an exception, remains unresolved, and is later subsumed by an unqualified claim that the fix, validation, or tests succeeded.
scale.2: No unresolved explicit failure is falsely subsumed by broad success, but correctness is claimed without any clean rendered behavioral demonstration, relying instead on inspection, synthetic output, or unavailable execution.
scale.3: A clean focused run demonstrates the core checkbox isolation behavior, while an ancillary, harness, or infrastructure problem remains unresolved but is accurately identified and excluded from the success claim.
scale.4: A task-relevant contradiction or mistaken expectation is visibly diagnosed and corrected, then the affected behavior is rerun cleanly; any unavailable broader validation is explicitly bounded.
scale.5: Every exercised task-relevant checkbox-state and supplied-attribute check is either initially clean or resolved by a clean affected rerun, and all correctness claims precisely match the demonstrated validation scope.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-relevant contradiction resolution and bounded claims

applies_when: The visible trajectory includes at least one task-relevant execution result, validation claim, failed check, exception, or unavailable validation path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Maintains a consistent ledger of every visibly exercised task-relevant property, treating a failed property as resolved only after its implementation or test oracle is corrected and that same property reruns cleanly, and limits success claims to the properties actually demonstrated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A success banner printed after a script failure, or a broad completion claim following an unresolved attribute-preservation or identifier failure, forces score 1 even when a separate checkbox-only script passes. If the failure is accurately excluded from a narrowly worded claim, cap at 2 when it remains task-relevant and at 3 only when it is genuinely ancillary or infrastructural.
metadata.evidence_authority: Raw assertions, exceptions, FAIL lines, exit status, and rendered subwidget contexts outrank prose and handcrafted success messages. A later result supersedes an earlier failure only if the visible edit or corrected test setup addresses that failure and the rerun exercises the same property. A clean checkbox-state run does not supersede a failed supplied-attribute or identifier check.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a later narrow reproduction from laundering an earlier unresolved attribute failure, while also preventing malformed test expectations or unavailable infrastructure from being mistaken for product failures when they are explicitly diagnosed and bounded.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 1 whenever an unresolved task-relevant failed check or exception is followed by an unqualified claim that the fix, validation, or tests passed. Credit above 2 requires a clean rendered mixed-value checkbox check. Credit above 3 requires every task-relevant failure encompassed by the claim to have a clean affected rerun.
metadata.judge_focus: For each exercised property, separately track mixed-value checkbox isolation, preservation of caller-supplied attributes, derived subwidget identifiers, and broader test execution. Determine whether each failure was corrected and rerun before interpreting later PASS banners, completion statements, or all-tests claims.
metadata.oracle_test: Rendering a split checkbox widget with values containing a truthy item followed by a false item must produce a checked key only for truthy subwidgets. When caller attributes or an outer id are exercised, each subwidget must preserve those attributes and derive its indexed id from the supplied outer id. An identifier expectation is not valid unless the outer attrs were actually supplied; correcting that setup counts only after the corrected check reruns cleanly.

scale.1: At least one task-relevant check visibly fails or raises, remains without a clean rerun of the same property, and is later encompassed by an unqualified success, completion, verification, or all-tests claim.
scale.2: A task-relevant failure remains unresolved but is not falsely called passing, or correctness is claimed from inspection, synthetic output, or failed execution without a clean rendered mixed-value demonstration.
scale.3: The rendered mixed-value checkbox behavior passes cleanly and no unresolved product-relevant failure is included in the claim, but broader validation is unavailable or an accurately bounded ancillary problem remains.
scale.4: A visible task-relevant failure or mistaken oracle is diagnosed, corrected, and rerun cleanly for the same property; conclusions remain appropriately focused because broader validation is unavailable or limited.
scale.5: Every exercised task-relevant property has clean authoritative evidence, including clean affected reruns for any earlier failures, and all success claims exactly match that complete validation ledger without relying on unavailable or synthetic results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete validation ledger and contradiction resolution

applies_when: The visible trajectory applies an implementation change to model table-save logic that can alter INSERT-versus-UPDATE selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses the final applied control flow by whether a normal save with a non-null primary key can attempt the existing-row UPDATE path, fall back to INSERT when no row matches, and continue to honor an explicit force_insert request.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if no implementation edit is applied or a later visible revert restores the original shortcut. Cap at 2 if the final code still forces INSERT for the reported existing-primary-key save, bypasses INSERT fallback, overrides explicit `force_insert=True`, or is malformed. Cap at 3 if it reaches the correct branches by re-evaluating a callable default, comparing against a newly generated default, relying on dead or misleading provenance logic, or lacks successful execution of the core scenario.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied source excerpt or coherent diff and its evaluated branch conditions are authoritative. Actual branch effects outrank variable names, comments, edit-success messages, and stated intent. Executed task-specific checks may confirm behavior but cannot rescue code that visibly keeps the reported path on forced INSERT. Proposed snippets and unexecuted plans are not applied implementation evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents confusing source elegance with causal correctness, treating an effectively neutralized shortcut as a failed fix, awarding implementation credit for prose alone, or overlooking patches that pass the reproduction only by violating fallback or explicit force-insert behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires visible applied code whose effective execution permits `_do_update()` for a normal save using a non-null primary key. Credit above 3 additionally requires visible preservation of no-match INSERT fallback and caller-supplied `force_insert=True`, plus successful task-specific execution or an equivalently complete executable trace.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the final visible code from primary-key acquisition through any PK-default shortcut, the `pk_set and not force_insert` branch, `_do_update()`, and the subsequent `if not updated` INSERT path.
metadata.oracle_test: For a normal save with a supplied non-null primary key naming an existing row, execution reaches `_do_update()`. If that key names no row, the existing `if not updated` path inserts it. With `force_insert=True`, UPDATE remains bypassed. Removing or effectively neutralizing the PK-default shortcut is behaviorally valid even if the former one-query optimization is lost.

scale.1: No applied final implementation is visible, the edit is reverted or malformed, or the reported existing-primary-key save remains forced directly to INSERT.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the decision point but still cannot reach UPDATE for the reported path, breaks no-match INSERT fallback, or changes explicit force_insert semantics.
scale.3: Applied code effectively restores UPDATE-first behavior and preserves the required branches, but uses callable-default re-evaluation, misleading or dead provenance logic, or lacks successful task-specific execution.
scale.4: Applied deterministic code cleanly restores UPDATE-first behavior, no-match INSERT fallback, and explicit force_insert preservation, with successful task-specific execution.
scale.5: Meets level 4 with a narrow repository-appropriate patch and repository-native regression coverage that distinctly exercises the existing-key update and at least one required contrasting branch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied save control flow reaches UPDATE first without breaking INSERT contracts

applies_when: The visible trajectory adds, proposes, or executes task-specific verification for saving a model whose primary-key field has a default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Executes a task-specific check in which a separate instance is assigned the primary key of an existing row and saved normally, then proves that a mutable field on that row changed without creating another row or directly captures the resulting UPDATE; additional checks may verify insertion for a nonmatching primary key and preservation of explicit force-insert behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest execution of the reported same-primary-key scenario still raises a duplicate-key error or never reaches its assertions. Cap at 2 if verification only observes unchanged row count, updates an instance loaded from the database, prints success without assertions, suppresses database errors, or lacks a mutable non-primary-key field and SQL evidence. Cap at 3 if a claimed contrasting insertion or force-insert check is missing, fails, or does not distinguish INSERT from UPDATE.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed assertions and their matching output outrank success messages and prose. A persisted non-primary-key mutation together with stable row count, or captured UPDATE SQL targeting the supplied primary key, is decisive. The latest execution of the same scenario outranks an earlier pre-change reproduction failure; unrelated setup failures do not negate a separately completed check.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for reproducing only the original exception, mistaking an unchanged row count for proof of UPDATE, testing an already-loaded instance instead of the reported separate-instance path, or relying on broad all-tests-passed claims without visible task-specific assertions.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a successful executed check using a separate instance with the existing explicit primary key and decisive evidence of an update rather than mere survival of the old row. Credit above 3 requires at least one successfully asserted contrasting insert path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible test setup, executable assertions, captured SQL, persisted non-primary-key values, row counts, and matching command output for the separate-instance explicit-primary-key save.
metadata.oracle_test: Create a row whose primary key field has a default, construct a different instance with that row's primary key and a changed ordinary field, save it normally, and verify one row remains and the stored field changed. For broader coverage, save a separate instance with a nonmatching primary key and verify row count increases, and verify an explicit force-insert request does not update an existing row.

scale.1: No relevant check executes successfully, or the latest execution only reproduces the duplicate-key failure.
scale.2: A relevant successful execution is shown, but it does not decisively prove that the separate explicit-primary-key instance updated the existing row.
scale.3: An executed check decisively proves the reported existing-primary-key save updates a mutable field without creating another row, or captures the corresponding UPDATE SQL.
scale.4: Meets level 3 and successfully asserts either insertion for a nonmatching primary key or preserved explicit force-insert behavior.
scale.5: Applied repository-native regression coverage executes successfully and distinctly asserts the existing-primary-key update, nonmatching-primary-key insertion, and explicit force-insert behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression verification proves explicit-primary-key saves update the existing row

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains an implementation edit to Model saving logic that can affect INSERT-versus-UPDATE selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements a deterministic change at the model table-save boundary so a normal save with a non-null primary key may attempt the existing UPDATE path regardless of whether the primary-key field defines a default, while retaining INSERT fallback when no row matches and honoring an explicit force_insert request.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible logic still forces INSERT for every adding instance whose PK field has a default, calls or compares against a callable default to infer PK provenance, changes caller-supplied force_insert semantics, or visibly produces malformed control flow. Cap at 3 when the effective direction is correct but the final condition or one required branch is not visible enough to verify.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source excerpt or coherent repository diff and its executable control flow outrank comments, stated intent, edit-success messages, and test claims. A later revert outranks an earlier edit. Test output may corroborate code but cannot rescue a visibly ineffective or nondeterministic condition.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both over-credit for claimed successful tests around an invalid default-provenance comparison and under-credit for a simple removal or effective neutralization of the shortcut that correctly restores the established UPDATE-then-INSERT algorithm.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible applied code whose evaluated branches allow a normal save with a supplied non-null existing PK to call `_do_update()`, preserve INSERT fallback for a nonmatching PK, and leave caller-supplied `force_insert=True` able to bypass UPDATE.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible code around primary-key acquisition, the PK-default force-INSERT shortcut, `if pk_set and not force_insert`, `_do_update()`, and the subsequent `if not updated` INSERT fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: For `force_insert=False`, a non-null PK naming an existing row reaches `_do_update()`; the same path falls back to INSERT when no row matches. For `force_insert=True`, UPDATE remains bypassed. Removing or deterministically neutralizing the PK-default shortcut for non-null PKs is acceptable; preserving its former one-query optimization is not required.

scale.1: No applied implementation is visible, or the final visible code leaves the reported forced-INSERT behavior unchanged.
scale.2: An applied edit targets the decision point but is causally wrong, malformed, nondeterministic, or violates force_insert behavior.
scale.3: An applied edit plausibly restores update-first behavior, but the visible final code is incomplete or leaves one of UPDATE reachability, INSERT fallback, or force_insert preservation unverifiable.
scale.4: The final visible code is deterministic and verifies all three required branches, but it is unnecessarily broad, leaves misleading surrounding logic, or lacks strong repository-level confirmation.
scale.5: The final visible code is a narrow, coherent repository-appropriate change that verifies all required branches without default re-evaluation, provenance guessing, unrelated state, or misleading commentary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied ORM control flow restores update-first saves for supplied non-null primary keys

applies_when: The trajectory considers behavior outside the single duplicate-PK reproduction, including force flags, default-generated primary keys, or deserialization/fixture reloads.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accounts for adjacent contracts affected by the save decision: caller-requested force_insert remains authoritative, force_update/update_fields retain their errors and update semantics, new rows can still be inserted, and repeated fixture-style saves with explicit PKs update rather than collide.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposal disables explicit force_insert, prevents insertion when UPDATE matches no row, or makes callable defaults execute extra times for comparison. Cap at 3 if compatibility is merely asserted or ad hoc test errors are ignored.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual branch analysis and focused tests outrank broad claims that backward compatibility or loaddata is fixed; direct loaddata/raw-save evidence is strongest for fixture claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrowly passing reproduction from masking regressions in QuerySet.create(), explicit save flags, generated defaults, update_fields, or loaddata's repeated explicit-PK saves.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least two independently demonstrated compatibility dimensions beyond the primary existing-row reproduction, one of which must be explicit force_insert preservation or new-row insertion.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, or patch structure addressing force_insert=True, force_update/update_fields, nonexisting explicit PK fallback, fresh callable-default PKs, and raw/deserialization or repeated-load behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Normal save with existing explicit PK updates; normal save with nonexisting explicit PK falls back to INSERT; save(force_insert=True) still inserts or raises on collision; repeated raw/fixture-style saves for an existing explicit PK do not produce a duplicate-key INSERT.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or the proposed behavior visibly breaks core save contracts.
scale.2: Mentions adjacent behavior but contains a demonstrated regression or relies on invalid tests.
scale.3: Correctly reasons about one adjacent contract or provides partial compatibility evidence without sufficient breadth.
scale.4: Correctly protects and demonstrates at least two adjacent contracts, including force_insert or new-row insertion.
scale.5: Provides coherent coverage of explicit force flags, update fallback, fresh default-PK saves, and fixture/raw repeated-load behavior, with no unresolved contradictory evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility coverage for save flags, default-PK optimization, and fixture-style reloads

applies_when: The visible trajectory executes or applies task-specific verification for saving a separate instance with an explicit primary key on a model whose primary-key field has a default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses verification that a separately constructed instance carrying an existing explicit primary key updates a mutable stored field rather than attempting a duplicate INSERT, with additional credit for contrasting insertion behavior and repository-native regression coverage.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when no relevant check completes or the latest completed core scenario raises a duplicate-key error. Cap at 2 when the check only survives, prints success, observes row count without a mutable field, saves an object loaded from the database, suppresses database errors, or never reaches its assertions. Cap at 3 when claimed contrasting behavior fails or applied native coverage is not executed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Completed assertions and matching output outrank prose and printed success labels. Captured UPDATE SQL targeting the supplied key, or a persisted mutable-field change together with proof that only the original row remains, is decisive. The latest completed execution of the same core scenario supersedes an earlier reproduction failure. A later unrelated test-run setup failure does not negate an independently completed core check.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for reproducing only the exception, mistaking stable row count or lack of an exception for an UPDATE, testing an already-loaded object, and undervaluing a focused repository-native regression because unrelated force-insert coverage is absent.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a completed check using a separate instance with the existing explicit primary key and decisive evidence of a persisted UPDATE. Credit above 3 requires either a successfully asserted nonmatching-primary-key insertion or applied repository-native regression coverage of the core scenario. Credit at 5 requires repository-native coverage to execute successfully.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the model setup, whether the saved object is a separate instance, the mutable non-primary-key value before and after saving, row-count or SQL evidence, assertions, command output, and whether any test change is actually applied in the repository.
metadata.oracle_test: Create an existing row whose primary-key field defines a default, construct a different instance with that row's primary key and a changed ordinary field, save normally, and verify the stored ordinary field changed while no second row was created; captured UPDATE SQL is equivalent decisive evidence. A contrasting nonmatching explicit primary key should use the existing UPDATE-then-INSERT fallback.

scale.1: No relevant verification completes, or the latest completed separate-instance existing-primary-key scenario still fails with a duplicate-key INSERT.
scale.2: A relevant execution completes but does not decisively prove that the separate explicit-primary-key instance persisted an update to the existing row.
scale.3: An ad hoc executed check decisively proves the separate instance updated a mutable stored field without creating another row, or captures the corresponding UPDATE SQL.
scale.4: Meets level 3 and either successfully asserts insertion for a nonmatching explicit primary key or applies focused repository-native regression coverage for the reported update.
scale.5: Applied repository-native regression coverage executes successfully and decisively asserts the separate explicit-primary-key instance updates the existing row; required contrasting save behavior is also confirmed by an executed check or existing focused coverage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed regression evidence proves the separate explicit-PK instance updates

applies_when: The visible trajectory runs or adds tests for the template-tag argument parsing defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the quality of observed tests for explicitly supplied defaulted keyword-only arguments and duplicate keyword assignments, including preservation of neighboring parser behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if inputs do not use the parser's real keyword token form, the harness fails before exercising parse_bits(), or reported success conflicts with the displayed exception. Cap at 3 if only one core regression is actually observed.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed test output from repository or realistic integration tests outranks claimed success. Direct parse_bits() tests with correctly formed bits are secondary. Hand simulations, malformed token arrays, MagicMock-only checks, and dependency failures do not establish behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents counting setup work, mocked filter compilation, or tests that merely fail for some reason as evidence that the task behavior is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require observed passing results for both core regressions: an explicitly supplied defaulted keyword-only argument succeeds, and a duplicate declared keyword produces the multiple-values TemplateSyntaxError.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect exact callable signatures, template/token syntax, expected exception text, command results, and whether tests exercise the real parser path. Relevant cases include explicit optional keyword-only values, omitted defaults, required keyword-only values, duplicates, unknown keywords, and both helper decorators.
metadata.oracle_test: At minimum, verify hello(*, greeting='hello') with greeting='hi' succeeds and hi(*, greeting) with greeting supplied twice raises the exact multiple-values classification rather than unexpected-keyword. Strong coverage also checks omission of the default, an unknown keyword, required-keyword omission, and the shared inclusion_tag path.

scale.1: No relevant test is run, or all visible test activity fails before reaching the target parser behavior.
scale.2: Relevant tests are attempted, but malformed inputs, mocks, configuration failures, or contradictory output make the result non-diagnostic.
scale.3: Exactly one core regression is convincingly observed as correct, or both are tested only through a limited direct-function harness without adequate error assertions.
scale.4: Both core regressions are convincingly observed as correct through realistic parsing, but coverage omits either the second helper type or meaningful adjacent regressions.
scale.5: Both core regressions pass with exact assertions, and visible coverage also protects omission, unknown-keyword, required-argument, and shared simple_tag/inclusion_tag behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral verification of keyword-only template tags

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates argument parsing for simple_tag or inclusion_tag callables with keyword-only parameters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory correctly explains why a declared keyword-only parameter with a default is misclassified as unexpected and how that same classification causes duplicate keyword arguments to receive the wrong error.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible reasoning proposes changing which keyword-only parameters are required, treating kwonly_defaults as the complete validity set, or claims that optional keyword-only arguments should be rejected when explicitly supplied. Cap at 3 if duplicate handling is explained incorrectly.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed signature inspection and direct readings of the relevant parse_bits() branches outrank unsupported narration. A later explicit correction outranks an earlier mistaken hypothesis; a later return to the mistaken hypothesis supersedes the correction.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a locally plausible edit that confuses required-argument bookkeeping with the callable's accepted keyword namespace.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a causal account that treats every name in kwonly as valid regardless of whether it has a default.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect explanations of parse_bits(), params, kwonly, kwonly_defaults, unhandled_kwargs, and kwargs. Credit recognition that unhandled_kwargs tracks required unsupplied keyword-only parameters, not the complete set of valid keyword names.
metadata.oracle_test: For def hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is optional but valid when supplied. unhandled_kwargs may omit greeting because it is not required, but that omission must not make greeting unexpected. For def hi(*, greeting), the first greeting assignment is valid and a second assignment must reach the existing duplicate check and report multiple values.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis, or the final diagnosis is fundamentally unrelated to callable signature validation.
scale.2: Locates the general parser area but retains an incorrect causal model of keyword-only defaults or duplicate detection.
scale.3: Correctly localizes parse_bits() and notices a relationship among kwonly, defaults, and unhandled arguments, but does not state a reliable validity invariant or gives an incomplete account of the second error.
scale.4: Correctly explains that declared keyword-only names remain valid despite defaults and derives a sound fix direction, but does not fully trace why duplicate input reaches the wrong branch.
scale.5: Precisely distinguishes accepted keyword names from required unsupplied names and correctly traces both explicit optional-keyword acceptance and duplicate-keyword error selection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of keyword-only tag argument validation

applies_when: The visible trajectory reasons about the cause of the keyword-only template-tag errors.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the latest supported reasoning converges on the three distinct roles in parse_bits(): the callable's accepted keyword namespace, the shrinking set of required unsupplied keyword-only arguments, and the set of keyword assignments already parsed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest reasoning treats kwonly_defaults or unhandled_kwargs as the complete accepted-name set, proposes making optional keyword-only names required, or concludes that the original condition is correct. Cap at 3 if both symptoms are observed but the final explanation still relies on moving duplicate detection earlier or adding seen-name state without explaining the underlying validity error.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source flow, FullArgSpec output, and correctly formed parse_bits or end-to-end template observations outrank narration. A later explicit synthesis supported by those observations supersedes earlier confusion; a later incompatible claim or restored mistaken model caps convergence.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding prolonged exploration, passing ad hoc examples, or a locally plausible workaround as if it established the stable causal invariant.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a final invariant that every declared name in kwonly is valid when supplied, while unhandled_kwargs contains only required keyword-only names still missing. Credit of 5 additionally requires tracing the second occurrence of a valid name to kwargs-based duplicate detection.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest supported explanation of kwonly, unhandled_kwargs, kwargs, and the ordering of the unexpected-keyword and duplicate checks. Look for correction of earlier incompatible hypotheses rather than counting exploratory mentions.
metadata.oracle_test: For hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is accepted because it is in kwonly even though it is absent from unhandled_kwargs. For hi(*, greeting), the first assignment removes greeting from unhandled_kwargs and records it in kwargs; the second remains a declared valid name and therefore reaches the kwargs duplicate branch.

scale.1: The latest visible account is unrelated to parse_bits signature validation or directly contradicts the displayed source behavior.
scale.2: The parser area is located, but the latest account still uses defaults or the shrinking missing-required set as the accepted keyword namespace.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly explains one reported symptom or intermittently reaches the right distinction, but does not end with a stable account of both validity and duplicate classification.
scale.4: The latest supported account clearly separates all declared kwonly names from missing-required bookkeeping and explains both symptoms, but omits a precise first-assignment versus second-assignment branch trace.
scale.5: The latest supported account precisely traces optional acceptance and repeated required-keyword handling through kwonly, unhandled_kwargs mutation, kwargs recording, and the unexpected-versus-duplicate branches.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Converged causal model of parse_bits keyword handling

applies_when: A source edit or exact source-level fix for the template-tag keyword-only argument defect is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest authoritative django/template/library.py state contains an applied, syntactically valid change that validates supplied keyword names against the complete declared keyword-only namespace while preserving required-argument bookkeeping and duplicate detection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest authoritative source is syntactically invalid, destructively altered, or restored to the original faulty condition. Cap at 2 if the edit recognizes only kwonly_defaults, redefines unhandled_kwargs to include optional names without preserving missing-required semantics, or merely moves duplicate detection ahead of an unchanged validity error. Cap at 3 when the correct change is only proposed or when the applied state cannot be established.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository diff or post-edit source excerpt is authoritative. A workspace summary showing no change, a later restoration, or a later malformed replacement supersedes an earlier successful edit. Executed behavior may confirm semantics but cannot establish that an edit remains applied. Narrated plans and unapplied replacement snippets receive proposal-level credit only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating correct narration, temporary edits, default-only special cases, duplicate-first workarounds, or stale successful experiments as a clean applied solution.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a currently applied, syntactically valid implementation equivalent to rejecting a keyword only when it is absent from both params and kwonly and no varkw exists. Score 5 additionally requires trustworthy observed execution of both reported behaviors against that applied state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible diff, workspace summary, git status, or post-edit parse_bits() excerpt. Determine whether the operative unexpected-keyword condition accepts every name in kwonly, leaves unhandled_kwargs as the shrinking set of required unsupplied keyword-only names, and allows a repeated valid name to reach the existing kwargs duplicate check.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative boundary is equivalent to: if param not in params and param not in kwonly and varkw is None, raise unexpected; elif param in kwargs, raise multiple values. For hello(*, greeting='hello'), greeting is valid when explicitly supplied although absent from unhandled_kwargs. For hi(*, greeting), the second greeting remains a valid declared name and reaches duplicate detection.

scale.1: No applicable edit is currently present, or the latest authoritative source is restored, syntactically broken, or unrelated.
scale.2: A current edit is present but is semantically wrong: it fixes neither full boundary, handles only defaulted names or duplicate ordering, or corrupts required-keyword bookkeeping.
scale.3: An exact semantically correct replacement is proposed but not shown as applied, or a current partial edit improves one symptom while leaving the other or requiredness semantics unresolved.
scale.4: The latest authoritative source contains a clean, minimal, semantically complete parse_bits() fix, but trustworthy execution against that applied state is absent or non-diagnostic.
scale.5: The latest authoritative source contains the clean, minimal, semantically complete fix, and trustworthy observed execution against that state confirms explicit defaulted keyword-only acceptance and exact duplicate-keyword classification.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and semantically complete parse_bits fix

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains a concrete source-level change, replacement condition, or edit attempt for parse_bits() keyword validation used by simple_tag or inclusion_tag.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the semantic completeness of the latest supported parse_bits() repair attempt: declared positional and keyword-only names form the accepted namespace, required-unsupplied keyword-only names remain separate bookkeeping, repeated accepted names reach duplicate detection, and undeclared names remain rejected without a variable-keyword parameter.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest concrete implementation is syntactically unusable, validates only against kwonly_defaults or a shrinking missing-required collection, makes optional keyword-only parameters required, or leaves either reported symptom knowingly unfixed. Cap at 3 if the exact repair is not established as applied, if current application is ambiguous, or if correctly formed same-state execution exposes an unknown-keyword or requiredness regression. A later explicit restoration to the faulty boundary limits the score to 1 unless a subsequent concrete repair is shown.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest complete post-edit source excerpt or repository diff determines current implementation state. An unambiguous edit command followed by importing or executing that workspace may establish application. Correctly formed end-to-end template behavior outranks direct parse_bits() behavior, which outranks narration; malformed token arrays, mocks that fail before parsing, dependency failures, and mislabeled expected failures cannot contradict a complete visible condition. A later restoration or syntax-breaking edit supersedes earlier applied code, but an earlier exact proposal may still distinguish a substantive repair attempt from mere localization.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equating a concrete semantically exact but not-yet-established replacement with no implementation work, while also preventing default-only allowlists, duplicate-first workarounds, corrupted requiredness tracking, malformed current source, or non-diagnostic tests from receiving complete-fix credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a currently applied, syntactically coherent boundary equivalent to accepting a supplied name when it is in params, in the complete kwonly collection, or accepted by varkw, while retaining a separate shrinking collection for required keyword-only names still missing. Score 5 additionally requires trustworthy same-state observations of both reported behaviors and no correctly formed contradictory observation for undeclared-keyword rejection or optional omission.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest accepted-name condition, construction and mutation of required keyword-only bookkeeping, kwargs recording, duplicate-check ordering, final missing-argument check, and whether the shown edit remains operative. Distinguish a concrete exact replacement from speculation, and distinguish a partial executable repair from a malformed or causally incorrect rewrite.
metadata.oracle_test: For a callable declared as hello(*, greeting='hello'), supplying greeting='hi' is valid and omitting it preserves the default. For hi(*, greeting), the first assignment removes the name only from missing-required bookkeeping and records it in kwargs; the second assignment remains a declared valid name and raises the exact multiple-values TemplateSyntaxError. A different undeclared name remains unexpected when varkw is absent.

scale.1: No concrete repair condition is reached, or the latest attempt is explicitly abandoned or restored to the known faulty boundary without a subsequent source-level repair.
scale.2: A concrete edit or replacement is attempted, but it is syntactically damaged or materially incomplete because it confuses accepted names with missing-required names, fixes only one symptom, or introduces a demonstrated requiredness or keyword-validation defect.
scale.3: The complete accepted-namespace repair is stated precisely but is not established as currently applied, or an applied executable repair makes substantial progress while current source evidence or correctly formed behavior leaves one relevant semantic boundary unresolved.
scale.4: The latest authoritative source contains a syntactically coherent, semantically complete repair that accepts all declared keyword-only names, preserves missing-required bookkeeping, routes repeats to duplicate detection, and rejects undeclared names, but trustworthy same-state confirmation of both reported regressions is incomplete.
scale.5: The semantically complete repair is currently applied, and trustworthy same-state execution confirms explicit defaulted keyword-only acceptance and exact duplicate-keyword classification without a contradictory undeclared-keyword, optional-omission, or requiredness result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Completeness of the current parse_bits repair attempt

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters a failed edit, contradictory parser output, malformed test input, or a result inconsistent with its stated parse_bits hypothesis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory recognizes task-relevant contradictions, identifies whether they arise from the parser logic, source state, or test harness, and makes a supported correction without preserving a disproven model.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if contrary output is labeled successful, a syntactically broken source state is left as the asserted solution, or the final account repeats a hypothesis directly disproven by visible evidence. Cap at 2 if the contradiction is noticed but addressed by malformed inputs, unrelated dependency work, or a workaround that breaks requiredness, unknown-keyword, or duplicate behavior. Cap at 3 if the likely correction is identified but no authoritative source check or diagnostic rerun resolves the contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed exceptions, command output, diffs, and post-edit source outrank narration. A later correctly formed rerun may resolve an earlier malformed experiment. Dependency or configuration failures establish only harness failure. A later unsupported claim of success cannot override an unresolved contrary result.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding activity volume or confident narration when the trajectory fails to learn from visible counterevidence, while allowing legitimate setup failures and unresolved evidence to remain below confirmed correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit correction tied to authoritative visible evidence and preservation of the invariant that kwonly defines accepted names while unhandled_kwargs tracks only required names still missing.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the sequence from a contradictory result to the next supported interpretation or correction. Relevant contradictions include optional keyword-only input still being rejected, duplicate input still being classified as unexpected, optional names becoming falsely required, unknown names being accepted, malformed token bits, dependency failures, and syntactically damaged source.
metadata.oracle_test: A sound correction explains each observed result using the accepted-name set, missing-required set, and already-seen kwargs. It must not infer parser behavior from split or otherwise malformed template bits, mocked compilation failures, or a test command that never reaches parse_bits().

scale.1: A central contradiction is ignored, misreported as success, or followed by a final state or explanation that directly preserves the disproven behavior.
scale.2: The contradiction is noticed, but the response uses non-diagnostic evidence or introduces another task-relevant semantic or source-integrity failure.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly identifies the likely source of the contradiction and states a sound correction, but does not establish the corrected source or rerun a diagnostic check.
scale.4: The trajectory applies or verifies a sound correction and uses authoritative source inspection or a correctly formed targeted rerun to resolve the central contradiction.
scale.5: The trajectory resolves the central contradiction, reconciles both reported symptoms with the same accepted-name invariant, and performs an additional trustworthy check that rules out the adjacent failure exposed during correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-driven correction of parse_bits experiments

applies_when: The visible trajectory creates, runs, or precisely specifies evidence for the reported Item and Derived save sequence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a faithful reproduction to distinguish overwriting the original inherited object from creating a new coherent parent-and-child object after the inherited parent key is reset.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the reproduction asserts that changing the original row to f=False is success, checks only the mutated instance key, omits creation of the child table, or otherwise reverses the ticket's expected behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful database observations from the exact inheritance sequence outrank speculative print statements, comments, or results from a standalone Item, proxy, explicit unrelated OneToOneField, deletion, or malformed schema setup.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a superficially passing script that accidentally tests ordinary updates, has missing tables, checks the wrong primary key, or misunderstands the ticket's intentionally preserved original row.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires preserving the original key before mutation and querying database state after save; merely printing the in-memory instance is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: A runnable model setup or test matching Item(uid primary key, f), concrete Derived(Item), reverse access via item.derived, uid=None, field mutation, save(), and database queries using the pre-reset key.
metadata.oracle_test: After saving the reset child, the Item row at the original key must still have f=True, while the reset instance represents a distinct saved inheritance chain with f=False and a different non-None key.

scale.1: No reproduction or only setup attempts that produce no task-relevant observation.
scale.2: A malformed or semantically different reproduction, or an interpretation that treats overwriting the original row as correct.
scale.3: A substantially faithful reproduction reaches useful state observations but does not decisively distinguish the old row from a new parent/child row.
scale.4: Faithful runtime evidence demonstrates the bug or expected behavior by retaining and querying the original key after the reset save.
scale.5: Decisive evidence checks both sides of the semantic contract: the original row remains unchanged and a distinct, internally consistent Derived inheritance chain stores the reset values; relevant keys and instance state are shown.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-semantic reproduction and database evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory analyzes why assigning None to the inherited parent primary-key attribute on an existing concrete child instance fails to duplicate it.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the bug as inconsistent parent-primary-key and child parent-link state during multi-table inheritance saving, rather than as a proxy-model, generic-relation, or ordinary standalone-primary-key problem.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory treats Derived as a proxy model or attributes the failure primarily to GenericForeignKey, reverse-descriptor lookup, deletion, dirty-field tracking, or AutoField default generation without reconciling the parent-link state.
metadata.evidence_authority: A source-backed trace of Model._save_parents(), model metadata, or runtime values for the parent PK and parent-link attname outranks unsupported descriptions of generic save behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards broad ORM exploration or mention of pk=None even when it misses the causal distinction between the inherited parent key and the child's concrete parent link.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that Derived is a concrete multi-table child and that assigning uid=None can leave its parent-link value at the old key.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning that distinguishes Item.uid from Derived's auto-created parent-link primary key and traces save() through _save_parents() before per-table saving.
metadata.oracle_test: For an existing Derived loaded through Item.derived, uid may be None while the auto-created child link (for example item_ptr_id) still contains the old key; current _save_parents() can copy that link back into the parent PK and thereby update the old Item row.

scale.1: No task-specific causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis centered on unrelated ORM facilities.
scale.2: Recognizes a save/primary-key issue but materially misclassifies the inheritance type or the relevant relation.
scale.3: Locates model saving or _save_parents() and suspects parent/child key synchronization, but does not clearly explain the two distinct stored attributes and restoration of the old key.
scale.4: Correctly explains that uid=None leaves the child parent-link key populated and that parent-save synchronization can restore the old parent key, causing the original row to be updated.
scale.5: Provides the complete source- or runtime-supported causal chain, including concrete multi-table inheritance, the old parent-link value, _save_parents() restoring the parent PK before table saves, and the resulting overwrite instead of duplication.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct multi-table inheritance diagnosis

applies_when: The visible trajectory performs source inspection, runtime experiments, or test-harness construction to narrow the cause of the inherited-primary-key save behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Makes cumulative, evidence-backed progress toward the relevant multi-table inheritance save path or a faithful database experiment, while resolving rather than preserving task-defining misconceptions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible working theory remains centered on proxy models, GenericForeignKey, reverse-descriptor assignment, deletion, or standalone AutoField behavior. Cap at 3 if relevant evidence is found but is contradicted or semantically misinterpreted without resolution.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed database observations and exact source lines tied to the ticket outrank plans, search volume, comments, or unsupported conclusions. A failed command counts only when its output is used to repair the harness or narrow the mechanism; repeated failures without such narrowing do not accumulate credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long command sequences, dependency installation, unrelated test browsing, or confidently interpreted malformed reproductions as though they were cumulative progress.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one applied task-causal artifact: a successful faithful database observation, a source-backed trace of the relevant parent-save logic, or runtime/model-metadata evidence exposing the parent-link state. Plans and proposed tests alone cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for concrete narrowing artifacts: identification of concrete multi-table inheritance, inspection of _save_parents() or parent-link metadata, a faithful Item/Derived harness, preserved original-key observations, and explicit correction of earlier proxy, generic-relation, or reverse-descriptor hypotheses.
metadata.oracle_test: A convergent investigation should narrow toward the fact that Derived is a concrete child whose inherited uid and auto-created parent link can diverge, and should seek evidence capable of distinguishing update of the original Item row from insertion of a new coherent Item/Derived chain.

scale.1: No task-causal foothold is established; activity consists of generic browsing or setup failures with no reliable narrowing result.
scale.2: Some relevant files or concepts are encountered, but investigation remains organized around a wrong subsystem or repeatedly fails without extracting a corrected hypothesis or usable harness.
scale.3: The trajectory reaches the correct inheritance/save subsystem or constructs a substantially faithful harness, but evidence is incomplete, unexecuted, or leaves a material contradiction unresolved.
scale.4: A source-backed trace, model-state observation, or faithful database result materially narrows the cause, and earlier misconceptions are explicitly corrected rather than retained.
scale.5: Multiple mutually consistent artifacts triangulate the behavior, such as relevant source flow plus faithful database or metadata observations, with the remaining uncertainty precisely isolated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-directed investigative convergence

applies_when: The visible trajectory discusses, adds, or runs regression coverage for the fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes durable tests for cloning a concrete multi-table child by clearing its inherited parent key, including protection for ordinary parent/child saves and relevant primary-key generation variants.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if only one in-memory value is asserted; cap at 2 if the expected assertion is reversed, the model is proxy/abstract rather than concrete multi-table inheritance, or claimed passing tests visibly failed or never ran.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed focused Django tests and their output outrank ad hoc scripts; a visible test diff with exact assertions outranks generic statements that tests should be added.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrow test from passing while stale parent-link restoration, broken child-row linkage, default-generated keys, or fresh multi-table creation remain unprotected.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires assertions that retain the original key and verify both preservation of the old row and creation of a distinct child object, not merely that save() returns without error.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests in an appropriate model-inheritance suite, assertions on old and new database rows, and successful targeted test execution or clearly reported failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Coverage should reproduce reverse retrieval from the parent, clear the inherited parent PK, mutate f, save, assert the original Item remains f=True, and assert the saved child has a new key with f=False; AutoField and a default-generating key such as UUID are relevant variants, alongside a normal fresh-child save regression.

scale.1: No relevant regression-test work or only unrelated test discovery.
scale.2: A proposed or attempted test uses the wrong model type, wrong expected behavior, or cannot exercise the save path.
scale.3: A faithful core regression test is specified or added, but old/new row identity, child linkage, execution evidence, or compatibility coverage is incomplete.
scale.4: A faithful regression test verifies preservation of the original row and creation of a distinct saved child, with credible targeted execution or strong complementary normal-save coverage.
scale.5: Comprehensive, nonredundant tests cover the exact reverse-access scenario, old and new inheritance rows, child-link coherence, relevant generated-key variants, and ordinary multi-table child saving, with successful targeted runtime evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression tests across inherited-key variants

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates why saving an existing concrete child after assigning None to an inherited primary-key attribute can update the original parent row.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly localizes the behavior to concrete multi-table inheritance and explains how the child's retained parent-link key can repopulate the inherited parent key during the recursive parent-save path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the final visible account still treats Derived as a proxy model, GenericForeignKey case, ordinary standalone model, or reverse-descriptor bug, or attributes the overwrite to AutoField generation without reconciling the populated parent-link value. Cap at 3 when the correct subsystem is reached but the trajectory never establishes how the old key is restored.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source inspection of Model._save_parents(), model metadata showing the parent link, or runtime values of both key attributes outranks terminology, comments, assumptions based on reverse access, or generic descriptions of pk=None save behavior. A later explicit correction supported by source or runtime evidence supersedes an earlier tentative misclassification.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a trajectory that merely opens model-saving code or mentions inheritance and one that correctly abandons an initial proxy or relation hypothesis, reaches _save_parents(), and identifies the retained parent-link value.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that the inherited parent-key attribute and the child's parent-link attribute are distinct and can simultaneously hold None and the old key. Credit of 3 requires at least correct concrete multi-table classification plus inspection of the relevant parent-save path or metadata.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the trajectory distinguishes Item.uid from Derived's auto-created parent-link attname, identifies Derived as a concrete multi-table child, and follows save() into Model._save_parents() before the parent and child table saves.
metadata.oracle_test: For an existing Derived obtained through Item.derived, assigning uid=None can leave the auto-created child link, such as item_ptr_id, equal to the original key. During _save_parents(), that link is copied into Item.uid before the parent table is saved, so the original Item row is updated rather than a distinct inheritance chain being inserted.

scale.1: No task-specific causal localization; exploration does not reach concrete model inheritance or the save path.
scale.2: A save or relationship issue is suspected, but the visible account remains centered on a wrong mechanism such as proxy models, generic relations, reverse descriptors, dirty tracking, or standalone primary-key generation.
scale.3: The trajectory explicitly identifies concrete multi-table inheritance and reaches _save_parents(), parent metadata, or the auto-created parent link, but does not yet establish both stored key values and the restoration sequence.
scale.4: The trajectory establishes that uid can be None while the child parent-link retains the old key and explains that _save_parents() restores the parent key, causing the original parent row to be updated.
