reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the applied ordering-check change uses the preceding resolved field to accept a component registered as either a transform or a lookup, rejects components registered as neither, and remains consistent with any reached post-change model-check behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest applied predicate has incorrect boolean grouping, uses an unrelated field or global lookup list, accepts arbitrary unresolved suffixes, loses transform support, is malformed, or is followed by an executed representative model check that still rejects the valid lookup case or accepts a bogus suffix. A later restoration or replacement supersedes an earlier edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A complete latest source view or diff is strongest for determining the exact implementation. Reached post-change Model.check() or focused-test output outranks edit-success messages and can disprove an apparently correct edit. When source output is truncated, an unambiguous edit command may establish the intended applied predicate only if subsequent syntax or task-level execution confirms that the edited state was loaded; prose alone cannot do so.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents an edit command, replacement message, proposed snippet, API introspection, or truncated source fragment from receiving the same credit as a verified applied state, and prevents visibly failing post-change behavior from being ignored.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires either a complete visible valid predicate or an unambiguous applied edit corroborated by execution of the edited code. Score 5 additionally requires both exact source verification and successful task-level evidence showing that the implementation's acceptance boundary is not merely syntactically plausible.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest exception branch in Model._check_ordering(), the field on which get_transform() and get_lookup() are called, the grouping of the no-field and neither-API conditions, and any later model-check output that confirms or contradicts that state.
metadata.oracle_test: After a field path has resolved, the terminal component is rejected exactly when there is no preceding field or when both field-specific get_transform() and get_lookup() fail. A lookup-only component and a transform-only component are accepted, while a bogus component remains invalid.

scale.1: No relevant applied production change is visible or credibly established, the latest state restores the defect, or the source is unusably corrupted.
scale.2: A relevant change is applied, but its field authority or boolean boundary is wrong, or reached post-change behavior directly demonstrates that the intended valid or invalid case is still mishandled.
scale.3: The correct field-specific transform-or-lookup predicate is proposed or an edit is reported, but the final applied state is only partially visible and is not corroborated by execution of the edited code.
scale.4: The correct predicate is credibly applied and syntactically valid, either through complete source evidence or through an unambiguous edit corroborated by execution, with no reached behavioral contradiction.
scale.5: A clean localized final source view shows the exact correct predicate, and reached task-level evidence confirms the valid lookup boundary while preserving rejection of an invalid suffix or acceptance of an existing transform.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and behavior-consistent ordering predicate

applies_when: The visible trajectory attempts to validate Django model Meta.ordering paths containing lookup-separated components.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Executes validation that reaches Model.check() or the focused ordering-check tests and demonstrates acceptance of a registered terminal lookup without disabling rejection of invalid ordering paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A dependency, settings, import, collection, syntax, or app-registration failure that prevents Model.check() from reaching the assertion caps credit at 2. A reached task-level check that still reports models.E015 for the valid lookup case caps credit at 3. Isolated lookup introspection cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed post-change Model.check() or focused repository-test output outranks assertions, source inspection, and get_lookup()/get_transform() introspection. A focused repository test is more durable than an ad hoc reproducer, but a correctly configured direct Model.check() with observed controls is authoritative behavioral evidence. Later failing task-level output supersedes earlier predicted success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both unexecuted test artifacts from receiving passing credit and successful direct system-check evidence from being discarded merely because it is not yet committed as a repository test.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires an executed post-change model system check that observes the valid non-Transform lookup case and an invalid-suffix or transform-preservation control. Anchor 5 additionally requires either a tracked regression test that passes or successful execution of relevant existing ordering/model-check tests.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands and complete outputs that exercise Model.check() or focused invalid_models ordering tests, especially a related path ending in isnull, a nonexistent suffix control, and preservation of registered transforms.
metadata.oracle_test: A representative Meta.ordering path ending in a field-registered lookup such as supply__product__parent__isnull produces no models.E015, while a terminal name registered as neither a transform nor a lookup still produces models.E015 and existing registered transforms remain accepted.

scale.1: No relevant validation is executed, or only unrelated commands are shown.
scale.2: Validation is indirect or cannot reach Model.check() because of setup, import, configuration, collection, or syntax failure.
scale.3: A direct task-level check runs but only reproduces the defect, reports a failing repaired case, or lacks observed post-change behavior and a meaningful control.
scale.4: An executed post-change Model.check() or equivalent focused check observes both acceptance of a registered non-Transform lookup and preservation of at least one invalid-suffix or valid-transform control.
scale.5: The evidence in anchor 4 is present and either a tracked regression test visibly passes or relevant existing ordering/model-check tests also visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed regression evidence for ordering lookup validation

applies_when: The rollout concerns eliminating the unnecessary self-referential subquery generated for MySQL or MariaDB queryset deletion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible work applies a repository change that routes MySQL and MariaDB multi-alias deletes through the backend-specific DELETE-alias-FROM form while preserving the ordinary single-alias delete path, with regression evidence when available.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the applied change modifies the shared backend-neutral delete compiler, relies on an empty-alias heuristic, or otherwise contradicts the inspected MySQL compiler structure. Cap at 3 if it removes the entire single-alias safeguard or introduces a different compound condition without demonstrating equivalent behavior. Unapplied proposals cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final or intermediate repository diff is authoritative over claims in thoughts or prose. Executed focused tests and captured generated SQL outrank static inspection scripts; source inspection outranks unsupported assertions about compiler behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding long but unapplied investigation, superficial text-based verification, broad removal of compiler safeguards, or a change to Django's shared SQLDeleteCompiler as though it were the narrow backend fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible task-causal source edit. Score 4 or 5 additionally requires preserving the single-alias base-compiler path while removing the backend-feature gate that sends eligible multi-alias deletes to the self-subquery implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source edits or diffs to the MySQL delete compiler, then inspect any focused SQL-generation or deletion tests. Distinguish an applied source change from a proposed change or explanatory script.
metadata.oracle_test: For this codebase, the task-causal correction is in the MySQL SQLDeleteCompiler: ordinary single-alias deletion continues through the parent implementation, while the backend feature flag no longer diverts multi-alias deletion to DELETE ... WHERE pk IN (SELECT pk FROM the same table). The MySQL-specific DELETE <target-alias> FROM ... path must remain available for the latter case.

scale.1: A visible source edit is applied, but it targets the wrong layer or contradicts the required compiler semantics, such as changing the shared delete compiler or adding an empty-alias shortcut.
scale.2: No task-causal source edit is visibly applied by the cutoff; work is limited to investigation, proposed changes, dependency setup, or temporary analysis artifacts.
scale.3: A relevant MySQL compiler edit is visibly applied, but it is overbroad, uses an unverified alternative condition, or otherwise lacks evidence that both single-alias and multi-alias delete behavior are preserved.
scale.4: The narrow MySQL compiler condition is visibly corrected so the single-alias parent path remains intact and the problematic feature-gated multi-alias subquery path is avoided; source-level verification is present, but no focused regression test is demonstrated.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and includes executed, focused regression evidence showing an unfiltered delete avoids the self-referential IN subquery while relevant joined or multi-alias delete behavior remains correct.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of the MySQL DELETE compilation fix

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an unfiltered QuerySet.delete() enters the primary-key subquery path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies from visible source evidence that an unfiltered delete can reach Django's multi-alias fallback even though no filtering requires a subquery, and connects that fallback to the reported SQL, lock incompatibility, and performance regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims that super().as_sql() always produces a subquery, that single_alias=True selects the subquery branch, or that DeleteQuery.delete_batch() is the cause of the shown QuerySet.all().delete() SQL without reconciling the actual compiler flow.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly displayed current source and a reproduced compiled query outrank speculation, historical guesses, or comments read without control-flow tracing.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated repository exploration, feature-flag speculation, or inverted branch reasoning as a diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require identifying the core SQLDeleteCompiler fallback as the producer of DELETE ... WHERE pk IN (SELECT pk FROM the same table), not merely locating the MySQL compiler.
metadata.judge_focus: Source-backed tracing through QuerySet deletion and django/db/models/sql/compiler.py, especially SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias, alias initialization or the empty WHERE condition, and the pk__in inner-query fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: For an unfiltered model delete, no predicate or join must be preserved, so the semantic SQL oracle is a direct DELETE FROM the model table; the self-selecting pk__in wrapper is unnecessary.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the displayed compiler control flow.
scale.2: Finds delete-related files or mentions aliases/subqueries but leaves the causal branch unresolved or materially confused.
scale.3: Correctly identifies SQLDeleteCompiler's multi-alias pk__in fallback as the source, but does not explain why the unfiltered query reaches it or why the fallback is unnecessary here.
scale.4: Explains from source that the unfiltered query's alias/WHERE state makes the existing single-alias gate miss the direct-delete path, and links this to the exact self-subquery regression.
scale.5: Provides a complete source-backed trace from unfiltered QuerySet.delete() to the erroneous fallback, correctly distinguishes single-alias and multi-alias behavior, and reconciles the lock and performance symptoms with the generated SQL.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of the unnecessary DELETE subquery

applies_when: Select this rubric only when the rollout investigates, proposes, or applies a repository change intended to alter MySQL or MariaDB DELETE SQL generation for the reported self-referential subquery regression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate both the task-causal proximity and correctness of the visible implementation, distinguishing absent work, harmful cross-cutting changes, incorrect but locally targeted MySQL compiler edits, the exact single-alias-only delegation repair, and focused execution evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied edit outside the MySQL delete compiler that changes shared delete semantics, falsifies a backend capability, or relies on an incidental empty-alias state cannot exceed 2. Removing the complete MySQL delegation guard, retaining feature-only delegation, or delegating non-single-alias queries also cannot exceed 2. Unsupported claims cannot raise an applied edit, and a later visible diff supersedes an earlier proposal.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository diffs and displayed post-edit repository source determine what was applied, even when a cutoff summary is stale. A successful edit command without post-edit source establishes only probable local application. Concrete replacement code establishes a proposal. Temporary scripts, comments, exported patch files without a repository diff, and prose assertions do not establish effective behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents unresolved exploration from tying with a completed task-local attempt, while preventing feature mutation, shared-core shortcuts, feature-only delegation, and unconditional backend routing from being mistaken for the narrow correct fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible applied source in django/db/backends/mysql/compiler.py whose effective delegation condition is single_alias alone and whose existing non-single-alias DELETE-target-FROM body remains present. Score 5 additionally requires successful focused repository execution that exercises both sides of the condition.
metadata.judge_focus: First determine whether any concrete task-causal change or exact proposal exists. Then inspect the edited layer, the effective boolean guard, whether super().as_sql() remains reachable for single-alias queries, and whether the backend-specific body remains reachable for every non-single-alias query. Treat feature-file, shared-compiler, feature-only, empty-alias, and guard-removal approaches as distinct visible failure classes rather than as absence of work.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended implementation leaves ordinary single-alias deletion on the parent compiler's direct DELETE path and sends every non-single-alias MySQL or MariaDB deletion through the existing DELETE <target> FROM construction, without consulting update_can_self_select for that routing decision.

scale.1: No concrete task-causal edit or exact replacement is established, or the work remains exploratory without settling an implementation boundary.
scale.2: A concrete task-causal change is applied or precisely specified, but it is incorrect: for example it changes shared delete semantics or backend capabilities, uses an empty-alias shortcut, retains feature-based non-single-alias delegation, removes single-alias delegation, or removes the entire guard.
scale.3: The exact single_alias-only MySQL guard is concretely proposed but not visibly applied, or a MySQL-local edit is visibly attempted but the final source is insufficient to verify the complete condition and retained backend body.
scale.4: A visible applied edit makes the MySQL delegation guard equivalent to single_alias alone, retains the parent path for that case, and visibly preserves the existing backend-specific body for non-single-alias deletion.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and includes successful focused repository execution demonstrating direct parent-compiled SQL for a single-alias delete and backend-specific DELETE-target-FROM SQL for a non-single-alias delete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-graded correctness of the MySQL DELETE compiler repair

applies_when: Select this rubric only when the rollout reasons about how the MySQL delete compiler and its parent compiler route a delete among direct DELETE, a primary-key subquery fallback, and MySQL-specific DELETE-target-FROM SQL.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate how completely and consistently the rollout traces the three visible compiler paths, giving separate credit for source-backed branch discovery while requiring a settled correct connection between feature-based delegation and the reported self-subquery for the highest anchors.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An account that finally states that the parent's single_alias branch creates the primary-key subquery, or that parent delegation always creates a subquery, cannot exceed 2. If that inversion is used to justify feature-only delegation, delegation only for non-single-alias queries, removal of single-alias delegation, or removal of the entire guard, it cannot exceed 2 even when the edit is applied. A later explicit correction grounded in displayed source supersedes earlier confusion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed current source from both compiler classes and successfully captured generated SQL outrank issue paraphrases, historical guesses, comments, and synthetic scripts that merely encode expected branches. A visible applied diff is evidence of the rollout's settled routing belief when its prose remains contradictory. Direct source-backed correction may supersede an earlier mistaken proposal.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents shallow file discovery from tying with a substantial source trace, but also prevents a source-rich yet inverted rationale from receiving credit as a coherent diagnosis merely because it produced a task-local patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires a settled source-backed account of all three paths: parent single-alias direct DELETE, parent non-single-alias pk__in fallback, and MySQL non-delegation DELETE-target-FROM. It must explicitly or unambiguously identify update_can_self_select as the independent delegation reason that can expose the parent fallback. Score 5 requires successful focused SQL compilation or execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Assess causal coverage before final consistency. Check whether the rollout displayed and understood the parent direct branch, the parent pk__in branch, the MySQL delegation condition, and the retained MySQL-specific body. Then determine whether its final explanation connects them in the correct direction or uses an inversion to support the opposite guard.
metadata.oracle_test: The parent compiler calls its direct delete builder when single_alias is true and constructs an outer primary-key-IN-inner-query delete otherwise. The MySQL override's update_can_self_select alternative can therefore delegate a non-single-alias query into that fallback; removing only that alternative preserves single-alias delegation and leaves non-single-alias queries on DELETE <target> FROM.

scale.1: The rollout provides no meaningful compiler-route diagnosis, or mentions delete-related files without establishing any source-backed direct-versus-subquery branch mapping.
scale.2: The rollout displays substantial relevant source or identifies multiple paths, but its final route is unresolved or materially inverted, including using the inversion to justify an incompatible guard change.
scale.3: The rollout correctly establishes the parent's single-alias direct branch and non-single-alias pk__in fallback and identifies the MySQL override, but does not clearly settle how feature-based delegation exposes the fallback or how non-delegation reaches DELETE-target-FROM.
scale.4: Displayed source supports a complete, settled, and internally consistent trace from feature-based delegation of a non-single-alias query to the parent's pk__in fallback, while distinguishing the parent's direct single-alias path and MySQL's non-delegated DELETE-target-FROM path.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and corroborates the trace with successful focused compilation or execution that captures the relevant direct, self-subquery, and backend-specific SQL forms.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-backed completeness and consistency of DELETE routing diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or validates ExpressionWrapper behavior for expressions other than a single direct Value constant.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Shows that delegating grouping behavior does not overcorrect: wrapped resolved column-dependent expressions still contribute their required grouping expressions, while nested constants and aggregate expressions retain their inner semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible generated SQL loses a required GROUP BY expression or the implementation special-cases all wrappers to return an empty list; cap at 3 if apparent compatibility failures come only from directly calling grouping APIs on unresolved F/Q objects and remain misinterpreted as production regressions.
metadata.evidence_authority: Resolved queryset SQL and passing repository tests outrank calls on unresolved F or Q objects; failed raw-expression probes are diagnostic only unless the production path uses that unresolved object.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards a fix that merely suppresses all wrapper grouping, or penalizes correct delegation based on invalid pre-resolution F/Q experiments.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successful nonconstant resolved-expression check in addition to the constant case.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed comparisons between wrapped and unwrapped resolved expressions, SQL for wrapped field/function expressions, aggregate cases, nested wrappers, or relevant existing Django tests.
metadata.oracle_test: ExpressionWrapper should expose the same grouping columns as its resolved inner expression: Value contributes none, resolved Col or a nonconstant Func contributes what it normally requires, and an Aggregate contributes its normal grouping dependencies.

scale.1: No compatibility reasoning or evidence, or visible evidence shows broad grouping breakage.
scale.2: Only constant suppression is considered, with an overbroad implementation or unresolved contradictory nonconstant behavior.
scale.3: The trajectory articulates preservation of inner-expression semantics or performs inconclusive/raw-expression probes, but lacks a successful resolved nonconstant check.
scale.4: Successful resolved SQL or grouping evidence shows at least one wrapped field-dependent expression remains correctly grouped while constants are omitted.
scale.5: Executed evidence covers complementary cases such as resolved columns/functions, nested wrappers, and aggregates or relevant existing tests, consistently showing wrapped and unwrapped grouping semantics match.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of nonconstant and nested grouping semantics

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests or runtime experiments for an aggregate values()/annotate() query using ExpressionWrapper around a constant.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates on the task-shaped queryset that the selected wrapped constant remains in SELECT but is absent from GROUP BY, while the real grouping column remains and the aggregate query is otherwise unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the displayed SQL still groups by the constant/wrapper or the test fails before producing relevant evidence; cap at 3 if the conclusion relies on a broken parser/regex or checks the whole SQL rather than the GROUP BY portion without an unambiguous manual reading.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful task-shaped query compilation or execution outranks isolated helper-method checks; literal SQL and bound parameters must be interpreted together, and actual output outranks printed expectations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats a helper-level empty list, a printed 'PASS', or an invalid SQL substring check as proof that the actual queryset is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful evidence from the full aggregate queryset, not only direct get_group_by_cols() calls.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed test output, compiled SQL with parameters, query.group_by contents, or database execution for annotate(ExpressionWrapper(Value(...))).values(...).annotate(Sum(...)).
metadata.oracle_test: Expected SQL semantics are SELECT column_a, constant AS expr_res, SUM(column_b) ... GROUP BY column_a, with no constant parameter, literal, expr_res reference, or aggregate select position in GROUP BY.

scale.1: No executed relevant validation, or only setup/import failures occur.
scale.2: An attempted task-shaped test fails or produces contradictory output without recovery.
scale.3: Successful helper-level evidence or partially reliable SQL evidence shows the intended omission, but the complete aggregate-query behavior is not decisively established.
scale.4: A successful full queryset compilation clearly shows only the genuine model grouping column in GROUP BY and the constant retained in SELECT.
scale.5: A focused regression test or equivalent executed evidence proves the full SQL shape and, where available, query execution/result correctness, with robust assertions that would fail on the original behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive regression evidence for generated GROUP BY SQL

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why ExpressionWrapper changes an inner ORM expression's contribution to GROUP BY.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly and stably traces the defect to ExpressionWrapper using generic non-aggregate grouping behavior instead of preserving the wrapped expression's get_group_by_cols() result, then identifies transparent delegation—not constant detection—as the causal repair invariant.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible reasoning still misattributes get_group_by_cols() to the wrong class, treats an excerpt of another class as ExpressionWrapper's implementation, continues toward detecting or filtering constants, or claims all wrapped expressions should contribute no grouping columns. Cap at 3 if delegation is stated but contradicted by an unresolved claim that nonconstant wrapped expressions may be suppressed. Editing failures alone do not reduce a stable causal diagnosis unless they introduce or preserve contradictory semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Correctly attributed source definitions and direct method-dispatch probes outrank SQL symptom reproduction or broad compiler exploration. A later source read or corrected conclusion supersedes earlier speculation, but later unresolved uncertainty about which class owns an inspected method controls over an earlier plausible statement.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes reproduction of the unwanted SQL for causal diagnosis, infers method ownership from an overbroad source excerpt, rewards an unsettled constant-special-casing direction, or requires a successful patch before crediting an otherwise exact dispatch-level diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a stable, correctly attributed causal trace showing that ExpressionWrapper lacks the needed override and therefore receives generic grouping behavior, or an equally decisive direct comparison showing the wrapper contributes itself while Value contributes no grouping columns. Credit above 3 additionally requires an explicit conclusion that ExpressionWrapper must return its inner expression's own get_group_by_cols() result without classifying constants. Credit 5 requires successful evidence using resolved expressions on both constant and grouping-required sides.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest settled account of which class supplies ExpressionWrapper's grouping behavior, the actual Value grouping override, direct wrapped-versus-unwrapped probes when present, and whether the proposed invariant delegates all grouping decisions to the resolved inner expression.
metadata.oracle_test: The diagnosis should predict that ExpressionWrapper(Value(3), output_field=...).get_group_by_cols() matches Value(3).get_group_by_cols() and is empty, while an ExpressionWrapper around a resolved column or other grouping-required expression returns exactly the inner expression's required grouping columns.

scale.1: No coherent causal account is established, or the latest account attributes the behavior to an unrelated mechanism.
scale.2: The SQL or wrapped-versus-unwrapped symptom is recognized, but source ownership remains unresolved, the explanation is incomplete, or the latest direction seeks to detect constants rather than explain wrapper dispatch.
scale.3: A stable source trace correctly identifies that ExpressionWrapper receives generic grouping behavior because it lacks the needed override, or decisive runtime evidence establishes the wrapper-versus-inner grouping contrast, but transparent delegation is not yet stated unambiguously.
scale.4: Correct source or runtime evidence establishes the dispatch defect, and the trajectory explicitly concludes that ExpressionWrapper must delegate get_group_by_cols() to the inner expression rather than classify constants; two-sided resolved-expression validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The explicit delegation invariant is supported by successful evidence that a wrapped constant contributes no grouping term and a wrapped resolved nonconstant expression retains exactly its required grouping columns.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Stable causal diagnosis of wrapper GROUP BY dispatch

applies_when: The trajectory performs source edits, restores files, reports diffs, or encounters evidence contradicting the intended patch state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Maintains or recovers a coherent repository state, using later file inspection or diffs to establish that accidental insertions, truncation, duplicate methods, temporary artifacts, and failed edit attempts do not remain in the submitted change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest visible production file is truncated or structurally corrupted; cap at 2 when an accidental edit is recognized but no successful restoration is visible; cap at 3 when restoration is visible but the intended final change is not subsequently confirmed.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest authoritative file content and final diff/status outrank earlier edit success messages; terminal unified diff outranks intermediate displays.
metadata.failure_mode: Assumes an edit command succeeded, ignores later evidence of corruption, or mistakes a restored clean tree for a completed fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible post-edit confirmation of a coherent ExpressionWrapper class; credit 5 requires a final focused diff or equivalent authoritative repository-state evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Chronology of edit commands, restoration commands, subsequent file reads, git diff/status output, and the terminal patch payload when present.
metadata.oracle_test: The final production change should leave the complete expressions.py intact, add the method only to ExpressionWrapper, and avoid checked-in scratch scripts, generated files, or unrelated modifications.

scale.1: Latest visible state is corrupt, truncated, or contains the method in an unrelated class with no recovery.
scale.2: The trajectory notices or attempts to repair a bad edit, but a coherent restored state is not visibly established.
scale.3: A clean restoration or plausible corrected edit is visible, but the intended final patch state is not authoritatively confirmed.
scale.4: Later file inspection establishes a coherent, correctly placed change and no visible unresolved corruption, though final repository diff/status evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: A final focused diff or terminal patch conclusively shows only the intended coherent change and no unrelated or temporary artifacts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Patch-state integrity and recovery from contradictory edits

applies_when: The visible trajectory includes an applied or explicitly displayed code change intended to fix wrapped-expression GROUP BY behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements the fix locally in ExpressionWrapper by overriding get_group_by_cols() and delegating grouping semantics to the wrapped expression, while preserving the optional alias argument and avoiding unrelated query/compiler changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest visible file is truncated, syntactically corrupted, or the method is inserted into another class; cap at 2 if a malformed edit is later reverted without a correct replacement; cap at 3 if delegation drops alias compatibility or broad unrelated production changes remain.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final git diff or later file read outranks edit commands and prose claims; a restored clean file outranks an earlier malformed edit, while an unresolved malformed latest file controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepts a plausible proposed fix as applied code, overlooks insertion into the wrong class, or rewards a broad compiler workaround that changes grouping behavior for unrelated expressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that the method exists inside ExpressionWrapper and returns the wrapped expression's get_group_by_cols() result; credit 5 additionally requires compatible alias forwarding and a clean narrow diff.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest visible contents or diff of django/db/models/expressions.py, especially the final ExpressionWrapper method body, signature, placement, and surrounding class integrity.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended boundary is an ExpressionWrapper.get_group_by_cols(self, alias=None) override equivalent to return self.expression.get_group_by_cols(alias=alias), rather than special-casing Value or modifying SQLCompiler/Query grouping globally.

scale.1: No visible applied implementation, or the latest visible implementation is corrupt or unrelated.
scale.2: A relevant edit is attempted but is visibly malformed, reverted without replacement, or placed outside ExpressionWrapper.
scale.3: A visible ExpressionWrapper override delegates to the inner expression but has a compatibility or hygiene defect such as failing to forward alias, or the final state is not clearly established.
scale.4: A correct, narrow delegation override is visibly present in ExpressionWrapper with no substantive surrounding corruption, but final diff-level confirmation or alias handling is incomplete.
scale.5: A clean final diff visibly adds only the correctly placed delegation override, preserves alias semantics, and leaves unrelated production behavior unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise ExpressionWrapper implementation boundary

applies_when: The task concerns an ExpressionWrapper changing whether a wrapped ORM expression appears in SQL GROUP BY.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible trajectory correctly establishes and, when attempted, implements the invariant that ExpressionWrapper preserves its inner expression's get_group_by_cols() result, so wrapped constants remain omitted without suppressing grouping required by nonconstant expressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final asserted repair globally filters constants in the SQL compiler, unconditionally returns no GROUP BY columns, changes Value instead of wrapper transparency, or otherwise suppresses columns needed by nonconstant wrapped expressions. Cap at 3 if a proposed or applied delegation remains visibly malformed, targets the wrong class, or is contradicted by unresolved task-shaped output.
metadata.evidence_authority: An intact applied diff plus executed task-shaped checks outranks direct runtime probes; direct probes and exact source tracing outrank an unsupported explanation. Later corrected conclusions supersede earlier exploration, but an unrepaired contradictory final implementation supersedes a correct earlier hypothesis.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for symptom recognition alone, speculative constant detection, compiler-level workarounds, or a return-empty implementation that fixes the example by breaking valid wrapped expressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit conclusion that ExpressionWrapper should use the wrapped expression's own GROUP BY columns rather than independently classifying constants or returning the wrapper itself. Score 5 additionally requires an intact applied implementation and visible behavioral validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source findings, direct get_group_by_cols() probes, the stated repair invariant, the actual ExpressionWrapper edit if present, and SQL or regression checks covering a wrapped Value plus an expression that legitimately requires grouping.
metadata.non_evidence: Repository browsing, dependency installation, repeated restatement of the issue, unrelated GROUP BY internals, unexecuted test scripts, and future-tense intentions without an explicit semantic repair are not evidence for higher anchors.
metadata.oracle_test: ExpressionWrapper(Value(3), output_field=...).get_group_by_cols() must match Value(3).get_group_by_cols() and yield no constant grouping term, while wrapping a resolved column or nonconstant function must preserve the inner expression's required grouping columns.
metadata.stage: early causal diagnosis through initial implementation validation

scale.1: No task-relevant causal finding about how ExpressionWrapper determines GROUP BY columns.
scale.2: Recognizes a GROUP BY problem but ends with an incorrect causal model or a repair that special-cases constants, changes unrelated compiler behavior, or suppresses all wrapped grouping columns.
scale.3: Correctly observes that wrapped and unwrapped constants differ, or traces the inherited default behavior, but does not unambiguously specify transparent delegation to the inner expression; any attempted edit is unresolved or semantically contradictory.
scale.4: Explicitly derives the correct delegation invariant from source or direct probes and states a compatible minimal repair, but no intact implementation with task-shaped behavioral validation is visible.
scale.5: Applies the delegation repair intact and visibly verifies that a wrapped constant is omitted from GROUP BY while required grouping behavior for at least one nonconstant wrapped expression is preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ExpressionWrapper GROUP BY semantic delegation

metadata.judge_focus: Applicable model source rather than forms, tests, or exploratory artifacts

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-applicable behavioral evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a related-model instance with a false-valued field or attribute named filterable triggers Query.check_filterable().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Diagnoses that build_filter() applies check_filterable() to the resolved RHS, that an ordinary model instance can expose filterable=False as application data, and that this must not be confused with Django's filterability marker on query expressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the model field changes an expression's own filterable marker, attributes the failure to the LHS ForeignKey, or reports a reproduction that actually uses filterable=True or a materially different lookup.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful minimal ORM reproduction or instrumented runtime trace showing a model instance reaching check_filterable() outranks inference from grep results; source-code tracing outranks unsupported explanation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a collision on an arbitrary RHS object's data attribute for an invalid SQL expression or a reserved model-field name.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence that the rejected object is the RHS model instance or another non-expression object, rather than a Field, ForeignKey, annotation, or Window expression.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of build_filter(), resolve_lookup_value(), check_filterable(), and the concrete type and value of the RHS that raises NotSupportedError.
metadata.oracle_test: For ModelA(filterable=False) used as the RHS of ModelB.objects.filter(foreign_key=model_a), getattr(model_a, 'filterable') is False and the current unconditional check raises even though model_a is an ordinary query value without the expression protocol.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis is present, or the explanation is unrelated to Query.check_filterable().
scale.2: Locates check_filterable() and notices the shared attribute name, but misidentifies the checked object or gives only speculative causality.
scale.3: Explains that the RHS model instance's false-valued filterable field is read by getattr() and causes the exception, but does not establish the expression/non-expression boundary with tracing or reproduction.
scale.4: Provides source-based tracing or a credible reproduction showing the RHS model instance reaches check_filterable(), with the relevant filterable=False value and resulting exception.
scale.5: Provides decisive runtime or source evidence for the complete causal chain and explicitly derives that only expression-like RHS values should be subject to the filterability marker while ordinary values remain valid.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies the RHS attribute collision and expression-protocol boundary

applies_when: The trajectory evaluates whether the fix preserves NotSupportedError for Window or other query expressions marked filterable=False, including nested source expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes that solving the ordinary-RHS collision does not permit Window expressions or other genuinely non-filterable expression trees in WHERE clauses and does not regress ordinary expression filtering.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible evidence shows a Window or nested non-filterable expression is accepted, or if the proposed implementation bypasses all RHS checks; cap at 3 when only synthetic classes are exercised.
metadata.evidence_authority: Django test-runner results against real expression and query classes outrank standalone copied functions or ad hoc mock classes; existing expressions_window tests define the expected rejection behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating disappearance of the reported exception as sufficient even when the safety check for invalid SQL expressions has been accidentally disabled.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible evidence for both the newly valid related-instance query and at least one genuinely non-filterable expression remaining invalid.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible existing tests, added assertions, or runtime checks covering both sides of the semantic boundary: ordinary false-valued RHS objects pass, while expression-protocol objects marked filterable=False still raise.
metadata.oracle_test: The related model instance with filterable=False is accepted as a value, while a Window expression, including one reached through get_source_expressions(), continues to raise the established 'is disallowed in the filter clause' NotSupportedError.

scale.1: No compatibility reasoning is present, or the approach intentionally removes filterability enforcement.
scale.2: Mentions Window or existing behavior without checking it, or presents evidence that invalid expressions are now accepted.
scale.3: Shows source-level reasoning or synthetic checks that genuine non-filterable expressions should still fail, but lacks real ORM evidence for both sides.
scale.4: Shows real evidence that the reported RHS case succeeds and a genuine non-filterable expression still fails, but does not cover recursive source-expression behavior or the relevant existing test suite.
scale.5: Shows focused passing evidence for the valid RHS case, preserved Window/non-filterable rejection, recursive checking where applicable, and no contradictory regression result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrates compatibility with genuine non-filterable expressions

applies_when: The trajectory creates, edits, locates, or plans Django tests for filtering a ForeignKey by an instance whose model has a false-valued filterable field.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a permanent Django regression test that exercises the public QuerySet API with a related model instance exposing filterable=False and demonstrates that the valid ForeignKey filter can be constructed or evaluated without NotSupportedError.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the test uses filterable=True, filters the BooleanField itself instead of using the instance as a related RHS, or never reaches query construction; cap at 3 if it only asserts that no exception was raised without checking query behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: A committed repository test and its runner output outrank temporary scripts; a public ORM query outranks direct calls to check_filterable() or copied mock logic.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting a mock getattr demonstration, direct helper invocation, or superficially similar Boolean-field query as a regression test for the actual ForeignKey RHS bug.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible permanent test code reproducing the collision through QuerySet.filter(), not merely a temporary script or synthetic object.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test model and test-case changes under the Django test suite, including the exact field name, false value, ForeignKey RHS lookup, and meaningful query assertion.
metadata.oracle_test: Create or use a related object whose BooleanField is literally named filterable and is False, pass that object to an exact ForeignKey lookup, and assert the expected queryset result or generated-query semantics.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence or test design is present.
scale.2: Only generic, malformed, or materially different experiments are shown.
scale.3: A faithful temporary reproduction or a precise permanent-test plan is shown, but no repository regression test is added.
scale.4: A permanent regression test visibly exercises the exact public ORM scenario and makes a meaningful assertion, but execution is absent or the fixture coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: A focused permanent regression test with the exact filterable=False related-instance scenario is visibly added and passes under the appropriate Django test runner.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds a task-specific ORM regression test

applies_when: A rollout prefix addresses the ORM failure caused by a concrete right-hand-side object exposing a false filterable attribute.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly isolates and validates a scoped ORM boundary: ordinary lookup RHS values, including model instances with a false field or attribute named filterable, must not be rejected as though they were non-filterable SQL expressions, while genuine non-filterable expressions must remain prohibited in WHERE clauses.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if visible evidence shows the proposed boundary would broadly bypass filterability validation, or if an exact reproduction does not fail as claimed and the discrepancy is not resolved. Cap at 4 if the approach relies only on model-specific naming, checks only synthetic objects, or does not verify that genuine non-filterable expressions remain rejected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful repository-backed reproduction and focused test output outrank hypotheses and prose. A command observation showing edited source or a subsequent readback can establish an applied experiment, but the cutoff git diff is authoritative about whether the change persisted. Direct test failures or successful counterexamples override claimed correctness.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad exploration, mock-only demonstrations, or fixes that merely avoid the reported exception by disabling the intentional expression filterability safeguard.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either a successful task-shaped reproduction or a visibly applied, narrowly scoped implementation accompanied by a focused executable check. Credit of 5 requires both the exact regression check and a non-regression check for a genuine non-filterable ORM expression.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source analysis, repository edits or readbacks, and executable outputs for an exact RHS model-instance reproduction, a narrowly targeted distinction between ordinary values and ORM expressions, and a preservation check using a genuinely non-filterable expression such as Window.
metadata.oracle_test: A related-model instance whose concrete filterable field value is False must remain a valid RHS for an exact ForeignKey lookup, while an ORM Window expression with filterable=False must still raise NotSupportedError when used in a filter clause.

scale.1: The visible work adopts a contradictory or harmful direction, such as removing filterability enforcement generally, changing unrelated behavior, or persisting with a disproven causal claim.
scale.2: The visible work only locates files, searches symbols, installs dependencies, or speculates; it neither establishes the RHS-versus-expression collision nor produces a task-shaped reproduction or scoped implementation.
scale.3: The visible work correctly identifies that an ordinary RHS object's filterable attribute collides with expression capability checking, or makes substantial progress toward an exact reproduction, but has neither a successful exact reproduction nor an applied implementation with a focused executable check.
scale.4: The visible work has a successful task-shaped reproduction or a visibly applied scoped fix with focused executable evidence, and its direction preserves the expression/value distinction, but exact regression coverage or the genuine non-filterable-expression preservation check is still missing.
scale.5: The visible work applies a scoped expression/value-boundary fix, demonstrates that the exact model-instance RHS regression is resolved, and separately demonstrates that a genuine non-filterable ORM expression is still rejected.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validated RHS-versus-expression filterability boundary

applies_when: A rollout prefix investigates or changes ORM filterability validation for a lookup RHS object exposing a false filterable attribute.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work accurately distinguishes an ordinary lookup RHS value whose application attribute happens to be false from an ORM expression whose filterability capability intentionally prohibits use in a WHERE clause, using source tracing, task-shaped execution, or a narrowly scoped boundary experiment.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the work continues to misidentify the checked object after contrary source or runtime evidence, claims a failed reproduction when the shown command succeeded, or treats dependency and database setup failures as confirmation. Cap at 3 if the proposed change bypasses filterability checks for all RHS objects, relies solely on a field-name special case, or an edit is asserted without readback or executable evidence. Cap at 4 when exact related-instance coverage, persisted implementation evidence, or the genuine non-filterable-expression preservation check is absent.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct task-shaped queryset output and focused repository tests are strongest. Source readbacks establishing the exact call path and runtime observations establishing the RHS object's type and concrete attribute value are stronger than general hypotheses. A focused synthetic check may validate the intended type or capability boundary at an intermediate level but cannot replace exact ORM coverage at the highest level. The cutoff diff establishes persistence, while direct command output may establish a transient applied experiment. Successful non-reproduction is valid evidence about the exercised configuration and must be reported as such rather than treated automatically as proof or contradiction.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding symbol search, setup activity, and repeated speculation as causal diagnosis; prevents penalizing truthful non-reproduction merely because it succeeds; and prevents fixes that evade the reported exception by weakening the expression safeguard generally.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a correct source-backed account that the ordinary RHS value itself reaches filterability validation, or informative task-shaped execution that tests that account. Credit above 3 requires either an exact task-shaped reproduction, a narrowly applied implementation with focused boundary evidence, or direct runtime evidence establishing both the ordinary-value identity and the capability-check collision. Credit of 5 requires a persisted scoped change, exact related-instance regression coverage, and executable confirmation that a genuine non-filterable ORM expression remains rejected.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine whether the work identifies the actual object passed from lookup-value resolution into filterability validation, distinguishes an application field value from ORM expression capability metadata, and avoids confusing the RHS with a queryset, field definition, lookup name, or unrelated SQL object. Then inspect any edit and executable evidence for acceptance of ordinary values without disabling rejection of genuinely non-filterable expressions.
metadata.oracle_test: An exact relational lookup accepts an ordinary related instance whose concrete application field named filterable is false, while a genuine ORM expression with filterable capability set to false still raises the documented unsupported-filter error in a filter clause.
metadata.stage: early causal diagnosis through focused implementation validation

scale.1: The work adopts a harmful or directly disproven direction, such as removing filterability enforcement generally, changing unrelated lookup semantics, or knowingly conflating every object with a false attribute with a prohibited ORM expression.
scale.2: The work is limited to navigation, dependency setup, generic symbol inspection, or unresolved speculation, or it materially misidentifies the object being checked despite visible source or runtime evidence.
scale.3: The work correctly traces the ordinary lookup RHS into filterability validation and explains the collision with expression capability metadata, or obtains informative task-shaped runtime evidence, but it has not yet demonstrated a scoped boundary change or an exact failing case. A truthful unresolved non-reproduction may reach this level when its conditions are examined rather than ignored.
scale.4: The work demonstrates the boundary through an exact task-shaped reproduction and scoped applied experiment, or through a narrowly applied change with focused executable evidence showing that ordinary false-attributed values are accepted while expression-like non-filterable objects remain rejected. Exact repository regression coverage or a genuine ORM-expression preservation check is still missing.
scale.5: A persisted narrowly scoped implementation is accompanied by exact regression coverage accepting the related-instance RHS with a false application field and a separate executable check confirming that a genuine non-filterable ORM expression remains prohibited.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precisely established RHS-versus-expression filterability boundary

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change for nested ordering paths whose final component is a relation field's attname.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Confines the fix to related-ordering expansion in SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name(), comparing the resolved relation field's attname against the final lookup component (for example pieces[-1]) while preserving expansion of Meta.ordering when the relation name itself is ordered.

scale.2: Targets the compiler area but proposes a broad or semantically incorrect special case.
scale.3: Suggests using the final path component or equivalent, but does not provide a complete safe condition or preserve relation-name behavior clearly.
scale.4: Provides an exact narrow edit in find_ordering_name() that compares field.attname with the terminal lookup component and explains preserved behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise compiler fix preserving relation ordering semantics

applies_when: The visible prefix attempts to execute or compile querysets for the reported self-referential ForeignKey ordering behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the quality of completed empirical evidence showing the erroneous join and ordering direction and comparing it with semantically informative control orderings.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if all reproduction attempts fail before SQL is produced. Cap at 3 if the trajectory reports conclusions inconsistent with its own generated SQL or uses a materially different relationship shape that does not exercise the self-referential terminal-attname case.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual query compiler output or passing assertions outrank predicted SQL and prose. Repository status and command observations determine whether a reproduction completed; installation attempts and scripts that terminate before query compilation are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents dependency installation, model introspection, or copied issue SQL from being mistaken for a successful, causally discriminating reproduction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require visible successful compilation or execution of the problematic queryset. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require at least one completed control that isolates terminal-attname handling from general ordering behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect completed command output for generated SQL, especially the ordered column, direction, and join structure for the terminal-attname form and controls such as explicit primary-key traversal, annotation-based column ordering, or reversed direction.
metadata.oracle_test: The defective form visibly adds traversal to the self-related table and inherits its default ordering direction, while explicit traversal to the primary key or direct local-column ordering avoids that expansion and honors the requested direction.

scale.1: No reproduction attempt or no task-relevant executable setup.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction but never obtains generated SQL or query results.
scale.3: Successfully produces the defective SQL and verifies at least one of the unexpected join or direction properties, without a completed discriminating control.
scale.4: Successfully reproduces the defect and a control that demonstrates direct FK-column ordering behaves differently, with the relevant SQL differences identified.
scale.5: Provides a repeatable minimal reproduction with multiple complementary controls or assertions that jointly isolate relation expansion, join count, and requested direction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reproduces the SQL defect with discriminating controls

applies_when: The trajectory creates or runs a reproduction for the reported self-referencing ForeignKey ordering behavior or inspects compiled SQL for equivalent models.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces task-specific runtime evidence that contrasts explicit ForeignKey-attname ordering with related-object ordering and confirms both ORDER BY direction and whether the unnecessary self-join is present.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if setup never reaches query compilation, or if the trajectory calls an observed DESC/extra join correct. Cap at 3 if temporary instrumentation changes behavior or the reproduction omits the self-reference or Meta.ordering prerequisite.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful executed output from the repository version outranks predicted SQL or prose. Failed setup attempts are only evidence of environment work, not ORM behavior. Query SQL and result ordering together outrank either alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for dependency installation, speculative tracing, or SQL inspection that does not distinguish the two independent symptoms: direction reversal and redundant join creation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require successful reproduction output for record__root_id and at least one control variant, with explicit interpretation of ORDER BY direction and join count.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed queryset compilation or tests using a model with Meta.ordering=('-id',), a nullable self-ForeignKey, and an outer model relation; relevant variants are record__root_id, -record__root_id, record__root__id, and record__root.
metadata.oracle_test: Before the fix, record__root_id exhibits recursive '-id' ordering and an extra LEFT OUTER self-join; the correct semantics are ordering directly by the already joined table's root_id column, ASC by default and DESC with a leading '-'. record__root__id is a useful correct control.

scale.1: No successful task-relevant runtime or SQL evidence.
scale.2: Attempts a reproduction but it fails before query compilation, or the setup omits a causal prerequisite.
scale.3: Successfully reproduces the problematic SQL or a control query, but not a decisive contrast covering both direction and join behavior.
scale.4: Shows executed SQL for the failing path and a control, correctly identifying inherited direction and the redundant self-join.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive SQL reproduction of direction and join behavior

metadata.evidence_authority: The cutoff-visible diff is authoritative for applied behavior and outranks prose. An exact expression or patch at the relation-deconstruction boundary outranks a generic casing promise. Executed deconstruction, migration-state, and app-registry assertions outrank printed expectations or self-authored success messages.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring mere investigation as a safe correction, treating an unapplied suggestion as a repository change, accepting a downstream fallback because it suppresses the exception, or overlooking that a patch changes app-label semantics globally.

metadata.judge_focus: First identify the concrete intervention the trajectory endorses; exploratory possibilities that remain unresolved do not count as selected corrections. Then inspect the visible repository diff and executed checks to distinguish a verbal direction, an exact proposal, an applied edit, and a validated edit.

Exact-case app lookup remains required, conventional lowercase-label relations remain unchanged, and truly missing applications retain their existing lazy-reference diagnostics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the trajectory remains committed to globally lowercasing app labels or making app-label lookup case-insensitive despite visible source or test evidence that app labels are case-sensitive. Assign 1 when self-authored or tautological output is presented as confirmation of that claim, or when confident causal conclusions are built without any command that exercises the claimed behavior. A speculative hypothesis that is explicitly left unresolved is not itself a contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and output from a reproduction exercising Django's actual registry, relation, or migration behavior outrank assistant assertions. Relevant version-control diffs or history outrank guesses about what changed between releases. Self-authored print statements, comments, and hypothetical examples do not verify framework behavior. The cutoff summary and git diff are authoritative for whether work remains applied, but transient edits may count only as experimental evidence when their observed result is shown.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding verbose source browsing, repeated restatement of the error, fabricated confirmation, or a fix at the error-reporting site when no evidence connects it to the causal normalization path.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require evidence identifying the semantic boundary that app labels retain their registered case while model names are normalized case-insensitively, and connecting the failure to the code path that constructs or serializes the lazy related-model reference. Anchor 5 additionally requires a focused regression test or equivalent reproduction that exercises the reported mixed-case case.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands and their observations for concrete narrowing among relation resolution, model-reference construction or deconstruction, migration state, and app-registry lookup. Credit successful minimal reproductions, exact source-path tracing, and relevant regression-history evidence; distinguish these from repeated searches that leave the same unsupported premise unchanged.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, the correct semantic reference is that Django app labels are case-sensitive, model names are case-insensitive, and a related-model reference must preserve the registered app-label spelling while normalizing only the model-name component. Productive investigation should trace why a mixed-case app label becomes lowercase in the lazy reference rather than changing app-registry semantics globally.

scale.4: Repository evidence coherently identifies the exact causal boundary: the app-label spelling must be preserved while only the model name is normalized, and the implicated reference-construction or serialization path is localized; no focused regression test or validated applied fix is yet shown.
