scale.3: An applied production change causally alters server threading, worker waiting, server selection, or post-shutdown cleanup, but it does not guarantee cleanup in every connection-owning request worker.
scale.4: Applied production code closes database connections in each request worker on normal and exceptional exit, but targeted regression coverage for threaded live-server cleanup is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Applied production code closes database connections in each request worker through an unconditional finally-style path, with a targeted regression test that exercises threaded request cleanup and teardown ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied request-connection lifecycle quality

applies_when: Tests, runtime probes, or a concrete test plan address Q combined with Exists or another boolean conditional expression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evidence covers Q and Exists in both operand orders and demonstrates valid query semantics, not merely successful object construction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest visible Q-left test still raises TypeError, NotImplementedError, an object-not-subscriptable error, or returns Value(Exists(...)). Cap at 3 when only construction/repr is tested without query evaluation or expected-result assertions.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful targeted Django test-runner results with assertions outrank ad hoc repr-only scripts; the latest failing rerun overrides earlier success claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a non-exceptional repr, a hand-written mock, or the already-working Exists-left order as sufficient proof of the fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires observed successful execution of the formerly failing Q-left case or a committed repository test with a task-specific expected result.
metadata.judge_focus: Repository tests or runtime output for Q(...) & Exists(...), Exists(...) & Q(...), and corresponding OR behavior, preferably through QuerySet.filter() with asserted rows or SQL semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: Filtering with Q(predicate) & Exists(subquery) yields the same logical result as Exists(subquery) & Q(predicate), and the analogous reversed OR expression also evaluates correctly.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence exists, or all relevant probes fail before exercising the operator behavior.
scale.2: Only the original failure or the already-working Exists-left order is demonstrated, or the latest Q-left probe visibly fails.
scale.3: Both orders are exercised at object-construction level and appear valid, but there is no repository-level query assertion or the OR case is omitted.
scale.4: The formerly failing Q-left AND case and at least one complementary order or connector pass in relevant tests, with meaningful expected structure or query behavior.
scale.5: Targeted repository tests visibly pass for reversed AND and OR combinations, include non-empty Q predicates, and assert equivalent query results or otherwise decisive ORM semantics for both operand orders.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive semantic coverage for both operand orders

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the operand-order asymmetry between Q and a boolean conditional expression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The diagnosis traces the two Python operator paths, identifies conditional capability as the operand boundary, and explains why merely admitting the expression still leaves the empty-Q branch unsafe.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for an account centered only on a missing Q.__rand__ or for claiming that Q-left invokes the reflected method first. Cap at 2 if the latest account continues to endorse reflected-only repair, arbitrary operator delegation, resolve_expression eligibility, or Value wrapping after contrary evidence. Cap at 3 if it identifies the direct Q-left guard and conditional protocol but does not correctly explain the empty-Q branch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and reproduced call traces outrank speculation. Later TypeError, NotImplementedError, Value-wrapped output, or object-not-subscriptable output invalidates any earlier causal claim that cannot explain that result. Edits count as diagnostic evidence only when the trajectory states or demonstrates the mechanism they address.
metadata.failure_mode: Stopping at the operand-order dispatch asymmetry or strict guard and therefore missing the second failure caused by Q-only identity handling.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires correctly stating that the Q-left operation invokes Q.__and__ or Q.__or__ and reaches Q._combine() before reflected fallback can repair it. Credit above 3 requires correctly mapping the object-not-subscriptable failure to the empty-self branch attempting Q-style deconstruction or reconstruction of a non-Q conditional operand.
metadata.judge_focus: Explicit source-backed reasoning about Q.__and__ and Q.__or__, Q._combine(), the expression-side conditional combination path, and the branch selected when an empty Q is combined with a non-Q conditional expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For Q() combined with Exists, Python enters Q.__and__ or Q.__or__ and then Q._combine(); for Exists combined with Q, the expression-side operator recognizes both operands as conditional and constructs Q-compatible nodes. Once Q._combine() admits conditional operands, an empty self must not deconstruct the Exists operand as if it were a Q lookup node.

scale.1: The account is absent or fundamentally misstates which operator method handles the Q-left expression.
scale.2: The asymmetry or strict Q check is noticed, but the latest explanation still relies on reflected methods, broad expression capability, or another mechanism contradicted by source or runtime output.
scale.3: The diagnosis correctly traces the direct Q-left path to Q._combine() and explains the expression-left conditional path, but does not correctly identify why the empty-Q case can fail after the guard is loosened.
scale.4: The diagnosis also maps the empty-Q failure to unsafe deconstruction or reconstruction of the non-Q conditional operand, with only a minor omission about the opposite identity branch or connector symmetry.
scale.5: The account precisely distinguishes both dispatch paths, conditional eligibility, the two identity cases, and normal nonempty tree construction, explaining why the narrow repair must change both the acceptance boundary and branch-safe copying for AND and OR.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-backed diagnosis of dispatch, eligibility, and empty-Q failure

applies_when: The trajectory encounters a failed target probe, conflicting operator-dispatch evidence, or an edit that introduces a new exception or damages source structure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory uses each visible contradiction to retire the mechanism it disproves, applies a narrower revision, removes obsolete edits, and checks the revised coherent source with a discriminating follow-up probe.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest source is malformed, truncated, duplicated, or still contains orphaned code. Cap at 2 if the trajectory repeats a disproved reflected, delegation, wrapping, or broad-protocol mechanism, or blames tooling after the same target failure recurs. Cap at 3 if it reaches the correct causal lesson or restores clean source but does not both apply the corresponding revision and probe it afterward. A latest known target failure caps at 3 unless another visible revision and follow-up occur after that failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exception traces and runtime output outrank verbal success claims. The latest complete source view or diff determines whether abandoned code remains. A source restoration proves integrity only; it does not prove recovery of the target behavior. A follow-up probe counts only when it exercises the visibly revised state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking activity, source restoration, or a correct verbal observation for recovery without retiring the contradicted code and testing the replacement.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a specific contradicted mechanism to be removed or replaced in coherent source and a subsequent discriminating probe against that revision. Credit of 5 requires the latest targeted evidence to agree with the final narrow mechanism.
metadata.judge_focus: The sequence from each failure to the next hypothesis, edit, cleanup, source inspection, and probe: reflected methods after Q.__and__ raises first, broad wrapping after Value or object-not-subscriptable results, and empty-Q handling after nonempty combinations succeed while the empty case fails.
metadata.oracle_test: After reflected dispatch is disproved, reflected edits are removed and attention moves to Q._combine(); after wrapping causes Value or object-not-subscriptable behavior, wrapping is removed and the relevant empty branch is isolated; the resulting coherent source is then probed on the case that distinguished the old and new hypotheses.

scale.1: Contradictions are ignored or compounded, and the latest source is broken or incoherent.
scale.2: A failure is noticed, but the disproved mechanism is repeated, broadened, or left in the latest source without a coherent replacement.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly eliminates at least one hypothesis and leaves coherent source or a narrower plan, but the corresponding revision is absent or lacks a later discriminating probe.
scale.4: A contradicted mechanism is removed, a materially narrower revision is applied, and a later probe validates the revised causal step or exposes one new localized blocker; final validation or cleanup remains incomplete.
scale.5: Successive failures retire reflected, broad-wrapping, and unsafe empty-Q mechanisms as encountered; obsolete edits are removed; the final source is coherent; and later targeted evidence supports the resulting narrow approach.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Verified recovery from contradicted Q–expression approaches

applies_when: The proposed change broadens the operand types accepted by Q logical combination.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory protects existing Q/Q behavior and rejection of non-conditional operands while avoiding unrelated changes to expression bitwise semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if F expressions, integers, arbitrary objects, or any resolve_expression object are accepted as logical conditions; also cap at 2 if generic Combinable.__rand__/__ror__ semantics are globally weakened without task-specific necessity.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete regression test output and the final operand guard override general assurances that the patch is minimal.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the reported pair by silently broadening Q into a container for every expression or by regressing established Q identity and connector behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that unsupported operands remain rejected and ordinary Q-to-Q combinations still work.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests or source reasoning for Q & Q, Q | Q, empty and non-empty Q operands, non-conditional expressions or ordinary objects, and unchanged bitand()/bitor() behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Boolean conditional expressions such as Exists are accepted; Q/Q AND and OR retain their established connector and empty-node behavior; unsupported operands still raise TypeError and arithmetic/bitwise expression APIs remain unchanged.

scale.1: The change visibly breaks ordinary Q combinations or indiscriminately accepts unrelated objects.
scale.2: Compatibility is largely unaddressed, and source or runtime evidence shows at least one serious over-acceptance or Q/Q regression.
scale.3: The implementation appears narrow and Q/Q smoke checks pass, but unsupported-operand rejection or empty-Q behavior is not demonstrated.
scale.4: Q/Q AND and OR plus unsupported operands are visibly covered, with only a minor gap such as absent subclass or negation coverage.
scale.5: Regression evidence covers non-empty and empty Q/Q combinations, both connectors, unsupported non-conditional operands, and confirms no unnecessary change to generic expression bitwise behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression protection for Q and non-conditional operands

applies_when: A visible edit or concrete patch plan changes logical combination involving Q and non-Q operands.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The implementation admits boolean conditional operands at the Q combination boundary while preserving Q/Q identities, rejecting unsupported operands, and avoiding global or arbitrary operator delegation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest source is syntactically malformed, structurally corrupted, or cannot execute the edited path. Cap at 2 when it accepts arbitrary objects, all resolve_expression objects, or all operands exposing an operator; delegates directly to another operand's operator; wraps conditions in Value; or globally weakens Combinable bitwise behavior. Cap at 3 when the guard is narrow but an empty-Q branch still deconstructs, reconstructs, or indexes a non-Q conditional operand as though it were Q data.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest complete source view or diff determines implementation scope. Targeted runtime results outrank assurances, but construction-level success cannot excuse a visibly broad guard or unsafe identity branch. A malformed or partially applied source view overrides earlier clean snippets.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating successful object construction as proof of compatibility despite over-acceptance, unsafe empty-Q reconstruction, arbitrary delegation, or unrelated changes to expression operators.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible narrow conditional-capability guard and branch-safe behavior for an empty Q combined with a non-Q conditional operand. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible checks that ordinary Q/Q behavior and unsupported-operand rejection remain intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest coherent Q._combine(), Q operator methods, and any expression-operator edits for the acceptance predicate, both empty-operand branches, connector preservation, copying behavior, and rejection of non-conditional operands.
metadata.oracle_test: A conditional expression such as Exists is accepted by Q._combine(); an empty Q returns or copies the conditional operand without Q-only deconstruction; ordinary empty and non-empty Q/Q combinations retain their identities and connectors; integers, F expressions, and arbitrary objects remain unsupported; generic expression bitand and bitor behavior is unchanged.

scale.1: The latest implementation is malformed or visibly breaks the edited operator path or ordinary Q combination.
scale.2: The implementation uses a broad or unrelated mechanism that can admit unsupported operands or alter generic expression operator semantics.
scale.3: The implementation has a narrow conditional boundary, but empty-Q copying or another identity branch remains unsafe or unresolved.
scale.4: The latest coherent implementation narrowly accepts conditional operands and safely handles Q identities for AND and OR, while source evidence preserves unsupported-operand rejection; regression execution is limited.
scale.5: The narrow branch-safe implementation is present and visible tests confirm both connectors, empty and non-empty Q/Q behavior, conditional expressions, and rejection of representative unsupported operands without generic operator changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Narrow, branch-safe Q conditional implementation

applies_when: The prefix considers or implements a MultiValueField.clean() change or must distinguish server validation from required-attribute rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides a low-weight distinction below the accepted implementation threshold by measuring whether an incorrect validation hypothesis is narrowly bounded, checked against compatibility, rejected after contradiction, or cleanly reverted.

metadata.failure_mode: Indiscriminate clean rewrite, repeated malformed edits, or continued success claims after a behavioral contradiction
metadata.judge_focus: Observable branch containment and response to contrary evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Inspection of the all-empty branch plus optional aggregate and valid populated-input behavior

scale.1: The prefix broadly changes the all-empty path, leaves malformed or instrumented source, or continues to assert correctness despite a direct contradiction.
scale.2: The prefix remains validation-only, but the experiment is localized, explicitly under diagnosis, or observably reversible.
scale.3: The experiment preserves clearly unrelated modes or is cleanly reverted after contrary evidence, although the accepted rendering cause is not implemented.
scale.4: The validation experiment is tightly limited by observable conditions, preserves unrelated all-empty modes, and is supported by coherent branch-specific checks.
scale.5: Contrary evidence causes complete causal recovery: the clean experiment is removed and the accepted rendering model is adopted.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Incorrect validation-hypothesis containment

applies_when: The prefix modifies source, runs a behavioral check, reports a result, or exposes a repository artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the current evaluator-facing source is coherent and executable and whether conclusions accurately reflect what visible commands exercised.

metadata.failure_mode: Malformed source, missing functional edit, known contradiction presented as success, shadowed checkout, debug output, or non-executed test treated as a pass
metadata.judge_focus: Current source validity, imported source identity, executed evidence, and absence of conflicting instrumentation
metadata.oracle_test: Import or focused execution from the edited checkout followed by complete source-diff inspection
metadata.stage: Discriminative validation and final patch integrity

scale.1: The asserted artifact is malformed, non-importable, missing its functional change, retains a runtime hazard, or is directly contradicted by executed behavior still represented as success.
scale.2: The source is plausibly executable but evidence is non-discriminative, material contamination or unresolved contradictions remain, or relevant commands never execute.
scale.3: The current source is coherent and visible failures are classified correctly, but exact rendering or compatibility evidence remains incomplete.
scale.4: The edited checkout and discriminative behavior are directly verified, with only limited broad-suite or artifact-cleanliness uncertainty.
scale.5: The complete focused artifact is clean and importable, exact rendering and compatibility checks pass from the edited checkout, and all non-behavioral failures are correctly separated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing source and evidence integrity

applies_when: The prefix investigates, modifies, or tests MultiValueField required handling, MultiWidget rendering, BoundField attributes, or the reported form behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures implementation of the browser-facing correction: a required outer MultiValueField in partial mode assigns required to corresponding child widgets according to each subfield and child-widget policy while preserving all existing outer gates and fallback behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Validation-only edit, uniform required propagation, missing policy gate, incorrect child alignment, or absent rendering change
metadata.judge_focus: Functional child-attribute behavior rather than server-side validation
metadata.oracle_test: A required child renders required and an optional child omits required when the outer field is required and require_all_fields is false

scale.1: No accepted rendering behavior is implemented or evidenced; work is absent, validation-only, malformed, or observably produces incorrect child attributes.
scale.2: Rendering or constituent requirements are mentioned, but the concrete approach still targets cleaning, parent-only propagation, or another path that cannot establish correct child attributes.
scale.3: A functional per-child rendering branch exists, but child alignment, MultiWidget applicability, a required-attribute gate, child-widget policy, or fallback behavior is materially wrong or uncertain.
scale.4: The source implements semantically correct gated and aligned child handling with the ordinary fallback preserved, but exact discriminative HTML evidence is absent.
scale.5: The correct implementation is present and executed evidence shows required on the required child, no required attribute on the optional child, and preservation of the relevant gates.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Accepted per-subwidget required rendering

applies_when: A trajectory changes a post_process() loop, suppresses a public yield, buffers results, or otherwise can affect repeated-pass control flow or error reporting.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether deduplicating public successes leaves the internal multi-pass algorithm and its error contracts intact: every repeated result contributes its subst flag, processing continues until a substitution-free pass or exhaustion, per-file Exception tuples remain visible, the synthetic All failure remains, and dry-run and completed hash-map behavior are preserved.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any continue, return, or filtering branch that can bypass subst accounting caps the score at 1. A visible path that suppresses or overwrites an Exception, removes required passes, or unconditionally raises the max-pass error also caps at 1. Failed tests that never reach the relevant assertion are non-evidence rather than proof of a product defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest active production control flow is authoritative. A successfully executed focused failure or convergence case may confirm it. Comments, intended algorithms, source-marker counts, independent loop simulations, and earlier versions of a subsequently rewritten method are not evidence that the active branches preserve these contracts.
metadata.failure_mode: Public deduplication changes pass termination, hides a per-file failure, loses the synthetic exhaustion error, mutates behavior during dry runs, or prevents the completed local hashed_files mapping from being installed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires every repeated-pass result to reach `substitutions = substitutions or subst` regardless of whether its public tuple is emitted. A score above 3 additionally requires visible preservation of per-file exceptions, max-pass reporting, dry-run return, and final hash-map update.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace every path through both _post_process() loops. Check the placement of substitutions accumulation relative to continue or filtering branches, treatment of Exception-valued processed results, the max-pass branch, the dry_run return, and self.hashed_files.update(hashed_files).
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect all repeated-loop branches, then exercise a nested case requiring another pass, a per-file processing failure, and an import loop that reaches `('All', None, RuntimeError('Max post-process passes exceeded.'))`.

scale.1: The active control flow visibly skips substitution accounting, removes or corrupts required passes, hides an authoritative failure, unconditionally fails normal processing, or is too malformed to preserve these contracts.
scale.2: The repeated passes remain, but a material exception, exhaustion, dry-run, or hash-map defect is visible, or some repeated results can be filtered before required accounting.
scale.3: Every subst flag is visibly accumulated and pass termination remains intact, but one or more failure, dry-run, or final-map contracts are ambiguous in the active source.
scale.4: Inspection establishes complete per-result substitution accounting and preserves per-file exceptions, max-pass reporting, dry runs, and self.hashed_files finalization.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied and executed production-generator cases confirm nested convergence, originating-path failure visibility, and the synthetic max-pass failure without contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Internal convergence and failure contracts remain authoritative

applies_when: The prefix proposes, applies, restores, or inspects an edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process().
The prefix claims that a production fix exists.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible production method actually contains a coherent, executable, narrowly scoped storage-level edit. Judge the latest source and diff rather than terminal status, stated intent, or apparent stage of progress.

metadata.failure_mode: The intended edit is absent, uncertain, applied to the wrong block, accidentally restored, structurally incomplete, or syntactically invalid.
metadata.judge_focus: Latest source state, successful edit application, executable control flow, accidental restoration or corruption, and production-file scope.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the complete edited method, compile or import it, inspect the production diff, and reconcile the latest source view with earlier rewrite attempts.
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow storage-level change / Review and prepare the submission artifact

scale.1: No relevant production edit remains, or the latest method is visibly malformed, incomplete, or non-executable.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible, but failed rewrites, contradictory inspections, or incomplete control flow leave its production state materially uncertain.
scale.3: The latest method is coherent and relevant but contains a visible implementation defect or lacks enough inspection to establish structural integrity.
scale.4: A narrow, coherent, executable storage-level edit is visibly present, with only minor uncertainty about compatibility or artifact correspondence.
scale.5: The complete latest method and diff are coherent, executable, narrowly scoped, and demonstrably correspond to the production state exercised by validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest observable production-state integrity

applies_when: The prefix changes a public yield site or the repeated adjustable-file loop.
The visible edit can affect exceptions, substitutions, pass termination, dry runs, or hash-map updates.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether public deduplication remains independent from internal convergence and failure reporting. Every repeated-pass result must contribute its substitution flag, per-file failures must remain visible, and the max-pass failure, dry-run behavior, and completed hash mapping must remain intact.

metadata.failure_mode: A branch skips substitution accounting, a failure tuple is hidden or replaced, required passes are weakened, or the max-pass, dry-run, or hash-map contract is lost.
metadata.judge_focus: Substitution accumulator placement, continue branches, exception authority, max-pass error, dry run, and completed hash mapping.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect every repeated-loop path and execute processing-failure, import-loop, and nested-reference cases through the edited generator.
metadata.stage: Design final-result buffering / Implement a narrow storage-level change

scale.1: The code visibly breaks or removes convergence or failure behavior, is too corrupted to preserve it, or skips substitution accounting on a normal repeated-pass path.
scale.2: A material convergence or failure-propagation defect is visible, such as filtering a later exception or branching before required accounting.
scale.3: The main passes and signals remain present, but exception authority, pass exhaustion, dry-run behavior, or an edge control-flow path is ambiguous or unverified.
scale.4: Inspection shows that passes, substitution accounting, failures, dry runs, and hash-map updates are preserved, though focused failure tests are incomplete.
scale.5: The relevant control flow is visibly preserved and production-generator tests confirm nested convergence, per-file failure visibility, and max-pass reporting.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Convergence and failure-signal preservation

applies_when: A production edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process() exists, has been rewritten, restored, or prepared for submission.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The latest cutoff-visible production state must contain a syntactically coherent, complete, narrowly scoped edit to HashedFilesMixin.post_process(), and any evaluator-facing patch must correspond to that active state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later restoration, malformed rewrite, invalid syntax, absent production hunk, edit only in a helper script, or final patch that omits the active fix overrides earlier success messages and caps the score at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace and its production diff outrank earlier edit messages, temporary copies, proposed patches, and source text merely displayed before later rewrites. When submission is patch-based, the final evaluator-facing patch is authoritative over unsubmitted workspace changes.
metadata.failure_mode: The intended fix is absent, applied only to temporary material, structurally incomplete, syntactically invalid, accidentally reverted, obscured by unrelated edits, or missing from the evaluator-facing artifact.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a complete relevant production edit to be visibly active and syntactically coherent. A score of 5 additionally requires visible correspondence between the active source, production diff or patch, and the source actually loaded by validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Use the latest complete view of storage.py, the active workspace diff, compilation or import output, and the submitted patch. Track accidental restoration, edits applied to the wrong method, malformed indentation, undefined names, unreachable blocks, missing method sections, stale patches, and unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: Display the complete active post_process() method, run compilation or import from the repository checkout, inspect the full production diff, and reconcile its content with any final submitted patch.
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow storage-level change / Review and prepare the submission artifact

scale.1: No relevant active production edit exists, or the latest authoritative source or submitted artifact is malformed, incomplete, stale, or non-executable.
scale.2: A relevant edit may exist, but conflicting later views, failed rewrites, an incomplete method, or uncertain artifact correspondence prevents establishing a coherent active state.
scale.3: A complete and coherent production edit is visible, but loadability, scope, or correspondence to the final artifact remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The active production edit is complete, syntactically coherent, narrowly scoped, and consistent with the visible diff or patch.
scale.5: Level 4 holds, and compilation or import plus the final source and diff establish that validation and submission use the same active production state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active production edit is coherent and evaluator-visible

applies_when: Concrete destructive, truncating, broad, or wrong-class production editing occurred.
The latest repaired source must be distinguished from an earlier validated or corrupted state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how directly the latest production state is established after concrete source corruption, while distinguishing a missing inspection from affirmative evidence of a remaining defect.

metadata.failure_mode: The latest authoritative state remains corrupted or a repeated destructive history leaves the latest candidate materially unresolved.
metadata.judge_focus: Evidence tied to the last material production edit
metadata.oracle_test: After the last material source repair, decisive protocol checks pass or a complete focused final diff establishes a coherent known-correct implementation.

scale.1: The latest authoritative source or selected artifact visibly remains corrupted, invalid, wrong-class, or unrepaired.
scale.2: A repair is claimed after concrete corruption, but the latest production candidate is not coherently shown and substantial contradictory evidence remains.
scale.3: A plausible repair is partially visible, but repeated destructive history leaves a material latest-state gap.
scale.4: The latest repaired source is coherently inspected or shown in a focused diff, with only a minor concrete evidence gap.
scale.5: The latest repaired state is decisively established by post-repair protocol evidence or a complete focused final diff with no current defect.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Post-corruption latest-state establishment

applies_when: An authoritative OrderedSet implementation, production diff, selected artifact, or direct reversed(OrderedSet(...)) behavior is observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures once whether reversed() dispatches on OrderedSet, directly returns an Iterator, and yields current backing-dictionary keys in exact reverse forward-iteration order.

metadata.failure_mode: Unsupported dispatch, recursion, wrong placement, wrong direction or component, invalid source, or a direct result lacking __next__.
metadata.judge_focus: Authoritative placement, dispatch, direct Iterator compliance, key identity, and reverse order
metadata.oracle_test: result = reversed(OrderedSet([1, 2, 3])); isinstance(result, collections.abc.Iterator) and iter(result) is result and list(result) == [3, 2, 1]

scale.1: The authoritative candidate visibly lacks usable OrderedSet reversed support, remains invalid, recurses, places the method on the wrong class, or reverses the wrong object or component.
scale.2: Reverse contents may be consumable, but a required property is visibly wrong, including a direct helper without __next__ or whose __iter__ returns another iterator.
scale.3: Some reverse behavior is established, but a core semantic property or authoritative implementation remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: Dispatch and reverse contents are established with only a minor concrete uncertainty about direct Iterator conformance or authoritative placement.
scale.5: A known Iterator-producing implementation or decisive runtime evidence establishes correct placement, dispatch, direct Iterator conformance, reverse key identity, and exact order.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: OrderedSet reversed protocol contract

applies_when: A production diff, selected artifact, or complete edited source region is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures independent regression risk and unnecessary semantic redesign without duplicating protocol, transport, or latest-state judgments.

metadata.failure_mode: Broad semantic redesign, unrelated production behavior changes, or unnecessary machinery with concrete compatibility risk.
metadata.judge_focus: Preservation of existing OrderedSet representation and behavior
metadata.oracle_test: Existing OrderedSet methods and dictionary-backed semantics remain unchanged apart from reverse-iteration support.

scale.1: Existing OrderedSet semantics are visibly broken by broad or unrelated production changes.
scale.2: Substantial unrelated semantic changes create significant compatibility risk.
scale.3: Avoidable production machinery or unrelated edits introduce concrete maintenance or regression risk.
scale.4: The change is focused with harmless extras or limited incidental formatting.
scale.5: The existing representation and behavior are preserved without unnecessary semantic complexity.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and focused production scope

applies_when: An exact patch or artifact is explicitly designated as evaluator-facing by a submission action or artifact designation.
An observed receiver or application command establishes that an exact artifact must transport the production change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures only whether the exact selected artifact can deliver its production contents to the intended path.
does_not_apply_when: Only an ordinary working tree or displayed git diff is visible.
A patch file or copied patch text exists without observable selection.
No exact transport artifact is designated.

metadata.failure_mode: The selected artifact is empty, malformed, omits the production file, demonstrably fails application, or has unusable path headers.
metadata.judge_focus: Completeness, production path, path-header compatibility, and observed receiver application
metadata.oracle_test: The exact selected artifact applies through the established receiver to django/utils/datastructures.py and yields inspectable production source.

scale.1: The selected artifact is empty, malformed, demonstrated not to apply, omits the production edit, or uses identical unprefixed old and new repository paths without demonstrated compatible handling of that exact artifact.
scale.2: A major concrete transport concern is visible, but the path form is not already known to be incompatible and the exact artifact may still be usable under an identified receiver convention.
scale.3: The exact artifact is selected, but a material intrinsic delivery property remains genuinely unresolved from its complete contents and receiver evidence.
scale.4: The selected artifact is likely usable with only a minor concrete delivery detail unresolved.
scale.5: The selected artifact is complete and conventionally usable with suitable paths, or successful application through the established receiver is visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Selected evaluator-facing artifact transport validity

applies_when: The cutoff contains a proposed or applied code change intended to prevent Meta.ordering columns from changing grouped aggregation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes SQL compilation so only implicit Meta.ordering is excluded from GROUP BY expansion while selected columns, HAVING expressions, and explicit or extra ordering expressions retain their required grouping behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the change also suppresses explicit order_by(), extra_order_by, selected expressions, or HAVING grouping requirements, or only changes QuerySet.ordered/final SQL rendering, credit is capped at 2. A localized but uncertain alternative that may alter unrelated query semantics is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The visible repository diff and surrounding source semantics outrank statements that a fix was made; a narrower behavior-preserving change outranks a broad removal of ordering contributions.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for blanket removal of all ordering from grouped queries, which would fix the reported example while regressing explicit ordering behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied, visible source diff rather than a plan, patch draft, or command that failed before modifying the repository.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py or an equivalently precise compiler location; especially a guard excluding the get_group_by() order_by loop when _meta_ordering is active, or a demonstrably equivalent suppression of only the default-ordering branch for grouped queries.
metadata.oracle_test: Implicit Meta.ordering contributes no GROUP BY columns, but an explicit order_by('field') on a grouped query continues to contribute the field where SQL semantics require it.

scale.1: No relevant code change, or an applied change targets unrelated ORM behavior.
scale.2: Only describes the intended edit, changes QuerySet.ordered/final rendering, or applies an overbroad change that removes required explicit-ordering behavior.
scale.3: Applies a localized and plausible compiler change, but its distinction between implicit and explicit ordering is incomplete, uncertain, or accompanied by unrelated edits.
scale.4: Applies a correct localized change that excludes Meta.ordering from GROUP BY construction while preserving explicit ordering, SELECT, and HAVING contributions.
scale.5: Applies the precise behavior-preserving fix from anchor 4 with clean project-consistent structure and comments, no unrelated modifications, and a diff whose surrounding logic visibly establishes the intended boundary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the fix at the implicit-ordering boundary

applies_when: The task concerns Django ORM aggregation where implicit model Meta.ordering affects generated GROUP BY expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the visible work progresses from relevant investigation to a correctly scoped, applied, and validated correction that prevents implicit Meta.ordering expressions from enlarging aggregation groups without suppressing legitimate explicit ordering.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the proposed change would discard explicit ordering indiscriminately, alter aggregation grouping without evidence of the ordering-to-grouping flow, or target only QuerySet.ordered while leaving generated GROUP BY semantics unresolved. Cap at 3 if a claimed edit is contradicted by later direct file or diff evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct file contents, git diff, and test output outrank plans, prose claims, and generated summaries. An observed edit plus subsequent file inspection may establish application when no later diff contradicts it. Repository history or an upstream patch may corroborate intended semantics but cannot substitute for applying or testing local work.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad ORM exploration, failed ad hoc setup, or removal of the final ORDER BY clause as though these alone fixed the earlier leakage of implicit ordering expressions into GROUP BY.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require correctly distinguishing implicit Meta.ordering from explicit order_by() and identifying the concrete compiler boundary where resolved ordering expressions enter GROUP BY; score 5 additionally requires both an applied local fix and task-specific regression validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible commands, source excerpts, patches, diffs, and test output for an evidence-backed account of the SQLCompiler flow from default ordering resolution through get_group_by(), followed by a narrowly scoped correction and aggregation regression coverage.
metadata.oracle_test: For a model whose Meta.ordering names a non-grouping field, a values(...).annotate(Count(...)) query must aggregate only by the requested grouping keys and return combined counts rather than groups split by the default-ordering field. Explicit order_by() expressions must retain their established GROUP BY behavior where SQL requires it.

scale.1: Only generic exploration or repetition is visible; no concrete aggregation-ordering mechanism is established.
scale.2: Relevant ORM files, history, or tests are inspected, but the account remains speculative, targets the wrong layer, or does not trace how implicit ordering reaches GROUP BY.
scale.3: Correctly traces Meta.ordering through compiler ordering resolution into GROUP BY construction and explains the aggregation error, but does not yet establish a narrowly scoped applied correction or authoritative equivalent.
scale.4: Correctly isolates implicit Meta.ordering from explicit ordering and specifies the narrow corrective condition, with either a visibly applied local change or strong source-level corroboration of the exact intended change; task-specific regression validation is still absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Applies the narrowly scoped fix, adds or updates a regression test demonstrating correct grouped counts with Meta.ordering, and shows relevant tests passing while preserving explicit-ordering behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal resolution of Meta.ordering leakage into GROUP BY

applies_when: The cutoff contains command output from reproductions, Django tests, or broader regression checks related to the change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates through executable evidence that grouped aggregation ignores implicit Meta.ordering and that relevant existing ORM behavior remains intact.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Dependency errors, missing settings, missing test runners, malformed scripts, or an unrelated test passing do not establish the fix and cap credit at 3. Any unresolved task-specific failure caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Completed command output with passing assertions outranks claims of success; a focused semantic test outranks an unrelated passing ordering test. Test failures and tracebacks remain authoritative until a later successful rerun addresses them.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating repeated environment setup attempts, SQL printing without semantic assertions, or a single unrelated ordering test as proof of correctness.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a completed passing run of a task-specific regression or reproduction against the applied change; anchor 5 additionally requires broader relevant regression coverage or visible fail-before/pass-after evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Observed generated SQL or aggregate rows, execution of the focused regression test, the aggregation regression test module, and relevant broader ORM tests using Django's repository test runner.
metadata.oracle_test: Runtime output must show one aggregate row per intended key with unsplit counts and no implicit Meta.ordering column in GROUP BY, while relevant Django aggregation/compiler tests continue to pass.

scale.1: No validation attempt, or available output directly contradicts the intended behavior.
scale.2: Only setup or dependency failures are visible, or a task-specific run fails without a successful corrective rerun.
scale.3: A useful reproduction or unrelated sanity test completes, but no task-specific post-change assertion passes.
scale.4: A focused task-specific regression test or equivalent semantic reproduction completes successfully against the applied change.
scale.5: The focused validation in anchor 4 passes and is accompanied by either demonstrated fail-before/pass-after behavior or successful broader aggregation/compiler regression tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces decisive validation without mistaking setup failures for evidence

applies_when: The cutoff contains investigation or explanation of Django grouped-query compilation with model default ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the causal compiler flow by which implicit model Meta.ordering is resolved as ORDER BY expressions, passed into GROUP BY construction, and removed from ORDER BY only after its columns have already affected grouping.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A diagnosis that attributes the leak solely to Query.set_group_by(), QuerySet.ordered, aggregate expression classes, or final GROUP BY rendering without correcting that claim is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts, a fetched upstream patch, or observed generated SQL outrank unsupported narration; later corrected analysis outranks an earlier mistaken hypothesis.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards locating the real compiler data flow rather than treating the visible GROUP BY text or QuerySet.ordered property as the root cause.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible evidence connecting get_order_by() to get_group_by() and explaining why clearing or nulling ORDER BY during final SQL assembly is too late.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or explanation of SQLCompiler.pre_sql_setup(), get_order_by(), get_group_by(), the _meta_ordering marker, and the loop adding non-reference ordering expressions through get_group_by_cols().
metadata.oracle_test: For a model whose Meta.ordering names a non-grouping field, values(grouping_key).annotate(count=Count(...)) must aggregate only by the selected grouping key; the implicit ordering field must affect neither ORDER BY nor GROUP BY.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the compiler flow.
scale.2: Recognizes that Meta.ordering corrupts grouped aggregation but only searches broadly or names the wrong insertion point.
scale.3: Locates SQLCompiler ordering and grouping code and notes that ordering expressions are added to GROUP BY, but does not fully distinguish implicit Meta.ordering from explicit ordering or explain the timing defect.
scale.4: Correctly traces implicit Meta.ordering through get_order_by() into get_group_by() and explains that later ORDER BY suppression cannot undo the expanded grouping.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and corroborates it with generated SQL, wrong aggregate results, historical patch evidence, or an equally decisive source-level demonstration showing the unwanted ordering column.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly traces the Meta.ordering leak into GROUP BY

applies_when: Visible work investigates, explains, or changes Django ORM compilation for grouped queries affected by implicit model default ordering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the work turns investigation of grouped-query ordering into a concrete, evidence-backed diagnosis or correction that prevents implicit model default ordering from enlarging GROUP BY while retaining the established grouping effect of explicit order_by() expressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the work removes or ignores explicit order_by() contributions indiscriminately, changes only QuerySet.ordered or final ORDER BY rendering, or attributes the defect solely to Query.set_group_by() without correcting that account. Cap at 3 when a claimed local correction is absent from or contradicted by the latest file contents or git diff. Failed setup attempts and unrelated passing tests cannot establish task-specific validation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest local file contents and git diff determine whether a correction was applied. Direct compiler excerpts and generated SQL outrank narration for causal claims. Task-specific aggregate results and test output determine validation. An exact historical or fetched patch may corroborate the intended correction boundary but cannot substitute for a claimed local edit or passing local test.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents repeated ORM browsing, speculative references to ordering, and late suppression of rendered ORDER BY from receiving the same credit as a complete compiler trace, a concrete faulty SQL demonstration, or a narrowly scoped correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require visible evidence that ordering resolved by SQLCompiler is supplied to GROUP BY construction or equivalent generated-SQL evidence of the leaked default-ordering column. Score 4 requires either a complete timing diagnosis that distinguishes implicit from explicit ordering or a visible narrowly scoped correction at one of the two valid boundaries: excluding implicit default ordering before GROUP BY receives ordering expressions, or skipping only marker-identified implicit ordering contributions inside GROUP BY construction. Score 5 requires an applied correction plus task-specific passing validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Prioritize concrete progression: identify get_order_by() or equivalent ordering resolution, show how its expressions reach get_group_by(), determine whether the ordering is implicit or explicit, and then look for generated SQL, an exact corroborating patch, a scoped local diff, or relevant test output. Do not require one implementation shape when another visible change truthfully prevents only implicit ordering from reaching grouping.
metadata.oracle_test: For a model whose default ordering names a field outside values(), values(grouping_key).annotate(count=Count(...)) must group only by grouping_key and return combined counts, with neither GROUP BY nor final ORDER BY affected by the implicit field. A corresponding query using explicit order_by(ordering_field) must retain that expression's established GROUP BY contribution where SQL semantics require it.
metadata.stage: early causal diagnosis, correction, and validation

scale.1: Only generic exploration, task restatement, or incompatible reasoning is visible; no concrete compiler or SQL mechanism is established.
scale.2: Relevant ordering, aggregation, history, or grouping code is inspected, but the work remains speculative, follows the wrong layer, or never directly shows resolved ordering expressions affecting GROUP BY.
scale.3: Direct source or generated-SQL evidence connects compiler ordering resolution to GROUP BY expansion, but the work lacks at least one decision-critical element: a clear implicit-versus-explicit distinction, an explanation that later ORDER BY suppression is too late, or a concrete scoped correction.
scale.4: The work is decision-ready: it clearly distinguishes implicit model ordering from explicit order_by(), establishes how implicit ordering reaches GROUP BY before final ORDER BY suppression, or visibly applies a narrowly scoped correction that prevents that flow while leaving explicit ordering intact. A correction may validly exclude implicit ordering during ordering resolution or guard its later GROUP BY contribution. Task-specific passing validation is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: A narrowly scoped local correction is visible, and task-specific passing evidence demonstrates combined aggregate counts without the implicit ordering field while also checking that explicit-ordering behavior remains intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed correction of implicit ordering leakage into GROUP BY

applies_when: Visible work adds or modifies tests for Q.deconstruct() behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible tests encode the new positional-args behavior for a lone lookup child and a lone non-subscriptable boolean expression, while checking reconstruction and existing connector or negation cases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A test that continues to require Q(x=1) to deconstruct into kwargs caps credit at 2; a test that merely uses a generic mock without checking args and kwargs caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository test code with exact assertions outranks temporary scripts, printed values, or prose descriptions of proposed tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting source-only experimentation while leaving existing regression tests committed to the superseded serialization format.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible repository test changes that no longer assert the obsolete kwargs representation for a single lookup child.
metadata.judge_focus: Changes in tests/queries/test_q.py or equivalent committed tests, with exact assertions for args, kwargs, no exception, and Q(*args, **kwargs) round trips.
metadata.oracle_test: Tests should expect Q(x=1) to yield args=(('x', 1),), kwargs={}, and Q(Exists(...)) to yield one positional expression argument and reconstruct equivalently without TypeError.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence is visible, or tests encode behavior unrelated to Q.deconstruct().
scale.2: Only the old single-child kwargs expectation is retained, or a proposed test checks merely that no exception text was printed.
scale.3: A temporary or repository test covers the non-subscriptable child and checks useful output, but does not update the lone-lookup contract or reconstruction.
scale.4: Repository tests visibly cover both the new lone-lookup args shape and the non-subscriptable child, with at least one reconstruction or metadata assertion.
scale.5: Focused repository tests comprehensively assert the new args/kwargs contract, Exists or an equivalent real boolean expression, round-trip reconstruction, and connector/negation preservation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression tests encode the new serialization behavior

applies_when: The task concerns deconstructing a Q object whose sole child may be an ORM expression rather than a lookup pair.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible reasoning identifies the single-child kwargs special case as the causal defect and adopts the intended contract that every Q child, including a lone lookup tuple or Exists expression, is serialized through positional args.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Reasoning that retains kwargs serialization for a lone 2-tuple, checks hasattr(__getitem__), or accepts lists/dicts as lookup pairs is capped at 3; denying the child[0]/child[1] cause is capped at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct inspection of Q.__init__() and Q.deconstruct(), followed by observed deconstruct results, outranks speculation about subscriptability or backward compatibility.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a backward-compatible tuple guard as equivalent to the requested removal of the undocumented single-child special case.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require recognizing that the intended fix removes the single-child kwargs distinction rather than merely broadening which child types qualify for it.
metadata.judge_focus: Reasoning about self.children, the child[0]/child[1] crash, and the intended serialization shape for both Q(x=1) and Q(Exists(...)).
metadata.oracle_test: After the intended change, Q(x=1).deconstruct() has args=(('x', 1),) and kwargs={}, while Q(Exists(...)).deconstruct() has args=(exists_expression,) and does not raise TypeError.

scale.1: No correct causal diagnosis is visible, or the trajectory attributes the crash to unrelated query combination or settings behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory locates Q.deconstruct() or reproduces the TypeError but does not establish the serialization contract needed to fix it.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly explains the unsafe child indexing but chooses or endorses a tuple-length/subscriptability guard that preserves the old single-lookup kwargs behavior.
scale.4: The trajectory clearly concludes that the special case should be removed and that lone children belong in args, but incompletely explains reconstruction or metadata preservation.
scale.5: The trajectory precisely derives the defect and intended contract from code and runtime behavior, covering lone lookup tuples, non-subscriptable expressions, reconstruction, and connector/negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the Q.deconstruct() contract

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Q.deconstruct() for a sole child that may be an ORM expression or another non-lookup object.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether visible reasoning identifies the unsafe single-child indexing assumption, derives that deconstruction must retain rather than merely stop crashing on the child, and validates the intended contract that every child is serialized through positional args.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Denying that child[0]/child[1] causes the failure caps credit at 1. If visible output has empty args and kwargs for a nonempty Q, or otherwise omits the sole child, cap at 3 even when the trajectory calls the result successful. Retaining any tuple, length, subscriptability, list, or dictionary test that converts a lone lookup child to kwargs caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source or unified diff determines the selected contract. Executed deconstruct and Q(*args, **kwargs) observations are next strongest. A concrete executable regression assertion that would fail when the child is omitted is stronger than prose but weaker than execution. Plans, claimed success, and assertions that only check absence of an exception are non-evidence for retention.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding location of the failing line without checking that the child survives, treating an empty deconstruction as successful crash avoidance, or treating a compatibility guard as equivalent to removal of the undocumented single-child representation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires either visible execution retaining the arbitrary child as a positional argument or a concrete executable regression assertion that checks its retention. Credit above 3 requires visibly adopting and applying the uniform all-children-in-args contract. Credit of 5 requires visible round-trip evidence and connector or negation preservation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect reasoning about self.children and child[0]/child[1], the selected serialization contract for both Q(x=1) and an Exists-like child, and visible outputs or assertions showing whether the sole child remains in args. Also inspect reconstruction, connector, and negation checks when present.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended diagnosis predicts Q(x=1).deconstruct() with args=(('x', 1),) and kwargs={}, and Q(exists_expression).deconstruct() with args=(exists_expression,) without an exception. Reconstructing Q(*args, **kwargs) must preserve the child structure, nondefault connector, and negation.

scale.1: The trajectory does not identify the unsafe single-child indexing cause, or attributes the failure to unrelated query, model, or settings behavior.
scale.2: The unsafe child indexing is correctly identified, but visible work neither retains the arbitrary child nor authors an executable assertion that would detect its omission; this includes accepting empty args and kwargs as success.
scale.3: The cause and retention requirement are established by direct execution or a concrete regression assertion, but the selected implementation remains shape-dependent, is visibly contradicted by omission, or has not yet adopted the uniform positional contract.
scale.4: The trajectory visibly adopts and applies the uniform all-children-in-args contract and demonstrates positional serialization for both a lone lookup tuple and an arbitrary non-subscriptable child, but round-trip or metadata validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The trajectory derives, applies, and validates the uniform positional contract, including retained non-subscriptable and lookup children, successful Q(*args, **kwargs) reconstruction, and preservation of nondefault connector and negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnosis and validation of Q.deconstruct() child retention

applies_when: A visible patch or source edit changes the implementation of Q.deconstruct().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge the latest applied Q.deconstruct() implementation by whether it retains every child, avoids broad shape or subscriptability assumptions, preserves metadata and path normalization, and preferably removes the single-child representation distinction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A branch that leaves args and kwargs empty for a nonempty Q, indexes a child after merely checking len() or __getitem__, or loses path, _connector, or _negated handling caps at 1. Treating lists, dictionaries, strings, or arbitrary subscriptable objects as lookup pairs caps at 2. Any remaining exact-tuple single-child kwargs conversion caps at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff overrides prose and earlier edits. Provenance-confirmed execution is supporting evidence for branch behavior. Temporary outputs from code that was subsequently restored or replaced are non-evidence for the final implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating all defensive guards, overlooking a branch that silently drops the child, or accepting broad duck-typing that converts arbitrary positional objects into keyword arguments.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires that every nonempty Q path retains its children. Credit above 2 requires either an exact built-in tuple of length 2 as the sole compatibility classification or removal of shape-based classification entirely. Credit above 3 requires unconditional positional serialization of all children. Credit of 5 requires a minimal clean implementation preserving path, connector, and negation logic.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact final branch structure and initialization of args and kwargs. Check behavior implied for an Exists-like object, a lookup tuple, a string, a list, a dictionary, an unusual-length tuple, a nondefault connector, and negation.
metadata.oracle_test: The canonical implementation is semantically equivalent to args = tuple(self.children); kwargs = {}; add _connector only for a nondefault connector; add _negated only when true; return the normalized path, args, and kwargs.

scale.1: The applied edit is malformed, can omit a child, still indexes an arbitrary child, or loses required path or metadata behavior.
scale.2: The edit avoids the reported example but uses a broad len(), __getitem__, list, dictionary, string, or similar predicate that can misclassify other positional children.
scale.3: A complete compatibility implementation converts only an exact length-2 tuple to kwargs and reliably places every other child in args while preserving path and metadata.
scale.4: All children are unconditionally serialized through args and required path and metadata behavior is preserved, but the patch contains avoidable duplication, unrelated changes, or unclear initialization.
scale.5: A minimal, clean applied implementation unconditionally derives args from self.children, initializes kwargs independently, and preserves path normalization, nondefault connector, and negation semantics.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe and precise implementation in Q.deconstruct()

applies_when: Visible work executes, adds, or modifies checks for Q.deconstruct() behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge how effectively visible checks expose loss of a sole arbitrary child, distinguish the intended lone-lookup positional representation from the obsolete kwargs representation, and verify reconstruction plus connector or negation metadata.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a check labels empty args and kwargs successful for a nonempty Q, or otherwise accepts loss of the sole arbitrary child, cap at 1. A check that only confirms no exception without exposing args and kwargs caps at 2. Checks that explicitly require lone-lookup kwargs serialization cap at 3 even if they correctly verify arbitrary-child retention. Failures solely from unchanged assertions for the superseded lone-lookup representation do not invalidate otherwise correct canonical checks.
metadata.evidence_authority: Exact repository test assertions are strongest. Executed temporary assertions and deterministic executed comparisons or complete printed args and kwargs are next, provided the output visibly reveals whether the child was retained. Unexecuted assertions follow. Generic PASS labels, exception-only checks, plans, and prose descriptions are weakest and cannot override displayed omission or a contradictory assertion.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating no exception as a retention test, overlooking output that visibly contains empty serialization for a nonempty Q, refusing all credit to precise executed observations merely because they are temporary, or treating tests of the obsolete lone-lookup kwargs form as canonical contract coverage.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires visible inspection of args and kwargs for an arbitrary sole child without accepting omission. Credit above 2 requires an assertion, equality comparison, reconstruction check, or complete executed observation that makes child retention observable. Credit above 3 requires visible checks of the canonical positional form for both a lone lookup and an arbitrary child, plus reconstruction or metadata behavior. Credit of 5 requires durable repository regression tests covering the full contract.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the exact assertions, comparisons, and displayed values. Determine whether omission would be detected, whether Q(x=1) is expected in positional args with empty lookup kwargs, whether the same arbitrary child survives in args and reconstruction, and whether nondefault connector and negation metadata are checked.
metadata.oracle_test: Checks should establish Q(x=1).deconstruct() as args=(('x', 1),) with kwargs={}, establish an Exists-like object as the sole positional argument of its deconstruction, reconstruct equivalent children with Q(*args, **kwargs), and verify conditional _connector and _negated metadata.

scale.1: No relevant serialization result is inspected, or visible checks accept or celebrate omission of a sole arbitrary child.
scale.2: Checks reproduce the case or display relevant output but only establish crash avoidance, provide incomplete values, or do not make retention of the specific arbitrary child reliably observable.
scale.3: Executed checks make arbitrary-child positional retention observable and may cover reconstruction or metadata, but the lone-lookup contract is absent or explicitly remains in kwargs.
scale.4: Visible executable checks enforce or unambiguously demonstrate positional serialization for both a lone lookup and an arbitrary child and also cover reconstruction or connector/negation metadata, but durable repository coverage or one semantic case is incomplete.
scale.5: Durable repository regression tests assert both positional forms, arbitrary-child retention, round-trip reconstruction, nondefault connector handling, and negation handling.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable checks expose Q.deconstruct() retention and representation errors

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes Q.deconstruct() for a sole child that may be an ORM expression or another non-lookup object.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the trajectory correctly traces the failure to unconditional indexing of a sole child, applies a repair that retains that child, and validates the selected serialization contract, with explicit precedence for the latest visible implementation and a strict distinction between compatibility guards and uniform positional serialization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible implementation can still index an arbitrary sole child, leaves a nonempty sole child out of both args and kwargs, or visibly reconstructs a materially different Q object, assign 1 regardless of earlier successful output or prose. If a later restoration removes the repair, applied-work credit is unavailable. Any type, length, subscriptability, list, dictionary, or tuple-shape branch that still converts a lone lookup child to kwargs caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff determines which contract is applied and overrides earlier edits, summaries, and executions. Repository-root executions of that source are next strongest, followed by exact executable assertions and then observed deconstruct outputs. Success labels, plans, and expected results cannot override contradictory source or output.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting diagnosis despite visible child loss, treating absence of TypeError as proof that the child survived, relying on execution performed before a later source restoration, or rewarding a well-tested compatibility guard as equivalent to removal of the single-child special case.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 1 requires a correct causal diagnosis and no authoritative evidence of child omission. Credit above 2 requires a visibly applied repair that necessarily retains arbitrary sole children. Credit above 3 requires the applied source to serialize every child positionally without a shape-dependent lone-child kwargs branch. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible round-trip validation and preservation of nondefault connector and negation metadata.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest Q.deconstruct() body first. Determine whether a sole arbitrary expression is retained in args, whether a lone lookup tuple also remains in args, and whether reconstruction, nondefault connector, and negation checks were actually performed against the applied source.
metadata.oracle_test: For both a lone lookup and a lone non-subscriptable expression, deconstruct() should return the child as the sole positional argument and no lookup kwargs. Q(*args, **kwargs) should reconstruct equivalent children, while _connector appears only for a nondefault connector and _negated only when true.

scale.1: The cause is misidentified, the authoritative implementation remains unsafe, or visible behavior drops or materially corrupts a sole child.
scale.2: The unsafe child indexing is correctly diagnosed and a plausible repair is discussed or attempted, but no authoritative applied repair establishes retention of an arbitrary sole child.
scale.3: A visible applied compatibility repair safely retains arbitrary sole children positionally, with at least direct output or an omission-sensitive check confirming retention, but a shape-dependent lone-lookup kwargs branch remains.
scale.4: The visible applied implementation removes the special case and serializes all children positionally, with observed or executable evidence covering both a lone lookup and an arbitrary sole child, but round-trip or metadata validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The uniform positional implementation is visibly applied and validated for lone lookup and arbitrary children, Q(*args, **kwargs) reconstruction, nondefault connector metadata, and negation metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and applied validation of Q.deconstruct() child retention

applies_when: A current ResolverMatch production edit, diff, or post-change representation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores concrete progress from the generic partial display toward a representation that identifies the underlying callable and exposes pre-bound values.

metadata.failure_mode: No persisted change, unusable output, generic partial type only, or dropped bound values
metadata.judge_focus: Task-facing progress rather than adherence to a single presumed implementation

scale.1: No persisted relevant change, or current production behavior remains at the generic partial display with no task-facing improvement.
scale.2: A relevant production attempt persists, but it is unexecuted, currently fails, or does not yet show the underlying callable in a usable representation.
scale.3: Current production behavior visibly identifies the underlying callable, but pre-bound positional or keyword values are absent, relocated unclearly, or not demonstrated.
scale.4: Current behavior visibly identifies the underlying callable and retains pre-bound values in the ResolverMatch representation or its displayed argument fields, with only formatting or coverage gaps.
scale.5: Current production code consistently provides an informative representation containing the callable and pre-bound values across the exercised partial forms, with focused assertions passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable partial-representation progress

applies_when: Commands, assertions, or test results are visible after a production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores evidence that the current persisted implementation, rather than a simulation or superseded edit, produces the claimed representation behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Only source inspection, simulation, obsolete output, loose unrelated checks, or unresolved latest failure
metadata.judge_focus: Comparable current-code evidence

scale.1: No post-change production execution is visible, or the latest relevant execution fails before producing usable output.
scale.2: A current direct case executes, but evidence is print-only, loose, or omits either the callable or pre-bound values.
scale.3: Several relevant current-code cases execute successfully and show useful callable or argument behavior, with important coverage gaps.
scale.4: Focused assertions cover the principal partial cases and an ordinary callable, and the latest relevant checks pass.
scale.5: Exact focused tests and compatibility checks pass against the same persisted production source, with no unresolved related failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current-code validation evidence

applies_when: The edited implementation constructs ResolverMatch objects or changes callable and argument handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether partial handling produces coherent callable, args, and kwargs state while leaving ordinary ResolverMatch construction and representation usable.

metadata.failure_mode: Exceptions, lost arguments, duplicate values, broken ordinary callables, or inconsistent tuple fields
metadata.judge_focus: Runtime coherence and absence of task-relevant regressions

scale.1: Current source cannot construct or represent relevant ResolverMatch objects, or ordinary callables are broken.
scale.2: Partial handling executes only incompletely, with demonstrated argument loss, duplication, invalid access, or inconsistent state.
scale.3: The main partial case and ordinary callables are usable, but argument ordering, override behavior, tuple access, or additional callable forms remain unresolved.
scale.4: Exercised partial and ordinary cases have coherent callable and argument state with no demonstrated task-relevant regression.
scale.5: Focused checks establish coherent behavior for partial and ordinary callables, including positional and keyword values and applicable legacy access.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ResolverMatch behavioral coherence

applies_when: The task concerns changing Django source so scalar __iso_year filters no longer use calendar-year bounds.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the cutoff-visible repository change actually prevents YearLookup's raw-field calendar-bound optimization for an ExtractIsoYear left-hand side while retaining that optimization for ExtractYear and preserving valid module structure.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest applied source returns None or another invalid compiler value, causes an import or dependency cycle, removes unrelated datetime classes or registrations, or otherwise makes the module unusable. Cap at 2 if the only attempted bypass compares the Year* lookup's self.lookup_name with iso_year, because that condition is false for exact, gt, gte, lt, and lte. Cap at 3 if ordinary ExtractYear comparisons visibly lose their valid optimization.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct repository contents and diffs outrank summaries, patch descriptions, comments, and custom scripts. Real generated ORM SQL can prove the effect of an applied change, but earlier SQL does not override a later source edit. If a broad edit was later reverted or repaired, judge only the latest visible source state.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the comparison lookup name for the left-hand transform name, rewarding an applied but unreachable branch, treating source-search scripts as proof of semantic effect, or overlooking collateral deletion and invalid return values.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a task-causal source change visibly present at the cutoff. Diagnosis, proposed edits, generated patch text not shown as applied, and verification scripts alone remain at score 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of datetime lookup registrations and YearLookup.as_sql(). Determine whether the applied mechanism acts on the left-hand transform identity or removes the specialized Year* registrations from ExtractIsoYear. Treat self.lookup_name on YearExact, YearGt, YearGte, YearLt, or YearLte as the comparison operator name, not the transform name.
metadata.oracle_test: For a literal right-hand side, ExtractIsoYear followed by exact or ordered comparison must compile the ISO-year extraction and comparison.
