ExtractYear followed by the same comparison must retain calendar-year bounds. Removing YearExact/YearGt/YearGte/YearLt/YearLte registrations from ExtractIsoYear is valid; checking self.lhs.lookup_name for iso_year is also valid if implemented without a dependency cycle.

scale.1: The latest applied change visibly breaks lookup compilation or module integrity, such as returning an invalid value, creating a dependency cycle, or removing unrelated required datetime code.
scale.2: No effective task-causal implementation is present: there is no applied source change, or the applied change is a no-op such as comparing the Year* comparison lookup name with iso_year.
scale.3: An applied change can affect the faulty path but is incomplete or overbroad, such as bypassing ISO-year bounds while also losing the ordinary-year optimization or leaving relevant comparison coverage uncertain.
scale.4: The latest applied source correctly routes ISO-year scalar comparisons through extraction, preserves ordinary-year bounds, and has no visible architectural or collateral defect, but no focused durable regression test is applied.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and includes an applied focused regression test whose assertions cover an ISO/calendar boundary and protect ordinary __year behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Apply an effective ISO-year fix without damaging lookup compilation

applies_when: The trajectory inspects, proposes, or modifies Django datetime extraction tests relevant to year and iso_year filtering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Updates the regression suite so calendar-year lookups alone retain BETWEEN expectations and ISO-year filtering is checked against ISO-boundary data, including direct lookup or filtered annotation behavior that would fail under calendar-year bounds.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If tests continue to require BETWEEN or zero EXTRACT occurrences for iso_year, credit is capped at 2. A test using only mid-year dates, where calendar and ISO years coincide, cannot exceed 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Committed test diffs and their exact fixtures/assertions outrank plans, comments, ad hoc scripts, or claims that existing tests are sufficient.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting SQL-shape assertions inherited from the broken optimization, or testing ExtractIsoYear annotations without filtering and therefore missing the faulty lookup path.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an applied test change that fails with the old optimization for semantic reasons, not merely a source-registration introspection assertion.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes in tests/db_functions/datetime/test_extract_trunc.py or an equivalently authoritative existing test module, especially removal of iso_year from assertions that require BETWEEN/no EXTRACT and addition of a result assertion covering dates whose ISO year differs from their calendar year.
metadata.oracle_test: A boundary fixture such as late December assigned to the following ISO year or early January assigned to the preceding ISO year must be included/excluded according to isocalendar().year when filtered through __iso_year.

scale.1: No relevant test understanding, or proposed/applied assertions preserve the broken ISO-year BETWEEN expectation.
scale.2: Identifies that existing expectations are wrong but supplies no concrete regression assertion, or only changes superficial SQL text checks.
scale.3: Provides a concrete ISO-year filter test or corrects the old optimization expectation, but not both; alternatively, the data lacks an ISO/calendar boundary distinction.
scale.4: Applies both parts: ordinary year remains covered by optimization assertions, and an ISO-boundary filter regression would fail before the fix and pass after it.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and covers the important entry paths or operators without redundancy, such as implicit __iso_year filtering plus filtered ExtractIsoYear annotation or representative exact/range comparisons.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression test changes

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes why a scalar __iso_year filter is compiled using calendar-year bounds.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible analysis correctly traces the ISO-year transform into its comparison lookup, explains why YearLookup discards extraction, and identifies a discriminator or registration change that can actually separate ISO year from calendar year.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the analysis claims self.lookup_name on YearExact, YearGt, YearGte, YearLt, or YearLte equals iso_year, claims calendar-year January-to-December bounds implement ISO years, or proposes returning no SQL result. Cap at 3 if it identifies the registration problem but recommends an import that would create a visible datetime/lookups dependency cycle.
metadata.evidence_authority: Inspected source definitions, lookup-object output, and real query structure outrank narrative repetition. Runtime output showing the lookup object's class and lhs.lookup_name is stronger than an unsupported claim. Concrete ISO-boundary examples support semantics but do not replace dispatch tracing.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding verbose source exploration as complete diagnosis, conflating transform and comparison lookup names, or accepting a proposed condition that cannot be true on the object where it is evaluated.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require both the YearLookup fast-path trace and a correct account of where iso_year can be observed or how removing ExtractIsoYear's specialized registrations avoids the fast path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the claimed object chain for field__iso_year comparisons: the field resolves ExtractIsoYear, then exact, gt, gte, lt, or lte resolves a Year* lookup. Verify whether the analysis places iso_year on the left-hand transform and the comparison name on the Year* lookup itself.
metadata.oracle_test: For field__iso_year=2020, the comparison lookup name is exact and its lhs is the ExtractIsoYear transform whose lookup_name is iso_year. YearLookup's direct-value branch replaces that transform with its underlying field and calendar bounds. A sound remedy therefore changes the registrations or consults the lhs transform without creating a cycle.

scale.1: No task-causal explanation is present, or the explanation is fundamentally incompatible with the visible lookup and SQL behavior.
scale.2: The analysis recognizes that ISO-year boundaries differ from calendar years and that BETWEEN is wrong, but does not correctly locate the dispatch mechanism or proposes a contradicted discriminator.
scale.3: The analysis connects ExtractIsoYear's registered Year* comparisons to YearLookup's raw-field bounds path, but does not clearly distinguish the transform identity from the comparison lookup identity.
scale.4: The analysis correctly traces the lookup chain, distinguishes lhs.lookup_name from self.lookup_name, and identifies at least one architecture-safe remedy that would affect the faulty path.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and grounds the diagnosis in inspected lookup structure or generated SQL plus a concrete ISO/calendar boundary example, while explicitly preserving the valid ordinary-year optimization.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnose the ISO-year dispatch path with an actionable discriminator

applies_when: The trajectory attempts to validate a fix for ISO-year filtering or its interaction with the calendar-year optimization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the strength of cutoff-visible execution evidence that ISO-year filters use extraction semantics and that ordinary year filters still use their valid bounds optimization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when post-change ORM output still shows calendar-year BETWEEN bounds for an ISO-year scalar filter, when boundary results are wrong, or when the assistant declares success despite such output. Failed setup attempts without contradictory ORM behavior cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful targeted Django tests and actual ORM query results have highest authority, followed by generated ORM SQL, then lookup-object inspection or pre-fix reproduction. Static text searches, hand-simulated logic, and assistant assertions are not behavioral validation. Test failures must be interpreted against the task semantics rather than outdated assertions that require the known-bad BETWEEN behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a grep-based 'fix is present' script as equivalent to exercising Django, accepting only an annotation projection without filtering, or interpreting obsolete tests that assert BETWEEN for iso_year as the semantic oracle.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require successful post-change execution through Django's ORM or test runner. Merely finding the edited line, checking a source string, or running a script that does not compile a real queryset cannot exceed anchor 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed ORM query output and relevant Django test-run results. Prefer boundary-sensitive result assertions over SQL-shape checks, and SQL generated by the real query compiler over static source inspection or custom scripts that merely search for patch text.
metadata.oracle_test: A post-change ISO-year queryset should compile to backend-specific ISO-year extraction rather than calendar-year BETWEEN bounds. A regular year queryset should still compile to the bounds optimization. Strongest evidence includes dates near New Year whose ISO year differs from their calendar year and covers exact or ordered comparisons.

scale.1: Executed post-change ORM or test evidence contradicts the required behavior, or a claimed pass is based on output that still demonstrates the bug.
scale.2: There is no successful task-relevant behavioral execution; validation is absent, fails during setup, or consists only of static source and patch-text checks.
scale.3: A real pre-fix reproduction or lookup-identity inspection succeeds, establishing the cause, but no successful post-change ORM query or relevant test is shown.
scale.4: Successful post-change evidence from the real ORM or test runner demonstrates ISO-year extraction and either correct filtering behavior or preservation of the ordinary year optimization, but does not establish both with boundary-sensitive coverage.
scale.5: Successful post-change ORM tests establish correct ISO-year results at calendar/ISO boundary dates and also verify that ordinary year filtering retains its valid optimization, with relevant comparison behavior covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validate ISO-year filtering through real ORM behavior

applies_when: The trajectory executes queries, Django tests, or other runtime checks intended to validate the ISO-year fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces trustworthy runtime evidence that ISO-year filters use backend ISO-year extraction and return correct boundary rows, while ordinary year filters continue to use the calendar-bound optimization and relevant Django tests pass.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Observed post-edit ISO-year SQL containing raw-field BETWEEN, an official relevant test failure not explained as an obsolete assertion, or an import/syntax failure caused by the edit caps credit at 2. Environment-only failures do not prove correctness.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful relevant Django test run with semantic assertions is strongest, followed by an executed ORM query showing both SQL and correct rows, followed by SQL-only evidence. Static source checks and predicted output are non-decisive.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a custom script that searches for a code line, prints expected behavior, or manually invokes a branch as proof that Django generated correct SQL and results.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires at least one successfully executed ORM or official-test path after the final relevant edit. Anchor 5 additionally requires both ISO-year correctness and regular-year regression evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Exact commands and observed outputs: Django's tests/runtests.py results, generated WHERE SQL, and database query results for boundary dates. Distinguish successful execution from missing dependencies, setup errors, and scripts that only inspect source strings or object types.
metadata.oracle_test: The ISO-year WHERE clause contains the backend equivalent of EXTRACT(isoyear FROM field) compared using the requested operator, excludes calendar-only false positives at year boundaries, and ordinary __year with a literal still uses BETWEEN or equivalent bounds.

scale.1: No successful relevant execution, or runtime evidence directly shows the fix is broken.
scale.2: Only setup failures, source-text checks, mocked branch demonstrations, or contradictory runtime output are visible.
scale.3: A successful ORM check shows corrected ISO-year SQL or correct boundary results, but lacks the other semantic dimension and lacks regular-year protection.
scale.4: Successful runtime evidence shows corrected ISO-year SQL and semantic filtering, or an authoritative targeted Django regression test passes after the final edit.
scale.5: Authoritative tests pass and visible evidence also confirms ISO-year extraction/boundary results plus continued ordinary-year optimization; broader relevant tests show no regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive SQL and runtime validation

applies_when: A visible source edit or executable check concerns recognition of BigAutoField or SmallAutoField descendants as AutoField subclasses.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied AutoFieldMeta implementation transitively recognizes descendants of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField while preserving ordinary AutoField subclass behavior, unrelated-field rejection, and the existing AutoField instance-check contract.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if visible applied code leaves a required BigAutoField or SmallAutoField descendant rejected, accepts an unrelated field, breaks AutoField identity or normal subclasses, makes __instancecheck__ invalid by changing _subclasses to a non-class/non-tuple value, or is syntactically invalid. Cap at 2 when only Options._get_default_pk_class or another individual caller is broadened while the shared AutoField issubclass contract remains false.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final unified diff or post-edit source read has highest authority. Later successful executable checks against the edited source are next, followed by an edit command or rewrite script that visibly targets the correct method. Prose claims and pre-edit tests have no authority over contradictory applied source. Successful descendant checks do not override a visible regression in another metaclass method.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents preferring one exact source expression over equivalent correct implementations and prevents awarding high credit to a descendant-only fix that silently corrupts _subclasses or __instancecheck__.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires evidence of an applied edit at AutoFieldMeta rather than only a caller-specific validation change. Credit above 3 requires preservation of the superclass fallback or demonstrably equivalent ordinary AutoField behavior, plus no visible type-contract break between _subclasses and __instancecheck__.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the effective definitions of AutoFieldMeta._subclasses, __subclasscheck__, and any edited __instancecheck__. Accept equivalent tuple-based, explicit-class, generator, loop, or MRO implementations when their visible semantics satisfy the full contract.
metadata.oracle_test: The effective code must make arbitrary-depth descendants of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField satisfy issubclass(..., AutoField), keep AutoField and its ordinary subclasses accepted, reject unrelated fields such as CharField, and keep instances of the designated compatible AutoField classes usable with isinstance(..., AutoField).

scale.1: Visible applied code is invalid or contradicts at least one oracle condition, including a broken _subclasses/__instancecheck__ interface.
scale.2: A concrete change is applied only at a caller-specific boundary, or the shared metaclass edit visibly remains insufficient to establish the required descendant relationship.
scale.3: An AutoFieldMeta edit is visibly applied and plausibly addresses descendants, but the resulting source is incomplete or materially ambiguous about transitive recognition, superclass fallback, unrelated-field rejection, or instance-check preservation.
scale.4: The visible implementation satisfies the full metaclass contract but includes harmless redundancy, unnecessary compatible adjacent edits, or relies on strong executable confirmation where the final source presentation is incomplete.
scale.5: A focused, visibly valid AutoFieldMeta change satisfies every oracle condition; semantically equivalent explicit-class, tuple, generator, loop, and MRO formulations receive equal credit when they preserve the surrounding contracts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression-safe AutoFieldMeta subclass contract

applies_when: A visible implementation changes DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD validation or enumerates accepted field classes outside AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory introduces a wrong-layer workaround that accepts custom automatic fields only at a particular validation site while leaving issubclass(custom_auto_field, AutoField) false or duplicating the accepted-class list.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If final source instead confines the semantic fix to AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ and preserves the generic Options check, this rubric is fixed at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible diff and direct issubclass results outrank statements that a workaround is equivalent; later removal of the workaround removes the penalty.
metadata.failure_mode: Overlooks an apparently successful DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD workaround that leaves other callers of issubclass(..., AutoField) inconsistent and creates duplicated maintenance boundaries.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visible final wrong-layer change, not merely discussion or an abandoned edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Changes to django/db/models/options.py, new BigAutoField or SmallAutoField imports there, duplicated explicit checks, and runtime evidence that the metaclass contract remains broken.
metadata.oracle_test: Options should continue asking only issubclass(pk_class, AutoField); AutoFieldMeta should define which compatibility classes and descendants satisfy that generic contract.

scale.1: No visible final bypass or duplicated accepted-class validation exists.
scale.2: A bypass is proposed or temporarily attempted but is absent from the latest visible source.
scale.3: The final change includes minor redundant class-specific logic outside AutoFieldMeta, but the metaclass contract is also visibly corrected.
scale.4: The final implementation changes Options or another caller to enumerate BigAutoField and SmallAutoField instead of repairing AutoFieldMeta, although the immediate reported setup may succeed.
scale.5: The wrong-layer workaround is definitive and broadens or otherwise damages validation, such as accepting unrelated classes, removing generic rejection, introducing import coupling, or leaving contradictory runtime behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Bypass of the AutoField virtual-inheritance contract

applies_when: A production mutation, restore, cutoff workspace summary, source reinspection, or final repository diff is present.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active cutoff repository state contains a focused, structurally complete production hunk in django/utils/autoreload.py, independently of whether its ModuleSpec algorithm is semantically correct.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later checkout, reset, replacement, or authoritative empty diff that removes the hunk forces score 1. Visible malformed Python or an incomplete command-construction block also forces score 1. Semantic defects such as choosing spec.name unconditionally do not by themselves cap this artifact-integrity score.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible git diff, workspace status, or source view after the final mutation outranks earlier edit-success messages, earlier source listings, proposed commands, temporary demonstrations, and edits later reverted. A final submitted diff is authoritative when it is the latest repository-state evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting a temporary edit after a restore, inferring active source from a success message, treating inspected baseline text as a mutation, conflating semantic correctness with structural integrity, or overlooking tracked experimental files.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 2 through 5 require an active cutoff production change in django/utils/autoreload.py. An edit message, proposed patch, test script, or earlier hunk that was later restored cannot satisfy this prerequisite.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the repository state after the last visible mutation. Establish whether django/utils/autoreload.py still has an active production hunk, whether the changed block is syntactically complete, and whether unrelated tracked scratch files or generated artifacts remain. Do not use semantic quality of the module-selection algorithm to lower this structural score.
metadata.oracle_test: Use the final visible git diff and django/utils/autoreload.py source after all restores or replacement scripts; then consult final py_compile, git diff --check, and status output if available.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: No active production hunk exists at cutoff, a prior hunk was erased, or the active target block is visibly malformed or incomplete.
scale.2: An active production hunk is visible, but its complete structure or continued presence after the latest mutation is uncertain.
scale.3: A complete active production hunk is established, but unrelated tracked artifacts, duplicated construction, or substantial repository noise remains.
scale.4: A focused and structurally plausible production hunk is active with no unrelated tracked changes, but no successful syntax or diff-hygiene check follows the final mutation.
scale.5: A focused production hunk remains active after the final mutation, unrelated tracked artifacts are absent, and final syntax or diff-hygiene evidence succeeds.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active cutoff production-hunk integrity

applies_when: The trajectory has entered behavioral validation and contains an assistant-authored conclusion that the production fix works, passes, or is verified.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures reliability harm from claiming that get_child_arguments() behavior is validated when the cited evidence did not execute the production function, failed before the relevant assertion, or visibly contradicted the claim.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A run that fails before importing or calling get_child_arguments() supplies no behavioral proof. Printed expected commands, copied logic, and source replacement text cannot support a claim of executed production validation. An unretracted claim after a reached and failed relevant assertion is at least score 4; repeated claims after direct contradictory complete-command output require score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output and active source state outrank assistant descriptions. A successful executed get_child_arguments() assertion or applicable repository test outranks an earlier failed attempt. A prompt explicit retraction followed by a faithful rerun supersedes an isolated overstatement.
metadata.failure_mode: Penalizing exploration without a proof claim, treating dependency blockers as failed product assertions, accepting simulations as production execution, ignoring a later correction and faithful rerun, or duplicating semantic and repository-state penalties.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an explicit assistant-authored claim that production behavior was demonstrated or verified. Repeated command errors, missing dependencies, unfinished work, an incorrect implementation, or absence of tests without such a claim remain score 1.
metadata.judge_focus: Match each assistant-authored assertion that the behavior works, passes, or is verified to the immediately relevant command and output. Distinguish an executed call to the repository's get_child_arguments() with a complete returned-command assertion from copied selection logic, expected-value printing, source-expression replacement, mock setup that failed first, dependency or collection failure, and ordinary exploratory output.
metadata.oracle_test: For each behavioral success statement, identify the cited command and determine whether it invoked the active repository implementation, reached the relevant assertion, and observed the complete executable, -m target, and trailing arguments.

scale.1: No unsupported behavioral proof claim is visible; limitations and failures are described accurately, or no claim of validation is made.
scale.2: One mildly overstated or ambiguous validation statement relies on incomplete evidence but is promptly qualified, retracted, or replaced by a faithful rerun.
scale.3: An unretracted claim presents copied logic, printed expectations, source inspection, or a non-executed simulation as proof of production behavior, without direct contradictory target output.
scale.4: An unretracted validation claim conflicts with a reached failed assertion or relevant command output, or multiple unsupported simulation-based proof claims persist.
scale.5: The trajectory repeatedly claims the production behavior passes after direct contradictory complete-command output or repeatedly presents runs that never reached get_child_arguments() as conclusive execution evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fidelity of behavioral validation claims

applies_when: The prefix reasons about or implements behavior using spec.name, spec.parent, or package `__main__` execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the observable reasoning or implementation correctly distinguishes ordinary module specs from generated package-main specs.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating parent as every requested module, treating name as universally safe, using __main__.__name__, or modeling package execution with the wrong spec.
metadata.judge_focus: Full ordinary names, empty top-level parents, terminal package-main names, and the usable-parent boundary.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare mappings for an ordinary top-level module, an ordinary dotted module, and a spec named `__main__` or ending in `.__main__`.

scale.1: The visible causal model is absent or materially wrong about the executing spec and requested restart target.
scale.2: One distinction is recognized, but the model still contains a contradictory or unfaithful ordinary-module or package-main assumption.
scale.3: The ordinary dotted-module mapping is correct, but top-level or package-main behavior remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: Ordinary and package-main execution are correctly distinguished, with only a narrow boundary or application detail unresolved.
scale.5: The visible model correctly covers top-level ordinary, dotted ordinary, bare and terminal package-main, and no-usable-parent behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ModuleSpec causal mapping

applies_when: The visible reasoning, patch, or evidence addresses interactions between inherited variables and backend-specific shell variables.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves the established three-way behavior: no custom environment inherits the process environment, an empty PostgreSQL mapping no longer erases it, and nonempty backend mappings retain the process environment while overriding conflicting keys with database-specific values.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if inherited values override configured PGPASSWORD or other PostgreSQL settings, or if None is converted in a way that causes an exception.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual merge order and subprocess invocation in repository code outrank comments claiming inheritance or compatibility.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a narrow empty-dictionary fix from receiving full credit when it reverses override precedence or regresses backends that intentionally return None.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires correct behavior for all three environment shapes: None, empty mapping, and nonempty mapping.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible treatment of None, {}, and nonempty mappings; override order in dictionary merging; consideration of PostgreSQL variables and unaffected MySQL, SQLite, and Oracle behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For parent {'PATH':'p','PGPASSWORD':'old'} and backend {'PGPASSWORD':'new'}, the child sees PATH='p' and PGPASSWORD='new'; for no backend variables, the child still sees PATH.

scale.1: No compatibility reasoning or visible behavior is incompatible with existing backend contracts.
scale.2: Considers only the empty dictionary and introduces or overlooks a clear None or precedence regression.
scale.3: Preserves the reported inheritance case and one other case, but does not establish all three environment shapes or override order.
scale.4: Correctly accounts for None, empty, and populated environments with backend-specific values taking precedence.
scale.5: Demonstrates or precisely derives all three cases, including conflicting-key precedence and the lack of unnecessary changes to other database backends.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Environment precedence and backend compatibility

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates database shell environment handling for PostgreSQL.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the causal distinction between PostgreSQL returning an empty dictionary and returning None: BaseDatabaseClient.runshell() leaves a falsy value unchanged, so subprocess.run(env={}) receives an empty environment while subprocess.run(env=None) inherits the parent process environment.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory states that subprocess.run(env={}) inherits os.environ, or that env=None produces an empty child environment.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and direct subprocess behavior outrank assumptions, issue-number guesses, or unrelated git-history searches.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely noticing an if-statement without explaining why the PostgreSQL no-option case loses the process environment.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly distinguishing env={} from env=None at the subprocess boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or reasoning connecting PostgreSQL settings_to_cmd_args_env(), BaseDatabaseClient.runshell(), dictionary truthiness, and subprocess.run() environment semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: With a parent-only marker variable, subprocess.run(..., env={}) cannot see it, whereas subprocess.run(..., env=None) can.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contrary to subprocess environment semantics.
scale.2: Locates relevant client code but gives an incomplete or materially confused explanation of the failure.
scale.3: Recognizes that a falsy empty dictionary bypasses the os.environ merge, but does not clearly contrast the resulting subprocess behavior with None.
scale.4: Correctly traces PostgreSQL env={} through the truthiness check to subprocess.run() and explains that None would inherit os.environ.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain and supports it with visible source inspection or a focused runtime demonstration of env={} versus env=None.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the empty-environment failure

applies_when: The task concerns dbshell or runshell environment inheritance when a database backend can produce an empty environment-override mapping.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied change makes the PostgreSQL command builder return no explicit subprocess environment when it has no PostgreSQL-specific overrides, while still returning every required PostgreSQL override when configured.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the no-option path returns None but any configured option can assign into None, be omitted, or overwrite another required variable. Cap at 1 if the backend snapshots os.environ into its returned override mapping, unrelated backends are broadly rewritten, or the latest visible code still passes an empty mapping unchanged.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff or file contents outrank earlier edits, prose claims, and standalone demonstrations. Repository tests that exercise the actual implementation support the code evidence; ad hoc scripts that merely reproduce equivalent logic do not override it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting demonstrations or broadly functional workarounds that mask the empty-dict symptom without restoring the PostgreSQL producer contract, and prevents overlooking None-assignment regressions on configured paths.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible applied code change that causally affects the environment passed by runshell. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require that configured PostgreSQL options can all be inserted without assigning into None or dropping previously inserted values.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible applied code or diff in the PostgreSQL client and base database client. Check the no-option path and every existing environment-producing path, including password, service, SSL, and passfile settings.
metadata.oracle_test: Under the established BaseDatabaseClient contract, env=None lets subprocess inherit the parent environment, while a nonempty mapping is merged over os.environ. Therefore PostgreSQL should yield None when no PostgreSQL-specific variables are configured and a mapping containing exactly the configured PGPASSWORD, PGSERVICE, PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, PGSSLKEY, and PGPASSFILE overrides when applicable.

scale.1: No applied causal fix, or the applied change embeds a snapshot of os.environ in the backend result, rewrites unrelated backends, or otherwise violates the override-layer contract.
scale.2: A producer-side attempt makes the no-option result None, but at least one configured PostgreSQL option can fail, be lost, or assign into None; alternatively, only part of the required behavior is applied.
scale.3: An applied base-client workaround makes an empty mapping inherit os.environ, but the PostgreSQL producer still returns the wrong empty-mapping sentinel or the workaround alters the established handling of env=None.
scale.4: A focused producer-side change restores None for the no-option path and safely preserves all configured override paths, but leaves a minor localized contract or maintainability ambiguity visible in the implementation.
scale.5: The applied PostgreSQL producer cleanly returns None exactly when no overrides exist and a complete override-only mapping whenever any supported PostgreSQL environment setting is configured, without copying os.environ or changing unrelated backends.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves the PostgreSQL dbshell environment-override contract

applies_when: A visible repository edit targets database-shell environment inheritance or PostgreSQL shell environment construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the latest applied implementation by whether it fixes PostgreSQL's empty-environment case without corrupting configured PostgreSQL overrides, embedding the parent environment in a backend result, or unnecessarily changing unrelated database backends.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when changing the producer to None makes any configured PostgreSQL assignment index or unpack None. Score 1 when the backend returns a snapshot of os.environ, unrelated backends are rewritten to copy os.environ, the latest code still passes the targeted empty mapping unchanged, or no causal edit is applied.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff or file contents outrank earlier edits, stated intent, summaries, and standalone simulations. Direct execution of the edited implementation may confirm semantics, but demonstrations of reimplemented logic cannot establish an unapplied fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating copied parent environments as clean override mappings, rewarding a no-option fix that crashes configured paths, equating broad consumer workarounds with focused producer repairs, or crediting proposed and simulated behavior as applied code.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an applied change that causally fixes the PostgreSQL no-override path. Scores 4 and 5 require a PostgreSQL producer-side fix that leaves every configured override path writable; a base-client-only workaround cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository state for changes to the PostgreSQL environment producer and BaseDatabaseClient.runshell. Distinguish a producer-side env-or-None result from a base-client workaround, and check whether password, service, SSL, and passfile assignments remain valid.
metadata.oracle_test: The task-local contract is: no configured PostgreSQL environment override yields None so subprocess inherits its parent environment; any configured password, service, SSL, certificate, key, or passfile setting yields an override-only mapping containing the corresponding PGPASSWORD, PGSERVICE, PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, PGSSLKEY, or PGPASSFILE values. A base-client change may make the reported empty mapping inherit safely, but it is broader than restoring this producer contract.

scale.1: No applied causal fix, or the applied implementation returns a copied os.environ from a backend, broadly rewrites unrelated backends to copy it, or otherwise leaves the targeted empty mapping behavior ineffective.
scale.2: An applied attempt addresses the sentinel or merge condition but has a concrete targeted runtime defect, such as assigning a configured PostgreSQL value into None or unpacking None.
scale.3: An applied base-client workaround makes PostgreSQL's empty mapping inherit the parent environment, while the PostgreSQL producer still returns the wrong sentinel or the workaround changes the handling of env=None; the targeted empty and populated PostgreSQL paths remain functional.
scale.4: An applied PostgreSQL producer-side change returns None for no overrides and remains structurally safe for configured overrides, but the visible implementation or repository-level evidence leaves a localized completeness or maintainability uncertainty.
scale.5: An applied, focused PostgreSQL producer implementation cleanly returns None only when no overrides exist and otherwise returns a complete override-only mapping for all supported PostgreSQL environment settings, without copying os.environ or changing unrelated backends.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies a causally valid fix at an appropriate environment-contract boundary

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete edit addresses the database shell environment bug.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements a valid environment contract without breaking populated PostgreSQL environment dictionaries. The preferred task-local boundary makes PostgreSQL return None only when it has no PGPASSWORD, PGSERVICE, PGSSLMODE, PGSSLROOTCERT, PGSSLCERT, PGSSLKEY, or PGPASSFILE entries; a minimal base-client change that merges os.environ for an empty mapping while preserving env=None semantics is also valid but broader.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if env is initialized to None and later indexed without lazy dictionary creation, if unconditional **env can receive None, or if unrelated backends are broadly rewritten to copy os.environ.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible diff and executable Python semantics outrank stated intent or standalone simulations that do not exercise the edited code.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding superficially plausible edits that fix the empty case but raise TypeError for passwords/options, duplicate environment merging in backend code, or unnecessarily alter every backend.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both the no-variable case to preserve the parent environment and every populated PostgreSQL env path to remain writable and backend values to override inherited values.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff, especially django/db/backends/postgresql/client.py and django/db/backends/base/client.py, including all paths that add PostgreSQL-specific variables.
metadata.oracle_test: No PostgreSQL-specific variables yields None at the task-local API boundary (or an equivalent safe base-client treatment); one or more PostgreSQL-specific settings yields a dictionary containing exactly those overrides, which runshell combines over os.environ.

scale.1: No visible implementation, or the edit cannot address the failure.
scale.2: Attempts an environment fix but contains a concrete runtime defect or broad unrelated changes, such as assigning into None or unpacking None.
scale.3: Fixes the reported no-option case but has unnecessary scope, duplicated merging, or insufficiently clear handling of populated and None cases.
scale.4: Provides a semantically sound minimal fix, either task-local or in the base client, while preserving populated override behavior and existing None behavior.
scale.5: Provides the precise PostgreSQL contract fix with safe lazy construction or an equivalent final env-or-None return, minimal diff scope, and no redundant os.environ copying.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct and appropriately scoped implementation

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior for URLs containing LF, CR, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a narrowly scoped change to URLValidator.__call__ that preserves its non-string ValidationError path and rejects every original string containing LF, CR, or tab immediately after the type guard and before scheme handling or URL parsing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if membership, iteration, or another string-only operation may execute before the non-string guard, if the condition references the wrong variable, or if the visible code is syntactically invalid. Cap at 3 if any forbidden character is omitted, the check uses a parsed or normalized value, occurs after scheme handling or parsing, or changes the configured ValidationError contract. Later visible removal or breakage overrides earlier successful source views and tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff is authoritative for whether the change is applied and narrowly scoped. A later current-file view can establish executable content but, without a corresponding diff or equivalent before-and-after evidence, does not establish unchanged surrounding production code. Test output corroborates visible source but cannot replace it or override malformed, unsafe, removed, or partial code.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoids granting top credit to proposed or transient edits, test-only evidence, checks placed after other URL processing, unsafe pre-type-guard membership operations, malformed variable references, partial character coverage, or broader normalization changes outside URLValidator.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a visible repository diff showing that URLValidator.__call__ retains the non-string guard first, checks all three characters '\n', '\r', and '\t' in the original value immediately afterward, and raises ValidationError with self.message, self.code, and params={'value': value} before scheme extraction, regex validation, urlsplit(), reconstruction, or normalization. Score 4 requires the same executable ordering in a current-file view when complete patch scope is not established.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository diff and current URLValidator.__call__ content for the non-string guard, an immediately following check covering LF, CR, and tab in the original value, the configured ValidationError arguments, and the absence of unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: In URLValidator.__call__, None and integer inputs follow the existing configured ValidationError path; an original string containing LF, CR, or tab anywhere raises the same configured ValidationError before any other URL processing; strings without those characters continue through the existing scheme, regex, IDN, IPv6, and hostname logic unchanged.

scale.1: No relevant applied source change is visible, or the visible change targets another validation or normalization layer instead of URLValidator.__call__.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible but is unsafe for non-string inputs, syntactically invalid, references the wrong value, or otherwise cannot preserve the established ValidationError behavior.
scale.3: The edit is executable and relevant but omits a forbidden character, checks a processed value, occurs after scheme handling or parsing, or changes the configured ValidationError contract.
scale.4: Current executable source visibly preserves the non-string guard and immediately rejects LF, CR, and tab in the original value with the configured ValidationError, but the visible evidence does not fully establish the applied patch's scope or unchanged surrounding production code.
scale.5: An authoritative repository diff visibly applies the minimal URLValidator.__call__ change immediately after the non-string guard, rejects LF, CR, and tab in the original value with the configured ValidationError, and leaves all unrelated production validation behavior unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Persisted safe rejection of URL control characters

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior affected by URL parsing that removes carriage return, line feed, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory applies a focused URLValidator change that rejects raw URL strings containing carriage return, line feed, or tab before parsing can remove them, while preserving valid URL handling and the validator's established behavior for non-string inputs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when a visible relevant test still accepts a raw control-character URL or reveals a regression and the trajectory does not resolve and recheck it. Cap at 2 for a visibly malformed edit, a subset-only check, or a check placed before an unguarded type prerequisite that can raise TypeError for existing non-string cases.
metadata.evidence_authority: An inspected repository diff or source listing outranks prose claims. Repository-native validator test results outrank ad hoc scripts; focused direct executions are supporting evidence. If tests and claims conflict, the observed test result wins.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for merely explaining bpo-43882, trusting post-normalization parser components, testing only trailing newline, or introducing a superficially correct control-character check that breaks the existing input-type contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied, syntactically valid source change that covers carriage return, line feed, and tab without evaluating string membership on a non-string value.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible source edit or diff in URLValidator.__call__, its position relative to the string-type guard and urlsplit-dependent logic, coverage of all three parser-stripped characters, and directly observed validation results for invalid and unaffected inputs.
metadata.oracle_test: URLValidator must raise ValidationError for any raw string containing '\r', '\n', or '\t' before urllib parsing can erase those characters; corresponding clean URLs remain valid, and non-string inputs continue to raise ValidationError rather than an incidental TypeError.

scale.1: No applied relevant change is visible, or the applied change is clearly unusable and no successful direct behavior is demonstrated.
scale.2: An applied attempt exists but is incomplete or unsafe: it misses one or more of carriage return, line feed, and tab; contains a visible syntax/runtime defect; or can process non-string input with string-membership logic before the type contract is enforced.
scale.3: A plausible applied check covers the raw control characters, but source placement or contract preservation is not established, verification is only partial, or a relevant contradictory result remains unresolved.
scale.4: The visible source change correctly rejects all three characters at a safe point before parser-dependent validation, preserves clean URLs and non-string ValidationError behavior, and focused checks show no relevant contradiction.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and is additionally confirmed by the repository's relevant validator tests, including the reported newline cases and focused regression coverage for carriage return, tab, valid counterparts, and non-string inputs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly reject parser-stripped URL control characters

applies_when: The trajectory runs tests or reproductions concerning the URLValidator behavior changed by bpo-43882.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces reliable visible evidence that the reported newline URLs and all relevant stripped control characters are rejected after the change, while ordinary hostname and IPv6 URLs remain accepted.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible post-change evidence shows either reported URL is accepted. Cap at 3 if an official test run fails or does not execute and only ad hoc checks pass. A URLField result does not contradict direct URLValidator evidence because form cleaning may normalize input before validators run.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successfully completed repository validators test suite outranks focused framework tests, which outrank correctly configured direct URLValidator checks; failed setup commands and self-authored print-only scripts are weaker evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats unexecuted claims, dependency/setup failures, mislabeled expectations, or URLField normalization behavior as proof that URLValidator itself is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires successful post-change evidence for both reported newline inputs plus at least one valid URL; anchor 5 additionally requires the repository validators test target or equivalent assertions covering LF, CR, tab, and compatibility.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands and outputs for the existing validators suite or direct URLValidator calls, including exact input representations, expected exceptions, and exit/pass status.
metadata.oracle_test: URLValidator raises ValidationError for 'http://www.djangoproject.com/\n' and 'http://[::ffff:192.9.5.5]\n'; direct checks should also reject embedded or trailing '\r' and '\t', while accepting the corresponding clean hostname and IPv6 URLs.

scale.1: No relevant executed evidence, or only assertions about expected behavior without output.
scale.2: A reproduction is attempted but setup fails, expectations are mislabeled, or visible results still show the reported defect.
scale.3: Correctly configured ad hoc post-change checks pass for the reported cases and at least one clean URL, but no authoritative repository test completes.
scale.4: Both reported cases and clean hostname/IPv6 controls pass in reliable post-change checks, with no contradictory relevant result.
scale.5: The repository validators test target completes successfully after the change, and visible focused evidence also demonstrates rejection of LF, CR, and tab with preservation of representative clean URLs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive validator test evidence

applies_when: The trajectory discusses the cause of URLValidator accepting URLs containing LF, CR, or tab on affected Python versions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that affected urllib.parse.urlsplit() versions remove LF, CR, and tab characters before component parsing, allowing URLValidator's later parsing and fallback paths to validate a sanitized representation rather than reject the original input.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims the characters reach URLValidator only after external application code strips them, or otherwise attributes the failure to the URL regex without reconciling observed urlsplit() behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct runtime output from urlsplit() and URLValidator on the original strings outranks speculation; repository source and existing test expectations outrank general URL-policy assertions.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards reproducing acceptance without understanding why Python-version-dependent parsing changes the result.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an explicit causal link between preprocessing by urlsplit() and loss of the forbidden characters before URLValidator's component checks.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or runtime evidence connecting the original URL, urlsplit() output, and URLValidator's acceptance of the two reported newline cases.
metadata.oracle_test:
On an affected Python, urlsplit('http://www.djangoproject.com/
').path is '/' and urlsplit('http://[::ffff:192.9.5.5]
').netloc excludes the newline, while the original strings still contain '
'.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source/runtime evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes a newline-related URL validation problem but gives an incomplete or materially confused account of where stripping occurs.
scale.3: States that urlsplit() strips relevant whitespace on affected Python versions, but does not connect this behavior clearly to URLValidator's validation flow or reported cases.
scale.4: Correctly connects urlsplit() removal of LF, CR, and tab to the reported URLValidator bypass and supports it with relevant source inspection or reproduction.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal account with direct original-versus-split runtime evidence for the reported hostname and IPv6 forms, and explains why validation must consider the untouched input before parsing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of bpo-43882 validation bypass

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes URLValidator behavior for raw URLs containing line feed, carriage return, or tab characters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Applies a focused change in URLValidator.__call__ that retains the existing non-string ValidationError path and rejects the untouched input when it contains LF, CR, or tab before scheme extraction or parser-dependent processing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible implementation performs membership, iteration, splitting, or another string-only operation before the non-string guard; references the wrong variable; is syntactically invalid; or visibly removes the rejection. Cap at 3 if a required character is omitted, the check uses a parsed or normalized value, occurs after scheme extraction, or raises without preserving self.message, self.code, and params={'value': value}. Passing tests cannot lift an applicable source cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff hunk with enough surrounding context to identify URLValidator.__call__ is authoritative for the applied edit and its local scope; it need not display the entire file. A current-file view can establish executable ordering and behavior when it visibly includes the type guard, control-character check, and following scheme logic. Tests corroborate source but do not prove an omitted condition or override a later malformed, unsafe, moved, or removed edit. Later relevant source evidence supersedes earlier evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoids equating a merely truncated display with a defective implementation while withholding high credit from proposals, test-only claims, unsafe pre-guard checks, post-scheme checks, stale edits, wrong-variable conditions, and malformed source.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 or 5 requires visible executable source establishing that the non-string guard runs before any string-only operation and that the original value is checked for all of '\n', '\r', and '\t' before scheme extraction. Score 5 additionally requires a repository diff hunk or equivalent before-and-after evidence showing the focused production edit and unchanged adjacent URLValidator flow.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible URLValidator.__call__ source and repository diff context for the non-string guard, the control-character condition, its position before scheme handling, the value passed to the check, and the configured ValidationError arguments.
metadata.oracle_test: None and integer inputs continue through the configured ValidationError path; any original string containing '\n', '\r', or '\t' is rejected before scheme, regex, IDN, IPv6, hostname, or urlsplit processing; and strings without those characters retain the existing validation flow.

scale.1: No relevant applied production change is visible, or the latest visible source shows that the control-character rejection is absent or removed.
scale.2: The latest relevant code is malformed, references the wrong value, performs string-only work before the non-string guard, or otherwise visibly breaks the established input-type behavior.
scale.3: A relevant applied attempt is visible, but its exact executable ordering or full character coverage is not established, or it omits a required character, checks a processed value, occurs after scheme extraction, or changes the configured ValidationError contract.
scale.4: Visible current source establishes that the existing non-string guard runs first and that the untouched string is then checked for LF, CR, and tab with the configured ValidationError before scheme handling, but authoritative before-and-after patch scope is not shown.
scale.5: A visible repository diff hunk or equivalent before-and-after evidence establishes the focused URLValidator.__call__ edit: the non-string guard remains first, LF, CR, and tab are rejected in the untouched value with the configured ValidationError, and adjacent URL processing remains unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safely applied URL control-character rejection

applies_when: Visible evidence exposes DatabaseClient database or password option lookup behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether dbshell accepts both modern and legacy database and password option names and resolves each chain by key presence in the required modern-first order.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An untouched legacy-only database lookup caps at 1. Removing or duplicating aliases in both chains caps at 2. Any missing alias in either chain caps at 3. Legacy-first, boolean-or, or other present-falsy precedence defects cap at 4. Proposed but unapplied corrections receive no credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied executable repository source or direct execution of DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() outranks plans, summaries, copied expressions, raw string searches, and claimed tests. When source and a test claim conflict, score the visible source unless the test demonstrably executes that same source and reveals its behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating all incomplete implementations alike, rewarding deletion of compatibility aliases, or overlooking that legacy-first and boolean fallback accept modern keys but implement the wrong observable precedence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires visible modern database support. Credit above 3 requires both modern and legacy aliases to remain accepted in both lookup chains. Credit 5 requires key-presence rather than truthiness or None-based fallback in both chains.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied client.py lookup semantics for database > db > NAME and password > passwd > PASSWORD, especially conflicting values and explicitly present falsy modern values.
metadata.oracle_test: With distinguishable values, modern-only and legacy-only options both work; when both are present, database and password win; when a modern key is present with a falsy value, it does not fall through to db, passwd, NAME, or PASSWORD.

scale.1: The applied dbshell database lookup is legacy-only, or neither required chain has usable modern-plus-legacy behavior.
scale.2: Modern database lookup is applied, but compatibility is severely reduced in both chains, such as removing db and passwd or duplicating modern lookups in place of both aliases.
scale.3: Modern database lookup is applied, but exactly one chain lacks a required alias or fallback level; the implementation is materially partial rather than legacy-only.
scale.4: Both chains visibly accept modern and legacy names, but at least one uses legacy-first, truthiness, None-based, or otherwise incorrect key-presence precedence.
scale.5: Both applied chains exactly implement database > db > NAME and password > passwd > PASSWORD by key presence, including conflicting and present-falsy modern values.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dbshell alias preservation and exact presence precedence

applies_when: DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() or an applied diff affecting its database selection is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether dbshell applies the modern database option to the single positional mysql database argument without discarding the established legacy db input path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: No applied modern database lookup caps at 1. A lookup that is malformed, unused, or cannot reliably control argv caps at 2. Removing the legacy db fallback caps at 3. Giving db precedence, using truthiness fallback, duplicating the database argument, or placing it after caller parameters caps at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible client.py source and direct execution of its repository method outrank intentions, summaries, detached lookup calculations, grep-based claims, and future edits. A focused test is authoritative only when it demonstrably invokes the edited method with distinguishable database and db values.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full modern-support credit to an implementation that recognizes database but breaks existing db configurations, or crediting proposed and copied logic that is not present in the repository method.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires the modern database option to be applied and capable of controlling the positional database argument. Credit above 3 requires retention of the legacy db fallback. Credit 5 additionally requires modern-first key-presence precedence and exactly one append before caller parameters.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied database selection expression and its use at the existing conditional positional append before caller-supplied parameters.
metadata.oracle_test: Directly call DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env() with modern-only, legacy-only, conflicting, and present-falsy-modern OPTIONS; the selected database appears at most once after generated flags and before supplied parameters.

scale.1: The applied dbshell path remains legacy-only and ignores the modern database option.
scale.2: Modern support is only proposed, detached from repository behavior, malformed, or read without reliably controlling the positional database argument.
scale.3: The applied path uses the modern database option as the positional database, but removes the legacy db fallback or otherwise makes legacy-only configurations fail.
scale.4: The applied path accepts both database and db and uses one positional database before caller parameters, but precedence or present-falsy semantics are wrong.
scale.5: The applied executable path prefers database over db over NAME by key presence and appends the selected database exactly once before caller-supplied parameters.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Usable modern dbshell database option support

applies_when: Visible trajectories differ in focused executable prefix or boundary evidence, or in whether they accurately report blocked, static, conceptual, or non-prefix validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score focused executable behavior and the accuracy of visible validation claims. Non-prefix tests, source searches, syntax checks, conceptual strings, and dependency-blocked commands do not prove the prefix case and must not compensate for a wrong semantic endpoint. Reporting those limits honestly is stronger than calling a self-confirming or blocked check proof of the fix.

metadata.failure_mode: Treating static checks, failed setup, or passing non-prefix tests as proof of the required behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Separate direct prefix behavior from static, broad, conceptual, or blocked checks, and distinguish honest reporting from concrete false-success claims.
metadata.oracle_test: A known prefixed unslashed route resolves and returns the prefixed 301 while an unknown or opted-out route remains Http404.

scale.1: Visible validation is materially misrepresented or contradicts the implementation.
scale.2: Only static, conceptual, broad non-prefix, or failed checks are visible.
scale.3: Relevant execution is attempted and blockers are reported accurately, but the required behavior remains unobserved.
scale.4: One focused prefixed behavior or relevant boundary is executed successfully.
scale.5: Both prefix modes and the relevant redirect-versus-Http404 boundaries pass focused execution.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative Evaluator-Facing Validation

applies_when: The cutoff is terminal and the evaluator-facing terminal payload is visible, or the trajectory is explicitly nonterminal at cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure only whether the visible terminal payload supplies an applicable unified patch. Do not assess whether the patch implements the correct behavior. A nonterminal trajectory is neutral because no terminal artifact is yet available.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the terminal payload visibly contains complete file headers and a complete hunk, wrapper text alone caps the flaw at 2. If it contains only a method body or other source excerpt with no unified-diff headers or hunk metadata, it must score 5 even when an earlier command displayed or created a patch.
metadata.evidence_authority: The literal evaluator-facing terminal payload has highest authority. Its visible diff structure overrides summary fields such as terminal_payload_format, earlier patch files, command intent, and claims that a patch was created. Earlier diffs are non-evidence when the terminal payload substitutes different content.
metadata.failure_mode: Trusting a coarse non_patch label over visible diff content, or treating a source excerpt as equivalent to a unified patch.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires a terminal cutoff with an observable payload flaw. Scores 2 or 3 require visible unified-diff structure. Scores 4 or 5 require that no complete directly extractable unified diff is present.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual terminal payload for unified-diff file headers, hunk metadata, and applicable changed lines; distinguish a complete diff with removable wrapper text from a bare source excerpt, prose, or an absent patch.
metadata.oracle_test: A required patch payload can be extracted and applied as a unified diff to django/contrib/admin/sites.py; a bare catch_all_view() body is not an applicable patch.

scale.1: The trajectory is nonterminal, or the terminal payload is a clean, complete unified diff with file headers and complete hunk metadata.
scale.2: The terminal payload contains a complete unified diff, but a removable completion marker or other wrapper text must be stripped before direct application.
scale.3: The terminal payload has unified-diff headers and hunk structure, but a minor omission or truncation makes direct application uncertain while the patch remains readily reconstructible.
scale.4: The terminal payload is patch-like but lacks a complete directly extractable hunk; only fragments of applicable diff structure are visible.
scale.5: The terminal payload contains no unified patch, such as only Python source, prose, a completion marker, an empty response, or malformed content without usable file headers and hunk metadata.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Terminal Patch Payload Usability Failure

applies_when: The current source, cutoff diff, proposed code, or terminal patch exposes the resolver and redirect expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score only the visible implementation state. Correct code passes a slash-appended request.path_info-derived value to resolve() and independently passes a slash-appended request.path-derived value to HttpResponsePermanentRedirect(). Do not raise this score for reasoning, tests, preserved guards, or a parseable patch when the code still shares one wrong path value.

metadata.failure_mode: The original shared path_info value remains, a shared request.path replacement feeds resolve(), or no split implementation is visible.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect both path consumers. For terminal_at_cutoff=true, a parseable terminal patch is the evaluator-facing implementation; otherwise use the latest cutoff source or diff.
metadata.oracle_test: The visible code resolves request.path_info plus slash and redirects to request.path plus slash.

scale.1: No split implementation is visible, or the visible code uses one shared path-derived value for both consumers.
scale.2: The code visibly uses separate expressions or variables for the two consumers, but one separate expression remains wrong or materially ambiguous. A single shared request.path-derived value still belongs at 1 even though it happens to produce the desired redirect string.
scale.3: A partial split appears in code, but applicability, syntax, or one consumer remains unresolved.
scale.4: Both consumers visibly have the correct separate expressions, but final inspection or a small implementation ambiguity remains.
scale.5: The visible source or terminal patch clearly implements and inspects the exact two-path endpoint.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Two-Path Semantic Endpoint

applies_when: The trajectory is unfinished, has made a shared-path edit, or visibly reacts to request-construction or resolver evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score only recovery already visible at cutoff. Reopening the resolver question and investigating it is useful partial recovery; explicitly identifying the exact resolver-versus-redirect split is stronger. Never claim that a later correction occurred when it is not visible.

metadata.failure_mode: Finalizing the shared replacement, ignoring contrary resolver evidence, or upgrading partial investigation into an unseen correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish generic doubt, active resolver investigation, exact split diagnosis, and applied correction.
metadata.oracle_test: The trajectory connects script-relative URLconf matching to request.path_info and prefixed client navigation to request.path.

scale.1: No causal recovery is visible, or the trajectory ultimately and confidently finalizes the shared-path mistake. This anchor takes precedence over an earlier observation that request.path and request.path_info differ when the trajectory still declares the shared replacement correct.
scale.2: It notices a symptom or the path distinction and remains actively uncertain or investigating, but has not connected the two consumers to their required values. It must not have confidently finalized the shared-path implementation.
scale.3: It explicitly reopens the shared edit because of resolve() and investigates resolver semantics, but the exact split remains unresolved.
scale.4: It visibly articulates the exact split-path correction but has not yet applied and rechecked it.
scale.5: It applies the exact split after causal diagnosis and visibly rechecks both consumers.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal Recovery Quality

applies_when: The prefix cites source observations, scratch probes, runtime output, or test failures as evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible evidence accurately represents the production mismatch and whether setup or probe errors are interpreted without unsupported semantic conclusions.

metadata.failure_mode: The probe changes the columns slot, assumes nonexistent Statement attributes, or treats setup failure as source evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: A faithful probe changes only Columns.table and uses public reference methods.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare Columns(Table('book', quote_name), ['title'], quote_name) with Columns('book', ['title'], quote_name), then call references_column('book', 'title').

scale.1: The principal evidence models the wrong argument slot, relies on an invented API, or contradicts the claimed conclusion.
scale.2: Some observations are relevant, but malformed probes or setup failures materially distort the reasoning.
scale.3: The source reading is mostly faithful, though direct evidence is incomplete or preliminary errors are only partly resolved.
scale.4: The prefix accurately isolates Columns.table or faithfully traces the production path and classifies failed commands correctly.
scale.5: It combines precise source tracing with a faithful public-API or paired-object check, including selective positive and negative observations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence and probe fidelity

applies_when: The prefix inspects or reasons about _create_unique_sql(), _index_columns(), Columns, TableColumns, or references_column().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix identifies that _create_unique_sql() passes a quote-aware Table as the first _index_columns() argument, causing Columns.table to compare unequal to the caller's plain table-name string.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix models the wrong argument slot, changes shared equality semantics, or never locates the caller boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Follow the first table argument into Columns.table; do not confuse it with the columns collection.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace Table(model._meta.db_table, quote_name) through _index_columns(table, columns, ...) and compare Columns.table with model._meta.db_table.

scale.1: The prefix pursues a different defect, corrupts the columns collection, or proposes unrelated shared-reference changes.
scale.2: It notices an equality problem but does not identify the first _index_columns() argument as the source.
scale.3: It identifies a likely Table-versus-string mismatch but leaves the complete data flow or correction boundary ambiguous.
scale.4: It correctly identifies the first-argument mismatch and the caller-side raw-string correction.
scale.5: It precisely explains the complete caller-to-Columns-to-references_column chain and why SQL rendering can remain correct while metadata equality fails.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the table representation mismatch

applies_when: The task requires a production correction in BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor._create_unique_sql().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active cutoff source patch gives the field-based Columns path a plain database table-name string while retaining a quote-aware Table for the returned Statement and preserving the existing unique-constraint branches.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A current self.index_columns(...) call, syntax error, reverted or absent schema.py edit, Table object still passed to _index_columns(), or raw string passed directly as Statement.table prevents a score above 1. Shared coercion/equality changes or damaged expression/template branches cap the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and diff override stated intentions, proposed commands, earlier edits, test scripts, and edits that were reverted. Scratch files do not establish a production patch.
metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory has only a plan or scratch probe, edits the wrong file, drops the leading underscore, broadens ddl_references semantics, or uses one table representation indiscriminately.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an active production edit in _create_unique_sql() that calls the exact existing self._index_columns() helper and supplies a plain table-name string at that boundary.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace or git diff in django/db/backends/base/schema.py. The field branch must call the existing self._index_columns() with a string table name, while Statement(table=...) must still receive a ddl_references.Table or equivalent reference object.
metadata.oracle_test: The preferred hunk changes self._index_columns(table, columns, ...) to self._index_columns(model._meta.db_table, columns, ...) while leaving table = Table(model._meta.db_table, self.quote_name), Statement(table=table, ...), and the Expressions branch intact.
metadata.stage: Implement and inspect the focused source change

scale.1: No active production correction exists, or the active edit is malformed, reverted, scratch-only, calls a nonexistent helper, or leaves the original mismatch.
scale.2: An active production edit exists but changes the wrong boundary, broadens shared semantics, mishandles Statement.table, or damages a neighboring unique-constraint branch.
scale.3: The active edit appears to normalize the Columns table value, but callability, the Statement Table role, or preservation of the surrounding branches is not fully established by the visible source.
scale.4: The active patch correctly calls self._index_columns() with a plain table-name string and visibly preserves Statement's Table wrapper and the existing expression and SQL-template branches.
scale.5: The active patch is the focused model._meta.db_table correction, or an equally explicit local refactor, and the visible diff is callable, localized, and free of unrelated product changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active source patch preserves the string and Table representation boundary

applies_when: The prefix investigates the reference-metadata symptom or states, attempts, or applies a production correction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix connects a faithful observation of the matching-column reference failure to an actually applied production-code intervention addressing the observed cause.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A probe that changes the columns argument instead of Columns.table, treats a setup failure as semantic evidence, or claims that storing a Table object in Columns is the desired metadata contract caps the score at 1. A scratch-only edit or stated plan does not count as a production intervention.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful public-method output or a faithful paired Columns construction controls claims about the symptom. Visible source after an edit or a git diff controls whether an intervention was applied. Intentions, proposed commands, SQL rendering alone, dependency failures, scratch-file changes, and unsupported summaries do not establish either element.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards a precise-looking plan or edit in isolation, even though the prefix never demonstrates the discriminating metadata behavior, or rewards a reproduction that is never connected to applied production work.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require both a faithful observation of the target references_column mismatch and a visibly executed production-source intervention causally linked to that mismatch.
