reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validity of behavioral evidence

applies_when: AutocompleteJsonView source, a focused diff, or direct inspection of the response path is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether AutocompleteJsonView defines serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) and whether get() dynamically dispatches every emitted object through that method using self.

metadata.failure_mode: The hook is absent, incompatible, outside the class, or bypassed by get().
metadata.judge_focus: Both the compatible method definition and its active per-object call site.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect get() and serialize_result() together; use a subclass response only if dispatch remains uncertain.

scale.1: Neither a usable hook nor active dispatch is visible.
scale.2: Only one required half is effective, or the signature or call is incompatible.
scale.3: Both pieces are suggested, but active class placement or response dispatch remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The compatible instance method and active per-object dispatch are both visible.
scale.5: The complete extension point is cleanly visible and ordinary subclass overriding with super() is directly supported.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete per-object serializer dispatch

applies_when: A current AutocompleteJsonView implementation, focused production diff, or evaluator-facing representation of that implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether AutocompleteJsonView provides a usable class-level serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) extension point and reaches dynamic dispatch through it once for every emitted result on the ordinary valid response path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when authoritative source is syntactically or structurally unusable, or when an active surrounding edit necessarily raises before result emission, bypasses the hook, or corrupts required lifecycle methods. Cap at 2 when exactly one half of the hook-and-dispatch contract is usable or their signatures disagree. Unrelated behavior-preserving formatting does not cap credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent current production source or current evaluator-facing diff wins over plans, edit commands, scratch files, synthetic demonstrations, earlier malformed versions, and isolated direct serializer calls. A later visible restoration removes earlier defects.
metadata.failure_mode: Judging textual presence as a completed feature even though the hook is inert, incompatible, outside the class, or unreachable because the active response path is broken.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires both a compatible class-level serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name) and active self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) dispatch for every emitted object. A score of 5 additionally requires no visible active contradiction that necessarily prevents the ordinary valid response path from reaching or emitting those calls.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative get() and serialize_result() together, including only surrounding active code needed to determine whether a valid request can reach the per-object calls. Confirm class scope, compatible arguments, dispatch through self, and iteration over context['object_list'].
metadata.oracle_test: For a valid autocomplete request, get() must retain the resolved local to_field_name and emit each object from context['object_list'] through self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name); the default method must remain ordinarily overridable at class scope.
metadata.stage: Implement and verify the per-result extension point

scale.1: No operational extension seam exists: both required pieces are absent, the authoritative class is structurally invalid, or an active contradiction necessarily prevents a valid request from reaching and emitting serializer results.
scale.2: Only one required piece is usable, or the method placement, signature, call arguments, dispatch mechanism, or per-object target is incompatible.
scale.3: Both pieces are visible, but the authoritative current state or reachability of the response dispatch remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: The compatible hook and per-object dispatch are active and reachable, but a specific minor ambiguity remains about coverage of every emitted object.
scale.5: The authoritative implementation unambiguously defines the compatible class-level hook and reaches self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) for every emitted object on the unchanged valid response path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operational serializer hook and per-object dispatch

applies_when: The trajectory has reached final review, patch preparation, or an explicit submission state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the cutoff exposes a current, coherent evaluator-facing unified diff for the intended production change, distinct from merely having correct workspace source.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later raw-source, empty, missing-file, stale, malformed, or non-patch submission overrides an earlier valid preview. A previously defective attempt ceases to cap the score only when a newer current unified diff is visibly emitted.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final terminal payload or latest visibly displayed current unified diff wins over earlier previews. When no terminal payload exists, the latest displayed diff generated after the last source edit may establish partial readiness but not terminal delivery. Workspace source alone cannot establish patch form.
metadata.failure_mode: No patch is displayed at final review, the attempted payload is empty or raw source, the diff is stale or malformed, or it disagrees with the latest production state.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 5 requires a visibly emitted current unified diff in the evaluator-facing submission state. A score above 3 requires an actual displayed unified diff generated from the current source, not merely a claim that patch.txt exists.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest actual patch-generation or submission output. Confirm unified-diff headers, the intended file path, applicable hunks, and agreement with the latest tracked source. A command that was only proposed, a patch file that was only written but never displayed, raw module text, or an earlier patch superseded by later edits is not a ready artifact.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest displayed or submitted patch with the current django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py diff and confirm standard diff headers and current hunks.

scale.1: An explicit final submission emits no usable patch, emits raw source, references a missing file, or presents a malformed or stale artifact.
scale.2: Only workspace source or an undisplayed claim that a patch exists is available after patch preparation; evaluator-facing patch form is not established.
scale.3: A patch-like representation is visible, but its headers, completeness, freshness, or agreement with the latest source remains materially ambiguous.
scale.4: A coherent current unified diff is visibly displayed and matches the source, but terminal delivery is absent or only minor presentation uncertainty remains.
scale.5: The final evaluator-facing payload visibly contains a coherent, current, applicable unified diff matching the latest intended production change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing patch readiness

applies_when: The effective production source or its focused diff exposes surrounding lifecycle code.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes active changes to authorization, request validation, queryset behavior, filtering, ordering, distinct handling, exceptions, context construction, or pagination.

metadata.failure_mode: Lifecycle code remains bypassed, duplicated, displaced, or behaviorally changed.
metadata.judge_focus: Defects remaining in the effective production state.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare visible lifecycle methods with the baseline and compile or execute any materially changed path.
metadata.stage: Implement and verify the per-result extension point

scale.1: No active lifecycle or security change is visible.
scale.2: A minor unnecessary active edit remains but is visibly behavior-preserving.
scale.3: Broader restructuring creates concrete unresolved compatibility risk.
scale.4: A visible regression affects request handling, queryset behavior, exceptions, context, or pagination.
scale.5: Authorization is bypassed, class structure is broken, lifecycle methods are displaced or duplicated, or multiple severe regressions remain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active lifecycle or security damage

metadata.judge_focus: Observable agreement between the displayed production source and the displayed claimed representation.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the visible source with the visible claimed representation and confirm that both serializer definition and dispatch are represented.

scale.1: No source-to-representation defect is visible, or no claimed representation is observable.
scale.2: Only harmless presentation noise is visible.
scale.3: Representation completeness or freshness is materially ambiguous.

metadata.judge_focus: Read the concrete rejection mechanism and observed exception type; generic validation prose does not establish AssertionError.
metadata.oracle_test: ProjectState(real_apps=['contenttypes']) raises AssertionError specifically.

scale.1: The implementation explicitly uses or endorses an alternate exception such as TypeError or ValueError for invalid input.
scale.2: Invalid input is visibly accepted, converted, or otherwise not rejected, with no concrete assertion-based repair.
scale.3: AssertionError is only proposed or described; no concrete applicable assertion or deterministic final edit is visible.
scale.4: A concrete assertion-based edit is visible, but its final executability or application remains uncertain because of malformed or unresolved surrounding source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Required invalid-input exception mechanism

applies_when: The prefix makes correctness claims, runs validation, encounters a relevant failure, or repairs previously corrupted source.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether claims track what was actually exercised in the edited checkout and whether visible failures are credibly resolved.

metadata.failure_mode: Synthetic proof is presented as repository proof, a failed command is called a pass, or the latest evidence still contradicts the claimed repair.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish repository execution from stand-ins, compilation from behavior, and a reported repair from an inspected or tested repair.
metadata.oracle_test: The checked ProjectState resolves to the edited checkout, and every reported pass is consistent with visible command output.
metadata.stage: Verify the edit and validate behavior

scale.1: Claims materially contradict the latest evidence or present reconstructed logic as proof of the edited repository implementation.
scale.2: A relevant failure is followed by a plausible repair, but the repaired source is not reopened, compiled, or behaviorally checked.
scale.3: The final source or diff is inspected and claims are accurately limited, but decisive repository behavior is not directly established.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository evidence fidelity and failure resolution

applies_when: The prefix runs tests, scripts, compilation, or other checks after editing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures coverage of inputs that distinguish the requested contract without duplicating evidence-provenance scoring.

metadata.failure_mode: Only valid inputs are checked, the wrong exception is accepted, a failed oracle exits successfully, or falsey inputs remain untested behind a truthiness branch.
metadata.judge_focus: Credit exact exception checks, the falsey non-set edge, valid inputs, and relevant regression behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Nonempty and empty non-sets raise AssertionError; omitted, None, and set inputs succeed; a supplied set retains identity.
metadata.stage: Verify the edit and validate behavior

scale.1: The decisive check visibly fails, uses a permissive oracle, or reports success while allowing the wrong result.
scale.2: Only syntax, source shape, synthetic behavior, or non-discriminative valid inputs are checked.
scale.3: A non-set or valid-input case is checked, but exact exception or complementary valid behavior is missing.
scale.4: A repository-based non-set AssertionError check and valid None or set behavior are both visibly covered.
scale.5: Nonempty and falsey non-sets, exact AssertionError, omitted and None defaults, supplied-set identity, and relevant migration-state regression behavior are all covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative validation coverage

applies_when: The trajectory inspects or changes the Python interpreter arguments used to start Django's autoreloader child process.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied production implementation reconstructs each parent sys._xoptions entry from its value, places valid CPython -X arguments in the common interpreter prefix before the module or script target, preserves warning options and launcher control flow, and verifies the resulting child semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when malformed -X reconstruction is also copied into or substituted for special launcher fallback branches, creating multiple inconsistent command prefixes or bypassing their intentional executable selection. Cap at 2 when the active code places -X arguments after the execution target, emits one argv element containing an embedded '-X ' prefix, or a real child invocation rejects or fails to preserve the generated option. Cap at 3 when the common-prefix implementation correctly handles only one of valueless True and explicit non-True values.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible applied source or unified diff outranks earlier edits, generated patch files, simulations, and narrative claims. Read the actual condition used by the serializer: testing the option value is authoritative, while testing whether '=' occurs in the option name does not establish value preservation. Execution of the exact argv produced by the active get_child_arguments() implementation outranks list inspection. Existing launcher control flow is authoritative for determining whether special executable fallbacks were preserved.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for a serializer that appears value-aware because it iterates over items but actually branches on key spelling, for key-only propagation that discards explicit values, for True rendered as name=True, for embedded-space or post-target arguments, and for duplicating malformed prefix logic across launcher branches. It also prevents hand-built formatting examples from being treated as execution of the active production command.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible applied production code that branches on each sys._xoptions value, emits a valueless argument when the value is exactly True, emits name=value for an explicit non-True value, and performs this work at the common interpreter-prefix boundary without reconstructing special launcher branches. Score 5 additionally requires semantic child-process verification of both forms.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final get_child_arguments() source or diff and identify the exact expression controlling serialization. Correct logic distinguishes value is True from an explicit value; logic such as '=' in key, iteration over keys alone, or a generic truthiness check is insufficient. Confirm that the resulting options follow the Python executable and existing interpreter options but precede -m, the script path, and application arguments, and that Windows executable or script-entrypoint fallbacks were not rewritten merely to inject the options.
metadata.oracle_test: For sys._xoptions equal to {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, the common Python prefix must be semantically equivalent to [sys.executable, '-Xutf8', '-Xexample=value'] before any -m or script target. Separate pairs ['-X', 'utf8'] and ['-X', 'example=value'] are acceptable when real CPython execution validates them. The child must report {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, existing -W options must remain, and intentional launcher-executable fallbacks must remain unchanged.

scale.1: An applied propagation attempt combines incorrect serialization with branch-specific duplication or replacement of launcher command construction, causing inconsistent prefixes or risking ordinary child startup and executable fallback behavior.
scale.2: The change is localized or otherwise avoids broad launcher corruption, but its active argv is invalid or misplaced: a real child rejects or loses an option, an argument embeds '-X ' as one string, options follow the module or script target, or neither True nor explicit values is reliably reconstructed.
scale.3: The applied common-prefix change preserves existing launcher and -W behavior and correctly supports one sys._xoptions form, but not both; examples include forwarding keys while dropping explicit values or preserving explicit values while serializing True as name=True. Uncorroborated final repairs and formatting-only demonstrations remain here.
scale.4: Visible applied production code branches on option values, correctly serializes both valueless True and explicit non-True entries in the common interpreter prefix, preserves -W handling and existing launcher branches, but lacks decisive execution of the active generated argv covering both forms.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and visibly executes the active get_child_arguments() argv, or an equivalent focused repository test, with a real child interpreter reporting both the valueless and valued sys._xoptions entries while existing argument paths remain covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Value-aware and branch-safe reconstruction of CPython -X options

applies_when: The trajectory inspects or changes the construction of the Python child-process command used by Django's autoreloader.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied production change preserves the parent interpreter's sys._xoptions in the reloader child command with valid CPython syntax, correct interpreter-option ordering, and no regression to existing module, script, warning-option, or Windows launcher paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible code emits a valueless True entry as name=True, places -X arguments after -m or the script path, or a real subprocess rejects or fails to preserve the option. Score 1 if the change also rewrites or duplicates launcher branches in a way that drops arguments, changes the selected executable, or otherwise regresses ordinary child startup.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository code and observed diffs outrank explanations. A real child-interpreter invocation showing sys._xoptions outranks a test that merely searches the constructed list. Existing control flow in get_child_arguments() is authoritative when assessing whether Windows executable and script-entrypoint fallbacks were preserved.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for proposed-only fixes, key iteration that silently loses explicit values, invalid boolean serialization such as -Xutf8=True, single argv elements containing an embedded '-X ' prefix, post-script option insertion, and broad launcher rewrites masked by optimistic manual-test claims.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require an applied production-code change that correctly handles both sys._xoptions values equal to True and explicit non-True values while placing interpreter options before the execution target.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied diff or observed source for get_child_arguments() and any altered launcher branches. Verify that -X arguments occur immediately after the Python executable and before -m, a script path, or application arguments; valueless entries are emitted as -Xname or as the two arguments -X and name; valued entries are emitted as -Xname=value or as -X and name=value.
metadata.non_evidence: Exploration volume, completion claims, generated patch files, syntax-only checks, tests that mutate sys._xoptions and only assert string presence, and statements that a format works without child-interpreter output are not evidence of semantic propagation.
metadata.oracle_test: For a parent state such as sys._xoptions == {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, the child Python prefix must be semantically equivalent to [sys.executable, '-Xutf8', '-Xexample=value'] before the module or script target. The child must observe {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, existing -W options must remain present, and unrelated Windows entrypoint behavior must remain intact.

scale.1: No relevant production change is visibly applied, or the active change structurally regresses child startup by corrupting executable selection, duplicating argument construction, dropping existing arguments, or breaking launcher fallback branches.
scale.2: A localized production change attempts propagation but is semantically invalid or misplaced, such as serializing a valueless True entry as name=True, constructing an argv element with an embedded '-X ' prefix, or appending interpreter options after the module or script target.
scale.3: A localized applied change places -X options before the execution target and preserves existing control flow, but only forwards option names and therefore drops explicit sys._xoptions values; it handles the motivating valueless flag but not the full observable contract.
scale.4: The applied change correctly serializes both valueless True entries and explicit values, places them before the execution target, and preserves warning, module, script, and launcher behavior, but lacks decisive task-relevant execution evidence covering both forms.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and includes focused visible verification in which a child interpreter receives both a valueless and a valued -X option and reports the corresponding sys._xoptions, or an equivalent repository test proves the same behavior while covering existing argument paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly reconstructs CPython -X options in reloader child arguments

applies_when: The trajectory creates, edits, runs, or discusses tests or runtime probes for autoreloader child arguments and Python -X behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive evidence that get_child_arguments() preserves -X utf8 and representative value-bearing options, keeps interpreter flags before the execution target, and does not change output when sys._xoptions is empty.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when claimed success accompanies SyntaxError, import/setup failure, invalid script paths, empty child output, or a command proving the generated -X form is rejected and the contradiction remains unresolved. Cap at 3 if only synthetic formatting code is tested rather than Django's function.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing repository test of get_child_arguments() or an end-to-end child-interpreter probe is strongest; actual failure output overrides printed PASS labels, source-string checks, and hand-computed expected lists.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes self-authored PASS messages, syntax compilation, source grep checks, or tests of a copied expression for evidence that the autoreloader command is semantically valid.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one executed or visibly well-formed repository test that exercises the actual get_child_arguments() implementation with controlled sys._xoptions and a valid script/module setup.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible additions to tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py, focused test-run output, or executable subprocess probes that exercise the actual modified function and CPython parser rather than duplicating the implementation in a standalone list comprehension.
metadata.oracle_test: A focused test patches sys._xoptions to include {'utf8': True} and expects '-Xutf8' before the target; stronger coverage also checks a key with a string value, an empty mapping, coexistence with '-Werror', and an actual child reporting the expected sys._xoptions or UTF-8 mode.

scale.1: No relevant validation evidence, or the visible evidence directly demonstrates failure.
scale.2: Only malformed, irrelevant, or purely asserted checks are visible; material failures are not resolved.
scale.3: A valid limited probe or well-formed unexecuted focused test supports the utf8 case, but it does not exercise the actual function comprehensively or lacks reliable execution evidence.
scale.4: The actual get_child_arguments() path is tested successfully for utf8 with correct ordering, and visible checks protect empty/default behavior or coexistence with warning options.
scale.5: Focused repository or end-to-end evidence passes for flag-style and value-bearing -X options, correct pre-target ordering, empty/default behavior, and existing warning handling, with no unresolved contradictory output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific tests and runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or modifies code that forwards Python -X options through Django's autoreloader.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements forwarding in django/utils/autoreload.py at the common get_child_arguments() interpreter-prefix boundary, preserving option names and values in valid CPython command-line form before the module or script arguments while retaining existing -W handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if -X arguments are appended after the completed script command, if True is serialized as utf8=True for a flag that rejects that value, if option names are replaced by values, or if existing -W options are dropped. Cap at 3 when explicit key=value options are visibly discarded or malformed without contrary runtime proof.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source or unified diff outranks earlier proposals and narrative claims; valid CPython execution of the generated argv outranks formatting guesses.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepts code that mentions sys._xoptions but puts flags where manage.py consumes them, serializes dictionary values incorrectly, or only patches one restart branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible code placing reconstructed -X arguments immediately after sys.executable/interpreter flags and before -m, the script path, and application arguments.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible working-tree diff or patch, especially the construction and ordering of args in get_child_arguments(), handling of sys._xoptions entries, and preservation of sys.warnoptions.
metadata.oracle_test: For sys._xoptions {'utf8': True, 'example': 'value'}, the interpreter prefix is semantically equivalent to [sys.executable, '-Xutf8', '-Xexample=value', ...]; '-X' and its option may alternatively be separate argv elements if execution proves the form valid. These interpreter arguments precede '-m'/module or the script path.

scale.1: No implementation evidence, or visible code does not forward -X options.
scale.2: A forwarding attempt is visible but is at the wrong boundary, has invalid ordering or serialization, or breaks the existing interpreter argument construction.
scale.3: Visible code forwards common flag-style options such as utf8 at the correct pre-script boundary and preserves -W options, but value-bearing options, portability, or branch coverage remains materially incomplete.
scale.4: Visible code correctly forwards flag-style and value-bearing sys._xoptions at the common argument-construction boundary, in valid order, without disturbing existing -W behavior or normal module/script assembly.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 with a minimal, idiomatic implementation whose visible structure covers every get_child_arguments() path that uses sys.executable and avoids changing intentional launcher-executable behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise child-argument implementation and -X serialization

applies_when: The reported AttributeError arises while a function decorator is used through Django's method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Observable analysis correctly traces the failure to _multi_decorate() passing a functools.partial of the bound method into the user decorator, where code such as func.__name__ cannot access ordinary function metadata.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to assert that the principal failure occurs in _update_method_wrapper() or because functools.wraps raises while copying attributes after visible evidence shows the exception occurs inside the user's wrapper closure.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduced traceback or runtime inspection showing the decorator receives functools.partial outranks unsupported explanations about the decorator itself, _update_method_wrapper(), or wraps() failing during decoration.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a partial decorator, a decorator-returned partial, or outer wrapper metadata propagation for the actual partial bound-method argument captured by the user's decorator.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the runtime source at bound_method = partial(method.__get__(self, type(self))) followed by dec(bound_method), not merely observing that partial lacks __name__.
metadata.judge_focus: Traceback, runtime type inspection, and reasoning that connects partial(method.__get__(...)) to the decorator's captured func and the failing func.__name__ access.
metadata.oracle_test: In the reported logger example, the first decoration-time call may receive _update_method_wrapper's dummy function, but the invocation-time call receives functools.partial(<bound method Test.hello_world ...>); accessing that object's __name__ raises AttributeError.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis unrelated to the observed AttributeError.
scale.2: Recognizes that functools.partial lacks __name__ but attributes the failure to the wrong call site or mechanism.
scale.3: Connects the failure generally to _multi_decorate() passing a partial into the decorator, without a complete runtime trace.
scale.4: Accurately traces construction, decoration, closure capture, and invocation of the partial-bound method, supported by relevant source inspection or runtime evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in 4 and explicitly distinguishes invocation-time bound_method handling from _update_method_wrapper's dummy-decoration metadata path, resolving any earlier contradictory hypothesis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies the runtime partial-metadata failure

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a change intended to prevent decorators used through method_decorator() from receiving a metadata-deficient callable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible repair supplies the invocation-time decorator input with the original method's standard wrapper assignments while retaining a callable, per-instance-bound, attribute-assignable adapter and the existing decorator composition behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for a change confined to `_update_method_wrapper()` when the invocation-time decorator input remains metadata-deficient. Cap at 3 for exposing only `__name__`, passing the raw bound method without addressing decorators that assign attributes, decorating the unbound method in a way that alters binding or timing, or unwrapping the partial without demonstrating equivalent call and composition semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed targeted reproductions and repository tests against the applied code outrank claimed behavior. Source semantics of `partial`, bound methods, `update_wrapper`, and the decorator loop outrank passing examples that omit decorator attribute assignment or composition.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating disappearance of the single AttributeError as sufficient even though the patch copies only one attribute, changes when decorators run, loses instance binding, prevents decorator attribute assignment, or disrupts multiple-decorator behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied change on the invocation-time callable path that preserves the full standard wrapper-assignment contract rather than only synthesizing `__name__`; credit 5 additionally requires visible checks of both the reported failure and existing method-decorator behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the proposed or applied change at `_multi_decorate()` and any demonstrations of the object passed to decorators. Check preservation of standard wrapper assignments, bound invocation, decorator-added attributes, multiple-decorator order, arguments, and return behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic reference is an attribute-assignable callable for the current instance that invokes `method.__get__(self, type(self))`, carries the original method's normal `functools.WRAPPER_ASSIGNMENTS` before user decorators inspect it, accepts decorator-added attributes, and is then processed in the existing decorator order.

scale.1: No repair relevant to the invocation-time decorator input, or only edits the example decorator to avoid metadata access.
scale.2: Attempts a repair at the dummy metadata-copy path or another non-causal location, leaving the runtime decorator input deficient.
scale.3: Targets the causal invocation path but remains incomplete or semantically risky, such as copying only `__name__`, using a raw bound method, changing decoration timing, unwrapping the adapter, or presenting an unapplied idea without compatibility evidence.
scale.4: Applies a general wrapper-assignment-preserving invocation adapter and demonstrates the reported logger case, while leaving broader decorator assignment or composition compatibility unverified.
scale.5: Meets 4 and visibly verifies preserved invocation arguments and result behavior together with decorator-added attributes and single or multiple decorator compatibility using relevant existing or focused tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repairs the decorator input while preserving binding and wrapper semantics

applies_when: The reported AttributeError occurs while a function decorator is invoked through Django's method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible analysis consistently explains that `_multi_decorate()` creates a partial around the instance-bound method, passes that partial into the user decorator, and the returned wrapper later fails because its closure accesses function metadata on the captured partial.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 while the latest reasoning still treats `_update_method_wrapper()`, a partial decorator, a decorator-returned partial, or `wraps()` attribute copying as the principal cause despite visible evidence that the exception occurs in the user's invocation-time closure. Cap at 2 if the trajectory acts on that contradicted diagnosis without revising it.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduced invocation traceback and runtime inspection of the object received by the user decorator outrank speculative readings of `functools.wraps`, decorator return types, or `_update_method_wrapper()`. Later evidence-backed corrections outrank earlier hypotheses only when the trajectory stops relying on the contradicted hypothesis.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full diagnosis credit for merely observing that partial lacks `__name__`, or for a late correct sentence embedded in an unresolved sequence of mutually incompatible explanations.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both the source-level construction-and-decoration chain and a settled distinction between `_update_method_wrapper()` decorating a dummy function for attribute discovery and `_wrapper()` decorating the per-instance partial during invocation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest causal explanation together with source excerpts, tracebacks, and runtime type observations connecting `partial(method.__get__(self, type(self)))`, `dec(bound_method)`, closure capture, and the later `func.__name__` access.
metadata.oracle_test: In the logger example, `_update_method_wrapper()` can call the decorator with an ordinary dummy function without triggering the reported failure. On method invocation, `_wrapper()` constructs `functools.partial(method.__get__(self, type(self)))`, passes it to the decorator, and the resulting closure later evaluates `func.__name__` where `func` is that partial.

scale.1: No relevant causal account, or the account is incompatible with the visible traceback and source.
scale.2: Recognizes missing function metadata on a partial but locates the principal failure in the wrong object, phase, or call path.
scale.3: Identifies the invocation-time partial and `dec(bound_method)` path, but the trace is incomplete or the latest reasoning still retains a contradictory `_update_method_wrapper()`/`wraps()` explanation.
scale.4: Provides a coherent and currently stable construction-to-closure-to-failure trace and distinguishes the dummy metadata path from invocation, but lacks either direct runtime corroboration or an explicit resolution of earlier contradictory claims.
scale.5: Provides the stable trace in 4, corroborates it with both relevant source and runtime or traceback evidence, and explicitly resolves any earlier competing diagnosis without later regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Establishes and retains the invocation-time partial-metadata diagnosis

applies_when: Runtime or test evidence exercises a metadata-reading decorator through method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible tests or runtime output demonstrate that a wraps-based decorator can read the decorated method's assignments, invoke the method with correct binding, and return the expected result without the reported AttributeError.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the purported test avoids reading the decorator input's metadata, decorates a normal function rather than invoking a method through method_decorator(), or returns the wrong value. Cap at 3 if later output from the same relevant test still raises the original exception.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-change test output from the repository implementation outranks standalone simulations; explicit assertions outrank success messages or printed output alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating absence of an exception in an altered or weakened reproduction as proof that wrapper assignments and method binding are preserved.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible post-change execution of the reported method_decorator path and evidence that the observed name is the original method name, not dummy, inner, or a fallback string.
metadata.judge_focus: A focused regression test or faithful reproduction using method_decorator(), a decorator that observes func.__name__ or related assignments, and an actual instance-method call.
metadata.oracle_test: A class method such as hello_world decorated with method_decorator(logger) must execute successfully, the logger closure must observe func.__name__ == 'hello_world', and the call must preserve normal self binding and the method's return value.

scale.1: No relevant runtime or test evidence is visible.
scale.2: Only pre-change reproduction, partial-object experiments, or an invalid or unfaithful test is visible.
scale.3: A focused post-change example runs without the original exception, but metadata identity or return and binding behavior is not decisively asserted.
scale.4: A faithful post-change test visibly confirms the original method name and successful bound invocation with the expected result.
scale.5: A repository regression test or equally rigorous asserted test confirms the reported behavior, including method identity and return and binding semantics, with visible passing output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Demonstrates the reported behavior with decisive runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the AttributeError raised by a decorator used through method_decorator().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the latest visible causal account consistently identifies the invocation-time partial passed to the user decorator as the metadata-deficient object captured by the returned wrapper.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest account or applied remedy treats _update_method_wrapper(), functools.wraps() copying from the dummy function, a partial decorator, or the final exposed method as the principal failure. Also cap at 2 if a later edit passes the raw bound method, unwraps to .func, or changes only _update_method_wrapper() while claiming that this follows from the diagnosis, unless the conflict is explicitly recognized and corrected. Cap at 3 when the correct path is stated but an incompatible hypothesis remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A faithful invocation traceback or runtime observation of the object received by the user decorator outranks speculation. Relevant source inspection outranks general statements about partial. Later edits and explanations determine whether an earlier correct diagnosis was retained; a later incompatible action is stronger evidence than an unreconciled earlier sentence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents full diagnosis credit for merely noticing that partial lacks __name__, for a correct sentence embedded in unresolved competing theories, or for reasoning that is contradicted by the trajectory's own next implementation step.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit localization to the invocation-time bound_method construction and dec(bound_method) handoff, together with a closure or call-time explanation for the eventual metadata access.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest reasoning, traceback or runtime inspection, relevant _multi_decorate() source, and any subsequent edit for a consistent chain from partial(method.__get__(...)) through dec(bound_method) to the later metadata access in the decorator closure.
metadata.oracle_test: During method invocation, _wrapper() creates an attribute-settable partial around method.__get__(self, type(self)), passes that partial to the user decorator, and the returned closure later accesses metadata such as func.__name__ on the captured partial. The dummy function used by _update_method_wrapper() is a separate attribute-discovery path.

scale.1: No relevant causal account is visible, or the latest account is incompatible with the observed exception and source path.
scale.2: The trajectory observes missing metadata on a partial but assigns the principal failure to the wrong object or phase, or later acts on such an incompatible diagnosis without correction.
scale.3: The invocation-time partial and decorator handoff are identified, but closure capture, call timing, or the distinction from the dummy metadata path remains incomplete or contradicted by unresolved later reasoning.
scale.4: The latest account coherently traces partial construction, dec(bound_method), closure capture, and call-time metadata access, and no later visible action contradicts that account.
scale.5: The stable account in 4 is directly corroborated by relevant source plus faithful runtime or traceback evidence and explicitly distinguishes the invocation path from _update_method_wrapper()'s dummy-decoration path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retains the correct invocation-time partial diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory executes tests, reproductions, or runtime experiments concerning method_decorator() and callable metadata.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate the strongest visible executable evidence from the latest repository state that the decorator receives the original method metadata while bound invocation and return behavior remain correct.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for commands that do not execute, exercise unrelated code, or are interpreted as passing despite visible failure. Cap at 2 if the purported validation avoids method_decorator(), avoids reading metadata on the decorator input, uses a defective reproduction whose own unrelated error prevents the target behavior from being observed, or the latest faithful run still raises the original exception or misbinds self. Cap at 3 when the focused run succeeds but relies only on prints or omits a decisive metadata, binding, or result assertion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing repository tests against the visibly applied state outrank focused reproductions; focused asserted reproductions outrank print-only runs; faithful causal experiments outrank generic partial demonstrations. Output must be attributable to the latest visible source state. A later failure of the same relevant scenario supersedes an earlier pass.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating an isolated partial experiment, an altered example, zero collected tests, or absence of the original exception as equivalent to asserted post-change validation of metadata identity and method semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied causal change followed by execution of a faithful method_decorator() scenario that checks the metadata observed by the user decorator and successful bound invocation. Credit 5 requires relevant repository regression tests and broader wrapper-contract evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands and output for a faithful method_decorator() invocation, metadata read inside the user decorator or its returned closure, the observed original method name, correct self binding, arguments and return behavior, and relevant existing decorator tests.
metadata.oracle_test: A faithful check decorates an instance method through method_decorator() with a decorator whose invocation-time closure reads func.__name__, invokes the instance method without an extra self argument, and observes the expected result. Broader checks cover standard wrapper assignments, decorator-added attributes, and multiple-decorator behavior.

scale.1: No usable executable evidence is visible, or the attempted command or test is invalid, unrelated, or visibly misreported.
scale.2: Only the pre-change failure, an isolated partial experiment, or an unfaithful or still-failing post-change scenario is visible.
scale.3: A useful causal experiment is visible without an applied repair, or an applied focused scenario runs successfully but lacks decisive assertions for metadata identity, binding, or result behavior.
scale.4: Against the visibly applied change, a faithful focused test or reproduction confirms that the decorator observes the original method metadata and that bound invocation returns the expected result.
scale.5: Meets 4 and also shows passing relevant repository tests plus asserted coverage of the broader wrapper contract, such as standard assignments, decorator-added attributes, or multiple-decorator compatibility.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Builds decisive executable evidence for the metadata repair

applies_when: The task requires a source-code or test change in the repository.
The visible rollout includes tool execution or an attempted implementation workflow.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure whether an explicit execution-stopping failure remains unrecovered at the cutoff and prevents delivery of an inspectable, task-relevant applied diff or complete patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if any later visible step resumes productive repository work. Cap at 3 if a usable task-relevant applied diff or complete patch is visible before the interruption, even if repository-summary fields are inconsistent.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct tool observations and complete emitted patch content outrank assistant claims of having edited files. Repository status or git diff outranks prose summaries of changes. An explicit execution-stopping error establishes blockage only when no later visible step resumes productive work.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating an unrecovered context, tool, or execution-capacity stop as equivalent to recoverable debugging, ongoing work, or successful patch delivery.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 3-5 require an explicit unrecovered execution-stopping failure at the cutoff; absence of a diff alone, ordinary test failures, dependency errors, or an ongoing nonterminal investigation cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect direct tool observations for an explicit failure that stops further execution, then check whether a task-relevant applied diff or syntactically complete patch was already visible before that failure.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, a usable artifact must contain an inspectable change addressing PostgreSQL time-zone preparation so complete named zones such as Etc/GMT signed names are not semantically reversed while the required handling of bare numeric offsets is preserved; a prose proposal or command that was never executed is not an artifact.

scale.1: No explicit execution-stopping failure is visible at the cutoff.
scale.2: An execution-stopping failure occurred, but later visible work clearly recovered and resumed productive implementation or verification.
scale.3: An execution-stopping failure remains unrecovered, but a usable task-relevant applied diff or complete patch was already visible before it.
scale.4: An execution-stopping failure remains unrecovered before any usable artifact, but the visible prefix preserves a complete, actionable, task-correct edit plan identifying both the required behavior and the concrete code location.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unrecovered execution blockage before a usable repository artifact

applies_when: A cutoff-visible patch or concrete edit proposal changes database time-zone preparation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements or specifies a minimal PostgreSQL-side classification that preserves named zones while retaining sign reversal for supported standalone offsets, without altering unrelated timezone APIs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed or absent final diff, code that flips both signs sequentially, or code that changes the fixed-offset behavior caps credit at 2; preservation limited to only one literal example caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff or terminal unified diff outranks prose and scratch-script copies; a frozen empty git diff or later restoration contradicts claims that edits remain applied.
metadata.failure_mode: Overfitting to one timezone literal, changing timezone._get_timezone_name() globally, or treating every string containing '+' or '-' as a numeric offset.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a cutoff-visible production-code change that leaves Etc/GMT-10 and Etc/GMT+10 unchanged while still mapping standalone +10 to -10 and -10 to +10.
metadata.judge_focus: Cutoff-visible changes to django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py, especially _prepare_tzname_delta(), and any directly necessary imports or helpers.
metadata.oracle_test: The production helper satisfies named-zone preservation and standalone-offset sign inversion, and Trunc()/Extract() continue to use that helper through PostgreSQL _convert_field_to_tz().

scale.1: No usable production-code change is visible, or the visible change is syntactically invalid or semantically opposite.
scale.2: A concrete change targets the right helper but is incomplete, contradicted by the cutoff state, or breaks standalone-offset conversion.
scale.3: A plausible PostgreSQL change preserves Etc/GMT names and retains basic offsets, but its classification is unnecessarily narrow, weakly justified, or misses supported offset forms.
scale.4: A focused, valid PostgreSQL change robustly distinguishes named zones from standalone offsets and preserves existing conversion behavior.
scale.5: The focused production change is minimal and idiomatic for this codebase, covers the general named-zone boundary rather than a single literal, and introduces no unrelated API or backend changes.
