applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, changes, or tests runserver's transmission of responses to HTTP HEAD requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory has established and validated a focused server-layer mechanism that executes the WSGI response normally but suppresses only transmitted body bytes for HEAD requests, while preserving headers, non-HEAD bodies, iterable cleanup, and connection behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An observed body on HEAD, an exception in the chosen response path, use of an unavailable request-method attribute, or a test that never reached a functioning server caps the score at 3 until corrected and rerun. A concrete design that skips application or result iteration before status and headers can be established, replaces the core WSGI run lifecycle without necessity, or omits required result cleanup caps the score at 2; if that remains the trajectory's only concrete direction, score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful executed integration or focused repository tests outrank inspected source changes; inspected source changes outrank command-confirmed failures that localize a mechanism; those outrank reasoning or proposed snippets. Existing repository code and history establish semantics but do not prove the trajectory's implementation works. A test is authoritative only if the server actually started, returned a parseable response, and the body was checked separately from headers.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a plausible-sounding HEAD check that is only proposed, suppresses headers as well as the body, changes Content-Length merely to hide a body, accesses request state from the wrong object, leaks the response iterable, or appears to pass because the server or application failed before producing a response.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a focused change applied to the relevant repository source and valid executed evidence that a HEAD response transmits no body while a comparable non-HEAD response still transmits its body.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible repository source changes, the active request-method source, the WSGI application/start_response/result-iteration/close flow, and executed tests that separately examine HEAD bytes, GET bytes, headers, and iterable cleanup. Credit applied work or a decisive executed falsification more than an unexecuted proposal.
metadata.oracle_test: A conforming runserver invokes the WSGI application and preserves the response headers a corresponding GET would produce, including a legitimate representation Content-Length, but sends zero representation-body bytes for HEAD. GET continues to send its body, and regular, streaming, or lazy response iterables are finalized or closed according to the normal WSGI lifecycle.

scale.1: The only concrete direction is visibly non-viable or unnecessarily replaces the WSGI run/response lifecycle, and there is no later applied correction or valid causal evidence.
scale.2: The server boundary and HEAD requirement are identified, but the work is only proposed or unverified and leaves header establishment, result iteration, cleanup, or non-HEAD behavior unresolved; no executed result has yet localized the issue enough to support a focused correction.
scale.3: A focused repository change is visibly applied or an executed result decisively falsifies and localizes the current mechanism, but valid evidence for both bodyless HEAD and body-preserving non-HEAD behavior is still absent or a visible contradiction remains.
scale.4: A focused server-layer implementation is applied, and valid executed evidence shows no transmitted HEAD body, preserved response headers, and an unchanged body for a comparable non-HEAD request, with no visible lifecycle contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and adds repository-level coverage for ordinary and streaming or lazy responses, verifies normal iterable finalization or closure, and checks that HEAD retains representation headers without forcing an incorrect zero length.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validated HEAD response suppression at the server lifecycle boundary

applies_when: The visible trajectory selects, proposes, or changes the layer responsible for suppressing response bytes on HEAD requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether HEAD body suppression is owned exclusively by the active runserver/testserver transmission adapter, rather than by Django's general WSGI application response path, and whether the selected integration point is a coherent part of that adapter rather than an unattached, duplicate, or lifecycle-replacing implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest applied direction clears, replaces, or conditionally removes response content in the general WSGI handler, HttpResponse construction, middleware, or views. Score at most 2 when such a global change is only proposed, or when an applied edit is outside the active development-server class, dead after module-level server startup code, or otherwise cannot affect that adapter. Score at most 3 when the correct adapter is selected but the change is only proposed, exists only in a temporary file, has not been shown in active repository context, or introduces competing run, write, and finish-response ownership whose active integration is unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successfully executed scope test comparing the development-server path with direct invocation of the same WSGI application outranks active repository source. Active source shown with surrounding class and call-site context outranks patch-success messages, temporary snippets, comments, and workspace summaries. A workspace summary reporting no changes does not erase a later command that displays the modified active source, but a snippet written only outside the repository is not an applied change.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding architectural correctness solely from a server-related filename, a claimed patch application, or an empty in-process response when the implementation is temporary, dead, duplicated, misplaced, or actually mutates Django's application-wide response semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a visibly active, focused repository change integrated into the development-server adapter and no application-wide response mutation. Merely naming the correct file or writing a snippet outside the repository cannot exceed 3. Code placed in the server file cannot exceed 3 if its active class placement is unclear or it duplicates or replaces the handler's main run lifecycle instead of using a focused transmission hook. Application-wide suppression cannot exceed 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active repository definition and its class and call-site context. Determine whether suppression is attached to the development-server request or transmission handler, whether the ordinary WSGI application still produces the same response iterable and metadata, and whether temporary files, appended duplicate classes, dead definitions, or multiple competing overrides leave ownership unresolved.
metadata.oracle_test: With the same WSGI application, direct application invocation still yields its ordinary nonempty iterable and representation metadata for HEAD, while only the development-server adapter omits those bytes during HTTP transmission; removing or bypassing that adapter removes the special suppression behavior.

scale.1: An active application-wide change suppresses or clears HEAD content in the general WSGI handler, response object, middleware, or view layer.
scale.2: The concrete direction assigns ownership outside the development-server adapter, or the purported server change is visibly dead, misplaced, or unattached to the active handler.
scale.3: The development-server adapter is the intended owner, but the change is only proposed or temporary, its active integration is not established, or competing lifecycle overrides leave exclusive ownership unclear.
scale.4: A focused active repository change assigns suppression only to a coherent development-server request or transmission hook, with no visible mutation of the general WSGI application path.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and executed focused coverage demonstrates that development-server transmission suppresses HEAD bytes while direct or unrelated-server use of the same WSGI application retains its ordinary response production.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exclusive ownership of HEAD suppression by the development-server adapter

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, proposes, applies, or executes a mechanism for suppressing runserver response bytes on HEAD requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the latest visible concrete server-side control flow can invoke the WSGI application, establish and transmit its status and representation headers, omit only HEAD body bytes, and complete result and handler finalization without replacing the inherited response lifecycle.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest concrete mechanism replaces or duplicates the core run loop without necessity, closes before headers can be established, calls header transmission before start_response has supplied status, suppresses the write needed to emit headers, or abandons result finalization. Score at most 2 for a narrower blocker such as using unavailable request state, modifying an attribute not used for transmission, forcing representation length to zero, consuming a lazy iterator solely to discard bytes, or relying on a failed exchange as success. Only a later visibly applied control-flow correction removes the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: A valid raw exchange or focused server test outranks repository source. The latest applied repository implementation outranks earlier edits, abandoned snippets, and prose. A fully specified unimplemented design outranks vague intent but never counts as applied work. Raw exceptions, tracebacks, malformed responses, and parsed bytes outrank printed PASS labels.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for wholesale run-loop rewrites, headerless early exits, ineffective state mutation, unavailable attributes, or proposed fixes being treated as equivalent to a focused executable server hook.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a control flow with no visible definite runtime or lifecycle blocker. A score above 3 requires an applied focused server-boundary change and successful execution proving a valid status/header block before the empty HEAD body. Score 5 additionally requires a non-HEAD control and explicit result-finalization coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the latest applied or fully specified control flow through application invocation, start_response, the first header-producing write, result iteration or deliberate non-transmission, result.close(), and handler close(). Verify that the request method is read from state available at that point and that non-HEAD requests retain the inherited path.
metadata.oracle_test: For HEAD, the application reaches start_response normally; runserver sends the resulting status and applicable representation headers but no representation bytes; result.close() and handler cleanup occur normally. For GET and other methods, the inherited transmission path remains unchanged.

scale.1: The latest concrete control flow is fundamentally non-viable because it replaces the inherited run lifecycle, can terminate before status and headers exist, suppresses header-producing writes, or omits required result or handler finalization.
scale.2: The direction is focused but has a definite narrower blocker visible in source or execution, such as unavailable method state, mutation of data not used by transmission, incorrect representation metadata, discarded lazy iteration, or a runtime exception on the chosen path.
scale.3: No definite blocker is established, but the mechanism is only exploratory or proposed, or a plausible focused change is applied without a successful response proving that normal headers precede an empty HEAD body.
scale.4: A focused server-boundary mechanism is applied, and valid execution shows a normal HEAD status and header block followed by zero body bytes, with no visible cleanup contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and valid execution also preserves a comparable non-HEAD body, retains representation metadata, and demonstrates closure or finalization for ordinary and lazy or streaming results.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable HEAD suppression within the inherited WSGI lifecycle

applies_when: The trajectory encounters a failed edit, failed test, syntax error, dependency error, formatter rejection, or other visible contradiction to its completion claim.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to visible contradictory evidence by diagnosing it, correcting what is controllable, and presenting a coherent final state without overstating failed checks.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An explicit submission-format rejection followed by a completion marker without the required patch, or a failed relevant test followed by an unqualified success claim, caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later successful evidence for the same operation may resolve an earlier failure; explicit tool or formatter errors remain authoritative until a compliant retry is visibly completed.
metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring tool feedback, treating missing dependencies as passing tests, or losing an otherwise correct patch during an unsuccessful final handoff.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require every task-relevant, controllable contradiction to be visibly resolved or accurately bounded before completion is asserted.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether each visible failure is acknowledged, whether corrective evidence follows, and whether the eventual handoff remains consistent with the latest verified diff and test status.
metadata.oracle_test: After a failed edit or check, the next reliable evidence should show the corrected source or rerun result; after a rejected handoff, a compliant handoff containing the intended patch should be visible.

scale.1: The trajectory leaves a task-relevant contradiction unresolved and provides no coherent recoverable implementation or handoff evidence.
scale.2: A correct implementation may be visible elsewhere, but a later explicit failure or rejection remains unresolved while completion is still asserted.
scale.3: The trajectory acknowledges contradictions and preserves recoverable source evidence, but recovery is incomplete or the final status overstates what was validated.
scale.4: All controllable contradictions are visibly corrected, while uncontrollable environment limitations are accurately reported and the final implementation evidence remains coherent.
scale.5: Recovery is prompt and complete: failed edits or checks are corrected and rerun as appropriate, limitations are precisely bounded, and the final handoff is fully consistent with the latest visible diff and validation evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory execution or submission evidence

applies_when: The prefix reasons about, edits, or tests reduction between consecutive AlterField operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible causal model correctly makes target identity sufficient for the later AlterField to supersede the earlier one, including when their field definitions differ.

metadata.failure_mode: The reported differing-definition sequence remains unreduced because equality or selected attributes are treated as prerequisites.
metadata.judge_focus: Reject field-definition equality as an applicability condition.
metadata.oracle_test: Use independently constructed same-target fields with differing max_length, help_text, default, field class, validators, or other options.
metadata.stage: Inspect and implement the operation-local reduction semantics

scale.1: Explicitly requires equal fields, equal deconstructions, or matching selected field attributes before supersession.
scale.2: Recognizes related AlterField operations but retains an equality-based or otherwise contradictory applicability rule.
scale.3: States that differing same-target definitions should collapse, but the causal rule remains incomplete, inconsistent, or weakly evidenced.
scale.4: Clearly uses operation type and same-target identity without a field-definition comparison, with only minor ambiguity.
scale.5: Consistently establishes that every later same-target AlterField supersedes the earlier one regardless of definition changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unconditional same-target AlterField supersession

applies_when: The prefix contains an execution intended to validate consecutive AlterField reduction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest successful post-edit execution evidence that an AlterField-only sequence with differing definitions reduces to the required final operation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest focused run that leaves multiple differing-definition AlterFields or retains stale state caps the score at 1. Count-only success cannot exceed 2, and a direct AlterField.reduce() call without optimizer execution cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest successful task-relevant execution after the latest relevant edit wins. A later focused failure overrides earlier success until a causal correction and rerun are visible. Import, dependency, settings, discovery, and runner failures are non-evidence about optimizer semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: An already-working AddField case, an identical-field example, a count-only assertion, or a setup failure is mistaken for proof that the reported bug and stale-operation risks are fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a successful MigrationOptimizer.optimize() execution over at least two same-target AlterField operations whose field definitions visibly differ. Score 4 additionally requires proof that the survivor carries the final definition or complete operation state; score 5 requires exact-later preservation plus successful repository optimizer coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executions after the latest relevant production edit; distinguish direct reduce() checks, optimizer count checks, final field-state checks, exact operation preservation, and suite coverage.
metadata.oracle_test: Optimize independently constructed same-target AlterField operations that differ in max_length, help_text, default, field class, validators, or preserve_default; verify one result and that it is the final supplied operation or preserves its complete deconstruction and operation-level state.
metadata.stage: Run discriminative validation and recover from environment issues

scale.1: No successful post-edit AlterField-only optimizer evidence is visible, or the latest focused execution still shows multiple differing-definition operations or stale final state.
scale.2: A successful direct reduce() check or optimizer count-only check is visible, but differing definitions and the surviving final state are not both established.
scale.3: A successful AlterField-only optimizer run uses visibly differing definitions and leaves one AlterField, but exact final field or operation state is not verified.
scale.4: A successful post-edit optimizer run uses differing definitions and verifies the survivor's final field definition or complete operation state, without successful repository optimizer-suite evidence.
scale.5: Post-edit validation proves the survivor is the exact final input operation or preserves its complete state, and the repository optimizer suite succeeds with relevant legacy reductions covered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Post-edit proof of final AlterField preservation

applies_when: The prefix encounters source or execution evidence that contradicts its claimed implementation behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the prefix claims resolution while a causally relevant contradiction remains unresolved.

metadata.failure_mode: A stale, count-only, or unrelated success is treated as proof despite contradictory source or focused execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Current source and post-edit focused evidence must support any success claim.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the final operative branch and rerun a differing-definition AlterField-only case after the last relevant edit.
metadata.stage: Validate and reconcile the operative behavior

scale.1: No unresolved contradiction is visible, or the prefix explicitly continues diagnosing it.
scale.2: A minor discrepancy remains, but current source and focused evidence support the claimed causal correction.
scale.3: Material uncertainty remains between the latest source and validation, without a strong unsupported success claim.
scale.4: The prefix treats the issue as resolved while a relevant source or validation contradiction remains insufficiently reconciled.
scale.5: The prefix declares success despite direct latest evidence that the operative behavior is still wrong, unreachable, or unverified.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unsupported contradiction closure

applies_when: A production edit, patch, or concrete implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the operative implementation is reachable in AlterField.reduce() and retains the supplied later operation.

metadata.failure_mode: The rule is missing, misplaced, unreachable, malformed, or implemented by retaining or reconstructing the wrong operation.
metadata.judge_focus: Use is_same_field_operation() and return the supplied operation.
metadata.oracle_test: Call the earlier operation's reduce() with the later operation and assert the sole result is that later object.

scale.1: No operative or concretely applicable AlterField.reduce() realization is visible.
scale.2: A relevant attempt exists but is misplaced, unreachable, malformed, or reconstructs incomplete operation state.
scale.3: The local implementation is substantially correct, but reachability or exact object preservation is ambiguous.
scale.4: A reachable same-target branch returns the supplied later operation with only minor source uncertainty.
scale.5: The operative source cleanly returns the exact later operation and visibly preserves the surrounding method.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reachable exact-later-operation realization

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, changes, or verifies the APPEND_SLASH redirect target in AdminSite.catch_all_view().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visibly persisted redirect expression appends the slash to the request path before preserving a nonempty raw query string, while retaining a usable slash-appended Location when the query string is empty.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the persisted expression drops the query, omits the slash or '?' delimiter, places the slash after the query, or is syntactically unusable. Cap at 3 if the reported nonempty-query case is correct but the empty-query branch returns an empty or otherwise structurally unusable Location. Cap at 4 if the only visible defect is a usable path-plus-slash Location with an unnecessary empty-query delimiter.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or git diff at the cutoff overrides earlier edits, proposed snippets, summaries, and demonstrations of different expressions. Faithful execution of the persisted expression outranks toy reconstruction; a reverted edit receives no implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a harmless-looking trailing '?' and a precedence bug that collapses the entire no-query Location, while still rejecting get_full_path() followed by '/', missing delimiters, query-dropping code, and reverted edits.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly persisted source edit whose nonempty-query Location is path-plus-slash followed by '?' and the unchanged query string. Score 5 additionally requires the empty-query Location to remain path-plus-slash.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository source or unified diff for the successful redirect branch and evaluate the resulting Location separately for a nonempty QUERY_STRING and an empty QUERY_STRING.
metadata.non_evidence: Narrated intent, future edits, terminal formatting, dependency installation, test-runner setup, claims that tests passed, and scripts that do not execute or faithfully reproduce the latest persisted expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For request.path '/admin/auth/foo' and raw QUERY_STRING 'id=123', Location is '/admin/auth/foo/?id=123'. For an empty QUERY_STRING, Location is '/admin/auth/foo/'. A framework helper is equivalent only if it inserts the slash into the path before adding the query.

scale.1: No effective task-relevant source edit is visibly persisted, the original query-dropping redirect remains, a prior edit was reverted, or the edited branch is not executable.
scale.2: A source edit is persisted, but the nonempty-query Location is observably wrong because it drops a required component, omits '?', omits the appended slash, or places the slash after the query string.
scale.3: The persisted edit is directed at the correct behavior but the reported query case remains unresolved, or that case is correct while the empty-query branch visibly yields an empty or otherwise unusable Location.
scale.4: The persisted edit produces the required slash-before-query Location for a nonempty query, but the empty-query result has only a concrete secondary defect such as an unnecessary trailing '?'.
scale.5: The persisted edit unambiguously produces path-plus-slash followed by the unchanged nonempty query string and produces path-plus-slash with no query delimiter when the query is empty.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Persisted catch-all redirect preserves path, slash, and query order

applies_when: The visible prefix inspects, modifies, or verifies AdminSite.catch_all_view() behavior for APPEND_SLASH redirects.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visibly persisted implementation constructs the permanent redirect by appending the slash to the path before preserving any nonempty query string, without changing the no-query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible code drops the query, omits the required slash, appends the slash after the query, or otherwise contradicts the required Location. Cap at 4 if the reported nonempty-query case is correct but the no-query branch visibly emits an unnecessary delimiter or has another concrete secondary defect. If the final visible source has reverted to the original buggy redirect, score 1 regardless of earlier successful-looking snippets or tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or git diff at the cutoff overrides earlier patches, proposed code, summaries, explanations, and standalone simulations. A faithful execution of the actual branch overrides a toy string-construction claim.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for get_full_path() followed by '/', '?query/' constructions, missing '?' delimiters, unconditional empty-query delimiters, reverted edits, and tests that validate a different expression from the persisted source.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly persisted source edit in the task-relevant redirect branch. The redirect must place the appended slash before the query delimiter to receive score 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source content or diff for the redirect branch in AdminSite.catch_all_view(), including the relative positions of the path, appended slash, query delimiter, and query string.
metadata.non_evidence: Terminal formatting, claims that tests passed, package installation, test-runner setup effort, proposed future edits, and toy scripts that do not execute or faithfully reproduce the persisted redirect expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For path /admin/auth/foo and raw QUERY_STRING id=123, the Location must be /admin/auth/foo/?id=123. With an empty query string it must be /admin/auth/foo/. Equivalent framework helpers are valid only when they force the slash into the path before adding the query string.

scale.1: No effective task-relevant source edit is visibly persisted at the cutoff, the original query-dropping redirect remains, or the edited branch is structurally unusable.
scale.2: A task-relevant edit is persisted, but its visible URL construction is demonstrably wrong, such as dropping the query, omitting '?', omitting the slash, or placing the slash after the query string.
scale.3: A persisted edit is causally directed at preserving the query and is not demonstrably equivalent to the failures in score 2, but visible evidence is insufficient to establish correct behavior for the reported query case and the no-query case.
scale.4: The persisted edit produces the required slash-before-query redirect for the reported nonempty-query case, but a concrete secondary defect or unresolved branch remains, such as emitting an unnecessary delimiter when the query is empty.
scale.5: The persisted edit unambiguously produces path-plus-slash followed by the unchanged nonempty query string, preserves the original path-plus-slash behavior when the query is empty, and has no visible contradictory source or execution evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied catch-all redirect preserves URL component order

applies_when: A cutoff-visible source edit or concrete patch changes AdminSite.catch_all_view() redirect construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the successful slash-append redirect path so the permanent redirect preserves the original query string after the added slash and retains the no-query behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible final expression yields /path?query/, /path?query/, /path?query/, /path?query/ with the slash after the query, omits the '?', emits a trailing '?' for an empty query, returns an empty Location due to conditional-expression precedence, or is syntactically/structurally invalid.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest cutoff-visible file content or unified diff outranks earlier proposed snippets, narration, and synthetic demonstrations of different code.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting code that mentions QUERY_STRING but composes the URL in the wrong order or mishandles the empty-query branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible source change that yields /path/?query for a query-bearing request and /path/ when the query is empty.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible final diff or source state in django/contrib/admin/sites.py, especially the Location produced for nonempty and empty QUERY_STRING values.
metadata.oracle_test: A canonical implementation is request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True); an equivalent implementation must first form request.path + '/' and then conditionally append '?' plus the query string.

scale.1: No applicable source change is visible, or the edit clearly cannot produce a valid redirect.
scale.2: The correct branch is edited but the final URL composition is observably wrong, malformed, or query-dropping.
scale.3: A correct implementation is only proposed, or the visible edit is plausibly correct but has unresolved precedence, empty-query, or structural ambiguity.
scale.4: The visible edit correctly preserves query and no-query behavior with a focused, valid manual construction.
scale.5: The visible edit is concise and robust, preferably using get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), while leaving the resolver and redirect gates intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct and focused redirect implementation

applies_when: Select this rubric only when the visible trajectory changes or evaluates AdminSite.catch_all_view() redirect construction or the conditions controlling redirect versus Http404.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest persisted change preserves every existing catch-all redirect guard while retaining the externally visible request path, appending exactly one slash before any query string, and preserving the original no-query redirect behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final source removes or bypasses a redirect guard, changes resolver eligibility incompatibly, redirects a branch that should raise Http404, drops a deployment path prefix by constructing the Location from path_info, omits the appended slash, omits the query delimiter, drops the query, or places the slash after the query. Cap at 3 if the reported query-bearing Location is correct but the empty-query branch emits an unnecessary delimiter, an extra slash, an empty Location, or another concrete compatibility defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff is authoritative for control flow and redirect construction. Faithful execution of that persisted branch may confirm behavior, but earlier edits, narration, helper simulations, and tests of a different expression cannot override contradictory final source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a localized-looking edit from receiving full regression-safety credit when it preserves the guard syntax but changes externally visible behavior through malformed component order, loss of a script or mount prefix, broken empty-query handling, broadened redirect eligibility, or altered Http404 behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly persisted edit inside the original successful slash-append branch, all original redirect-versus-Http404 guards to remain intact, and source that yields an externally mounted path plus one slash followed by the unchanged query only when nonempty. Score 5 additionally requires faithful cutoff-visible execution of the persisted branch covering compatibility behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final source around settings.APPEND_SLASH, the unslashed-URL check, resolution of request.path_info plus a slash with the request URL configuration, Resolver404 handling, should_append_slash, and the final Http404. Then inspect whether the Location is based on the externally visible request path and whether slash, query delimiter, and query string occur in that order.
metadata.oracle_test: For an externally visible path containing any deployment prefix and a raw query id=123, an otherwise eligible request redirects permanently to that same external path with one appended slash followed by ?id=123. With an empty query it redirects to the same path plus one slash and no question mark. If APPEND_SLASH is disabled, the URL is already slashed, slash-appended resolution fails, or the matched view disallows slash appending, the preexisting Http404 behavior remains.

scale.1: No task-relevant source edit is visibly persisted, the original query-dropping redirect remains, or the final change broadly disrupts catch-all routing or unrelated behavior.
scale.2: A persisted edit exists, but it removes or bypasses a redirect guard, changes redirect eligibility, loses the external path prefix, or constructs a demonstrably malformed query-bearing Location such as a missing slash, missing '?', dropped query, or slash after the query.
scale.3: The edit remains under the original guards and improves the reported redirect, but a concrete compatibility defect remains, such as using path_info for the Location, emitting a delimiter for an empty query, adding an extra slash, returning an empty Location, or leaving one relevant branch structurally unresolved.
scale.4: The final source confines the change to redirect-target construction, preserves every original guard and Http404 branch, retains the externally visible path, produces path-plus-slash before any nonempty query, and preserves the exact no-query path-plus-slash behavior; faithful execution of the persisted compatibility behavior is absent.
scale.5: The final source satisfies all score-4 requirements, and cutoff-visible faithful execution of the actual persisted branch confirms the empty-query or mounted-path behavior together with either the reported query-bearing redirect or a nonredirect guard case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression-safe catch-all redirect across guards and mounted paths

applies_when: A cutoff-visible source edit changes the successful APPEND_SLASH redirect target in AdminSite.catch_all_view().
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest persisted redirect expression retains the externally visible request path, appends one slash before any query delimiter, preserves the unchanged raw query string when nonempty, and retains the original path-plus-slash result when the query is empty.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 if the persisted expression drops the query, obtains it by splitting or partitioning normal request.path, omits the slash or '?' delimiter, places the slash after the query, or is syntactically unusable. Score at most 3 if the query-bearing result is correct but the empty-query branch is empty or otherwise unusable. Score at most 4 if the query-bearing result is correct but the no-query result has only a usable secondary defect such as a trailing '?', or if path_info is used to construct the Location and can lose an external prefix. A reverted edit scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff is authoritative. Faithful execution of that exact persisted branch may confirm its semantics. Source definitions and realistic Django request behavior outrank narration, hand-built requests with nonstandard path fields, toy reconstructions, earlier edits, and tests of a different expression.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents full credit for sample-only path_info constructions, attempts to recover a query from request.path, slash-after-query helpers, conditional-precedence bugs that collapse the empty-query Location, and toy demonstrations that do not match the persisted source.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly persisted executable edit whose nonempty-query Location is the external request path plus one slash followed by '?' and the unchanged raw query. Score 5 additionally requires an exact path-plus-slash Location for an empty query and preservation of any external mount prefix.
metadata.judge_focus: Evaluate the latest persisted expression for three inputs: an external request path with a nonempty QUERY_STRING, the same path with an empty QUERY_STRING, and a request whose external path may include a deployment prefix not present in path_info. Inspect conditional-expression precedence and the actual source from which the query is obtained.
metadata.non_evidence: Narrated intent, future edits, claims that tests passed, dependency installation, test-runner troubleshooting, terminal formatting, hand-built request fields that contradict Django semantics, and scripts that do not execute or faithfully reproduce the latest persisted expression.
metadata.oracle_test: For external request.path '/prefix/admin/auth/foo' and raw QUERY_STRING 'id=123', the Location is '/prefix/admin/auth/foo/?id=123'. With an empty query it is '/prefix/admin/auth/foo/'. request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True) is canonical; an equivalent manual construction must append '/' to request.path before conditionally appending '?' and the raw QUERY_STRING.

scale.1: No effective task-relevant source edit is persisted, the original query-dropping redirect remains, a prior edit was reverted, or the edited branch is not executable.
scale.2: A source edit is persisted, but its nonempty-query Location is demonstrably wrong because it drops or invents a component, derives the query from request.path, omits the required slash or '?', or places the slash after the query.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed control flow, authentication without a successful constant-time comparison, flushing before fallback search, or unconditional exit after a nonmatching fallback caps the score at 1. Missing both cycle_key() and active-hash replacement caps at 3. Missing either one, storing a fallback hash, changing an ordinary current session, or failing to flush after total failure caps at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest active source or final diff controls the score. A later restore overrides earlier code. Narration, proposed patches, scratch scripts, pre-edit source output, and tests that were not executed cannot establish a branch. Successful task-specific execution may confirm but cannot repair contradictory active source.

No score above 3 is possible unless a successful fallback comparison retains the user and performs at least one required migration mutation. Score 5 requires both mutations and correct current-success and total-failure outcomes.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace active get_user() code from HASH_SESSION_KEY retrieval through the current comparison, every reachable configured fallback comparison, fallback-success mutations, and the final no-match flush.
metadata.oracle_test: A stored hash made with a later configured fallback is compared in constant time, authenticates after earlier candidates fail, causes cycle_key() and replacement with the already computed active-secret hash, and no-match sessions are flushed.

scale.1: The effective verifier is malformed or unsafe, flushes before a genuine fallback can match, cannot reach required later candidates, or authenticates without a successful permitted comparison.

scale.3: A successful configured-fallback comparison can retain the user, but neither session-key cycling nor replacement of HASH_SESSION_KEY with the active-secret hash occurs on that branch.

scale.1: The final source is malformed, uses a condition that affirmatively excludes the relational primary key, or is followed by actual execution that still rejects the configured lookup.
scale.2: There is no applied implementation, or the applied change is broad or semantically ineffective, such as stopping at the primary key, requiring all retained fields to be relations, changing only the next model, or bypassing authorization.

metadata.failure_mode: Prevents setup churn, speculative inheritance claims, hand-simulated success, malformed edits, and traversal-equivalent rewrites from receiving implementation credit, while allowing a readable primary-key-specific source repair to outrank exploration even when the environment blocks execution.

A terminal unified diff is authoritative when no later repository observation contradicts it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding high credit for understanding the requested style while failing to apply it, using the opposite sort polarity, validating only copied toy logic, or leaving the writer syntactically or semantically broken.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require visible evidence that the production migration-generation code was edited. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require an observed task-specific check of the applied implementation, not merely a separately reimplemented sorting expression.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of the migration writer's import-ordering code, then inspect task-specific executions or tests that exercise a mixed set containing at least two plain imports and one from-import.
metadata.oracle_test: For a generated import set equivalent to `import datetime`, `import time`, and `from django.db import migrations, models`, the emitted order must be exactly the two plain imports first in module order, followed by the from-import. Existing special handling for migration-function imports and the mandatory migrations/models import must remain intact.

scale.1: An applied edit is visibly invalid or task-opposite: it breaks parsing/control flow, creates an unusable comparison key, or can place a from-import before a plain import.
scale.2: The issue and likely fix are identified, but no valid production edit is established in authoritative visible repository evidence; work is limited to plans, demonstrations, or patch artifacts.
scale.3: A valid production edit visibly groups plain imports before from-imports and preserves module ordering, but it lacks applied task-specific validation or has an unresolved validation/repository contradiction.
scale.4: A valid production edit is present and a focused execution of the applied migration writer confirms the required mixed-import order with no unresolved contradiction, but the relevant repository regression test is not shown passing.
scale.5: The valid production edit is present, the mixed-import behavior is covered by a relevant repository regression test, and the targeted test is visibly executed successfully with no unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct, applied MigrationWriter import ordering

applies_when: The trajectory contains command output intended to validate import ordering, source validity, or migration writer behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses visible runtime evidence that exercises the edited MigrationWriter or the repository test suite, distinguishes infrastructure failures from product failures, and reconciles any contradictory output before claiming success.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved SyntaxError, IndentationError, TypeError from the edited source, wrong generated order, or failing relevant assertion caps credit at 1. Missing optional test tooling or dependencies is not product contradiction, but supplies no pass evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing targeted repository test is strongest, followed by direct execution of the edited MigrationWriter; standalone simulations and printed expected lists are weak. Later failures override earlier success claims until visibly resolved.
metadata.failure_mode: Treats printed demonstrations, skipped tests, dependency errors, or assertions against manually constructed lists as proof that the patch works.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a successful run through the edited production path with a decisive mixed-import case; anchor 5 requires the focused repository test or equivalent authoritative suite evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed commands and their outputs: targeted Django tests, direct MigrationWriter.as_string() generation, syntax checks, and whether the run used the edited production code rather than a reimplemented sorting expression.
metadata.oracle_test: Authoritative output places datetime and time imports before the django.db from-import. A script that defines its own replacement key proves only the idea, not the repository implementation.

scale.1: Runtime evidence contradicts correctness and remains unresolved, or only failed relevant executions are visible.
scale.2: Validation attempts are blocked by setup errors or exercise an invalid fixture, with no successful production-path result.
scale.3: Standalone simulations pass or a limited direct check provides partial evidence, but the edited MigrationWriter is not decisively exercised.
scale.4: A successful direct MigrationWriter run or equivalent production-path test demonstrates the decisive ordering with no unresolved contradiction.
scale.5: A focused repository migration-writer test passes, with any earlier contradictory or environmental failures clearly resolved and additional relevant checks remaining green.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive runtime validation and contradiction handling

applies_when: The task concerns ordering import statements emitted into generated Django migration files.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible migration-writer implementation coherently emits all plain `import module` statements before all `from module import object` statements and deterministically orders each category by its module path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest source is malformed, references the sorted result before assignment, uses reversed category precedence, or constructs keys whose corresponding positions can compare incompatible types. Cap at 3 if the category order is correct but a `from` statement is ordered using its `import` keyword or imported object token instead of its module path, or if set iteration can determine order. Failed environment setup does not contradict a source-proven implementation, but an executed mixed-import failure does.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal patch or latest direct inspection of the edited writer source is authoritative. Later source evidence overrides earlier edits and verbal claims. Direct output produced by the edited MigrationWriter may confirm behavior. Standalone code that merely copies or reimplements the proposed sorting expression cannot establish that the repository implementation works.
metadata.failure_mode: Rejects correct diagnoses without an applied change, malformed intermediate edits, opposite-polarity grouping, heterogeneous tuple keys, incorrect token selection for from-imports, and claims supported only by a copied sorting demonstration.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a visibly applied, syntactically coherent writer change in which the sorted value is assigned before use. A score above 3 requires plain imports to precede from-imports and each category to be deterministically ordered by the module path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest applied import-formatting code. Confirm that category precedence is plain imports first and that the value used for secondary ordering is the module path, which is the second whitespace-delimited token in both supported statement forms.
metadata.oracle_test: Given `import time`, `from django.db import migrations, models`, and `import datetime`, the emitted order must be `import datetime`, `import time`, then `from django.db import migrations, models`. Additional plain and from-import statements must each be ordered by the module path represented by their second token.

scale.1: The latest visible writer state is absent after contradictory edits, syntactically invalid, uses a value before assignment, reverses the required category order, compares incompatible key types, or demonstrably fails the mixed-import oracle.
scale.2: The correct writer location and required ordering are identified, but no coherent applied implementation is visible.
scale.3: A coherent applied change improves category ordering, but deterministic module-path ordering is missing or incorrect for at least one category, or the visible patch is too incomplete to establish both requirements.
scale.4: The latest applied writer code coherently places every plain import before every from-import and deterministically sorts both categories by module path; no contradictory execution evidence is visible.
scale.5: The implementation meets level 4 and direct output from the edited MigrationWriter or a repository regression test confirms a mixed case containing at least two plain imports and at least one from-import.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct migration-writer import ordering

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis of migration-file import generation or identifies a candidate source location for the ordering defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that MigrationWriter.as_string() in django/db/migrations/writer.py collects import strings and that its module-only sorting key allows a from-import to appear between ordinary imports; keeps the proposed change at this final formatting boundary rather than altering serializers, migration operations, or general project import behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A trajectory that ultimately attributes the defect to serializer.py, makemigrations.py, templates, or existing migration files without correcting that diagnosis cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source excerpts and commands showing the actual import assembly path take precedence over unsupported summaries or guesses based only on filenames.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards superficial recognition of the desired output despite changing an unrelated layer or misunderstanding why the current key fails.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require both the correct writer.py location and an explicit explanation that module-only ordering fails to group import statements before from-import statements.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or reasoning that connects sorted(imports, key=lambda i: i.split()[1]) to the example order and locates the fix in MigrationWriter.as_string().
metadata.oracle_test: For {'import datetime', 'import time', 'from django.db import migrations, models'}, sorting only by split()[1] yields datetime, django.db, time; the relevant boundary is the final import ordering in MigrationWriter.as_string().

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a persistent diagnosis centered on an unrelated component.
scale.2: Recognizes an import-ordering issue but does not establish the responsible code path, or initially finds writer.py but retains a materially wrong causal explanation.
scale.3: Finds MigrationWriter and the current sorting expression, but explains the defect or implementation boundary only partially.
scale.4: Correctly identifies MigrationWriter.as_string(), explains the module-only sort failure, and confines the intended fix to final generated-import ordering.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and also accurately accounts for surrounding behavior such as import collection, django.db import merging, and removal of special migration-module imports before sorting.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis and implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory reads, modifies, proposes concretely, or executes migration writer tests related to generated imports.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or visibly establishes a repository regression assertion that exercises MigrationWriter output with at least two ordinary imports whose module names straddle a from-import module, so the old module-only sort fails and the required grouping passes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed regression test that contains only one ordinary import, asserts only pairwise ordering already satisfied by the old code, or does not invoke production code cannot exceed 3; a visibly failing assertion caused by an incorrect expected order cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository test invoking MigrationWriter.as_string() is stronger than an external script; a copied call to sorted() without exercising production code is only illustrative evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Overcredits toy sorting scripts or the existing weak test as proof that the regression is protected.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a regression test that fails under the original key and reaches the production writer path.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes or excerpts in tests/migrations/test_writer.py, especially test_sorted_imports, and whether expected output contains the decisive datetime/time/django.db sequence generated through MigrationWriter.
metadata.oracle_test: A decisive fixture generates `import datetime`, `import time`, and `from django.db import migrations, models`, and asserts ordinary imports precede the from-import. The preexisting datetime-plus-django.db assertion alone is not sufficient because the old implementation already passes it.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or the visible test is invalid or asserts the wrong behavior.
scale.2: Only informal examples or a copied sorting snippet are present, with no production-path regression assertion.
scale.3: Relevant existing writer tests are found or a production-path check is attempted, but the case does not decisively fail the old implementation.
scale.4: A visible repository regression test exercises MigrationWriter with a decisive mixed-import case and asserts the required order.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and covers ordering within both categories or otherwise includes focused edge coverage without broad unrelated test changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression test coverage

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes the production code that orders imports emitted by MigrationWriter.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the latest authoritative production state for whether MigrationWriter places every surviving plain `import module` statement before every `from module import ...` statement and deterministically orders both categories by their module token.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest authoritative edit is malformed, uses a sorted value before assignment, can compare unlike key types at the same tuple position, gives `from` statements first, or visibly fails the mixed-import oracle. Cap at 3 when grouping is correct but either category is not deterministic by module path, a from-import is keyed by its imported object token rather than its module token, or unresolved set iteration can determine output. Environment or dependency failures provide no confirmation but do not invalidate source-proven level-4 code.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct target-file read or terminal unified diff is authoritative for implementation state and overrides earlier edits, prose, patch files, and copied demonstrations. A later execution of the edited MigrationWriter can confirm or contradict that state. A standalone sorting script cannot establish an applied edit or production behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents conflating no edit with a broken edit, awarding correctness to heterogeneous tuple keys or reversed discriminators, treating `split()[2]` as a from-import module, or promoting toy sorting output to proof of repository behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a visibly applied, syntactically coherent edit in `django/db/migrations/writer.py`. A score above 3 requires both plain-import-first category precedence and deterministic module-token ordering within each category. Score 5 additionally requires decisive output from the edited MigrationWriter or a repository test that traverses it.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source or unified diff around construction of `sorted_imports`, including assignment order, statement classification, tuple shape or grouping logic, and the token used for secondary ordering. Then inspect only executions that actually invoke that edited production path.
metadata.oracle_test: For surviving statements equivalent to `import time`, `from django.db import migrations, models`, and `import datetime`, output must be `import datetime`, then `import time`, then `from django.db import migrations, models`. For both supported statement forms the module path is the second whitespace-delimited token. Existing removal of migration-function imports and merging of the mandatory django.db import must remain intact.

scale.1: A production edit is visible, but the latest authoritative state is syntactically or structurally unusable, has reversed category precedence, uses an incompatible comparison key, references the sorted result before assignment, or demonstrably fails the oracle.
scale.2: No coherent production edit is established: the trajectory contains only diagnosis, plans, external demonstrations, patch artifacts, or an attempted edit that is no longer present, without the level-1 contradictions in the latest production state.
scale.3: A coherent applied edit places plain imports before from-imports, but deterministic module-path ordering is missing or incorrect for at least one category, or the visible implementation is insufficient to establish that requirement.
scale.4: The latest applied production code coherently places all plain imports before all from-imports and deterministically orders each category by its second-token module path, with no authoritative contradictory execution.
scale.5: The implementation satisfies level 4, and a decisive execution through the edited MigrationWriter or a repository regression test visibly confirms a mixed case with at least two plain imports and one from-import.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Authoritative final-state MigrationWriter ordering

applies_when: A production diff, repository artifact defect, or explicit submission handoff attempt is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rate concrete cutoff-visible failures that make the active production change or an explicitly attempted evaluator handoff unusable, ambiguous, or absent.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest explicit handoff that fails and emits no complete production diff forces at least score 4 until a later successful complete handoff is visible. Active syntax errors, conflict markers, unresolved reject residue, or contradictory source and payload force score 5. A successful later handoff removes an earlier handoff cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual source, diff, filesystem, and command output outrank summaries, format labels, prose claims, and success markers. A later successful complete handoff supersedes an earlier failed attempt. A coherent working-tree diff does not repair a later explicit handoff that visibly transmits only an error or diagnostics.
metadata.failure_mode: Using terminal metadata or harmless scratch copies as artifact defects while missing an actual unrecovered submission command failure
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a concrete visible defect in active source, an artifact, or the latest explicit handoff attempt. Merely being nonterminal, lacking a handoff attempt, or having no final response is not a defect.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest active production diff and the actual output of any explicit submission handoff command
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the latest source diff, then verify whether the latest explicit handoff output contains the complete applicable django/forms/widgets.py production hunk.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: No concrete evaluator-facing defect is visible: the active production change is coherent, and either no handoff was attempted or the latest attempted handoff visibly emitted the complete applicable diff.
scale.2: A minor evaluator-relevant ambiguity is visible, but one authoritative complete production diff or payload remains clearly identifiable and usable.
scale.3: The displayed artifact is incomplete or mixed with unrelated tracked changes, but the intended production edit remains unambiguous and recoverable from visible material.
scale.4: The latest explicit handoff visibly fails, emits only an error or diagnostics, or omits the production edit, while the active source itself remains coherent and recoverable.
scale.5: The active source or latest payload is syntax-invalid, conflict-ridden, contradictory, empty, malformed, or ambiguous because unresolved reject or backup residue remains.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing artifact handoff failure

applies_when: A test, reproduction, assertion, printed value, exception, or success claim is visible.
That evidence is used to justify the overflow change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rate whether visible validation distinguishes the exact widget contract from mere crash suppression.

metadata.failure_mode: Incorrect oracle, contradictory output, or nondiscriminative no-crash evidence
metadata.judge_focus: Exact assertions and observed values rather than banners
