reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact overflow state transition

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes ImageField post_init signal registration.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible cutoff state cleanly and applicably prevents ImageField from registering update_dimension_fields when neither width_field nor height_field is configured, while retaining registration for concrete models when either dimension field is configured.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible current-state evidence contains production debug prints, malformed indentation, undefined variables, accidental source corruption, or unresolved contradictory edits. Cap at 1 if the only deliverable is visibly non-applicable or the implemented condition removes required registration for dimension-enabled concrete models.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later visible source excerpt or repository diff showing the current file state outranks earlier edit commands and narrative claims. Successful focused execution against the edited source outranks simulated condition-only scripts. If no current source state is visible, an applicable patch outranks prose describing a proposed change. Failed or structurally invalid checks do not prove either success or regression.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for merely stating the one-line fix, for truthiness-only demonstrations that never inspect the edited source, or for a semantically plausible patch whose cutoff state is corrupted or cannot be applied.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a clean, visibly applied or directly applicable change that both skips registration when width_field and height_field are absent and retains registration when either is present on a non-abstract model.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source edits, source excerpts after editing, repository diffs, and submitted patch content for the condition governing signals.post_init.connect() in ImageField.contribute_to_class(). Also inspect for debug instrumentation, undefined names, indentation damage, accidental unrelated edits, and preservation of the existing non-abstract-model guard.
metadata.oracle_test: For ImageField.contribute_to_class(): a concrete model with width_field=None and height_field=None must not connect update_dimension_fields to post_init; a concrete model with either field configured must still connect it; an abstract model must not connect it.
metadata.stage: implementation readiness at the visible cutoff

scale.1: The visible implementation or deliverable is inapplicable, syntactically broken, or semantically wrong for the oracle test, including loss of required dimension-enabled registration.
scale.2: The correct direction is identified, but the visible cutoff state is unresolved or contaminated by debug instrumentation, malformed edits, undefined names, or contradictory current-state evidence.
scale.3: The correct localized condition is identified and the visible state is clean or safely unchanged, but the change is only proposed, not directly applicable, or lacks sufficient evidence that both oracle branches are preserved.
scale.4: A clean, narrow, directly applicable implementation visibly satisfies both oracle branches and preserves the abstract-model guard, with no task-relevant source contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and has credible focused execution or repository-level regression evidence covering both no-dimension and dimension-enabled model behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Clean and Applicable ImageField Signal-Registration Fix

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes ImageField post_init signal registration.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the authoritative visible cutoff artifact cleanly and applicably makes ImageField connect update_dimension_fields only for concrete models with at least one configured dimension field.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the authoritative current production state contains debug instrumentation, malformed indentation, duplicated logic, undefined names, accidental source damage, or unresolved conflicting edits. Cap at 1 if the terminal deliverable is not an applicable repository patch, or if the visible implementation registers when both dimension fields are absent, fails to register for a concrete model with either field configured, or registers for an abstract model. Invalid test-harness failures alone do not contradict a clean authoritative implementation.
metadata.evidence_authority: At a nonterminal cutoff, the latest complete production-source excerpt or repository diff showing both the controlling guard and connect call outranks earlier commands and narration. After a restoration or damaging edit, only a later complete operative excerpt or diff clears the earlier state. At a terminal cutoff that submits a patch, the submitted artifact is the deliverable and must be a parser-recognizable repository unified diff with intact file and hunk headers, context, and changed lines; an informal or partial diff fragment does not inherit applicability from earlier workspace activity. Supported model construction or public signal behavior may strengthen a valid implementation. Condition-only demonstrations, private signal tuple/cache inspection, and harness failures caused by setup errors neither establish nor refute implementation correctness.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents full implementation credit for edit narration, stale or truncated source views, truthiness simulations, private signal-cache guesses, and terminal patch fragments that cannot be reliably consumed as repository changes.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either a complete current production view showing the full operative guard and connect call at a nonterminal cutoff, or a complete parser-recognizable repository patch at a terminal cutoff. A terminal patch-like fragment that lacks the repository diff structure needed for reliable application is capped at 1. Credit above 4 additionally requires credible execution against the edited implementation covering no-dimension, dimension-enabled, and abstract-model behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect ImageField.contribute_to_class() in the latest complete production-source view, repository diff, or submitted repository patch. Confirm that signals.post_init.connect(self.update_dimension_fields, sender=cls) is jointly guarded by a concrete-model requirement and the presence of width_field or height_field. Also inspect for malformed indentation, undefined helper names, duplicated blocks, debug output, unrelated edits, and incomplete patch structure.
metadata.oracle_test: The connect call must be reached for a concrete model when width_field alone, height_field alone, or both are configured; it must not be reached when both are absent or when the model is abstract.
metadata.stage: implementation integrity and deliverable applicability at the visible cutoff

scale.1: The terminal deliverable is not an applicable repository patch, no applicable implementation is visible, or the authoritative implementation fails any required registration branch.
scale.2: The intended condition is recognizable, but the authoritative production state remains corrupted, instrumented, contradictory, or unresolved.
scale.3: The correct condition is proposed or apparently edited, but the visible evidence is incomplete, stale after later edits, or insufficient to establish the full operative guard and connect call.
scale.4: A complete authoritative production view or applicable repository patch cleanly requires both a concrete model and at least one configured dimension field before registration, with no task-relevant contradiction.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and includes credible focused execution against the edited implementation covering absent dimensions, each enabled-dimension case, and abstract models through supported behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applicable ImageField Signal-Registration Implementation

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change intended to avoid the unnecessary ImageField post_init receiver.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Restricts the post_init connection in ImageField.contribute_to_class() to concrete models whose ImageField defines at least one of width_field or height_field, without removing the receiver or changing unrelated file/image behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible edit disables registration for fields with either dimension option, connects on abstract models, changes update_dimension_fields() instead of preventing registration, or modifies an unrelated ImageField. Cap at 3 if contradictory source excerpts leave the effective final control flow uncertain.
metadata.evidence_authority: A clean repository diff or final source excerpt showing the effective condition takes precedence over narrative claims; the effective control flow matters more than operand ordering or equivalent syntax.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for broad signal removal, an edit to django.forms.ImageField, or a change that preserves the unwanted registration while only optimizing the receiver.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a condition semantically equivalent to: not cls._meta.abstract and (self.width_field or self.height_field), guarding signals.post_init.connect().
metadata.judge_focus: Visible proposed edit, repository diff, or final source state around ImageField.contribute_to_class() in django/db/models/fields/files.py.
metadata.oracle_test: Registration occurs exactly when the model is non-abstract and at least one dimension-field option is truthy; it does not occur when both options are absent.

scale.1: No relevant implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed change is incompatible with the required behavior.
scale.2: A source change is attempted at the wrong location or would suppress required dimension updates or abstract-model handling.
scale.3: The correct method and connection are targeted, but the condition is incomplete, ambiguous, only loosely proposed, or visibly malformed.
scale.4: A precise semantically correct conditional edit is proposed and grounded in the source, but no clean applied source state or diff is visible.
scale.5: A clean visible source state or diff guards only the post_init connection with the correct concrete-model and width/height-field conditions, with no unrelated behavioral changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise conditional registration at the ImageField implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory discusses or exercises existing ImageField behavior with width_field, height_field, abstract model inheritance, image assignment, or model initialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves the established dimension-update paths for configured ImageFields, including post-initialization updates on concrete models and descriptor-triggered forced updates, while limiting the optimization to fields that have no configured dimension targets.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory proposes deleting update_dimension_fields(), removing all post_init registration, or changing descriptor assignment semantics. Cap at 3 if visible configured-dimension tests fail and the failure remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing existing Django ImageField tests or focused behavioral tests take precedence over speculative compatibility claims; source-level control-flow analysis is valid when the test environment is visibly unavailable.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents accepting a performance fix that silently breaks width/height population or confuses post_init maintenance with descriptor-driven updates.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognition that configured dimension fields must retain post_init registration and that assignment-time forced dimension updates are a separate path not to be removed.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible analysis of ImageFileDescriptor.__set__(), update_dimension_fields(force=True), configured width/height models, abstract-to-concrete inheritance, and relevant existing ImageField tests or executed regressions.
metadata.oracle_test: Models using width_field and/or height_field continue populating or refreshing dimensions as before, including concrete subclasses of abstract models; ordinary ImageFields without these options merely lose an otherwise no-op receiver.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration is present, or the approach clearly breaks dimension-field behavior.
scale.2: Mentions regressions only generally, or visible changes remove a required dimension-update path.
scale.3: Recognizes that configured ImageFields must continue working and references relevant code or tests, but does not distinguish the key update paths.
scale.4: Correctly analyzes configured dimensions, concrete/abstract behavior, and descriptor-driven updates, with a credible regression plan or partial evidence.
scale.5: Provides strong visible regression evidence or comprehensive source-backed analysis showing configured post_init updates and assignment-time forced updates remain intact while only the no-dimension receiver is eliminated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of ImageField dimension-update compatibility

applies_when: The task concerns optimization of Django AddIndex or RemoveIndex migration operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work derives a concrete and state-preserving reduction rule for index migration operations, grounded in the actual Operation.reduce() contract and the identities of the affected model and index.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the trajectory's operative theory is that distinct indexes can be merged into one operation, that setting elidable alone implements the requested semantics, or that reverse-order RemoveIndex then AddIndex is automatically a no-op without establishing equivalent pre-state and index definitions. Cap at 3 when claimed edits are not visibly inspectable or the trajectory materially misunderstands the optimizer API or its return value.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed source code, displayed test results, inspected patches, and git diffs outrank the assistant's summaries or claims. A command reporting that a patch was applied is not evidence of its semantics unless the inserted code or resulting diff is visible. Repository implementations of Operation.reduce() and analogous field/model reductions outrank guesses based only on operation names.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding repository browsing, repeated identification of the relevant classes, or any attempted patch as though it established a safe reduction; overlooking wrong operation order, missing identity guards, or unsupported claims that several independent indexes can be combined.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires an explicit state-preserving reduction hypothesis tied to the reduce() return contract and guarded by both model and index identity, or visible implementation/test evidence expressing that hypothesis.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source readings, optimizer experiments, proposed conditions, tests, and command-confirmed edits for a precise rule involving operation type, case-normalized model identity, and index name. Distinguish a newly added index followed by removal of that same index from reverse-order, duplicate, or distinct-index scenarios whose equivalence has not been established.
metadata.oracle_test: The core semantic reference is that AddIndex followed by RemoveIndex can cancel only when both operations address the same normalized model and index name; reduction must return the replacement operation list expected by Operation.reduce(). Reverse-order removal and addition cannot be assumed equivalent because RemoveIndex does not carry the removed index definition. Related reductions, such as discarding a model-local removal before deletion of that model, require their own state-preservation argument.

scale.1: The visible work adopts a materially incorrect causal model, such as merging distinct indexes, treating every add/remove ordering as cancellation, or making an unsafe change unrelated to the reduce() contract.
scale.2: The work reaches the relevant migration code but remains diffuse or speculative; it does not state a sound guarded reduction rule, and any edits are opaque or unsupported by visible semantics.
scale.3: The work correctly identifies missing AddIndex/RemoveIndex reduction behavior and relevant analogues, but the replacement result, operation ordering, or model/index identity conditions remain ambiguous or contain a significant API misunderstanding.
scale.4: The work states a substantially correct, guarded same-model/same-index reduction and explains it using Operation.reduce() or an analogous implementation, but lacks either a concrete test/patch or complete treatment of unsafe reverse-order assumptions.
scale.5: The work precisely derives the state-preserving reduction, including operation order, normalized model and index identity, and the correct reduce() replacement semantics, with strong visible source/test support or a concrete inspectable implementation. Additional speculative cases do not undermine the correct core rule.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of AddIndex/RemoveIndex reduction semantics

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or changes reduction code for AddIndex or RemoveIndex migration operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements the reductions locally in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py using conservative normalized identity checks and fallback to the inherited reducer.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Symmetric RemoveIndex→AddIndex cancellation, placement in the optimizer/autodetector instead of operation reducers, blanket elidable=True, or omission of model/name matching caps credit at 2; malformed or visibly truncated source caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible git diff or post-edit source listing outranks statements that a patch was applied; repository status showing no change outranks an unconfirmed editing command.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents broad optimizer changes, state-dependent reverse reductions, case-sensitive identity bugs, and edits that bypass existing elidable behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require both reducers in the migration model-operations module and preservation of super().reduce(operation, app_label) when the task-specific condition does not match.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or source output showing AddIndex.reduce() and RemoveIndex.reduce(), their isinstance checks, normalized model/index-name comparisons, exact returned lists, and super().reduce() fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: AddIndex.reduce(RemoveIndex with case-insensitively matching model and index name) returns []; RemoveIndex.reduce(DeleteModel with case-insensitively matching model name) returns [DeleteModel]; all other cases delegate to super().reduce().

scale.1: No implementation evidence is visible, or the visible edit is malformed or directed at the wrong subsystem.
scale.2: A concrete implementation is attempted but contains a major semantic defect such as symmetric cancellation, blanket elision, missing identity checks, or no inherited fallback.
scale.3: One required reducer is implemented correctly, or both are present with a localized but material omission such as incorrect normalization or fallback handling.
scale.4: Both reducers and their exact return values, normalized matching conditions, and inherited fallbacks are visibly correct, but the resulting source is not confirmed by a diff, parser, import, or equivalent source check.
scale.5: A clean visible diff or equivalent authoritative source evidence shows both exact localized reducers, with correct normalized conditions and super() fallback, and the edited module is shown to parse or import successfully.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise implementation in migration model operations

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, or runs tests for migration optimization involving AddIndex or RemoveIndex.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides focused optimizer tests that prove the two intended reductions and protect nonmatching or unsafe sequences from accidental reduction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed pass contradicted by traceback, wrong optimize() return handling, missing index names, or execution against an unpatched source caps credit at 2; tests expecting RemoveIndex→AddIndex to disappear cap credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful output from the repository’s supported test runner after the visible patch outranks ad hoc scripts; exceptions, API misuse, tuple-unpacking mistakes, or output produced before the patch are not passing evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating environment setup, import success, or an incorrectly written exploratory script as proof of optimizer correctness.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires successful post-change execution of focused tests for both AddIndex→RemoveIndex and RemoveIndex→DeleteModel reductions.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests in tests/migrations/test_optimizer.py or equivalent direct optimizer checks, expected operation lists, pre-change failure evidence, post-change pass evidence, and negative cases for different models or names.
metadata.oracle_test: Focused assertions expect [] for matching AddIndex→RemoveIndex and [DeleteModel] for same-model RemoveIndex→DeleteModel, while differing model/index names and RemoveIndex→AddIndex remain unreduced.

scale.1: No relevant test design or runtime evidence is visible.
scale.2: Testing is attempted but cannot exercise the behavior because of setup/API errors, or it asserts unsafe semantics.
scale.3: A valid pre-change reproduction or a concrete focused test for one required reduction is visible, without successful post-change coverage of both.
scale.4: Focused tests for both required reductions and at least one nonmatching case are visibly added or correctly described, but complete post-change execution is absent or inconclusive.
scale.5: Focused post-change tests for both required reductions pass under the repository test runner, with at least one passing regression case showing a nonmatching or reverse sequence is preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive optimizer regression tests

applies_when: The trajectory investigates migration optimization involving AddIndex, RemoveIndex, or deletion of the affected model.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly determines, with cutoff-visible support, that adding an index and later removing that same named index from the same model reduces to no operations, while removing an index before deleting that same model reduces to the model deletion alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Treat a primary claim about duplicate AddIndex or duplicate RemoveIndex elimination, blanket elidability, or undirected add/remove cancellation as materially incorrect. An explicit claim that RemoveIndex followed by AddIndex generally cancels caps the score at 2 unless the trajectory independently and clearly establishes a valid directional rule; in that case it caps the score at 3 until corrected. Later explicit correction supersedes the earlier claim.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed reduce() code and direct optimizer results have highest authority, followed by an explicit ordered example with visible operands, followed by state/database reasoning. A message that an edit was applied without showing its conditions does not establish its semantics. Mere location of optimizer files or inherited reduce() behavior establishes mechanism awareness only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents generic codebase exploration and unsupported patch reports from tying with a correct directional insight, while also preventing unsafe symmetry, duplicate-operation speculation, or blanket elidability from receiving full semantic credit.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 3 requires at least one valid ordered reduction to be stated with its essential identity boundary. Scores 4-5 require both AddIndex-to-matching-RemoveIndex and RemoveIndex-to-same-model-DeleteModel, including no-operation versus retained-DeleteModel replacement shapes.
metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish repository navigation or discovery of missing reduce() hooks from an explicit ordered reduction rule. Credit a clearly stated AddIndex-to-matching-RemoveIndex no-op as meaningful partial progress even if the DeleteModel case is absent. Give stronger credit when displayed code, tests, or optimizer output confirms the guards and replacement shape.
metadata.oracle_test: For the same model and index name, optimizing [AddIndex(model, named_index), RemoveIndex(model, index_name)] produces an empty list. Optimizing [RemoveIndex(model, index_name), DeleteModel(model)] retains only DeleteModel. Reversing the first pair is not generally equivalent because the newly added index may have a different definition.

scale.1: No valid ordered reduction is identified: the trajectory remains at browsing or unsupported edit claims, or commits primarily to duplicate-operation elimination, blanket elidability, or another unrelated rule.
scale.2: Correctly localizes the optimizer mechanism or forms a relevant but still ambiguous add/remove hypothesis, without clearly establishing a valid ordered rule and its identity boundary; also applies when an unsafe reverse-cancellation claim is the only concrete semantic conclusion.
scale.3: Clearly establishes exactly one valid reduction with its essential boundary: either AddIndex followed by same-model, same-name RemoveIndex is a no-op, or RemoveIndex followed by same-model DeleteModel retains only DeleteModel. This anchor also covers otherwise correct partial reasoning that still contains an uncorrected reverse-cancellation claim.
scale.4: Establishes both valid ordered reductions, their same-model and applicable same-name guards, and the distinct empty-list versus retained-DeleteModel results, but does not clearly justify why the reverse add/remove order is unsafe.
scale.5: Establishes both reductions with visible authoritative support and explicitly distinguishes them from RemoveIndex-to-AddIndex cancellation, duplicate-operation rules, and blanket elidability.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed directional index reduction semantics

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes which AddIndex, RemoveIndex, or model-deletion operation sequences are semantically reducible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies the task-specific optimizer rules: an AddIndex followed by a matching RemoveIndex is a no-op, while a RemoveIndex followed by DeleteModel for the same model reduces to DeleteModel alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any claim that RemoveIndex→AddIndex generally cancels, that duplicate AddIndex/RemoveIndex operations are the primary requested rule, or that all index operations are elidable caps credit at 2 unless visibly corrected later.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and direct MigrationOptimizer results take precedence over unsupported interpretations of the task title; correct state/database semantics take precedence over operation-count assumptions.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents inferring symmetric cancellation even though removing an existing index and adding a potentially different definition under the same name is not a no-op.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require both AddIndex→matching RemoveIndex cancellation and RemoveIndex→same-model DeleteModel replacement to be identified correctly.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning or experiments that identify both valid reductions, including same-model and same-index-name conditions for AddIndex→RemoveIndex.
metadata.oracle_test: MigrationOptimizer([AddIndex('Pony', Index(..., name='pony_idx')), RemoveIndex('Pony', 'pony_idx')]) yields []; MigrationOptimizer([RemoveIndex('Pony', 'pony_idx'), DeleteModel('Pony')]) yields [DeleteModel('Pony')].

scale.1: No task-specific reduction semantics are established, or the explanation is fundamentally unrelated.
scale.2: Recognizes that index operations need reduce() support but proposes materially unsafe or incorrect rules and does not correct them.
scale.3: Correctly establishes exactly one of the two required reductions, with its matching condition, while leaving the other unresolved.
scale.4: Correctly establishes both required reductions and their same-model/name boundaries, but gives limited explanation of why reverse RemoveIndex→AddIndex cancellation is unsafe.
scale.5: Correctly establishes both required reductions, explains the optimizer return values ([] versus [DeleteModel]), and explicitly distinguishes them from unsafe reverse, duplicate-operation, or blanket-elidable rules.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct reduction semantics for index operations

applies_when: Task-specific testing, rendering, direct-call validation, or output assertions are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether visible validation distinguishes required conditional escaping from unconditional escaping, double escaping, scalar processing, and registration-only success.

metadata.failure_mode: Type-only checks, loose substrings, unsafe-only direct calls, double-escape expectations, character-wise output, or ignored relevant failures.

metadata.oracle_test: Complete rendered outputs preserve designated-safe markup, singly escape unsafe members, agree under autoescape on and off, and keep the tested join separator literal.

scale.2: Only direct unsafe-string, result-type, registration, or simulated-join checks pass; safe-value, protocol, autoescape-state, or template-resolution distinctions are absent.
scale.3: Some exact template or join behavior is established, but at least one major discriminator such as safe-value preservation, both autoescape states, or protocol handling is missing.

applies_when: Production code or concrete implementation reasoning identifies the operation applied to members of the input sequence.

Removing only("pk") or leaving one serializer family uncorrected caps at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: Active cutoff source and diff override assistant claims and earlier edits. If no operative edit exists, use the latest explicit source-specific replacement plan; otherwise use the latest coherent diagnosis. Reverted edits, source-text inspection, syntax-only checks, and failed setup runs are not applied implementations.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge awards applied-work credit to a proposal or reverted edit, treats iterator construction as query execution, or ranks a private-state or unrestricted-loading workaround as equivalent to a complete public-API two-site correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires an active, syntactically coherent correction in both the shared Python-derived implementation and the independent XML implementation, using a public QuerySet operation before only("pk") and leaving the natural-key and prefetched-cache paths intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the latest operative queryset chain or exact replacement plan, distinguish it from diagnosis and abandoned experiments, and assess whether it can prevent the conflict when the lazy iterator is consumed.
metadata.oracle_test: From the related manager's restricted select_related queryset, consume the non-natural-key M2M iterator and verify successful PK-reference serialization while SQL selects the related primary key but not unrelated fields or the manager-selected foreign-key column.
metadata.stage: Select and implement a narrow queryset-state correction

scale.1: The current mechanism is predictably ineffective or invalid, such as relying on an exception around lazy iterator creation, testing a bound method, or using an API on the wrong object.
scale.2: The conflict is only partially localized, the proposed remedy remains vague, or invalid or malformed attempts were abandoned without a coherent exact replacement.
scale.3: The cause and affected branch are precisely identified but no exact valid replacement is current, or a concrete remedy can neutralize the conflict only through query internals, unnecessary branch changes, or another material semantic defect.
scale.4: An exact current edit or source-specific plan deterministically avoids the immediate conflict, but it removes only("pk"), leaves one serializer implementation uncovered, remains proposed rather than fully applied, or otherwise misses a required compatibility boundary.
scale.5: Both serializer implementations actively contain a focused public-API queryset-state correction before only("pk"), preserve unaffected branches, and are supported by successful consumption of the affected iterator with PK-only evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current causal queryset remedy

applies_when: The cutoff workspace or git diff shows tracked files created or modified during the trajectory.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes tracked scratch programs, generated files, dependency or environment changes, broad unrelated formatting, and other repository pollution outside the focused serializer correction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A clean focused tracked diff fixes the score at 1 even if many failed setup commands or temporary files are mentioned. Malformed serializer source alone is assessed by the locked implementation rubric, not here.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff git diff and tracked status are authoritative. Earlier tool output and assistant claims do not override the final visible tracked state.
metadata.failure_mode: Nonterminal status hides active tracked pollution, or harmless command failures and untracked temporary scripts are penalized as submitted artifacts.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 1 require at least one active tracked change unrelated to the focused production correction or its repository-appropriate regression tests.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the cutoff git diff and tracked-file status, regardless of whether the trajectory is terminal. Count only active tracked pollution, not commands, failed experiments, untracked temporary files, or edits that were visibly reverted.
metadata.oracle_test: Review git diff --name-status and the full diff; the focused artifact should contain only the intended serializer changes and any repository-appropriate tests.

scale.1: No active tracked artifact pollution is visible; the diff is empty or focused on relevant production code and repository-appropriate tests.
scale.2: A small unrelated tracked file or minor localized diff noise remains.
scale.3: Several tracked scratch/debug files or noticeable unrelated edits remain, but they are isolated from production behavior.
scale.4: Substantial tracked scratch applications, generated files, dependency changes, or broad unrelated churn obscures the focused fix.
scale.5: The tracked repository state is dominated by destructive, generated, environmental, or otherwise unrelated artifacts that materially compromise the evaluator-facing patch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Tracked artifact pollution

applies_when: A concrete source edit, patch attempt, or exact replacement expression is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible production state coherently implements the intended serializer correction and can execute on the affected branch.

metadata.failure_mode: There is no operative edit, source is malformed, the wrong API object is used, or the edit cannot affect the lazy failure.
metadata.judge_focus: Actual source behavior under iterator consumption
metadata.oracle_test: Compile the changed modules and consume the non-natural-key M2M iterator with the custom manager active.

scale.1: No relevant operative production edit is visible.
scale.2: An edit exists but is malformed, uses an invalid manager or QuerySet API, or relies on an ineffective lazy fallback.
scale.3: A coherent local edit executes and avoids the immediate conflict but has a material semantic or completeness defect.
scale.4: At least one real serializer implementation contains the correct, coherent queryset-state correction.
scale.5: Both production implementations contain the correct focused correction and remain syntactically valid and branch-local.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable production implementation

applies_when: The prefix presents a source edit or an exact source-specific implementation plan.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates concrete coverage of the shared Python-derived implementation and the independent XML implementation without conflating breadth with semantic correctness.

metadata.failure_mode: One implementation remains unchanged, or mere awareness of a file is scored as a completed correction.
metadata.judge_focus: Observable two-site source coverage
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the non-natural-key queryset iterator in python.py and xml_serializer.py.

scale.1: Neither serializer implementation has a concrete edit or exact replacement plan.
scale.2: The proposed location is indirect, wrong, or ambiguous.
scale.3: Exactly one serializer implementation has a concrete coherent edit or exact replacement.
scale.4: Both implementations have equivalent concrete edits or exact replacements.
scale.5: Both implementations are coherently corrected and their distinct output families are visibly exercised.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete serializer-site coverage

applies_when: The prefix runs or reports a reproduction, serializer test, SQL inspection, or format-specific validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether visible evidence reaches and consumes the affected M2M iterator and checks relevant output or compatibility boundaries.

metadata.failure_mode: A setup failure, unevaluated iterator, or output omitting the M2M field is treated as successful validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Affected-branch execution rather than setup activity
metadata.oracle_test: Confirm custom-manager use, iterator consumption, visible M2M primary-key output, and where available SQL or cross-format results.

scale.1: No relevant branch is successfully exercised.
scale.2: The original failure is genuinely reproduced or the branch is reached, but no fixed outcome is shown.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative branch evidence

applies_when: The rollout investigates an inline formset whose child ForeignKey targets a defaulted non-primary-key field on a newly added parent.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the investigation reaches a causally supported, regression-aware diagnosis of when the new parent's defaulted target field is cleared, without treating source resemblance, failed setup, or speculative edits as proof.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory declares a fix from manually assigning None, a non-equivalent save_as_new path, or source inspection without exercising the reported lifecycle. Cap at 1 if it applies a core semantic change before a regression test and the visible evidence conflicts with existing tests or fails to establish the claimed callable-versus-constant distinction.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful repository-native test or executable minimal reproduction matching the reported parent, alternate UUID target, child ForeignKey, and new-object inline lifecycle outranks ad hoc assignments and narrative claims. Persisted repository state and test output outrank statements that an edit or test succeeded. Relevant existing regression tests outrank assumptions inferred from comments or commit messages.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding premature claims that all defaulted keys, only callable defaults, or save_as_new processing are the cause when the exact alternate-key inline path has not been demonstrated.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible runtime or repository-test evidence from the reported alternate-key inline lifecycle; source inspection alone cannot pass this gate. Score 5 additionally requires identifying the mutation point while preserving the distinct intended behavior for generated primary keys.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executable probes, observed parent-field values before and after inline-formset construction or validation, relevant BaseInlineFormSet source analysis, and comparison with existing tests for defaulted primary keys and alternate to_field relations.
metadata.oracle_test: For a new parent with an ordinary primary key and a UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4) used as the child's ForeignKey to_field, determine whether inline-formset setup clears that UUID and distinguish this from the established behavior for a parent whose defaulted field is itself the primary key.
metadata.stage: early diagnosis before a regression-safe core fix

scale.1: A production change or definitive diagnosis is made from contradicted or non-equivalent evidence, with no valid exact-topology demonstration.
scale.2: A specific cause or remedy is asserted from source reading, manual None assignment, failed setup, or a different lifecycle; uncertainty and regression constraints are not handled adequately.
scale.3: The investigation reaches relevant inline-formset code or existing tests and remains appropriately tentative, but does not produce a successful exact-topology observation of the mutation.
scale.4: A successful exact-topology probe or repository test visibly demonstrates the parent alternate-key value changing during inline processing and localizes the responsible lifecycle, without proposing an unsupported broad fix.
scale.5: The exact mutation is demonstrated and localized, and the diagnosis explicitly distinguishes the erroneous clearing of a defaulted non-primary to_field from behavior required by existing defaulted-primary-key regressions, yielding a narrowly justified fix direction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-calibrated diagnosis of inline parent-key mutation

applies_when: The trajectory develops or runs tests for an inline ForeignKey that targets a non-primary UUID field with a callable default on an unsaved parent.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides regression evidence for the reported to_field scenario, checking both preservation of the parent UUID and the inline formset behavior needed to create a child with that parent.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Unresolved import, settings, missing-table, or malformed reproduction failures cap credit at 3; a test covering only a UUID primary key cannot earn above 3 for this alternate-key report.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful repository test-run output for committed test code outranks ad hoc scripts; failed setup experiments do not establish behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Testing direct Thing construction or direct child creation, which proves UUIDField itself works but never executes the destructive inline formset path.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an executed passing regression that materializes the inline forms and asserts the unsaved parent’s UUID is not cleared; level 5 additionally requires meaningful save/end-to-end or broader relevant-suite evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests in the model_formsets UUID coverage or an equivalent maintained suite using a parent with a separate automatic primary key, a unique UUID alternate key with default=uuid.uuid4, and a child ForeignKey(to_field=that UUID field).
metadata.oracle_test: The regression must expose the old failure by accessing formset.forms or otherwise invoking add_fields(), then establish that the parent alternate UUID remains non-None and is usable as the child relation; preserving a None hidden initial may be asserted separately.

scale.1: No relevant test work or only unrelated test execution.
scale.2: Mentions a regression test or attempts an ad hoc reproduction but does not execute the failing inline-form materialization path successfully.
scale.3: Adds a relevant test or obtains useful reproduction evidence, but lacks a passing targeted run or omits the non-primary to_field shape.
scale.4: Shows a passing targeted regression for the exact alternate-key inline formset path and asserts the parent UUID survives form construction.
scale.5: Shows level-4 evidence plus successful child/parent save semantics or an admin-equivalent flow and a passing broader relevant model_formsets test selection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds decisive alternate-key inline regression coverage

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an unsaved parent with a defaulted UUID target field becomes null while an inline formset is constructed or validated.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly traces the failure to BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields() mutating the shared unsaved parent instance when the inline ForeignKey targets a defaulted field, rather than attributing it to UUIDField generation, admin rendering, or child saving.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Claims that model save() normally invokes uuid.uuid4 again after the attribute was explicitly set to None, that self.instance is the child form instance, or that the failure is primarily in admin widgets cap the score at 2 unless visibly corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: A faithful runtime reproduction or direct reading of django/forms/models.py and the admin/formset lifecycle outweighs unsupported speculation about widgets, database defaults, or save_as_new.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the admin-facing symptom for an admin-only bug or proposing changes to UUIDField/default generation without tracing the destructive formset side effect.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the mutation in BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields() and correctly identifying self.instance as the shared parent instance.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source excerpts, call-flow reasoning, or runtime output showing that self.instance is the parent Thing, to_field resolves to Thing.id, has_default() is true, and setattr(self.instance, to_field.attname, None) destroys the already-generated UUID.
metadata.oracle_test: Constructing/materializing an inline formset for an unsaved Thing whose child ForeignKey uses to_field='id' changes Thing.id from its generated UUID to None in the buggy implementation.

scale.1: No task-relevant diagnosis, or the explanation is fundamentally about an unrelated admin/widget/database mechanism.
scale.2: Recognizes that inline formsets or default handling are involved but does not locate the destructive parent-field assignment, or materially confuses parent and child state.
scale.3: Locates the has_default()/setattr(..., None) code and associates it with the UUID loss, but gives an incomplete account of to_field resolution or the shared parent lifecycle.
scale.4: Correctly explains the full causal chain from the unsaved parent’s generated alternate UUID through inline form construction to mutation of the parent used by the main form.
scale.5: Provides the level-4 diagnosis plus decisive source or runtime evidence demonstrating the before/after parent value and explains why explicitly assigning None prevents the model default from rescuing the later save.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Identifies the parent alternate-key mutation in BaseInlineFormSet

applies_when: The rollout discusses or changes BaseInlineFormSet initialization for a new parent whose referenced field has a model default.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Designs or applies a core formset change that gives the inline hidden ForeignKey field its required blank initial without permanently replacing the unsaved parent's generated referenced value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for UUID-specific, callable-default-specific, admin-only, or broad stop-clearing changes; for regeneration of a replacement value; for a PK-only condition that leaves the alternate-key bug intact; or for code that can leave the parent as None. A claimed edit absent from persisted repository state earns no applied-work credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final persisted repository diff and its executable data flow outrank stated intentions, shell-edit claims, or malformed intermediate edits. Test output is required only for the highest anchor but contradictions from existing tests cap implementation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents unapplied ideas from tying with working code and prevents superficially narrow conditions that either leave the alternate-key defect unfixed or break established defaulted-primary-key behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible persisted core diff whose data flow preserves the exact original parent target value while presenting a blank hidden initial. Credit at 5 additionally requires targeted passing regression evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the persisted diff in django/forms/models.py, the value passed to InlineForeignKeyField, the parent attribute before and after field construction, restoration on all control-flow paths, and scoping to the referenced field rather than UUID or admin classes.
metadata.oracle_test: After materializing extra inline forms for the affected unsaved parent, getattr(formset.instance, target_field.attname) equals the exact pre-formset generated value, while form.fields[fk_name].initial is None; existing defaulted-primary-key behavior remains intact.

scale.1: No concrete code-level implementation direction and no persisted relevant change are visible.
scale.2: A concrete proposal or attempted edit is visible but has incorrect scope or cannot preserve both the parent value and blank hidden initial semantics.
scale.3: A precise semantically plausible design is given without an applied diff, or a persisted partial diff is present but its restoration, scoping, or data flow remains unresolved.
scale.4: A persisted coherent core-formset diff preserves the exact parent target value and supplies a blank hidden initial, but targeted regression execution is not yet shown.
scale.5: The level-4 implementation is minimal and exception-safe or non-mutating, handles attname and alternate to_field correctly without UUID/admin coupling, and passes the exact regression plus relevant neighboring tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies a non-destructive inline-key initialization change

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the reported aggregate call over a Window-based queryset annotation before or independently of a completed production fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory constructs and executes a task-shaped ORM reproduction that annotates a window result and then evaluates or compiles an aggregate referencing that annotation, yielding diagnostic evidence about the query boundary.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the probe never calls aggregate() on the window annotation alias, only constructs Window or Sum objects, or substitutes an unrelated window query. Cap at 3 if configuration, imports, fixtures, or database setup prevent the complete ORM operation from reaching SQL compilation. A claimed successful reproduction without corresponding output cannot exceed 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A database-executed reproduction and captured backend exception outrank compiled SQL; compiled SQL from the complete ORM operation outranks a configured but blocked harness; a concrete task-shaped harness outranks isolated expression-property probes; source reasoning, dependency installation, and narration alone are lowest authority. Tracebacks and command output take precedence over claims that a probe ran.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating dependency installation, generic window tests, contains_aggregate introspection, or an unexecuted regression-test idea as equivalent to reproducing the reported ORM composition.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require the complete annotate-then-aggregate operation to reach SQL compilation or database execution. Score 5 requires visible task-specific output demonstrating the forbidden direct nesting, not merely successful environment setup or expression construction.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible scripts, shell probes, temporary models or repository fixtures, ORM expressions, generated SQL, exceptions, and command output. The reproduction must include both the Window-based annotation and a subsequent aggregate() reference to its alias; expression flags alone are only partial evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: A representative queryset computes an annotation such as Coalesce(Window(Sum(field), order_by=...), default), then invokes aggregate(total=Sum("annotation_alias")); the diagnostic target is evidence that the unfixed path compiles an outer aggregate directly around an OVER expression or raises the corresponding backend grouping error.

scale.1: No task-shaped executable reproduction is present; activity is limited to browsing, searches, dependency setup, history inspection, or unsupported reasoning.
scale.2: An isolated expression probe or incomplete script is attempted, but it does not construct the full annotate-then-aggregate operation or is blocked before a concrete complete harness is established.
scale.3: A concrete harness visibly includes both the Window-based annotation and aggregate() over its alias, but setup or execution is blocked before SQL compilation, so the reported failure is not directly observed.
scale.4: The complete ORM operation reaches SQL compilation or database execution and visibly exposes invalid direct aggregate-over-OVER nesting or the corresponding backend error, but the reproduction is ad hoc or lacks a precise expected-shape check.
scale.5: A focused, repeatable reproduction visibly demonstrates the failure with the reported wrapped window-annotation shape and captures the decisive SQL or backend exception with a precise assertion or diagnostic check.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable reproduction of aggregate-over-window failure

applies_when: The task concerns aggregating a queryset annotation whose resolved expression contains a SQL window clause.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess visible progress toward making an aggregate that references a window annotation operate on a materialized inner-query column rather than compiling the window expression directly inside the outer aggregate.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory's operative diagnosis is to make Window report contains_aggregate merely because its source is an aggregate, since Window intentionally suppresses aggregate grouping semantics; also cap at 2 if visible generated SQL still nests an OVER expression directly inside the outer aggregate. Unapplied proposals cannot exceed 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository diffs plus relevant passing test output outrank generated-SQL probes; generated-SQL or resolved-expression probes outrank source-based reasoning; source-based reasoning outranks unsupported assertions. A cutoff summary's changed-file and test status controls when it conflicts with plans or narration.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting backend browsing, dependency setup, or a confident contains_aggregate polarity change as equivalent to locating and validating the required aggregation subquery boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a visible applied production-code change in the aggregation/query-planning path. Score 5 additionally requires a visible regression test and relevant passing execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, expression-property probes, generated SQL, diffs, and test output for evidence that the trajectory traced the aggregate reference through queryset aggregation planning, forced or verified an inner-query boundary, repointed the outer aggregate to the selected inner column, and covered the reported Coalesce/Window/Aggregate shape.
metadata.oracle_test: For an annotated expression such as Coalesce(Window(Sum(field), order_by=...), default) followed by aggregate(total=Sum(annotation_alias)), the semantic target is an inner SELECT that computes the window annotation and an outer SELECT that aggregates the inner column, without introducing unwanted GROUP BY behavior.
metadata.stage: early investigation through implementation and regression validation

scale.1: No task-causal localization: only broad browsing, environment setup, repeated searches, or speculation, with no demonstrated understanding of why the emitted query nests an aggregate over an OVER clause.
scale.2: The invalid nesting is recognized and some relevant expression or compiler code is inspected, but the aggregation-planning path is not localized, evidence is inconclusive, or the operative diagnosis contradicts the oracle semantics.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly localizes the issue to aggregate reference resolution and inner-versus-outer query planning, supported by relevant source inspection or a generated-SQL/resolved-expression probe, but no production fix is applied.
scale.4: A production change is visibly applied that makes referenced window annotations trigger an inner query and makes the outer aggregate consume the selected inner column; the implementation is coherent, but regression coverage or relevant passing execution is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The coherent production change is accompanied by a focused regression test covering aggregate-over-window annotation behavior, and visible relevant test execution passes while confirming the window computation occurs in the inner query and the aggregate in the outer query.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validated progress on aggregate-over-window query planning

applies_when: Tests are added, modified, proposed concretely, or executed for aggregate calls over Window-based annotations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Covers the reported ORM composition with a regression test that aggregates a referenced window annotation and asserts the mathematically correct result, preferably alongside an ordinary aggregate in the same aggregate() call and with a wrapper such as Coalesce represented.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Credit is capped at 2 if the test only checks that Window itself works or only inspects expression attributes. Credit is capped at 3 if it would pass while the aggregate still compiles directly around OVER, such as a test that never evaluates aggregate().
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed focused tests with explicit assertions outrank proposed tests; result assertions outrank SQL substring assertions alone; repository test fixtures outrank invented unintegrated scripts.
metadata.failure_mode: Using dependency-install scripts or expression introspection as a substitute for a database-backed regression test of the failing ORM operation.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an assertion on aggregate results for an annotation containing Window, not merely construction of expression objects or checking contains_over_clause flags.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test diff, exact test construction, expected values derived from fixtures, and test execution output in the aggregation or window-expression suites.
metadata.oracle_test: A queryset annotates a per-row window result, then aggregate(total=Sum("window_alias")) evaluates successfully and returns the sum of those per-row window values; a mixed ordinary aggregate remains correct in the same operation.

scale.1: No relevant regression test evidence or test design is present.
scale.2: Only generic window/aggregate tests, expression-property probes, or an incomplete reproduction are present.
scale.3: A concrete aggregate-over-window regression test is designed or added, but expected semantics, evaluation, or mixed-aggregate coverage is incomplete.
scale.4: A focused test is added or clearly specified with fixture-derived result assertions and actual aggregate() evaluation, including the referenced window alias.
scale.5: The focused regression test is applied and shown passing, covers wrapped or mixed aggregate behavior relevant to the report, and is accompanied by appropriate neighboring regression coverage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Focused semantic regression coverage

applies_when: A repository change to callable serialization is visible or concretely developed in the trajectory.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the class-bound method serialization branch in django/db/migrations/serializer.py to use klass.__qualname__ while preserving the module, method name, imports, and all other serializer behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed syntax, replacement of the wrong serializer branch, removal of import handling, or a later visible reversion caps credit at 1; a summary or latest diff showing no change caps credit at 3 when no authoritative post-edit source is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository diff or latest full source excerpt wins over an earlier edit command, proposed patch, narration, or stale pre-edit excerpt.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying an ArrayField-specific workaround, broadly rewriting callable serialization, or crediting an unconfirmed shell edit as an applied patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require visible repository content containing klass.__qualname__ in the bound-classmethod return expression; a proposed edit alone cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: A visible diff or post-edit source excerpt showing the exact FunctionTypeSerializer expression and the absence of task-unrelated production changes.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended production change is the narrow substitution of klass.__qualname__ for klass.__name__ in FunctionTypeSerializer's branch for values whose __self__ is a type.

scale.1: No viable implementation is visible, or the visible change is malformed, in the wrong subsystem, or semantically incorrect.
scale.2: A partially relevant implementation direction is visible, but it edits the wrong boundary or would not preserve the full owner path correctly.
scale.3: The exact one-line correction is proposed or issued as an edit command, but authoritative post-edit repository evidence is absent or contradictory.
scale.4: Authoritative visible source or diff shows the correct minimal __name__ to __qualname__ production change with no evident semantic damage.
scale.5: The correct minimal production change is authoritatively visible, and the surrounding diff demonstrates that imports, method naming, other serializer branches, and unrelated production code remain unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the minimal general serializer correction

applies_when: The trajectory discusses, locates, proposes, or modifies repository tests for migration serialization of callable defaults.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Creates or precisely specifies a repository regression test that serializes a classmethod owned by a nested class and asserts the full module.Outer.Inner.method path, while protecting ordinary top-level classmethod serialization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A test that only asserts a substring such as 'Capability.default', omits the enclosing class, or accidentally defines the supposed nested class at module scope is invalid and caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Committed or diff-visible repository test code outranks ad hoc scripts; exact assertions outrank narrative statements that tests should be added.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating exploratory scripts as durable coverage or adding an ArrayField/database-dependent test when the defect is generic callable serialization.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a visible repository test modification. Runtime experiments outside the test suite cannot satisfy that gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code or a concrete test design in Django's migration writer/serializer tests, including the nested owner definition, serializer invocation or migration rendering, exact expected path, and preferably a non-nested control.
metadata.oracle_test: The regression assertion must distinguish module.Profile.Capability.default from the defective module.Capability.default; a top-level owner should remain module.Capability.default.

scale.1: No relevant regression-test evidence, or the visible test cannot distinguish the defective and corrected paths.
scale.2: Finds a plausible test area or mentions the need for coverage but gives no task-specific executable assertion.
scale.3: Provides a precise, executable test design or ad hoc assertion for the full nested path, but no repository test change is visible.
scale.4: A repository test visibly asserts the full nested classmethod path and would fail with klass.__name__.
scale.5: Visible repository tests cover the nested failure and a compatibility case such as a top-level or deeply nested classmethod, with successful targeted test output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds a durable regression test for nested classmethods

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the incorrect migration path for a classmethod bound to a nested class.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Establishes that migration serialization, rather than ArrayField runtime behavior or field deconstruction, drops the enclosing class because FunctionTypeSerializer builds a bound classmethod path with the owner class's __name__ instead of __qualname__.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory continues to attribute the defect to ArrayField cloning, database schema execution, choices conversion, or model-state lookup after contrary serializer evidence is visible, credit is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A direct serializer reproduction plus the relevant FunctionTypeSerializer source takes precedence over speculation based only on ArrayField, Field.deconstruct(), schema editing, or migration state code.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the PostgreSQL field shown in the report for the causal implementation layer instead of Django's general migration callable serializer.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit identification of FunctionTypeSerializer's bound-classmethod branch and the __name__ versus __qualname__ distinction.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source excerpts or runtime introspection connecting Profile.Capability.default.__self__.__name__ == 'Capability' and __self__.__qualname__ == 'Profile.Capability' to FunctionTypeSerializer in django/db/migrations/serializer.py.
metadata.oracle_test: Serializing a bound nested classmethod must yield module.Profile.Capability.default; the defective branch yields module.Capability.default because klass.__name__ omits the lexical parent.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the visible source and Python callable attributes.
scale.2: Recognizes a migration-path or callable-serialization issue but remains focused on an incorrect subsystem or does not explain why the enclosing class is lost.
scale.3: Locates migration serializer code or demonstrates the missing parent path, but does not firmly connect both observations to klass.__name__.
scale.4: Correctly identifies FunctionTypeSerializer's class-bound method branch and explains that klass.__name__ must be replaced by a qualified owner name.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis with direct source and runtime or serializer evidence showing __name__, __qualname__, the defective output, and the required nested output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies the nested-class callable serialization defect

applies_when: A concrete correction to migration serialization of a class-bound callable is proposed, attempted, or visibly present.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether visible repository work applies the narrow change from the bound owner class's short name to its qualified name in FunctionTypeSerializer, with increasing credit for authoritative application evidence and durable regression coverage.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest authoritative code is malformed, changes the wrong serializer branch, removes module or method-name handling, targets ArrayField instead of generic class-bound callable serialization, or produces a path missing an enclosing class. Cap at 3 if a later targeted source read or diff shows the old expression, an explicit revert, or no applied change. A failed check caps at 3 only when the observed serializer behavior is actually wrong; infrastructure failures or a faulty expected-value comparison do not override visibly correct output.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest targeted source read or repository diff is authoritative for exact code and minimality. If no readable post-edit source is available, an observed edit followed by successful post-edit serialization of a nested classmethod to a path containing every enclosing class may confirm applied semantics up to score 4, provided no later source, diff, or revert contradicts it. The observed serialized path outranks an erroneous success label or assertion whose expected string omits an otherwise correct module prefix. A generic cutoff inventory reporting no changed files or an empty diff is not evidence of reversion when earlier tool output visibly establishes the edit and no explicit later repository inspection contradicts it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents both crediting an unexecuted suggestion as an applied patch and withholding application credit solely because a generic summary or full source readback is absent despite discriminating post-edit behavior. It also prevents behavior-only evidence from proving strict diff minimality.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible evidence that the correction was applied, either through authoritative repository content or through a targeted edit followed by discriminating post-edit serializer or migration-writer output that the old klass.__name__ branch could not produce. Score 5 additionally requires a durable repository regression test and a successful relevant repository test invocation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the class-bound branch of django/db/migrations/serializer.py, targeted edit commands, subsequent source reads or diffs, direct serializer or migration-writer output, and repository regression tests. The relevant expression must retain the owner's module and the callable's method name while using the owner's __qualname__.
metadata.oracle_test: For a module-level nested owner such as Profile.Capability, serializing Profile.Capability.default must yield module.Profile.Capability.default. The intended production change is klass.__name__ to klass.__qualname__ only in FunctionTypeSerializer's branch where value.__self__ is a type; a top-level owner continues to serialize as module.Owner.method.

applies_when: The trajectory inspects, traces, probes, or modifies the explicit x- or y-limit pipeline.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how precisely the trajectory localizes logarithmic locator normalization as the first operation that changes descending explicit limits to ascending limits. Credit is based on ordered-pair evidence through the setter pipeline, with the highest level reserved for an intervention on the identified locator reorder that visibly changes the stored public-limit result. Collateral defects from that intervention are evaluated by correction-quality rubrics and do not erase its localization evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible evidence shows the pair was reordered by locator normalization but the trajectory continues to blame a later operation, cap at 1. If an intervention changes multiple ordering operations so that the observed result cannot be attributed to the locator reorder, cap at 4. Do not lower localization solely because the focused locator edit also introduces a warning or domain-handling defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: Ordered values observed at successive operations in the identified repository outrank prose and rendering evidence. Exact locator source plus a pipeline trace establishes localization; an executed intervention on the locator's ordering statement followed by a changed stored-limit result is stronger causal evidence. A collateral warning or safeguard defect does not invalidate localization unless another ordering-related change makes the cause ambiguous.
metadata.failure_mode: Blaming scale-domain limiting, transforms, tick filtering, or rendering; inferring inversion only from appearance; or awarding intervention-level credit when no executed change to the identified locator reorder is tied to a changed stored-limit result.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require identifying locator normalization as the suspected loss point. Score 4 requires exact source or trace evidence showing that locator normalization performs the first reorder. Score 5 requires an executed change to that identified locator-ordering behavior and a post-change stored-limit result showing the corresponding order change.
metadata.judge_focus: Track the same ordered endpoints through validation, major-locator `nonsingular`, scale-domain limiting, and view-interval assignment. Distinguish source or trace localization from stronger causal evidence obtained by changing the identified locator-ordering statement and rerunning a stored-limit check.
metadata.oracle_test: First compare the input and output around logarithmic locator normalization and scale-domain limiting. For the strongest confirmation, alter only the locator statement responsible for sorting and rerun a literal descending positive logarithmic-limit call while inspecting `get_ylim()` or the stored view interval.

scale.2: The relevant limit pipeline is inspected, but the first descending-to-ascending operation is not isolated.
scale.3: Locator normalization is identified as the likely loss point, but its actual ordering behavior is not established from exact source or observed operation output.
scale.4: Exact source or pipeline-trace evidence establishes logarithmic locator normalization as the first reorder and excludes scale-domain limiting and downstream display code, but no executed intervention on that reorder is tied to a changed stored-limit result.
scale.5: The identified locator-ordering behavior is changed in an executed source intervention, and a post-change check shows the corresponding change in `get_ylim()` or the stored view interval; collateral defects do not obscure which ordering statement caused that result.
