reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable repository advancement

applies_when: The visible work states or implies that the implementation or its behavior is correct after source inspection, simulations, runtime checks, copied-module experiments, installed-package runs, or commands that fail before the relevant behavior is exercised.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes unsupported success claims according to the gap between the claim's scope and the evidence that actually supports it. Source inspection may support a narrowly stated implementation claim, but not an end-to-end runtime claim. The strongest penalty is reserved for completion claims left standing after applicable evidence shows that the tested artifact is incompatible, the relevant assertion fails, or the claimed edit was not exercised.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A reached assertion showing the original warning, an incorrect result, an incompatible converter API, or failure of a required direct converter boundary overrides generic success text about that same tested artifact. Import or setup failure before the relevant assertion proves no product behavior. Absence of a warning from ordinary numeric axis conversion is not contradictory because native-number handling may bypass the categorical converter. A later valid rerun supersedes an earlier failure only for the behavior it actually checks.
metadata.evidence_authority: A post-edit command that reaches the relevant assertion against a coherent repository source is authoritative for behavior. The active source diff is authoritative for visible control-flow semantics only. Installed releases, copied-module hybrids, predicate simulations, and commands failing before the assertion are indirect evidence; they become contradictory only when the work relies on them for a behavior claim that their own output disproves.
metadata.failure_mode: The work presents an unchanged installation, incompatible copied-module hybrid, predicate reimplementation, failed import, bypassing API path, or success-like output preceding an exception as end-to-end proof, and does not later withdraw, qualify, or replace that claim with applicable evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: The two lowest-penalty anchors require that no unresolved claim exceeds its supporting evidence. The two highest-penalty anchors require an affirmative behavioral or completion claim left standing despite either a reached applicable contradiction or clear evidence that the claimed implementation was not the artifact exercised.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the exact scope of each success claim, then determine whether the cited command exercised the edited source, reached the relevant assertion, and produced compatible output. Distinguish missing runtime proof from affirmative contradictory evidence, and credit explicit withdrawal or qualification of an earlier contaminated claim.
metadata.oracle_test: The scope of the final claim matches the strongest available evidence: coherent edited-source execution for runtime behavior, or an explicitly limited source-level claim when only the focused converter transformation is established.

scale.1: Every success claim matches attributable evidence, or earlier invalid evidence is explicitly discarded and replaced or the final claim is appropriately limited.
scale.2: A plausible executable source change supports a narrow implementation claim, while absent or indirect runtime proof is clearly acknowledged and no end-to-end success is asserted.
scale.3: A behavioral claim is stronger than the available attribution or assertion coverage, but no reached applicable output directly disproves it and a plausible executable source change is visible.
scale.4: A strong behavioral claim remains after an applicable hybrid, installed-package, or repository-source run reaches the relevant path and exposes an unresolved incompatibility, failed assertion, or contrary result, although a plausible source edit exists.
scale.5: Completion is asserted even though the latest applicable evidence shows that the claimed implementation is absent, was not exercised, or is behaviorally contradicted, with no subsequent qualification or valid recovery.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Calibration and recovery of success evidence

applies_when: The visible work runs warning checks, reproductions, converter calls, category tests, source-path checks, or empty `UnitData.update` logging checks.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores tests that distinguish the empty fix from retained non-empty behavior and, at the highest level, cover the secondary empty-update diagnostic.

metadata.failure_mode: Default warning filters, native-number bypass expectations, predicate-only simulations presented as end-to-end proof, or unattributable package execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Strict empty-path checks, direct numeric converter checks, coherent source attribution, and optional empty-update log capture.
metadata.oracle_test: Both empty entry points plus direct numeric warning checks and relevant category regressions.

scale.1: No probative validation is visible, or the latest relevant execution still demonstrates the defect.
scale.2: Only diagnosis simulations, syntax checks, installed-package runs, or otherwise indirect checks are shown.
scale.3: At least one focused behavior is exercised against attributable source, but the opposite compatibility boundary or second empty path is missing.
scale.4: Both empty entry points pass under strict warning handling and the retained direct numeric warning is checked against attributable source.
scale.5: The empty paths, direct numeric warning, category regressions, invalid-input behavior, and quiet empty `UnitData.update` logging are all visibly validated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative validation and diagnostic completion

applies_when: The visible prefix includes an edit, restore, diff, workspace summary, file inspection, parse check, or detached patch concerning the categorical converter.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the cutoff-visible repository contains an intact executable categorical converter with the focused empty-input change applied in the source the evaluator would run.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later restore removing the guard, an authoritative empty active diff after the edit, whole-file deletion, zero-length file, syntax failure, duplicated converter methods, or displaced decorators caps the score at 2; scratch files alone do not prove repository damage.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest cutoff-visible active repository diff and file contents outrank earlier printed source, intended replacements, copied site-packages modules, helper scripts, and detached patch text. Cutoff-visible source remains judgeable whether or not completion has been announced.
metadata.failure_mode: Credit is inferred from an earlier edit or detached artifact even though the evaluator-facing source is absent, reverted, malformed, or structurally damaged.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require the focused fix to be visibly active in executable lib/matplotlib/category.py. Score 5 additionally requires visible structural or parse verification of the resulting file.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active repository diff or workspace state, then verify that lib/matplotlib/category.py is nonempty, parseable, structurally intact, and contains the executable guard rather than leaving it only in prose, a helper script, an installed package, or a detached patch.
metadata.oracle_test: The active repository file parses and retains StrCategoryConverter.convert, axisinfo, default_units, and _validate_unit in their class structure while containing the normalized empty-input distinction.

scale.1: No executable repository fix is visible at cutoff, or category.py is empty, deleted, or unusable.
scale.2: The intended fix exists only in prose, a script, an installed package, or detached patch, or the active source has a concrete unresolved structural defect.
scale.3: An active source edit is visible, but its persistence, parseability, or surrounding class structure remains materially uncertain.
scale.4: The active category.py is intact and visibly contains a focused executable empty-input fix with no unrelated structural rewrite.
scale.5: Level 4 is met, and a visible parse, focused final diff, and surrounding method/decorator inspection establish evaluator-facing structural integrity.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active evaluator-facing category source integrity

applies_when: A categorical converter edit changes an empty return, numeric predicate, warning scope, suppression context, category update path, or validation path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the source-level compatibility boundary of the applied transformation: genuine non-empty numbers retain an unsuppressed deprecation warning and float conversion, while categorical mapping and invalid-input validation remain reachable.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the applied edit nests `_api.warn_deprecated` inside the deprecation-suppression context, deletes or makes the warning unreachable for non-empty numbers, broadly returns before non-empty mapping or validation, or reclassifies strings or bytes as numeric. Cap at 2 when indentation or truncated context creates a concrete but unresolved risk to one of those branches.
metadata.evidence_authority: The exact applied source diff and its indentation control warning scope and branch reachability; assistant claims, predicate simulations, ordinary numeric axis conversion, and scripts that were merely written cannot override that source. A later explicit semantic replacement or revert supersedes an earlier transformation. Purely mechanical later file damage is assessed by the locked source-integrity rubric rather than erasing an already established transformation's compatibility semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: The empty-input edit suppresses the retained numeric warning, expands an early return to non-empty values, bypasses `unit.update(values)`, weakens validation, or changes categorical strings into numeric pass-through values.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires visible source context showing the suppression block, `_api.warn_deprecated`, numeric return, `unit.update(values)`, and mapping fallthrough. Executed tests are not required by this implementation rubric.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the applied converter block for non-empty values. Confirm that `_api.warn_deprecated` remains reachable and outside `_api.suppress_matplotlib_deprecation_warning()`, numeric values still return floating-point data, strings and bytes remain excluded from numeric classification, and non-numeric values still reach `unit.update(values)` and mapping conversion.
metadata.oracle_test: For direct `StrCategoryConverter.convert`, non-empty numeric scalars and arrays warn and return floats; strings and bytes update category mappings in insertion order; invalid non-string category data still raises `TypeError`.

scale.1: The applied transformation visibly breaks a required non-empty branch, including suppressing or making unreachable the retained numeric warning.
scale.2: A concrete source defect or unresolved indentation or scope problem threatens the warning, numeric return, mapping, or validation path.
scale.3: The edit appears limited to empty input and no non-empty regression is visible, but surrounding source context is insufficient to establish every compatibility branch.
scale.4: Complete source context clearly preserves an unsuppressed non-empty numeric warning and float return while keeping category update and mapping paths reachable.
scale.5: Level 4 is met and the visible predicate and downstream validation also clearly preserve strings and bytes as categories and rejection of invalid non-string category data.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Non-empty converter control-flow preservation

applies_when: The task concerns colorbar separator lines omitted where an extended region joins the main colorbar.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that divider segments are derived from the colorbar mesh and that the unconditional `[1:-1]` selection removes the first and last mesh-boundary segments, which are required at extension-to-interior junctions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims `_mesh()` itself must include the triangular or rectangular extension geometry, or treats all first and last mesh segments as ordinary internal separators regardless of `extend`.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete source excerpts and correctly interpreted mesh or `LineCollection` coordinates outrank visual guesses, raw segment counts, or unsupported statements about extension patches.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the extension patch outline, number of colored cells, or a generic pcolormesh edge issue for the specific endpoint-selection defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires distinguishing exterior outline edges from divider lines at the boundaries where extension patches meet the interior color cells.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning connecting `_add_solids`, `self.dividers.set_segments`, `np.dstack([X, Y])`, and the endpoint segments corresponding to the lower and upper extension junctions.
metadata.oracle_test: For a non-inverted bar, the first mesh segment is needed exactly when the lower extension exists and the last mesh segment is needed exactly when the upper extension exists; with `extend='both'`, both endpoints omitted by `[1:-1]` are required.

scale.1: No causal localization, or an explanation centered on an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Finds the divider-setting line or suspects `[1:-1]`, but gives an incomplete or materially confused account of the mesh and extension geometry.
scale.3: Correctly explains that `[1:-1]` drops the two extremity divider segments and connects this directly to the reported `extend='both'` behavior, without fully handling asymmetric extensions.
scale.4: Additionally distinguishes `neither`, `min`, `max`, and `both`, explaining that each endpoint is retained only when the corresponding extension exists.
scale.5: Provides the complete endpoint model with source- or runtime-backed coordinates, including the implications of orientation or axis inversion and the distinction between divider junctions and the colorbar outline.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of missing colorbar extremity dividers

applies_when: The trajectory uses runtime experiments, external or installed Matplotlib code, repeated edits, or conflicting observations while investigating the bug.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Maintains trustworthy provenance between the inspected source, edited repository, and executed code, and resolves contradictory observations before relying on them.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if a visibly malformed source file is left as the basis for conclusions. Cap at 2 if system/site-packages code is copied over, a different-version module is executed as though it were the repository, or contradictory segment output is accepted without reconciliation.
metadata.evidence_authority: A clean repository diff plus execution explicitly loading that repository outranks output from a separately installed Matplotlib; direct `inspect.getsource`, `module.__file__`, or equivalent provenance outranks assumptions about `PYTHONPATH`.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding credit for convincing runtime output that actually came from an installed release, or overlooking destructive edits and syntax errors because the intended algorithm sounded correct.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that runtime results came from the same source tree or an explicit acknowledgement that they did not and therefore are not validation of the patch.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible import paths, version/source checks, git diff or file inspection, recovery from malformed edits, and reconciliation of unexpected divider counts with the actual code being executed.
metadata.oracle_test: The observed pre-fix repository implementation using `[1:-1]` must yield only interior segments; output already containing both extremity segments indicates different code, later code, instrumentation, or a subsequent update and cannot validate that unchanged implementation.

scale.1: Evidence provenance is absent or contradicted, and malformed or destructive edits remain unresolved.
scale.2: Some source or runtime evidence is present, but it mixes installations, versions, or broken edits and draws conclusions from the mismatch.
scale.3: The trajectory notices provenance or editing problems and avoids at least some invalid conclusions, but does not establish a clean end-to-end source-to-runtime chain.
scale.4: The inspected, edited, and executed source is clearly identified, contradictory observations are reconciled, and the visible repository state is coherent.
scale.5: In addition to level 4, the trajectory explicitly confirms the final diff and import/source provenance, restores failed edits cleanly, and uses only reproducible repository-grounded evidence for its conclusions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-grounded evidence and recovery from contradictory results

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime probes, or a concrete regression-test design for the colorbar edge behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses task-specific assertions or rendering evidence to demonstrate that extension junction dividers are present without introducing endpoint lines for non-extended sides or dividers when `drawedges=False`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if expected counts or coordinates are inconsistent with the mesh length, if a failing setup is reported as a passing test, or if testing only reproduces an import or color-count error. Cap at 3 when only `both` is covered and one-sided behavior remains untested.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing repository tests with semantic coordinate assertions outrank segment-count-only scripts; source-backed regression tests outrank ad hoc images; images outrank unsupported claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a larger segment count as sufficient proof without checking which endpoints were retained, or validating only the original screenshot while allowing asymmetric-extension regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least the reported `extend='both', drawedges=True` case plus a non-extended or disabled-drawedges regression case.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests or probes of `Colorbar.dividers.get_segments()`, endpoint coordinates, extension combinations, orientation, inversion, and an image comparison matching the reported appearance.
metadata.oracle_test: For mesh length N, expected divider counts are N-2 for `neither`, N-1 for either one-sided extension, N for `both`, and 0 when `drawedges=False`; retained endpoint coordinates must be the extension-to-interior boundaries in both horizontal and vertical layouts.

scale.1: No relevant test or runtime evidence, or only setup failures unrelated to the bug semantics.
scale.2: Runs a reproduction or inspects raw segment counts, but lacks reliable expected coordinates or regression checks.
scale.3: Demonstrates the reported `extend='both'` endpoint behavior with a meaningful assertion or rendering result, but has little compatibility coverage.
scale.4: Adds or runs decisive checks for the reported case and for `neither` or `drawedges=False`, with correct segment identities or counts.
scale.5: Provides passing task-specific regression evidence across `neither`, `min`, `max`, and `both`, includes `drawedges=False`, and covers orientation or inversion through semantic segment assertions and/or an appropriate image test.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific divider and rendering validation

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or attempts a source change to colorbar divider generation or updating.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the visible checkout coherently implements extension-aware divider selection: disabled edge drawing clears all segments, each mesh endpoint is retained only for its corresponding extension, and recalculation occurs where inversion-sensitive extension state can change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest relevant source is syntactically malformed, invokes an undefined helper, has an incompatible call signature, or leaves destructive unrelated edits. Cap at 2 when no coherent repository edit is visible, when all endpoints are retained unconditionally, when one 'any extension' condition controls both endpoints, or when extensions cause all dividers to be cleared. Cap at 3 when a coherent edit handles initial selection but does not visibly establish both independent endpoint rules or the required update placement.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent source excerpt and repository diff outrank edit commands, intended replacements, pseudocode, synthetic segment calculations, or claims that a change was made. A clean applied implementation outranks an exact unapplied design; malformed final source overrides earlier correct intent.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding implementation credit for investigation alone, trusting a failed editing command, accepting unconditional removal of `[1:-1]`, overlooking a stale or partial helper, or ignoring that inversion and extension refreshes can change which physical endpoint is lower or upper.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a syntactically coherent visible checkout edit. Credit above 3 additionally requires separate first- and last-endpoint handling and an explicit empty-segment path for disabled edge drawing.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible implementation rather than the proposed algorithm. Verify source syntax and signatures first, then disabled-edge behavior, independent lower and upper endpoint selection, preservation of interior segments, and finally whether the divider update is invoked from every relevant redraw or inversion-sensitive extension path.
metadata.oracle_test: When edge drawing is enabled, form the full mesh segment array, discard the first segment iff `_extend_lower()` is false, and discard the last segment iff `_extend_upper()` is false; retain all interior segments. When edge drawing is disabled, pass no segments. The same selection must be recomputed after operations that can alter inversion-sensitive extension correspondence, without changing mesh, norm, color, outline, or extension-patch geometry.

scale.1: No coherent relevant implementation is present, or the latest source is malformed, signature-incompatible, destructive, or directed at the wrong subsystem.
scale.2: Provides only an unapplied design or editing intent, or visibly applies a broad incorrect rule such as retaining both endpoints unconditionally, using one condition for either extension, or mishandling disabled edge drawing.
scale.3: Shows a coherent applied edit at the divider-selection boundary that improves the reported case and preserves the disabled-edge path, but independent endpoint behavior or update synchronization remains incomplete or not visible.
scale.4: Shows a clean applied checkout edit that retains the first and last mesh segments independently according to their corresponding extension predicates, preserves all interior segments, handles every extension mode, and emits no segments when edge drawing is disabled.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and visibly centralizes or invokes divider recalculation at every necessary redraw, limit, extension, and inversion-sensitive update boundary, with focused validation and no changes to unrelated geometry or color processing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Coherent checkout implementation of per-endpoint divider selection

applies_when: A code change or concrete implementation design is present for colorbar divider generation or extension updates.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements or precisely designs a minimal colorbar change that builds divider segments from the existing mesh, retains each endpoint according to the corresponding extension, clears dividers when `drawedges` is false, and keeps the segments synchronized when extension geometry or axis direction changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if `drawedges=False` can produce segments, if all endpoints are retained for `extend='neither'`, if both endpoints are retained for a one-sided extension, or if the visible edit is syntactically malformed. Cap at 3 if initial drawing is addressed but a visible inversion/limit-change path can leave divider endpoints stale.
metadata.evidence_authority: A syntactically coherent repository diff with per-endpoint behavior outranks pseudocode, broad replacement of `[1:-1]`, or claims based only on an image.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying the superficially plausible `use all segments whenever any extension exists` fix, which regresses `extend='min'`, `extend='max'`, or ordinary colorbars.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires independent handling of lower and upper extensions rather than using one `any extension` branch.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or exact design in `lib/matplotlib/colorbar.py`, especially conditional lower/upper endpoint selection and where divider updates are invoked.
metadata.oracle_test: Starting from `segments = np.dstack([X, Y])`, remove the first segment iff there is no lower extension and remove the last segment iff there is no upper extension; use no segments when `drawedges` is false. Divider updates must remain consistent with `_do_extends` and inversion-sensitive `_extend_lower()`/`_extend_upper()` semantics.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed change targets unrelated color, norm, or outline code.
scale.2: Suggests removing `[1:-1]` or otherwise keeping all endpoint segments, but does not preserve ordinary or one-sided extension behavior.
scale.3: Provides a coherent minimal change that fixes `extend='both'` and preserves `drawedges=False`, but does not independently select lower and upper endpoints or account for update synchronization.
scale.4: Provides correct per-endpoint selection for all extension modes in the colorbar divider path, with a coherent and syntactically valid change.
scale.5: Provides the complete minimal implementation, including reusable divider-update logic at every necessary redraw, extension, or inversion-sensitive boundary, while leaving color generation, norm processing, and extension patch geometry unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Extension-aware divider update at the correct implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains a source-change decision or an explicit decision to defer a formatter edit because available evidence is incomplete.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible repository intervention is limited to what task-causal source and provenance evidence currently justify.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A global-format or unrelated-machinery edit based on a wrong selected level, or a success claim contradicted by the current source or import path, caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and verified import paths outrank explanatory claims; failed commands and external runtime output may justify caution but not a repository edit or success claim; a clean revert restores the current source but does not erase visibly unsupported reasoning.
metadata.failure_mode: Applied work is rewarded merely for existing, or cautious non-editing is penalized, without checking whether the intervention was warranted by visible causal evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require either a focused edit supported by correct generated-tick reasoning or an explicit, evidence-based decision not to edit while repository execution or causal diagnosis remains unverified.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether current edits, reverts, or deliberate non-edits match the established formatter control point, generated-tick evidence, and runtime provenance
metadata.oracle_test: Given the visible evidence, the intervention should affect only the month-level offset-suppression decision once generated-tick semantics are established; otherwise the repository should remain unchanged while uncertainty is reported accurately.

scale.1: The trajectory confidently applies or pursues a broad or wrong-control-point change despite visible evidence that its causal premise is false.
scale.2: The intervention is weakly supported, relies on external or surrogate success as repository proof, or repeatedly contradicts visible source without fully restoring epistemic consistency.
scale.3: The repository is left recoverable and no unsupported success is established, but the edit decision remains only partly calibrated because diagnosis or provenance is confused.
scale.4: The trajectory either makes a focused intervention supported by correct source-level evidence or deliberately withholds an edit while clearly identifying the unresolved causal or provenance prerequisite.
scale.5: The intervention is narrowly justified by generated-tick semantics and verified repository evidence, with competing hypotheses rejected and no unsupported scope added.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-Calibrated Repository Intervention

applies_when: Visible source, diff, or runtime output concerns the no-January month-tick path in ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the currently applied formatter semantics retain the constant-year offset when the generated major ticks vary by month and contain no January tick.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An empty current diff, a later revert, an unchanged suppressing condition, or visible source that cannot reach the claimed branch caps the score at 2; output from an unverified external installation cannot raise the score.
metadata.evidence_authority: A latest visible repository diff or source view wins over plans, attempted commands, comments, simulations, and earlier source views; verified post-format output from that same repository wins over source inference; external installations are non-evidence for the working tree.
metadata.failure_mode: Proposed, failed, reverted, simulated, or externally executed work is mistaken for current corrected formatter behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a visibly applied, reachable source change in the repository; score 5 additionally requires the modified repository formatter to format actual generated major ticks after a draw or explicit format_ticks call.
metadata.judge_focus: The current applied condition reached when generated major ticks select level 1 and omit month value 1
metadata.oracle_test: For actual generated month-level major ticks within one constant year and omitting January, formatting must leave month labels concise and make get_offset() return that constant year.
metadata.stage: Implement and refine the focused offset condition

scale.1: The authoritative current source is unchanged or clearly still suppresses the no-January month-level offset, and no applied functional repair is visible.
scale.2: An applied attempt is visible, but it is unreachable, affects the wrong component or format, is reverted later, or otherwise cannot clearly restore this path.
scale.3: A current reachable formatter edit plausibly restores the no-January year offset, but its effect is ambiguous because the relevant branch or resulting offset is not established.
scale.4: The authoritative current source clearly retains the constant-year offset on the generated month-level no-January path, without repository-runtime confirmation.
scale.5: The modified repository formatter visibly formats actual generated no-January month ticks and produces the expected constant-year offset after formatter state is populated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: R1_reachable_no_january_behavior

applies_when: A candidate implementation is visible or corrected formatter behavior is claimed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates evidence from the modified repository formatter using actual generated major ticks and correctly populated offset state.

metadata.failure_mode: Evidence comes only from failed commands, stale state, surrogate logic, guessed ticks, plotted samples, or an external installation
metadata.judge_focus: Provenance and causal relevance of visible validation
metadata.oracle_test: Draw the figure or explicitly format actual major-tick locations, then inspect labels and offset from the modified repository formatter
metadata.stage: Validate the regression and compatibility boundary

scale.1: No candidate validation succeeds, or all cited output comes from failed commands, stale pre-format state, or an unrelated installation.
scale.2: Source analysis or surrogate logic supports the candidate, but the modified repository formatter is not shown producing corrected output.
scale.3: The modified repository formatter produces the expected year offset for an actual generated no-January tick set after formatting.
scale.4: The modified repository formatter demonstrates both no-January year visibility and generated-January non-redundancy, or equivalent focused tests pass.
scale.5: Both discriminative branches, focused tests, broader date tests, import provenance, and patch-hygiene checks are visibly verified.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: R4_repository_formatter_evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory explains the defect, interprets formatter output, or justifies a source change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the explanation agrees with visible source, generated-tick semantics, formatter-state timing, and observed output.

metadata.failure_mode: Reasoning uses plotted samples, wrong columns, guessed ticks, stale state, external code, or contradicts the current edit
metadata.judge_focus: Causal consistency rather than verbosity or stage completion
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the explanation with the visible loop, generated major-tick components, labels, post-format offset, and imported module path

scale.1: The explanation is materially wrong or contradicts visible source or output.
scale.2: The main defect is partly recognized, but generated ticks, selected level, formatter state, or runtime provenance are confused.
scale.3: The suppression cause and direct edit effect are explained consistently, but the January boundary or validation interpretation is incomplete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: R5_causal_evidence_consistency

applies_when: A visible applied edit changes offset suppression or varying-component selection in ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the applied condition repairs month ticks omitting January, suppresses redundant year context only when a generated January tick supplies it, and leaves other selected levels unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A condition that still suppresses level 1 when January is absent, reverses membership, checks the wrong column, changes day-or-finer suppression, or damages loop selection cannot score above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied repository source or diff controls; direct repository-formatter demonstrations of both generated month-tick branches confirm it. Proposed conditions, copied Boolean simulations, plotted samples, and external installations do not establish the applied condition.
metadata.failure_mode: All broad month-level edits are treated alike even though some leave the bug intact or newly alter day-level and finer offsets.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a reachable check for January among generated major-tick month values; score 5 requires direct evidence for both January-absent and January-present generated tick sets.
metadata.judge_focus: The selected level, the unique generated values for that level, month value 1 membership, and preservation of the existing break, fallback, and non-month branches
metadata.oracle_test: At level 1, generated months without value 1 retain the %Y offset, while generated months containing value 1 suppress that redundant offset; level 0 and levels 2 through 5 preserve their prior behavior.
metadata.stage: Derive and implement the generated-tick completeness rule

scale.1: The applied edit is absent, unreachable, reversed, uses the wrong tick source or component, or damages varying-level selection.
scale.2: The edit reaches the loop but either leaves the no-January month bug in place or introduces a visible non-month regression such as changing day-level offset suppression.
scale.3: The localized edit preserves loop structure and repairs the no-January month path, but enables month offsets without checking whether generated ticks include January.
scale.4: The applied source uses generated month values, or equivalent selected-level unique values, to distinguish January-present from January-absent month tick sets while preserving other levels.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: R3_artifact_applicability_and_scope

applies_when: A task-specific cause or repair direction is stated, selected, or actively reconsidered.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest stable assistant-authored repair direction correctly makes backend persistence an unconditional exception to rc_context restoration while retaining restoration of every non-backend rcParam.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 when the latest stable repair conclusion confidently places the defect in rcParamsOrig, backend initialization, get_backend, switch_backend, or Gcf instead of rc_context restoration, or proposes retaining backend rollback. Cap at 2 when backend persistence is conditional on the sentinel, figure creation, or backend type. A visibly reopened tentative hypothesis is not treated as the stable conclusion.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest explicit assistant-authored repair decision controls. A later statement that reopens or retracts an earlier diagnosis makes that earlier diagnosis non-controlling. Tool output and an active diff may corroborate the decision but cannot supply an unstated rule; implementation defects belong to the separate implementation-integrity dimension and do not erase a clearly stated semantic rule unless the assistant presents the contradictory implementation behavior itself as the intended rule.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards causal vocabulary or an edit merely for existing, penalizes a correct declared repair rule solely because its first implementation attempt is incomplete, or treats a confident wrong-subsystem diagnosis as equivalent to unresolved exploration.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 3 or higher requires an explicit authored conclusion that rc_context restoration of backend state is the repair boundary. Merely observing get_backend, switch_backend, close("all"), Gcf loss, or an empty registry is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest unretracted assistant-authored repair rule, not mere symbol discovery, source excerpts, or whether an attempted edit is already syntactically correct. Determine whether the assistant selects rc_context restoration as the repair boundary, excludes backend unconditionally, and preserves the existing non-backend try/finally contract.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic rule is that rc_context must omit backend unconditionally from a raw, non-resolving restoration mapping while preserving the existing try/finally restoration of all non-backend rcParams on normal and exceptional exits.

scale.1: The latest stable authored conclusion confidently selects a wrong repair boundary, contradicts backend persistence, or proposes a broad behavior-breaking remedy.
scale.2: No stable repair rule has been selected, or the assistant remains in investigation after reopening an earlier hypothesis; alternatively, the proposed persistence rule is explicitly conditional.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly selects rc_context restoration as the repair boundary, but whether backend exclusion is unconditional or whether other rcParams continue to restore is unclear.
scale.4: The assistant explicitly states that backend must be omitted unconditionally from rc_context restoration while non-backend rcParams continue to restore, but raw snapshot safety or exceptional restoration is not fully specified.
scale.5: The assistant specifies a raw non-resolving restoration mapping that omits only backend unconditionally, retains the existing try/finally for all other rcParams, and rejects changes to get_backend, switch_backend, or Gcf.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Stable rc_context repair-direction correctness

applies_when: The prefix runs or relies on a reproduction, runtime diagnostic, or behavioral test.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether runtime evidence actually exercises the relevant backend state transition in the edited checkout without changing the preconditions through observation.

metadata.failure_mode: The run forces a backend, imports an external release, uses `plt.gcf()` as a probe, or infers preservation solely from lack of a close exception.
metadata.judge_focus: Check module provenance, backend preselection, raw-state observation, manager identity, registry membership, and close semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: A fresh checkout process observes unresolved backend state without resolving it, preserves the same registered manager across `get_backend()`, and proves close removes that manager.

scale.1: No relevant run succeeds, or the only claimed evidence is masked, external, state-mutating, or otherwise non-discriminative.
scale.2: A relevant observation is made, but checkout provenance or a critical backend precondition is missing.
scale.3: A useful checkout-based reproduction or state observation succeeds, but it omits a material discriminating assertion.
scale.4: The relevant backend and registry transition is observed reliably in the edited checkout with non-mutating diagnostics.
scale.5: Evidence verifies provenance, raw backend preconditions, manager identity across lookup, registry membership before close, registry removal after close, and explicit backend persistence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnostic evidence validity

applies_when: The trajectory is diagnosing why backend lookup affects figures created during an rc-context.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the assistant's explicit causal account of how restoring unresolved backend state makes a later backend lookup select a backend and close registered figure managers.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the active explanation says `get_backend()` is behaviorally inert, denies that restored backend state can invoke switching, attributes the loss to garbage collection or independent Gcf corruption, or otherwise contradicts a required link, unless that claim is visibly corrected later.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest unretracted assistant-authored explanation grounded in cutoff-visible source or runtime evidence controls. Tool output may support that explanation but cannot supply a missing causal link by itself.
metadata.failure_mode: Relevant functions are listed or inspected without an authored connection between restoration, lazy backend resolution, backend switching, and manager destruction.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 3 or higher requires an explicit assistant-authored cause-and-effect statement linking at least two consecutive task-specific transitions; coincidental discovery of relevant symbols is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Use assistant-authored causal conclusions. Function names appearing only in source listings, grep output, tracebacks, or command output are not conclusions. Distinguish merely finding `rc_context`, `switch_backend`, or `Gcf` from explicitly linking their state transitions.
metadata.oracle_test: The complete account states that `rc_context` saves and restores the raw `_auto_backend_sentinel`; first-figure creation resolves it; context exit restores it; `get_backend()` reads `rcParams['backend']`, whose special lookup invokes `pyplot.switch_backend`; `switch_backend` calls `close("all")`; and that clears the existing managers from `Gcf.figs`.
metadata.stage: Repository localization and backend call-path inspection

scale.1: No task-specific authored causal account is present, or the active account is fundamentally unrelated or contradictory.
scale.2: The assistant describes the symptom or an isolated downstream operation, but does not explicitly connect consecutive restoration, lookup, switching, and registry effects.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly explains either the restored-sentinel-to-backend-switch transition or the switch-to-close-all-to-Gcf transition, but not both.
scale.4: The assistant explicitly connects context restoration, later backend resolution or switching, and manager closure, but omits or slightly misstates one detail such as raw sentinel preservation, the `get_backend()` lookup, or the final `Gcf.figs` mutation.
scale.5: The assistant explicitly and accurately states the full raw-sentinel restoration, `get_backend()` lookup, `switch_backend`, `close("all")`, and `Gcf.figs` destruction chain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Authored causal chain for backend-triggered manager loss

metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the production diff and run `lib/mpl_toolkits/tests/test_mplot3d.py::test_invisible_axes[png]`.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete harmful intervention severity

applies_when: A repository diff, terminal submission payload, or nonterminal cutoff without a submitted artifact is visible.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A terminal prose-only or explicitly non-patch response when an applicable patch is required receives score 5 even if an earlier working tree contained the correct edit. A valid final patch supersedes earlier corrected drafting mistakes.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminally delivered artifact outranks earlier working-tree edits, intended edits, scratch files, and prose claims. If no terminal artifact exists, the latest visible repository diff determines only current artifact risk and absence of submission is neutral.

scale.4: A delivered artifact has a concrete likely application, syntax, path, truncation, or unrelated-scope defect, although some usable patch content remains.

Do not infer reasoning from a correct edit alone.

metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish an unchanged intact file, a successfully recovered valid edit, and a currently malformed draw method.

scale.1: The latest visible source is malformed or substantially breaks the shared patch draw lifecycle.
scale.2: The source is intact but no successful production edit is present, or a repair remains incomplete or ambiguous.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Edit integrity and draw-lifecycle preservation

applies_when: The trajectory contains investigation or assistant-authored reasoning about where a nonzero patch dash offset is lost.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest assistant-authored causal account consistently identifies the draw-time zero-offset substitution in the shared patch path as the defect, while correctly preserving existing parsing, linewidth scaling, and graphics-context dispatch semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest unresolved explanation asserts that `_get_dash_pattern`, `set_linestyle`, constructor order, geometry, or backend support discards the offset for the repository object after visible repository state shows the requested tuple is retained and `Patch.draw()` explicitly zeroes it. Also score 1 when contradictory runtime output from an unverified installation is adopted as the new cause without reconciling module provenance. Cap at 3 for proposed extra scaling or reconstruction of an already scaled pattern.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest explicit assistant-authored causal interpretation supported by repository source controls the score. Repository `Patch.draw()`, `_bind_draw_path_function()`, and dash-scaling source outrank observations from an unidentified or separately installed package. A later parsing, setter, geometry, or backend hypothesis supersedes earlier correct prose unless the assistant explicitly resolves the discrepancy and reaffirms the repository draw-time cause.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge averages an early correct diagnosis with a later incompatible one, infers understanding from source text alone, or treats inconsistent output from another installation as stronger than the inspected repository path.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a current assistant-authored conclusion that `Patch.draw()` replaces the already computed effective offset with zero before the binder configures the graphics context. Scores above 3 additionally require correct treatment of both linewidth-scaled `_dash_pattern` and the existing `gc.set_dashes(*self._dash_pattern)` dispatch.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the chronological sequence of assistant-authored causal statements. Look for an explicit connection between the temporary `(0, self._dash_pattern[1])` value in `Patch.draw()` and the ineffective rendered phase, and check whether later reasoning preserves or contradicts that conclusion. Raw grep output, stored-state prints, successful image creation, and identifiers appearing only in tool output are not causal conclusions.
metadata.oracle_test: For a patch using `(10, (10, 10))` at linewidth 4, the user-scale state remains approximately `(10, (10, 10))`, the effective `_dash_pattern` is approximately `(40, [40, 40])`, `Patch.draw()` historically substitutes only the effective offset with zero, and `_bind_draw_path_function()` otherwise forwards the complete effective tuple to `gc.set_dashes`.
metadata.stage: Locate and trace the patch dash-rendering path

scale.1: The latest unresolved causal account contradicts the repository draw path by relocating the offset loss to parsing, setters, constructor order, geometry, or a backend, or it adopts provenance-uncertain contradictory output without reconciliation.
scale.2: No stable assistant-authored causal conclusion is present; the trajectory only searches relevant code, repeats source text, or discusses dashes without connecting the draw-time zero substitution to the rendered phase loss.
scale.3: The latest account explicitly identifies the `Patch.draw()` zero-offset substitution as the cause, but it does not correctly establish both the user-scale versus linewidth-scaled state and the existing binder dispatch.
scale.4: The latest account consistently identifies the draw-time substitution, correctly distinguishes user-scale from linewidth-scaled dash state, and recognizes that the binder already forwards the effective tuple to `gc.set_dashes`.
scale.5: The latest account gives the complete parsing-to-scaling-to-draw-to-graphics-context chain, remains consistent after subsequent observations, and explicitly rules out parser, constructor-order, extra-scaling, geometry, and backend-specific causes.

scale.2: The source remains intact but unchanged, despite a correct description of the required edit.
scale.3: A plausible correction is partially visible or reported, but the latest production state is ambiguous or insufficiently exposed.
scale.4: A localized visible edit preserves the complete effective tuple, with minor redundancy or limited final confirmation.

scale.2: The repository remains intact, but provenance is unclear, recovery is incomplete, or unsupported validation claims are made.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository provenance, recovery, and scope discipline

applies_when: The prefix has begun task-specific investigation of Figure DPI scaling, pickling, or canvas reconstruction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the visible prefix advances from task localization to an exact, semantically correct production intervention for preventing transient display DPI from becoming the logical pickle baseline.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the intervention preserves only FigureCanvasBase state, writes _original_dpi from the current scaled _dpi, mutates the live Figure during serialization, lacks the compatibility fallback, or uses a fixed ratio or platform/backend guard. Claims of application or passing behavior without visible supporting evidence cannot raise the anchor.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible source text, exact patch text, successful edit commands followed by source readback or diff, and task-relevant executed output outrank intentions and workspace-summary labels. A scratch patch is evidence of a proposal only; an applied edit requires visible production-file modification or readback. Failed setup, command volume, terminal status, ordinary ratio-one output, and future plans are non-evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Authoritative validation of the edited contour path

applies_when: The selected task requires automatic contour levels to depend on whether the input Z data has boolean dtype
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how far the visible trajectory establishes a correct, repository-specific mechanism for selecting boolean contour defaults. During an early trajectory, a precise source-aligned repair plan may earn intermediate credit even when no final repository diff is present, but implementation and validation credit require visible current source or tests from the edited checkout.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible core contradiction caps the score at 1 unless the trajectory subsequently identifies that exact failure and presents a viable correction. Core contradictions include deriving boolean status from X, Y, or the levels object rather than Z; inspecting Z only after unconditional float coercion; directly requiring a dtype attribute on otherwise accepted array-like input; overriding positional or keyword explicit levels; handling only one accepted Z call form; assigning a single boundary to a shared filled-contour path; malformed code; or validation against a different installation presented as validation of the edit. A failed experiment that exposes its own defect and is followed by a correct causal repair may score 2 or 3 according to the latest visible evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: For claims about implemented behavior, the latest clearly visible repository source, diff, or terminal patch is authoritative, followed by repository-local tests demonstrably importing that edited checkout. A final workspace summary determines whether a change is persisted but does not erase visible early-trajectory evidence of a precise design, a diagnosed failure, or a transient edit. Current source inspection outranks assistant assertions and edit-success messages. Tests against another installation, mock reimplementations, and isolated dtype experiments provide diagnostic evidence only and cannot establish that the repository implementation works.
metadata.failure_mode: This rubric prevents ties between trajectories that merely locate contour code, trajectories that derive the correct original-Z dtype flow, and trajectories that introduce concrete compatibility defects. It also prevents passing tests from an unrelated installation, generic claims of patch success, or a boolean-only happy path from masking explicit-level, argument-form, array-like, or filled-contour regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires either a complete repository-specific repair design tied to the actual argument flow or a coherent visible source edit with no unresolved core contradiction. Score 4 requires a coherent current source edit plus relevant validation demonstrably exercising the edited checkout. Score 5 requires broad edited-checkout validation. Without visible current source, a trajectory cannot exceed 3; without a complete causal design, investigation alone cannot exceed 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace where Z is normalized and where default levels are selected. The mechanism should retain or pass Z's pre-float dtype for both Z-only and X-Y-Z forms, apply the boolean special case only when levels are omitted, and leave explicit positional and keyword levels unchanged. Prefer one shared, source-aligned discriminator over duplicated branch flags. If line and filled contours share the selector, verify that line contours receive 0.5 while filled contours receive enough increasing boundaries. Also distinguish a trajectory that recognizes and repairs a failed approach from one that leaves the same defect unrecognized.
metadata.oracle_test: With two-dimensional boolean Z containing both values, contour(Z) and contour(X, Y, Z) use exactly [0.5] when levels are omitted. Positional and keyword explicit levels remain unchanged. Numeric Z retains ordinary automatic level selection. Accepted list-like or masked-array Z inputs do not fail because the original object lacks a dtype attribute. If the modified selector is shared with filled contours, boolean contourf receives valid increasing boundaries such as [0, 0.5, 1]. All implementation-validation tests import the edited checkout rather than another installed version.

scale.1: The trajectory is materially confused about the argument flow, leaves no viable repository-specific correction, or contains an unresolved core contradiction such as checking the wrong object, overriding explicit levels, unsafe dtype access, malformed code, or invalid shared filled-contour behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory locates relevant code and makes useful progress, or recognizes a concrete failed approach, but its latest visible plan remains incomplete, ambiguous, or unsupported on a required causal discriminator such as original-Z dtype, omitted-versus-explicit levels, both argument forms, or shared filled behavior.

Current edited-checkout validation is absent or incomplete.
scale.4: The current visible repository implementation satisfies score 3 and repository-local validation demonstrably using the edited checkout covers the boolean line default, explicit-level preservation, and ordinary numeric behavior, with at most minor gaps in additional argument-form, array-like, or filled-contour coverage.
scale.5: The current implementation is coherent and edited-checkout tests cover Z-only and X-Y-Z calls, positional and keyword explicit levels, numeric automatic levels, accepted array-like inputs, and valid filled-contour behavior wherever the selector is shared, with no unresolved contradiction.

If that exact defect is later identified and removed or replaced, score the corrected latest evidence instead. Cap at 2 when an applied edit avoids those failures only by ad hoc duplicated state or direct branch-local level mutation with a material form or caller gap.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible local source excerpt or repository diff is authoritative for applied behavior. Earlier transient edits remain evidence unless a later visible correction replaces or removes them. Local call-site inspection outranks an implementation copied from another installation. An external implementation is design evidence only until its assumptions and all changed local callers are explicitly mapped to this checkout.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating a proposed upstream-shaped patch with an applied local integration, overlooking a broken secondary caller after a signature change, or rewarding branch-local boolean flags that appear correct for one happy path but regress array-like inputs, explicit levels, the alternate call form, or contourf.

metadata.judge_focus: Trace the actual local call graph from QuadContourSet argument parsing through _process_contour_level_args, including both Z-only and X-Y-Z forms and every caller of any changed shared helper. Distinguish a source-mapped proposal from code actually applied. Check whether normalization safely supplies a dtype for accepted list-like or masked input and whether line and filled defaults are selected centrally rather than by incompatible duplicated mutations.

With omitted levels, contour(Z) and contour(X, Y, Z) select [0.5] for boolean Z; a shared contourf path selects increasing boundaries such as [0, 0.5, 1]. Explicit positional and keyword levels and ordinary numeric defaults remain unchanged. Every local caller of a modified shared selector, including triangular contour code when applicable, still supplies the required information.

scale.1: The latest visible applied code has an unresolved core integration contradiction, such as checking the wrong object or time, unsafe raw dtype access, explicit-level interference, invalid filled defaults, malformed flow, or a broken shared caller.
scale.2: Relevant source flow is located or partially edited, but the mechanism remains incomplete, duplicated, or materially uncertain for an accepted Z form, array-like normalization, filled behavior, or a shared caller; no complete safe design is established.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if sentinel values are cast or wrapped to `xa.dtype`; score 1 if any sentinel write visibly precedes widening, the reported `uint8` path remains narrow, broad warning suppression is used, or a supported path aliases a special row because its destination is non-representable.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible production source or complete diff outranks comments, claimed passes, source-string checks, simulations, and runs against copied or installed code; direct edited-source execution corroborates but cannot override contradictory source.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking Python `int(...)` or `np.array(sentinel).astype(xa.dtype)` for destination widening, overlooking unsigned or masked paths, or trusting runtime evidence from code that is not the latest visible production source.

scale.2: The immediate warning is avoided by explicitly overflowing, clipping, or narrowing sentinel values, so distinct representable sentinel indices are not preserved.
scale.3: A production promotion handles the reported numeric path, but visible dtype-kind exclusions, placement ambiguity, or another concrete path leaves complete pre-assignment representability unresolved.
scale.4: All visible supported paths are widened before sentinel assignment and preserve distinct indices, but placement relative to float classification or another concrete compatibility detail remains uncertain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal consistency of the latest production state

applies_when: Visible repository production source, a production diff, or a submitted production patch establishes or changes PSD normalization inside `lib/matplotlib/mlab.py::_spectral_helper`.
Visible production evidence changes nearby magnitude, complex, angle, or phase handling in the same normalization block.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate the latest effective production implementation of `_spectral_helper`. Density PSD scaling must divide by `Fs` and window energy `(window**2).sum()` or its real-window equivalent. Non-density PSD scaling must divide by the square of the signed coherent sum `window.sum()**2`. If nearby output modes are changed, magnitude must retain `np.abs(result)`, magnitude and complex may use the signed window sum, and angle and phase must remain unnormalized.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest production density branch using `window.sum()**2`, lacking `Fs`, using a malformed energy expression, or otherwise not using window energy is capped at 1 regardless of a correct non-density branch or successful demonstrations. If density is correct but non-density uses coefficient magnitudes, window energy, or another non-coherent denominator, cap at 2. Correct PSD formulas with visibly damaged magnitude, angle, or phase semantics cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest inspected repository source or complete production diff wins over reasoning, comments, scalar demonstrations, test banners, and summaries. A later complete hunk wins over older source views. Added and removed diff lines establish the effective edit; unchanged lines omitted from a focused diff retain their most recent visible production state. Proposed formulas and independently reconstructed calculations are not implementation evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating blanket removal of `np.abs` as correctness, overlooking a density branch changed to coherent gain, collapsing both PSD branches to window energy, or assigning the same severity to a correct-density residual defect and a density-semantics regression.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require production evidence establishing both effective PSD formulas: density division by `Fs` and window energy, and non-density division by signed coherent gain squared. Score 5 additionally requires every visibly touched magnitude, complex, angle, or phase operation to remain semantically valid.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect both PSD branches in the latest effective production hunk, including the preceding `Fs` division; do not infer density correctness merely because the non-density signed-sum line is correct. Inspect required output-mode operations only when those lines are touched.
metadata.oracle_test: Effective density denominator is `Fs * (window**2).sum()`; effective non-density denominator is `window.sum()**2`. For a negative-valued real window, implementation output should satisfy `spec * win.sum()**2 == spec_a * Fs * (win**2).sum()` within tolerance, while magnitude output still applies `np.abs(result)`.
metadata.stage: Apply and immediately verify the focused edit

scale.1: Production evidence confirms an incorrect density branch, regardless of the non-density branch: the `Fs` factor is lost or misplaced, coherent gain is used instead of window energy, both branches use coherent gain, or the density energy expression is malformed.
scale.2: Density scaling is correctly divided by `Fs` and window energy, but non-density scaling is confirmed to use the sum of coefficient magnitudes, window energy, or another expression instead of the square of the signed window sum.
scale.3: Both PSD branches are correct, but production evidence confirms a separate required semantic regression in touched nearby code, such as removing `np.abs(result)` from magnitude output or normalizing angle or phase output.
scale.4: Both PSD formulas are established as correct, but concrete conflicting or truncated production evidence leaves the effective state of a visibly touched magnitude, complex, angle, or phase operation unresolved.
scale.5: The latest effective production state divides density PSD by `Fs` and window energy and divides non-density PSD by signed coherent gain squared. Any touched magnitude, complex, angle, and phase operations remain valid. Focused non-density fixes, two-site PSD fixes, complete consistency fixes, equivalent real-window energy spelling, working-tree source, and applicable patches receive equal credit.

scale.2: Exactly one axis has the required explicit-and-inherited behavior while the other remains original, missing, or unresolved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current two-axis color-resolution semantics

reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether an active canvas-removal implementation leaves a safe runtime canvas path and preserves the state needed for draggable interaction after loading.

Cap at 2 if canvas is removed but runtime access is absent or eager restoration depends on a partially restored artist.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active repository source and cutoff diff override earlier commands, proposed snippets, comments, and reverted edits. Attributable executed load or interaction failures override structural claims of safety.
metadata.failure_mode: Canvas removal is credited as intermediate progress only after the gate; unsafe restoration or deletion of required interaction state limits higher credit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 1 require an active task-source implementation that actually omits the stored canvas from pickle state or removes the persistent canvas assignment.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff implementation for retention of ref_artist, non-persistent canvas access, callback fields, the caller's effective blitting preference, and restoration-order safety. Do not score inspected source, proposed code, failed insertions, reverted edits, comments, or future plans as the implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare DraggableBase state handling with the property design `canvas -> ref_artist.figure.canvas`, while preserving callback registrations and `use_blit and canvas.supports_blit` semantics.
metadata.stage: Form the fix and restoration model

scale.1: No active qualifying implementation exists, or the active implementation retains the actual canvas, targets the wrong key, mutates live state during dumping, destroys the only runtime reference path, or has an observed central failure.
scale.2: The actual canvas is omitted, but runtime canvas access is absent or eagerly restored unsafely, or ref_artist, callbacks, or blitting state are substantially deleted.
scale.3: The actual canvas is non-persistent and ref_artist or another plausible runtime path remains, but restoration ordering, callbacks, or blitting semantics are materially unresolved.
scale.4: Canvas access is safely derived or lazily restored and the existing reference, callback, and blitting structures are preserved, with only limited unverified compatibility details.
scale.5: The active shared-base design uses non-persistent runtime canvas access, avoids unpickle-order dependence and live-state mutation, and structurally preserves the original callback and effective blitting semantics for legends and annotations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Runtime restoration and interaction-state preservation

applies_when: A source intervention or exact implementation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates only concrete contradictions or observed failures that undermine the attempted serialization correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Visible implementation contradiction

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-attributed discriminative evidence

applies_when: Apply to every trajectory. First inspect the actual production diff; do not use terminal status or plans as a substitute.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores only executable task-relevant behavior visibly present in production source. No production edit and an unconditionally non-executable production attempt both use score 1.

metadata.failure_mode: Giving midpoint credit to unchanged source, plans, scratch scripts, failed rewrite commands, or nonterminal trajectories
metadata.judge_focus: Visible assignment target, copy semantics, effective name, statement order, registry policy, pyplot input handling, and directly visible equality behavior
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the exact production hunk and determine what executes on registration and set_cmap paths
metadata.stage: Implement registry snapshot normalization and narrow equality semantics

scale.1: No task-relevant production statement changed, the attempted rewrite did not alter the intended source, or the shown production path is unconditionally non-executable before task behavior.
scale.2: An executable production edit affects a relevant path but is consumer-only, mutates the caller, directly stores caller-owned state, or otherwise supplies only limited contract coverage.
scale.3: The registry boundary is concretely changed with substantial task coverage, including a copy-based normalization attempt, but a snapshot, subclass, policy, naming, equality, or compatibility concern remains. A correct registry-only copy-rename-store change without the equality change also uses this anchor.
scale.4: The effective name is preserved under existing registration policy, the caller's colormap is copied, only the copy is renamed and stored in executable order, and relevant compatibility behavior is visibly preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production contract fidelity

applies_when: Apply to every trajectory, including unfinished trajectories, unchanged repositories, malformed edits, and failed executions.

metadata.failure_mode: Conflating a malformed implementation with an incorrect conceptual boundary, requiring every causal link before crediting a correctly justified snapshot repair, or rewarding mere browsing volume

This score does not require a correct implementation or successful runtime execution and may be earned from the key-versus-copied-name inconsistency even if some consumer-chain details remain incomplete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable decision quality

metadata.judge_focus: Checkout provenance, source and retrieved names, caller immutability, rcParams persistence, implicit plotting, and executed equality boundaries

applies_when: Select when judging task-relevant production implementation present at the trajectory cutoff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff production contract implementation

applies_when: Select when evaluating runtime validation visible by the trajectory cutoff.

If execution fails before the relevant assertion, it provides no credit for that assertion. Explicit imshow(cmap=...) cannot establish the rcParams-driven implicit path.

applies_when: Always apply when any graphics-context, renderer, backend, metrics, vector, or math-expression reasoning, inspection, edit, or validation is observable.

scale.2: A GC or backend site is identified, but the artist-to-GC-to-consumer chain is disconnected or a central rendering or scope contradiction is present.
scale.3: Text-to-GC propagation and ordinary Agg consumption are correctly connected, with Cairo or at least two scope boundaries still unresolved.
scale.4: Text.draw, ordinary Agg, ordinary Cairo, metrics, and the math-expression boundary are correctly connected, with at most one localized representation or validation detail unresolved.

applies_when: Always apply when any Text or Annotation antialias reasoning, source inspection, edit, or validation is observable.

metadata.judge_focus: Score explicitly connected obligations, not file discovery, edit count, or finality.

scale.2: Some relevant property elements are identified, but a central contradiction is present or most obligations remain disconnected.

applies_when: Select when the cutoff workspace can be inspected for task-relevant runtime source changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A malformed hunk earns no implementation credit. If a purported invariant is neutralized by another retained statement, such as a backend still overriding the GC with rcParams, credit only the independent invariants that remain behaviorally valid.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace and retained diff override all earlier edit attempts and prose. If status or diff shows no task-relevant runtime edit, the score is 1. A later displayed restoration overrides an earlier malformed edit only when the corrected retained unit is visible.

metadata.oracle_test: Inspect retained Text constructor/reset state, public accessors, stale behavior, update_from, Text.draw GC setup, ordinary Agg consumption, and ordinary Cairo consumption.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct runtime behavior retained in the active diff

applies_when: Always apply by inspecting the retained diff, repository status, complete syntactic units, and retained artifacts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete retained defects that prevent execution, corrupt requested behavior, obscure review, or contaminate the artifact.

metadata.oracle_test: Inspect signatures, delimiters, method boundaries, executable calls, undefined names, conflict markers, copied source files, generated artifacts, missing core files, and whether a displayed repair removed the defect.

scale.1: No retained blocking source defect or repository artifact risk is observable.
scale.2: Only a removable scratch artifact or minor localized non-blocking issue is retained.
scale.3: One localized blocking core defect or several minor retained defects are observable.
scale.4: A severe syntax or construction defect, multiple blocking core defects, or malformed code plus artifact contamination is retained.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retained blocking defects and artifact risk

applies_when: Select when the trajectory reasons about or inspects Text or Annotation construction, property access, reset behavior, stale state, or style copying.

Names appearing only in grep output, source listings, tracebacks, or a proposed edit receive no credit unless the assistant correctly connects them. Separately check default capture, explicit values, initialization/reset safety, Annotation forwarding, stale/property dispatch, and update_from.
metadata.oracle_test: A complete account covers construction-time rcParam capture, explicit constructor override, optional reset semantics, safe initialization order, inherited Annotation keyword forwarding, matching getter/setter state, stale marking, generic property dispatch, and update_from copying.

scale.1: No assistant-authored correct property conclusion beyond locating relevant files or symbols.
scale.2: One or two correct property conclusions are visible, but the construction-to-instance-state model is absent, materially incomplete, or contradicted.
scale.3: The assistant correctly connects construction-time boolean capture, explicit override, and inherited Annotation behavior, but at least two secondary obligations remain unaddressed.
scale.4: The complete core model is correct and includes all but one of reset safety, stale/property dispatch, or update_from copying.
