reference_golden_rubrics.title: Per-instance Text property reasoning

applies_when: The visible cutoff contains repository-state evidence and investigation, editing, or validation relevant to the SubFigure spacing defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Classify current causal repair viability using the scale as a strict first-match decision table. The latest repository summary and complete diff determine what is persistent, while the visible trajectory may still establish causal precision, an inspectable attempted implementation, or an exact repair direction. Distinguish speculative propagation theories from the concrete boundary where GridSpec retains spacing but actual SubFigure bounds discard it. Do not reward activity volume, environment setup, rendered output, or stored spacing alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest clean repository cannot receive persistent-edit credit, but may receive up to 4 for an exact, source-grounded repair plan. A wrong-layer edit affecting parent subplot parameters, inner Axes, ordinary subplots, constrained-layout padding, or child layout configuration is capped at 3. An actual-bbox edit that imports ordinary subplot margins, changes omitted or explicit-zero behavior, inverts extents, mishandles spans, or competes with an active layout engine is capped at 4. An incoherent or destructive current artifact scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the latest repository summary, changed-file list, untracked-file list, and complete diff to determine persistence. Use visible source inspection and command output to assess causal understanding and attempted implementation even when the final diff is clean. Repository runtime source and individual SubFigure bbox observations outrank GridSpec attributes, overall tight boxes, rendered images, prose claims, and mixed-version installed-package results.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents clean but materially different investigations from collapsing into one score, while still withholding persistent implementation credit when the authoritative diff is empty. It also separates exact canonical repair directions from speculative spacing propagation and wrong-layer configuration changes.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires an inspectable persistent repository runtime edit that reaches actual SubFigure bounds. Score 4 requires either such a bbox edit with incomplete compatibility evidence or an exact source-grounded plan that identifies canonical spacing geometry and the necessary compatibility guards. Scores 1 through 3 do not require a persistent edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine persistence first, then classify the strongest currently demonstrated causal leverage: incoherent direction, speculative investigation, concrete spacing-loss boundary, exact canonical repair or actual-bbox edit, or complete persistent repair.
metadata.oracle_test: The decisive observable is individual SubFigure bbox_relative or pixel-space bbox geometry. A sound repair uses full-parent spacing-aware GridSpec positions, keeps explicit zero adjacent and unmanaged omitted spacing unchanged, preserves top-row orientation and ordered extents, and leaves layout-engine-provided bboxes authoritative.

scale.1: The current artifact is destructive, malformed, or incoherent, or the investigation commits to a causally contradicted direction without a concrete recovery—for example treating inner Axes placement or child layout configuration as the SubFigure-bbox repair.
scale.2: No persistent repair exists, and the visible work remains generic, speculative, indirect, or dominated by environment and mixed-installation activity. It may confirm that spacing values are stored or images differ, but it does not isolate how actual SubFigure bounds lose the spacing.
scale.3: The work establishes a concrete task-specific causal boundary—such as GridSpec retaining spacing while the ratio-only SubFigure transform omits it—but does not present an exact compatible repair. This also includes a localized, inspectable wrong-layer edit whose effect is clear but does not update actual SubFigure bounds.
scale.4: Either an exact source-grounded repair direction is demonstrated without a persistent final edit, including canonical full-parent GridSpec positions, actual bbox updates, explicit-versus-omitted handling, and layout-engine authority; or an inspectable runtime edit reaches actual SubFigure geometry but has incomplete validation or a remaining compatibility risk.
scale.5: The latest persistent repository runtime edit applies canonical spacing-aware geometry to actual SubFigure bounds and visibly preserves full-parent edges, explicit-zero and omitted-spacing semantics, ordered row-major extents, relevant ratio or nesting behavior, and authoritative layout-engine bbox overrides.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest persistent causal repair state

applies_when: The visible prefix contains an attempted source change, patch, or completion claim addressing hexbin mincnt behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work applies the inclusive mincnt threshold to the C-supplied hexbin path and, when a completion response is present, delivers that change as a usable repository patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if a completion response is visible but does not provide a usable patch despite earlier correct edits. Cap at 1 if visible source or diff evidence retains the strict comparison, changes the no-C branch instead, reverses the threshold, or otherwise contradicts the required inclusive behavior.

Without a terminal completion, observed repository edits and git diff output are authoritative.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for a correct verbal diagnosis, simulated demonstration, or local edit when the visible completion artifact is absent or cannot be applied as a patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible evidence that the C-supplied accumulation condition was changed from a strict threshold to an inclusive threshold. Score 5 additionally requires a terminal, syntactically usable unified diff.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the edited hexbin implementation or an actual diff for the C-supplied branch, then inspect any visible completion response for a usable unified diff containing that edit. A documentation clarification from 'more than' to 'at least' is compatible but not required.

metadata.evidence_authority: Quoted or displayed repository source takes precedence over recollection, issue paraphrases, simulated logic, or behavior observed from an unrelated installed Matplotlib version.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for locating hexbin or mentioning mincnt without identifying the off-by-one comparison that causally produces the reported behavior.

metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires a successful mutation-sensitive execution after the visible source edit and affirmative evidence that the exercised module came from the evaluator-facing checkout.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the temporal order of edits and checks, the imported module path, the constructor actually exercised, the mutation timing, and the literal output. Setup failures, syntax checks, standalone tuple or copy experiments, pre-edit observations, and behavior from another installation are not successful post-edit validation.
metadata.oracle_test: After constructing `_AnnotationBase` and `OffsetFrom` through the edited checkout, mutate each caller-owned two-element container and verify that the stored coordinate or resulting placement remains based on the original values.

scale.1: A claimed validation conclusion is visibly contradicted by its output, or a known source-tree mismatch is represented as edited-checkout behavior despite contrary path evidence.
scale.2: A successful-looking mutation result from an unidentified, separately installed, or otherwise non-target source tree is relied on as task validation, without resolving the mismatch; no stronger direct contradiction qualifies for 1.
scale.3: No successful post-edit mutation check from the target checkout is claimed: checks are absent, fail before exercising the constructor, occur before the edit, or are explicitly recognized as non-authoritative.
scale.4: A successful post-edit mutation check from the identified target checkout validates at least one affected constructor path, but equivalent evidence for both annotation coordinates and `OffsetFrom` is not established.
scale.5: Successful post-edit checks from the identified target checkout validate both annotation-coordinate and `OffsetFrom` mutation independence, with relevant compatibility or focused regression evidence also passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: [R5] Mutation-validation evidence reliability

applies_when: A trajectory investigates or changes how compiled seaborn.objects axes are finalized from scale information.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses the actual compiled scale associated with each subplot coordinate to trigger nominal-axis treatment, covering inferred and explicit Nominal scales without changing unrelated continuous, temporal, ordinal, or non-coordinate mappings.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if activation depends only on string dtype, only on explicit p._scales entries, only on a particular mark, or globally modifies every axis in the figure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository-backed data-flow tracing and applied diffs outrank guesses based on variable dtype, mark orientation, tick-label strings, or user scale declarations alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Implementing the visible effect in legacy categorical.py, applying it globally, or missing inferred/faceted/paired coordinate scales.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a concrete and plausible mapping from each rendered x/y axis to its resolved Nominal scale.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible code or concrete design tracing Plotter scale setup, subplot axis keys, paired/faceted coordinates, and final axis objects.
metadata.oracle_test: Both Plot(data, x='category') with inferred scale and Plot(...).scale(x=Nominal()) receive nominal treatment on every applicable subplot, while a continuous coordinate remains unchanged.

scale.1: Does not locate the relevant objects-API scale and plotting path, or targets an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Finds Nominal and figure-finalization code but has no viable per-axis scale resolution, or proposes an over-broad proxy.
scale.3: Traces most of the scale/subplot data flow and proposes a plausible boundary, but leaves inferred or multi-subplot handling unresolved.
scale.4: Provides or applies a coherent per-axis implementation that is driven by resolved Nominal scale identity and excludes unrelated scales.
scale.5: Applies a minimal, well-integrated implementation with clear handling of inferred, explicit, shared, faceted, or paired coordinate axes and no proxy-based activation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Targets the compiled coordinate scale at the correct implementation boundary

applies_when: The task concerns coordinate axes backed by explicit or inferred seaborn.objects Nominal scales.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that a nominal coordinate axis must reproduce the categorical-axis contract: half-step outer bounds, no grid on that coordinate axis, and reversed category order when the nominal coordinate is y.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims ordinary matplotlib margins are sufficient, proposes inverting nominal x axes, or treats only explicitly supplied so.Nominal scales as affected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed observations and repository source such as categorical axis adjustment code outrank unsupported descriptions; task text outranks speculation about desired semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Over-crediting generic repository exploration or a partial diagnosis that notices only limits, grid, or inversion.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires all three behaviors and explicit recognition that inferred Nominal scales are in scope.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning or code that connects Nominal coordinate scales to all three categorical-axis behaviors and distinguishes x from y behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For categories at positions 0 through n-1, x bounds are (-0.5, n-0.5); y bounds are (n-0.5, -0.5); gridlines on the nominal coordinate are suppressed.

scale.1: Shows no task-specific diagnosis or materially misstates categorical-axis behavior.
scale.2: Recognizes nominal data as categorical but establishes only one behavior, or includes a substantive semantic error.
scale.3: Correctly establishes at least two behaviors and identifies relevant legacy/core code, but omits the third behavior or inferred-scale scope.
scale.4: Correctly explains all three behaviors and explicit/inferred scope, with source-backed comparison to existing categorical plotting behavior.
scale.5: Provides a complete source-backed causal account, including x versus y orientation, category-position bounds, and why normal autoscale margins do not satisfy the contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly diagnoses nominal-coordinate axis semantics

applies_when: The repository exposes seaborn.objects plotting tests or a runnable environment capable of inspecting matplotlib axis state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or executes focused checks that directly observe nominal limits, grid visibility, and y-axis direction for inferred and explicit scales, while protecting continuous-axis and multi-subplot behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if tests do not run, only create an image, exercise only legacy categorical functions, or report failures without isolating implementation behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing targeted repository tests with assertions outrank ad hoc scripts; successful direct state inspection outranks saved images or unevaluated proposed tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding dependency installation, API trial-and-error, generic test execution, or plots saved without semantic assertions as decisive validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successfully executed task-specific assertion or an applied focused test suite covering the three required semantics.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test additions, test commands, outputs, and direct matplotlib state assertions rather than image creation alone.
metadata.oracle_test: Tests inspect exact x/y limits, nominal-axis gridline visibility under a grid-enabled theme, and y inversion; coverage includes inferred Nominal and explicit Nominal, with at least one non-nominal regression case.

scale.1: No task-specific test plan or runtime evidence is visible.
scale.2: Attempts a reproducer or installs dependencies, but execution fails or no relevant axis property is asserted.
scale.3: Creates a valid baseline or detailed focused test plan that checks some required properties, but lacks successful post-change assertions or complete semantic coverage.
scale.4: Adds or successfully runs focused assertions for all three behaviors, with either inferred/explicit coverage or a non-nominal regression check.
scale.5: Shows passing targeted tests for all three behaviors across inferred and explicit Nominal scales, plus mixed-scale or faceted/shared regression protection and relevant existing tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provides focused regression tests and executable evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix contains investigation, implementation, or validation work concerning nominal coordinate-axis rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate how far the trajectory has visibly advanced from source inspection to an applied and empirically checked solution for nominal-axis limits, grid suppression, and y-axis inversion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when all proposed implementation or testing remains unapplied. Cap at 2 when the prefix repeatedly inspects relevant code but never resolves a concrete causal path. Any applied change that visibly conflicts with the categorical reference behavior or breaks a relevant test caps the score at 1 until corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output, repository diffs, and test results outrank thoughts, plans, and claimed conclusions. The changed-files and git-diff summaries control whether work was actually applied. A failed probe is evidence only of an attempted check, not of the behavior it intended to verify.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents granting implementation credit for a correct-sounding plan, repeated reading of the same files, dependency installation alone, or a plotting script that fails before observing any task-relevant behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a successful focused execution or a visible applied repository change. Score 5 additionally requires automated validation of the applied behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository commands and outputs, successful task-specific plotting probes, diffs in scale or figure-finalization code, and tests that assert half-step limits, disabled nominal-axis gridlines, and inverted nominal y axes.
metadata.oracle_test: For coordinate variables using an explicit or inferred Nominal scale, compare against seaborn's categorical-axis semantics: the visible range spans one half unit outside the first and last category positions, gridlines on that nominal axis are suppressed by default, and a nominal y axis is ordered in the categorical direction by inversion; explicit limits and supported user overrides must remain coherent.

scale.1: A visible applied change or asserted conclusion contradicts the nominal-axis reference behavior, causes a relevant failure, or targets an unrelated mechanism, and the contradiction remains unresolved.
scale.2: Work remains exploratory: relevant files may be inspected, but no stable causal implementation path is established and no successful focused probe or repository change is visible.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly localizes the scale-to-axis finalization path and specifies a concrete, task-appropriate implementation and validation approach, but neither a successful focused probe nor an applied change is visible.
scale.4: The trajectory produces either a successful task-focused execution that observes relevant axis behavior or a visible implementation change with partial validation, but the complete three-part behavior is not yet covered by passing automated checks.
scale.5: A visible implementation is accompanied by passing focused automated checks covering nominal half-step limits, nominal-axis grid suppression, and nominal y-axis inversion, including relevant explicit or inferred scale cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed progress on nominal coordinate-axis behavior

applies_when: The proposed fix can affect formatter types, rcParam-dependent formatting, or multiple seaborn APIs that generate numeric legends.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects ordinary numeric legends and formatter diversity while covering the affected seaborn.objects path and, where applicable, the scatterplot path reported by the task.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A ScalarFormatter-only type check, private-state dependency, unconditional suffix, or failure of normal-range/custom-formatter behavior caps credit at 2; testing only one API caps at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed targeted and existing test results outrank unsupported compatibility claims; public `Formatter.get_offset()` behavior outranks ScalarFormatter-private-attribute assumptions.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the demonstrated `1e6` example with a numeric hack that breaks ordinary values, additive offsets, mathtext, localized labels, engineering formatters, or the second reported plotting API.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence that an empty `get_offset()` leaves existing labels unchanged and that the implementation does not assume every offset or label is directly float-parseable.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, or diff behavior for empty offsets, non-ScalarFormatter instances, additive offsets, scientific scaling, formatter-produced mathtext/locale strings, and both reported plotting interfaces.
metadata.oracle_test: Every Matplotlib `Formatter` exposes `get_offset()`; an empty result must be a no-op, while nonempty scientific or additive text must remain semantically attached to the legend without corrupting custom formatting.

scale.1: Ignores compatibility and proposes behavior that visibly breaks ordinary formatting or semantic mapping.
scale.2: Handles only one hard-coded ScalarFormatter case or depends on parseable decimal/scientific strings.
scale.3: Uses the public formatter interface and recognizes the empty-offset no-op, but provides no compatibility evidence.
scale.4: Provides focused evidence for affected and unaffected formatter cases, while covering only one reported plotting path or leaving one material edge case open.
scale.5: Demonstrates no-op behavior for ordinary/custom formatters, correct scientific and additive-offset semantics, and regression protection for both relevant seaborn plotting paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Formatter and plotting-path compatibility protection

applies_when: The trajectory encounters inconsistent offset results, failed reproductions, or confusion between seaborn plot, plotter, scale, and Matplotlib axis APIs.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory evidence by correcting the experimental setup, isolating the formatter lifecycle, and converging on conclusions supported by the repository's actual legend-generation path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Repeatedly drawing conclusions from tracebacks, unrelated axes, stale formatter state, or nonexistent APIs without correcting them caps credit at 2; unresolved mutually inconsistent conclusions cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later controlled reproduction using the same `PseudoAxis` or scale setup as production supersedes earlier failed or contradictory experiments only when the contradiction is explicitly resolved.
metadata.failure_mode: Accumulating exploratory commands while treating each transient result as authoritative, leading to incorrect fixes such as dividing/multiplying labels or changing the mapped point sizes.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a successful controlled reproduction after earlier contradictory observations, with a clear explanation of why the earlier observation was invalid.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible correction of wrong dataset names, rendering APIs, axis selection, locator invocation, formatter attachment, view interval, and pre/post-`format_ticks` state observations.
metadata.oracle_test: The controlled sequence is: attach formatter through an axis or `PseudoAxis`, set the relevant view interval, obtain/filter locator values, call `format_ticks`, then inspect `get_offset()` and the resulting semantic legend data.

scale.1: Persists with invalid experiments or ends with a conclusion contradicted by its own visible evidence.
scale.2: Notices setup problems but continues to rely on failed calls, wrong axes, or pre-initialized formatter state.
scale.3: Corrects some mistakes and obtains relevant evidence, but leaves major contradictions unresolved.
scale.4: Builds a valid controlled reproduction, explains prior contradictory results, and uses it to narrow the fix boundary.
scale.5: Systematically reconciles all material contradictions with production-faithful evidence and derives a precise, formatter-safe implementation and test strategy.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from contradictory formatter experiments

applies_when: The trajectory executes a reproduction, inspection, patch check, or regression test involving a continuous numeric semantic legend.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates with executable evidence whether a continuous seaborn semantic legend preserves the magnitude represented by raw large-number values when its formatter emits shortened labels.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the only successful evidence concerns x/y coordinate ticks, an absent legend, unchanged artist sizes, or a standalone formatter, cap at 3. A failing post-change semantic assertion or a final empty diff caps applied-work credit at 3, while unrelated setup failures do not erase an otherwise successful authoritative reproduction.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing assertion against the current repository's semantic legend is strongest. Next is successful inspection of seaborn scale `_legend` values and labels. A standalone formatter experiment is weaker even when correct. The final working-tree summary and git diff determine whether code or tests were actually applied; prose claiming a fix cannot override an empty diff.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding post-fix credit for rendering a figure, inspecting coordinate ticks, describing a future test, or observing shortened formatter labels without checking the semantic legend produced by seaborn.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied repository change followed by a successful inspection or assertion showing that raw million-scale semantic values are communicated by the resulting legend. Credit of 5 additionally requires automated regression coverage in the repository.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect successful commands that expose raw semantic legend locations together with their labels, or post-change assertions against scale `_legend` data or rendered legend text. Distinguish these from coordinate-axis ticks, standalone formatter output, image creation without text inspection, and proposed but unapplied checks.
metadata.oracle_test: Given continuous semantic values near 3e6 and 4e6, the legend text must unambiguously denote those raw magnitudes, for example as `3e6` and `4e6` or as shortened labels accompanied by an equivalent shared scale indicator.

scale.1: No successful evidence about numeric semantic-legend text is present, or the trajectory's successful observations concern only an unrelated object and support a contradicted conclusion.
scale.2: A relevant reproduction is attempted, but setup or API failures prevent both a valid formatter demonstration and inspection of a seaborn semantic legend.
scale.3: A successful pre-fix experiment establishes the magnitude-loss symptom, either through a standalone formatter with paired raw locations and shortened labels or through direct inspection of the affected seaborn semantic legend, but no applied post-fix semantic check succeeds.
scale.4: An applied repository change is followed by a successful focused inspection or assertion showing that an affected seaborn semantic legend now communicates the raw large-number magnitudes, but durable automated regression coverage is absent.
scale.5: The repository contains and passes focused automated regression coverage that exercises the affected seaborn semantic scale or rendered legend and rejects shortened labels lacking their required magnitude indicator.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable magnitude evidence for numeric semantic legends

applies_when: Select this rubric when the trajectory investigates formatter behavior or continuous numeric semantic-legend generation through runtime observations, source inspection, or both.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether exploration converges to a stable, evidence-supported account that raw semantic legend locations remain intact while formatter-generated labels can omit separately presented magnitude information, with credit determined by the strongest valid causal observation and the trajectory's final treatment of contradictory experiments.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Failed calls and speculative parsing ideas do not by themselves cap credit when they are visibly abandoned. Cap at 2 when the final operative account still relies on an unrelated coordinate axis, stale pre-format formatter state, nonexistent APIs, altered raw locations, or parsing and multiplying rendered strings. Cap at 3 when a valid causal observation is later left in direct conflict with the trajectory's concluding mechanism.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct inspection of a seaborn semantic scale or legend pairing raw locations with displayed labels outranks standalone formatter experiments. A controlled formatter attached to a valid axis or production-like pseudo-axis outranks informal calculations. Within the same authority level, later evidence supersedes earlier evidence only when the trajectory explains the setup difference; an unexplained later contradiction does not erase the earlier observation but prevents convergence credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring command volume, source familiarity, or an isolated successful formatter call as convergence even though the trajectory finishes with incompatible lifecycle claims or adopts a brittle reconstruction mechanism.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires at least one successful observation pairing raw large-number locations with shortened labels or showing public formatter-wide magnitude text after those locations are processed. Credit above 3 requires the final account to reconcile material empty-versus-nonempty offset observations and to reject changes to semantic locations and numeric interpretation of rendered strings.
metadata.judge_focus: First identify the strongest successful causal observation, distinguishing semantic `_legend` data from coordinate ticks and valid attached-formatter experiments from failed setup. Then inspect the trajectory's latest supported account: whether it preserves raw locations, treats magnitude as formatter-wide presentation, explains conflicting offset results, and abandons rather than operationalizes brittle parsing proposals.
metadata.oracle_test: A production-faithful investigation can show raw legend locations around millions paired with shortened labels. Processing those locations may initialize separate formatter-wide scientific or additive text. The defect is loss of that presentation context, not corruption of the raw semantic locations or mapped artist values.

scale.1: No successful task-relevant causal observation is obtained, or the trajectory ends with a mechanism contradicted by its own authoritative evidence.
scale.2: It identifies the general source area or large-number symptom, but successful evidence is confined to unrelated objects or the final account still depends on failed setup, stale formatter state, or numeric reconstruction of rendered text.
scale.3: It obtains one valid causal observation—such as raw semantic locations paired with shortened labels, or shortened labels paired with post-format public magnitude text—but leaves lifecycle conflicts unresolved or does not connect the observation reliably to the production legend boundary.
scale.4: It combines production-boundary evidence with a valid formatter observation, preserves raw semantic locations, rejects parsing-based reconstruction, and explicitly explains the material contradictory results, yielding a coherent implementation target.
scale.5: It efficiently triangulates production semantic-legend data, formatter lifecycle behavior, and relevant source flow; reconciles every material contradiction; and derives a precise formatter-safe implementation and regression-test target without unsupported detours in the final account.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Convergence to a stable causal account of legend magnitude loss

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or performs a change to continuous numeric semantic-legend label construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Progresses from locating the legend-label boundary to a concrete repository change that formats raw legend locations, retrieves public formatter-wide presentation text afterward, and communicates it without parsing formatter output or altering semantic locations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Parsing, converting, multiplying, or dividing rendered labels or offset strings; replacing raw legend locations with scaled values; changing global formatter settings; or depending on formatter-private state caps credit at 2. A final empty diff caps credit at 3. A claimed or temporary edit cannot override the final working-tree state.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final working-tree summary and visible diff determine whether production code or tests are applied. A final diff outranks temporary edits and prose claims. In the absence of a diff, exact safe pseudocode outranks general intent, while formatter strings remain opaque presentation rather than numeric data.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating source diagnosis as implementation, accepting a temporary or vanished edit as applied work, or reconstructing numeric values from locale-sensitive, mathtext, additive-offset, or custom-formatter strings.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible final repository edit at the continuous semantic-legend boundary. Credit of 5 additionally requires successful focused verification of the changed semantic legend and no-op behavior when the formatter supplies no shared offset text.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final repository diff first, then the most concrete unapplied edit or pseudocode. Distinguish merely locating `format_ticks(locs)` from explicitly ordering `format_ticks`, public `get_offset`, empty-offset handling, presentation attachment, and preservation of raw `locs`.
metadata.oracle_test: A safe implementation retains raw `locs`, obtains `labels` by formatting those locations, retrieves the formatter's public shared offset text only afterward, and attaches nonempty text to legend presentation without interpreting it numerically; empty text leaves labels unchanged.

scale.1: No concrete legend-label boundary is identified, or the approach would modify mapped data, artist values, or unrelated global formatting.
scale.2: A concrete fix is proposed or attempted, but it parses or numerically reconstructs formatter output, uses private state, hard-codes notation, substitutes raw-value formatting, or otherwise violates formatter presentation semantics.
scale.3: No qualifying final edit is visible, but the trajectory gives an exact safe plan that preserves raw locations, calls `format_ticks` before public `get_offset`, treats the result as opaque presentation text, and makes an empty result a no-op.
scale.4: A visible final production edit implements that ordering and presentation-only behavior while preserving raw semantic locations, but focused successful post-change verification is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: A minimal visible final patch implements the formatter-safe behavior and is followed by successful focused checks for an affected large-number semantic legend and an unaffected empty-offset case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implementation maturity of the formatter-safe legend repair

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters package installation, import-path, dependency, or test-environment ambiguity while evaluating the Blueprint change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory attributes runtime behavior to the correct source and, when execution remains ambiguous, accurately separates that limitation from any independently visible repository implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed repository runtime result based only on site-packages or a separately installed Flask cannot receive runtime credit. Cap at 2 only when no coherent final repository guard is independently visible, or when visible local-source behavior contradicts the claimed fix; otherwise an applied coherent guard may receive score 3 despite untrustworthy runtime attribution.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff or post-edit excerpt establishes whether local source was changed but does not prove execution. A traceback, module path, or command explicitly resolving Flask to the repository establishes runtime authority. External site-packages behavior cannot override repository source and cannot validate its execution.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating external-package behavior as repository validation, or conversely treating an invalid runtime check as proof that no applied repository work exists.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a decisive task-specific check visibly executed from the repository source. Score 3 requires either a coherent final repository guard or an explicit accurate qualification that local execution was not established.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect import paths, tracebacks, PYTHONPATH usage, repository diffs or post-edit source, and whether external-package observations are distinguished from the checked-out implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: Runtime attribution is established when the exercised Blueprint resolves to src/flask/blueprints.py in the checkout and Blueprint("", import_name) raises ValueError. Independently, a displayed final guard in that constructor is static implementation evidence, not execution evidence.

scale.1: The trajectory materially misattributes external behavior to the repository, and the final visible repository state is absent, malformed, reverted, or contradicted by local-source behavior.
scale.2: Runtime authority remains unresolved and no coherent applied empty-name guard is visible in the final repository source; activity is limited to investigation, setup, copying, or proposed work.
scale.3: A coherent empty-name guard is visibly applied in the repository, or the inability to establish local execution is accurately qualified, but decisive runtime evidence is external, mixed, absent, or uncertain.
scale.4: A decisive empty-name check visibly executes the modified repository source, while unrelated installation or suite failures are correctly separated from the feature result.
scale.5: The trajectory explicitly resolves earlier environment conflict, confirms the repository module path, and reruns decisive empty-name and nearby compatibility checks against that source with accurate qualification of unrelated failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-source evidence survives environment ambiguity

applies_when: The visible trajectory concerns validation of the name passed to flask.Blueprint construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation adds creation-time validation in Blueprint.__init__ so an empty name raises ValueError before the Blueprint is initialized with that name.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the final visible repository state has no guard, restores it away, leaves syntactically malformed code, or only changes a temporary or installed copy, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final repository diff or final source excerpt outranks plans, narrated claims, temporary edits, and earlier malformed edits; a later checkout or restoration outranks an earlier modification.
metadata.failure_mode: Giving implementation credit for merely locating the constructor, proposing a guard, editing the wrong copy, or showing an edit that was subsequently reverted.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible evidence that the repository source contains an effective empty-name guard which raises ValueError before self.name is assigned.
metadata.judge_focus: A visible patch, diff, or final source excerpt in src/flask/blueprints.py showing an empty-name guard in Blueprint.__init__ before self.name is assigned.
metadata.oracle_test: Constructing Blueprint("", import_name) raises ValueError immediately, while Blueprint("valid", import_name) remains constructible.

scale.1: No effective repository implementation is visible, or the final visible code clearly still accepts the empty string.
scale.2: The correct location or intended guard is described, but no applied repository change is visible, or the visible edit is malformed, reverted, or in a non-repository copy.
scale.3: An applied guard is visible but its effectiveness or placement is materially uncertain, such as validation after assignment or incomplete final context.
scale.4: An effective ValueError guard for the empty string is visibly applied in Blueprint.__init__ before assignment, but it is broader than necessary, unusually ordered, or uses a less consistent formulation.
scale.5: A clean, minimal guard equivalent to `if not name: raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")` is visibly applied in Blueprint.__init__ before the existing dotted-name check and before self.name assignment.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Blueprint constructor rejects the empty-string name

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime checks, or executable evidence concerning Content-Length behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses task-specific evidence from the real request-preparation code to demonstrate the absence of an automatically generated Content-Length on a bodyless GET and the continued correctness of body-bearing requests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when real execution still shows Content-Length on a default GET or exposes a syntax/runtime failure caused by the change; cap at 3 when only mocks pass while actual-library execution is unavailable or failing for unrelated environment reasons.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful assertions against the actual modified library outrank source-only reasoning; source-only reasoning outranks reimplemented mock logic. A failing real-library test outranks passing simulations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating mock logic, expected-output printouts, or an unrelated import failure as proof that repository behavior is correct.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful visible execution against the repository implementation for the bodyless GET case, not merely a copied helper or hand-calculated simulation.
metadata.judge_focus: Executed assertions or printed headers from Request.prepare or PreparedRequest, targeted repository tests, syntax checks, and clearly reported failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Request('GET', url).prepare() or an equivalent real preparation path has no automatically generated Content-Length header after the change; a request with a concrete body reports its actual byte/body length.

scale.1: No relevant validation evidence, or visible evidence disproves the intended behavior.
scale.2: Only informal reasoning or expected outputs are shown, or attempted tests fail before exercising the relevant code and no stronger evidence is supplied.
scale.3: A focused simulation, extracted-method test, syntax check, or source inspection supports the fix, but the real preparation path is not successfully exercised.
scale.4: The actual repository preparation path successfully demonstrates a bodyless GET without Content-Length and at least one body-bearing request with a correct length.
scale.5: The evidence in 4 is supplemented by focused regression coverage for explicit headers, empty or seekable bodies, authentication recomputation, or streaming behavior, with all shown checks passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive prepared-request evidence

applies_when: The trajectory examines behavior beyond the single default GET reproduction, including bodies, methods, explicit headers, authentication, files, or streams.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves established request-body and header semantics while fixing the reported case, and responds correctly when broader evidence exposes an over-broad or incomplete approach.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if known failing evidence is ignored or the final visible state retains a demonstrated regression; cap at 3 if contradictions are acknowledged but the resulting source state remains unresolved or untested.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed behavior from the repository and final visible source state outrank comments about HTTP conventions; later corrected evidence outranks abandoned earlier assumptions.
metadata.failure_mode: Declaring success after the narrow GET check while silently breaking uploads, encoded data, streams, explicit headers, authentication, or other methods.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires concrete visible consideration of at least two compatibility paths in addition to default GET, one of which must involve a real body or explicit header.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, tests, and revisions covering non-empty bodies, empty-but-present bodies, explicit Content-Length, POST/PUT behavior, seekable bodies, streams, and auth-induced recomputation.
metadata.oracle_test: The fix changes only automatic framing for requests with no body as needed by the task: measurable bodies retain accurate framing, explicit user intent is not silently removed, and secondary preparation paths do not reintroduce the unwanted header.

scale.1: No compatibility analysis, or visible changes indiscriminately remove Content-Length handling.
scale.2: Mentions compatibility concerns but ignores contradictory evidence or leaves a demonstrated regression in the visible final state.
scale.3: Checks at least one adjacent case or revises an initial mistake, but coverage is narrow, simulated only, or leaves an unresolved concern.
scale.4: Shows coherent protection for multiple adjacent paths, including a body-bearing case, and resolves visible contradictions before the cutoff.
scale.5: Demonstrates systematic compatibility across ordinary bodies plus at least one special path such as explicit headers, seekable/streaming bodies, or auth recomputation, with the final visible implementation consistent with all evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and regression protection across body/header paths

applies_when: The trajectory displays an applied source change affecting automatic Content-Length generation or recomputation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied request-preparation code bases automatic Content-Length generation on whether a body is present, consistently across initial preparation and later recomputation, without suppressing valid body lengths or discarding caller-supplied framing.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if final code still synthesizes Content-Length for the ordinary bodyless path, contains a broken signature or wrong-variable guard, or an unresolved executable check shows failure for the bodyless target or an ordinary body-bearing request. Cap at 3 if a method-wide rule suppresses measurable GET/HEAD bodies or a visible secondary path can produce, re-add, or corrupt the header.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final applied repository code outranks explanations and copied logic. A task-relevant executable failure outranks passing simulations. Successful real preparation confirms behavior but cannot excuse a visible secondary path that re-adds, suppresses, or corrupts Content-Length.
metadata.failure_mode: Equating a GET/HEAD blacklist with body awareness, overlooking a later recomputation or stream branch, or granting strong credit after a relevant body-bearing check fails.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied body-presence-based change that reaches the real preparation boundary and does not categorically suppress length computation for every GET or HEAD body.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final applied diff and surrounding flow through prepare_body, stream handling, prepare_content_length, and authentication recomputation. Track body=None separately from empty-but-present and non-empty bodies, and inspect method guards, actual guard variables, existing headers, and task-relevant failed checks.
metadata.oracle_test: Body absence, not the HTTP verb, controls automatic omission: body=None does not synthesize Content-Length; present measurable bodies retain their established length handling; empty-but-present bodies remain distinguishable where the preparation path preserves that distinction; explicit caller headers are not silently deleted.

scale.1: No relevant applied implementation is visible.
scale.2: An applied change exists, but final code still fails the ordinary bodyless target, is structurally broken, or has an unresolved executable contradiction on the target or an ordinary present body.
scale.3: The ordinary bodyless target is fixed, but the implementation uses a method-wide exclusion that suppresses valid body-bearing GET/HEAD framing, or a visible secondary path can generate an incorrect or reintroduced Content-Length.
scale.4: The applied code uses body presence to fix the bodyless target and preserves ordinary non-empty body lengths across visible call paths, but one edge such as empty-but-present bodies, explicit headers, streams, or recomputation remains unresolved or imperfect.
scale.5: The applied code consistently distinguishes absent from present bodies across initial and recomputation paths, preserves measurable and empty-present body semantics, and respects existing caller-supplied Content-Length without any visible contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consistent body-presence framing semantics

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or displays a source change intended to stop automatic Content-Length on GET requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible change is narrowly placed in request preparation and omits automatically generated Content-Length for a GET with no body while retaining correct length handling for requests that actually carry bodies and preserving caller-supplied headers.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible edit still inserts Content-Length for a bodyless GET, is syntactically malformed, or can call len(None); cap at 3 if it suppresses length for non-empty GET bodies, overwrites explicit caller headers, or broadly changes transport behavior without justification.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final diff or current file excerpt outranks earlier proposed edits, prose summaries, or mock implementations.
metadata.failure_mode: Overfitting to the HTTP verb, truthiness, or a single call site in a way that breaks bodyful requests, empty-but-present bodies, authentication recomputation, or explicit headers.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an actual visible source edit at the preparation boundary whose control flow leaves a bodyless GET without an automatically inserted Content-Length.
metadata.judge_focus: The displayed diff or edited source in requests/models.py, including conditions around prepare_body, prepare_content_length, and prepare_auth.
metadata.oracle_test: Preparing a default GET yields no automatic Content-Length; a non-empty encoded, byte, multipart, or seekable body retains an accurate length when determinable; an explicit Content-Length remains available rather than being deleted.

scale.1: No implementation is visible, or the edit is unrelated to request header preparation.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible but is broken or does not prevent automatic Content-Length on a bodyless GET.
scale.3: The edit fixes the reported default GET case but has a visible semantic weakness, such as suppressing all GET/HEAD body lengths, using body truthiness, mishandling explicit headers, or missing a recomputation path.
scale.4: The edit cleanly fixes the bodyless GET path at an appropriate source boundary and preserves ordinary non-empty body length behavior, with no visible regression.
scale.5: The edit satisfies 4 and visibly accounts for explicit headers and all relevant preparation/recomputation paths with a minimal, coherent change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically precise implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains tests, runtime checks, syntax checks, or executable simulations concerning Content-Length preparation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides internally consistent executable evidence that bodyless request preparation omits an automatically generated Content-Length while requests with present bodies retain correct length handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when an executable check reaches the changed logic and visibly fails the bodyless target or ordinary present-body behavior, when patch-caused syntax or call-contract failure remains unresolved, or when final applied source directly contradicts the claimed passing behavior. Do not apply this cap solely because an unrelated dependency or interpreter incompatibility prevents importing the repository.
metadata.evidence_authority: A task-relevant failure from the actual modified library outranks passing simulations. Final applied source that directly contradicts a simulation also outranks that simulation. Successful actual-library preparation outranks source inspection and extracted logic. An import or dependency failure occurring before request preparation is non-evidence about framing behavior and does not by itself contradict a focused simulation.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating every failed command as equally disqualifying, or rewarding passing mock output despite a later relevant assertion failure or contradictory final implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful execution through the repository's real Request.prepare or equivalent PreparedRequest path for a bodyless request and at least one present-body request.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect assertions or printed headers from the repository preparation path, focused helper execution, syntax checks, and every visible task-relevant failure. Determine whether a failed command stopped at unrelated environment setup or actually reached the modified Content-Length logic.
metadata.oracle_test: A real prepared bodyless GET has no synthesized Content-Length; a prepared request with a concrete measurable body has its correct length. Simulations may support this conclusion only when final applied source and all task-relevant observed results are consistent with them.

scale.1: No relevant executable or source-backed validation is shown.
scale.2: Relevant validation is attempted, but a task-relevant failure or contradictory final applied source remains unresolved and defeats the claimed behavior.
scale.3: Focused simulation, helper execution, syntax checking, or source-backed reasoning consistently supports both the bodyless target and present-body length behavior, but the real repository preparation path is unavailable or unexecuted; unrelated environment failures may be present.
scale.4: The real repository preparation path successfully shows no synthesized Content-Length for a bodyless request and a correct length for at least one concrete present body, with no unresolved task-relevant failure.
scale.5: The evidence in 4 is supplemented by passing focused checks for at least two special paths such as an explicit header, an empty-but-present body, a seekable or streaming body, or authentication recomputation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliable prepared-request validation

applies_when: The task concerns automatic Content-Length generation while preparing HTTP requests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible applied code prevents an automatically generated Content-Length header when the prepared request has no body while retaining correct length handling when a body is present.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the applied code still assigns Content-Length on the bodyless path, tests or comments describe a guard absent from the code, the guard reads the request body as though it were the HTTP method, or the changed method signature and its callers are inconsistent. Cap at 3 if a later visible recomputation can undo the fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository code and the final visible diff outrank assistant explanations and simulated tests. Direct tests exercising the real preparation path outrank copied or reimplemented logic. Surrounding source establishes whether another call path can re-add or corrupt the header.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding stated intent or mock tests despite contradictory applied code, or treating method-wide suppression of Content-Length as equivalent to the required body-presence behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible applied source change that reaches the real request-preparation path and prevents automatic Content-Length generation for a bodyless request.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied diff and surrounding request-preparation data flow, including every visible call that initially computes or later recomputes Content-Length. Check the actual guard variables, indentation, and behavior for no body, a non-empty body, an explicitly empty body, seekable bodies, streams, and an existing user-supplied header where those paths are visible.
metadata.oracle_test: Preparing a normal GET with no request body must not synthesize Content-Length. A present body must still receive its correct byte length through the established seek, length, or streaming logic, and an explicit user header must not be silently discarded.

scale.1: No relevant applied change, or the applied change clearly leaves the reported bodyless-request behavior unchanged.
scale.2: A relevant patch is applied, but a visible implementation contradiction, wrong variable, broken call contract, or unconditional assignment means the target path can still add Content-Length or fail.
scale.3: The primary bodyless path is plausibly improved, but a visible secondary computation path can re-add the header, or the implementation is too incomplete to establish preserved body-length behavior.
scale.4: The applied code fixes ordinary bodyless GET preparation, but uses an overbroad method-based or truthiness-based rule that can suppress a valid body length in an edge case; no failure is shown on the ordinary target path.
scale.5: The applied code consistently uses body presence across initial and recomputation paths: bodyless requests do not synthesize Content-Length, present bodies retain correct length handling, and existing explicit headers remain respected.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct body-aware Content-Length behavior

applies_when: A concrete source observation, helper definition, traceback, type result, failed conversion, malformed edit, or contradictory check is followed by an interpretation or implementation decision.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the quality of the causal inference drawn from task-relevant evidence. This rubric scores whether evidence changes the record's technical belief or intended strategy correctly; it does not require the corrected strategy to be present in the current source.

metadata.failure_mode: Discriminative evidence is ignored, misread, or used to retain a conversion it visibly falsifies
metadata.judge_focus: The causal link from an observed fact to the next technical conclusion, not progress, completion, or artifact polish
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the stated diagnosis or next strategy directly with the immediately preceding source observation, traceback, helper implementation, or type result

scale.1: The record materially misreads task-relevant evidence, pursues unrelated changes, or retains a contradicted diagnosis without identifying the contradiction.
scale.2: The record notices a contradiction or relevant helper but retains the disproven strategy, draws the wrong runtime conclusion, or leaves the causal diagnosis substantially confused.
scale.3: The record draws a useful partial inference or repairs a local mistake, but its task-level conclusion remains mixed, unsupported, or inconsistent with another observed result.
scale.4: A concrete observation causes the correct task-specific diagnosis or replacement choice, including correctly separating a pre-existing environment barrier from method behavior; limited uncertainty may remain.
scale.5: The record uses one or more discriminative observations to falsify a wrong approach, identify the precise method-type cause and effective boundary, and explicitly select or restore the repository-consistent native-string strategy. Score 5 even if that selected correction is not yet applied; artifact state is assessed elsewhere.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation strength and claim accuracy

applies_when: Multiple files, vendored or generated code, scratch tests, or source-rewriting utilities are visibly changed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures evaluator-facing scope and boundary contamination only; it does not rescore syntax, method semantics, or debugging insight.

metadata.judge_focus: Authoritative source boundaries, conflicting edits, and retained auxiliary artifacts

scale.2: Minor redundant production normalization or limited auxiliary material remains without obscuring the source result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository-boundary contamination

applies_when: The task concerns serialization of the qop directive by HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible implementation evidence makes the generated Digest Authorization header contain a qop directive whose emitted value is enclosed in literal double quotes, such as qop="auth", whenever the qop branch is used.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unquoted emitted qop value, malformed Python string, missing qop directive, or change only to prose/tests caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal diff or post-edit source observation outranks explanatory prose; a directly generated header outranks source-pattern assertions when they conflict.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking escaped source notation, a standalone formatting demonstration, or an RFC quotation for evidence that the production header builder was corrected.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible source or patch evidence that the emitted header contains literal double quotes around the qop value, not merely a plan or an example detached from the implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: The changed header-construction expression in requests/auth.py and any directly observed generated Authorization header.
metadata.oracle_test: For a Digest challenge using qop auth, build_digest_header must serialize the relevant field as qop="auth" rather than qop=auth while retaining the surrounding nc and cnonce fields.

scale.1: No visible implementation change addresses the emitted qop field, or the visible change clearly leaves it unquoted or unusable.
scale.2: The required quoting is identified or demonstrated outside the production path, but the visible production change is absent, incomplete, or malformed.
scale.3: The production location is changed toward quoting, but the visible evidence is ambiguous about literal emitted quotes or contains a material formatting concern.
scale.4: The production header builder visibly emits a double-quoted qop value, with no visible contradiction, but exact runtime output is not directly demonstrated.
scale.5: The production header builder visibly emits qop with literal double quotes and decisive output evidence shows qop="auth" in a generated Digest Authorization header.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Digest Authorization qop value is double-quoted

applies_when: Visible validation activity concerns the modified Digest header serialization or source syntax.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Visible checks provide task-specific evidence that the modified production code is syntactically valid and produces a Digest header with a quoted qop value while excluding the old unquoted form.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failing relevant test, syntax error, or observed qop=auth output caps credit at 2 unless a later visible correction is followed by a successful check; legacy dependency/import failures alone do not contradict the formatting fix.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful focused execution of the production header builder is strongest, followed by repository tests, syntax compilation, and exact source inspection; self-authored string simulations and prose are weaker.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full validation credit for grep-only assertions, duplicated formatting snippets, fabricated stand-ins, or declaring all tests passed when only source text was inspected.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a successful check against production source or production behavior after the edit; credit 5 requires direct generated-header or focused-test evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands and observations from syntax checks, focused tests, direct build_digest_header execution, or generated-header inspection after the edit.
metadata.oracle_test: A focused check should find qop="auth" in the generated Digest Authorization value and should not find the old qop=auth delimiter form; syntax validation should cover requests/auth.py.

scale.1: No relevant validation is visible, or the latest relevant evidence shows an unresolved syntax or output failure.
scale.2: Only prose, a detached string example, or a failed check is visible, with no successful production-source validation afterward.
scale.3: A successful exact source inspection or syntax check validates part of the change, but no production behavior or focused regression check is shown.
scale.4: Successful production-source validation combines syntax or exact inspection with task-specific evidence, but the actual header builder is not directly exercised.
scale.5: A successful focused execution or test of the production Digest builder visibly produces qop="auth" and preserves the expected neighboring Digest fields, with no unresolved contradictory result.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive validation of quoted qop output

applies_when: The task concerns serialization of the qop directive by HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Maintained Digest-auth source visibly emits the existing qop directive with its value enclosed in literal double quotes, and higher credit reflects successful validation of the changed expression rather than source-text matching alone.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An authoritative unquoted qop value or no applied task-relevant source change caps credit at 2. Renaming the Authorization wire directive to qop-options, changing only a generated copy, or leaving a malformed formatting expression caps credit at 3. A detached demonstration cannot override contradictory maintained source.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal repository diff or post-edit inspection of requests/auth.py establishes the applied implementation. A generated header is strongest validation; successful execution of the exact changed formatting expression or successful parsing/compilation of the maintained file is also qualifying validation. Grep, source-text assertions, prose, RFC quotations, and tests that merely search file contents do not establish the higher validation anchor.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating grep-only source matching as executed validation, over-rewarding prose or synthetic claims without an applied patch, or confusing qop-options terminology with the actual qop wire directive.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied maintained-source expression using the wire key qop and enclosing its emitted value in literal double quotes. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible successful semantic or syntax validation tied to that changed source expression.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final authoritative change in requests/auth.py and then inspect visible validation of that exact changed expression, such as a successful syntax parse or compilation, execution of the formatting expression, or a generated Digest Authorization header.
metadata.oracle_test: Under the existing Digest qop branch, the Authorization field must have the form qop="auth" or an equivalent quoted-value expression, followed by the existing nc and quoted cnonce fields. The RFC term qop-options is not the Authorization field name. Do not penalize literal versus formatted construction absent visible output showing an incompatible offered option list.

scale.1: No task-relevant change is visibly applied to maintained source, and the production qop serialization remains uncorrected.
scale.2: Quoting is only proposed or demonstrated outside the production path, or authoritative source still emits an unquoted or missing qop value.
scale.3: An applied edit attempts quoting but uses qop-options as the wire key, changes only a generated artifact, or leaves a visible syntax, formatting, or surrounding-field defect.
scale.4: Maintained source visibly emits a double-quoted value under the qop directive while preserving nc and cnonce, with no task-relevant contradiction, but validation is absent or limited to source inspection or text matching.
scale.5: The correct maintained-source qop quoting change is applied and preserved, and visible successful validation exercises the changed formatting, generates the relevant header, or parses or compiles the maintained source; no task-relevant contradiction is present.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implemented and validated Digest qop quoting

applies_when: A visible change targets the Digest Authorization header construction path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The change is confined to the authoritative Digest header source path and preserves the directive name and neighboring authentication fields while adding qop value quoting without unrelated behavioral expansion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Renaming the wire directive to qop-options, modifying only a generated build artifact, emitting an offered comma-separated option list where a selected qop token is required, or introducing unrelated authentication changes caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible diff outranks earlier transient edits and claims; authoritative source under requests/ outranks generated copies under build/lib/.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating qop-options as the literal wire key, editing generated artifacts as the source of truth, or broadening qop selection semantics when only quoting was requested.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a valid change to requests/auth.py that retains the wire directive name qop and preserves nc and cnonce serialization.
metadata.judge_focus: The terminal diff’s file paths and changed expression, especially requests/auth.py, the qop directive name, selected value handling, nc, cnonce, and surrounding control flow.
metadata.oracle_test: The resulting field remains structurally qop="<selected value>", nc=<nonce-count>, cnonce="<client-nonce>" in the existing qop branch; qop-options is RFC terminology, not the Authorization header field name.

scale.1: No relevant authoritative-source change is visible, or the change targets the wrong subsystem.
scale.2: A relevant edit is visible but uses the wrong directive name, wrong artifact, malformed field structure, or materially changes qop semantics.
scale.3: The authoritative source is changed and the qop field is recognizable, but the patch includes avoidable scope expansion or leaves compatibility details uncertain.
scale.4: The change is confined to the correct source path, retains qop, nc, cnonce, and existing control flow, with only minor uncertainty about selected-value handling.
scale.5: A minimal valid diff changes only the Digest qop serialization needed for quoting, keeps the wire key qop and neighboring fields intact, and introduces no unrelated source or generated-artifact edits.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct and minimal Digest header implementation boundary

applies_when: The task requires double-quoting the qop value emitted in a Digest Authorization header
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation must apply a source change that emits the existing Digest Authorization directive as qop="..." while retaining the qop field name and its surrounding nonce-count and client-nonce construction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if the edit quotes a value but renames the wire field to qop-options, damages the format expression, or changes only a generated copy. Cap at 2 if authoritative source evidence still emits an unquoted qop value. Score 1 when no task-relevant source change is visibly applied by cutoff.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal unified diff or repository diff for the maintained source file has highest authority. If absent, successful edit commands followed by direct source inspection may establish applied work. Plans, explanations, synthetic string demonstrations, grep-only tests, generated build copies, and claimed success cannot override the authoritative source state.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding proposed-but-unapplied work, mistaking source-text checks for implementation, or treating the prose term qop-options as the literal Authorization directive name.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a visibly applied edit in the maintained authentication source; credit above 3 additionally requires the emitted wire directive to remain named qop and its value to be enclosed in double quotes.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the authoritative source diff or executed source edit that constructs the Digest Authorization header, especially the emitted qop field name, double-quoted value, and preservation of the adjacent nc and cnonce fields.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, the relevant emitted form is qop="auth" or an equivalent quoted value expression under the existing qop branch. The RFC term qop-options describes the value grammar and is not a replacement wire-field name. Literal versus formatted value construction is not itself a quality distinction when both visibly preserve the requested quoting and surrounding header structure.

scale.1: No task-relevant edit is visibly applied to maintained source by cutoff, or the trajectory terminates without an applied patch.
scale.2: A source edit is applied, but it is unrelated, leaves the emitted qop value unquoted, or otherwise does not implement the requested serialization.
scale.3: The edit attempts to quote the value but changes the directive name to qop-options, modifies only generated output, or introduces a visible syntax or formatting defect.
scale.4: Maintained source visibly emits a quoted value under the qop directive and preserves the surrounding structure, but the final artifact is incomplete or contains a task-relevant ambiguity or contradiction.
scale.5: Authoritative cutoff evidence clearly shows an applied maintained-source patch emitting qop="..." under the existing Digest path, retaining the qop field name and adjacent nc/cnonce structure, with no task-relevant contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied Digest Authorization qop quoting fix
