reference_golden_rubrics.title: Focused validation quality

applies_when: The trajectory contains current workspace edits or a visible repository diff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete executable-integrity defects in the production source present at the cutoff, independent of whether the trajectory has been declared terminal.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later visible restoration or correction removes credit for an earlier defect. Conversely, a parseable patch display cannot erase a different active production file that is visibly truncated, import-broken, or conflicting.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace, latest source display, and current diff override earlier failed edits, proposed commands, backup copies, scratch scripts, and edits later restored with version control.
metadata.failure_mode: The current workspace contains production corruption, an exact-path runtime error, unsafe deletion during iteration, duplicate semantic fixes, or broad unrelated compatibility modifications.
metadata.hard_gate: Severity above 2 requires a concrete defect or materially unrelated production change visible in the active cutoff source; absence of a task fix alone is handled by the production-behavior rubric.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the current production files and diff for truncation, malformed syntax, unresolved names, live-view deletion, conflicting implementations, and unrelated compatibility damage. Do not infer validity or invalidity merely from terminal status.
metadata.oracle_test: Compile the active changed production files and execute the None-removal branch without mutating a live mapping view or relying on newly broken compatibility imports.

scale.1: No concrete integrity defect is visible in the active production source; it is unchanged or contains a narrow, parseable, safely iterable edit.
scale.2: Production source remains valid, but minor tracked clutter, a harmless redundant file, or a small unrelated reversible edit is present.
scale.3: The active workspace contains broad compatibility edits, multiple questionable production changes, or incomplete source whose executability is materially uncertain without a demonstrated exact-path failure.
scale.4: A serious active defect is visible, such as live-view deletion, a broken newly introduced import, conflicting global and merge-layer mechanisms, or production changes dominated by unrelated compatibility work.
scale.5: The active production repository is visibly unusable because a core file is truncated or malformed, syntax or names are unresolved on import, conflicts remain, or the exact target path has a demonstrated unrecovered runtime failure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current workspace production-source integrity

applies_when: The trajectory considers or changes `requests/compat.py`, `builtin_str`, `to_native_string`, or other callers of these compatibility symbols.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps the shared `builtin_str` symbol usable as the native string type and confines the fix to method normalization, avoiding regressions in `isinstance(..., builtin_str)`, content-length conversion, and Python 2 behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the visible patch makes `builtin_str` a function while `isinstance(..., builtin_str)` remains; cap at 2 for a new global conversion helper when the existing `to_native_string` already supplies the required semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository call sites such as `isinstance(string, builtin_str)` in `utils.py` take precedence over stand-alone demonstrations that a replacement callable decodes bytes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a locally plausible bytes fix from receiving high credit when it breaks a shared symbol's type contract elsewhere in Requests.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires preserving `builtin_str` as a type-compatible alias and avoiding shared compatibility-layer mutation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible searches for callers, inspection of `to_native_string`, recognition that `builtin_str` is used as an `isinstance` type argument, and whether an unsafe global approach is abandoned or remains in the patch.
metadata.oracle_test: `to_native_string('GET')` must still pass through text, `to_native_string(b'GET')` must decode it, and `isinstance('GET', builtin_str)` must remain valid rather than raising `TypeError`.

scale.1: Leaves a demonstrated shared-contract break, especially a callable `builtin_str` used as the second argument to `isinstance`.
scale.2: Introduces an unnecessary compatibility-layer helper or broad mutation without resolving all affected callers.
scale.3: Does not alter shared compatibility symbols but provides little visible analysis of their callers or cross-version implications.
scale.4: Preserves shared contracts and explicitly inspects relevant callers or identifies the risk of redefining `builtin_str`.
scale.5: Preserves the compatibility layer, demonstrates why the fix belongs only at the Session method boundary, and visibly recovers from or rules out broader approaches using concrete caller evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of shared compatibility contracts

applies_when: The trajectory presents tests, executable checks, or test plans concerning HTTP method conversion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides decisive evidence that byte-valued methods become valid native-text HTTP verbs while existing text-method behavior remains unchanged, preferably through the repository request-preparation path rather than a reimplemented stand-alone helper.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if tests merely reimplement the proposed conversion instead of invoking production code while being presented as integration proof, or if failing tests are described as passing.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository test exercising `Session.request` or prepared-request behavior outranks isolated Python expressions; observed command output outranks assertions that were not run.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating demonstrations of Python's built-in `str`/`decode` behavior as proof that the Requests code path was fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence for both a byte method and an ordinary text method, with expected prepared/native method values stated explicitly.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code and observed output for both byte and text inputs, whether the production implementation is exercised, and whether failures are honestly separated from unrelated environment incompatibilities.
metadata.oracle_test: Representative checks are `b'GET' -> 'GET'`, `b'get' -> 'GET'` after normal uppercasing, and `'get' -> 'GET'`; no network response is required if the prepared method is directly asserted.

scale.1: No relevant validation is visible, or visible evidence contradicts the claimed behavior.
scale.2: Only informal claims, source-string checks, or a faulty test are shown.
scale.3: A successful isolated conversion demonstration covers the core byte case but does not exercise production code or adequately cover text compatibility.
scale.4: Relevant production-path or close unit evidence covers byte and text methods, but execution is blocked or coverage omits an important assertion such as prepared method type/value.
scale.5: A focused regression test exercises the actual request-preparation path for byte and text methods and is shown passing, with unrelated environment failures clearly distinguished.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific regression evidence for byte and text methods

applies_when: A rollout investigates or changes handling of byte-valued HTTP method arguments in this Requests codebase.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible implementation converts an ASCII byte method such as b'GET' to the native text method 'GET' at the request boundary while preserving existing compatibility-helper contracts and ordinary text-method behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if visible code leaves the transmitted method in bytes-repr form or changes builtin_str from a type into a function while an unchanged isinstance(..., builtin_str) call remains. Cap at 2 for an applied ad hoc UTF-8 method conversion that bypasses the repository's ASCII-native-string contract, or for a broad helper change with unresolved dependent call sites.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible current diff or later source inspection overrides earlier plans and narration. Executed behavior checks override unsupported claims. Repository definitions and call sites override standalone reimplementations used only in temporary scripts.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a patch merely because a standalone b'GET' example works while the patch accepts the wrong encoding, duplicates an existing conversion policy, or breaks unrelated isinstance and Content-Length behavior through a global compatibility change.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied conversion that visibly maps ASCII HTTP-method bytes to native text and preserves ordinary text methods, without leaving a known shared-helper contract violation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source edits, diffs, source re-reads, and executed checks affecting Session.request, to_native_string, compat.builtin_str, and consumers of those helpers. Distinguish code actually shown as applied from merely suggested alternatives.
metadata.oracle_test: For this task, b'GET' must normalize to native text 'GET', and 'GET' must remain 'GET'. The repository's to_native_string(method) with its default ASCII encoding is the semantic reference. builtin_str must remain suitable for existing type checks and numeric stringification unless every dependent use is coherently preserved.

scale.1: A visible applied change violates a required contract: the method remains bytes-repr text, or a shared string type is replaced by a callable while an existing type check still uses it.
scale.2: The target example is converted, but the applied implementation uses ad hoc UTF-8 handling instead of the task's ASCII/native-string contract, or makes broad compatibility changes with unresolved dependent behavior.
scale.3: The diagnosis is correct and no direct contract break is established, but the visible implementation is absent, incomplete, or uses a custom conversion whose repository-wide compatibility is not established.
scale.4: An applied implementation correctly normalizes ASCII byte methods and preserves text methods and visible dependent contracts, but it is broader or less directly aligned with the existing conversion utility than necessary.
scale.5: The applied implementation uses the existing native-string conversion at the Session request boundary, preserving its default ASCII semantics and shared compatibility-helper contracts; visible checks or source evidence support both byte and text method behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safely normalizes byte-valued HTTP methods without breaking shared string contracts

applies_when: The visible prefix examines, changes, or tests production handling of direct request `data` supplied as bytes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the current visible production request-preparation path preserves an already encoded direct body payload as the same bytes, without decoding, stringifying, re-encoding, or routing it through structured form encoding.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visible decoding, stringification, re-encoding, rejection, or fall-through of direct bytes into key/value iteration caps the score at 1. A shared-utility modification that preserves bytes globally caps the score at 3 even if a copied demonstration succeeds. Failed imports alone do not contradict clear localized source behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful assertion against the checked-out `PreparedRequest.body` outranks current production source control flow, which outranks an applicable visible diff. Copied implementations, simulated utilities, source-pattern checks, and claims that no exception occurs are explanatory only and cannot prove repository behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting intent after a type-check edit while ignoring the branch bytes actually enter, or treating standalone helper output as proof that the edited repository preserves the prepared body.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an applied production branch whose effective control flow returns direct bytes unchanged before iterable or key/value form processing. Score 5 additionally requires execution of the checked-out preparation path with both type and exact-value assertions.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace a direct bytes value through the current `_encode_params` and `prepare_body` control flow, including branches reached after any edited type check, and inspect prepared-body type and exact value when executed.
metadata.oracle_test: Prepare a PUT with `data=u'ööö'.encode('utf-8')` and assert `isinstance(prepared.body, bytes)` and `prepared.body == b'\xc3\xb6\xc3\xb6\xc3\xb6'`.
metadata.stage: Implement and validate opaque body handling

scale.1: Current production control flow visibly decodes, stringifies, rejects, alters, or routes direct body bytes into structured form encoding.
scale.2: The failure mechanism is correctly identified, but no applied current production path visibly preserves direct body bytes.
scale.3: Applied code plausibly preserves bytes only through a broad shared-utility change, or the current production path is materially contradictory or incomplete.
scale.4: Current localized production source unambiguously returns direct body bytes unchanged before structured encoding, but the checked-out prepared body is not executed and inspected.
scale.5: The checked-out production preparation path is executed and directly verifies that the prepared body is bytes and exactly equals the original payload byte-for-byte.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective opaque body-byte preservation

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Derive the body and URL semantic boundary; Implement the narrow context-specific repair stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the implementation respects the distinction between opaque request bodies and native-text consumers instead of changing shared utility semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: Global utility change, unrelated caller impact, or failure to distinguish body and URL requirements
metadata.judge_focus: Edit location, retained global utility contract, and separation of body and query consumers
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the production diff and both consumers of `_encode_params`
metadata.stage: Derive the body and URL semantic boundary; Implement the narrow context-specific repair

scale.1: The implementation changes shared native-string semantics or otherwise applies binary-body behavior to unrelated text consumers.
scale.2: The main change is broad or mixed with unrelated production edits, despite addressing the reported conversion.
scale.3: The change is in request preparation, but the body/query boundary or effective control flow remains incomplete or ambiguous.
scale.4: The byte-preserving change is localized in request preparation and visibly leaves mapping, tuple-list, file-like, streaming, and neighboring preparation control flow intact.
scale.5: The implementation explicitly preserves body bytes and performs required native-text conversion only at the URL consumer boundary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consumer-boundary localization

applies_when: The task concerns malformed HTTP hostname labels escaping as a dependency or Unicode exception instead of a Requests InvalidURL exception.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work has produced a coherent, appropriately scoped fix that converts malformed host-label failures into Requests InvalidURL behavior while preserving valid URL preparation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible syntax or import break caps the score at 1. A direct reproduction that still leaks UnicodeError or an urllib3 parsing exception caps it at 2. If attempted edits were reverted or no effective change is present, the score cannot exceed 3. Broadly catching unrelated transport failures or changing all hostname handling without compatibility evidence caps the score at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current source or displayed diff and executed command output outrank plans, comments, summaries, and claimed success. Later visible inspections or executions outrank earlier ones when they conflict. A direct local reproduction using the edited source outranks reasoning based only on an installed dependency's behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting confident narration, temporary or corrupted edits, catches placed around code that cannot raise the observed exception, and broad exception wrapping that changes the exception class without establishing the requested host-label semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires a coherent applied source change and a successful direct reproduction showing Requests InvalidURL. A score of 5 additionally requires the expected invalid-label semantics and visible regression evidence for relevant valid and malformed hosts.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the causal diagnosis of the ASCII-host validation gap or escaping dependency exception, the effective source edits at cutoff, and executed checks of exception type, message, malformed neighboring labels, and valid ASCII or internationalized hosts.
metadata.non_evidence: Dependency installation, repository browsing, repeated restatement of the issue, proposed future edits, standalone IDNA experiments, and network failures from valid hosts do not establish that the repository fix is effective.
metadata.oracle_test: For requests.get("http://.example.com"), the semantic target is requests.exceptions.InvalidURL with the invalid-label meaning, specifically "URL has an invalid label."; valid ordinary and IDNA hostnames should remain preparable.

scale.1: The visible current source is syntactically or import-invalid, or the work remains centered on a visibly disproven mechanism with no coherent correction.
scale.2: There is partial diagnosis or an applied attempt, but visible execution contradicts it: the task case still leaks the wrong exception, the catch is at an ineffective location, or the edit has materially wrong exception semantics.
scale.3: The causal mechanism and a specific viable correction are identified, but the correction is not durably applied, is not shown coherent, or lacks a successful direct task reproduction; there is no stronger visible contradiction.
scale.4: A coherent applied correction passes a direct task reproduction with Requests InvalidURL, but exact invalid-label semantics, regression coverage, or compatibility of a broader-than-necessary change remains unestablished.
scale.5: A coherent and appropriately scoped applied correction visibly produces Requests InvalidURL with the expected invalid-label semantics and is supported by relevant malformed-label and valid-host regression checks, with no conflicting evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Malformed host-label fix readiness

applies_when: The task concerns malformed HTTP hostname labels escaping Requests as Unicode or dependency parsing exceptions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible diagnosis or current source uses a causally effective, narrowly scoped mechanism to turn malformed hostname-label failures into Requests InvalidURL without unnecessarily changing valid hostname preparation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax, import, or undefined-exception defect caps the score at 1. A catch placed around an operation visibly shown not to raise the escaping exception, or a direct post-edit reproduction that still leaks UnicodeError or a dependency parsing exception, caps the score at 2. Catching broad transport or connection failures rather than a label-related parse exception caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed traces establishing the failure location and direct reproductions using the current edited source outrank plans and summaries. Current source or displayed diffs determine whether a change is applied. Later executions outrank earlier baseline failures. A standalone IDNA experiment may establish label behavior but cannot establish repository effectiveness.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding all-host IDNA rewrites merely because one reproduction passes, catches installed around parse_url or connection setup after traces show the exception occurs later, incomplete exception imports, and broad transport wrapping. It also avoids treating an exact message as more important than a correctly scoped Requests exception boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a coherent applied change and direct execution showing requests.exceptions.InvalidURL for the task URL. A proposed but unapplied precise correction cannot exceed 4. A global change to process every hostname through IDNA cannot exceed 3 because it expands compatibility surface beyond the ASCII-label gap, even when the task reproduction succeeds.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect where the observed failure actually arises, whether the proposed or applied check can intercept that path, and whether its scope is limited to invalid labels or the corresponding dependency location-parse failure. Distinguish a clean, specific proposal from an applied edit, and inspect applied edits for completeness and execution evidence.
metadata.non_evidence: Dependency installation, baseline reproduction alone, repository browsing, future-action narration, network success or DNS failure for valid hosts, and standalone IDNA output do not prove that an applied correction intercepts the Requests execution path.
metadata.oracle_test: Acceptable causal mechanisms include rejecting empty ASCII hostname labels during URL preparation with Requests' invalid-label semantics, or narrowly converting the dependency's malformed-location exception at the send path where it is visibly raised. For requests.get("http://.example.com"), the externally observable exception must be requests.exceptions.InvalidURL; ordinary ASCII and internationalized hosts must not be rejected merely by the new mechanism.

scale.1: The visible mechanism is incoherent or unusable: source has a syntax/import/undefined-name defect, or the proposed handling is unrelated to hostname-label parsing.
scale.2: A mechanism is attempted or described, but visible evidence disproves its causal placement or completeness: it catches around an operation shown not to raise the failure, remains unfinished, or direct execution still leaks the dependency or Unicode exception.
scale.3: The diagnosis is broadly relevant but the mechanism has excessive or uncertain scope, such as reprocessing every hostname through IDNA or wrapping general transport failures; alternatively, only a generic direction is given without a precise effective boundary.
scale.4: A precise and plausibly compatible mechanism is identified—targeted empty-label validation or narrow normalization of the label-related dependency exception at its actual escape point—but it is not yet applied and directly confirmed, or an applied version lacks decisive execution evidence. No visible contradiction is present.
scale.5: A coherent applied, narrowly scoped mechanism is directly shown to make the task URL raise requests.exceptions.InvalidURL at the effective preparation or send boundary, with no visible source defect, leaked lower-level exception, or evidence that valid hostname preparation is being broadly disrupted.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Malformed-label correction mechanism quality

applies_when: The trajectory contains investigation or reasoning about how Requests processes an HTTP(S) hostname beginning with a dot.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accurately identifies why `.example.com` escapes Requests' existing invalid-label handling and fails only after URL preparation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that the existing non-ASCII `except UnicodeError` branch already handles `.example.com`, or that transport connection code is the root validation boundary, caps this rubric at 2 unless visibly corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and direct `PreparedRequest` or `Request.prepare()` observations outrank assumptions inferred from the exception emitted by a subsequently installed urllib3 version.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a dependency-specific late `LocationParseError` or `UnicodeError` for the causal defect instead of finding the skipped hostname-validation branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires connecting the ASCII fast path in `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` to the malformed leading empty label and the later low-level failure.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or controlled probes showing that `.example.com` is ASCII, `unicode_is_ascii(host)` is true, the IDNA-validation branch is skipped, and the prepared URL can retain the malformed host.
metadata.oracle_test: Before the fix, preparing `requests.Request('GET', 'http://.example.com')` can produce `http://.example.com/`; the hostname is ASCII and therefore bypasses `_get_idna_encoded_host`, although direct IDNA encoding rejects its empty leading label.

scale.1: No relevant causal analysis is visible, or the explanation is incompatible with the observed source flow.
scale.2: Recognizes that the hostname is malformed but gives only speculative reasoning or locates the defect primarily in transport/connection handling.
scale.3: Correctly identifies either the ASCII-branch bypass or the distinction between preparation and later connection failure, but does not establish the complete chain.
scale.4: Correctly explains the complete chain from ASCII hostname classification through skipped IDNA validation to a late dependency failure, with supporting source inspection or a controlled probe.
scale.5: Provides precise, directly supported diagnosis of the branch conditions, empty leading label, successful pre-fix preparation, and why the existing Unicode-error conversion does not execute for this input.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of the leading-empty-label failure

applies_when: The trajectory contains a proposed or applied code change intended to convert the leading-dot hostname failure into a Requests `InvalidURL`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements the fix in `PreparedRequest.prepare_url` at the ASCII-host invalid-label guard, rejecting a leading dot with `InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.')` before transport begins.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A solution confined to `HTTPAdapter.send`, a broad catch of urllib3 location exceptions, or a patch that returns only a generic `Failed to parse` message is capped at 3; visibly broken syntax or a restored-away change is capped at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: A clean visible source diff takes precedence over narrative claims; an unchanged, restored, malformed, or merely proposed edit receives no implementation credit beyond what is actually visible.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing a late symptom in urllib3 integration, or broadening all hostname processing when a small preparation-time guard is sufficient.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a syntactically coherent early validation change in `requests/models.py` that makes a leading-dot ASCII host raise the requested exception and message.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff or file contents around the hostname branch in `requests/models.py`, including exception type, exact message, control flow, syntax, and unrelated edits.
metadata.oracle_test: The minimal task-specific change extends the existing ASCII invalid-host check from a leading wildcard to a leading wildcard or leading dot, for example `host.startswith((u'*', u'.'))`, and raises `InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.')`.

scale.1: No relevant surviving implementation is visible, or the visible source is syntactically broken or restored to the original behavior.
scale.2: A change is visible but targets the wrong layer, cannot intercept the observed path, or does not produce the requested Requests exception semantics.
scale.3: The input is converted to `InvalidURL`, but through a late transport catch or an unnecessarily broad hostname-policy change with observable semantic risk.
scale.4: A correct preparation-time leading-dot check with the exact exception and message is visible, but the patch includes minor unnecessary edits or lacks a clearly minimal form.
scale.5: A clean, minimal, syntactically correct change extends the existing ASCII invalid-label guard in `requests/models.py`, preserves surrounding behavior, and yields the exact requested exception and message.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise early validation implementation boundary

applies_when: The prefix states a causal conclusion, proposes a workaround, or retains a production edit outside the normalization correction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how strongly the prefix commits to an unsupported cause or workaround, while preserving credit for concrete, recoverable hypothesis testing.

metadata.failure_mode: A broad or fabricated workaround is treated as established despite lacking discriminating evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Difference between tentative exploration, plausible wrong existing-code hypotheses, asserted downstream fixes, and invented or unsafe requirements.

scale.1: No unsupported commitment is visible; alternatives are tentative or rejected using relevant observations.
scale.2: A distraction or weak hypothesis appears but remains provisional and causes no retained production change.
scale.3: A plausible but incorrect existing-code hypothesis is pursued substantially or tested without decisive normalization evidence.
scale.4: An incorrect downstream or request-path correction is asserted or retained while normalization remains broken.
scale.5: An invented protocol requirement, unsafe credential channel, fabricated behavior claim, or broadly disruptive workaround is strongly asserted or retained.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unsupported commitment severity

applies_when: The prefix investigates, tests, edits, or prepares a correction for the reported authenticated-proxy failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Ranks the most advanced task-specific work actually visible by cutoff, distinguishing passive inspection, generic diagnostics, concrete tested hypotheses, observed credential-loss transformations, applied source experiments, and the working normalization correction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 4 when the latest implementation changes an alternative layer while the reported normalization defect is not demonstrated fixed. Cap at 3 when no executed output shows either a credential-removing Requests transformation or changed production behavior. Unsafe credential propagation, unresolved syntax damage, or a terminal artifact that cannot execute caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest executed behavior and latest repository state override claims, plans, earlier experiments, and intended edits. A visible source diff plus executed output outranks narration; a failed command establishes only the failure it displays. Terminal status controls whether an unresolved edit is merely recoverable or the submitted artifact.
metadata.failure_mode: Generic parsing and direct proxy-header checks are treated as equivalent to observing credential loss, or a locally successful but unrelated production edit is mistaken for the completed task fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a visible production change in `requests.utils.prepend_scheme_if_needed` that conditionally restores parser-provided userinfo before the final authority, plus an executed required authenticated normalization check. No edit, a wrong-layer edit, or an unexecuted proposed fix cannot reach 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed commands, their outputs, the latest source diff, and the stated connection between a proxy URL containing userinfo and downstream proxy authorization. Distinguish an observed credential-removing Requests transformation or behavior-checked source experiment from direct header generation on an untouched URL.
metadata.oracle_test: For an explicit-scheme proxy such as `http://user:pass@example.com/path?query`, `prepend_scheme_if_needed(..., 'http')` must preserve the URL by reconstructing the authority from parsed `auth` and `netloc`; username-only userinfo must also survive so downstream proxy-header extraction remains possible.

scale.1: Only passive browsing, generic discussion, unsupported speculation, or unexecuted plans are visible; no concrete task-specific hypothesis is exercised.
scale.2: Relevant proxy or URL source is inspected, but no concrete existing-code hypothesis is behaviorally exercised, no production edit is attempted, and no Requests transformation is shown removing credentials.
scale.3: A concrete existing-code hypothesis is exercised through a targeted command, direct parsing or untouched-URL header behavior is checked, or a production edit is attempted without executed evidence of its changed behavior; no credential-removing Requests transformation is observed.
scale.4: Either executed output shows a Requests URL transformation turning a credential-bearing URL into a credential-free result and the downstream proxy-auth path is inspected, or a task-directed production hypothesis is actually applied and its intended local behavior is successfully checked; the exact normalization correction is not yet demonstrated.
scale.5: The latest source visibly implements conditional preservation of parser-provided userinfo in `prepend_scheme_if_needed`, and an executed required authenticated normalization check demonstrates that correction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Visible task-directed progress

applies_when: The prefix runs or reports checks concerning proxy credentials, URL normalization, or proxy authorization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores only executed checks that distinguish preservation through normalization from behavior of downstream helpers on an untouched authenticated URL.

metadata.failure_mode: Only source reading, intended tests, setup errors, original-URL parsing, unusual missing-component cases, or generic live requests are shown.
metadata.judge_focus: Required authenticated forms, established unauthenticated cases, and downstream authorization from the normalized result.

scale.1: No relevant behavioral check is executed, or the only required normalization check visibly fails without resolution.
scale.2: Executed checks are indirect, such as parsing or generating headers from the original authenticated URL, and do not cross the normalization boundary.
scale.3: Credential loss or preservation is directly demonstrated for one required authenticated form.
scale.4: Both required authenticated forms are checked, or one required form is combined with meaningful compatibility or normalized downstream-header evidence.
scale.5: Both required forms, established unauthenticated compatibility, and downstream proxy authorization from the normalized result are directly verified with accurately reported outcomes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Normalization-discriminative validation

applies_when: The prefix inspects proxy URL transformation or offers an explanation for disappearing proxy credentials.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores observable understanding of where credentials disappear and why downstream proxy authorization consequently fails.

metadata.failure_mode: The prefix remains generic, tests only an untouched URL, or commits to another cause without examining normalization.
metadata.judge_focus: Direct comparison across normalization and explanation of the separately parsed authentication and authority components.

scale.1: No task-specific causal evidence is visible, or the stated explanation conflicts with observed behavior.
scale.2: Relevant proxy or URL code is inspected, but the credential-loss transformation is not identified.
scale.3: The normalization helper or credential disappearance is identified, but the component-level reconstruction omission is not fully explained.
scale.4: The prefix explains that authentication is parsed separately from host and port and is omitted during authority reconstruction.
scale.5: The exact omission, reconstruction location, both userinfo forms, and downstream proxy-authorization consequence are correctly connected using visible evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact causal localization

applies_when: A task-relevant repair rule, source edit, concrete patch, or post-edit behavioral observation is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the visible trajectory has an active, causally appropriate shared-normalization repair whose current behavior is confirmed by repository-attributable evidence, rather than only a plausible proposal, scalar-specific heuristic, or superseded edit.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved later result showing payload coercion, raw-object return, lost or reverted source, malformed code, or patch-caused established-container failure caps the score at 2. A concrete established-owner rule that is not behaviorally checked after application is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest displayed active source or final diff outranks edit claims and earlier source. Repository-local output produced after that source state outranks simulations, installed-package results, and pre-edit observations. A later stash, revert, source replacement, or focused contradiction supersedes earlier success.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a precise but unvalidated edit as equivalent to an applied repair, or treating a scalar-only pass as validation of a payload-based classification rule.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require one coherent active rule at the shared `.values` extraction point plus a post-edit repository-local assignment or construction observation showing that the custom owner itself is retained.
metadata.judge_focus: The final visible `as_compatible_data` rule, whether it remains active, and post-edit repository-local evidence that the current rule preserves a custom owner while retaining intentional container conversion.
metadata.oracle_test: Under the current checkout, inspect the helper condition and determine whether a custom owner survives as the item of a zero-dimensional object array, including an ndarray-valued `.values` owner, while pandas Series and DataFrame still convert and the terminal `np.asarray(data)` path remains reachable.

scale.1: No coherent repair is active at the cutoff: the generic extraction remains, the candidate was reverted or stashed without restoration, or the current source is unusable.
scale.2: An active attempt exists, but it is caller-specific, generic, payload-based, malformed, or has an unresolved later focused or established-container contradiction; scalar-only success does not raise it above this anchor.
scale.3: A coherent candidate is visible but applied readiness is incomplete: either a concrete established-owner rule lacks a post-edit repository-local behavioral check, or an active owner-side structural rule lacks attributable confirmation for the current source state.
scale.4: A coherent owner-side or established-owner rule is active at the shared helper, a post-edit repository-local assignment or construction check shows the custom owner is retained by type or identity, and no later contradiction or loss of the edit is visible.
scale.5: In addition to anchor 4, repository-local checks for the current source establish zero-dimensional object shape and owner identity for scalar- and ndarray-valued custom owners, intentional Series and DataFrame conversion, and a final active artifact preserving terminal NumPy normalization.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied semantic repair readiness

applies_when: Production source, a prepared patch, a reported edit, or a final diff makes the implementation state observable.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the selected rule forms a coherent effective repair at the original shared-helper location. It does not grade the semantic family of the rule.

metadata.failure_mode: A reported edit, unapplied patch, malformed block, or superseded source state is treated as an active coherent implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Active source state, syntax, helper placement, and unresolved later edits
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the exact helper hunk after the last edit and compare it with the final diff or source display

scale.1: No concrete repair exists in production or patch form, or the visible source is unusable and no coherent final rule can be identified.
scale.2: A concrete attempt exists but is malformed, located at the wrong conversion point, contradicted by its final source state, reverted, or followed by an unverified corrective edit.
scale.3: A coherent concrete patch or active helper rule exists, but application, imports, final source state, or later correction remains visibly uncertain.
scale.4: The active helper contains one coherent localized rule at the original extraction point and no visible source defect defeats it.
scale.5: The active helper, final source display, syntax evidence, and scoped diff all agree on the same coherent localized implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective implementation coherence

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Choose the causal classification family stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates only the semantic family of the selected rule, not whether it is active, tested, terminal, or clean.

metadata.failure_mode: No selected rule receives a midpoint, or scalar success makes a payload heuristic appear equivalent to an owner-side rule.
metadata.judge_focus: Concrete owner type versus owner structure versus payload structure versus generic extraction
metadata.oracle_test: Apply the exact condition to Series, DataFrame, Index, scalar-valued owner, ndarray-valued owner, and an owner advertising ndim

scale.1: No concrete replacement rule is visible, or generic extraction remains and still unwraps the scalar custom owner.
scale.2: The rule excludes scalar payloads or decides from payload ndarray type, payload shape, payload `ndim`, payload `__array__`, or an equivalent payload property.
scale.3: The rule decides from owner structure such as owner `ndim`, shape, or array protocol.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the visible source and MCVE.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of boolean-weight normalization

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes weighted reduction behavior for boolean weights.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible repository state contains a coherent, task-causal correction that makes the valid-weight denominator numeric, preserves ordinary weighted behavior, and is supported by consistent execution evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when the latest edit has not been executed after being applied, the final applied state is unclear after multiple replacements, or relevant outputs conflict with the claimed fix. Cap at 2 when the reported case still fails, the edit changes numerator semantics without justification, or an apparently patch-caused relevant regression remains unresolved. Unrelated environment incompatibilities and baseline-confirmed pre-existing failures do not reduce credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository-backed source excerpt or git diff overrides earlier edits and narrative claims. Executed outputs using the local modified source override asserted expectations. A direct denominator result and weighted-mean result outrank generic test counts. Failures proven unchanged on an unmodified baseline are non-evidence against the patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for identifying the boolean-dot cause while leaving only a proposed edit, an obsolete or uncertain working-tree state, redundant broad coercions without semantic confirmation, or test narratives contradicted by visible outputs.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visibly applied edit that ensures the denominator dot has at least one numeric operand and direct execution showing the reported boolean case produces a numeric weight sum of 2 or mean of 1.0.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source or diff affecting the valid-data mask, weights, dot reduction, or sum-of-weights denominator; then inspect executed checks of the reported boolean-weight mean and denominator. Credit applied code, not merely a suggested cast.
metadata.oracle_test: For data [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] and boolean weights [True, True, False], valid-weight reduction must be numeric 2 and weighted mean must be 1.0. The correction may numerically coerce the validity mask or weights in the denominator path, but should retain numeric-weight, zero-weight, missing-data, dimensional, and Dataset semantics.

scale.1: No task-causal edit is visibly applied, or the latest applied behavior still returns the incorrect boolean denominator or weighted mean.
scale.2: An applied attempt targets the denominator but is materially incoherent, overbroad in a way that changes numerator behavior, or contradicted by unresolved relevant execution evidence.
scale.3: A plausible task-causal edit is visible, but its latest form is not directly re-executed, the final applied state is ambiguous after revisions, or evidence is insufficient to establish both numeric normalization and preservation of surrounding behavior.
scale.4: A correct applied denominator fix passes the reported case, but includes avoidable redundant coercion or has only narrow validation that leaves preservation of ordinary weighted semantics weakly supported.
scale.5: A stable, narrowly task-causal applied fix makes the denominator numeric, directly demonstrates the reported mean or weight-sum oracle, and has consistent visible evidence that ordinary numeric, zero-weight, missing-data, dimensional, or Dataset behavior is preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied correctness of the boolean-weight denominator fix

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes weighted reduction behavior for boolean weights.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest verifiable repository state applies a coherent numeric-denominator correction, leaves weighted numerator semantics intact, and has execution evidence consistent with that exact final state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 when a correctly specified post-edit check reaching the changed code shows the reported case failing, numerator semantics changing, zero-total weights not becoming NaN, or a relevant repository failure remains unresolved without a clean baseline demonstration. Also cap at 2 when redundant coercion of both denominator operands is combined with unresolved relevant execution, because the visible evidence does not establish which final transformation is necessary or safe. Score at most 3 when the latest replacement is not re-executed or the final working-tree state cannot be determined. Do not cap for an incorrect expected value, a dimension-mismatched ad hoc script, an unrelated environment failure, or a failure visibly reproduced on an unmodified baseline.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest source excerpt or git diff overrides earlier edits and prose. Execution against that exact state overrides success claims. The direct oracle mean and numeric denominator outrank aggregate test counts. A clean-checkout rerun of the same failing command establishes a baseline failure. Ad hoc checks with mathematically wrong expectations, mismatched dimensions, stale imports, or unrelated dependency failures are non-evidence unless their inputs independently demonstrate a real semantic regression.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a passing sample from masking an unresolved or redundantly transformed implementation, prevents earlier successful runs from being attributed to an unexecuted final replacement, and prevents mathematically incorrect ad hoc expectations from being mistaken for regressions.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a visibly applied final edit with at least one numeric operand in the denominator dot and post-edit execution showing mean 1.0 or numeric sum of weights 2 for the reported case. Anchor 5 additionally requires direct denominator evidence and at least one correctly specified preservation check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest repository-backed form of `_sum_of_weights`, `_reduce`, and `_weighted_sum`; identify which operand is made numeric and whether the final applied form was executed. Then inspect the exact boolean-weight mean and denominator outputs and any correctly specified compatibility checks.
metadata.oracle_test: For data [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] and boolean weights [True, True, False], the denominator must be numeric 2 and the weighted mean must be 1.0. A valid correction makes either the non-null mask or the denominator weights numeric while retaining masking, dimensions, ordinary numeric weights, and zero-total-weight NaN behavior.

scale.1: No task-causal correction is applied in the latest verifiable state, or direct execution of that state still yields the boolean denominator or mean bug.
scale.2: The reported case passes after an applied attempt, but correctly specified relevant failures remain unresolved, numerator or zero-weight semantics are contradicted, or redundant transformation of both denominator operands is accompanied by unresolved execution evidence.
scale.3: A plausible denominator correction is visible, but the latest replacement was not re-executed, the final applied state is ambiguous, or only narrow evidence exists without establishing that the observed success belongs to the final code.
scale.4: A stable applied correction makes the denominator numeric and the reported case passes against that state, while numerator and zero-weight behavior remain intact; validation is narrow or the conversion is broader than necessary.
scale.5: A stable denominator-local correction directly produces numeric sum of weights 2 and mean 1.0, leaves numerator semantics unchanged, and has coherent correctly specified evidence for ordinary numeric weights, zero weights, missing data, dimensions, or Dataset behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final-state correctness and coherence of the boolean-weight denominator fix

applies_when: A visible edit or exact implementation proposal changes the reduction used for boolean weights.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the implementation guarantees a numeric sum-of-weights reduction while preserving the validity mask, weighted numerator values, zero-total-weight handling, dimensions, and behavior for non-boolean weights.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if boolean-by-boolean denominator reduction remains possible, the non-null mask is removed, weights are summed without masking, or zero totals cease to become NaN. Cap at 3 if both denominator operands are coerced without a demonstrated need, or if an unconditional shared-helper conversion visibly changes non-boolean dtype or numerator semantics. Do not cap merely because a safe boolean-only promotion is implemented in `_reduce` rather than directly in `_sum_of_weights`.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest repository-backed diff or source excerpt overrides earlier proposals and narration. Call-site and dtype analysis outrank assumptions that a shared helper edit is inherently broad. Runtime results may confirm safety but do not rescue source that drops masking or changes reduction semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents judging file or helper locality as a proxy for semantic scope, while still withholding top credit from redundant dual coercion, unconditional dtype broadening, numerator changes, or accidental sample-only fixes.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied implementation with at least one numeric operand in the denominator dot, retention of `da.notnull()` masking, and retention of the zero-total-weight `.where(...)` behavior. A shared `_reduce` edit qualifies only when its condition and affected callers visibly preserve weighted numerator values.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact changed expression and every affected caller of `_reduce`. Determine which operand becomes numeric, whether promotion is denominator-local or conditional on boolean dtype, and whether `_weighted_sum` can change in value or alignment semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: For data `[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` and weights `[True, True, False]`, the denominator must be numeric `2` and the mean `1.0`. Promoting either the validity mask or the denominator weights is valid. A boolean-only promotion in shared `_reduce` is also valid when multiplying ordinary numeric data by promoted boolean weights remains numerically equivalent and alignment, dimensions, masking, and zero-total handling are unchanged.

scale.1: No concrete numeric-promotion mechanism is present, or the implementation still permits a boolean mask and boolean weights to reach the denominator dot unchanged.
scale.2: A concrete edit is present but removes or bypasses valid-data masking, changes the denominator to an unmasked weight sum, breaks zero-total handling, or visibly changes weighted numerator values.
scale.3: The edit likely fixes the reported denominator but redundantly coerces both operands, unconditionally broadens shared reduction dtypes, has unresolved call-path ambiguity, or is only an exact unapplied proposal.
scale.4: An applied single-operand promotion makes the denominator numeric and preserves masking and zero-total handling; it is denominator-local or safely conditional on boolean dtype in a shared helper, but preservation across all affected callers is only briefly established.
scale.5: The applied implementation uses one necessary numeric promotion, with source-backed analysis showing that every affected call path preserves numerator values, non-boolean weights, dimensions, alignment, missing-data masking, and zero-total-weight NaN behavior.

applies_when: The trajectory executes or reports behavioral checks concerning stacking, variable selection, squeezing, dataset reconstruction, or roundtrip preservation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A reached relevant assertion failure remains controlling until a visible correction or reversion is followed by a passing equivalent check. Validation of reset_coords(drop=True), deletion of every scalar coordinate, or another broad removal is capped at 2 unless a valid sliced-sample scalar-coordinate preservation check passes. Results from another installation, simulations, source-text checks, and tests that fail before behavioral execution cannot establish scores above 2 by themselves.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reached assertion or directly printed behavior from the checked-out implementation outranks verbal claims and tests against another installation. Relevant repository tests outrank ad hoc examples. Dependency, import, collection, or malformed-input failures are not behavioral evidence for or against the repair, though they provide no validation credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Counting environment or collection errors as regressions, accepting malformed examples as preservation tests, validating a different installation than the edited checkout, or mistaking an MCVE pass under broad coordinate deletion for evidence of semantic safety.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires checked-out execution that either establishes the causal residual coordinate with a valid preservation baseline or validates an applied repair on the reported case without a reached relevant assertion failure. Score 5 requires the repaired checkout to pass the reported roundtrip and valid preservation coverage capable of detecting loss of residual dimensions or legitimate sliced-sample scalar coordinates.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether commands exercised the checked-out source, whether the selected-and-squeezed arrays were observed directly, whether test inputs were valid, whether tests reached relevant assertions, and whether preservation checks could expose broad coordinate loss.
metadata.oracle_test: Direct inspection should show that selecting and squeezing a one-level stack leaves a conflicting scalar coordinate named by the consumed stacked dimension, while a residual-level case may already lack that coordinate. Valid post-repair checks should show the reported roundtrip succeeding while residual dimensions and a legitimate scalar sample coordinate remain present.

scale.1: No trustworthy execution of the checked-out behavior; conclusions rely on another installation, simulation, source-text inspection, or unsupported claims.
scale.2: The issue is locally reproduced or an edit is exercised, but checks cover only the minimal case, use invalid inputs, support broad coordinate deletion without a discriminating preservation case, or leave a reached relevant failure unresolved.
scale.3: Valid checked-out experiments directly isolate the residual coordinate or expose and acknowledge a relevant preservation regression, but no applied repair has both a successful reported roundtrip and valid preservation evidence.
scale.4: Checked-out execution establishes the causal coordinate and either validates the applied repair on the reported roundtrip or supplies a valid preservation baseline; no reached relevant assertion contradicts the stated conclusion, but residual-level or sliced-sample coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: The checked-out targeted repair passes the reported roundtrip and valid repository or equivalent preservation checks that exercise residual dimensions or MultiIndex levels and legitimate sliced-sample scalar coordinates, with every reached relevant contradiction visibly resolved.

metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible applied source or diff controls implementation scoring. Checked-out execution performed after that edit controls behavioral support. reference_golden_rubrics.title: Structural diagnosis of the consumed stacked-dimension artifact

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes multi-dimension min_count behavior in the nanops reduction path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates visible evidence that the current implementation applies the focused shared-helper correction: sequence-valued axes are accepted, and each output position's valid count is the product of exactly the reduced axis lengths minus the missing-value count over those same axes. Judge the latest observable repository state or successful source mutation. A successful narrow mutation that removes the rejection or installs the exact selected-axis expression supersedes an earlier source view even when no later view is shown; do not infer unobserved syntax damage from line-oriented editing alone. Later source inspection, parser/import output, or relevant public reduction behavior may contradict that mutation. Basic all-dimension success proves removal of the exception but not partial-axis counting. Broad helper-signature, scalar-path, or caller rewrites do not receive focused implementation credit merely because a simple example runs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 when current direct evidence shows full-input counting for a partial reduction, invalid shape indexing, reversed missing-mask polarity, a threshold result that should be null but is not, or a sequence-axis rejection with no later successful removal. Score at most 1 after a later syntax/import failure or source view makes the helper unusable. Score at most 3 when a relevant partial-axis execution fails without proving the selected-axis formula wrong, or when unnecessary helper-signature, scalar-path, or caller rewrites leave the focused semantics uncertain.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later direct source views, parser/import results, and public reductions outrank earlier plans and calculations. A successful final source mutation is evidence that its explicit change is applied and supersedes an earlier source view unless later observable evidence contradicts it; absence of a post-mutation view is not itself a contradiction. Standalone NumPy calculations establish algebra only. Basic full reductions establish exception removal only, while a partial multi-axis threshold case is authoritative for per-output semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating exception removal with correct partial-axis counting, rewarding broad rewrites as a focused fix, accepting whole-array size because full reductions pass, treating standalone algebra as repository behavior, or disregarding either a successful latest mutation or a later concrete contradiction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require observable application in `_maybe_null_out` of both semantic edits: removal of the sequence-axis rejection and multiplication of only the shape entries selected by `axis`, while retaining missing-value reduction over the same axes. They also require a focused helper change rather than an unnecessary helper-signature, caller, or scalar-control-flow redesign. Score 5 additionally requires discriminative public or direct-helper evidence of per-output partial multi-axis thresholding.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the latest observable change is the minimal shared `_maybe_null_out` correction, using an expression equivalent to `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod() - mask.sum(axis)` and preserving promotion and null filling. Distinguish focused applied edits from broad rewrites, simple all-dimension successes, failed threshold behavior, and later source corruption.
metadata.oracle_test: For an input shaped (2, 3, 4) reduced over axes (0, 1), each of the four outputs has six candidates and is independently nulled exactly when `6 - mask.sum((0, 1)) < min_count`; the unchanged shared helper must govern both sum and product.
metadata.stage: Derive and implement the shared nanops correction

scale.1: No applied task-relevant correction is observable, or later source/import evidence shows that the current helper is unusable.
scale.2: An applied attempt is observable, but current direct evidence shows a decisive semantic defect such as a remaining rejection, whole-input counting, invalid indexing, reversed mask logic, or incorrect threshold nulling.
scale.3: The selected-axis idea is present, but the current implementation is broad, incomplete, limited to one path, contradicted by a relevant execution failure, or otherwise not established as the focused coherent helper correction.
scale.4: The latest observable source state or successful narrow mutation applies the exact selected-axis product and removes the rejection in the shared helper without a later contradiction, while preserving surrounding logic; validation is basic or lacks a discriminative partial threshold case.
scale.5: The focused shared-helper correction is observably current and coherent, and discriminative evidence confirms independent partial multi-axis threshold behavior, with shared sum and product coverage.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression or compatibility damage

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, edits, or validates multi-axis min_count behavior in the shared nanops reduction helper.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates visible application of the focused multi-axis min_count correction in the shared helper. The intended edit accepts sequence-valued axes and computes each output position's valid count as the product of exactly the reduced axis lengths minus the missing-value count over those same axes, while leaving established scalar, promotion, and null-filling control flow intact. Judge defects causally: a failure in a partial multi-axis reduction directly tests the new selected-axis logic, while a full reduction to one scalar may only establish exception removal and must not discredit an otherwise exact narrow edit when the failure arises in unchanged scalar or environment-sensitive code. Broad rewrites receive less credit because they make causal attribution and compatibility uncertain.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 when current direct evidence shows that the applied edit retains the sequence-axis rejection, indexes a shape tuple with a tuple or array, counts dimensions outside the selected axes, reverses missing-mask polarity, or causes a partial multi-axis result to violate the strict valid-count threshold. Also cap at 2 for an edit-caused helper exception such as unconditional access to `result.ndim` on a scalar object. Score 1 when no task-relevant edit is applied or later source, parser, or import evidence proves the helper unusable. A failing full reduction to a scalar caps the score only when the visible edit changed the scalar branch or otherwise establishes that the new selected-axis expression caused the failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later direct source views, parser or import results, and repository-connected reductions outrank plans, mutation intent, and standalone calculations. A successful narrow replacement establishes the reported line change unless later direct evidence contradicts it. Partial multi-axis reductions retaining an unreduced output dimension are authoritative for selected-axis counting; full reductions establish exception removal and scalar-path behavior but do not by themselves prove or refute per-output counting. Incorrect test expectations, unsupported APIs, unrelated dependency failures, and failures isolated to visibly unchanged environment-sensitive code do not override a coherent focused mutation.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating removal of the exception with correct selected-axis counting, treating every scalar full-reduction failure as caused by the narrow fix, rewarding broad helper rewrites as equivalent to a focused mutation, accepting whole-input size for partial reductions, or relying on standalone NumPy arithmetic as proof of repository behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require observable application in the shared helper of both removal of the sequence-axis rejection and an expression equivalent to `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod() - mask.sum(axis)`, with no edit-caused structural or partial-reduction contradiction. A broad helper, signature, caller, or scalar-control-flow rewrite cannot exceed 3 without a later coherent source view and successful repository-connected validation. Score 5 additionally requires a partial multi-axis case with remaining output positions that exercises both valid_count equal to min_count and valid_count below min_count, plus evidence that the shared path still serves sum and product.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine first whether the latest applied change is the narrow two-part helper correction or a broader rewrite. Then inspect whether reduced-axis lengths and missing counts use the identical axis set. Attribute failures to the changed logic only when the visible source or a discriminative partial reduction provides that causal link; do not let an unchanged scalar branch erase credit for an exact focused edit.
metadata.oracle_test: For shape `(2, 3, 4)` reduced over axes `(0, 1)`, each of the four outputs has six candidates and valid count `6 - mask.sum((0, 1))`. An output remains non-null at valid count six when `min_count` is six and becomes null below six when `min_count` is six. The same unchanged shared helper governs sum and product.
metadata.stage: Apply and causally validate the shared nanops correction

scale.1: No task-relevant correction is observably applied, or later direct source, parser, or import evidence shows that the current helper is unusable.
scale.2: An applied attempt has a decisive defect attributable to the edit, such as a remaining rejection, invalid selected-axis indexing, wrong axis set, edit-caused scalar exception, or incorrect partial multi-axis threshold behavior.
scale.3: The selected-axis idea is applied, but the implementation broadly rewrites helper control flow or callers, is only partly observable, is confined to one operation, or remains materially uncertain after relevant validation.
scale.4: A focused current helper edit removes the sequence-axis rejection and uses the exact selected-axis product with matching missing-value reduction while preserving surrounding control flow; no causally relevant contradiction is visible, but validation is basic or lacks a discriminative partial-output boundary case.
scale.5: The focused current correction is coherent and repository-connected partial multi-axis evidence confirms independent output behavior on both sides of the strict threshold, with the shared sum and product paths preserved.
