scale.4: Provides a decisive regression setup with ignored and non-ignored files and verifies the expected recursive selection under the affected path semantics.
scale.5: Provides the anchor-4 test as a maintainable repository test and also shows before/after failure discrimination or an equivalent direct assertion of normalized discovery paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces a decisive recursive ignore-path regression test

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why a configured ignore-path regex fails during recursive discovery, especially for a directory argument ending in a slash or on Windows.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the task-causal mismatch between the path strings produced during recursive discovery and the POSIX-or-Windows alternatives compiled for `ignore-paths`, rather than treating configuration loading or recursive ignoring in general as broken.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory concludes that configuration is absent, that `ignore-paths` universally fails, or that absolute paths are inherently the defect despite visible evidence that the requested relative-path case works on POSIX. Cap at 3 if it identifies only the directory-without-trailing-separator symptom without explaining why matching the subsequently discovered file also fails on Windows.
metadata.evidence_authority: Concrete printed path values and direct regex-match results under Windows path semantics outrank speculation; relevant source inspection outranks unrelated configuration experiments.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards plausible but incorrect diagnoses such as stale configuration, an uncompiled regex, absolute-path matching, or merely failing to test each individual file.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an explicit causal chain from the recursive input/path construction to a representation that the compiled all-POSIX and all-Windows regex alternatives do not match.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or experiments connecting `PyLinter._discover_files`, `os.walk`/`os.path.join`, the `regexp_paths_csv` transformation, and a path such as `src/gen\about.py` or another mixed-separator result caused by starting from `src/` on Windows.
metadata.oracle_test: With `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]` and the recursive argument `src/`, the semantic reference is that Windows recursive discovery must present a consistently normalized path such as `src\gen\about.py` or `src/gen/about.py` to the dual-format regex, not a mixed-separator spelling.

scale.1: No task-specific diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the inspected code and observed behavior.
scale.2: Finds the recursive discovery and ignore helpers but gives only a vague or materially incorrect explanation of the failure.
scale.3: Recognizes a path-format, separator, or trailing-slash sensitivity and supplies some relevant source or regex evidence, but does not establish the complete Windows recursive causal chain.
scale.4: Correctly explains that recursive discovery from the supplied spelling can produce a path representation incompatible with both compiled path-regex alternatives, with concrete source and path-match evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and decisively distinguishes it from configuration loading, generic absolute-path, directory-only, and file-level-filtering hypotheses using focused comparative evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnoses the Windows recursive-path representation failure

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or edits production code to make recursive `ignore-paths` matching use stable path separators.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Confines the implementation to normalizing recursive filesystem arguments or equivalent discovered-path inputs before traversal and ignore matching, preserving the established `ignore-paths` regex semantics and shared ignore helper.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for globally changing regex matching from `match` to `search`, rewriting user regexes, appending separators merely to force a directory match, or substituting `_ignore_paths` for `config.ignore_paths` without evidence of a stale-value defect. Cap at 3 for adding duplicate per-file filtering without addressing the mixed-path source.
metadata.evidence_authority: A coherent diff in the recursive discovery path outranks prose. A narrowly equivalent normalization backed by path evidence can receive full credit; broad changes to regex matching or configuration parsing cannot.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for overbroad semantic changes that may make the reported example pass while changing anchored-regex behavior or unrelated ignore options.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a concrete localized implementation or exact patch plan that normalizes the path used by recursive discovery while retaining `_is_ignored_file` and existing option values.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or concrete patch plan in `pylint/lint/pylinter.py`, especially `_discover_files`, that applies `os.path.normpath` at the recursive input/traversal boundary before `os.path.isdir`, `os.walk`, and yielded-path construction.
metadata.oracle_test: Normalizing an input such as `src/` with the host path rules before `os.walk` makes all descendants use one separator convention, allowing the existing transformed `^src/gen/.*$` pattern to match on Windows.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed edit is unrelated to recursive path discovery.
scale.2: Proposes a broad or incorrect production change that alters regex semantics, configuration parsing, or unrelated lint behavior.
scale.3: Works near `_discover_files` and could suppress the reported files, but duplicates filtering, handles only a symptom, or leaves the path representation inconsistent.
scale.4: Presents a localized normalization change at the recursive discovery boundary that preserves existing ignore semantics and plausibly fixes the Windows case.
scale.5: Presents the anchor-4 implementation with clear ordering and scope, explains why normalization occurs before traversal/path construction, and shows that package, non-package, and explicit non-directory inputs retain their established control flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Targets normalization at the recursive discovery boundary

applies_when: The trajectory contains a proposed or applied change to modify_sys_path or its immediate callers.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible implementation preserves an arbitrary sys.path[0] while continuing to remove "", ".", or the current working directory and retaining coherent existing PYTHONPATH cleanup behavior without unrelated control-flow changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An inverted condition, unconditional arbitrary-path removal, malformed function, or early return that visibly suppresses required unrelated cleanup caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file content or unified diff outranks earlier proposed snippets and verbal summaries; runtime evidence cannot rescue visibly inverted or malformed code.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistakes a patch that removes arbitrary entries, returns at the wrong time, or accidentally rewrites multiple pop sites for the requested guard.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visible coherent implementation whose condition removes the three intended working-directory forms and preserves other first entries.
metadata.judge_focus: The exact condition around the initial removal, placement and reuse of cwd, safe access to sys.path, and the unchanged or equivalently correct behavior of subsequent PYTHONPATH branches.
metadata.oracle_test: For first entries "", ".", and os.getcwd(), the entry is removed; for "something" or another non-cwd path, it remains. Existing leading/trailing-colon PYTHONPATH processing remains reachable and coherent.

scale.1: No implementation, syntactically corrupted implementation, or behavior opposite to the requested fix.
scale.2: Shows the intended idea but the visible code is incomplete, inverted, unsafe, or introduces a clear control-flow regression.
scale.3: Implements the central guard correctly but leaves a visible robustness or compatibility concern, such as unsafe empty-list access or questionable alteration of adjacent cleanup logic.
scale.4: Provides a coherent focused implementation that preserves arbitrary first entries, removes all three cwd representations, and keeps the surrounding PYTHONPATH behavior intact.
scale.5: Provides a precise, robust, and minimal implementation with safe indexing where relevant, consistent cwd handling, and no unnecessary behavioral or formatting changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic correctness and boundary of the implementation

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis, source inspection, or runtime evidence concerning pylint.modify_sys_path and runpy execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that modify_sys_path unconditionally removes sys.path[0], although runpy or an embedding application may place an arbitrary library path there, and distinguishes that entry from current-working-directory representations that pylint intentionally removes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory concludes that arbitrary first entries should be removed, or reverses which entries are protected, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and successful direct runtime observations outrank unsupported narrative; a genuine runpy reproduction outranks a hand-written simulation of pop behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards superficial recognition of a sys.path issue despite misunderstanding which entries are safe to remove.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly distinguishing arbitrary injected paths from "", ".", and os.getcwd().
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of pylint/__init__.py, pylint/__main__.py, sys.path before/after output, and reasoning connecting the unconditional first pop to the reported embedding failure.
metadata.oracle_test: With sys.path beginning with "something", calling the relevant pylint path-modification behavior must not remove "something"; the original unconditional sys.path.pop(0) does remove it.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis incompatible with the reported behavior.
scale.2: Mentions sys.path or runpy but does not localize the unconditional first-entry removal or misstates its effect.
scale.3: Localizes the unconditional sys.path.pop(0) and explains that it can remove an injected path, but does not fully distinguish the intended removable entries.
scale.4: Correctly explains the arbitrary-path failure and the intended treatment of "", ".", and os.getcwd(), with source-based reasoning.
scale.5: Provides the complete source-supported causal model and decisive observed before/after evidence, while also distinguishing the initial removal from the later PYTHONPATH-specific cleanup.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of the sys.path mutation

applies_when: The trajectory contains a proposed or applied change to modify_sys_path or its immediate path-cleanup logic.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The applied change guards the original initial sys.path removal so that "", ".", and the current working directory are removed while arbitrary caller-injected first entries are preserved, without introducing a concrete defect into the surrounding PYTHONPATH cleanup.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 if the applied patch uses reversed polarity, still unconditionally removes the initial arbitrary entry, or introduces an early return that bypasses required existing cleanup. Score at most 3 if the central guard is correct but the patch newly adds a concrete adjacent defect such as accessing sys.path[1] without establishing that index 1 exists, changing a required pop target, or duplicating cleanup. Score 1 if the latest function is malformed or incoherent. Do not penalize unchanged legacy positional cleanup solely because it was not redesigned.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest applied repository source or unified diff outranks proposed snippets, simulations, summaries, and test claims. Executions of the actual modified function or focused repository tests corroborate source semantics but cannot override a visibly malformed, inverted, or regression-inducing patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating a focused correct fix as defective merely because it leaves legacy PYTHONPATH logic unchanged, while still withholding high credit from patches that obtain the simple repro behavior by introducing unsafe adjacent edits or bypassing existing cleanup.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a visibly applied, syntactically coherent guard at the original initial-removal site that preserves arbitrary first entries and removes all three requested working-directory representations. Merely proposing the guard or testing an unattached helper cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final applied diff or file state for the condition replacing the original unconditional initial pop, its polarity and placement, and any newly edited adjacent pop indices, bounds checks, or returns. Treat untouched pre-existing PYTHONPATH branches as neutral rather than requiring this task to redesign them.
metadata.oracle_test: At the original initial-removal point, first entries "", ".", and os.getcwd() are removed, while "something" or another unrelated injected path is retained. Any surrounding PYTHONPATH code changed by the patch remains reachable, uses valid indices, and removes the intended entry; unchanged surrounding branches are outside the demanded fix.

scale.1: The latest applied function is malformed or incoherent, or the initial removal plainly retains the original opposite behavior.
scale.2: No valid applied selective guard exists, or the applied approach has reversed polarity, still removes arbitrary first entries, or uses broad control flow such as an early return that visibly suppresses required cleanup.
scale.3: The applied initial guard has the correct polarity and requested value set, but the patch newly introduces a concrete adjacent defect such as unsafe new indexing, a wrong pop target, duplicated cleanup, or another material regression.
scale.4: A coherent applied guard correctly preserves arbitrary first entries and removes "", ".", and cwd; adjacent cleanup is unchanged or equivalently coherent, with no visible introduced regression, but focused runtime corroboration is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Meets the score-4 implementation standard and is corroborated by trustworthy execution of the actual modified function or a focused repository test covering arbitrary-entry preservation and removal of "", ".", and cwd.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct selective initial removal without new adjacent regressions

applies_when: The trajectory contains executed commands or tests intended to validate modify_sys_path or the reported runpy behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces trustworthy observed evidence that arbitrary leading entries leave the complete path list unchanged, while "", ".", and the current working directory each cause exactly one leading removal with the remaining list preserved.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A dependency failure before modify_sys_path executes, an unattached simulation, a harness that changes sys.path while importing the function under test, misleading expected-result logic, or an assertion that checks only index 0 despite possible duplication caps credit at 3. Any observed duplicate arbitrary entry, altered tail, wrong removal, or failed relevant assertion caps credit at 2 unless a later valid run decisively corrects it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing assertions and observed before/after lists from the actual applied function or a repository test outrank printed expectations, copied helper logic, simulations, and narrative claims. A genuine runpy reproduction outranks direct invocation. The latest corrected valid harness outranks earlier harness mistakes, but visible applied source that cannot produce the claimed output caps credit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating printed success messages, copied conditional logic, index-only checks, dependency failures, or preservation by duplication as decisive behavioral validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require observed passing execution of the actual applied function for an arbitrary prefix and for at least two of "", ".", and cwd, with assertions or complete before/after lists sufficient to detect duplication and tail reordering.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed input lists, observed output lists, assertions, and exit status. Confirm that tests invoke the repository's applied modify_sys_path or a genuine runpy path, compare complete list contents and order, and separately cover arbitrary preservation and intended removals.
metadata.oracle_test: For a fixed tail such as ["sentinel-a", "sentinel-b"], ["something", *tail] remains exactly unchanged. Each of ["", *tail], [".", *tail], and [os.getcwd(), *tail] becomes exactly tail. A runpy reproduction with an injected arbitrary prefix leaves that prefix and the rest of the caller's path ordering intact.

scale.1: No relevant executed behavioral evidence is visible, or observed execution shows the target behavior is wrong.
scale.2: Execution is attempted but does not reach the applied function, uses an invalid or contradictory harness, or visibly produces duplication, tail corruption, or an incorrect removal.
scale.3: Trustworthy execution establishes only one side of the contract, or covers both sides without enough list-state evidence to exclude duplication or reordering.
scale.4: Observed passing execution of the actual applied function proves exact arbitrary-list preservation and exact removal for at least two of "", ".", and cwd, with no contradictory relevant result.
scale.5: Observed passing execution proves the complete four-case exact-list oracle and also demonstrates the reported runpy scenario or an equivalent end-to-end invocation through pylint's module entry path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Behavioral proof of exact preservation and single removal

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, runs, or discusses tests for the reported caplog.clear() behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides task-specific evidence that get_records("call") and caplog.records agree before and after clear, that both become empty, that caplog.text is cleared, and that records logged after clear appear in both views.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A failing task reproduction caps credit at 2 unless a later visible change and rerun resolves it; a passing run whose imported module is shown to come from another installation caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A test run demonstrably loading the modified checkout outranks unexecuted test text, isolated list simulations, or runs against an installed pytest copy.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking equality immediately after clear for a complete fix even though get_records may remain frozen and omit later records.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evidence for a new record emitted after clear, not merely equality of two empty lists.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code and command output covering pre-clear logging, clear, post-clear equality/emptiness, post-clear logging, and text behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: In one call phase: initial equality; log A and equality; clear and equality with both lists empty and text empty; log B and equality with only B present.

scale.1: No relevant behavioral test or runtime evidence is present.
scale.2: Uses only a toy list simulation, malformed fixture setup, or an unproven external pytest run.
scale.3: Runs or specifies the original reproduction through clear and demonstrates empty-list consistency, but omits continued capture or text clearing.
scale.4: Covers clear, empty records/text, and logging after clear with credible local execution, but lacks one explicit identity/content assertion or has minor provenance uncertainty.
scale.5: Provides and passes a focused local regression test covering equality before clear, emptiness and text reset after clear, and synchronized capture of new post-clear records.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive behavioral test for clear and continued capture

applies_when: The trajectory relies on test output, imports, environment changes, or contradictory results to justify the proposed fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures reliance on runtime evidence that does not demonstrably exercise the modified checkout, and failure to respond correctly when focused or regression tests contradict the proposed solution.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later provenance check and successful rerun against the modified checkout reduces this failure mode; merely asserting that a failure is unrelated without evidence does not.
metadata.evidence_authority: A shown imported module path and focused rerun determine provenance; explicit failing output overrides the trajectory's verbal claim that tests passed or the fix works.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding apparent test activity when it exercises system pytest, or accepting selective passing tests while an observed all-stages regression remains unresolved.
metadata.hard_gate: Severity above 3 requires either repeated reliance on the wrong installation or continued endorsement of an implementation after a directly relevant regression failure.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands, reported pytest versions and module paths, PYTHONPATH usage, visible diffs, failing outputs, and whether the trajectory revises its hypothesis after contradictions.
metadata.oracle_test: The executed pytest must import _pytest.logging from the checkout containing the visible change, and failures in the original reproduction or phase-history tests must trigger diagnosis and revision.

scale.1: Evidence provenance is clear, relevant contradictions are resolved, and conclusions match the visible results.
scale.2: Minor environment uncertainty or an incidental failure exists, but the trajectory recognizes it and does not rely on it for correctness.
scale.3: Important test provenance is unproven or a relevant failure is only partially investigated, making conclusions uncertain.
scale.4: The trajectory relies substantially on system-installed pytest, malformed simulations, or dismisses a directly relevant failure without resolution.
scale.5: The trajectory repeatedly claims success despite visible reproduction or phase-regression failures, or continues modifying code based on evidence known not to exercise the checkout.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unsupported or contradictory runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory changes handler reset behavior, stash handling, or get_records phase selection, or runs broader logging fixture tests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Demonstrates that the fix preserves pytest's phase-separated logging contract: entering a new phase does not erase records retained for earlier phases, and get_records(when) continues to honor its requested phase.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any visible failure showing setup records disappearing after call begins, call records disappearing during teardown, or get_records ignoring its when argument caps credit at 1 until a revised implementation passes the same scenario.
metadata.evidence_authority: A focused phase-transition test against the modified checkout outranks a broad suite summary; an observed phase-history failure overrides an otherwise passing reproduction.
metadata.failure_mode: Overfitting to the single call-phase reproduction and regressing the established all-stages behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either a passing phase-transition test or an exact source-based explanation tied to _runtest_for resetting the shared handler before assigning each phase entry.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, existing test inspection, or executed tests involving setup/call/teardown records, especially test_caplog_captures_for_all_stages or an equivalent pytester test.
metadata.oracle_test: After setup logging, get_records("setup") retains setup records during call; get_records("call") contains call records independently; teardown obtains a fresh active list without mutating the saved setup or call lists.

scale.1: The visible implementation or test evidence erases or conflates phase histories.
scale.2: Phase behavior is not considered despite a change to shared reset or stash semantics.
scale.3: Mentions phase preservation or runs broad tests, but provides no decisive phase-transition evidence.
scale.4: Correctly protects phase isolation with credible source reasoning or a focused passing test, though coverage is not complete across all three phases.
scale.5: Shows decisive passing evidence across setup, call, and teardown and explains why the implementation preserves prior phase lists while clearing only the active phase.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protection of setup, call, and teardown record history

applies_when: The trajectory inspects, proposes, applies, or validates source changes involving caplog.clear(), capture-handler reset, phase-record storage, or get_records(when).
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the latest visibly established implementation of the boundary between user-requested clearing and pytest's phase lifecycle: explicit clear must empty the active saved list in place and reset text, while lifecycle reset must install a fresh list and phase lookup must continue to use the requested saved phase.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A checkout-backed failure showing erased phase history, disconnected post-clear capture, a missing phase mapping, or ignored phase selection limits the score to 1 until a later visible source correction passes the same scenario. Without such runtime confirmation, source that erases the complete phase mapping, bypasses requested-phase lookup, or leaves reset unable to clear records is limited to 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest concrete source listing or unified diff has precedence over prose and toy simulations. A later focused checkout-backed failure overrides an otherwise plausible diff; an edit command without a resulting source display is only a proposal. Earlier edits superseded by later visible source are not scored as the final implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating equality immediately after clear as proof of a correct fix while lifecycle reset now mutates saved phase lists, the phase mapping has been discarded, post-clear records cannot reach get_records(when), or only a proposed separation exists.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires visible applied source with distinct operations for lifecycle replacement and explicit in-place clearing. A score of 5 additionally requires that the phase mapping and requested-phase lookup remain unchanged and that the text stream is reset.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the latest source through handler lifecycle reset, the fixture's explicit clear path, phase-list assignment, get_records(when), and text reset. Separately identify unchanged source, an attempted but causally wrong edit, a structurally destructive edit, and a runtime-confirmed regression.
metadata.oracle_test: At a phase boundary, reset installs a new records list before that list is saved for the new phase. During that phase, explicit clear mutates the saved active list to empty and resets the stream without replacing or deleting the phase mapping; a later record is appended to that same active list, while earlier phase lists remain intact.

scale.1: The latest applied source is nonfunctional or an authoritative run confirms structural breakage, such as a missing phase mapping, erased prior-phase records, disconnected post-clear capture, ignored phase selection, or diagnostic code that no longer clears records.
scale.2: A concrete source edit addresses the symptom but has a visible causal boundary error not yet confirmed by a focused run, such as clearing or replacing the complete phase mapping, globally clearing the lifecycle-reset list in place, copying the active list into phase storage, or always returning the current handler list.
scale.3: Relevant source remains unchanged, the correct separation is only proposed, or an applied partial refactor does not visibly establish both lifecycle list replacement and explicit in-place clearing.
scale.4: The latest visible source implements separate lifecycle-reset and explicit-clear operations, preserves phase-specific lookup, and resets text, but a minor ambiguity remains about scope, active-list aliasing, or validation.
scale.5: The latest visible source cleanly uses fresh-list replacement only for lifecycle transitions and in-place clearing only for explicit caplog.clear(), preserves the complete phase mapping and requested-phase lookup, resets text, and contains no contradictory focused evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied separation of user clear from lifecycle reset

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change intended to fix caplog.clear() and get_records() synchronization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Confines in-place record clearing to the user-facing caplog.clear() path, while retaining list replacement for pytest's internal phase reset, or implements an equivalently narrow design that keeps the active phase synchronized without erasing prior phases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A diff changing the shared LogCaptureHandler.reset implementation from assignment to list.clear(), with no separate lifecycle mechanism, caps credit at 2 because _runtest_for invokes reset at every phase boundary. Deleting all phase stash entries or making get_records always return the current handler also caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The actual visible diff has precedence over prose summaries; an equivalent design is acceptable only when its source-level behavior is explicit.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting the tempting one-line global self.records.clear() change even though it makes setup, call, and teardown reuse and clear the same list.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a concrete implementation boundary that preserves both active-phase aliasing and historical phase lists.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or explicitly stated edit showing which method performs in-place clearing, which method retains replacement semantics, and how the text stream is reset.
metadata.oracle_test: A suitable design keeps reset() able to install a fresh records list for a new phase, while caplog.clear() clears the existing active list in place and resets captured text.

scale.1: No concrete implementation is identified, or the change targets unrelated code.
scale.2: Implements a broad fix that resolves the immediate equality check but destroys phase history, such as globally clearing in reset, clearing the whole stash, or ignoring the requested phase in get_records.
scale.3: Targets relevant code and plausibly handles clear(), but leaves the phase-reset boundary ambiguous or incompletely implemented.
scale.4: Shows a narrow implementation that separates explicit clearing from lifecycle reset and also resets text, with only minor clarity or style gaps.
scale.5: Shows a minimal, idiomatic implementation in the logging capture classes that clears the active records list in place only for caplog.clear(), preserves fresh-list phase resets, and leaves unrelated handlers and APIs unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise implementation boundary for explicit clear versus lifecycle reset

applies_when: A source change is proposed or applied to pytest's unittest TestCase --pdb handling
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes only the --pdb tearDown-deferral decision in src/_pytest/unittest.py so deferral occurs only when neither the test method nor its containing TestCase class is marked by unittest.skip, preserving existing behavior for method-level skips and non-skipped tests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Replacing _is_skipped(self.obj) solely with _is_skipped(self._testcase), the class, or another single target is capped at 3 because it can regress method-level unittest.skip behavior; edits outside the unittest --pdb boundary without necessity are capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible repository diff or post-edit source excerpt outranks a stated intended change. Checking both method and class skip state outranks replacing the method check with a class or instance check alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a superficially successful class-skip fix that drops the pre-existing method-level skip protection or alters general teardown semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an applied source edit that preserves the existing self.obj skip check while adding class-level skip detection in the usepdb branch.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible edits or diffs around TestCaseFunction.runtest, especially a combined skip predicate using self.obj and the containing class such as self.parent.obj; cleanliness and locality of the change are also relevant.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended predicate is semantically equivalent to: usepdb and not (_is_skipped(test_method) or _is_skipped(containing_TestCase_class)).

scale.1: No implementation direction, or a change aimed at an unrelated subsystem.
scale.2: Suggests changing skip or teardown behavior broadly but does not identify a safe predicate and boundary.
scale.3: Identifies the correct usepdb branch and proposes a plausible edit, or applies a one-sided check that does not preserve both method- and class-level skip handling.
scale.4: Applies the correct combined method/class skip predicate in TestCaseFunction.runtest with no visible unrelated production changes.
scale.5: Applies and visibly confirms a minimal, readable diff implementing the exact combined predicate while retaining the surrounding deferred-teardown lifecycle unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal and compatibility-preserving implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory considers tests or compatibility consequences beyond the single class-level skip reproducer
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects method-level unittest.skip behavior, class-level unittest.skip behavior, and ordinary non-skipped TestCase execution under --pdb, ideally by extending the repository's existing pdb teardown-skipped test and running relevant unittest tests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible evidence shows method-level skipped tests now invoke tearDown, or normal non-skipped tests no longer execute tearDown, credit is capped at 1. A replacement predicate that inherently loses method-level detection caps credit at 2 absent corrective evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository regression tests with behavioral assertions outrank ad hoc print-based examples; targeted test results outrank broad suite claims without output. Failures in relevant tests outrank unrelated passing tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents accepting a narrow fix that solves the reported class case while undoing the earlier method-level skip protection or suppressing tearDown for normal tests.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires evidence covering both class-level and method-level unittest.skip under --pdb, because preserving the original method-level fix is essential.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible examination or modification of testing/test_unittest.py, especially the existing pdb teardown-skipped coverage; runtime checks for method-level skip, class-level skip, and non-skipped setUp/test/tearDown behavior; relevant suite results.
metadata.oracle_test: Under --pdb: class-skipped and method-skipped TestCase methods produce skipped outcomes with no setUp/tearDown tracking; a non-skipped TestCase still runs its normal lifecycle. Existing unittest-focused tests remain green.

scale.1: Relevant evidence shows a compatibility regression in method-level skip or normal TestCase lifecycle behavior.
scale.2: Mentions regressions or runs unrelated tests, but does not cover the pre-existing method-level skip behavior.
scale.3: Exercises one compatibility case in addition to the reproducer, or locates the existing regression test without demonstrating adequate coverage.
scale.4: Shows successful task-relevant runtime coverage for class-level skip, method-level skip, and at least one non-skipped TestCase behavior under the applicable execution path.
scale.5: Adds or clearly prepares a focused repository regression test for class-level skip alongside existing method-level coverage and shows the targeted test plus an appropriate unittest-focused suite passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Regression protection for existing unittest and debugger semantics

applies_when: The trajectory executes task-specific tests or commands intended to demonstrate the class-level unittest.skip behavior under --pdb
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses the affected repository code to demonstrate that a class-decorated unittest.TestCase with failing or tracked setUp/tearDown is reported only as skipped under --pdb, with neither lifecycle method executed and no teardown error or debugger entry.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Any later task-specific post-change run that still reports a tearDown exception, error status, or debugger entry caps this rubric at 1 until a subsequent visible correction and clean rerun supersedes it.
metadata.evidence_authority: A post-edit run against the local source outranks logic-only scripts, normal runs without --pdb, runs against an unrelated installed pytest, or assertions based only on missing captured print output. A visible post-edit failure outranks claimed success.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating a normal run, a pure attribute-check script, a test against a newer external pytest, or suppressed stdout as proof that the local --pdb bug is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a direct post-change --pdb run against the modified checkout that exits with a clean skipped result and no teardown failure.
metadata.judge_focus: Commands using the local checkout, preferably through PYTHONPATH or the repository test harness; output must include --pdb, the class-level decorator, skip outcome, and absence of tearDown effects.
metadata.oracle_test: The minimal reproducer should finish as one skipped test under --pdb; sentinel exceptions in setUp and tearDown must not appear, and the run must not show an additional error.

scale.1: Visible post-change task-specific evidence still shows tearDown execution or another direct contradiction, or the only claimed validation is demonstrably invalid.
scale.2: Only generic, non-pdb, external-version, or logic-level checks are shown; they do not exercise the failing path.
scale.3: Shows either a credible pre-change reproduction or a clean --pdb run, but not enough evidence to tie the clean result to the applied local change and absence of lifecycle execution.
scale.4: Shows a clean post-change local --pdb run of the class-level skip reproducer with a skipped-only outcome and no teardown error.
scale.5: Shows both the original failure and the corrected post-change behavior, or an equivalent tracked/sentinel assertion proving setUp and tearDown remain untouched, using the modified repository implementation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive --pdb reproduction and post-change runtime evidence

applies_when: The task concerns PDB-specific deferred tearDown handling for a class-skipped unittest.TestCase
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether an applied repository change gates PDB-specific deferred tearDown using an object that carries the effective class-level unittest skip state, preserves ordinary non-skipped TestCase execution, and leaves no observed recurrence of the reported teardown failure unresolved.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied guard that checks only a pytest collector, checks only the test method for a class-level skip, or uses reversed polarity is scored 1 regardless of non-diagnostic passing output. A semantically causal edit followed by the same class-skip tearDown exception, error outcome, or debugger entry is capped at 2 until the provenance discrepancy is visibly resolved or a later clean local rerun supersedes it. Visible suppression of tearDown for an ordinary non-skipped TestCase also caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed repository source or a repository diff outranks proposed code and prose. Runtime semantics of the inspected object determine whether the guard can observe class-level skip state. A clean --pdb run proven to load the edited checkout outranks indirect scripts. A post-edit task command launched from the checkout that still reports the target tearDown error remains an unresolved contradiction unless visible evidence proves it loaded stale or external code or a later clean modified-checkout rerun supersedes it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for proposed-only fixes, guards aimed at objects that cannot carry class-level unittest skip state, and apparently correct edits whose subsequent recurrence of the reported failure is ignored rather than diagnosed or cleanly rerun.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 2 through 5 require a visible applied source edit. Scores 3 through 5 require correct polarity and inspection of the TestCase class, its instance, or an equivalent object carrying inherited class-level __unittest_skip__. Score 4 requires a clean post-edit class-level skip run under --pdb using the modified checkout.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied source condition in the unittest TestCase runtest path, the runtime object supplying __unittest_skip__, and any post-edit class-skip --pdb executions. Distinguish a cleanly validated edit from an edit followed by the same teardown error without a diagnostic resolution or clean rerun.
metadata.oracle_test: With --pdb, a unittest.TestCase class decorated with unittest.skip must produce only a skipped outcome and must not execute setUp or tearDown. An otherwise equivalent non-skipped TestCase must retain its normal lifecycle.

scale.1: No relevant source edit is applied, or the applied guard has wrong polarity or inspects an object that cannot reveal the class-level unittest skip state.
scale.2: A semantically plausible class-skip guard is applied, but a later task-specific --pdb execution still shows the reported tearDown failure, error outcome, debugger entry, or broken ordinary lifecycle, and that contradiction remains unresolved.
scale.3: A semantically causal guard is applied with no unresolved visible contradiction, but validation is absent, indirect, non-pdb, or not demonstrably tied to the modified checkout.
scale.4: A semantically causal guard is applied and a direct post-edit --pdb run using the modified checkout cleanly reports the class-decorated TestCase as skipped without a teardown error, but ordinary lifecycle or stronger sentinel coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: A semantically causal guard is applied and authoritative validation proves the class-skipped TestCase does not execute setUp or tearDown under --pdb while an ordinary non-skipped TestCase retains its lifecycle, with focused repository regression coverage or an appropriate relevant suite also passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied class-skip teardown guard and contradiction resolution

applies_when: The task concerns unittest class-level skipping interacting with pytest PDB teardown handling
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the visible prefix contains an applied source change that prevents PDB-specific deferred tearDown handling for a TestCase skipped at class level while retaining the intended handling of relevant non-skipped tests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the applied condition checks an object that does not carry the class-level skip attribute or has the wrong polarity. Cap at 3 if a task-specific execution using the modified checkout still invokes tearDown or reports its error and the contradiction remains unresolved. Installation failures alone are not evidence that the source fix fails.
metadata.evidence_authority: An actual repository diff or displayed post-edit source outranks proposed code and prose. Semantics of the object being checked outrank a claimed success from an unrelated, stale, or non-diagnostic installation. A task-specific run proven to load the modified source outranks speculative reasoning.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for correctly describing class-versus-method skip inheritance while applying no fix, checking the pytest parent node instead of the parent class, or treating a non-diagnostic passing run as proof.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible applied edit to the relevant repository source. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require that the edited condition inspect an object that actually carries the class-level unittest skip state, such as the TestCase class or its instance, rather than only a pytest collector node or test method.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the repository source change in the unittest TestCase execution path, especially which runtime object supplies the class-level __unittest_skip__ state and whether that state gates deferred tearDown behavior. Then inspect executions that demonstrably use the modified checkout.
metadata.oracle_test: For a unittest.TestCase class decorated with unittest.skip, running pytest with --pdb must report the test as skipped without invoking setUp or tearDown; an otherwise equivalent non-skipped TestCase must retain normal lifecycle behavior.

scale.1: No relevant repository source edit is visibly applied; the prefix contains only exploration, diagnosis, or a proposed future change.
scale.2: A relevant edit is applied, but its polarity or inspected object cannot detect the class-level skip state, so the task-causal defect remains in the code.
scale.3: A plausibly causal edit is applied, but a task-specific run using the modified checkout visibly contradicts it and the discrepancy remains unresolved.
scale.4: A semantically causal edit is applied to gate deferred tearDown using the effective class-level skip state, with no applicable contradictory result, but validation is incomplete, indirect, or does not cover both skipped and ordinary lifecycle behavior.
scale.5: A semantically causal edit is applied and direct task-specific validation using the modified checkout shows class-skipped execution under --pdb avoids setUp and tearDown while relevant non-skipped behavior remains intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal correctness of the applied class-skip teardown fix

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes or edits mark extraction or mark storage code for class inheritance.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest cutoff-visible implementation or concrete patch design gathers class-local marks across the class MRO without changing non-class extraction or copying inherited marks during decoration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An unresolved traceback on functions, modules, singleton `pytestmark`, or decoration caps the score at 2. Traversing `type(obj).__mro__`, using inherited `getattr` for each MRO entry, or deduplicating marks by name also caps the score at 2. MRO gathering without storage-time isolation caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent repository diff plus direct behavior of its edited functions outranks earlier abandoned snippets, prose intentions, standalone reimplementations, or code copied into another installation. A traceback or counterexample produced by the latest code overrides a claim that the implementation works.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding an attractive MRO loop despite cutoff-visible evidence that it walks the metaclass hierarchy, duplicates inherited values, breaks ordinary function decorators, removes meaningful repeated marks, or smears inherited marks onto a subclass.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visibly applied code that distinguishes classes from non-classes, reads class-local `pytestmark` values rather than inherited values, and preserves an own-marks-only path for `store_mark`.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible state of `get_unpacked_marks`, `store_mark`, and their call sites. Check class detection, the hierarchy actually traversed, use of each class's own namespace, normalization of singleton and list forms, ordering, and whether storage requests only directly stored marks.
metadata.oracle_test: For classes, gather and normalize `base.__dict__.get("pytestmark", [])` over the reversed linearized class MRO so established base-to-derived ordering and repeated marks are retained. For non-classes, preserve direct lookup. `store_mark` must retrieve only marks directly stored on the decorated object, commonly through a `consider_mro=False` path.

scale.1: No coherent implementation boundary is present, or the latest visible edit is unusable and its basic defect is not isolated.
scale.2: A relevant design is proposed but not applied, or an applied attempt has a decisive unresolved defect such as wrong-hierarchy traversal, inherited lookup per entry, non-class failure, malformed normalization, or name-based deduplication.
scale.3: The latest applied code handles the simple two-base class case and retains a viable non-class path, with no demonstrated crash, but ordering, normalization, or storage-time own-mark isolation remains incomplete or unsupported.
scale.4: The latest applied code uses class-local MRO lookup, preserves non-class extraction, and isolates storage from inherited marks; only a minor compatibility detail remains uncertain and no visible evidence contradicts it.
scale.5: A coherent minimal applied implementation visibly covers class-local reversed-MRO gathering, singleton/list normalization, non-class behavior, storage-time isolation, established ordering, and preservation of repeated same-name marks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Coherent applied boundary for MRO-aware mark extraction

applies_when: The trajectory creates, locates, proposes, or runs tests related to marker inheritance or mark selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses repository-relevant tests to demonstrate that a test class inheriting from independently marked bases receives both marks, with exact ordering and compatibility cases that expose duplicate or non-class regressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when tests run against a different installed pytest, fail from malformed fixtures, or assert only raw `TestDings.pytestmark`. Cap at 3 when task behavior passes but a relevant existing marker test visibly fails without resolution.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful execution against the edited checkout with exact assertions outranks ad hoc scripts, installed external pytest versions, collect-only output without marker assertions, or unexecuted test proposals.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating import success, collection count, raw inherited attributes, or hand-written stand-ins for pytest's mark classes as proof of the fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a passing task-specific test that proves both base marks reach the collected class/item rather than merely showing that one test was collected.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test code and command output for marker lists, `-m` selection, existing marker tests, and focused regression cases.
metadata.oracle_test: A decisive scenario marks `Foo` and `Bar` separately, derives `TestDings(Foo, Bar)`, and verifies both marks on the collected test or selection by `-m "foo and bar"`; exact mark-list coverage should follow reversed MRO ordering and include a repeated-decoration or non-class compatibility case.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or only unrelated commands and broken reproductions.
scale.2: A reproduction illustrates the symptom but does not exercise pytest's edited collection behavior, or the visible test result fails.
scale.3: A focused runtime check demonstrates both marks through `get_unpacked_marks` or marker selection, but lacks exact ordering or compatibility coverage.
scale.4: Passing task-specific pytest evidence verifies both inherited marks and at least one compatibility dimension such as functions, singleton `pytestmark`, repeated marks, or reversed parent order.
scale.5: Passing repository-integrated regression tests verify both-base inheritance, exact established order, storage/decorator behavior, and relevant existing marker tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-decisive test coverage and runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory discusses why a multiply inherited test class exposes marks from only one marked base class.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that ordinary `getattr(obj, "pytestmark", ...)` follows Python attribute lookup and stops at the first matching base, while pytest must explicitly gather class-local `pytestmark` values across the class MRO.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory treats `type(obj).__mro__` as the class hierarchy, claims the method function itself should directly contain class marks, or continues to use inherited `getattr` for every MRO entry after evidence of duplication.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed class `__mro__` and `__dict__` contents plus the repository implementation of `get_unpacked_marks` outrank assumptions based only on `TestDings.pytestmark`.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking Python's first-match attribute result for all marks attached throughout the class hierarchy.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing that MRO traversal must read class-local attributes rather than repeatedly using inherited `getattr` results.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source references, reproductions, or reasoning that distinguish inherited attribute lookup from entries defined in each class's own `__dict__`.
metadata.oracle_test: For `TestDings(Foo, Bar)`, `TestDings.__dict__` has no `pytestmark`, `Foo.__dict__` contains `foo`, and `Bar.__dict__` contains `bar`; plain attribute lookup on `TestDings` exposes only `Foo`'s value.

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source/runtime evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes that multiple inheritance or MRO is involved but does not locate the first-match `pytestmark` lookup or proposes an invalid hierarchy traversal.
scale.3: Locates `get_unpacked_marks` and explains that plain `getattr` loses one base's marks, but does not distinguish inherited values from class-local `__dict__` values.
scale.4: Correctly explains class-only MRO traversal using each class's own `pytestmark` definition and preserves the non-class path conceptually.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis with visible supporting evidence, including why inherited `getattr` duplicates the first base and why MRO order and class-local lookup are both necessary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of attribute lookup versus mark inheritance

applies_when: The task requires EncodedFile.mode to stop advertising binary mode while EncodedFile remains a text-writing wrapper
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the applied source coherently exposes the wrapped stream's mode without the binary marker and preserves the wrapper's text-only write semantics without unrelated behavioral changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied change that accepts bytes in EncodedFile.write caps the score at 4. An unreachable, incorrectly nested, duplicated, syntactically malformed, or incomplete mode implementation caps the score at 1 even if narration or an isolated mock claims success.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository source or unified diff outranks plans, summaries, claimed verification, and standalone reimplementations. Relevant tests may confirm behavior but cannot override contradictory or malformed applied source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding proposed work over applied code, accepting a malformed property because its intended logic is correct, or treating byte acceptance as an equivalent solution to correcting the advertised mode.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require an applied, syntactically coherent mode override that removes every 'b' from the wrapped production stream's mode. Score 5 additionally requires preserving the existing rejection of bytes on Python 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible applied source or diff for EncodedFile.mode, method placement and reachability, and any simultaneous change to EncodedFile.write. The production path wraps a binary-mode file but presents a text-writing interface.
metadata.oracle_test: For a production EncodedFile wrapping a stream whose mode is 'rb+', observable EncodedFile.mode should be 'r+' and contain no 'b'; writing text should retain existing behavior, while passing bytes on Python 3 should still raise TypeError.

scale.1: Applied source is malformed, unreachable, internally duplicated, or otherwise cannot reliably provide the required mode contract.
scale.2: Applied source is coherent but leaves binary mode advertised, targets the wrong behavior, or contains no implemented mode correction.
scale.3: An applied mode correction exists but is incomplete or semantically unreliable for the production EncodedFile wrapper; no stronger contradiction from anchor 1 applies.
scale.4: The applied source reliably removes the binary marker from observable mode, but also broadens byte-write behavior or makes another unnecessary task-adjacent behavioral change.
scale.5: The applied source coherently and minimally exposes the wrapped mode without 'b', remains valid for the production wrapper path, and preserves EncodedFile's existing text-only write contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: EncodedFile text-mode contract correctness

applies_when: The trajectory considers or changes EncodedFile.write, writelines, safe_text_dupfile, or adjacent capture behavior while addressing the mode bug.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps EncodedFile's existing text-stream contract—str is encoded to the binary buffer and bytes remain rejected on Python 3—while limiting the behavioral fix to truthful mode reporting.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied or latest-visible change that accepts bytes, suppresses the Python 3 TypeError, duplicates writes, or otherwise broadens the wrapper contract caps credit at 1 until visibly reverted.
metadata.evidence_authority: The actual latest repository diff outranks explanations claiming compatibility; explicit unchanged code or direct tests outrank assumptions based on omitted excerpts.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a workaround that makes the reported example pass by accepting bytes while leaving the stream's advertised and actual contracts inconsistent.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires visible evidence that the applied patch does not broaden write() to accept bytes and does not alter unrelated capture behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diffs and latest source for write(), writelines(), safe_text_dupfile(), and unrelated capture code, plus tests demonstrating retained TypeError behavior for bytes.
metadata.oracle_test: After the fix, EncodedFile.write("text") still succeeds by encoding to the wrapped binary buffer, while EncodedFile.write(b"bytes") still raises TypeError on Python 3.

scale.1: The latest visible implementation broadens byte acceptance, removes the intended TypeError, duplicates writes, or introduces another clear write-path regression.
scale.2: The trajectory proposes changing write semantics or makes broad adjacent changes, but the final visible state is unresolved or contradictory.
scale.3: The intended mode-only boundary is stated, but preservation of the existing write path is not established by visible source or evidence.
scale.4: The visible solution leaves write semantics intact and is narrowly scoped, though explicit regression evidence is limited.
scale.5: The applied diff is confined to truthful mode reporting and visible source or targeted tests decisively confirm both successful str writes and continued bytes rejection.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves the text-only write contract and narrow compatibility boundary

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters a failed predicate, contradictory runtime output, or multiple successive candidate fixes for mock sentinel detection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether observed failures refine the implementation from repeated equality-result coercion, through a bounded but semantically incomplete fallback, to an applied and validated identity-based DEFAULT predicate.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if, after evidence that comparison results are non-scalar, the latest implementation still coerces or reduces those results with bool, any, all, iteration, or element-wise interpretation. Cap at 3 if the trajectory instead catches comparison exceptions and treats them as non-matches, or if the final identity edit is not visibly established. Any unresolved failure after the latest edit prevents a score above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later runtime observations and the latest visible source or diff override earlier claims. An unreconciled failure of the latest code controls over prior passing output. Tests count only when they ran against the implementation visibly in effect.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated reformulations of the disproven equality mechanism, while recognizing that exception containment is a partial recovery distinct from both unsafe result reduction and the complete identity solution.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require visible abandonment of equality and containment on p.new plus an applied identity-based predicate preserving the attribute_name exclusion and all loaded DEFAULT sentinels.
metadata.judge_focus: Compare each observed failure with the next candidate and the latest visible source. Determine whether the trajectory repeats overloaded equality, merely catches its failure, or removes value comparison by checking identity against every loaded DEFAULT sentinel.
metadata.oracle_test: Once p.new in sentinels or p.new == sentinel is observed to yield ambiguous non-scalar truth, robust recovery is to avoid __eq__ entirely and test any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels). Explicit array values then count zero and actual DEFAULT singletons count one.

scale.1: Contradictory evidence is ignored, or the trajectory ends on code visibly shown to fail without acknowledging the failure.
scale.2: The failure is noticed, but the latest candidate still coerces, reduces, or interprets the same overloaded equality result, or makes a success claim contradicted by later output.
scale.3: The trajectory contains the observed failure with exception handling or reaches identity only as an unestablished final proposal, without completing the semantic recovery.
scale.4: The trajectory explicitly rejects equality-based candidates and leaves a visibly applied identity predicate preserving the required counting conditions, but validation of that final state is limited.
scale.5: The trajectory uses failed outputs to explain why equality remains unsafe, visibly applies the identity predicate, and validates the final state with both an explicit array-like value and a genuine DEFAULT patch without unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from failed equality fixes toward identity semantics

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the collection-time ValueError involving a patch whose explicit new value is an array or array-like object.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that num_mock_patch_args is only determining whether a patch uses a mock DEFAULT sentinel, and that membership/equality against an explicit array invokes overloaded equality whose non-scalar result is forced into a boolean context.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims that bool(array), any(array-valued comparisons), or ordinary equality inherently resolves ambiguous array truth without contrary runtime evidence being reconciled.
metadata.evidence_authority: A reproduction using the actual expression or collection path outranks an unsupported explanation; inspected source and unittest.mock patching semantics outrank assumptions about what num_mock_patch_args should count.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a trajectory that notices NumPy in the traceback but misunderstands the fixture-argument accounting or recommends another boolean coercion of the same array-valued comparison.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require identifying both the failing membership/equality operation and the intended DEFAULT-sentinel classification.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, reproductions, or source inspection connecting p.new in sentinels in src/_pytest/compat.py to array-valued equality and the distinction between explicit new values and DEFAULT-generated mock arguments.
metadata.oracle_test: For @patch(target, new=np.array([...])) the patch consumes no injected mock argument, while @patch(target) has p.new equal by identity to the relevant mock module's DEFAULT singleton and consumes one argument.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or diagnosis points to an unrelated collection/fixture mechanism.
scale.2: Locates num_mock_patch_args or mentions ambiguous array truth, but does not accurately connect it to sentinel membership and mock-argument counting.
scale.3: Accurately explains the failing array-valued equality in p.new in sentinels, but only partially explains why DEFAULT patches and explicit-new patches must be classified differently.
scale.4: Correctly explains the failure and DEFAULT-versus-explicit-new semantics, supported by relevant source inspection or a focused reproduction.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal account with decisive visible evidence, including why identity with DEFAULT avoids invoking user-defined or array equality and why the earlier multi-module sentinel list must still be respected.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of overloaded equality during mock-sentinel detection

applies_when: A concrete source change or complete patch strategy for num_mock_patch_args is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the mock-patch argument classification at its narrow boundary so each patch's new value is recognized only when it is the exact DEFAULT singleton from one of the loaded mock modules, without evaluating overloaded equality or altering unrelated argument discovery.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible implementation still uses p.new in sentinels, p.new == sentinel, bool of such a result, or any/all over equality results. Cap at 3 if it broadly catches comparison exceptions or recursively interprets array elements instead of using sentinel identity.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible file or diff outranks earlier proposed edits and prose. A later corrected identity implementation supersedes earlier bool, equality, all, or any attempts.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for fixes that suppress the reported NumPy example while retaining overloaded equality, miscounting explicit values, dropping support for simultaneous mock and unittest.mock modules, or making an unnecessarily broad compatibility change.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a concrete implementation that cannot invoke p.new.__eq__ while checking DEFAULT sentinels.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff or exact proposed expression in src/_pytest/compat.py, especially preservation of not p.attribute_name, iteration over all loaded mock-module DEFAULT values, and identity-based comparison such as any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels).
metadata.oracle_test: The classification predicate is logically: not p.attribute_name and any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels); all existing no-patch and mock-module fallback behavior remains scoped as before.

scale.1: No concrete implementation, or the implementation is unrelated to the failing classification.
scale.2: A concrete change is present but still evaluates overloaded equality/membership or otherwise remains vulnerable to ambiguous truth values.
scale.3: Avoids the immediate exception through broad exception handling or custom result interpretation, but does not precisely implement DEFAULT singleton identity semantics.
scale.4: Uses identity against loaded DEFAULT sentinels at the correct source location and preserves the surrounding classification conditions, with only minor style or scope shortcomings.
scale.5: A minimal, clean identity-based change exactly at the sentinel predicate preserves all surrounding fallback and multi-module behavior with no unrelated modifications.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal and semantically correct sentinel-classification implementation

applies_when: The trajectory presents commands, scripts, or test results intended to demonstrate the bug or validate a candidate fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Supplies trustworthy runtime evidence that the original array-valued patch fails before the correction and that collection succeeds after it, while distinguishing direct helper checks from an end-to-end pytest collection test.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when claimed success conflicts with visible ValueError, import/configuration failure, stale-module execution, or a test that does not execute the final implementation. Cap at 1 if no test or reproduction reaches the relevant predicate.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful repository-backed pytest collection/run after the final visible implementation outranks synthetic helper tests; observed failures outrank claims that tests passed. Tests executed before a later code change do not validate that later change.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating dependency installation, hand-simulated boolean lists, or assertions against a helper not loaded from the edited tree as proof that pytest collection is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 5 requires post-change collection-level evidence using an explicit array new value; anchor 4 requires at least post-change focused execution of the actual helper or equivalent patching object.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible command output for an actual @patch(..., new=np.array([...])) test collected by the repository pytest, plus focused helper-level evidence when full execution is blocked.
metadata.oracle_test: A test module containing @patch(valid_target, new=np.array([-5.5, 3.0])) is collected without the ambiguous-truth ValueError and does not acquire a spurious fixture parameter.

scale.1: No relevant executable evidence reaches the failure or candidate fix.
scale.2: Only a weak/synthetic attempt is shown, or execution is blocked or contradicts the claimed result.
scale.3: The failure is convincingly reproduced and a focused post-change predicate simulation succeeds, but the edited helper or pytest collection is not exercised reliably.
scale.4: Post-change execution of num_mock_patch_args or getfuncargnames with realistic patch objects demonstrates correct array and DEFAULT behavior, without full collection proof.
scale.5: Shows decisive post-change pytest collection/run of the array-patch reproducer succeeding, preferably alongside visible before-fix failure or an equivalent control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive reproduction and collection-level validation

applies_when: The visible trajectory encounters failed experiments, contradictory runtime output, or multiple successive candidate predicates.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses contradictory evidence to reject bool/equality/any/all-based candidates and converges on a final identity-based predicate, without continuing to claim that disproven approaches work.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory retains or submits an equality-based candidate after its own output demonstrates ambiguous truth. Cap at 3 if it reaches identity only at the cutoff without inspecting or exercising the resulting source.
metadata.evidence_authority: Later runtime observations and the final visible source outrank earlier thoughts. An unreconciled failure after the latest edit controls over prior passing output.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding lengthy experimentation when the final code repeats a visibly falsified idea, while recognizing trajectories that productively correct an initially mistaken approach.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit abandonment of disproven equality-based approaches and a final identity-based implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: The sequence between observed ValueErrors, revised reasoning, final source state, and any subsequent validation; explicit recognition that equality with an array remains array-valued.
metadata.oracle_test: After observing that bool(p.new in sentinels), any(p.new == sentinel ...), or similar constructs still raise, the robust recovery is comparison by is against each DEFAULT singleton.

scale.1: Ignores contradictory evidence or ends on a candidate visibly shown to fail.
scale.2: Recognizes some failure but continues using the same overloaded-equality mechanism or makes unsupported success claims.
scale.3: Moves away from the disproven mechanism but ends with broad exception handling, an uninspected last edit, or incomplete reconciliation.
scale.4: Clearly explains why earlier candidates failed and leaves a visible identity-based final implementation, though post-correction validation is limited.
scale.5: Systematically uses failed outputs to refine the causal model, confirms the final identity-based source, and reruns relevant validation with no unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from disproven candidate fixes

applies_when: A concrete source change or complete patch strategy for mock patch-argument detection is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates how safely the visible implementation classifies a patch as consuming an injected mock argument, distinguishing exact DEFAULT identity checks from exception-based containment fallbacks and from unsafe interpretation of equality results.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the latest implementation coerces, reduces, iterates, or otherwise interprets equality results, including bool(p.new in sentinels), any/all over p.new == sentinel, or any/all over elements of an array-valued comparison. Cap at 3 when it still performs equality or containment but catches comparison exceptions and treats them as a non-match. Cap at 3 when identity-safe code is only proposed or its application is not visibly established.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest displayed source or diff outranks edit plans and earlier intermediates. A visibly successful edit command is weaker than a later source display but stronger than prose alone. Test output applies only to the exact implementation visibly in effect when the test ran.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating element-wise reductions as a valid sentinel test while still distinguishing a bounded exception fallback from a reduction that can falsely classify non-sentinel values.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require applied code semantically equivalent to not p.attribute_name and any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels). Merely proposing identity or suppressing comparison exceptions cannot pass this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible predicate used by num_mock_patch_args, including the not-p.attribute_name gate, treatment of every loaded mock module's DEFAULT object, and whether explicit new values can invoke or be classified through overloaded equality.
metadata.oracle_test: A patch with no attribute_name consumes one argument exactly when p.new is identical to DEFAULT from one of the loaded mock implementations. An explicit multi-element array or an object with adversarial __eq__ consumes zero without having equality invoked; each genuine loaded DEFAULT singleton consumes one.

scale.1: No concrete relevant change is visible, or the latest implementation retains the original failing membership predicate without a working guard.
scale.2: The latest implementation still decides sentinel status by coercing or reducing overloaded equality results, or otherwise produces incorrect patch-argument counts.
scale.3: The latest implementation catches equality or containment failures and treats them as non-matches, or identifies identity as the solution without visibly establishing an applied identity-safe predicate.
scale.4: Applied code uses identity against every loaded DEFAULT sentinel and preserves the attribute_name gate and surrounding counting behavior, but focused verification is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The latest applied identity-safe predicate is visibly confirmed with both an explicit array or adversarial-equality value and a genuine DEFAULT patch, with no contradictory later edit or unrelated behavioral change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied DEFAULT classification with graded safety of partial fixes

applies_when: The task concerns chained exception information being lost when a pytest report crosses a serialization boundary.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Determine whether the visible work correctly identifies and addresses loss of the complete explicit or implicit exception chain while serializing and reconstructing pytest failure reports.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible reasoning continues to blame exception-chain discovery or terminal formatting after evidence shows ExceptionChainRepr already contains all exceptions. Cap at 3 for one-way serialization, one-way deserialization, unverified textual replacement, malformed source, or a claimed fix not confirmed in repository content. Modern external-package behavior alone cannot earn implementation credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source inspection, the cutoff repository diff or inspected post-edit source, and focused test output outrank assistant summaries or claims that a script applied a fix. Evidence from the task repository outranks behavior of separately installed modern pytest or xdist versions. A proposed patch is not an applied patch unless its resulting repository content is visibly confirmed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for reproducing ordinary local formatting, modifying the already-correct chain builder, testing an unrelated installed version, or serializing only the newest exception while describing the full round-trip fix without applying it.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible, coherent repository changes covering both encoding and reconstruction of the full chain; score 5 additionally requires a passing repository-relevant round-trip or integration test.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository-local evidence about ExceptionChainRepr and report serialization, especially whether the chain is already present before transport, whether only the outermost reprtraceback/reprcrash is currently encoded, and whether serialization and deserialization preserve every chain element and separator description.
