metadata.oracle_test: A report containing three explicitly chained exceptions and one containing three implicit-context exceptions must survive the repository's report-to-serializable and report-from-serializable path with all traceback representations in order, the correct direct-cause versus during-handling separator text, outermost crash information, and report sections intact.

scale.1: Visible work adopts a task-contradictory cause, damages the relevant source, or implements a representation that cannot preserve the exception report.
scale.2: Exploration or edits remain non-causal, unsupported, or focused on local formatting/chain construction rather than the report transport boundary; no coherent preservation design is established.
scale.3: Correctly and evidentially identifies that the complete chain exists in memory but is flattened during report serialization, and describes the needed two-way preservation; however, no complete confirmed implementation is present.
scale.4: A coherent repository change visibly serializes and reconstructs every chain element with descriptions and existing report data, but focused round-trip or integration validation is absent or inconclusive.
scale.5: Meets score 4 and focused passing tests visibly demonstrate round-trip preservation for both explicit causes and implicit contexts, including ordering and separator semantics, without regressing ordinary exception reports.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves chained exceptions across report serialization round trips

applies_when: The failure appears only after a pytest report crosses the serialization boundary used by xdist.
The local exception representation already contains multiple explicit-cause or implicit-context exceptions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that pytest constructs an ExceptionChainRepr correctly, but report serialization in src/_pytest/reports.py preserves only its outermost reprtraceback and reprcrash and therefore loses the chain during round-trip reconstruction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims repr_excinfo, __cause__/__context__ traversal, or terminal formatting is the root defect after visible evidence shows an ExceptionChainRepr containing the full chain. Cap at 1 if it proposes changing an unrelated installed xdist package instead of the repository.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and local-checkout runtime observations outrank guesses based on the task wording, comments, or behavior of separately installed pytest/xdist versions.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing correct creation or rendering of the chain with the later transport step that discards it.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the loss at the report serialization/deserialization boundary rather than merely discussing exception formatting or xdist generally.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime evidence connecting ExceptionChainRepr.chain to BaseReport._to_json/_from_json and showing that the existing representation already contains all chained exceptions.
metadata.oracle_test: For either three-level example, excinfo.getrepr(chain=True) yields an ExceptionChainRepr whose chain has three elements, while the pre-fix report round trip reconstructs only a ReprExceptionInfo for the newest exception.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or an off-repository/off-component diagnosis contradicted by visible evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes chained exceptions or serialization in general but attributes the defect to the wrong function, package, or chain-construction logic.
scale.3: Locates src/_pytest/reports.py or report round-tripping as suspicious, but does not clearly explain that ExceptionChainRepr.chain is omitted while only the newest reprtraceback/reprcrash survive.
scale.4: Correctly explains the omitted chain and the resulting outermost-only reconstruction, supported by direct source inspection or a focused object-structure observation.
scale.5: Provides decisive local evidence for both sides of the causal boundary: the original representation contains every chain element and the current serialized/deserialized form loses them.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of chained-exception loss

applies_when: Visible work performs or defines a focused check concerning chained exception reports and report serialization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses repository-local structural or executed checks to establish where the exception chain is lost and, after implementation, to demonstrate that explicit-cause and implicit-context chains survive report serialization with their ordering and separator semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign level 1 when a claimed validation is contradicted by its visible output or does not execute meaningfully. Cap at level 2 for modern external-package demonstrations, ordinary Python traceback output, or getrepr-only checks presented as proof of transport behavior. Cap at level 3 for static proposals, one-sided object inspection, pre-fix failure reproduction, or an unexecuted regression test. Cap at level 4 when only one chaining mode is successfully validated or when a targeted relevant failure remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing focused output against the task repository outranks proposed tests, assistant interpretations, or output from separately installed modern packages. A repository-local report round trip outranks standalone rendering. Direct structural assertions on ExceptionChainRepr.chain and its serialized reconstruction outrank visual claims. Failed or aborted commands provide no positive proof beyond any independently visible output produced before failure.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating dependency installation, unrelated current-package behavior, local traceback formatting, failed exploratory scripts, or test proposals as proof that the repository serializer preserves chained exceptions.
metadata.hard_gate: Level 3 requires successful repository-local evidence about at least one side of the causal boundary. Level 4 requires an executed report serialization round trip. Level 5 requires successful post-change round trips for both explicit causes and implicit contexts.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands, scripts, assertions, and output that use the task checkout. Distinguish ordinary ExceptionInfo.getrepr or Python traceback rendering from BaseReport._to_json/_from_json or pytest_report_to_serializable/pytest_report_from_serializable. Check what each successful probe actually establishes and whether both chaining modes are exercised.
metadata.oracle_test: Before the fix, a repository-local three-level ExceptionChainRepr contains every exception but its report round trip returns only the newest representation. After the fix, explicit values 11, 12, and 13 retain two direct-cause descriptions, while implicit values 21, 22, and 23 retain two during-handling descriptions, in order and as an ExceptionChainRepr.

scale.1: No meaningful task-specific validation is present, or the visible check is invalid and its claimed conclusion is contradicted by the output.
scale.2: Validation is limited to ordinary traceback or getrepr rendering, external installed-package behavior, unsuccessful experiments, or an unexecuted general test idea; it does not establish report-transport behavior.
scale.3: A successful repository-local probe establishes that ExceptionChainRepr contains the full chain before transport, precisely reproduces pre-fix loss across the report boundary, or defines a concrete repository-relevant round-trip test, but no successful post-change serialization round trip is shown.
scale.4: A successful repository-local post-change report round trip preserves the full ordered chain and separator descriptions for one chaining mode, or equivalently strong executed coverage is present but the second required mode is absent.
scale.5: Successful repository-local post-change round trips cover both explicit-cause and implicit-context chains and assert all exception elements, order, separator descriptions, reconstructed ExceptionChainRepr type, and relevant report sections.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validates the chained-exception transport boundary with repository-local probes

applies_when: Visible work addresses serialization or reconstruction of ExceptionChainRepr in the task repository.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the visible work defines and implements a symmetric builtin-only wire representation for every exception-chain element and reconstructs the same ordered ExceptionChainRepr without breaking ordinary exception reports.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign level 1 when the visible representation contains live traceback objects in the wire payload, edits the wrong component after the transport boundary is established, or leaves malformed or destructive source. Cap at level 2 when either direction is absent, chain elements remain unconverted, only the newest exception is retained, or reconstruction still unconditionally produces ReprExceptionInfo. Cap at level 3 when complete logic appears only in a proposed patch or write command without authoritative post-edit confirmation. A failed syntax check or targeted round trip caps at level 2 until visibly resolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible repository diff or direct post-edit read-back of the complete relevant functions is authoritative for implementation. A successful write command, replacement-script message, import-only edit, assistant summary, or truncated source excerpt is not proof that the resulting encoder and decoder exist. Directly inspected repository constructors and data shapes are authoritative for design credit. Repository-local execution is authoritative for validation; behavior from separately installed packages is not.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal credit for a precise symmetric schema and a trajectory that merely identifies the omitted chain, mentions changing both directions, adds an import, performs a one-sided replacement, stores live representation objects, or claims success without showing the resulting source.
metadata.hard_gate: Level 3 requires visible field-by-field logic for both encoding and decoding, not merely a statement that both directions should change. Level 4 requires authoritative visibility of the complete resulting repository implementation in both directions and syntactically coherent use of the repository's constructors. Level 5 additionally requires a successful repository-local round trip.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible encoder and decoder logic in the repository report-serialization path. For each chain tuple, verify conversion of ReprTraceback, every nested ReprEntry or ReprEntryNative, ReprFileLocation, and separator description; verify reconstruction in the same order as ExceptionChainRepr, restoration of sections, and preservation of the existing ReprExceptionInfo fallback.
metadata.oracle_test: Create one report with a multi-element ExceptionChainRepr containing distinct traceback-entry variants, crash locations, separator descriptions, and sections. Its serialized form must recursively contain only builtin transport values. Reconstruction must return an ExceptionChainRepr with equivalent ordered elements and sections. A separate ordinary ReprExceptionInfo report must continue to round-trip through the fallback path.

scale.1: The work remains off the report-transport boundary, adopts an incompatible wire shape, visibly damages the source, or provides no usable encoding or reconstruction approach.
scale.2: The correct boundary may be identified and a concrete attempt may exist, but the visible work lacks field-by-field logic for one direction, omits nested entry conversion or other required chain fields, preserves only the outermost exception, or reconstructs the wrong representation type.
scale.3: Visible code or equally precise pseudocode specifies matching field-by-field encoding and decoding for every chain tuple, nested traceback-entry variant, crash location, description, sections, and the non-chain fallback, but the complete resulting repository implementation is not authoritatively visible.
scale.4: A complete post-edit source view or repository diff confirms syntactically coherent builtin-only encoding and matching reconstruction of all chain elements as ExceptionChainRepr, including sections and ordinary-report compatibility, but successful focused execution is absent or inconclusive.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and a successful repository-local report round trip confirms builtin-only transport data, representation type, chain order, traceback-entry variants, crash fields, separator descriptions, sections, and ordinary ReprExceptionInfo compatibility.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements a transport-safe symmetric ExceptionChainRepr wire format

applies_when: The task requires proving that serialized pytest reports retain chained exceptions.
Both explicit __cause__ chains and implicit unsuppressed __context__ chains are part of the reported behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Adds or executes focused regression tests that pass chained failure reports through pytest's serialization hooks or BaseReport round trip and demonstrate preservation and terminal rendering of all exceptions and the correct cause/context separators.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if evidence bypasses report serialization or uses unrelated installed package versions. Cap at 3 if only one chaining mode is covered. Any visible targeted failure caps at 2 until explained and resolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful targeted tests against the modified local source outrank standalone Python traceback output, tests against a separately installed modern pytest/xdist, or unexecuted test proposals.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking ordinary local traceback rendering or current PyPI xdist behavior for proof that the repository's report serializer is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an actual report serialization round trip; merely confirming that Python or excinfo.getrepr prints a chain does not exercise the bug.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests or command output using the repository checkout, preferably in testing/test_reports.py, that exercise pytest_report_to_serializable and pytest_report_from_serializable or the equivalent _to_json/_from_json path.
metadata.oracle_test: The explicit chain retains values 11, 12, and 13 with two 'direct cause' separators; the implicit chain retains 21, 22, and 23 with two 'During handling' separators after serialization and reconstruction.

scale.1: No task-specific test evidence or proposal.
scale.2: Runs only ordinary exception/getrepr rendering, unrelated package-version experiments, or tests that do not cross the serialization boundary.
scale.3: Defines or runs one meaningful report-round-trip case, or proposes both required cases precisely without successful execution.
scale.4: Runs successful round-trip coverage for both explicit-cause and implicit-context chains and checks that all exception values and separator semantics survive.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive regression tests for explicit and implicit chains

applies_when: The task requires changing pytest's bpaste submission behavior in the repository
The visible repository contains the paste creation code that supplies a lexer parameter
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work applies the task-causal lexer correction and makes that correction available as a valid, minimal unified diff.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if visible source or diff retains a Python-family lexer, changes the wrong request field, or introduces task-relevant behavior beyond the required correction. Dependency failures, unavailable network services, unsuccessful live bpaste probes, and scratch files absent from the submitted diff are not contradictions.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible unified diff or direct post-edit source observation outranks plans, summaries, and claims. The latest visible source state wins over earlier observations. A terminal unified diff establishes deliverability; an earlier correct git diff establishes applied work but does not substitute for a missing or malformed terminal patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating a correct proposal, an applied but undelivered edit, and a valid submitted patch as equivalent; also prevents irrelevant environment or live-service failures from obscuring a source-level fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require cutoff-visible evidence that the repository source was actually changed to send lexer=text. Score 5 additionally requires a syntactically consumable unified diff exposing that change.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source diff and the cutoff submission artifact. The intended change sets the bpaste request's lexer value to literal text while preserving the request's contents, expiry, endpoint, encoding, and response handling.
metadata.oracle_test: For create_new_paste(contents), the encoded POST parameters should contain code=contents, lexer=text, and expiry=1week, with the existing bpaste endpoint and response parsing otherwise preserved.

scale.1: No task-relevant applied change is visible, or the visible change clearly preserves or worsens the incorrect lexer behavior.
scale.2: The text-lexer correction is identified or proposed, but no visible source edit or diff establishes that it was applied.
scale.3: Some applied task-relevant work is visible, but the final source semantics are incomplete or ambiguous, or a visible contradiction prevents confirming the required request parameters.
scale.4: The latest visible source state or git diff correctly and minimally applies lexer=text with surrounding request behavior preserved, but the cutoff artifact is absent, malformed, or not a consumable unified diff.
scale.5: The correct minimal lexer=text implementation is visibly applied and exposed at cutoff as a valid unified diff, with no contradictory task-relevant changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied pastebin lexer fix with deliverable patch

applies_when: Visible source, diff, or patch evidence concerns src/_pytest/pastebin.py or the request assembled by create_new_paste.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the bpaste request assembled by create_new_paste so its lexer value is exactly text for every supported Python version while preserving the paste contents, expiry, endpoint, encoding, and response handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A final artifact that retains or restores the python/python3 lexer caps credit at 1. Absence of a final patch when only an earlier workspace diff proves the edit caps credit at 4. Changes to code, expiry, URL, request encoding, or response parsing without task-specific justification cap credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final unified diff is strongest; otherwise a later direct git diff or file read outranks narration. A valid final patch outranks generic trajectory summaries that report no changed files, while a later explicit revert outranks an earlier edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for an unexecuted proposal, a Python-3-only adjustment, an endpoint rewrite, or broad unrelated modifications.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require direct visible evidence that the repository content or submitted patch contains the change; a proposed command or prose description alone is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: A visible applied edit or unified diff at the params dictionary in src/_pytest/pastebin.py, with lexer set to the literal text and no unnecessary behavioral changes.
metadata.oracle_test: The relevant payload dictionary is semantically equivalent to {'code': contents, 'lexer': 'text', 'expiry': '1week'}, still POSTed as ASCII-encoded urlencode data to https://bpaste.net.

scale.1: No visible relevant edit, or the authoritative artifact still submits a Python lexer or introduces a clearly incorrect request.
scale.2: Only proposes the correct edit, or makes an ambiguous/wrong-boundary change without direct evidence of the resulting source.
scale.3: Visible implementation moves toward lexer=text but is conditional, incomplete, or accompanied by unjustified changes to other request or response behavior.
scale.4: A direct file read or git diff proves the exact minimal source edit and preserved surrounding behavior, but the final deliverable is absent or does not itself expose the patch; alternatively, a final patch is correct but contains minor unrelated changes.
scale.5: The authoritative final unified diff cleanly replaces only the version-dependent python/python3 lexer expression with the literal text in create_new_paste, preserving all other request and response behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements the minimal request-payload correction

applies_when: The repository contains or the trajectory discusses tests for create_new_paste, mocked urlopen calls, or encoded bpaste request data.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Updates or adds a deterministic regression test proving that create_new_paste sends lexer=text while retaining the expected URL, code contents, and expiry fields.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the visible repository test still expects python or python3 after the source is changed to text, credit is capped at 3. Unreconciled focused test failure caps credit at 2. Live-service success or failure alone cannot earn above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing repository test that exercises create_new_paste with mocked network I/O outranks syntax checks, source-text searches, custom scripts that merely restate the implementation, and live bpaste.net requests affected by network or service drift.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating py_compile, grep-based self-checks, synthetic old-versus-new printouts, or unstable network probes as proof of the request's runtime semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a visible applied test change or a credible focused execution of an already-correct assertion; anchor 5 requires both the applied regression assertion and credible passing execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes to the focused pastebin test and credible execution output, especially inspection of the mocked urlopen URL and URL-encoded request body.
metadata.oracle_test: A mocked call to create_new_paste(b'full-paste-contents') reaches https://bpaste.net with decoded form data containing lexer=text, code=full-paste-contents, and expiry=1week, and the mocked response remains parsed as expected.

scale.1: Visible evidence shows a relevant deterministic regression failure that is left unresolved, or testing asserts the old Python lexer as correct.
scale.2: No applied focused regression assertion is visible; evidence is limited to no test, syntax checking, source searching, synthetic scripts, or live-network probing.
scale.3: The stale Python-lexer assertion is concretely identified or a precise mocked-request test update is described, but no applied test diff is visible.
scale.4: A focused test is visibly updated to require lexer=text and preserve the other request fields, but no credible passing run is shown; alternatively, a credible focused pass is shown without visible evidence of the necessary test change.
scale.5: A visible focused regression test asserts lexer=text plus the preserved URL, code, and expiry behavior, and credible execution shows that test passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protects the encoded-request behavior with a focused regression test

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the pytest 5.1.2 regression in conftest discovery or import on Windows.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the concrete path transformation that lowercases the conftest/package path and explains how that transformed path reaches package-aware conftest import.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the regression primarily to unrelated importlib, assertion rewriting, `findpaths.py`, or a literal `.lower()` call after visible source identifies `normcase` in `unique_path`.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current source and focused version-history diffs outrank speculation based only on the issue wording; Windows `normcase` semantics outrank observations from running it on Linux.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking Linux's no-op `normcase` behavior, or a nearby historical refactor, for evidence that the Windows-specific transformation is harmless or unrelated.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the active `unique_path` implementation and at least one conftest-loading call site.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible repository evidence connecting `_pytest.pathlib.unique_path`, `os.path.normcase`, its Windows lowercasing behavior, and calls from conftest discovery/import in `_pytest/config/__init__.py`.
metadata.oracle_test: On Windows, `normcase(str(path.realpath()))` changes mixed-case components such as `Python/PIsys` to lowercase before the resulting `py.path.local` is used for conftest package discovery/import.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by visible source evidence.
scale.2: Recognizes a generic Windows casing/import problem but does not locate the active transformation and conftest call chain.
scale.3: Locates `unique_path` or `normcase` and correctly notes Windows lowercasing, but only partially connects it to conftest package import.
scale.4: Connects `unique_path` calls in conftest handling to `normcase` lowercasing and the resulting package import failure, supported by current source or focused history.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain with source-backed version context: the 5.1.2 path-identity change applies `normcase` to a real path, the lowercase path is then used by package-aware conftest import, and this explains the reported missing mixed-case parent package.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of Windows conftest casing regression

applies_when: The trajectory considers compatibility with the existing mixed-casing fix, symlink handling, conftest caching, or path-type contracts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves real-path and conftest-cache semantics while correcting lowercase import paths, and reconciles the new failure with the earlier wrong-cased-working-directory behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory removes all `unique_path` use, restores the full pre-5.1.2 conftest implementation without compatibility evidence, or changes path-type behavior after encountering evidence that the helper is intended only for `py.path.local`. Cap at 3 if it notices the conflict but leaves it unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: Existing repository tests and current call-site contracts outrank assumptions that reverting to the complete 5.1.1 implementation is automatically safe.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating removal of every prior casing fix as equivalent to removing only the harmful lowercase transformation, or expanding the helper to `pathlib` types without evidence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit preservation or testing of real-path resolution and existing wrong-cased-directory/conftest behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning or tests covering `realpath`, `_dirpath2confmods`, `_conftestpath2mod`, the existing `test_conftest_badcase`, symlink deduplication comments, and the helper's `py.path.local` scope.
metadata.oracle_test: The corrected implementation both avoids lowercasing paths used for package import and retains physical-path resolution needed to avoid duplicate conftest loading through aliases or symlinks; existing bad-casing behavior must not be casually discarded.

scale.1: Ignores compatibility entirely or knowingly breaks established conftest/path behavior.
scale.2: Mentions compatibility but makes a broad revert or unsupported path-type change that conflicts with visible contracts.
scale.3: Recognizes the tension between case preservation and path identity but provides no decisive implementation or test evidence resolving it.
scale.4: Keeps real-path resolution and the existing helper/call-site structure, with reasoned or partial evidence that prior conftest behavior remains intact.
scale.5: Demonstrates that the narrow fix preserves real-path, cache/deduplication, and existing wrong-cased-working-directory behavior through focused tests or equally decisive repository evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of prior path-identity and conftest behavior

applies_when: The task concerns pytest conftest loading or package imports affected by Windows path casing
The visible trajectory contains repository investigation, a proposed repair, an applied edit, or validation related to path canonicalization
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge how far the visible trajectory has progressed toward a narrow, technically coherent repair that preserves import-usable path casing while retaining required real-path identity behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if a visible check exposes a syntax error, incompatible path-type assumption, loss of required canonical identity, or other defect in the current edit and the defect remains unresolved. Cap at 3 for a broad rollback or expanded path abstraction change when the visible evidence supports a narrower repair. Failed installation caused only by missing or incompatible environment dependencies is not evidence against the patch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository source, command output, applied patch content, and test or static-check results outrank assistant claims. Explicit edit commands and subsequent file contents outrank summary fields when they conflict. Historical commits and changelog entries support localization but do not prove that a proposed repair was applied or correct.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding repeated diagnosis as completed work, accepting normcase removal solely because it sounds plausible, treating irrelevant Linux-only casing checks as Windows validation, or overlooking a visibly broken or unnecessarily broad applied patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible task-causal repository edit. Score 4 additionally requires a successful relevant check of the edited code. Score 5 requires behavioral regression coverage or equivalent direct evidence for mixed-case Windows conftest loading while preserving real-path or symlink identity.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the trajectory localizes the regression to the conftest path canonicalization flow, understands the distinct effects of realpath and normcase on Windows, applies a narrow compatible edit, and obtains relevant validation. Distinguish commands that changed repository files from prose describing intended changes.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended semantics are to avoid feeding case-folded path spellings into Python package or conftest import resolution while still resolving physical path identity as required; a representative behavioral check loads conftest.py from mixed-case Windows directory components without duplicate loading through alternate spellings or symlinked paths.
metadata.stage: early diagnosis through implementation and validation

scale.1: No coherent task-causal localization, or the current applied edit is visibly broken, unrelated, or contradicts the required import and path-identity semantics.
scale.2: The trajectory identifies some or all of the likely casing mechanism and may describe a plausible repair, but no task-causal repository edit is visibly applied; alternatively, an applied edit has an unresolved visible contradiction.
scale.3: A task-causal edit is visibly applied and plausibly addresses case-folding, but it is unvalidated, unnecessarily broad, or leaves compatibility and path-identity behavior materially uncertain.
scale.4: A narrow, coherent edit is visibly applied and at least one successful relevant check supports its syntax or behavior, with no unresolved contradictory evidence.
scale.5: A narrow repair is visibly applied and direct regression evidence demonstrates mixed-case conftest import success while also checking preservation of canonical real-path or duplicate-loading behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-causal, evidence-backed repair of conftest path casing

applies_when: A concrete source change is present or precisely proposed for the Windows path-casing defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the `py.path.local` canonicalization helper narrowly so real-path resolution remains but path spelling is not forced through Windows case normalization.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the change broadly reverts conftest handling, removes real-path resolution, edits unrelated import machinery, or introduces invalid/unsupported dispatch such as calling `resolve()` on `PurePath`; cap at 3 if `normcase` remains active or the edit is only described but not visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: A displayed diff or post-edit file content outranks a verbal claim; the helper's documented `py.path.local` contract outranks speculative support for unrelated path classes.
metadata.failure_mode: Overengineering the fix with `Path`/`PurePath` branches or reverting the entire prior conftest change when the defective behavior is localized to case normalization.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires concrete evidence that the active return expression no longer wraps the resolved path string in `normcase`.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or edit to `src/_pytest/pathlib.py`, especially the return expression of `unique_path` and cleanup of the now-unused `normcase` import.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended narrow transformation is equivalent to constructing the same path type from `str(path.realpath())` without applying `normcase`, with the unused `normcase` import removed.

scale.1: No relevant implementation direction, or a destructive/unrelated change.
scale.2: Suggests altering conftest or path handling but leaves the implementation boundary vague or introduces clear type/semantic defects.
scale.3: Precisely proposes the narrow `unique_path` change, or shows a partial edit, but lacks a complete clean visible patch.
scale.4: Shows a clean minimal edit that removes the `normcase` call while retaining `realpath`, with no unrelated source changes.
scale.5: Shows the complete minimal implementation: `unique_path` preserves the resolved path's spelling, the unused `normcase` import is removed, and the diff remains confined to the necessary helper boundary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal case-preserving implementation boundary

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, or runs a regression test for the reported default-discovery failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a minimal test that proves default pytest discovery does not import an unrelated package initializer while still collecting and running an ordinary test.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the scenario explicitly selects the hostile __init__.py, places the passing test inside a package whose import naturally requires that initializer, or only demonstrates an unrelated Python-version/assertion-rewrite failure.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository test visible in the current diff plus its focused passing output is strongest; a faithful external reproduction is next; commands that fail before collection because of installation or interpreter incompatibility are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents weak tests that avoid the import only because nothing is collected, the package is ignored manually, or the tested layout differs causally from the report.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both the hostile nested __init__.py and a separately collectable test, with an asserted successful result rather than merely absence of one output line.
metadata.judge_focus: A pytester/testdir-style repository test, or equivalent controlled runtime reproduction, containing a nested package whose __init__.py raises or asserts, a separate normally named passing test, default python_files configuration, and assertions on successful collection/outcomes.
metadata.oracle_test: With foobar/__init__.py containing assert False and test_foo.py containing a passing test at the root, default pytest should report the normal test as passed and no collection error for foobar/__init__.py.

scale.1: No task-relevant reproduction or regression-test design is present.
scale.2: Creates a partial or confounded scenario without a reliable expected outcome.
scale.3: Faithfully reproduces the hostile nested initializer and ordinary test, but does not add/assert a durable regression test or obtain decisive output.
scale.4: Adds or precisely designs a repository-style regression test with explicit successful outcome assertions.
scale.5: Shows the focused regression test in the current diff and decisive passing output under the modified source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-matching regression test for an unrelated package

applies_when: The trajectory encounters failed installations, incompatible interpreter behavior, unsuccessful fixes, or evidence that conflicts with its current hypothesis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Separates environment failures from semantic collection evidence, revises disproven hypotheses, and restores or replaces incorrect edits before drawing conclusions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory declares success after the task reproducer still reports foobar/__init__.py, treats setup/Python incompatibility as proof of collection semantics, or leaves a visibly malformed or speculative edit while claiming it is correct.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output and the final repository state outrank stated confidence; a failed post-change reproducer falsifies the claimed fix unless a distinct environment cause is demonstrated.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding confident but falsified diagnoses, accidental source corruption, and misleading tests run against a different installed pytest than the edited checkout.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one visible correction or explicit qualification when contradictory evidence occurs; absent contradiction, it requires a clean distinction between inspected facts and untested hypotheses.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible handling of metadata-generation failures, missing dependencies, Python-version AST errors, failed reproductions, transient malformed edits, and test output that shows an attempted fix did not address the import.
metadata.oracle_test: Only an execution that reaches pytest collection in a suitable environment can confirm the regression or fix; installation failures and Python 3.10 incompatibilities in pytest 5.2.x do not establish init-file behavior.

scale.1: Contradictory output is ignored and unsupported success claims or damaged edits remain.
scale.2: Notices some environment or test problems but continues relying on invalid evidence or a falsified fix.
scale.3: Distinguishes major setup failures from semantic evidence, but recovery is incomplete or conclusions remain weakly supported.
scale.4: Explicitly retracts or revises disproven claims, restores bad edits, and uses source/runtime evidence consistently.
scale.5: Demonstrates a clean evidence chain with environment identity established, contradictions resolved, final repository state checked, and conclusions limited to what was actually observed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence discipline and recovery from contradictory results

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change intended to stop unrelated package initializers from being imported during discovery.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Restricts package object mounting to the semantic case that needs collection from the package initializer, without disabling package recognition, ordinary test discovery, or explicit/custom __init__.py collection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible proposal removes __init__.py from pytest_collect_file globally, suppresses all package initializer imports, deletes the init-module collection block, or adds sibling-path heuristics that would break legitimate package collection.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible git diff and surrounding source context outrank prose claims or transient edits later reverted; a focused guard around mounting outranks broad exclusions elsewhere.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents an overbroad fix that makes the reproducer pass by silently removing supported collection of tests from __init__.py or breaking package traversal.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the change boundary to target eager mounting in Package.collect and preserve the existing conditional path that collects tests from __init__.py when configured.
metadata.judge_focus: A current diff or precise patch plan in src/_pytest/python.py that guards or relocates Package.collect's self._mount_obj_if_needed() using the configured python_files match for the package initializer, while leaving package traversal and _collectfile behavior intact.
metadata.oracle_test: Package discovery may still create Package nodes, but their __init__.py must be mounted during collection only when that initializer matches python_files and is itself eligible to provide tests; normal package setup/import behavior for actual package tests remains available.

scale.1: No implementation boundary is identified, or the proposed edit is unrelated to the import trigger.
scale.2: Suggests a broad exclusion or destructive edit that can suppress supported package or __init__.py behavior.
scale.3: Proposes guarding eager import but leaves the condition vague, misplaced, or insufficiently tied to python_files semantics.
scale.4: Specifies the correct focused guard or relocation around Package.collect object mounting and explicitly preserves existing package traversal and init-module collection.
scale.5: Shows a clean current diff implementing that focused boundary with surrounding context demonstrating no unrelated collection logic was altered.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise fix boundary for package object mounting

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an ordinary nested package __init__.py is imported during recursive collection in this pytest version.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the collection node and exact eager-import transition responsible for importing a non-test package's __init__.py, while distinguishing that regression from intentional package discovery.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory concludes that Module._ALLOW_MARKERS, the mere existence of the __init__.py pattern, or the conditional yield of an init Module is itself the demonstrated cause despite visible evidence that Package.collect imports before that conditional yield.
metadata.evidence_authority: A task-matching runtime trace or direct inspection of the executed Package.collect and import path outranks commit-message speculation; current source outranks recollection of older pytest behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents confusing intentional recognition of __init__.py as a package boundary with the newly introduced eager import that makes unrelated packages fail collection.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires identifying the unconditional object mounting/import in Package.collect, not merely noting that __init__.py appears in collection patterns.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing or source reasoning that connects pytest_collect_file creating a Package for __init__.py to Package.collect unconditionally calling self._mount_obj_if_needed(), which invokes _getobj/_importtestmodule before any matching test file requires the package.
metadata.oracle_test: For a root containing a passing test and foobar/__init__.py with assert False, default discovery must not execute foobar/__init__.py merely because the package directory was traversed; the regression is explained by eager mounting of every discovered Package node.

scale.1: No causal localization, or an explanation contradicted by the visible collection code.
scale.2: Recognizes that package/__init__.py collection is involved but attributes the failure only to broad pattern matching, marker flags, or generic recursion.
scale.3: Narrows the regression to Package collection or the 5.2.3 package-marker change, but does not establish the exact eager import path.
scale.4: Correctly identifies unconditional self._mount_obj_if_needed() in Package.collect as the likely trigger and explains that it imports the package initializer too early.
scale.5: Provides source or runtime-backed end-to-end causality: generic discovery creates a Package for __init__.py, Package.collect eagerly mounts/imports it, and this happens even when no matching test in that package requires import.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of eager package initialization

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why an unrelated package initializer executes during recursive pytest collection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies whether the initializer executes because Package collection unconditionally mounts the package object and thereby imports its module, while distinguishing this execution step from package discovery and intentional collection of tests from an initializer.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the final operative explanation makes marker flags, replacement of an initializer-specific collector, filename matching, or generic recursion the cause of execution. Cap at 3 when eager mounting is identified but remains coequal with one of those competing causes or when the trajectory proposes suppressing initializer collection wholesale. Earlier exploratory claims do not count as contradictions only if they are explicitly retracted or corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: A focused runtime trace or reversible experiment against the inspected checkout is strongest. Direct inspection or comparison of the relevant Package.collect, object acquisition, and import code is sufficient for a source-backed diagnosis. Faithful reproduction confirms the symptom but not its cause. Commit messages and filename-pattern observations are supporting context only.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents symbol spotting, marker-history narratives, and confusion between creation of a Package node and execution of its initializer from being treated as a resolved diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit source-backed statement that unconditional object mounting in Package.collect executes the unrelated initializer before initializer-test eligibility is established. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible focused validation of that transition.
metadata.judge_focus: Evaluate the final evidence-supported causal account visible at the cutoff: Package recognition, entry into Package.collect, the unconditional object-mount operation, its use of object acquisition or module import, and the separate conditional path for collecting tests from an initializer.
metadata.oracle_test: Recognizing a nested directory as a package may remain valid. The regression-causing transition is Package.collect unconditionally obtaining its object, which imports the package initializer before default discovery has found a test-driven reason to do so; explicitly selected or configured initializer tests remain supported.

scale.1: No relevant causal account is present, or the account is incompatible with the displayed collection code.
scale.2: The operative explanation attributes execution to filename matching, marker handling, initializer-collector replacement, or generic recursion without identifying eager Package object mounting as the import trigger.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies unconditional mounting in Package.collect and plausibly connects it to import, but the chain is incomplete, intentional initializer collection is conflated with the regression, or a competing trigger explanation remains active.
scale.4: The final source-backed account clearly explains that Package.collect eagerly mounts the object and imports the unrelated initializer, and distinguishes that operation from package recognition and configured or explicit initializer test collection.
scale.5: Level 4 is satisfied and a focused trace, executed-source comparison, or reversible experiment visibly confirms that changing the eager-mount transition changes initializer execution without broadly disabling supported package behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization of eager Package import

applies_when: The task concerns corruption of pytest report or discovery names caused by post-processing the path assembled in getmodpath
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the latest visible implementation makes getmodpath return the assembled dotted path unchanged, rather than corrupting it or eliminating its return value.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest visible source or patch deletes the return statement, places it outside getmodpath, returns an undefined value, or otherwise makes the method implicitly return None. Cap at 2 if no applied source state is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct repository evidence from file inspection or git diff wins over earlier edits, stated intentions, terminal narration, synthetic string demonstrations, and attempted commands. A final emitted patch is authoritative when no later repository observation contradicts it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding deletion of the entire offending line as equivalent to replacing the corrupting return expression with a valid unchanged return.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a visibly applied source change that preserves an explicit return of the assembled path; proposing the change or demonstrating string replacement behavior alone is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of getmodpath after parts are reversed and joined. Confirm that the resulting string is returned unchanged and that the method still has an executable return before reportinfo begins.
metadata.non_evidence: Diagnosis, repository browsing, dependency installation, toy calls to str.replace, intended future edits, and claims that the issue is fixed do not establish implementation correctness without visible applied source evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For a collected name whose assembled path is test_boo[..[], getmodpath must return exactly test_boo[..[]; ordinary assembled paths must likewise remain unchanged.

scale.1: The latest visible implementation removes or invalidates getmodpath's return, returns an undefined value, or otherwise causes implicit None or malformed execution.
scale.2: The cause or desired fix is discussed or demonstrated, but no applicable source change is visibly applied.
scale.3: An applicable source change is visible, but whether getmodpath returns the assembled path unchanged is incomplete or genuinely ambiguous.
scale.4: The implementation visibly returns the assembled path unchanged, but broader edits or conflicting repository evidence leave surrounding method integrity uncertain.
scale.5: The latest visible implementation cleanly and unambiguously returns the assembled path unchanged, with the method boundary and surrounding control flow intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied getmodpath return-value preservation

applies_when: The visible trajectory creates, proposes, inspects, or runs tests for the reported regression.
Evidence is available concerning whether setUp or tearDown executes for a skipped unittest test under --pdb.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides repository-relevant evidence that a unittest test skipped at method or class level remains skipped under --pdb and that neither setUp nor tearDown executes, using an observable side effect or deliberately failing lifecycle methods rather than only checking skip metadata.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the command visibly ran a different pytest installation, omitted --pdb, never collected the test, or ended in an unrelated collection/configuration error, it is not passing regression evidence and caps credit at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: A passing repository test against the modified checkout outranks synthetic attribute checks, plain unittest runs, or executions of a separately installed newer pytest. Actual command output outranks statements that a test would pass.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a plain unittest run, a modern released pytest run, a hand-simulated boolean check, or an environment failure as proof that the repository fix works.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require an end-to-end --pdb path and an assertion or failure sentinel proving tearDown was not called; checking __unittest_skip__ alone cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests in the pytest test suite or faithful subprocess executions that exercise pytest's local code with --pdb and make an erroneous tearDown invocation unambiguously fail.
metadata.oracle_test: A reproduction with failing setUp and tearDown must report exactly the intended skip and no lifecycle error under --pdb; equivalent call-recording evidence is acceptable.

scale.1: No relevant test design or runtime evidence is visible.
scale.2: Only generic skip experiments, plain unittest behavior, or attribute inspection is shown, without exercising the failing pytest --pdb path.
scale.3: A relevant end-to-end regression test is clearly designed or added, but it is not run successfully against the local checkout, or available execution is blocked by an unrelated environment problem.
scale.4: A focused repository-level test visibly exercises --pdb and proves the skipped test's tearDown is not called, but execution evidence is incomplete or only one important skip form is covered.
scale.5: The focused regression test is visibly present and passes against the local checkout, reporting the intended skip without setup/teardown errors; method-level behavior is covered and class-level or equivalent skip coverage is also demonstrated where appropriate.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive regression test for skipped unittest lifecycle with --pdb

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, proposes, or applies a correction for skipped unittest lifecycle behavior under debugger-enabled pytest execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible trajectory has converged on the owning control flow and leaves a coherent, non-destructive correction state: skipped TestCase methods or classes do not acquire deferred tearDown work, while tests that execute retain debugger-before-teardown behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for a latest visible malformed or destructive source state, including duplicate methods, undefined item/report variables, broad teardown suppression, or exception-list mutation used to infer skipping. Cap at 2 for an unresolved late workaround in teardown or generic runner code, or when the latest visible source no longer contains the claimed fix. Cap at 3 when claimed validation used another pytest installation, omitted --pdb, or failed before exercising the test.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible repository diff or complete edited excerpt outranks earlier prose. A relevant local test execution outranks simulated predicates and runs against separately installed pytest versions. When no edit exists, a source-grounded implementation-ready correction outranks broad assurances. Later corrections override earlier mistakes only when the contradiction is explicitly resolved.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating extended browsing, modern-version reproduction, hand-evaluated skip booleans, or a verbally plausible fix as equivalent to a coherent cutoff-visible correction, while overlooking later malformed or reverted source.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires the complete deferred-teardown/early-skip causal chain plus either an exact narrow correction or a concrete regression-test design. Score 5 requires a coherent applied current change and task-relevant local validation; proposed or removed work cannot receive 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Compare the latest visible source state, diff, and explicit conclusions with earlier investigation. Distinguish inspected facts from guesses, proposed code from code actually present, synthetic checks from repository execution, and a coherent current edit from an edit later removed or corrupted.
metadata.oracle_test: At the scheduling point in TestCaseFunction.runtest, unittest method-level and class-level skip metadata prevents saving/replacing tearDown; a non-skipped failing TestCase under --pdb still defers tearDown until after debugger interaction and performs cleanup once.

scale.1: The latest visible state is unrelated, materially destructive, syntactically or structurally incoherent, or based on a mechanism contradicted by inspected source.
scale.2: Relevant code is found, but the trajectory remains committed to a wrong ownership theory, an unsafe late workaround, or a claimed change that is absent from the latest visible source.
scale.3: The unittest adapter and deferred-teardown interaction are partially established without a complete safe correction, or a plausible correction is only sketched without proving method/class skip semantics and preservation of executed-test teardown.
scale.4: The complete causal boundary is established and the trajectory supplies either an exact narrow correction or a concrete repository regression-test design; any applied edit is coherent, but local task-relevant validation is absent or blocked.
scale.5: A narrow skip-aware correction is visibly present in the current source and task-relevant local evidence exercises the --pdb path, while visible reasoning or tests preserve deferred exactly-once teardown for tests that actually execute.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-visible safe progress on the skipped-unittest debugger regression

applies_when: The proposed fix changes the --pdb-specific unittest tearDown deferral logic.
The visible trajectory discusses or tests lifecycle behavior for non-skipped unittest failures or cleanup functions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Preserves the reason for the existing deferred-teardown mechanism: a non-skipped unittest failure under --pdb still reaches post-mortem debugging before tearDown destroys instance state, and the legitimate tearDown/cleanup executes exactly once afterward.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removing the usepdb deferral branch, preventing tearDown for all tests, invoking tearDown before debugger interaction, or allowing duplicate cleanup caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Existing repository tests and passing focused regression commands outrank broad assurances. The current deferred-teardown design and its associated cleanup regression history outrank proposals to remove it wholesale.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the reported skip by disabling the cleanup mechanism whose purpose is to preserve debuggable state and later execute legitimate cleanup.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit evidence that non-skipped --pdb behavior remains deferred and cleanup is not lost or duplicated.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source reasoning or tests covering non-skipped failing unittest methods, debugger timing, tearDown invocation count, and unittest cleanup behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: For a non-skipped failing TestCase under --pdb, debugger interaction occurs with pre-teardown state available, then tearDown and registered cleanups run once; skipped tests remain the exceptional no-teardown case.

scale.1: No consideration of non-skipped behavior, with a proposed change that visibly risks or breaks it.
scale.2: Mentions avoiding regressions but provides no precise lifecycle argument, or proposes broad teardown suppression/removal.
scale.3: Explains that non-skipped tests must retain deferred teardown and cleanup, but supplies no focused source or test evidence.
scale.4: The visible change is narrowly skip-gated and a relevant existing or proposed test clearly protects deferred, exactly-once teardown for non-skipped failures.
scale.5: The narrow implementation is accompanied by passing local evidence for both sides of the boundary: skipped tests perform no tearDown, while non-skipped --pdb failures preserve debugger-before-teardown ordering and execute teardown/cleanup exactly once.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Protection of non-skipped --pdb cleanup behavior

applies_when: The task concerns unittest.TestCase skip behavior specifically when pytest's --pdb option is active.
The visible trajectory contains source inspection, history inspection, or reasoning about the unittest execution path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies the task-specific control-flow defect: the --pdb branch in TestCaseFunction.runtest saves the original tearDown and replaces it with a no-op, while TestCaseFunction.teardown later invokes the saved method even when unittest recognized the test as skipped before setUp, the test body, and tearDown should run.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A diagnosis centered on changing the generic runtest protocol, suppressing all pytest teardown phases, or treating unittest.SkipTest capture in runner.py as the primary defect caps this rubric at 2 unless visibly corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and relevant git diffs/history take precedence over assumptions based on an installed modern pytest or generic runner behavior. Direct inspection of unittest.TestCase.run semantics outranks speculative fixture or runner explanations.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking ordinary pytest teardown phases, xunit fixtures, debugger exception filtering, or environment installation failures for the instance-specific cause.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require connecting the skip decision to creation and later invocation of _explicit_tearDown, not merely observing that teardown runs.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning tied to TestCaseFunction.runtest, _explicit_tearDown, TestCaseFunction.teardown, and unittest's early skip semantics.
metadata.oracle_test: For a method decorated with unittest.skip, unittest returns through its skip path without setUp or tearDown; pytest's --pdb-specific deferred-teardown mechanism must preserve that lifecycle.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the explanation is incompatible with the visible source flow.
scale.2: Recognizes a skip/teardown interaction but attributes it mainly to generic runner, fixture, or debugger exception handling without locating the deferred unittest tearDown path.
scale.3: Locates the --pdb handling in _pytest/unittest.py and notes that tearDown is postponed, but does not clearly explain why a method-level unittest skip leaves an invalid deferred call pending.
scale.4: Correctly explains that --pdb saves and suppresses tearDown during unittest execution and that pytest later calls the saved method even though unittest took its early skip path.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and supports it with precise current-source or relevant history evidence, including the distinction between normal unittest lifecycle behavior and pytest's deferred tearDown mechanism.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of deferred unittest tearDown under --pdb

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes unittest.TestCase skip behavior associated with debugger-enabled execution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory establishes the task-specific execution mechanism and reaches a technically coherent, non-destructive correction or actionable diagnosis using visible repository evidence.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory applies or endorses a change that relies on unavailable or already-consumed outcome state, references undefined objects, corrupts or duplicates methods, changes a generic runner path without evidence that it owns this behavior, or would suppress tearDown for ordinary executed or failing tests. Cap at 3 when claimed implementation or validation is contradicted by the latest visible diff, status, or test output.
metadata.evidence_authority: A relevant executed regression test or inspected final diff has highest authority, followed by direct inspection of the unittest adapter's setup, runtest, result-callback, and teardown paths; repository history is supporting evidence. Generic reasoning, behavior from an unrelated installed pytest version, mock scripts that do not execute the repository code, and unsupported claims have lower authority. Later visible source inspection or test output overrides earlier speculation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad code browsing, modern-version reproduction, or a plausible skip check as equivalent to proving the specific deferred-teardown regression; it also prevents giving high credit to an exact diagnosis followed by an unsafe lifecycle-state patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a source-grounded account of the pdb-only deferred explicit tearDown path and the unittest skip short-circuit, with no unresolved contradiction from visible code or tests. Score 5 additionally requires either a coherent applied change with task-relevant validation or an equally concrete, implementation-ready correction and regression-test design.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, history comparisons, reproduction output, edits, diffs, and tests for evidence that debugger mode defers the TestCase tearDown call and that unittest-decorated skips must retain unittest's rule that neither setUp nor tearDown runs. Distinguish code actually written or commands actually run from merely suggested work.
metadata.oracle_test: For a unittest.TestCase method decorated with unittest.skip and executed with --pdb, pytest must report the skip without invoking setUp or tearDown; ordinary executed tests must retain tearDown, including the debugger-related delayed-cleanup behavior for failures.

scale.1: The trajectory remains in an unrelated subsystem, asserts a materially wrong mechanism, or applies/proposes a visibly incoherent or destructive change that violates unittest lifecycle behavior.
scale.2: The trajectory finds relevant files or symptoms but gives a speculative, mixed, or contradicted explanation; any proposed remedy lacks a valid ownership or lifecycle basis.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies the unittest adapter and relevant skip or deferred-teardown code, but the causal chain, correction, or validation remains materially incomplete; no severe unsafe change is present.
scale.4: The trajectory correctly explains the pdb-specific deferred explicit tearDown interaction with unittest's skip short-circuit and presents a coherent correction or regression-test approach, but implementation or task-specific validation is incomplete.
scale.5: The trajectory gives a complete source-grounded causal account and either applies a coherent narrowly scoped correction with task-relevant validation or supplies an implementation-ready correction and regression test that preserve tearDown for tests that actually execute.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal correctness and safe solution readiness for skipped unittest teardown

applies_when: Visible experiments or existing tests reveal that an initially considered fix changes False, True, or None from matcher identifiers into constants, aliases, or errors.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes contradictory semantic evidence, abandons or repairs the flawed approach, and converges on the pytest DSL contract rather than defending a merely non-crashing result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory observes that False no longer matches the string 'False' yet continues to call the fix correct; cap at 3 if it recognizes the issue but has not produced a coherent corrected design.
metadata.evidence_authority: Existing test expectations and observed evaluate results take precedence over earlier assumptions and compile-only successes.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing recovery with repeated patch churn, or treating non-crashing compilation as decisive after semantic tests fail.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit correction after the contradiction and a revised approach that preserves matcher identity.
metadata.judge_focus: Chronological visible reasoning after failed matcher assertions or discovery of existing valid-identifier tests, followed by corrected source/design and new evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: Discovery that test_valid_idents includes 'True' and 'False', or that evaluate(lambda name: name == 'False') returns False, invalidates constant-conversion and rejection approaches.

scale.1: No relevant contradiction is encountered or acknowledged despite visible failing evidence.
scale.2: Contradictory matcher/test evidence is visible but dismissed, misread, or followed by the same semantically wrong approach.
scale.3: The semantic conflict is correctly recognized and the prior approach is rejected, but no complete corrected implementation or design is visible.
scale.4: The trajectory revises the approach to preserve matcher identifiers and supplies coherent source-level or runtime support for the correction.
scale.5: The trajectory promptly uses the contradiction to derive the exact DSL invariant, implements a compatible encoding/decoding solution, and rechecks both no-crash and matcher-semantic behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from semantic contradiction

applies_when: The trajectory investigates the Python 3.8+ failure from compiling pytest mark expressions containing False, True, or None.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that the custom mark-expression parser emits an ast.Name whose identifier is exactly False, True, or None, and that compiling this malformed AST—not the empty-expression NameConstant—is the crash boundary.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the reproducer primarily to the empty-expression ast.NameConstant(False) branch; cap at 3 if it later corrects that diagnosis.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source inspection and direct AST/compiler output override unsupported explanations about ast.NameConstant deprecation or ordinary Python parsing.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the spelling False for a boolean literal in pytest's DSL, or blaming NameConstant merely because modern ASTs display Constant nodes.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the problematic ast.Name construction on the identifier path.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of Scanner, not_expr, expression, and Expression.compile; AST dumps or direct compile reproductions that connect an IDENT token to ast.Name('False', Load()).
metadata.oracle_test: The failing path is Scanner('False') -> IDENT('False') -> ast.Name(id='False') -> compile(..., mode='eval'); an empty input follows a different branch.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or diagnosis is wholly unrelated to the custom mark-expression parser.
scale.2: Recognizes an AST/compiler problem but blames the empty-expression NameConstant branch or another incorrect primary cause.
scale.3: Connects False to identifier parsing and an invalid compiled name, but does not precisely locate the ast.Name construction or explain the Python 3.8+ boundary.
scale.4: Correctly identifies the IDENT-to-ast.Name path and the compiler restriction on False, True, and None, with supporting source or AST evidence.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain from lexer through not_expr and compile, distinguishes it from ordinary ast.parse and the empty-expression branch, and supports it with direct repository-specific evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of reserved-name AST crash

applies_when: The trajectory runs or adds checks intended to demonstrate that the interpreter-crash fix works.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides tests or runtime evidence that simultaneously establish non-crashing compilation and preserved matcher behavior for reserved identifiers, including their use inside boolean expressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when visible output shows that a matcher for 'False' is not called or returns the wrong result; cap at 3 when only compilation is demonstrated or test execution is blocked.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful repository tests and direct Expression.compile/evaluate executions outrank standalone ast.Constant experiments; failing repository assertions outrank earlier success claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Calling a constant-valued evaluation a passing regression test even though existing test_valid_idents expects True and False to be matched as strings.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one semantic assertion where the matcher recognizes the original reserved spelling, not only a no-crash compile check.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible additions to testing/test_mark_expression.py and outputs from those tests or direct imports of the repository module; checks should observe matcher inputs/results, not merely compile synthetic constants.
metadata.oracle_test: Explicitly exercise False, True, and preferably None as matcher identifiers; include a case such as 'False or other' or 'not False', and retain empty-expression behavior.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or visible tests fail before exercising the changed behavior.
scale.2: Only synthetic AST experiments are shown, or visible semantic results contradict pytest's identifier contract.
scale.3: The reproducer compiles without crashing, but matcher identity and composed-expression behavior are untested or blocked.
scale.4: Repository-specific checks demonstrate no crash and correct original-name matching for the reproducer, with some coverage of related names or composition.
scale.5: Focused regression tests visibly cover exact matcher semantics for all affected spellings, boolean composition, and unchanged empty/ordinary identifier behavior, with successful repository test output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive repository-specific regression evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix reaches pytest's mark-expression lexer, parser, evaluator, or Expression.compile path for the reserved-name compiler crash.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the applied repository state prevents match-expression spellings such as "False", "True", and "None" from becoming compiler-forbidden ast.Name nodes, while preserving their role as identifiers resolved by the supplied matcher.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest visible patch is syntactically malformed or internally inconsistent. Cap at 2 when the work only proposes a fix, edits the empty-expression ast.NameConstant case, or rejects the reported spelling. Cap at 3 when compilation is made safe by treating the spelling as a literal, renaming it without a correct reverse mapping, using an unsupported AST API unconditionally, or otherwise changing matcher lookup semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source state or submitted diff outranks earlier edits and narrative claims. A direct check using the actual Expression.compile and evaluate path outranks isolated ast experiments. Existing repository tests establishing these spellings as valid identifiers outrank assumptions that they are Python literals.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking DSL identifiers for Python boolean or None literals, rewarding ad hoc AST snippets instead of the actual evaluator path, accepting rejection as a fix, or crediting commands and plans that never produce a coherent applied implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a syntactically coherent, applied change on the identifier-to-AST compilation path. Credit above 3 additionally requires an applied reversible representation that sends the original exact spelling to MatcherAdapter and remains compatible with the repository's supported Python versions.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible implementation where IDENT tokens become AST nodes and where compiled names are resolved during evaluation; also inspect targeted tests or direct compile-and-evaluate checks.
metadata.oracle_test: Expression.compile("False") must not abort or raise solely because of the spelling, and Expression.compile("False").evaluate(lambda name: name == "False") must return True; analogous handling should preserve "True" and other accepted identifiers without changing boolean-expression composition.

scale.1: The latest visible state is malformed, contradictory, or still constructs a compiler-forbidden name without a coherent mitigation.
scale.2: The crash is diagnosed but no task-path fix is applied, the change targets an unrelated AST case, or the implementation avoids the crash by rejecting the affected spelling.
scale.3: A coherent applied change prevents the forbidden ast.Name compilation for the reported spelling, but it changes identifier semantics, lacks a correct reverse mapping, or violates supported-version compatibility.
scale.4: A coherent applied reversible encoding or equivalent solution prevents the crash, preserves exact matcher lookup semantics and ordinary expression behavior, and is compatible with supported Python versions, but targeted repository regression coverage is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and includes focused regression tests through Expression.compile and evaluate for the affected spellings as matcher-resolved identifiers, plus representative composed expressions, with relevant visible tests passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compile-safe handling of reserved-spelling match identifiers

applies_when: The trajectory implements or validates a change for compiling mark-expression identifiers spelled False, True, or None.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Produces a coherent compiler-safe representation for False, True, and None while preserving their treatment as matcher-controlled identifier strings, including recovery of the exact original spelling during evaluation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the visible source is syntactically malformed, targets only the empty-expression branch, or lacks a coherent applied identifier-path change. Cap at 2 for rejecting a reserved spelling or renaming it without any restoration mechanism. Cap at 3 for a coherent literal conversion or other crash-safe implementation that bypasses matcher lookup; reduce to 2 when direct repository-specific evaluation visibly proves the matcher semantics are wrong and the defect remains unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible coherent source change and repository-specific Expression.compile(...).evaluate(...) evidence outrank standalone AST experiments and claimed success. Direct evaluation showing the matcher receives the wrong key or is bypassed overrides successful compilation. Existing valid-identifier tests establish that these spellings are identifiers rather than Python literals.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating compilation success as semantic success; conflating DSL identifiers with Python constants; rejecting valid identifiers; using safe internal names without decoding them before matcher lookup; or repairing the unrelated empty-expression constant.
