metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires an applied representation that both avoids ast.Name with an exact reserved spelling and demonstrably restores that spelling for matcher lookup. A score of 5 requires focused regression coverage for all three spellings plus unchanged empty and ordinary identifier behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied parser, AST, compilation, and matcher-evaluation changes visible at the cutoff. Distinguish malformed edits, rejection, irreversible renaming, literal conversion, and reversible internal-name encoding. Check whether MatcherAdapter ultimately receives the exact source spelling.
metadata.oracle_test: For each spelling, compilation must not emit ast.Name with that exact identifier, while evaluation with a matcher that returns true only for the original spelling must return true and must receive that spelling. Empty input must remain false, and an unrelated identifier must still be resolved through the matcher unchanged.

scale.1: No coherent applied fix on the reserved-identifier path: the edit is malformed, addresses only empty input, remains contradictory, or cannot plausibly compile.
scale.2: The change coherently avoids the crash by rejecting the spellings or by renaming them without restoring the original matcher key, so identifier behavior is plainly lost.
scale.3: The applied change is compiler-safe and internally coherent, but converts the spellings to constants or otherwise bypasses matcher-controlled lookup; alternatively, a matcher-preserving strategy is proposed but not coherently applied and validated.
scale.4: The applied change uses a reversible compiler-safe representation and repository-specific evidence shows evaluation reaches the matcher with the exact original spelling.
scale.5: The reversible fix is applied and covered by focused tests for False, True, and None, with successful checks that empty input and ordinary identifiers retain their prior behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Crash-safe preservation of reserved mark identifiers

applies_when: The trajectory encounters installation, import, dependency, assertion-rewrite, or version conflicts while attempting reproduction or validation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Responds to contradictory or unusable runtime evidence by identifying which pytest code is actually running, avoiding contamination of installed packages, and returning to authoritative source-level or repository-native evidence without overstating validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Overwriting site-packages with an incompatible local module, continuing to cite external-version output as validation, or claiming success after a failed/import-broken run caps credit at 2 unless the contamination is visibly restored and the claim corrected.
metadata.evidence_authority: Import paths and versions printed by the executing process plus repository diff/status outrank assumptions; failures caused by incompatible Python or dependencies are evidence only of the environment failure, not of product behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating environment setup success, external-version behavior, syntax validity, or textual branch presence with semantic validation of the patch.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require explicit recognition that output from a pip-installed newer pytest does not validate this checkout and no unsupported claim that the local fix passed.
metadata.judge_focus: Version/path checks, use of PYTHONPATH or repository tooling, handling of failed installs, restoration after experimental overwrites, and accuracy of claims about what was actually tested.
metadata.oracle_test: The relevant execution imports pytest/_pytest from the checkout corresponding to the edited src/_pytest/skipping.py; otherwise the trajectory must label the run non-authoritative.

scale.1: Ignores contradictory evidence, leaves the environment corrupted, or makes false test-success claims.
scale.2: Notices some setup failures but repeatedly relies on unrelated installed versions or unsafe package overwrites without establishing authoritative evidence.
scale.3: Correctly labels the environment limitation and avoids a false pass claim, but recovery is inefficient or the provenance of remaining evidence is incomplete.
scale.4: Clearly distinguishes checkout behavior from external pytest behavior, restores or avoids contamination, and bases conclusions on authoritative visible source evidence when execution is blocked.
scale.5: Does everything in anchor 4 and obtains clean, provenance-explicit runtime evidence from the checked-out implementation or a repository-supported test environment.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence recovery and environment discipline

applies_when: A visible patch or concrete edit targets src/_pytest/skipping.py
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Makes marked-skip location normalization independent of the --runxfail xfail guard while retaining the guard's protection against xfail-specific report conversion and preserving existing unittest and xfail semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed syntax, duplicated or corrupted branch bodies, an unchanged runxfail-before-marked-skip elif chain, or moving the runxfail guard after xfail transformations without another effective guard caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The resulting source or git diff overrides prose summaries and structural-check scripts; a syntactically valid, semantically equivalent formulation is acceptable.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a visually small but ineffective edit, or accepting a task-specific fix that regresses the meaning of --runxfail for marked or dynamic xfail cases.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a visible source edit in pytest_runtest_makereport where a marked skip can reach the item.reportinfo() rewrite with runxfail true without exposing ordinary xfail reports to xfail conversion.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible final diff and resulting branch structure in pytest_runtest_makereport, especially the marked-skip condition and the runxfail guard.
metadata.oracle_test: The canonical minimal boundary is to make the final marked-skip rewrite an independent `if` rather than an `elif`; an equivalent ordering is valid only if marked skips are rewritten before the runxfail guard and xfail-specific branches remain guarded.

scale.1: No relevant source change, or the visible edit is syntactically broken or unrelated.
scale.2: A relevant edit exists but remains ineffective, duplicates fragile logic, or allows runxfail cases to undergo xfail report transformations.
scale.3: A plausible fix is described or partially implemented, but the visible branch structure does not establish both marked-skip correction and preserved xfail guarding.
scale.4: The visible implementation correctly separates marked-skip location rewriting from the runxfail bypass and is syntactically coherent, with no evident semantic regression.
scale.5: A minimal, coherent implementation establishes the required independence while preserving unittest handling, dynamic/marked xfail behavior, reason text, tuple shape, and one-based item line conversion.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically safe makereport implementation

applies_when: The task concerns marked-skip location reporting being bypassed by --runxfail in pytest_runtest_makereport.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible reasoning and repository state correctly separate marked-skip location normalization from xfail-specific report handling: a skipped report produced by a skip or active skipif mark must still reach the item.reportinfo-based longrepr rewrite when runxfail is enabled, while xfail-specific report transformations remain suppressed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Changing the runxfail `elif` to an independent `if` while leaving the marked-skip rewrite in its attached `elif` chain is ineffective and cannot exceed 2. Removing the runxfail guard so that xfail-specific branches execute under runxfail, or moving the guard to another position that still precedes marked-skip normalization, cannot exceed 3. Unresolved malformed source cannot exceed 2. A failed synthetic check caps the score at 4 when direct source still proves the required branch reachability, but caps it at 2 when it exposes malformed or ineffective control flow.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly displayed source contents and git diffs from the working checkout are authoritative for applied state. A command showing the edited file may establish an edit even if an automated trajectory summary says no files changed. A patch printed in prose, a heredoc not shown writing the target file, textual simulations, and tests against another installed pytest version establish only reasoning, not checkout behavior. Reliable execution against the modified checkout is strongest validation.
metadata.failure_mode: Avoid rewarding a correct diagnosis as if it were an applied fix, treating an external pytest run as validation of the checkout, accepting an `elif`-to-`if` edit whose attached chain remains blocked, or accepting broad guard deletion that repairs skip reporting by re-enabling forbidden xfail processing.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires cutoff-visible source whose branch ordering or predicate visibly permits marked-skip normalization under runxfail while retaining xfail non-interference. Behavioral execution is not mandatory when the resulting control flow is directly inspectable, but unresolved syntax errors or a displayed failing task-specific check preclude score 5.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the displayed pytest_runtest_makereport branch structure. Determine whether marked skipped reports can reach the item-based location rewrite under runxfail and whether the runxfail guard still prevents xfail-specific mutations. Give partial credit for an exact, implementation-ready control-flow repair even when it has not yet been applied.
metadata.oracle_test: With a test skipped by a skip mark or an active skipif mark, `-rs --runxfail` reports the test item's file and definition line rather than the internal skip-raising location. Under the same option, xfail-specific exception and stored-xfail report transformations remain bypassed.

scale.1: The visible work does not identify the runxfail branch as preempting marked-skip location normalization, or it relies on a contradicted account of skip and xfail report flow.
scale.2: The relevant branch and symptom are identified, but no concrete viable restructuring is given, or the visible edit is malformed or ineffective, such as changing the guard to `if` while the location rewrite remains in its attached `elif` chain.
scale.3: The causal diagnosis is correct and a concrete repair direction is given, or an applied edit lets marked skips reach normalization but also exposes xfail-specific report transformations under runxfail or otherwise leaves a material control-flow defect.
scale.4: The visible source or implementation-ready patch has a syntactically coherent ordering or predicate that lets marked skips reach item-based normalization while retaining the runxfail barrier for non-skip xfail handling, but application state or task-specific validation remains uncertain or conflicting.
scale.5: The modified checkout visibly contains the correct control flow: marked-skip normalization precedes or bypasses the runxfail xfail guard, xfail-specific transformations remain suppressed, and no cutoff-visible syntax or behavioral evidence contradicts the repair.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal correctness of marked-skip report handling under --runxfail

applies_when: The task concerns marked skip or skipif location reporting being altered by the --runxfail option
The visible trajectory investigates or changes pytest_runtest_makereport or directly related skip/xfail report logic
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly changes report-hook control flow so a skip caused by a skip or skipif mark still has its tuple long representation rewritten to the item's reportinfo location when --runxfail is enabled, without unnecessarily applying that rewrite to non-mark skips or breaking the hook's xfail and unittest report handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible control flow still lets a true --runxfail branch consume the same if/elif chain before the marked-skip rewrite, if the edit is malformed, or if the claimed fix is contradicted by the displayed code. Cap at 3 when the runxfail guard is simply deleted or xfail handling is broadly bypassed without visible reasoning or structure showing preserved non-skip behavior.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible repository state or terminal unified diff outranks earlier edits and assistant claims; local-checkout test output outranks simulations and prose. Tests run only against a separately installed PyPI pytest do not validate the checkout. Scratch scripts, textual patch plans, and self-authored logic demonstrations are supporting evidence only. If a generated summary conflicts with an explicit later git diff or file inspection, use the explicit repository observation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for changing an outer elif to if while leaving the marked-skip rewrite in the runxfail-controlled chain, moving the runxfail guard to another position that still precedes the rewrite, validating only a newer installed pytest, or treating an intended edit as applied work.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a syntactically coherent repair visibly applied to the checkout or supplied as the terminal patch. A proposal, diagnosis, or scratch-file experiment without an applied source change cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository diff, current source excerpt, or terminal patch for the ordering and reachability of the marked-skip longrepr rewrite relative to the --runxfail no-interference branch. Check that the marked-skip predicate, rep.skipped requirement, tuple-longrepr requirement, reason preservation, and item.reportinfo location update remain coherent.
metadata.oracle_test: For a report produced by a skip or skipif mark with --runxfail enabled, rep.skipped true, and tuple rep.longrepr, execution must reach the rewrite that preserves the reason and substitutes str(item.reportinfo()[0]) and reportinfo line plus one. A non-mark runtime skip must not be reattributed as a marked skip, and --runxfail must continue to suppress xfail-specific report interference. A canonical structure evaluates the marked-skip rewrite before the runxfail no-interference guard; an equivalent selective guard is also valid.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis or repair is visible; work remains exploratory, unrelated, or asserts behavior contradicted by inspected code.
scale.2: The hook and general branch interaction are noticed, but the applied edit is ineffective or malformed—for example, --runxfail still intercepts the chain before marked-skip rewriting—or the proposed change lacks a coherent causal account.
scale.3: The exact reachability bug is correctly diagnosed and a concrete valid direction is stated but not applied, or a broad applied change makes the rewrite reachable while leaving material uncertainty about preserving xfail/non-mark behavior.
scale.4: A coherent applied repair makes marked-skip location rewriting reachable with --runxfail and retains the relevant predicates and location transformation, but preservation of adjacent xfail/unittest behavior or task-specific verification is only partially demonstrated.
scale.5: The visible applied patch cleanly orders or guards the branches so marked-skip rewriting occurs under --runxfail while xfail, unittest, and non-mark skip behavior remain appropriately isolated; direct code inspection and, when available, checkout-relevant validation support the full causal claim.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly decouples marked-skip location rewriting from --runxfail handling

applies_when: The trajectory discusses, creates, or runs tests for dynamic xfail behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses pytest's own pytester/testdir infrastructure or an equivalent real invocation to prove that an xfail marker added through request.node.add_marker inside the test body converts the subsequent failure into an expected failure.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the test adds the marker during fixture/setup, uses pytest.xfail imperatively, or only checks that add_marker stores a Mark. Cap at 3 if claimed success actually ran a separately installed pytest rather than the modified checkout.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful output from a focused repository test is strongest, followed by an applied test diff with precise assertions, then a concrete unexecuted test proposal. Import/build failures and mock-only marker-list checks are not semantic pass evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating existing fixture-setup dynamic-xfail coverage, a static decorator, a mock-node storage test, or an environment error as proof of the reported in-body behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the marker addition to occur inside the test call body and the assertion to check xfailed/report behavior, not merely own_markers contents or fixture-setup behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: A visible test containing add_marker before a deliberate failing assertion, plus assertions on the resulting xfailed count/status and preferably the xfail reason; commands must exercise the repository code rather than an unrelated installed pytest.
metadata.oracle_test: A generated test executes request.node.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(reason='xfail')); assert 0, and the outer run reports one xfailed test with no ordinary failure.

scale.1: No relevant test work, or only unrelated test commands.
scale.2: Creates a loose reproduction or marker-storage check but does not assert expected-failure report semantics for an in-body marker.
scale.3: Provides the exact semantic regression case and expected outcome, but it is only proposed, cannot be shown to run against the checkout, or lacks a durable suite assertion.
scale.4: Adds a focused repository regression test with the correct in-body timing and precise xfailed/no-failure assertions; execution is absent or blocked for a clearly evidenced environment reason.
scale.5: The focused regression test is visibly applied and passes against the modified checkout, with trustworthy output showing the dynamic failure is reported as xfailed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds a decisive regression test for an in-body dynamic xfail

applies_when: The visible trajectory proposes, applies, revises, or reverts a source change intended to restore xfail markers added inside the test body
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the observable implementation progress toward reevaluating current xfail markers after the test body and supplying that result to pytest's existing call-report classification logic.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A refresh occurring only before yield, a marker-storage-only change, or a later explicit reversion cannot score above 2. If a post-call edit command succeeds but the operative statements are truncated or their connection to classification is not visible, assign 3 rather than treating it as either proposal-only or complete integration. If exact source shows a fresh value is computed but not consumed by classification, cap at 3. Claims of success contradicted by later source or focused execution receive no added credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later exact source view or diff outranks edit claims and plans. A successful targeted edit command followed by immediate source output that locates the change after yield is evidence of provisional application even when truncation hides an operative statement, but it is weaker than an exact diff and cannot establish full integration. An explicit checkout, restore, or later source view showing the original code supersedes earlier edits. A generic clean-workspace summary does not override a later exact diff or source view. Environment and assertion-rewriter failures do not validate or refute local xfail semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents tying proposal-only work with visibly applied post-call edits, over-crediting pre-yield refreshes, treating truncated output as an exact implementation, or ignoring an explicit reversion.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require observable evidence that a source edit was applied at a point after the test body. Scores above 3 require exact visible operative code or a diff showing evaluate_xfail_marks running post-call and the resulting Xfail value entering the established report-classification path. Score 5 additionally requires focused semantic validation or comparably decisive structural validation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible edit commands, immediate source inspections, and diffs around the hookwrapper yield and pytest_runtest_makereport. Determine separately whether work is merely proposed, provisionally shown at a post-call location, or exactly shown to call evaluate_xfail_marks and feed the resulting value into the existing failure, raises, strict-XPASS, and wasxfail branches.
metadata.oracle_test: A call that adds pytest.mark.xfail to request.node inside its body and then fails must have its current markers evaluated after the body; that Xfail must cause the call report to become skipped with wasxfail set. Existing behavior for static and conditional xfail, raises, strict XPASS, imperative pytest.xfail, run=False, and --runxfail must remain on the established classification path.

scale.1: No concrete post-call implementation direction is visible; work remains unrelated exploration or stops at identifying xfail code without specifying how fresh state reaches report classification.
scale.2: A correct post-call or report-time remedy is concretely proposed, but no surviving applied post-call edit is observable; this also includes relevant work whose only edit is pre-yield, storage-only, or explicitly reverted.
scale.3: A targeted post-call edit is provisionally observable through a successful edit command and nearby post-yield source context, or exact code shows only part of the refresh-to-classification path; truncation or missing operative integration prevents confirmation.
scale.4: Exact visible source or diff shows current xfail markers being evaluated after the test body and the resulting value being consumed by the existing call-report failure and XPASS classification branches, but focused semantic validation is absent.
scale.5: The exact post-call integration is narrow and complete, preserves the established option and classification behavior, and is corroborated by focused semantic execution or comparably decisive syntax and source-level validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies post-call xfail refresh with observable integration evidence

applies_when: The task concerns an xfail marker added dynamically during test execution
The visible prefix investigates or changes xfail evaluation, caching, or report classification
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible work correctly identifies and, when applied, repairs the lifecycle mismatch by making an xfail marker added inside the test body available to classification of that call, without replacing this with ineffective pre-call reevaluation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the only applied remedy reevaluates before yield or otherwise before the test body adds the marker, because it cannot observe the reported runtime addition. Cap at 3 if the correct post-call remedy is only proposed. Claims of success contradicted by inspected code or a focused local failure receive no extra credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct tool output showing source contents, a diff, or focused test behavior outranks assistant claims. Repository history and existing source establish lifecycle ordering when execution is blocked by environment incompatibility. Installation failures and tests run against a different installed package are not semantic validation of the local change.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad marker investigation, repeated setup-time evaluation, or speculative cache invalidation as though it solved a marker that does not exist until the test body is already running.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require command-confirmed applied source work that reevaluates or refreshes xfail after the test body can add the marker and before the call report is finally classified. A plan or diagnosis without such applied evidence cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect command-confirmed changes and source reasoning around pytest_runtest_setup, the pre- and post-yield portions of pytest_runtest_call, pytest_runtest_makereport, evaluate_xfail_marks, and the cached xfail value. Distinguish edits actually shown in file contents or diffs from proposed edits.
metadata.oracle_test: A test that calls request.node.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(reason=...)) inside its body and then fails must be classified as xfailed; static xfail, conditional and raises handling, strict XPASS behavior, imperative pytest.xfail, run=False, and --runxfail semantics must remain coherent.

scale.1: No relevant causal progress, or the work asserts an unrelated marker-storage cause despite visible lifecycle evidence.
scale.2: Relevant investigation is present, but there is no correct post-call mechanism; this includes an applied change confined to pre-yield evaluation or an incomplete diagnosis that does not locate report-time reevaluation.
scale.3: The lifecycle regression is precisely diagnosed and a concrete post-call or report-time remedy is described, but no such remedy is command-confirmed as applied.
scale.4: A command-confirmed change places reevaluation after the test body and feeds the resulting xfail state into call-report classification, but focused regression validation is absent or a bounded compatibility concern remains.
scale.5: A command-confirmed post-call fix is accompanied by focused semantic validation or comparably strong source-level proof and explicitly preserves the surrounding static, strict, raises, imperative, run=False, and --runxfail behaviors.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Dynamic xfail is reevaluated at the effective lifecycle point

applies_when: The proposed change re-evaluates xfail state after test execution and therefore can affect ordinary xfail, XPASS, strict, raises, or --runxfail behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accounts for compatibility of post-call re-evaluation with static xfail behavior, successful dynamically marked tests, strict mode, raises filtering, explicit pytest.xfail, and the --runxfail bypass.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the approach unconditionally rewrites failures as xfailed under --runxfail, ignores xfail.raises mismatches, or turns successful dynamic marks into ordinary passes regardless of strictness. Cap at 3 when compatibility is merely asserted without tracing or tests.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed targeted tests and existing source branch analysis outrank generic assurances. Existing makereport semantics may supply evidence when a minimal patch demonstrably reuses them unchanged.
metadata.failure_mode: Fixing the single reported assertion failure by ad hoc outcome rewriting while silently breaking XPASS, strict xfail, raises constraints, explicit xfail, or --runxfail.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit treatment of at least --runxfail and the distinction between an expected failing call and XPASS/strict or raises behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, source control flow, or tests showing that the refreshed Xfail object continues through existing makereport branches and that --runxfail prevents marker-based interference.
metadata.oracle_test: Without --runxfail, a matching failing call becomes XFAIL, a passing marked call follows XPASS and xfail_strict rules, and raises only accepts configured exception types; with --runxfail, marker-based report rewriting is bypassed.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or visible behavior broadly contradicts the established xfail contract.
scale.2: Mentions regression risk but implements or proposes ad hoc failure-to-skip conversion that bypasses important xfail options.
scale.3: Reuses some existing xfail report logic and mentions compatibility, but does not establish --runxfail plus XPASS/strict or raises behavior.
scale.4: Clearly preserves existing report branches and explains or tests --runxfail together with at least one of XPASS/strict and raises semantics.
scale.5: Provides strong visible evidence—targeted tests or a minimal well-traced implementation—that static and dynamic XFAIL, XPASS/strict, raises filtering, explicit xfail, and --runxfail behavior remain coherent.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves the broader xfail reporting contract

applies_when: The trajectory contains analysis of why an xfail marker added from inside the test body is absent from the resulting call report.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes that the marker is successfully added to the item's marker collection, but pytest caches/evaluates xfail before the test body and report generation subsequently consumes that stale result.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims add_marker or iter_markers fails to store or expose the marker despite visible source showing own_markers is updated. Cap at 3 if it claims a second evaluation before yield can observe a marker added inside the test body.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts and repository history showing the hook ordering or removal of post-call xfail evaluation override unsupported speculation. A demonstrated reproduction is supportive but not required for the causal conclusion.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a correct marker-storage implementation for the bug, or proposing another pre-test evaluation that cannot observe an in-test mutation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly locating the missed observation after the test body has run, rather than merely saying marker caching is involved.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tracing of request.node.add_marker through Node.own_markers and item.iter_markers, together with the ordering of pytest_runtest_setup, the pre-yield portion of pytest_runtest_call, the test body, and pytest_runtest_makereport.
metadata.oracle_test: The test body calls request.node.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(reason='xfail')) and then fails; setup and pre-yield call evaluation occur before add_marker, while report-time evaluation can see the new marker.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the visible source and lifecycle ordering.
scale.2: Recognizes an xfail timing or caching problem but does not distinguish marker storage from xfail-result caching, or places the needed observation before the test body.
scale.3: Correctly explains that setup/pre-call evaluation is stale after an in-test add_marker call, but does not trace how the stale value reaches report conversion.
scale.4: Accurately traces add_marker, iter_markers, the cached xfailed value, and report handling, identifying post-call re-evaluation as the missing behavior.
scale.5: Provides the level-4 causal account and corroborates it with decisive repository history or source comparison showing that post-yield/post-call xfail evaluation was removed during the regression-causing refactor.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies stale pre-call xfail evaluation as the regression

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change intended to restore dynamic xfail markers added during execution of the test body.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Changes the xfail handling path so that report classification can evaluate the item's current xfail markers after the call has completed, while preserving pytest's existing report transformation logic.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 for an implementation that only re-evaluates before yield, alters add_marker without addressing report-time state, or leaves makereport consuming the stale cached value. Cap at 3 if the new value is computed post-call but not used by the report conversion branches.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible diff and source context outrank prose claims. A syntactically valid, narrowly scoped post-call edit outranks broad rewrites or edits confined to Node.add_marker or the pre-yield part of pytest_runtest_call.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding an apparently plausible cache refresh that still executes before the dynamic marker exists, or an overbroad rewrite that bypasses established xfail report semantics.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires evaluation after the test body and before or during call-report xfail classification; pre-call-only refreshes cannot receive higher credit.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible edits or concrete proposed edits in src/_pytest/skipping.py, especially pytest_runtest_makereport after outcome/report retrieval or equivalent post-yield logic, and whether the resulting Xfail value reaches the existing failure/XPASS classification branches.
metadata.oracle_test: For a call failure after request.node.add_marker(xfail), evaluate_xfail_marks(item) at report time returns an Xfail whose reason is used to change the call report to skipped and set wasxfail.

scale.1: No implementation direction, or a change unrelated to xfail lifecycle and report generation.
scale.2: Targets relevant xfail code but refreshes only before test execution, modifies the wrong subsystem, or otherwise cannot observe an in-body marker.
scale.3: Proposes or partially applies post-call re-evaluation, but the integration with the existing makereport result path is incomplete, ambiguous, or unnecessarily invasive.
scale.4: Shows a focused post-call change that supplies freshly evaluated xfail state to the existing report-classification logic and is syntactically coherent.
scale.5: Shows a minimal, repository-consistent applied diff at the post-call report boundary, with correct option gating/state handling and no duplicated or dead xfail classification logic.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Places the fix at the post-call report boundary

applies_when: The task concerns newline translation in pytest's text file-descriptor capture path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible repository state preserves lone carriage returns when text FD capture is read, without making the active capture construction unusable or concretely breaking its decoding and helper contracts.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the latest applied source cannot support ordinary text FD capture because of invalid syntax, rejection of an existing constructor argument such as write_through, or destruction of an existing name or mode property. Score at most 2 if an applied workaround preserves CR by concretely bypassing errors="replace" or removing another behavior used by the active path. A broader helper override is not a concrete contradiction merely because it could affect hypothetical callers; absent a visible failing caller or lost property, treat that as residual risk under score 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct source excerpt or diff has highest authority; a later correction or revert supersedes an earlier edit. A generated workspace summary does not erase a source edit shown by later tool output. Direct execution of the modified FDCapture or EncodedFile path corroborates behavior, but isolated TextIOWrapper experiments establish only the mechanism. Successful execution cannot excuse a separate structural defect visible in the final source.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents execution evidence from hiding a malformed final class, prevents incomplete validation from downgrading an otherwise exact and inspectable call-site fix, and avoids treating every broader implementation risk as equivalent to a concrete runtime or decoding regression.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a syntactically valid applied source change that affects the text FD-capture read path. Score 5 requires a narrow configuration at the existing EncodedFile construction boundary and preservation of all existing arguments and helper properties.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible definition and construction of EncodedFile and the FDCapture text snapshot path. Check whether newline translation is disabled, whether the existing encoding, errors="replace", and write_through behavior still reach the active wrapper, and whether the name and mode properties remain properties. Distinguish a concrete defect in the active source from an unobserved risk of a broader implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: The active text FD-capture wrapper must read bytes ending in lone '\r' as text ending in '\r', not '\n'. Configuring the existing EncodedFile construction with newline="" is the narrow reference behavior; CRLF and LF must remain intact, invalid UTF-8 must continue to use replacement decoding, and write-through plus the helper's name and mode properties must remain available.

scale.1: No supported causal remedy is established and no usable fix exists, or the latest applied edit definitely makes ordinary text FD capture or an existing helper property unusable.
scale.2: An applied change can preserve carriage returns, but the latest source concretely removes required active-path behavior such as replacement decoding or another existing capture semantic.
scale.3: The universal-newline cause and a viable remedy are supported by visible evidence, but no valid repository source change affecting the text FD-capture path is applied.
scale.4: A valid applied alternative preserves carriage returns on the active path without a concrete break, but it is broader, redundant, or carries a specific unverified compatibility risk compared with configuring the existing construction directly.
scale.5: The latest source narrowly disables newline translation at the existing text FD-capture wrapper construction, retains encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", write_through=True and helper properties, and contains no visible contradiction; focused execution may corroborate but is not required to distinguish this anchor.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operationally safe preservation of carriage returns in text FD capture

applies_when: The cutoff contains test work intended to prevent recurrence of carriage-return normalization.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory adds a focused test in the repository test suite that writes output ending in a carriage return through the capfd path and asserts that readouterr returns the carriage return exactly rather than a newline.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the test asserts normalized newline output, only checks that bytes contain a carriage return, uses a modern external pytest rather than the checkout, or never exercises FDCapture text reading, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: An applied repository test exercising the public fixture outranks ad hoc TextIOWrapper experiments, comments, proposed tests, or tests that merely inspect raw bytes.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating low-level demonstrations of Python newline behavior as a durable pytest regression test.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an applied repository test that would fail on the original implementation and pass with newline="".
metadata.judge_focus: Visible changes under testing/, with preference for a test using capfd and exact string equality or an equivalent end-to-end fixture invocation; temporary standalone scripts are supporting evidence only.
metadata.oracle_test: A regression test equivalent to print("Greetings from DOS", end="\r"); out, err = capfd.readouterr(); assert out == "Greetings from DOS\r" must distinguish the faulty and corrected implementations.

scale.1: No relevant test work, or the asserted expectation encodes the faulty newline conversion.
scale.2: Only a temporary script, prose test idea, or low-level TextIOWrapper experiment is visible.
scale.3: A repository test is added but is indirect, incomplete, or does not clearly fail on the original FDCapture text path.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test directly exercises FDCapture or capfd and asserts preservation of a lone carriage return.
scale.5: A concise public capfd regression test is applied in the appropriate capture test module, checks exact returned output, and clearly distinguishes carriage return from line feed without relying on platform display formatting.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds a repository regression test through the public capfd behavior

applies_when: The cutoff contains diagnosis of the carriage-return change in capfd output.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory traces capfd through FDCapture and identifies that reading the EncodedFile TextIOWrapper with its default newline=None performs universal-newline translation, turning captured lone carriage returns into line feeds, while newline="" preserves original line endings.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory continues to attribute the defect to CaptureIO, UTF-8 decoding, logging, or write-time byte mutation after visible evidence shows raw bytes retain the carriage return, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A direct experiment reading identical bytes through TextIOWrapper with newline=None and newline="", together with the repository call path, outranks unsupported claims about CaptureIO, write-time conversion, logging, or explicit string replacement.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a superficially plausible newline diagnosis aimed at the sys-capture buffer or decoder instead of the FD text wrapper that capfd actually reads.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the conversion on the text read path used by FDCapture rather than merely observing that TextIOWrapper can translate newlines.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source tracing from capfd/readouterr through FDCapture.snap to the EncodedFile TextIOWrapper, supported by a read-back experiment that distinguishes raw bytes from decoded text.
metadata.oracle_test: Writing b"Greetings from DOS\r" to the FD capture temporary file and reading it through TextIOWrapper yields a trailing newline with newline=None but a trailing carriage return with newline=""; raw buffer bytes remain b"...\r".

scale.1: No causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis incompatible with the visible capture implementation.
scale.2: Recognizes generic newline translation but assigns it to the wrong object, phase, or capture mode.
scale.3: Identifies TextIOWrapper universal-newline behavior and demonstrates newline=None versus newline="", but does not connect it precisely to FDCapture.snap and EncodedFile.
scale.4: Correctly traces capfd to FDCapture.snap reading EncodedFile and explains why the default newline mode changes a lone carriage return.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain and decisive raw-bytes-versus-text evidence showing that capture preserves the bytes and only EncodedFile text reading normalizes them.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly identifies universal-newline translation in the capfd text read path

applies_when: The cutoff contains runtime commands, test results, or conflicting observations concerning the proposed capture fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory obtains reliable evidence that the checkout's corrected capture path preserves carriage returns and remains compatible with existing capture behavior, while responding appropriately to failures and distinguishing environment/setup problems from product behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a claimed pass actually uses an unrelated installed pytest, or the trajectory copies source into site-packages and treats that contaminated run as authoritative, cap at 2; unresolved syntax errors, TypeErrors, or failing relevant tests cap at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing tests run against the modified checkout outrank isolated simulations; exact repr/raw-byte observations outrank terminal rendering; failures from a mismatched installed pytest or modified site-packages do not validate the checkout.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding misleading passes from newer pytest installations, toy classes that do not use FDCapture, or experiments contradicted by the visible source state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful execution of either the original reproducer or a repository regression test against the modified checkout, with evidence that the checkout code was loaded.
metadata.judge_focus: Command provenance, whether the modified checkout is actually imported, exact repr-based output, focused repository tests, broader capture tests, syntax checks, and recovery after failed or contradictory experiments.
metadata.oracle_test: Authoritative validation shows repr(out) ending in "\\r" for the capfd reproducer under the modified checkout, while ordinary "\n", UTF-8 replacement behavior, and relevant existing capture tests continue to work.

scale.1: Relevant runtime evidence fails or contradicts the claimed fix and remains unresolved.
scale.2: Only isolated I/O experiments or contaminated/mismatched pytest runs succeed; checkout behavior is not established.
scale.3: The corrected mechanism is demonstrated with a faithful local FDCapture-style experiment and source syntax is sound, but no checkout-level fixture or repository test succeeds.
scale.4: The original reproducer or focused repository test succeeds against the modified checkout with exact carriage-return evidence.
scale.5: Checkout-level regression evidence succeeds and is accompanied by relevant compatibility coverage or existing capture tests, with any earlier contradictory results explicitly traced to setup or test defects.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Produces trustworthy validation without masking contradictory evidence

applies_when: The cutoff contains a source modification or concrete patch proposal for pytest's FD text capture.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The visible change preserves carriage returns by configuring the existing EncodedFile used by FD capture with newline="", without altering unrelated capture modes, decoding policy, buffering behavior, or the public behavior of the helper class.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A change that rejects the existing write_through keyword, silently drops existing TextIOWrapper options, incorrectly decorates __init__, contains invalid syntax, or changes FDCapture to strict decoding is capped at 1; an unnecessary raw-buffer rewrite or broad helper override with unresolved compatibility risk is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible source diff and Python syntax/runtime behavior outrank prose claiming that a malformed, overly broad, or incompatible edit is correct.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for fixes that happen to preserve carriage returns in an isolated example while breaking EncodedFile construction, write-through behavior, replacement decoding, or other capture paths.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a syntactically valid change that reaches the EncodedFile instance used by capfd and retains all existing constructor options.
metadata.judge_focus: The actual diff in src/_pytest/capture.py, especially the EncodedFile construction in FDCaptureBinary.__init__, argument syntax, and preservation of encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", and write_through=True.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended boundary is equivalent to adding newline="" to the EncodedFile(TemporaryFile(...), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", write_through=True) construction used by FDCapture, so FDCapture.snap can continue reading text without universal-newline conversion.

scale.1: No usable source change, or the visible change is syntactically/runtime invalid or breaks the existing EncodedFile call contract.
scale.2: A plausible edit targets capture.py but does not reliably affect the capfd text read path or removes an existing behavior.
scale.3: A working but unnecessarily broad or behavior-changing workaround preserves carriage returns while leaving material compatibility risk.
scale.4: A valid, narrow change configures the FD capture text wrapper for no newline translation and preserves all existing options, with only minor style or placement concerns.
scale.5: A clean minimal change at the existing EncodedFile construction boundary adds newline="" with correct formatting and leaves binary capture, sys capture, encoding, error handling, and write-through semantics unchanged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements a narrow, constructor-compatible newline-preservation fix

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, proposes, applies, rejects, or validates a repair for caplog.set_level state leaking across tests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether visible work correctly isolates the capture handler as state mutated by caplog.set_level and converges on restoring that handler independently of each affected logger, with credit for concrete lifecycle tracing and targeted counterexamples as well as for an applied repair.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if finalization reads state stored only on a different object, removes per-logger restoration, or the trajectory continues endorsing an approach after relevant output directly disproves it. Cap at 3 if restoration is hardcoded to NOTSET or derived from a root or named logger, or if validation only exercises another installed version. A disproven root-derived attempt is not itself a contradiction when the trajectory explicitly rejects it and uses the failure to establish independent handler restoration.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository source, edits, diffs, and command output are authoritative. Targeted repository-based output that compares handler and logger baselines may establish or refute a causal theory even when the tested edit fails. Runs against another installed version establish neither the repository edit nor its validation, though surrounding repository source analysis may still establish the mutation and teardown path.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating the handler baseline with a logger level, hardcoding the common default, storing restoration state on the logging plugin while reading it from the fixture, or denying credit to a decisive failing experiment that visibly establishes the correct independent-state model.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires cutoff-visible support for the exact invariant that the handler's own pre-mutation level is independent of root or named logger levels, established by concrete repository source structure, an exact applied save/restore edit, or a targeted counterexample that distinguishes those values. Credit above 4 additionally requires a lifecycle-correct applied repair and valid execution against the edited repository.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the visible account of where the handler level is mutated, which object owns its baseline, and where fixture finalization restores it. Distinguish a wrong-object edit, a generic leak diagnosis, a coherent default-only repair, an exact independent-baseline invariant, and a validated implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: Let the capture handler begin at H while changed loggers begin at distinct levels L1 and L2. After any root or named-logger caplog.set_level calls, fixture teardown must restore the handler to H and each logger to its own original level. Evidence should remain valid when H differs from NOTSET, L1, and L2.

scale.1: The visible state or endorsed theory is internally inconsistent, uses restoration data owned by a different object, removes required logger restoration, or remains endorsed despite direct disproof.
scale.2: The trajectory notices a leak or missing teardown behavior but does not concretely isolate the handler's independently owned baseline or present a coherent restoration model.
scale.3: The trajectory gives a concrete lifecycle account of the handler mutation and fixture teardown, or applies a coherent default-case repair while preserving logger restoration, but still assumes a default value, relies on a logger-derived value, or lacks evidence for an arbitrary handler baseline.
scale.4: Visible source analysis, an exact applied edit, or a targeted counterexample establishes that the handler's actual prior level must be preserved and restored independently while every changed logger retains separate restoration; edited-source validation may still be absent.
scale.5: A lifecycle-correct independent handler save/restore repair is visibly applied and valid repository execution demonstrates the sequential regression plus a discriminating variant such as a named logger, repeated calls, or a non-default initial handler level without a visible related regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal convergence on caplog handler restoration

applies_when: The trajectory investigates why caplog.set_level affects a later test's observed capture level.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly identifies that caplog.set_level changes both the selected logger and the shared LogCaptureHandler, while fixture finalization restores only saved logger levels, allowing the handler level to leak into subsequent tests.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory claims that _initial_logger_levels persists across fixture instances, that LogCaptureHandler.reset resets its level, or that restoring only the root logger necessarily restores the handler.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and a reproduction run against that source take precedence over assumptions based on documentation, unrelated pytest versions, or handler reset behavior inferred without inspection.
metadata.failure_mode: Confusing logger state with handler state, or attributing the regression to fixture scope, record clearing, assertion rewriting, or catching_logs without tracing the actual mutation and teardown paths.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly identifying the missing restoration of the handler level, not merely stating that a logging level leaks.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection or runtime evidence connecting LogCaptureFixture.set_level, LogCaptureFixture._finalize, caplog.handler, and the session-owned capture handler reused across test phases.
metadata.oracle_test: After one test calls caplog.set_level(42), logger teardown may restore the logger while caplog.handler.level remains 42; the next test should instead observe the handler's pre-change level, normally logging.NOTSET (0).

scale.1: Provides no task-causal diagnosis or gives a diagnosis contradicted by the visible source/runtime behavior.
scale.2: Recognizes a cross-test logging leak but does not distinguish the logger level from the capture handler level.
scale.3: Observes that set_level changes the handler and that teardown appears incomplete, but does not clearly connect this to the shared handler seen by the next test.
scale.4: Correctly explains that set_level changes both logger and handler while _finalize restores only logger levels, with source-based support.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain, including handler reuse across tests/phases, the distinction from reset/at_level behavior, and task-matching runtime or source evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of leaked caplog handler level

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a source change intended to restore caplog state after caplog.set_level.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements restoration within LogCaptureFixture by preserving the capture handler's actual pre-set_level level and restoring that value during fixture finalization, while retaining the existing per-logger restoration behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the implementation restores from logging.getLogger().level, hardcodes logging.NOTSET, modifies the LoggingPlugin's unrelated initialization state, or overwrites the saved value on every set_level call so the original state is lost.
metadata.evidence_authority: The concrete diff and surrounding lifecycle code override prose summaries; preservation of the actual prior handler value is authoritative over assumptions that it is always NOTSET or equals the root logger level.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying the fix at the session plugin, reset method, or root logger boundary instead of the fixture-owned mutation boundary, or restoring a guessed level rather than the actual prior handler level.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires both preservation of the prior handler level and restoration from that preserved value in LogCaptureFixture teardown.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or edit in src/_pytest/logging.py showing where the original handler level is captured and where it is restored.
metadata.oracle_test: For an initial handler level H, any sequence of caplog.set_level calls during one fixture may change the handler, but fixture finalization must restore exactly H; separately changed named and root loggers must still be restored by _initial_logger_levels.

scale.1: No relevant implementation is present, or the visible edit is syntactically or structurally unrelated to the leak.
scale.2: Attempts handler restoration at an incorrect boundary or restores a guessed/root-derived value that is not the saved pre-change handler level.
scale.3: Implements only one half of the lifecycle, or has a plausible save/restore design with unresolved initialization, repeated-call, or access-order problems.
scale.4: Correctly saves the handler's actual initial level and restores it in _finalize while preserving logger restoration, with only minor clarity or style concerns.
scale.5: Provides a clean, minimal, lifecycle-correct implementation that preserves the first pre-change handler state, restores it during fixture finalization, and avoids unrelated logging-plugin changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise per-fixture restoration implementation

applies_when: The task concerns caplog.set_level leaking its capture-handler level across tests
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible repository work applies a semantically correct repair that restores both the affected logger levels and the caplog capture handler's pre-test/default level during fixture teardown.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the applied edit stores state on an object different from the one read during LogCaptureFixture finalization, or restores the handler from a root/named logger level that need not equal the handler baseline. Cap at 2 if the trajectory visibly discovers its current edit fails a relevant case and has not yet applied a corrected edit. Unapplied proposals cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible source diff and command output from the task repository outrank narrative claims. A valid run must exercise the edited source; runs using an installed or different pytest version do not establish the repair. Existing at_level behavior is a semantic reference but is not evidence that set_level teardown was fixed.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents credit for restoring only logger objects, hardwiring the handler to an unrelated logger level, editing the session plugin while finalizing the fixture, or treating a proposed fix as completed work.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3-5 require a visibly applied edit in the task repository that restores the caplog handler level while retaining restoration of every logger recorded by set_level.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible edits to LogCaptureFixture/caplog teardown and any sequential-test reproduction. Confirm that set_level's capture-handler mutation is undone independently of which root or named logger was changed.
metadata.oracle_test: After one test calls caplog.set_level(42), a subsequent test's caplog.handler.level must return to the capture handler's pre-test/default value (normally logging.NOTSET), while root and named logger levels return to their own original values. Changing a named logger must not cause teardown to copy that logger's level into the shared handler.

scale.1: A visible applied edit is causally wrong or internally inconsistent, such as reading restoration state from a different object than the one on which it was stored or deriving the handler level from an affected logger.
scale.2: No task-correct repair is visibly applied, or the current edit has been shown by visible evidence to be incomplete or wrong and correction remains unfinished; diagnosis may still identify the handler leak.
scale.3: A task-correct handler-restoration edit is visibly applied and preserves per-logger restoration, but no valid task-specific execution of the edited source is shown.
scale.4: A task-correct edit is applied and a valid focused check against the edited source demonstrates the two-test handler-level regression is fixed.
scale.5: A task-correct edit is applied and valid regression coverage demonstrates cross-test restoration plus a relevant variant such as named loggers or repeated set_level calls, with no visible regression in related logging tests.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly applies caplog capture-handler level restoration

applies_when: The trajectory creates, runs, or discusses tests intended to demonstrate the caplog level leak or validate its repair.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses a two-test regression scenario in which the first test calls caplog.set_level and the second observes the capture handler's restored level, and supplies credible execution evidence against the modified repository implementation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if all passing evidence comes from a system/PyPI pytest rather than the modified source, or if the test merely prints a value without asserting the expected restoration. Cap at 3 when only a mocked direct _finalize call is exercised.
metadata.evidence_authority: A run using the repository's src/_pytest code and task-matching test has priority; runs using an independently installed newer pytest do not validate the patch. Repository test-suite results outrank standalone mocks when both are available.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating tests from a newer already-fixed pytest installation as evidence, validating only logger restoration, or mistaking unrelated assertion-rewrite/dependency failures for a failure of the proposed fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a cross-test assertion on caplog.handler.level and visible successful execution after the relevant change against the local implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test contents, command environment, pre-fix failure or direct bug reproduction, post-change pass, and any targeted existing logging-fixture tests.
metadata.oracle_test: A regression test equivalent to test_foo calling caplog.set_level(42) followed by test_bar asserting caplog.handler.level == logging.NOTSET must fail before the fix and pass afterward under the repository pytest.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence is shown, or the shown evidence contradicts the claimed behavior.
scale.2: Shows only prints, static reasoning, or execution under an unrelated installed pytest version.
scale.3: Shows a meaningful standalone/mock check or a local reproduction without a complete asserted post-change run.
scale.4: Runs an asserted two-test regression successfully against the modified local source, with any environment limitations clearly separated.
scale.5: Demonstrates the failure before the change and success after it against local source, and also runs relevant existing logging fixture tests or adds a repository-quality regression test.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific reproduction and regression evidence

applies_when: The task requires restoring recursive collection through directory symlinks in pytest's filesystem traversal.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible prefix contains an applied production-code change that makes pytest's recursive directory visitor recognize and descend into symlinked directories, rather than merely diagnosing or proposing that change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest authoritative source still uses is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) for the recursion gate, cap the score at 2. If the applied edit continues to exclude directory symlinks or changes unrelated collection logic without correcting that gate, cap at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: A terminal unified diff or the latest shell-observed source/diff is authoritative over earlier source, prose claims, speculative tests, and summary fields. When repository-state evidence conflicts, the latest visible state wins.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents giving implementation-level credit for an accurate root-cause analysis or proposed one-line patch that was never applied, while treating omission of the false argument and an explicit true argument as semantically equivalent.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require visible evidence that a relevant production-code edit was actually applied by the cutoff; commands merely suggested, explanations, and hypothetical snippets do not satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect cutoff-visible repository-state evidence for the recursive visit implementation in src/_pytest/pathlib.py, especially the os.DirEntry.is_dir call controlling recursion. Credit removal of follow_symlinks=False or an explicitly equivalent setting that follows directory symlinks.
metadata.oracle_test: For an os.DirEntry that is a symlink to a directory containing tests, the recursion gate must treat the entry as a directory and descend into its target, restoring the behavior of the prior entry.check(dir=1) traversal.

scale.1: No applied relevant fix, and the visible work lacks the correct traversal diagnosis or proposes/applies behavior that would still skip symlinked directories.
scale.2: Correctly identifies the follow_symlinks=False recursion bug and may state the exact repair, but no relevant production-code edit is visibly applied by the cutoff.
scale.3: A relevant production edit is visibly applied, but the latest evidence is incomplete or leaves material uncertainty that recursive collection will actually descend through directory symlinks.
scale.4: A semantically correct production fix is visibly applied and restores symlink-directory recursion, but the patch also contains unnecessary related changes or lacks clear evidence that the final relevant source remains internally consistent.
scale.5: The latest authoritative repository state visibly contains a focused production fix: the recursive visit gate follows directory symlinks by removing follow_symlinks=False or using an explicitly equivalent true setting, with no visible conflicting change.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied symlink-directory traversal fix

applies_when: The task concerns generated unittest xUnit fixtures appearing in pytest fixture listings.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Traces the visibility regression to the public name generated by the shared unittest xUnit fixture helper and connects it to underscore-sensitive fixture listing, with any visible applied edit remaining structurally valid and confined to that causal boundary.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A latest visible applied edit that leaves the unittest fixture decorator malformed, duplicates its name argument, removes scope or autouse behavior, or otherwise makes the claimed name-only remedy invalid caps at 1. Changing global fixture reporting or unrelated generic xUnit generators without source evidence that they cause this unittest-specific regression caps at 2. Runtime output from an installed pytest known not to represent the repository cannot independently justify an anchor above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct repository source for the unittest generator and fixture-reporting rule is strongest for the causal mechanism. Trustworthy paired listing output from the modified repository may corroborate ordinary-versus-verbose behavior. The latest visible diff or file contents override earlier intentions and summaries; malformed source, duplicate decorator arguments, or removed scope/autouse configuration override an otherwise correct verbal diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a correct missing-underscore explanation from receiving equal credit when the applied edit corrupts the very helper it identifies, and prevents broad reporting or generic xUnit changes from being mistaken for a unittest-specific causal fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a complete connection between the generated public name, underscore-based suppression in ordinary fixture listings, and verbose inclusion. If an applied edit is visible, anchors above 1 additionally require that the implicated unittest fixture decorator remain syntactically intact with its existing scope and autouse configuration.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the generated name in src/_pytest/unittest.py, the underscore-and-verbosity listing rule in src/_pytest/python.py, and the latest visible state of any applied edit to ensure it supports rather than contradicts the diagnosis.
metadata.oracle_test: The shared unittest helper initially generates a public name such as unittest_setUpClass_fixture_Tests; fixture-reporting code omits underscore-prefixed names when verbosity is not enabled; changing only that helper's name to _unittest_setUpClass_fixture_Tests therefore hides it from ordinary --fixtures while retaining it under --fixtures -v, without altering the decorator or generic xUnit generators.

scale.1: No relevant causal account is established, authoritative evidence disproves it, or the latest visible applied edit leaves the implicated unittest fixture decorator malformed or behaviorally invalid.
scale.2: Recognizes the visibility symptom but assigns the cause to the wrong subsystem, or applies unjustified changes to global fixture reporting or unrelated generic xUnit generators.
scale.3: Correctly identifies the generated public unittest fixture name or the underscore-sensitive listing behavior and plausibly relates them, but does not establish the complete source-grounded ordinary-versus-verbose chain.
scale.4: Explicitly connects the public name generated in src/_pytest/unittest.py to underscore-based suppression in ordinary fixture listings and inclusion under verbose listing; any visible applied edit is valid and confined to the unittest name generator.
scale.5: Satisfies anchor 4 and also establishes from visible evidence that the shared helper covers both class- and method-level unittest xUnit fixtures and that introduction of the explicit public unique name caused the regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal localization and edit consistency for unittest fixture visibility

applies_when: The shared unittest xUnit fixture generator or its surrounding decorator is changed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Shows that privacy is restored without regressing setup, teardown, cleanup, scope, or autouse behavior for generated unittest fixtures.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax error, collection failure attributable to the patch, removed autouse/scope configuration, or failed setup/teardown behavior caps at 1; unrelated edits to generic _pytest/python.py xUnit fixtures cap at 2 unless independently justified by the task.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing behavioral tests using the modified source outrank claims based solely on the generated string; visible syntax errors or lost decorator arguments override asserted compatibility.
