reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly traces the mixed-copy cause and establishes that an omitted fit-time copy_X inherits self.copy_X while an explicit boolean overrides it for both preprocessing and lars_path, without contradicting that account in visible applied code.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible applied code still passes self.copy_X to one copy-sensitive stage and the fit-local or resolved value to the other, cap at 3 even when the narrative or tests claim consistency. If applied code removes the fit-time parameter, always ignores explicit overrides, or always ignores the constructor setting, cap at 2. Claims that None is itself the copy policy or that the existing mixed behavior is correct force 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Displayed repository source and the latest visible scoped diff outrank summaries, claimed test success, synthetic simulations, and behavior from an installed external sklearn package. A correct plan may earn full diagnostic credit when no implementation is applied, but visible applied code that contradicts the stated contract controls the contradiction cap.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding complete diagnostic understanding from a correct verbal sentinel proposal while ignoring latest applied source that still implements mixed precedence or discards backward-compatible explicit fit overrides.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires identifying both copy-sensitive consumers and distinguishing an omitted fit argument from an explicitly supplied True or False. Credit of 5 additionally requires the complete constructor-fallback and explicit-override contract with no contradictory applied source.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect reasoning about LassoLarsIC.__init__, the fit signature, LinearModel._preprocess_data, and lars_path. Determine whether the trajectory distinguishes omission from explicit True or False and requires one effective value for both consumers.
metadata.oracle_test: With constructor copy_X=False and no fit override, both preprocessing and lars_path use False; an explicit fit(copy_X=True) makes both use True. Constructor True with an explicit False override behaves symmetrically.

scale.1: Gives an incorrect causal account, fails to recognize the conflicting copy_X controls, or treats the existing mixed behavior as correct.
scale.2: Notices duplicate controls but adopts an incompatible contract, such as removing the fit argument, always using self.copy_X, or always using the fit default; this anchor also applies when visible applied code enforces one of those contradictions.
scale.3: Identifies the default-shadowing problem and a None fallback, but does not require the resolved value at both preprocessing and lars_path, omits explicit override semantics, or has visible applied code that still splits the two stages.
scale.4: Correctly distinguishes omitted and explicit fit arguments and identifies both copy-sensitive stages, with no contradictory applied source, but leaves a minor case or explanation implicit.
scale.5: Source-traces the exact inconsistency and states the complete compatible contract: omission inherits self.copy_X, explicit True or False overrides it, and one effective value governs both preprocessing and lars_path; any visible applied source is consistent with that account.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-grounded copy_X diagnosis and precedence contract

applies_when: A visible patch or edited source for LassoLarsIC.fit is present at the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements a fit-time None sentinel and resolves one effective copy_X value before all copy-sensitive work, preserving explicit fit overrides and the existing fit API.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If one stage still uses self.copy_X while the other uses the fit-local or resolved value, credit is capped at 3. Removing copy_X from fit is capped at 2 because it breaks existing explicit fit calls. Syntax corruption or undefined-variable use forces 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final repository diff or latest complete source excerpt outranks earlier proposed patches, narrative claims, synthetic examples, and behavior observed from a separately installed package.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a fix to only the lars_path call for a complete fix, thereby retaining mixed behavior when fit(copy_X=...) explicitly overrides the constructor.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require fit(self, X, y, copy_X=None) or an equivalent compatible sentinel API, plus a resolved effective value used by both _preprocess_data and lars_path.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible final diff or final displayed source for the LassoLarsIC.fit signature, fallback assignment, _preprocess_data argument, and lars_path copy_X argument.
metadata.oracle_test: Resolve copy_X = self.copy_X when the fit argument is None, otherwise retain the explicit boolean; pass that resolved value to both LinearModel._preprocess_data and lars_path.

scale.1: The visible implementation is syntactically broken, uses an undefined value, changes the wrong class, or does not address the behavior.
scale.2: The patch changes the relevant area but breaks compatibility by removing the fit argument, hard-codes one policy, or otherwise cannot implement both inheritance and explicit override.
scale.3: The patch introduces a None sentinel or fallback but leaves the two copy-sensitive stages capable of receiving different values, or the final implementation is materially incomplete.
scale.4: The final code correctly resolves and consistently uses the effective value while preserving the API, but has a minor localized implementation or presentation defect that does not change the four required cases.
scale.5: The final code cleanly changes fit to a None sentinel, resolves the effective value once before preprocessing, and uses that same value for both _preprocess_data and lars_path with no functional defect.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Consistent, compatibility-preserving implementation

applies_when: The trajectory analyzes the duplicate copy_X controls in LassoLarsIC or states their intended precedence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Accurately identifies the mixed-copy bug and derives the compatibility-preserving rule that an omitted fit-time copy_X inherits self.copy_X while an explicitly supplied boolean overrides it consistently.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that fit should always use self.copy_X, always use the fit default, or treat None as a literal copy policy caps this rubric at 2; visible recognition that preprocessing and lars_path may receive different values is required for 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Quoted or displayed repository source takes precedence over summaries, assumptions based on newer installed scikit-learn versions, and synthetic demonstrations.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a superficial observation about duplicate names without understanding the two downstream consumers or the required backward-compatible precedence.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires distinguishing an omitted fit argument from an explicitly supplied True or False.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or reasoning connecting LassoLarsIC.__init__, LassoLarsIC.fit, LinearModel._preprocess_data, and lars_path, including the omitted-argument and explicit-override cases.
metadata.oracle_test: For LassoLarsIC(copy_X=False).fit(X, y), both copy-sensitive stages use False; fit(X, y, copy_X=True) makes both use True. The symmetric cases for constructor True and explicit False follow the same rule.

scale.1: The trajectory gives an incorrect causal account or proposes semantics that silently discard the constructor setting or explicit fit override.
scale.2: It notices duplicate copy_X declarations but does not trace the mixed use of self.copy_X versus the fit-local value, or advocates simply removing the fit argument without addressing compatibility.
scale.3: It correctly identifies the default-shadowing problem and says None should fall back to self.copy_X, but does not establish consistent use across both preprocessing and lars_path or does not cover explicit overrides.
scale.4: It states the correct omitted-versus-explicit precedence and identifies both copy-sensitive stages, with only a minor omission in the full True/False case analysis.
scale.5: It source-traces the exact inconsistency and states the complete contract: omitted fit copy_X inherits the constructor value, explicit True or False overrides it, and the one resolved value governs both preprocessing and lars_path.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis and copy_X precedence contract

metadata.contradiction_rule: A final diff that removes the fit parameter is capped at 2. Unrecovered broad replacements, unrelated constructor changes, duplicate or malformed docstrings, or repository source corruption cap credit at 2; invalid Python syntax forces 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final complete git diff takes precedence over claims that edits are targeted; a later clean reset and corrected diff supersedes earlier accidental edits only when visibly demonstrated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Narrow API, documentation, and regression boundary

applies_when: A visible edit or patch affecting LassoLarsIC.fit is present at the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements a backward-compatible fit-time sentinel under which omission inherits the constructor's copy_X setting and an explicit boolean controls both preprocessing and lars_path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removing the fit-time copy_X parameter, making it unusable, changing the wrong method, or leaving invalid Python or undefined names forces 1. If the parameter is retained but preprocessing and lars_path can receive different values, or either constructor fallback or explicit override is discarded, cap at 2. A behaviorally correct target edit with a visible unresolved executable collateral defect is capped at 3. Do not penalize equivalent inline fallback expressions solely because they are not assigned to a temporary variable.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest complete scoped repository diff is authoritative. When no complete diff is visible, use the latest displayed source for each relevant line without inferring undisplayed assignments or cleanup. Applied repository source outranks plans, summaries, synthetic demonstrations, external installations, and claimed test results.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating removal of the legacy fit argument as equivalent to a partial sentinel fix, inferring consistency from a correct narrative while preprocessing remains hardwired to self.copy_X, or withholding full credit merely because the same correct fallback expression is used at both consumers instead of a temporary variable.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires retaining a fit-time copy_X parameter with None or an equivalent omission sentinel and visibly establishing that omission and explicit True or False produce the same effective value at both copy-sensitive consumers. Credit of 5 requires a complete visible scoped diff showing that contract and no executable collateral defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible LassoLarsIC.fit signature and the values supplied to LinearModel._preprocess_data and lars_path, then inspect the same visible patch for executable collateral edits.
metadata.oracle_test: With constructor copy_X=False, an omitted fit argument sends False to both preprocessing and lars_path, while an explicit True sends True to both. With constructor copy_X=True, omission sends True to both and an explicit False sends False to both.

scale.1: The visible edit removes or breaks the fit-time copy_X API, changes the wrong behavior, contains invalid or undefined executable code, or otherwise cannot preserve explicit fit-time overrides.
scale.2: A compatible-looking sentinel is introduced, but omission or explicit override is mishandled, or preprocessing and lars_path can still receive different effective values.
scale.3: The target LassoLarsIC logic visibly satisfies constructor fallback and explicit override at both consumers, but the same patch leaves an executable collateral defect or material ambiguity that prevents trusting the applied state.
scale.4: The latest visible target source satisfies all four constructor-versus-fit cases at both consumers with no visible functional defect, but the available excerpts do not establish the complete scoped patch.
scale.5: A complete visible scoped diff retains the fit-time API with a None or equivalent sentinel and applies the correct effective value to both preprocessing and lars_path for omission and explicit True or False, with no executable collateral defect.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable compatibility-preserving copy_X implementation

applies_when: The trajectory executes or authors checks intended to validate StratifiedKFold shuffle behavior
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation exercises the checked-out implementation and asserts actual sample-to-fold membership, reproducibility, stratification, and non-shuffle compatibility rather than relying on printed fold order or unrelated package behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the claimed validation executed a different installed implementation, failed before reaching the assertion, compared only fold order or aggregate class counts, or contains a visible logic error that invalidates the conclusion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing repository tests against the edited checkout outrank faithful standalone reproductions; faithful reproductions outrank behavior from a separately installed package. Syntax compilation establishes only parseability, not shuffle semantics.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting modern-package output, standalone code with different allocation logic, py_compile success, or prose saying a test passed when the visible command failed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a membership-sensitive check tied to the checked-out implementation or a repository regression test. Merely printing outputs cannot receive the highest score.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect test provenance, assertions, command outcomes, and whether the chosen data can distinguish identical per-class permutations from independent class-relative assignments.
metadata.oracle_test: A discriminating regression uses at least two classes with aligned ordering and enough samples per class, checks that shuffle=True breaks deterministic cross-class positional pairing or otherwise changes sample-to-fold membership, verifies the same seed repeats exactly, and confirms every fold remains stratified. It should also cover shuffle=False or an uneven-count case to guard existing behavior.

scale.1: No usable validation evidence is produced, or all attempted checks fail before testing the relevant behavior.
scale.2: Only weak or non-authoritative evidence is shown, such as external-package behavior, syntax checks, aggregate balance, or printed output without a valid membership comparison.
scale.3: A faithful standalone check or source-level trace discriminates membership changes and has a valid observed result, but it does not execute the edited checkout as a repository regression.
scale.4: A targeted local regression or equivalent checkout-based check validates actual membership behavior and reproducibility, but omits at least one important invariant or broader compatibility check.
scale.5: Passing local regression evidence validates membership randomization, same-seed reproducibility, different-seed sensitivity, stratification and coverage, shuffle=False compatibility, and a nontrivial class-count case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validates the local fix with membership-sensitive regression evidence

applies_when: The trajectory encounters build failures, imports an installed sklearn version, or obtains runtime behavior that conflicts with the checked-out source or issue report
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Correctly separates evidence from the checked-out historical implementation from behavior of newer site-packages installations, and responds to failed or contradictory experiments by returning to source tracing or faithful simulation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Claiming the task is already fixed because a modern installed sklearn behaves correctly, or claiming a patch works based only on py_compile, a hand-written substitute, or a failed build, caps credit at 2
metadata.evidence_authority: Checked-out repository source and tests run against that source outrank site-packages behavior; a failed build or standalone script validates only what its output directly establishes
metadata.failure_mode: Allowing dependency installation, import shadowing, or modern API differences to override the actual source under repair
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicit provenance for runtime evidence or an explicit recovery after discovering that the imported sklearn is not the repository version
metadata.judge_focus: Visible commands showing import paths or versions, treatment of build errors, and whether conclusions are revised when experiments exercised a different implementation
metadata.oracle_test: The repository is an older development tree whose _make_test_folds stores rng = self.random_state; newer sklearn implementations may already use a different allocation algorithm and therefore are not behavioral oracles for this instance

scale.1: Ignores provenance and treats failed or unrelated execution as conclusive.
scale.2: Notices environment trouble but still bases the diagnosis or claimed validation on a different sklearn implementation or non-executed code.
scale.3: Acknowledges that build/import evidence is limited, but does not establish which implementation produced the observed behavior.
scale.4: Establishes repository versus site-packages provenance and confines conclusions to authoritative evidence, recovering from at least one contradiction when present.
scale.5: Combines explicit provenance, source-based reconciliation of conflicting observations, and a faithful fallback experiment or repository test plan without overstating unexecuted or failed validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Maintains repository-version evidence provenance and recovers from contradictions

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or performs a source change intended to repair StratifiedKFold shuffle behavior
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible solution converts the configured random_state into one mutable RNG consumed successively by per-class fold construction, while retaining the existing class-local fold assignment, trimming, balance, coverage, warning, and shuffle-disabled behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if each class still receives an integer seed that restarts the same stream, if the change merely reorders yielded folds, globally shuffles samples or labels, permutes dummy values without using the permutation, loses original-index correspondence, or replaces the allocation method with visibly inconsistent logic. Malformed or duplicated method structure scores 1 unless visibly repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source inspection or repository diff outranks patch commands and prose. A clean final diff outranks abandoned intermediate edits. If no applied diff is visible, judge only the concrete proposal and do not infer application.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting any use of shuffle, permutation, per-class seeds, successful text replacement, syntax compilation, or modern sklearn behavior as evidence that the historical RNG replay was fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require a coherent applied change in the historical StratifiedKFold implementation. Score 5 additionally requires membership-sensitive execution against that checkout showing preserved balance, coverage, reproducibility, and shuffle=False behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the final visible target-method source or repository diff. Verify where check_random_state is called, what object each per-class KFold receives, whether lazy split iteration advances that one object, and whether existing assignment and trimming logic remains intact.
metadata.oracle_test: The minimal historical fix is to obtain a mutable RNG with check_random_state before constructing the per-class KFold objects and pass that same object to them, so successive lazy KFold iterations consume advancing state. Equal-sized classes then receive different positional permutations while the same configured integer seed remains reproducible.

scale.1: No concrete implementation is given, or the latest visible target source is malformed, duplicated, or internally unusable.
scale.2: A concrete change is shown, but it retains reset RNG streams, changes only fold order, mishandles sample-index mapping, globally shuffles labels or samples, or otherwise violates the existing allocation invariants.
scale.3: A precise source-compatible design identifies one advancing mutable RNG and preserves the existing allocation logic, but no coherent applied repository change is visible.
scale.4: A coherent applied diff uses one advancing mutable RNG across per-class fold construction and preserves the surrounding allocation logic by inspection, but authoritative membership-sensitive checkout validation is absent or incomplete.
scale.5: The level-4 implementation is present and checkout-based tests demonstrate broken cross-class positional pairing, same-seed reproducibility, suitable different-seed membership variation, class balance, complete coverage, and unchanged shuffle=False behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies the advancing shared-RNG fix without rewriting stratified allocation

applies_when: The trajectory edits target source or develops a concrete implementation direction for the StratifiedKFold shuffle repair
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the severity of unresolved task-causal damage introduced by edits or implementation reasoning, including malformed method structure, unrelated broad changes, incorrect index mapping, reset RNG streams, global shuffling, and continued reliance on a mechanism already contradicted by visible source or experiments.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Do not penalize a wrong hypothesis that is explicitly rejected and repaired before cutoff. Cap severity at 2 when no harmful source change or incorrect implementation direction remains current. Persistent duplicated methods, invalid syntax, broken indentation, unrelated file-wide dtype rewrites, or loss of sample-to-label correspondence warrant the highest severity.
metadata.evidence_authority: A latest source inspection and final repository diff outrank earlier edit commands. A visible repair or reversion removes the corresponding damage. Prose claiming success cannot override malformed source, a contradictory diff, or a failed command.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding visible activity or successful replacement commands while ignoring that the resulting source is malformed, semantically contradicted, unnecessarily broad, or never restored.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require visible unresolved harmful code or an explicit current implementation plan that necessarily violates shuffle semantics or K-fold invariants; mere uncertainty, lack of a patch, build failure, or use of an external package is not enough.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible target source, repository diff, reversions, syntax results, and the trajectory's current implementation claim. Separate exploratory mistakes that were explicitly repaired from wrong mechanisms or source corruption still left unresolved.
metadata.oracle_test: A safe repair leaves the historical allocation and index-mapping structure intact and changes RNG consumption only as needed. Dangerous alternatives include shuffling labels globally, treating dummy-array values as samples, assigning fold labels through incorrect fancy indexing, independently reseeding classes, or rewriting the whole method without preserving uneven-count handling.

scale.1: No task-causal damage is visible: the source remains intact, or all mistaken edits and implementation claims are explicitly corrected or reverted.
scale.2: A localized speculative mistake or weak edit is visible, but it is recognized, contained, or does not leave an unresolved harmful implementation direction.
scale.3: An unresolved and insufficiently checked rewrite or implementation direction creates material regression risk, but no decisive invariant violation or source corruption is visible.
scale.4: The current edit or advocated mechanism visibly violates RNG progression, index correspondence, fold membership semantics, balance, coverage, or shuffle=False compatibility.
scale.5: Severe unresolved damage is visible, such as malformed or duplicated method structure, invalid syntax, broad unrelated source mutation, or an implementation that cannot preserve sample-to-label and fold assignment invariants.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Accumulates unrecovered source or semantic damage

applies_when: The trajectory contains reasoning or evidence about the source of non-monotonic KBinsDiscretizer edges under strategy='kmeans'.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that KMeans cluster labels and cluster_centers_ order are arbitrary even with ordered initialization, so adjacent-center midpoint computation is invalid unless the centers are first ordered.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that sorting already-computed midpoints is semantically equivalent to sorting centers caps credit at 2; a claim that deterministic initialization guarantees ordered returned centers caps credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and direct output showing unsorted cluster_centers_ take precedence over assumptions based on deterministic or sorted initialization; task-specific data takes precedence over unrelated random examples.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a superficial 'np.digitize needs sorted bins' observation while missing why the boundaries themselves were constructed from the wrong adjacency relationships.
metadata.hard_gate: Higher anchors require identifying center ordering before midpoint construction as the causal boundary, not merely observing that the final edge array is non-monotonic.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible explanation, inspected source, or runtime output connecting arbitrary cluster_centers_ ordering to midpoint order and the later np.digitize monotonicity failure.
metadata.oracle_test: For X=[0, 0.5, 2, 3, 9, 10] and five one-dimensional clusters, KMeans may return centers in label order such as [0.25, 3, 10, 2, 9]; midpoints between those adjacent array entries are not the decision boundaries between centers ordered on the number line.

scale.1: Misdiagnoses the failure, asserts centers are guaranteed ordered, or provides no causal account.
scale.2: Recognizes non-monotonic bin_edges or the np.digitize requirement but does not locate arbitrary center ordering as the cause, or proposes derived-edge sorting as equivalent.
scale.3: Correctly states that KMeans centers can be unordered and that this propagates to bin_edges, but gives little source-specific or semantic support.
scale.4: Correctly traces KMeans center label order through adjacent midpoint construction to np.digitize and distinguishes ordered initialization from ordered output.
scale.5: Provides the complete source-specific causal chain and decisive visible evidence or a concrete numerical example demonstrating that only ordering centers restores the intended one-dimensional neighbor relationships.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of unordered k-means centers

applies_when: The task concerns KBinsDiscretizer with strategy='kmeans' producing non-monotonic bin edges.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credit an applied implementation that numerically orders the fitted one-dimensional k-means centers before computing consecutive-center midpoint boundaries, thereby producing monotonic edges while preserving the nearest-center partition.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the applied change only sorts midpoint edges or the completed bin_edges array while leaving centers unordered during midpoint construction, cap the score at 2 even if np.digitize no longer raises or a demonstration reports success.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible repository state and its subsequent source or diff output outrank narrative claims, manual calculations, tests against an externally installed package, and proposed edits. Tests are corroborating evidence only.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking monotonic output edges for semantic correctness even though those edges were computed from nonadjacent centers in arbitrary label order.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a visibly applied source change that orders the fitted one-dimensional centers before adjacent-center midpoints are calculated.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible repository code or diff in the k-means branch of KBinsDiscretizer.fit. Verify that cluster_centers_ are sorted before the expression that averages neighboring centers; distinguish this from sorting midpoint or completed edge arrays afterward.
metadata.oracle_test: For one-dimensional k-means, sort centers by coordinate first, then place each internal boundary at the midpoint of consecutive sorted centers and retain the feature minimum and maximum as endpoints.

scale.1: No applied task-causal change is visible, or the applied change still permits non-monotonic edges and does not establish the required center ordering.
scale.2: An applied workaround sorts midpoint edges or completed bin edges after they were derived from unordered centers; the exception may be suppressed, but nearest-center boundaries are not preserved.
scale.3: The correct need to sort centers before midpoint construction is explicitly identified, but the authoritative visible repository state does not contain that repair.
scale.4: The applied implementation orders centers before midpoint construction, but a visible local defect or ambiguity prevents establishing a clean, complete implementation.
scale.5: The applied implementation clearly sorts the fitted one-dimensional centers before computing consecutive-center midpoints, retains the endpoint construction, and contains no visible contradiction to that semantic repair.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Construct k-means bin boundaries from numerically ordered centers

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies a code change to KBinsDiscretizer's strategy='kmeans' edge construction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Orders the one-dimensional fitted cluster centers before calculating adjacent midpoints, while retaining the feature minimum and maximum as the outer bin edges and leaving unrelated strategies unchanged.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the visible final implementation only sorts computed midpoints or the completed bin_edges array, credit is capped at 2 because it can suppress np.digitize's exception while preserving boundaries formed from non-neighboring centers. Missing col_min/col_max, malformed code, or edits outside the kmeans branch cap credit at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The final visible repository diff takes precedence over earlier proposed snippets or narration; sorting centers in place or assigning np.sort(centers) are semantically equivalent.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking monotonic output as sufficient even when sorting incorrectly constructed boundaries changes bin semantics and sample assignments.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require sorting centers before `(centers[1:] + centers[:-1]) * 0.5`; merely sorting midpoint or completed edge arrays cannot pass the gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch or working-tree diff around sklearn/preprocessing/_discretization.py showing the exact ordering operation relative to cluster_centers_, midpoint calculation, and endpoint concatenation.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended one-dimensional k-means boundaries are midpoints of consecutive centers after ascending spatial ordering: `centers.sort()` (or equivalent), then midpoint computation, then `np.r_[col_min, ..., col_max]`.

scale.1: No applicable implementation, syntactically broken/destructive code, or a change that does not establish monotonic k-means edges.
scale.2: Sorts midpoint-derived or completed bin_edges without first ordering centers, thereby avoiding the exception but not restoring correct nearest-center boundaries.
scale.3: Moves toward ordering centers but the visible change is incomplete, ambiguously placed, or mixed with unnecessary risky modifications.
scale.4: Correctly orders centers before midpoint construction in the kmeans branch and preserves endpoint construction and other strategies.
scale.5: Provides a minimal, clear, repository-local patch that exactly orders fitted one-dimensional centers before midpoint construction, preserves col_min/col_max and existing API behavior, and contains no unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct implementation at the k-means boundary

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or edits production code to correct the fit_predict and predict inconsistency.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Confines the implementation to restoring the selected best model state before the final E-step in BaseMixture.fit_predict, while preserving selected-fit bookkeeping and the public prediction semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible source is malformed, duplicates or drops warning logic, leaves log_resp undefined, or computes the final E-step before restoring best_params. Cap at 1 if the surviving change alters predict instead of correcting fit_predict, or deletes broad repository content without visible restoration.
metadata.evidence_authority: A displayed coherent diff or post-edit source excerpt takes precedence over an earlier proposed edit; repository status showing no change means only proposal-level credit. Later restoration of a malformed edit supersedes the malformed intermediate state.
metadata.failure_mode: Applying an algebraically irrelevant predict rewrite, corrupting the method while moving blocks, or fixing the symptom outside the shared BaseMixture fitting boundary.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4-5 require a coherent implementation boundary in BaseMixture.fit_predict that computes returned labels only after best_params are installed; changing predict alone cannot pass the gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible patch, diff, or exact edit plan for sklearn/mixture/base.py showing self._set_parameters(best_params), self.n_iter_, and self.lower_bound_ established before the final self._e_step(X), followed by log_resp.argmax(axis=1).
metadata.oracle_test: The final sequence is: retain the best initialization during the loop; restore best_params and selected bookkeeping; perform the final E-step on X; return its responsibility argmax.

scale.1: No relevant implementation direction, or the visible surviving direction is destructive or fundamentally incorrect.
scale.2: Names the right file or suggests reordering operations, but the proposed/visible edit is incomplete, malformed, or changes the wrong method.
scale.3: Gives a plausible exact edit that restores best_params before the final E-step, but lacks a coherent visible patch or omits preservation of important surrounding bookkeeping/control flow.
scale.4: Shows a coherent minimal patch or complete edit plan that moves best-state restoration and n_iter_/lower_bound_ bookkeeping before the final E-step without changing predict semantics.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and additionally demonstrates from the resulting source or diff that warning flow, return value, method structure, and unrelated mixture behavior remain intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Precise BaseMixture state-ordering correction

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates or changes GaussianMixture fit_predict and predict consistency.

Reasoning and success claims are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents awarding full credit for correct diagnosis without applied work, false-positive tests against site-packages, conversion inside an unsuitable path, or a dense-only workaround that regresses CSR support.

scale.1: The visible state is unusable or non-causal: source needed for the patch was removed or displaced, validation exercises only an unrelated installation, or the applied change clearly cannot implement the required behavior.

Execution of a copied module or separate installation and isolated simulations are only supporting evidence. Later source, diff, import-path, and traceback evidence overrides verbal success claims.

The negative control replaces an active estimator with one lacking an explicit sample_weight parameter and observes the established unsupported-sample-weight error.

An additional harmless helper guard does not erase a correct causal guard, but prevents score 5 unless absent from the final diff.

A later checkout, restore, unguarded source excerpt, syntax check failure, or clean diff showing no change overrides an earlier successful-looking command. Tests against copied or installed modules cannot establish the checkout state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves capability validation for every active voting estimator

applies_when: The visible trajectory selects, investigates, tests, or changes the feature-name construction and lookup path used by export_text.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how convincingly the visible work localizes the earliest executable feature-name failure by tracing preprocessing before recursion, distinguishing node positions from feature indices, accounting for leaf sentinels, and revising hypotheses when direct evidence disproves them. This dimension rewards durable causal information even when a final repair has not yet been completed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the final visible account leaves competing node-indexed and feature-indexed explanations unresolved after both are presented. Cap at 2 when the work settles on changing only the recursive lookup while retaining the eager sentinel-unsafe comprehension, or settles on indexing custom names by node count. Cap at 3 when custom-name handling is coherent but the same edit can fail when feature_names is absent. A visibly failed candidate patch does not itself impose a cap if its failure is used as a controlled counterexample and the invalid hypothesis is explicitly withdrawn.
metadata.evidence_authority: A direct target-source execution, exact counterexample, or visible failed expression that isolates the first exception outranks a plausible patch and general prose. An explicit correction after such evidence outranks an earlier mistaken edit. A complete applied diff is authoritative only for paths it actually preserves; it does not override a visible default-name regression or an earlier still-executed sentinel lookup. Target definitions and observed target arrays outrank later-version analogies and inaccurate mocks.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a syntactically plausible final edit more than a decisive causal counterexample; treating discovery of TREE_UNDEFINED without locating when it is evaluated as complete diagnosis; crediting a later-version snippet while contradictory target invariants remain unresolved; or overlooking that a custom-name-only construction can break default labels.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires direct source-consistent evidence that identifies the pre-recursion sentinel evaluation as the first possible exception, or a counterexample that disproves an alternative localization followed by an explicit correction toward that fact. Credit at 5 additionally requires one settled invariant covering supplied names, generated defaults, split lookup, and leaf handling.
metadata.judge_focus: Follow the visible reasoning from feature-name validation through eager name construction and guarded recursive rendering. Credit exact source tracing, counterexamples, and explicit retraction of disproven node-count or lookup hypotheses. Separately check whether any proposed invariant covers custom names, generated defaults, split nodes, and leaf entries.
metadata.oracle_test: tree_.feature has one entry per node: split entries are input-feature indices and leaf entries are TREE_UNDEFINED. With one supplied name, eager evaluation of feature_names[TREE_UNDEFINED] can fail before recursion. A coherent invariant either creates a node-aligned sequence with harmless leaf placeholders and reads it by node, or keeps names feature-indexed and reads names[tree_.feature[node]] only under the non-leaf guard. The default path must still produce feature_0.
metadata.stage: causal diagnosis and hypothesis correction before or during repair

scale.1: The work remains speculative or internally unresolved: incompatible node, feature, or sentinel explanations are presented without selecting one through evidence.
scale.2: A determinate causal attempt is made, but the settled account is contradicted by visible source or execution, such as retaining the earlier sentinel lookup or indexing feature names by node positions.
scale.3: Relevant source facts are established and a plausible cause is identified, but the first failing operation is not decisively isolated, a proposed invariant remains incomplete, or custom and default paths are not reconciled.
scale.4: The first failing operation is isolated by exact source tracing or a direct counterexample, and any disproven competing hypothesis is explicitly retracted; the trajectory converges on a viable invariant, though no complete applied repair or full custom/default verification is visible.
scale.5: The trajectory provides decisive causal localization and a settled source-consistent resolution: eager leaf-sentinel indexing is eliminated, node and feature domains remain distinct, split labels use the actual feature index, leaf names are harmless or unnecessary, default feature labels remain valid, and materially conflicting earlier hypotheses are explicitly superseded.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-backed localization of the first export_text name-resolution failure

applies_when: A concrete edit, diff, or implementation proposal for sklearn/tree/export.py is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Repairs custom feature-name resolution without indexing a one-element feature-name sequence with the leaf sentinel, while preserving node-to-feature name correspondence, default feature labels, leaf handling, and existing feature_names length validation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Changing only name = feature_names_[node] to use tree_.feature[node] while retaining the sentinel-unsafe comprehension is capped at 2. Expanding storage by node_count while indexing feature_names by node number is also capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A coherent repository diff outranks prose; when alternatives conflict, direct evaluation of the full modified data flow outranks similarity to a particular patch shape.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a locally plausible index substitution that leaves the original exception intact, generates names from node IDs, breaks default labels, or alters unrelated tree exporters.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require that no executed setup path indexes feature_names with TREE_UNDEFINED. Valid designs include a node-aligned list with a sentinel placeholder, or a feature-indexed name list/direct lookup used only after the existing non-leaf guard.
metadata.judge_focus: The complete visible indexing invariant across feature_names_ construction and the later split-node lookup, including custom names, default names, and TREE_UNDEFINED leaves.
metadata.oracle_test: Both of these invariants are valid: (a) feature_names_[node] is the name for tree_.feature[node], with a harmless placeholder at leaf nodes; or (b) names are indexed by feature number and accessed as names[tree_.feature[node]] only inside tree_.feature[node] != TREE_UNDEFINED. export_text with feature_names=None must still emit feature_0 for the sole feature.

scale.1: No concrete repair is present, or the edit is clearly unrelated or syntactically unusable.
scale.2: A partial or incorrect repair changes an index or collection size but leaves sentinel indexing, feature/node confusion, or another immediate failure intact.
scale.3: A viable repair direction is described, but the exact construction and lookup changes are incomplete or internally ambiguous.
scale.4: A complete semantically valid repair is precisely proposed but not visibly applied, or an applied repair is valid but includes a minor unnecessary or compatibility-risking change.
scale.5: A visible applied diff gives a minimal, internally consistent repair that handles custom and default names, respects the non-leaf guard and existing validation, and avoids unrelated changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Repeatedly asserting a hypothesis after visible evidence disproves it, or claiming tests passed after only a build/import failure, caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Checked-in source and constants from the target repository outrank guessed tree layouts; a comparable later implementation may support but not replace target-source reasoning; real target-version runtime evidence outranks all static inference.

metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an explicit correction of earlier incorrect reasoning or a disciplined pivot from an unavailable build to authoritative target-source evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible response to failed builds, failed simulations, contradictory observations, and discoveries about TREE_UNDEFINED; emphasis is on explicit correction rather than persistence with an invalid premise.
