reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery from build failures and contradictory indexing hypotheses

applies_when: The visible trajectory selects, investigates, tests, or changes the feature-name setup or lookup path executed by export_text.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work establishes that the earliest reachable feature-name exception occurs during eager setup before recursive rendering, rather than merely identifying a nearby indexing problem. Reward direct execution-order evidence, explicit correction of disproven downstream explanations, and authoritative inspection of a complete final data flow that prevents leaf sentinels from indexing supplied names.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the visible source state is malformed or the cutoff equally endorses incompatible eager-construction and recursive-lookup causes. Cap at 2 when the settled account changes only the guarded recursive lookup, indexes supplied names by node number, or still eagerly indexes supplied names for every tree_.feature entry. Cap at 3 when the likely eager cause is identified but execution order remains implicit, or when a potentially valid repair is only issued and its complete resulting state is not inspected. A failed hypothesis does not impose a cap when a later direct counterexample is acknowledged and the final account is source-consistent.
metadata.evidence_authority: A traceback or faithful execution of the exact eager expression that observes the exception outranks inferred prose. Next is checked-in target source combined with an explicit source-order proof. A visibly inspected, coherent final diff may prove localization by removing the eager evaluation and retaining guarded split lookup, but an edit command, partial snippet, claimed patch, later-version analogy, or malformed simulation does not establish the resulting data flow. Later explicit correction outranks earlier speculation only when the incompatible premise is actually withdrawn or made unreachable by an inspected final state.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a mention of TREE_UNDEFINED without locating when it is evaluated; treating a downstream subscript change as localization while the earlier comprehension remains reachable; accepting duplicated, truncated, or uninspected edits as proof; equating broad bounds filtering with a demonstrated causal account; or allowing a plausible final patch to override direct evidence that another expression fails first.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either direct evidence that supplied names are indexed by a leaf sentinel before recursion or an authoritative inspection of the complete final source state proving that this eager evaluation was removed while split lookup remains under the non-leaf guard. Credit at 5 requires decisive source-order localization plus a settled node/feature/sentinel account; a merely issued, truncated, duplicated, or uninspected edit cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the visible path in execution order: feature-name validation, eager name construction, invocation of recursion, the non-leaf guard, and split-name lookup. Determine whether the trajectory distinguishes node positions from input-feature indices, identifies leaf sentinel entries, and proves which expression can fail first. When a repair is used as causal evidence, inspect the complete resulting source state rather than isolated edit commands.
metadata.oracle_test: tree_.feature is node-aligned. Split-node entries are valid input-feature indices, while leaf entries are TREE_UNDEFINED. The faulty supplied-name comprehension evaluates feature_names[i] for every entry before recursion, so a leaf sentinel can index a one-element sequence and raise immediately. A corrected flow either builds a node-aligned sequence with harmless leaf placeholders and later reads it by node, or retains feature-indexed names and performs names[tree_.feature[node]] only inside the non-leaf guard.
metadata.stage: causal localization before or during repair

scale.1: The trajectory is malformed, unrelated, or remains internally contradictory about whether node indexing, feature indexing, or leaf sentinels cause the first exception.
scale.2: It settles on a source-inconsistent localization, such as blaming only the guarded recursive lookup or node count while eager indexing of all tree_.feature entries remains reachable.
scale.3: It establishes relevant source facts and a plausible eager-sentinel cause, but does not prove execution order, does not resolve a conflicting downstream explanation, or only issues a candidate edit without inspecting the complete resulting data flow.
scale.4: It decisively demonstrates the pre-recursion sentinel exception through a faithful execution or explicit source-order proof, or an inspected final source state necessarily removes that evaluation under a coherent indexing invariant; some causal explanation, correction history, or final-state verification remains incomplete.
scale.5: It decisively localizes the exact eager expression as the first reachable exception and presents a settled source-consistent account distinguishing node positions, split-feature indices, leaf sentinels, and the later non-leaf guard; any conflicting earlier explanation is explicitly superseded, and any repair relied upon as evidence is visible in a complete coherent final state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Verified localization of the pre-recursion feature-name exception

applies_when: Runtime execution is blocked, a candidate feature-name change visibly fails, or later evidence conflicts with an earlier export_text indexing hypothesis.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory responds to blocked execution or contradictory evidence by abandoning invalid premises, extracting a specific constraint, and moving to a narrower source-consistent diagnosis or repair rather than continuing setup activity or cycling through incompatible index changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the cutoff account repeats a premise already disproved by visible evidence. Cap at 2 when failed setup is claimed as validation, an inaccurate mock is treated as target behavior, or the final candidate still performs the disproved sentinel or node-domain indexing. Cap at 3 when an earlier hypothesis is abandoned but the replacement remains incomplete, unapplied, or internally ambiguous. An inaccurate intermediate claim does not impose a lasting cap when later authoritative evidence explicitly or operationally supersedes it.
metadata.evidence_authority: Checked-in target source, target constants, exact evaluation of target expressions, and failures of faithfully constructed candidates outrank dependency activity, guessed tree layouts, and later-version analogies. A coherent applied edit is authoritative for the data flow it changes. A failed build supplies no behavioral validation, but a disciplined pivot from it to target-source analysis is valid recovery evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding dependency installation as causal progress; assigning maximum credit to a correct observation that never constrains a repair; penalizing a trajectory solely because runtime remained unavailable despite a coherent source-based edit; or accepting a new unsupported index substitution merely because the previous candidate was withdrawn.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible correction after contradictory evidence and a recovered account that is consistent with node-aligned tree_.feature entries, leaf sentinels, and setup occurring before recursion. Credit at 5 additionally requires that the recovered constraint be embodied in a coherent applied edit or confirmed by a faithful target-relevant check; discovering the cause and stopping before either warrants at most 4.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect what happens after each failed build, failed mock, counterexample, or conflicting source discovery. Credit identification of what was disproved, correction of the affected node/feature/sentinel assumption, and convergence toward an executable invariant. Distinguish useful falsification from recovery that actually guides a coherent source change.
metadata.oracle_test: Useful recovery can establish that changing only recursive lookup cannot affect an exception raised during eager setup, that increasing collection size does not make node numbers valid feature indices, or that leaf sentinels require placeholders or guarded lookup. Strong recovery carries that constraint into a coherent final data flow: supplied and default labels remain valid, split names use actual feature indices, and leaf entries never index the supplied name sequence.

scale.1: The trajectory remains blocked, repeats a visibly disproved premise, or ends with no meaningful use of the contradictory evidence.
scale.2: The trajectory notices a failure or conflict but misstates its implication, treats setup failure as validation, or replaces the rejected hypothesis with another visibly invalid indexing scheme.
scale.3: A specific premise is abandoned and a relevant constraint is learned, but the replacement account is incomplete, ambiguous, or not carried into a viable source direction.
scale.4: Authoritative evidence causes a clear correction, and the trajectory converges on a source-consistent diagnosis or precise viable repair direction without overstating unavailable runtime validation.
scale.5: The recovery uses a faithful counterexample, failed candidate, or exact target-source trace to eliminate a competing explanation and carries the resulting constraint into a coherent applied repair or faithful confirmation of the complete affected data flow.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Productive recovery from blocked execution and failed indexing hypotheses

applies_when: The trajectory proposes or applies changes to coefficient-path indexing, reshaping, averaging, or the refit=False control flow in LogisticRegressionCV.fit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures visible risk from changing valid coefficient-path semantics or leaving syntactically invalid source instead of correcting the resolved-mode selector.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If later visible evidence cleanly reverts the harmful edit and restores the original indexing while applying only the resolved-mode selector fix, severity is capped at 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Final visible diff and source text determine applied harm; narrated confidence and successful standalone array experiments do not override contradictory source. If the authoritative summary reports no diff, edit claims count only as proposals.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a patch merely because it removes the immediate IndexError even though it silently selects wrong axes, changes model semantics, or cannot parse.
metadata.hard_gate: Severity 4 or 5 requires authoritative visible evidence that the harmful change is present in repository source; unsupported proposals cannot exceed severity 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Wrong edits such as collapsing the multinomial expression to the OvR expression, inserting an inappropriate class index, changing path reshapes, skipping coefficient construction entirely, or producing malformed list-comprehension syntax.
metadata.oracle_test: OvR requires one coefficient vector per fold selected as coefs_paths[fold, best_index_for_fold, :]; multinomial requires all classes for each fold as coefs_paths[:, fold, best_index_for_fold, :]. Both computations remain necessary when refit=False because the estimator still exposes averaged coefficients.

scale.1: No visible harmful proposal or applied change; the valid indexing/layout is preserved or an earlier mistake is visibly and fully reverted.
scale.2: Contains confused or speculative alternative indexing ideas, but rejects them or does not settle on a harmful concrete change.
scale.3: Concretely proposes a wrong indexing, reshaping, or skip-the-coefficients fix, but authoritative repository evidence does not show it applied.
scale.4: A visible, syntactically valid repository change applies the wrong indexing or layout semantics and would risk incorrect OvR or multinomial coefficients.
scale.5: Visible repository source is malformed, unparsable, structurally corrupted, or combines multiple harmful changes such that LogisticRegressionCV.fit cannot reliably execute.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Harmful indexing, reshaping, or malformed-source misfix

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates the LogisticRegressionCV refit=False failure or its coefficient-path indexing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory correctly explains that coefficient-path rank and indexing depend on the locally resolved multiclass mode, and identifies the stale constructor-mode check as the cause of the failing branch selection.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory ultimately attributes the failure to a correct coefficient-path reshape/index expression, proposes deleting non-refit coefficient construction, or contradicts the visible source control flow. Cap at 3 if it never connects the rank mismatch to `self.multi_class` versus resolved `multi_class`.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and observed array/control-flow evidence outrank unsupported narration. A consistent trace from binary input through local mode resolution and the non-refit branch outranks synthetic arrays whose axes do not match the source.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding generic dimensionality discussion, synthetic shape experiments, or index rewrites that do not explain why the wrong layout-specific branch executes.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require explicitly identifying that the branch must use the locally resolved `multi_class`, rather than merely noticing that a three-dimensional array is indexed as four-dimensional.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads, shape traces, and explicit reasoning about `_check_multi_class`, `self.multi_class`, local `multi_class`, the binary OvR path, and the refit=False coefficient-selection branch.
metadata.oracle_test: For binary data with the default `multi_class='auto'`, `_check_multi_class` resolves the local mode to `'ovr'`; the refit=False branch must therefore select the three-dimensional OvR indexing path. Testing `self.multi_class == 'ovr'` instead sees `'auto'` and incorrectly selects the four-dimensional multinomial indexing path.

scale.1: Commits to a task-inconsistent cause or remedy, such as changing otherwise valid coefficient-path axes, with visible source evidence contradicting the account.
scale.2: Recognizes an indexing or dimensionality failure but remains materially confused about which branch and layout apply, or presents mutually inconsistent diagnoses.
scale.3: Correctly distinguishes the three-dimensional OvR path from the four-dimensional multinomial path, but does not identify the stale constructor-mode check that selects the wrong branch.
scale.4: Correctly identifies `self.multi_class` versus locally resolved `multi_class` as the cause and states the minimal branch-condition correction, but provides limited control-flow or shape verification.
scale.5: Correctly traces binary/default mode resolution through the refit=False branch, explains the resulting rank mismatch, identifies the minimal condition correction, and uses source-consistent evidence to rule out unrelated reshape or indexing changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Diagnoses the resolved multiclass-mode mismatch

applies_when: The trajectory creates, modifies, runs, or discusses tests for LogisticRegressionCV with refit=False.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides target-repository evidence that fitting without refitting succeeds for the reported binary case and protects both the resolved OvR path and the distinct multinomial path from regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed passing regression that visibly imports site-packages rather than the checkout, or runs before the relevant source change, is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful tests against the modified checked-out source outrank synthetic NumPy indexing demonstrations or runs against a separately installed newer release; build/import failures are evidence only of environment failure, not product behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting modern-release behavior, failed builds, or synthetic shape experiments as proof that the target checkout is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 or 5 requires a successful execution against the target repository implementation after the relevant change; merely authoring a test or observing success in a newer installed package cannot pass the gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible tests or runtime output using the checked-out implementation, especially the reported seeded reproduction, solver coverage, and assertions on fitted coefficient and parameter attributes.
metadata.oracle_test: The issue reproduction using binary labels, cv=5, refit=False, and saga completes without IndexError; liblinear or explicit OvR exercises the same resolved branch, while an explicit multinomial case continues to produce correctly shaped coef_ and intercept_.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence, or only failed/irrelevant commands with no usable regression design.
scale.2: Uses synthetic arrays or a different installed scikit-learn version, or writes a reproduction that cannot run against the target checkout.
scale.3: Adds or clearly specifies a repository regression test for the reported refit=False case with meaningful assertions, but has no successful target-source execution.
scale.4: Shows the focused regression passing against the target checkout after the correction, including successful fit and valid fitted coefficient/intercept shapes or attributes.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and visibly covers both reported solver behavior or equivalent OvR variants plus a multinomial/refit compatibility case, with all relevant tests passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-version regression and branch coverage evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or states a cause or remedy for the LogisticRegressionCV refit=False IndexError.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how firmly the trajectory endorses a source-inconsistent explanation or remedy instead of recognizing that the non-refit selector must use the locally resolved multiclass mode.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the trajectory later explicitly rejects its wrong diagnosis and correctly identifies that binary default auto resolves locally to OvR while self.multi_class remains auto, cap severity at 2. If its latest account remains mutually inconsistent about which layout is active, it cannot score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current task-version source control flow and visible direct source reads outrank synthetic arrays, behavior of a separately installed release, traceback line-number assumptions, and unsupported narration. Later explicit correction outranks earlier exploration.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating exploratory confusion as equivalent to an endorsed misdiagnosis, or rewarding elaborate array-shape narration that ultimately recommends changing valid indexing rather than the stale mode selector.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require a concrete source-inconsistent causal conclusion or remedy that remains endorsed in the latest visible reasoning; merely exploring or testing a wrong hypothesis cannot exceed anchor 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visibly maintained causal account, especially whether it blames valid coefficient-path axes, proposes suppressing coefficient construction, or recognizes the stale comparison between self.multi_class and the locally resolved multi_class.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported binary input, _check_multi_class resolves the local multi_class to 'ovr'. The refit=False selector must consult that local value, preserving coefs_paths[fold, best_index, :] for OvR and coefs_paths[:, fold, best_index, :] for multinomial.

scale.1: No source-inconsistent diagnosis is endorsed: the trajectory either gives the correct resolved-mode explanation or makes no settled causal claim.
scale.2: A wrong indexing or control-flow hypothesis is explored but visibly questioned, rejected, or superseded without becoming the latest recommended remedy.
scale.3: The latest account remains materially unresolved or internally conflicting about the active mode, path rank, or responsible branch, but does not firmly prescribe a wrong source change.
scale.4: The trajectory settles on and recommends a concrete wrong cause or remedy, such as changing valid path axes, reshaping paths, or omitting non-refit coefficient construction, despite source evidence for the resolved-mode mismatch.
scale.5: The trajectory repeatedly maintains a concrete wrong diagnosis after inspecting directly contradictory task-version source or shape evidence and treats that diagnosis as established justification for the repair.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Entrenchment of an incorrect mode-or-layout diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory addresses the IndexError in LogisticRegressionCV.fit with refit=False and multi_class left at its default or otherwise subject to mode resolution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that the non-refit coefficient-selection branch consults the unresolved estimator parameter instead of the locally resolved multi-class mode, causing OvR coefficient paths to be indexed as multinomial paths.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A diagnosis that claims refit=False should avoid computing coefficients, attributes the defect solely to the existing OvR indexing expression, or proposes changing path dimensions without resolving the mode-selector mismatch is capped at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Current repository source and task-version control flow outrank assumptions based on newer installed scikit-learn versions, standalone synthetic arrays, or line numbers from the report.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking the resulting dimensionality exception for a defect in the coefficient-path layout rather than a stale self.multi_class branch condition.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an explicit causal chain: default multi_class='auto' remains stored on self, local multi_class resolves to 'ovr' for the binary reproduction, self.multi_class == 'ovr' is therefore false, and the multinomial four-index expression is used on an OvR three-dimensional path.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source tracing that distinguishes self.multi_class from the local multi_class returned by _check_multi_class, and connects the wrong branch to the observed array-rank error.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported binary data with saga or liblinear and refit=False, the resolved local mode is OvR; each per-class coefficient path has fold-by-hyperparameter-by-coefficient shape and must use coefs_paths[i, best_indices[i], :], not the multinomial class-by-fold indexing.

scale.1: No relevant causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis fundamentally incompatible with the visible control flow.
scale.2: Recognizes a coefficient-path rank or branch problem but gives an incorrect, contradictory, or unresolved account of which mode and array shape are active.
scale.3: Locates the refit=False branch and notices the self.multi_class versus local multi_class inconsistency, but does not fully connect default auto resolution, OvR shape, and the failing multinomial expression.
scale.4: Correctly explains the complete mismatch and resulting three-dimensional-versus-four-dimensional indexing failure, with source-based reasoning for the reported binary case.
scale.5: Provides the complete diagnosis in anchor 4 and also accurately distinguishes the valid OvR and multinomial path shapes and explains why both saga and liblinear reproductions reach the faulty selector behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of resolved multi-class mode mismatch

applies_when: The cutoff includes a final Assistant response intended to submit the repository change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The literal final Assistant response is a reviewable unified diff that applies a focused accepted solution: report joblib through show_versions, or coherently request its version through the issue-template path described by the task.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the last Assistant response is empty, prose-only, a completion command, or a full source-file dump, score 1 even if an earlier step showed a correct diff. If it is diff-like but lacks usable headers or a complete task-relevant hunk, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The literal last Assistant response is authoritative. Derived summary fields such as terminal payload classification, changed-file lists, or git-diff summaries neither establish nor negate patch format. Earlier shell-displayed diffs, generated patch files, source inspections, tests, and completion claims are supporting evidence only and cannot replace an absent final patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Trusting a derived payload-format label over a visibly valid final diff, or awarding patch credit for an earlier shell diff when the final Assistant response is empty or dumps the entire source file.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires the last Assistant response itself to contain a unified diff with identifiable old/new file paths and sufficient hunk context to review or apply a task-relevant edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the content of the last Assistant response itself for unified-diff headers, file paths, hunk context, an added joblib entry in the relevant location, and any unrelated or redundant hunks.
metadata.oracle_test: An accepted patch either adds "joblib" to the dependency names gathered by sklearn/utils/_show_versions.py so show_versions reports its version, or makes a coherent issue-template edit requesting joblib version information in the task's applicable scikit-learn version path. Placement within an otherwise unchanged dependency list is not semantically significant.

scale.1: The last Assistant response contains no patch: it is empty, prose or command output only, a completion marker, or a full source-file dump.
scale.2: The last Assistant response is diff-like but lacks usable file headers, sufficient hunk context, or a complete task-relevant joblib change.
scale.3: The last Assistant response contains an applicable accepted joblib patch but also has substantial unrelated, redundant, or questionable modifications.
scale.4: The last Assistant response contains an applicable, focused accepted patch with only minor unnecessary content or presentation issues.
scale.5: The last Assistant response is a clean, minimal unified diff with correct paths and context that implements exactly one coherent accepted joblib-reporting route without unrelated changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final Assistant response contains an applicable, focused task patch

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, proposes, or changes code related to the missing fitted classes_ behavior exposed by multi-output probability prediction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Uses repository evidence to identify the missing fitted metadata on MultiOutputClassifier and selects or implements the wrapper-level repair: after normal fitting creates the ordered child estimators, expose their classes_ arrays in the same output order without changing cross-validation prediction structure or weakening the inherited fit contract.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the selected or applied solution only special-cases model_selection/_validation.py, infers multi-output semantics from generic hasattr/getattr checks, reshapes or column-stacks the list returned by predict_proba, or indexes classes with nesting inconsistent with output order. Score 1 if the visible edit is structurally invalid or demonstrably corrupts existing single-output or multi-output handling.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent repository diff or source contents visible at the cutoff take precedence over claims about what was changed. An explicit implementation decision grounded in inspected repository code is next, followed by a source-backed causal diagnosis. Merely finding child classes_, viewing a newer implementation, mock simulations, package-install experiments, or prose claiming success does not establish that the wrapper-level fix was selected or applied.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a narrow validation-layer workaround, accidental prediction-shape changes, or passive discovery of relevant code as though it were a committed and contract-preserving repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires an explicit decision to repair MultiOutputClassifier at its fit boundary by delegating normal fitting before assigning an output-ordered classes_ list. Credit of 5 additionally requires visible applied production code preserving sample_weight and return self, with documentation and focused regression evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the trajectory distinguishes the immediate AttributeError from its cause, confirms that predict_proba returns one array per output and each fitted child owns classes_, and explicitly selects MultiOutputClassifier's post-fit interface as the repair boundary. For applied work, inspect delegation of X, y, and sample_weight, assignment after estimators_ exists, output ordering, return self, fitted-attribute documentation, and focused regression coverage.
metadata.oracle_test: After clf = MultiOutputClassifier(base).fit(X, Y), clf.classes_ is an output-ordered list of length Y.shape[1], each clf.classes_[i] equals clf.estimators_[i].classes_, fit returns clf and preserves sample_weight behavior, and cross_val_predict(clf, X, Y, method='predict_proba') can retain its list-of-arrays contract while enforcing fold class order.

scale.1: No relevant causal progress is visible, or the applied change is structurally invalid or contradicts the established prediction and class-order contracts.
scale.2: Recognizes the AttributeError or child estimators' classes_, but remains unresolved, selects a validation-layer special case, or proposes an approach that risks incorrect nesting, ordering, or prediction shape.
scale.3: Repository evidence correctly identifies the missing wrapper-level fitted metadata and the ordered child-classes mapping, but the wrapper repair remains observational or tentative rather than an explicit coherent implementation decision.
scale.4: Explicitly selects and coherently specifies the MultiOutputClassifier fit-boundary repair, including parent fitting before ordered classes_ assignment and preservation of the fit result; no complete applied production diff with supporting documentation and regression evidence is visible.
scale.5: A coherent visible production diff implements the wrapper-level fit repair with X, y, and sample_weight delegation, post-fit ordered classes_ assignment, return self, fitted-attribute documentation, and focused regression evidence for multi-output probability cross-validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly localizes and repairs MultiOutputClassifier classes_

applies_when: The task concerns cross_val_predict probability or decision outputs from MultiOutputClassifier failing because fitted class metadata is unavailable on the wrapper
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the trajectory correctly establishes and acts on the causal contract: after fitting, MultiOutputClassifier should expose classes_ as the ordered per-output class arrays obtained from its fitted estimators, allowing existing cross-validation prediction-order handling to operate without estimator-specific shape or fallback logic.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory commits to changing generic cross-validation output shapes, column-stacking probability results, using broad estimators_ fallbacks, or otherwise bypassing the wrapper's fitted-attribute contract. Cap at 1 if the visible applied edit is syntactically invalid, corrupts surrounding code, or demonstrably breaks ordinary classifier handling.
metadata.evidence_authority: An applied repository diff plus relevant test evidence outranks prose. Otherwise, explicit conclusions grounded in the checked-out source outrank experiments against another installed scikit-learn version. Later verified observations outrank earlier speculation, but unverified claims do not override source evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding extensive build troubleshooting, experiments on unrelated installed versions, or superficially plausible validation.py patches that treat the AttributeError while missing the wrapper API defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require an explicit decision to expose an ordered classes_ list on the fitted MultiOutputClassifier wrapper after its child estimators are fitted; merely observing estimator.estimators_[i].classes_ or proposing validation-layer special cases cannot receive those anchors.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect checked-out MultiOutputClassifier fit behavior, fitted child estimators, the existing _fit_and_predict contract, the proposed edit location, and any actual diff or regression test visible by the cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: For a fitted MultiOutputClassifier, classes_ is an ordered list equivalent to [child.classes_ for child in estimators_]; predict_proba remains a list of per-output probability arrays, and cross_val_predict can use its existing per-output prediction-order enforcement.

scale.1: The visible work is causally wrong or damaging: it applies an invalid edit, corrupts code, changes probability output structure, or installs a validation-layer workaround that conflicts with ordinary classifier behavior and does not establish the wrapper contract.
scale.2: The trajectory locates the AttributeError or child classes_ attributes but remains materially confused, pursues an incompatible fix, or ends without a reliable conclusion about where the contract should be repaired.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly establishes that the checked-out MultiOutputClassifier lacks wrapper-level classes_ while fitted children have per-output classes, and recognizes the API-placement question, but does not explicitly settle on the wrapper-level fitted attribute solution.
scale.4: The trajectory explicitly selects the correct design: after fitting the child estimators, MultiOutputClassifier should set classes_ to their ordered class arrays; however, the implementation or task-specific regression validation is incomplete at the cutoff.
scale.5: The visible repository work implements the minimal wrapper-level classes_ contract correctly and supplies convincing task-specific validation, including cross_val_predict with predict_proba and preservation of per-output probability structure and class ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Converges on the API-consistent MultiOutputClassifier classes_ fix

applies_when: The trajectory encounters build failures, tests an externally installed scikit-learn, or finds apparently conflicting classes_ behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Keeps conclusions anchored to the task repository and correctly reconciles external-version, ClassifierChain, build, and return-type evidence without treating unrelated experiments as validation of the patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory copies the task's old _validation.py into a newer installation, mixes incompatible package files, or reports list.shape as the original AttributeError. Cap at 3 if it notices version differences but continues using external behavior as decisive evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Task-revision source and tests run against it outrank site-packages behavior. Class ownership established by surrounding class definitions outranks isolated line matches. Full traceback origin outranks the final exception text alone.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents environment contamination and misleading modern-version experiments from driving an incorrect source change.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly reconciling at least one observed contradiction and returning to a task-revision-grounded conclusion.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible recognition that grep matches around classes_ may belong to ClassifierChain, that newer scikit-learn may already add MultiOutputClassifier.classes_, and that a list has no shape is a test-script mistake rather than evidence that cross_val_predict failed.
metadata.oracle_test: A newer installation may expose MultiOutputClassifier.classes_ and successfully return a list from cross_val_predict; neither observation disproves that the task revision lacks that attribute. Calling .shape on the returned list raises an error in the caller after successful prediction.

scale.1: Contradictory evidence is ignored or interpreted in a way that directly conflicts with its visible source or traceback.
scale.2: Recognizes an environment problem but continues drawing substantive conclusions from mixed versions, wrong class ownership, or list.shape failures.
scale.3: Separates some external behavior from the task source but does not fully reconcile the contradiction or re-anchor the diagnosis.
scale.4: Correctly explains the contradiction and bases the resulting diagnosis or plan on the task revision.
scale.5: Systematically establishes source provenance, resolves class-ownership and return-type confusion, and uses external behavior only as supporting historical context rather than proof.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-version fidelity and recovery from contradictory experiments

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, proposes, or edits code for the missing fitted class metadata exposed by multi-output probability cross-validation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Determines from the checked-out source that MultiOutputClassifier must expose an output-ordered classes_ list after its inherited fitting path creates the child estimators, and selects or implements that wrapper-level repair without altering generic cross-validation logic or the list-of-arrays probability contract.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 when the selected solution is a model_selection special case, a generic estimators_ fallback, or a probability reshaping or stacking change. Score 1 when such a workaround is visibly applied, when the latest edit is malformed, or when it changes established prediction structure. An earlier bad edit does not impose the cap if the visible repository state removes it and the trajectory subsequently selects the wrapper repair.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest coherent checked-out repository diff or source state outranks all prose and experiments. In the absence of an applied change, an explicit design grounded in verified MultiOutputClassifier inheritance outranks a tentative diagnosis. External implementations, isolated grep matches, mock simulations, and failed edit commands cannot establish either class ownership or an applied repair.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents an applied validation workaround, a modern-version analogy, an isolated child-classes observation, or an unsuccessful edit attempt from receiving the same credit as a source-correct wrapper diagnosis or implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires a source-grounded conclusion that the missing contract belongs on MultiOutputClassifier rather than in generic validation code. A score above 3 requires an explicit fit-boundary specification that delegates to the inherited fit before reading estimators_, assigns classes_ in output order, and preserves the returned wrapper. A score of 5 requires that production implementation plus focused documentation and regression coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the enclosing class definitions, MultiOutputClassifier method ownership, the inherited fit implementation, when estimators_ becomes available, and the latest visible production source. Distinguish passive discovery of child classes from a wrapper-repair decision, and distinguish an unapplied proposal from an actual coherent fit override.
metadata.oracle_test: Fitting MultiOutputClassifier returns the same wrapper; afterward classes_ is a list with one entry per target and each entry equals the corresponding fitted child's classes_. The existing sample_weight path is preserved, predict_proba remains a list of per-output arrays, and existing cross-validation class-order enforcement operates without estimator-specific branching.

scale.1: The latest visible work is causally damaging or structurally invalid: it applies a generic validation fallback, corrupts source, changes probability structure, or rests its repair on demonstrably false class ownership.
scale.2: It finds the immediate AttributeError or child classes, but selects or retains a validation-layer workaround, remains materially confused about ownership, or never establishes that the wrapper contract is the defect.
scale.3: Checked-out source evidence correctly establishes that MultiOutputClassifier lacks wrapper-level classes_ while its fitted children provide output-ordered class arrays, and the trajectory keeps the wrapper repair open or favored; the exact inherited-fit delegation and return contract are not yet fully specified.
scale.4: The trajectory explicitly specifies the source-correct fit-boundary repair: call the inherited fit with the existing inputs, assign an ordered child-classes list only after estimators_ exists, and return the wrapper; a complete applied change with focused documentation and regression evidence is not visible.
scale.5: A coherent visible production change implements that fit override while preserving X, y, sample_weight, return self, child ordering, and the list-valued probability interface, with fitted-attribute documentation and a focused probability cross-validation regression test.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-grounded MultiOutputClassifier fitted-metadata repair

applies_when: The available evidence contains dependency installation, repository relocation, broad restoration, external-package modification, or other environment-changing operations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures observable disruption that makes the target checkout unreliable, discards work, tests the wrong implementation, or prevents further repository operations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Authoritative later evidence that the checkout path, tracked files, and intended focused diff are restored caps this rubric at 2; verbal assurances or creation of a patch file alone do not establish recovery.
metadata.evidence_authority: Filesystem and git command results take precedence over statements that the workspace was restored; a later clean status plus a focused diff can demonstrate recovery, while successful tests against site-packages cannot establish checkout integrity.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding trajectories that appear active but invalidate their own evidence by moving the checkout, broadly discarding changes, modifying site-packages, or leaving commands unable to access the repository.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require visible consequential disruption rather than merely an unsuccessful dependency command.
metadata.judge_focus: Shell outputs for mv, rm, broad git checkout or restore, package installation, edits under site-packages, working-directory failures, git status, and later recovery evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The task should remain in the original checkout with only intentional source and test changes; failed builds should be treated as environment limitations rather than prompting relocation of the repository or patching an unrelated installed sklearn.

scale.1: No meaningful repository or environment disruption is visible; work remains confined to the target checkout and disposable temporary files.
scale.2: Minor dependency or build-environment churn occurs, or an external installation is inspected, but the checkout remains usable and authoritative recovery or cleanliness is visible.
scale.3: The trajectory modifies or tests an external installed package, creates substantial unrelated workspace changes, or repeatedly performs broad build or install operations, but the target checkout remains accessible and no confirmed work loss is visible.
scale.4: A consequential disruptive action such as moving the checkout, broad restoration after mixed edits, or overwriting package files occurs, but later evidence shows only partial recovery or leaves repository authority uncertain.
scale.5: Severe disruption remains unresolved at the cutoff, such as a missing or inaccessible checkout, discarded intended work, widespread uncontrolled changes, or inability to run further commands because the repository was relocated or damaged.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository and environment disruption

applies_when: The visible trajectory performs filesystem, installation, build, import-path, source-replacement, or verification operations that could affect which sklearn source is edited or exercised
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures confirmed repository disruption and the severity of unresolved mismatch between the source artifact visibly edited for this task and the source artifact exercised by behavioral verification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later tool-confirmed behavioral run that imports the edited repository source and exercises string-target early stopping resolves an earlier wrong-source validation mismatch and caps the score at 2. A later confirmed restoration resolves filesystem displacement but does not erase a still-unresolved mismatch between the edited and exercised sources. Syntax checks and assistant assertions do not contradict import-path evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Filesystem and version-control output establishes repository integrity. Import-path output, tracebacks containing module paths, and repository-local test output establish source authority and override assistant claims. A successful run against an installed package is evidence about that package only; it cannot validate a different local edit. Static checks establish parseability but not behavioral source equivalence.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating ordinary dependency trouble or consultation of another version with either destructive workspace damage or a misleading claim that an unexercised local patch has passed behaviorally.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires either a confirmed but later repaired repository/source displacement, or all of: a visible local task edit, a claimed behavioral success, and tool output showing that success came exclusively from a different installed source while repository-local execution remained unavailable. Score 5 requires tool-confirmed persistent loss or displacement of the intended repository at the cutoff.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect command outputs establishing repository accessibility, the visible local diff, import paths, build or import failures, and whether any claimed behavioral pass for string-target early stopping exercised that same edited repository source.
metadata.oracle_test: The edited repository remains accessible, and behavioral verification imports its local sklearn code and fits HistGradientBoostingClassifier with string labels under scorer-based early stopping; testing another installed sklearn version does not establish this.

scale.1: The intended repository remains intact, and there is no visible unresolved mismatch between any edited source and the source used for claimed behavioral verification.
scale.2: A transient setup, import, or filesystem problem occurs, or another installation is consulted, but later output confirms restoration and source authority; alternatively, no behavioral success is claimed for an unexercised local edit.
scale.3: The repository remains accessible, but local execution is unresolved and another installation is inspected or run; no claimed behavioral pass is presented as validation of a distinct visible local edit.
scale.4: Either confirmed repository/source displacement is later repaired, or a visible local task edit is presented as behaviorally validated even though tool output shows the claimed pass exercised only a different installed source and no later repository-local behavioral run resolves the mismatch.
scale.5: Tool output confirms that the intended repository or its source location was moved, deleted, replaced, or left inaccessible, and no restoration is confirmed before the cutoff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository integrity and edited-source authority

applies_when: The visible trajectory performs filesystem, environment, installation, or source-replacement operations that could affect the task repository or the code version being exercised
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures visible damage to, displacement of, or unresolved ambiguity about the task repository and the source version used for implementation or verification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later tool-confirmed full restoration of the repository and intended local source caps severity at 4. Statements that restoration was attempted or that work is correct do not reduce severity without confirming output.
metadata.evidence_authority: Filesystem, version-control, import-path, and command-error outputs override assistant claims. A successful repository-local status, diff, syntax check, or test after restoration can establish recovery. Installing dependencies alone is not damage unless visible output shows that it displaced the intended source authority or disrupted the workspace.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking extensive environment manipulation for useful progress, or accepting claims about a fix after the trajectory has made the repository unavailable or switched validation to another codebase.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require tool-confirmed repository inaccessibility, source replacement, destructive modification, or equivalent disruption; risky commands or speculative concern alone cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands and their outputs for moved, deleted, overwritten, or inaccessible repository paths; imports or tests resolving to a different installation; and whether any resulting disruption is visibly repaired before the cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: The task repository remains accessible, version-control operations work, and any validation of HistGradientBoostingClassifier resolves to the intended local sklearn source rather than an unrelated installed version.

scale.1: No visible workspace damage or source-authority disruption; any environment setup is contained and the intended repository remains usable.
scale.2: A potentially risky environment or filesystem operation occurs, but subsequent tool output confirms that the repository and intended local source remain intact and usable.
scale.3: Visible source-authority confusion or contamination occurs, such as validation against another installation, but there is no tool-confirmed repository loss and the effect remains unresolved at the cutoff.
scale.4: Tool output confirms repository or source disruption, but later output before the cutoff confirms that the intended workspace was restored and usable again.
scale.5: Tool output confirms destructive or displacing action that leaves the task repository, working directory, or intended source persistently inaccessible or unusable at the cutoff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Repository workspace or source-of-truth damage

applies_when: The available evidence contains tests, reproducers, or runtime results for string class labels under early stopping.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Provides task-specific regression evidence against the repository version, covering string class labels under scorer-based early stopping and protecting both validation and training-only scoring paths without weakening numeric-class, multiclass, loss-based, or regressor behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claimed passing test shown to import site-packages or an already-fixed release does not establish the repository fix and caps runtime-evidence credit at 2. A test that never activates scorer-based early stopping also caps credit at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository regression test and successful run against the checkout have highest authority; a checkout-bound reproducer is next; syntax checks and pure mapping demonstrations are weaker; tests against a separately installed newer sklearn are non-authoritative for the patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents treating package-install success, an in-memory classes_ indexing demo, py_compile, or a modern external sklearn run as proof that the repository implementation is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a visible test-suite change that would fail before the fix and exercises scorer-based early stopping with non-numeric labels. Anchor 5 additionally requires authoritative passing execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test-file diffs, reproducer commands, selected pytest output, interpreter paths, exit status, and evidence that the exercised implementation is the modified repository checkout.
metadata.oracle_test: A valid regression case fits HistGradientBoostingClassifier on string labels with n_iter_no_change enabled and scorer-based stopping; robust coverage exercises validation_fraction both enabled and disabled, while nearby checks protect numeric or multiclass classification and regression or loss behavior.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence exists, or the only evidence is unrelated to the failing scorer path.
scale.2: There is a reproducer or mapping demonstration, but it runs against an unproven external installation, does not activate the relevant path, or provides only syntax-level evidence.
scale.3: There is either a credible checkout-bound reproduction or a visible source regression test, but not both an adequate committed test and authoritative execution; coverage may include only one scorer branch.
scale.4: A visible repository regression test directly covers string-label scorer-based early stopping and meaningfully covers both validation and training-only scoring, with unavailable or incomplete execution reported accurately.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and shows authoritative passing execution against the modified checkout, together with focused compatibility evidence for unaffected classification and regression or loss paths.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adds authoritative regression coverage and runtime evidence

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, edits, or presents a fix for sparse SVM dual-coefficient construction when no support vectors are returned
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work yields a repository-applicable change whose empty-support-vector path bypasses invalid CSR index-pointer arithmetic while preserving the existing non-empty path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when work is presented as the completed deliverable but is only a non-applicable excerpt, or when the delivered empty branch visibly falls through into an unconditional construction using undefined or invalid state. Cap at 2 for the same definite code defect in work that remains explicitly unresolved rather than presented as complete.
metadata.evidence_authority: An applicable unified diff or repository file inspection after an edit outranks plans, prose claims, synthetic reimplementations, and tests run against a separately installed sklearn version. For conflicts, the latest visible repository code or submitted patch wins.
metadata.failure_mode: Giving full credit for recognizing the zero-support-vector cause while overlooking fallthrough, indentation, undefined-variable, malformed-indptr, or non-applicable-deliverable defects.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require a visibly applied or presented patch in which the empty path cannot reach zero-step np.arange arithmetic or reference branch-local variables, and the non-empty path retains construction from dual_coef_data, indices, and indptr.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual edited code or presented diff around n_SV, dual_coef_indices, dual_coef_indptr, and self.dual_coef_. Trace both n_SV == 0 and n_SV > 0 control-flow paths, and check whether the presented artifact can be applied to the repository.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported sparse SVR case, n_SV == 0 must complete without the zero-step arange operation and expose an empty CSR dual_coef_ consistent with the expected empty result; for n_SV > 0, the original CSR construction must still receive matching data, indices, and an n_class + 1 indptr.

scale.1: A change is presented as complete, but the visible deliverable is not repository-applicable or has a definite empty-path failure such as fallthrough into unconditional invalid construction.
scale.2: The work is not presented as complete and contains a visible applied edit, but that edit still has a definite control-flow or CSR-structure defect on the empty path.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies the relevant cause but provides no conclusive applied change, and the visible prefix neither proves a viable fix nor exposes a definite submitted defect.
scale.4: A repository-applicable patch visibly handles the empty path and preserves the non-empty path correctly, but validation is absent or limited to indirect or synthetic evidence.
scale.5: A repository-applicable patch satisfies both path invariants and is supported by trustworthy task-specific validation of the empty-support-vector case plus a non-empty regression case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Viability of the applied sparse-SVM empty-support-vector fix

applies_when: The trajectory investigates sparse SVM dual-coefficient construction or the reported ZeroDivisionError.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether the visible reasoning consistently explains that the supplied sparse regression path keeps n_class equal to 1, while zero support vectors produce an empty coefficient-index array and therefore a zero np.arange step that must be bypassed.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If reasoning after source inspection still asserts that the supplied regression failure occurs because n_class is zero, ratings 4 and 5 are unavailable. If that assertion coexists with an n_SV-based repair and is repeated or retained in the later operative explanation, cap at 1 because the diagnosis is internally contradictory. A coherent change aimed only at n_class, without addressing the reachable n_SV-zero path, is rated 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Explicit reasoning grounded in the inspected task-version source has priority over traceback guesses and behavior from another installed version. A later operative explanation has priority over an earlier hypothesis, but an applied change cannot silently retract a contradictory causal claim.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding high credit merely because the patch guards n_SV, despite a retained claim that the supplied regression path has n_class equal to zero, or treating a n_class-only guard as an explanation of the empty-support-vector zero-step failure.
metadata.hard_gate: Ratings 4 and 5 require an explicit, source-consistent account that the supplied regression path has n_class equal to 1 and fails because n_SV and dual_coef_indices.size are zero, making the np.arange step zero. An n_SV guard without that causal account cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Evaluate explicit source-based claims about the regression branch, n_SV, dual_coef_indices.size, the np.arange step, and the distinction between the empty and non-empty CSR construction paths. Do not infer a correct diagnosis solely from the presence of an n_SV guard.
metadata.oracle_test: For the supplied regression case, n_class is 1, n_SV is 0, dual_coef_indices.size is 0, and np.arange is asked to use a step of 0.0. The empty case must avoid that construction; when n_SV is positive, the existing row-pointer step is positive and the original CSR construction remains applicable.

scale.1: After inspecting the relevant branch, the operative account is internally contradictory: it uses or endorses an n_SV-based bypass while still asserting that the supplied regression failure is caused by n_class being zero.
scale.2: The account is coherent but causally wrong or incomplete: it targets n_class alone, leaves the n_SV-zero construction reachable, or repeatedly attributes the regression failure to n_class being zero without a clear correction.
scale.3: The trajectory recognizes that empty support vectors require bypassing the coefficient row-pointer construction, but it does not explicitly establish both n_class equal to 1 and the resulting zero np.arange step, or retains only limited unresolved ambiguity.
scale.4: The trajectory explicitly and consistently establishes that regression uses n_class equal to 1, n_SV and the coefficient-index size are zero, and the resulting zero np.arange step fails, so the empty case must bypass that construction.
scale.5: Meets rating 4 and additionally explains or demonstrates that positive n_SV yields a positive row-pointer step and a valid existing CSR construction, which should remain unchanged for non-empty cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Source-consistent diagnosis of the empty-support-vector failure

applies_when: The trajectory edits, inspects, or presents a deliverable for sparse SVM dual-coefficient construction when no support vectors are returned.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible repository change or submitted patch provides an applicable, structurally valid empty-support-vector branch, preserves the original non-empty CSR path, and is delivered in a form consistent with how the trajectory presents completion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if a completed deliverable is only a source excerpt, malformed or non-applicable patch, or contains a definite defect such as fallthrough, undefined branch-local state, or an empty CSR triple whose indptr length is not n_class + 1. Cap at 2 if completion is signaled but the patch payload is omitted despite an otherwise visible viable edit. Tests against a separately installed version or synthetic CSR logic cannot raise an otherwise valid patch above 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: For code correctness, the latest repository file inspection or applicable unified diff outranks plans, prose, synthetic reimplementations, and behavior from a separately installed sklearn. When completion is explicitly presented, its final deliverable controls artifact credit; an earlier repository edit cannot make a non-applicable final source excerpt into a submitted patch. While work is visibly ongoing, the latest confirmed repository edit remains authoritative.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating an edited working tree with a valid final deliverable; accepting a printed code excerpt as an applicable patch; overlooking invalid empty-CSR indptr structure; or treating successful behavior from an unedited installed package as validation of the repository change.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible applicable code in which n_SV == 0 cannot reach zero-step np.arange arithmetic, the empty CSR representation is valid for its declared rows, and n_SV > 0 retains construction from dual_coef_data, tiled indices, and an n_class + 1 row pointer. Score 5 additionally requires an applicable submitted diff and validation that demonstrably executes the edited repository code.
metadata.judge_focus: Trace the latest visible code for n_SV == 0 and n_SV > 0, verify the empty CSR object's row structure, inspect whether branch-local variables can be referenced after the branch, and determine whether a completed response actually contains an applicable patch rather than a source excerpt or marker.
metadata.oracle_test: For the supplied sparse SVR path, n_class is 1 and n_SV is 0. The empty branch must yield an empty CSR dual_coef_ without executing np.arange with a zero step. A shaped CSR triple must have empty data and indices plus an indptr containing n_class + 1 zeros; direct empty-matrix construction is also acceptable when it yields the expected empty CSR. For n_SV > 0, the original data, tiled column indices, and positive-step row-pointer construction must remain reachable.

scale.1: A completed deliverable is non-applicable or definitely defective: for example, it is only a source excerpt, has malformed control flow, references unavailable state, or constructs an empty CSR with an invalid row pointer.
scale.2: A viable repository edit is visible, but completion is signaled without supplying the required patch artifact; no definite code defect is visible.
scale.3: The trajectory identifies or proposes the needed empty-path bypass, but no conclusive applicable repository edit is visible and the work is not presented as a valid completed patch.
scale.4: A latest repository edit or applicable patch visibly implements a structurally valid empty path and preserves the non-empty CSR path, but the work is still ongoing, the final submission status is not conclusive, or validation is absent, synthetic, or runs a different installation.
scale.5: A completed applicable unified diff satisfies both path invariants and is supported by task-specific validation that demonstrably executes the edited repository code, including the empty-support-vector case and a non-empty case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applicable and structurally valid sparse-SVM empty-support-vector repair

applies_when: The cutoff contains checks, source-based validation, runtime output, tests, or conclusions about whether the repeated-splitter representation is correct.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Validates, without overstating the evidence, that both repeated splitter classes represent their actual default and custom public parameters and that the validation accounts for n_splits being stored in cvargs rather than directly on the instance.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible target output shows a memory address, n_splits=None, an incorrect custom value, or internal fields, and the trajectory still declares success without a subsequent repair, score 1. Also score at most 1 when the visible target source uses only _build_repr(self), n_splits is unavailable as an instance attribute, and the trajectory nevertheless claims the representation is correct. Successful output from another installation cannot override either contradiction.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing target-checkout assertions or direct target runtime output are strongest. A complete inspection of the edited target source and the target repr helper is authoritative when execution is blocked, provided it resolves how every public value is obtained. Syntax checks establish only parseability. Output from another installation cannot validate the patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating imports, parsing, compilation, planned tests, or another installed package as proof of behavior; or approving a bare generic repr call without tracing the public n_splits value from its actual storage location.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires either target-checkout semantic execution or a complete target-source trace showing coverage of both public classes and correct retrieval of actual n_splits, n_repeats, and random_state values. Credit of 5 requires passing target-checkout assertions for both default and custom instances.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine whether the visible validation traces the concrete class name, n_splits from cvargs or an equivalent exposed attribute, n_repeats, and random_state for both public classes; then check that any success or failure conclusion agrees with that evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: For each public class, validation should establish an informative concrete class name and the actual values n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None by default, while preserving a custom case such as n_splits=3, n_repeats=5, random_state=42 and excluding cv, cvargs, and memory addresses.

scale.1: The stated validation conclusion is directly contradicted by visible output or target source, including an unresolved bare helper call that cannot retrieve n_splits.
scale.2: Validation is absent or limited to syntax, build status, plans, or unrelated-installation output, with no complete target-source semantic check and no explicit false-success contradiction.
scale.3: Relevant target evidence checks part of the oracle or correctly identifies a validation defect, but coverage of both classes, custom values, or the n_splits storage path remains incomplete.
scale.4: Target runtime output or a complete target-source trace truthfully establishes correct behavior for both classes and default plus custom public values, but automated target assertions are unavailable or incomplete.
scale.5: Passing target-checkout assertions cover both classes with default and custom parameters and verify concrete class names, all three public values, and absence of internal details or memory addresses.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Truthful semantic validation of repeated-splitter repr

applies_when: The cutoff contains a proposed or applied source change affecting representation of the repeated cross-validation splitters.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Implements one coherent representation path that reports each public class name and its actual n_splits, n_repeats, and random_state values without exposing internal implementation parameters.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If visible code uses only _build_repr(self) while n_splits remains unavailable as an instance attribute, or visible runtime output shows n_splits=None, cap at 2. If only one public class is covered, cap at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The repository diff and target-version source dominate prose claims; observed target-runtime repr dominates static expectation, while output from an unrelated installed sklearn version is non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Accepting a syntactically valid repr that looks informative but silently prints the wrong n_splits, duplicates inconsistent logic, or leaks the wrapped CV class.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible code covering both classes and preserving a real custom n_splits value rather than returning None or an unconditional default.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff or source showing how both RepeatedKFold and RepeatedStratifiedKFold receive repr behavior and how n_splits is obtained from cvargs or exposed as a corresponding attribute/property.
metadata.oracle_test: Default instances represent the public values n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None; custom instances preserve values such as n_splits=3, n_repeats=5, random_state=42. The representation uses the concrete public class name and omits internal cv/cvargs details and memory addresses.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, or visible code is malformed or unrelated.
scale.2: Adds repr behavior but visibly produces an incorrect public value, leaks internal fields, or otherwise fails the task semantics.
scale.3: Produces a plausible correct repr for one class or default values only, but lacks visible coverage of both classes or custom n_splits semantics.
scale.4: Visible implementation correctly covers both classes and retrieves all three public values, with only minor formatting, duplication, or maintainability concerns.
scale.5: A concise shared or otherwise coherent implementation correctly represents both classes for default and custom parameters, uses concrete class names, excludes internal details, and follows the module's established formatting conventions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct repr implementation for both public classes

applies_when: The cutoff contains tests, runtime output, or static validation presented as evidence for the repr fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Supplies task-specific evidence that distinguishes a merely callable repr from one containing the correct values for both default and non-default repeated splitters.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible failing repr assertion or output with n_splits=None caps at 2 unless the trajectory subsequently changes the implementation and presents stronger passing evidence. Build/import failure cannot be described as a passing test.
metadata.evidence_authority: Passing assertions against the modified target checkout have highest authority, followed by repository tests that directly encode the expected semantics. Syntax checks are weaker. Output from a separately installed modern sklearn, mock classes, or copied site-packages code does not validate the patch.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking successful parsing, a failed build, or behavior of an unrelated installed sklearn release for proof that the target checkout is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires target-specific evidence checking both classes and at least one non-default n_splits value.
metadata.judge_focus: Tests or runtime assertions for both public classes, including custom n_splits, n_repeats, and random_state; provenance of the imported module; and treatment of build failures.
metadata.oracle_test: Assertions should reject object-address reprs and verify the concrete class name plus n_splits, n_repeats, and random_state for defaults and a custom case such as (3, 5, 42), using the repository's canonical repr formatting/order.

scale.1: No validation evidence, or evidence is misrepresented as passing despite an explicit failure.
scale.2: Only syntax/static checks, mock behavior, unrelated installed-package output, or a visible failing semantic result.
scale.3: Target-relevant evidence checks repr callability or defaults for at least one class, but omits both-class or custom-value coverage.
scale.4: Target-checkout tests or runtime assertions cover both classes and custom values, but omit a useful regression detail such as exact formatting or default coverage.
scale.5: Decisive target-version assertions pass for both classes with default and custom parameters, confirming concrete class names, correct values, canonical formatting, and absence of memory-address/internal-field output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decisive target-version repr evidence

applies_when: The cutoff contains source inspection or reasoning about RepeatedKFold, RepeatedStratifiedKFold, _RepeatedSplits, or _build_repr.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies both why the classes fall back to object repr and why blindly invoking the existing generic repr helper may still render n_splits incorrectly.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A demonstrated output with n_splits=None, or source showing no self.n_splits attribute, caps at 3 if the trajectory continues to claim that a bare _build_repr(self) fully solves the task without addressing the mismatch.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source for the target version overrides assumptions based on newer or separately installed scikit-learn versions; direct inspection of _RepeatedSplits.__init__ and _build_repr overrides unsupported claims.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a superficially plausible two-line repr addition without noticing that the generic helper retrieves constructor parameters through attributes.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires recognizing the n_splits storage mismatch or equivalent evidence that _build_repr(self) alone can produce n_splits=None.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible evidence connecting the absent inherited __repr__ on _RepeatedSplits to the default object representation, plus recognition that n_splits is stored in self.cvargs rather than directly on self.
metadata.oracle_test: RepeatedKFold and RepeatedStratifiedKFold inherit from _RepeatedSplits, which lacks an informative repr; their public n_splits value comes from cvargs['n_splits'], while n_repeats and random_state are direct attributes.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or an explanation contradicted by the inspected source.
scale.2: Locates the classes or notes the missing repr, but does not establish the inheritance path or parameter storage.
scale.3: Correctly attributes the object-style repr to the missing shared repr implementation and identifies _build_repr as relevant, but does not address n_splits being stored in cvargs.
scale.4: Correctly diagnoses both the missing shared repr and the n_splits storage mismatch, with supporting source observations, but leaves some formatting or implementation consequence unresolved.
scale.5: Provides a complete source-grounded causal account: shared inheritance causes the default repr, the helper derives public constructor parameters, and n_splits must be exposed or explicitly obtained from cvargs while internal cv details remain hidden.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the repeated-splitter repr failure

applies_when: The cutoff contains an applied or proposed source change affecting representation of RepeatedKFold, RepeatedStratifiedKFold, or their shared base.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assesses whether visible applied source provides both repeated cross-validation classes with an informative representation containing the concrete public class name and the actual n_splits, n_repeats, and random_state values, without exposing internal wrapper state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If target-version output visibly contains an object memory address, `n_splits=None`, an incorrect custom value, or internal `cv` or `cvargs` details, score 1. If the applied code only calls `_build_repr(self)` while inspected source shows no direct `self.n_splits`, cap at 2 regardless of claims, syntax success, or output from another installation.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible target-repository diff is required to establish applied work. Target-version runtime output overrides static reasoning; target-version source semantics override prose claims. Output from a separately installed sklearn version, intended edits, patch descriptions, syntax checks, and future test plans do not establish repr correctness.

An applied edit supported only by a separately installed package, copied incompatible module, standalone pandas simulation, syntax compilation, or execution that stops before dtype wrapping cannot exceed 2. A trajectory with no final applied implementation is not treated as a failed implementation test and defaults to the neutral anchor unless it contains a decisive checkout-grounded behavioral result.
metadata.evidence_authority: Validation against the final visible checked-out source or submitted patch outranks earlier runs. Successful repository assertions outrank direct helper executions with explicit comparisons, which outrank print-only checkout-linked observations. Import provenance must show that repository logic or an exact source-loaded helper was exercised. Installed-package runs, copied files under site-packages, and reimplemented simulations cannot prove checkout behavior. A traceback or failed assertion outranks a nearby success label, and pre-edit results do not validate later edits.
