scale.5: The displayed repository state is unusable, syntactically broken, destructively modified, or dominated by severe contaminating artifacts.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Visible source and artifact defects

applies_when: The trajectory is localizing or reproducing the pre-fix adjacent user-defined-literal failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures assistant-authored causal localization supported by cutoff-visible execution showing that the repository consumes the base literal while leaving the immediately adjacent UDL suffix, which then causes enclosing end validation to fail.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A call made at the beginning of an entire declaration, a whitespace-separated suffix, an invalid object type, or a run failing before literal parsing cannot establish direct remainder behavior. An enclosing error without a valid declaration harness and suffix-position evidence cannot substitute for the score-4 direct probe. Later valid output overrides earlier setup failures.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from the repository parser beginning exactly at `6.62607015e-34q_J` is authoritative for parser consumption and remainder. A valid complete `member` declaration is authoritative for enclosing failure. Repository regex output proves only lexical matching. Source listings, TODO comments, custom replacement regexes, proposed commands, and runs stopped by dependency or API errors are not execution evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating source-based reasoning, truthy regex output, analogous or spaced tokens, a generic declaration error, and an exact direct parser remainder.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an executed repository matcher or parser that reaches task code. Score 4 requires a direct repository parser probe beginning at the exact reported literal and showing both the complete consumed base and exact adjacent remainder. Score 5 additionally requires a valid complete `member` declaration with fallback disabled.
metadata.judge_focus: Require an assistant-authored conclusion connecting observed output to `_parse_literal`. Distinguish source inspection, a repository regex probe, a direct repository parser probe beginning at the literal token, and a valid complete `member` declaration with fallback disabled. Record the exact consumed spelling and exact remainder.
metadata.oracle_test: Before the fix, a direct parser probe beginning at `6.62607015e-34q_J` consumes exactly `6.62607015e-34` and leaves exactly `q_J`; the complete reported declaration parsed as `member` with fallback disabled then fails end validation at that suffix.

scale.1: No assistant-authored causal localization is present, or every attempted run stops before repository literal matching or parsing.
scale.2: The assistant correctly attributes the failure to `_parse_literal` leaving a suffix, but support is limited to source inspection, a TODO, narration, or a generic error.
scale.3: Executed repository evidence reaches task code but is limited to an exact regex span, an analogous or spaced token, or a valid enclosing suffix-position failure without an exact direct parser remainder.
scale.4: A direct repository parser probe beginning at `6.62607015e-34q_J` visibly consumes exactly `6.62607015e-34` and leaves exactly `q_J`.
scale.5: The exact direct span and remainder are shown, and a valid complete `member` declaration with fallback disabled visibly fails end validation at that adjacent suffix.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed causal reproduction of the adjacent UDL remainder

applies_when: The cutoff workspace contains an active source edit for C++ user-defined literal parsing or rendering.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active reachable source implements adjacent intact UDL suffix parsing with built-in-suffix disambiguation, a structured base-literal and identifier AST, evaluator-compatible IDs, and literal-operator xref rendering.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Unreachable code, `isalnum()` scanning, unrestricted built-in suffix prefix consumption, whitespace skipping, matching only a prefix such as `q` from `q_J`, or folding the suffix into `ASTNumberLiteral` caps the score at 2. Missing either call-like IDs or accepted literal-operator rendering caps the score at 3. A clean workspace with only the original TODO scores 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and reachability are authoritative. Executed output against that same source may resolve behavior not evident statically. Earlier edits that were reverted, scratch implementations, custom substitute classes, comments, intended patches, and source merely inspected from the repository are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Giving midpoint credit for inspected original source or absent edits, treating opaque text consumption as structured support, ignoring unreachable code, or overlooking missing ID and rendering integration.
metadata.hard_gate: Any score above 1 requires active reachable production code implementing UDL expression semantics. Score 3 requires structured adjacent parsing that preserves separate base-literal and suffix-identifier objects. Score 4 requires correct ID and rendering integration in addition to lexical semantics.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff diff for bounded integer and floating suffix handling, a no-leading-boundary C++ UDL identifier matcher, absence of whitespace skipping, reuse of the parsed base literal, a wrapper retaining `ASTLiteral` and `ASTIdentifier`, call-like ID generation, accepted `udl` description mode, and `operator""<suffix>` rendering with `cpp:parent_key`.
metadata.oracle_test: `1ULL` and `5f` remain ordinary literals; `1uludl`, `5fudl`, and `6.62607015e-34q_J` retain complete adjacent suffix identifiers; `42 suffix` is not wrapped; the issue ID is `clL_Zli3q_JEL6.62607015e-34EE`; rendering displays `q_J` while targeting `operator""q_J` with the enclosing lookup key.

scale.1: No active reachable production implementation is displayed; only original source, reverted edits, scratch code, tests, or an unreachable insertion is present.
scale.2: Active production code attempts UDL recognition but visibly truncates suffixes, accepts whitespace, misclassifies built-in suffixes, folds suffix text into an ordinary literal, or otherwise lacks a valid structured wrapper.
scale.3: Active reachable source correctly preserves an adjacent complete suffix in a wrapper containing separate base-literal and identifier objects, but exact call-like IDs or dedicated rendering remains absent or materially incomplete.
scale.4: Active source implements bounded built-in suffixes, intact adjacent identifiers across literal paths, structured AST storage, exact call-like IDs, an accepted description mode, and `operator""<suffix>` rendering with lookup context.
scale.5: The active implementation is complete across numeric, string, and character literals, preserves ordinary C++ behavior, and includes a coherent C-domain compatibility adaptation whenever shared suffix utilities changed.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active structured UDL semantics and rendering

applies_when: The visible work executes or attempts a matcher, parser, test, build, compilation, or patch-integrity check relevant to C++ literal handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the strength of cutoff-visible task-causal execution, from exact repository lexical diagnostics of the adjacent UDL failure through successful parser, ID, rendering, and regression validation of the active implementation. When a script invokes a literal matcher imported from the repository, the match group and the untouched input slice beginning at `match.end()` are repository matcher evidence even if the script subsequently performs custom scanning; only the repository match and direct remainder slice receive credit.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A generic end-of-definition failure, an invalid declaration object type, a parser call beginning at the wrong position, a truncated input or remainder, a truthy match without exact matched text, a custom substitute regex, zero selected relevant tests, fallback-only acceptance, or a run stopped by imports or setup cannot satisfy the score-3 diagnostic gate. Failed syntax or import checks against the active edit cap implementation validation at 2 regardless of earlier successes. Later valid execution against the same or newer active source overrides earlier harness failures.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from repository matchers, parsers, renderers, tests, compilers, and diff tools is authoritative only for behavior actually exercised. A script using the repository's imported numeric-literal matcher proves its exact match span; directly printing the original input from `match.end()` proves the exact remainder. A later custom suffix loop does not invalidate those two observations but proves nothing additional. Results against the active cutoff source outrank earlier or reverted states. Custom replacement regexes, inferred remainders, manual scanner results, proposed commands, dependency installation, source inspection, and commands failing before task code are not execution evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating exact repository matcher span-and-remainder output with manual scanning, generic parser failure, truncated probes, invalid harnesses, zero-test runs, or checks against reverted source; or treating lexical diagnosis alone as validation of an applied implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require either an imported repository matcher applied to the complete reported expression that visibly prints both the exact consumed base and the complete untouched remainder, or a successful discriminative parser, ID, or rendering assertion against active source. Scores above 3 require successful validation of an applied implementation. Score 5 requires the complete end-to-end validation matrix against the displayed final source.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact command input and observed output. Distinguish an imported repository literal matcher applied to the complete reported expression, a direct repository parser, a valid declaration harness, and successful checks against active source. Require the exact matched base and untouched remainder for lexical diagnostics, and inspect complete consumption, fallback settings, AST or ID assertions, rendering behavior, ordinary-suffix controls, selected-test counts, and source-state correspondence for implementation validation.
metadata.oracle_test: Before correction, the repository numeric matcher applied to the complete reported expression consumes exactly `6.62607015e-34` and the original input slice at match end is exactly `q_J * 1q_s`. After correction, the complete member declaration parses to end with fallback disabled; the issue UDL has ID `clL_Zli3q_JEL6.62607015e-34EE`; ordinary `1ULL` and `5f` remain number literals; `1uludl` and `5fudl` retain intact UDL identifiers; whitespace-separated suffixes are not wrapped; and rendering targets `operator""<suffix>`.
metadata.stage: Failure reproduction through discriminative regression validation

scale.1: No relevant execution reaches repository literal matching, parsing, rendering, or task-source integrity code; attempts stop during setup, imports, or invalid harness construction.
scale.2: Execution reaches task-related code but shows only a generic parser failure, a partial or truncated repository match, a truthy match without exact span and remainder, an isolated probe, zero relevant selected tests, or compilation/diff integrity without demonstrated UDL behavior.
scale.3: Exactly one of these is shown: the repository numeric matcher runs on the complete reported expression and visibly yields the exact consumed base plus the complete untouched remainder; or one valid discriminative parser, exact-ID, or rendering assertion passes against active source. A broader implementation-validation matrix is absent.
scale.4: Against active source, focused UDL cases and ordinary-suffix or whitespace controls pass, together with compilation or broader C++ regression evidence, but rendering or all affected-domain coverage remains incomplete.
scale.5: Against the displayed final source, complete declaration parsing with fallback disabled, exact IDs across literal categories, rendering and xref behavior, ordinary and ambiguity controls, all relevant C++ and affected C regressions, compilation, and diff integrity visibly pass.

scale.2: Only collection is changed; secondary rendering and body handling remain absent or visibly broken.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Pipeline coverage and documentation safety

applies_when: The prefix inspects, prototypes, edits, tests, or restores code related to docstring-signature overload handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest concrete progress displayed by the cutoff toward changing the actual autodoc pipeline. Earlier bounded edits remain evidence of progress after restoration, but must not be described as current repository behavior.

metadata.judge_focus: Production edits, executable production-equivalent prototypes, downstream integration, and distinction from planning-only exploration.

scale.1: Only source inspection, problem restatement, or an unexecuted plan is displayed.
scale.2: A print-based or isolated executable prototype demonstrates task-relevant parsing, but no production edit is displayed.
scale.3: A bounded production edit or substantive edit attempt collects multiple candidates or changes one real pipeline stage, even if later reverted or semantically incomplete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete task-directed implementation progress

applies_when: The prefix contains task-directed source edits, an executable implementation prototype, restoration of such edits, or commands checking overload-signature behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates the strongest coherent implementation work visibly demonstrated for extracting and separately rendering a leading block of overloaded docstring signatures, adjusted for defects exposed by later source inspection or execution.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Visible syntax damage, duplicated or missing method boundaries, undefined variables, or destructive file replacement caps the score at 1 unless a later authoritative restoration is shown. A task-shaped failure, rendering only the first result, or collapsing overloads into one synthetic signature caps the score at 3. Dependency failure alone is not a semantic failure if no task assertion ran.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible source or diff and command output outrank assistant claims. A focused execution outranks an unexecuted code sketch. Earlier coherent edits remain evidence after an explicit restoration, but they are not evidence of current repository behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents edit volume, success narration, dependency installation, print-only regex experiments, or reverted malformed patches from being mistaken for coherent applied progress.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4-5 require visible coherent production code spanning extraction and downstream rendering without syntactic corruption. Score 5 additionally requires a task-shaped check showing distinct overloads and preserved following prose.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect concrete parser, representation, rendering, and docstring-rewrite behavior; distinguish a coherent bounded attempt from edits that are only extensive, malformed, or contradicted by execution.
metadata.non_evidence: Plans, claimed success without displayed code or output, package installation, unrelated existing tests, backup files, and source inspection alone do not establish implementation behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: A docstring beginning with two or more valid same-name signatures must produce one separately rendered signature per complete arguments/return pair, consume only that contiguous leading signature block, and retain the first following prose line and later body text.

scale.1: The latest authoritative evidence shows destructive or syntactically malformed task edits with no later restoration, or no concrete task-relevant implementation behavior is demonstrated.
scale.2: A concrete prototype or bounded edit attempt exists, but it does not yet establish a coherent production path from overload extraction to usable rendering; any current repository state shown is intact.
scale.3: A coherent bounded production attempt or production-equivalent execution handles part of the overload path, but a visible material defect remains, such as collecting beyond the leading block, using only the first result, collapsing overloads, losing argument/return pairing, or failing a task-shaped check.
scale.4: Visible coherent production code integrates extraction with separate rendering and safe body rewriting, with no contradictory execution or source damage, but task-shaped verification is absent or leaves one material boundary or compatibility question unresolved.
scale.5: Visible coherent production code implements the complete leading-overload-block behavior, and task-shaped execution confirms distinct paired signatures, separate rendering, consumed-marker removal, and preservation of following prose without a contradictory regression result.

metadata.judge_focus: Apply only to explicit final artifacts and only for visible applicability, syntax, omission, or destructive-change defects.

scale.1: The explicit final artifact is focused, applicable, and contains the semantic source change, or no material obstruction is visible.
scale.2: Minor artifact noise or ambiguity exists, but the source change remains usable.
scale.3: The artifact requires limited evaluator-side inspection or repair, while relevant source progress remains recoverable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Explicit final artifact obstruction

applies_when: A production-source change for the positional-only default defect is active at the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active change stays within the semantic signature parser and preserves the existing compatibility guard, representations, and adjacent parameter-handling structure.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removal of the compatibility guard, corruption or duplication of surrounding code, a wrong-component workaround, or visible changes to unrelated parameter categories caps the score at 2. Harmless untracked diagnostics alone do not reduce the score.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest active production diff or displayed source controls structural preservation. Scratch implementations, backup files, and claims that surrounding behavior is unchanged do not establish preservation unless the relevant source context or applicable execution is visible.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring compatibility from silence, rewarding no-edit trajectories, treating a correct mapping formula as proof of preserved surrounding behavior, or penalizing incidental files that do not enter the evaluator-facing source.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require a visible active edit in the semantic parser with enough surrounding context to assess its scope. No active production edit receives score 1 if this rubric is selected.
metadata.judge_focus: Examine the active production diff and surrounding function body for localization to `signature_from_str`, retention of the `hasattr(args, 'posonlyargs')` boundary, continued use of `ast_unparse` and `Parameter.empty`, and preservation of annotation, ordinary positional, vararg, keyword-only, kwarg, and return-annotation handling. Do not use the correctness of the new default-index formula as the primary basis here.
metadata.oracle_test: The change remains in `sphinx.util.inspect.signature_from_str`, retains guarded access to `posonlyargs`, preserves source-like defaults and empty sentinels, and leaves the existing adjacent parameter and annotation loops structurally intact.

scale.1: No active production edit is visible, or the approach is confined to an unrelated component and cannot preserve the intended parser path.
scale.2: An active change exists but visibly removes a compatibility boundary, corrupts surrounding code, broadly rewrites unrelated behavior, or uses a wrong-component workaround.
scale.3: The edit is localized to the semantic parser, but the visible context is insufficient to establish preservation of the guard or adjacent parameter handling.
scale.4: The active diff visibly retains the compatibility guard, established representations, annotations, and separate adjacent parameter-handling structure.
scale.5: The focused structure is visibly preserved and applicable evidence also covers representative adjacent behavior such as ordinary defaults, annotations, varargs, keyword-only arguments, kwargs, or return annotations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Parser scope and surrounding-behavior preservation

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Assess the visible evaluator-facing state stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the change remains in the semantic parser and preserves guarded compatibility and unrelated parameter categories.

metadata.judge_focus: Use visible source structure rather than assuming preservation from silence.

scale.1: The approach changes the wrong component, broadly corrupts source, removes the compatibility boundary, or depends on unrelated parameter categories.
scale.2: The target is relevant, but scope or compatibility has a material visible risk.
scale.3: The edit is localized and surrounding structure appears retained, but fallback or adjacent behavior is not established.

scale.5: The focused edit visibly preserves annotations, ordinary defaults, fallback behavior, and other parameter categories with direct surrounding-case evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Scope and compatibility preservation

applies_when: The trajectory contains task-relevant inspection, reproduction, or modification of repository code.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete progress toward a working fix in the active checkout, using the latest visible production source and only validation performed against that source revision.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A fresh failure, syntax error, wrong default ownership, or wrong parameter kind from the latest active revision prevents score 5 and caps the score at 3 until a later visible correction is applied. Output predating a later edit cannot cap that later edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible production source or applicable diff determines the active implementation. Command output governs only the exact source revision and checkout module it exercised. A source display after an edit outranks earlier output for determining current necessary semantics, but does not prove an unobserved pass.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting standalone calculations as implementation, treating a failed run as successful exercise, applying stale output to newer source, or granting tested status to an unexecuted correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a visible active edit in the repository's production parsing path. Score 5 additionally requires fresh execution of that same revision through the checkout's target function or documentation path with the required mapping observed.
metadata.judge_focus: Order source edits and commands chronologically; distinguish localization, checkout reproduction, a known-bad production edit, a plausible later correction, and fresh successful execution of that correction.
metadata.oracle_test: For the active checkout, `signature_from_str('(a, b=0, /, c=1)')` yields `a` positional-only with `Parameter.empty`, `b` positional-only with string default `'0'`, and `c` positional-or-keyword with string default `'1'`.

scale.1: Only broad exploration or an unrelated standalone experiment is visible; the repository defect path is not causally localized.
scale.2: The defect path is localized or reproduced, but no active production edit exists and no stronger repository-facing advancement is visible.
scale.3: A direct checkout reproduction or relevant production edit exists, but the latest edit is visibly wrong, syntactically broken, from the wrong production component, or of uncertain applicability.
scale.4: The latest active production edit visibly implements a plausible correction with no fresh contradiction from that revision, but exact checkout behavior after the edit remains unverified.
scale.5: The latest active production edit is freshly exercised through the checkout and visibly produces the required names, kinds, and exact defaults without a remaining contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Chronological checkout implementation advancement

applies_when: The prefix exposes an assistant-authored mapping rule, a production-source implementation, or observed target behavior for positional-only defaults.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest cutoff-visible semantic state right-aligns `args.defaults` over exactly `posonlyargs + args`, preserving required leading parameters and source-like default representations.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If a fresh run of the latest active source assigns a default to required `a`, gives `b` the wrong value, raises an indexing/parameter-order error, or otherwise contradicts the claimed mapping, cap at 2. Do not apply output from before a later edit to that later source.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible active checkout source or final diff controls necessary semantics. A fresh execution of that same revision controls observed behavior. Earlier output, reverted edits, proposed patches, standalone models, and installed-package behavior cannot override the latest active source.
metadata.failure_mode: Group-local alignment, inclusion of keyword-only/vararg/kwarg counts, wrong default ownership, non-string AST values, stale-output attribution, or crediting tool output as assistant-authored reasoning.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a cutoff-visible active production edit in `sphinx/util/inspect.py::signature_from_str`; a correct rule present only in prose or a scratch script is capped at 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the assistant-authored formula and the latest active `signature_from_str` source. For the reproduction, determine whether `a` remains empty, `b` receives `'0'`, and `c` receives `'1'`. Names appearing only in AST dumps, tracebacks, grep output, or source listings do not establish an assistant-authored causal rule.
metadata.oracle_test: `signature_from_str('(a, b=0, /, c=1)')` must yield `a` as `POSITIONAL_ONLY` with `Parameter.empty`, `b` as `POSITIONAL_ONLY` with string default `'0'`, and `c` as `POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD` with string default `'1'`; the offset includes only `posonlyargs + args`.
metadata.stage: Derive and implement combined positional alignment

scale.1: No causal mapping is established, or the latest approach works at the wrong semantic layer and cannot restore the parser default.
scale.2: A relevant mapping or active edit is visible, but it is group-local, counts unrelated categories, assigns a default to the wrong parameter, or is contradicted by a fresh run of that source.

scale.5: The latest active production source unambiguously maps the reproduction to `a` empty, `b='0'`, and `c='1'`, preserves kinds and representation, and visibly generalizes the same right-alignment rule across the positional separator.

metadata.oracle_test: Trace key to name and identify display-name concatenation plus type() name creation

scale.1: The trajectory remains committed to an unrelated or destructive diagnosis and does not trace key into name.
scale.2: It identifies only concatenation or repeatedly converts module while leaving the key-derived name unaddressed.
scale.3: It locates the correct path but leaves one requirement unresolved without a concrete correction.
scale.4: It explicitly identifies both requirements or correctly interprets the second exception.
scale.5: It applies the complete local correction and verifies the relevant causal path while separating setup failures from product behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis and correction quality

applies_when: A repository source state, displayed diff, patch, or source-edit command is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures evaluator-facing source artifact readiness for the focused mock-subscription fix. Inspect whether the subscription-derived name is normalized for both display-name construction and dynamic type creation, while distinguishing absent edits, wrong-operand edits, partial corrections, provisionally complete edit commands, and clean final artifacts. A source-edit command may establish provisional completion only when it explicitly and syntactically targets the remaining expression and no later source view contradicts it.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later displayed source or diff showing an exposed name consumer overrides an earlier command or claimed completion. A visible relevant TypeError caps a resulting artifact at 3 unless a later uncontradicted edit explicitly corrects that exact consumer. Syntax damage, conflict markers, destructive unrelated changes, or scratch-only material cap the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the latest displayed resulting source or complete diff first. If no resulting view follows an edit command, an explicit syntactically valid command targeting the exact remaining expression is provisional evidence of that edit, but cannot earn the clean-final-artifact anchor. Summaries and scratch demonstrations cannot override contradictory repository source.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating no edit with a partial edit, treating normalization of the module or display prefix as normalization of the subscription-derived name, ignoring the type() consumer, or granting submission-level readiness from an unconfirmed command or scratch artifact.
metadata.hard_gate: A score of 4 or 5 requires evidence that the subscription-derived name is converted before both display-name construction and the first argument to type(). A score of 5 additionally requires a clean resulting source view or complete applicable diff that preserves the surrounding factory structure.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the evaluator-facing mock factory or subscription boundary for effective name normalization at both consumers, syntax and applicability, focused scope, and preservation of nearby attribute propagation and dynamic subclass construction.
metadata.oracle_test: Read the latest _make_subclass or __getitem__ state, supplemented only by an uncontradicted exact edit command, and determine whether the key becoming name is normalized for both concatenation and type() without damaging the surrounding factory.

scale.1: No repository source edit or targeted source-edit command is visible; the trajectory contains only inspection, reasoning, or scratch work.
scale.2: A repository edit is visible but is malformed, destructive, unrelated, or normalizes only the module or another operand that cannot repair the subscription-derived name.
scale.3: A focused coherent edit protects exactly one string-only use of the key-derived name, and no later uncontradicted command or resulting source completes the other use.
scale.4: Both name consumers are protected in resulting source, or an explicit uncontradicted edit command completes the sole remaining consumer, but the artifact lacks a clean final diff, retains a concrete nearby omission, or has not been confirmed as submission-ready.
scale.5: A clean, focused, syntax-correct resulting source view or complete applicable diff protects both name consumers and preserves the surrounding factory structure.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective source artifact integrity

applies_when: The visible source state or proposal touches autodoc mock construction or related behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures preservation of generated subclass construction, base resolution, and propagation of supplied class attributes.

metadata.failure_mode: Returning incoming bases, removing attribute propagation, bypassing generated subclasses, or introducing syntax or MRO damage
metadata.judge_focus: Collateral semantic safety
metadata.oracle_test: __mro_entries__ returns (self.__class__,), attrs.update(attributes or {}) remains effective, and dynamic subclass creation remains intact

scale.1: The visible state breaks base resolution, removes generated mock subclassing, or is syntactically unusable.
scale.2: A major preserved behavior such as attribute propagation is removed or a concrete compatibility regression is visible.
scale.3: The protocol remains recognizable, but the edit is broad, risky, or insufficiently controlled.
scale.4: The protocol and surrounding behavior are visibly unchanged by a focused correction.
scale.5: The focused correction is supported by successful mocked-base or relevant compatibility checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Mock subclass protocol preservation

applies_when: The prefix inspects, proposes, edits, or submits the Napoleon owner-resolution path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how much usable task-specific production progress is visibly present at the cutoff, without granting midpoint credit merely because the trajectory is unfinished.

metadata.failure_mode: The correction exists only in reasoning, scratch code, an unapplied file, or a non-patch payload.
metadata.judge_focus: Applied source state and evaluator usability

scale.1: No task-specific production correction is applied or displayed in an evaluator-usable form.
scale.2: A concrete correction is proposed or stored outside production, or an applied edit is too incomplete to constitute a usable path.
scale.3: A relevant production edit is applied, but its task behavior or surrounding compatibility remains materially unresolved.
scale.4: A coherent, scoped production correction is applied and appears usable for the reported case.
scale.5: The cutoff shows a clean, narrow, evaluator-facing production correction with supporting evidence and no unresolved task blocker.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing production progress

applies_when: A task-relevant failure, setup blocker, contradictory callback result, malformed edit, or failed validation attempt is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether observed failures are accurately classified, causally bounded, and left in a repair-ready state without unsupported semantic claims or additional source and environment damage.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when success is claimed despite a latest qualifying `None`, a same-module or generic-falsiness pass, an unlocalized malformed final artifact, or a terminal non-patch state. Cap at 2 when repeated dependency changes end in a compatibility failure, an unsafe ownership shortcut remains active, or an unverified insertion is not visibly wired into the owner lookup. A syntax failure does not itself cap credit when its exact malformed control-flow location is exposed, inspected, and accurately reported as unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest executed error or callback result and latest visible affected source block outrank earlier passing controls, assistant summaries, intended edits, and copied simulations. A clean cutoff workspace is authoritative when execution stopped before any production mutation.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards activity or a claimed pass while ignoring the latest contradictory output, or penalizes an accurately localized and actively inspected blocker as though it were an unrecognized final defect.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 3 require either a single clearly bounded prerequisite failure before production mutation, or exact localization of the active source or fixture defect with the affected block visibly inspected and no unsupported success claim. A completed causal rerun may also qualify.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest observed failure, the immediately following source or fixture state, and whether claims distinguish setup failure, malformed source, non-discriminative evidence, and qualifying callback behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: A qualifying semantic recheck invokes the repository `_skip_member` callback for a documented, configured, cross-module `functools.wraps` member and distinguishes literal `False` from `None`; setup and parser failures must instead be classified only as bounded blockers.
metadata.stage: Diagnose, implement, and validate the owner-resolution correction

scale.1: The latest contradiction is misreported as success, remains hidden behind non-discriminative evidence, or leaves an unlocalized or terminally unusable artifact.
scale.2: The failure is acknowledged, but follow-up work introduces dependency churn, an unsafe or disconnected edit, or another unresolved defect without bounding the original cause.
scale.3: A plausible causal source or fixture change is applied and the remaining uncertainty is reported accurately, but the active path is not shown parseable or semantically rechecked.
scale.4: The demonstrated cause is corrected or tightly contained and a relevant recheck completes, but qualifying callback identity or preservation coverage remains incomplete.
scale.5: The latest blocker is accurately and narrowly bounded with no unsupported success claim: either execution stopped cleanly at one prerequisite before production mutation, the exact active syntax or control-flow defect is exposed and inspected in a repair-ready state, or the corrected qualifying callback is successfully rechecked.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-calibrated contradiction handling

applies_when: A production edit, concrete final block, patch payload, or claimed evaluator-facing artifact is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures defects that prevent the proposed correction from executing or being evaluated; demonstrated blockers dominate stylistic or validation advantages.

metadata.failure_mode: A seemingly strong fix is nullified by the actual displayed source.
metadata.judge_focus: Imports, control flow, assignment safety, branch reachability, and payload validity

scale.1: No material blocker is visible in the applied or submitted correction.
scale.2: Minor scope or hygiene issues are visible without threatening execution of the corrected path.
scale.3: Material fragility or an unresolved branch concern is visible, but the reported path may still execute.
scale.4: A severe blocker is visible, such as a missing or wrongly scoped import, potentially unbound candidate, overwritten result, damaged exception structure, or correction only in an unapplied artifact.
scale.5: The evaluator-facing state is unusable: malformed or unimportable source, non-patch-only submission, no production correction in the claimed final artifact, or control flow that demonstrably disables the fix.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Blocking source or artifact defect

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, proposes, edits, or submits a correction to Napoleon's `_skip_member` owner-resolution path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the cutoff contains an evaluator-usable task-specific implementation in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py`, rather than only diagnosis, scratch code, tests, editing scripts, or an unapplied patch.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the latest visible source or cutoff diff shows that the production edit was reverted, never applied, or replaced by malformed/incomplete code, cap the score at 2 regardless of earlier successful experiments or prose.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff production source and its diff are authoritative. If workspace state is unavailable, an applicable terminal unified diff may establish the edit. Claims of success, scratch scripts, and unapplied patch files cannot override unchanged or reverted production source.
metadata.failure_mode: Luna treats investigation, an editing script, an untracked `fix.patch`, or an earlier transient edit as equivalent to an active production correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a visible active edit to `sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py` within or directly supporting `_skip_member`.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace diff and the complete resulting `_skip_member` block. Distinguish a production source edit from inspected historical source, proposed snippets, generated patch files, test-only changes, reverted edits, and commands that never changed the file.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator-facing source must alter owner discovery for wrapped class or exception members so the configured documented case can reach the existing explicit `return False` path.

scale.1: No task-specific production correction is active at the cutoff; only inspection, reasoning, reproductions, tests, or unrelated files are visible.
scale.2: A concrete correction is proposed or stored outside production, or an attempted production edit was reverted, malformed, or too incomplete to provide an executable owner-resolution path.
scale.3: A relevant production edit is active, but the displayed block is incomplete or leaves a material task-specific implementation question unresolved.
scale.4: A coherent, scoped production correction is active in `_skip_member` and is evaluator-usable for the reported decorated-member path.
scale.5: The active production state is a clean, narrow, structurally complete correction with all required imports and surrounding ownership/configuration control flow intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active task-specific production implementation

applies_when: The prefix compares competing task-specific explanations using source inspection, a constructed reference case, or executable behavior.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the prefix performs and correctly incorporates a focused check that discriminates between plausible explanations for why ordinary local URIs are not validated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the selected explanation conflicts with the inspected runtime branch or extrapolates a synthetic node example to the reported refuri without verification, cap at 3. If conflicting visible results are left unreconciled, cap at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Checkout source and checkout-grounded runtime observations outrank assumptions, synthetic node examples, comments, plans, and output from an unverified installation. Direct inspection of the nested checker outranks speculation about reference resolution when explaining the reported ordinary local URI.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking command volume, dependency setup, baseline reproduction, or an unverified refid/anchor theory for an experiment that actually distinguishes the decisive classification path.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit competing hypothesis, a discriminative visible result, and a subsequent causal account consistent with that result. Baseline reproduction alone cannot exceed 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether a source comparison or experiment answers a specific causal question about reference collection, URI representation, the non-HTTP classification branch, or result handling, and whether the resulting direction changes accordingly.
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported case, the resolved reference supplies a nonempty ordinary URI such as `doesntexist`; `write_doc()` queues it, and the nested checker unconditionally returns `local` for non-HTTP/HTTPS URIs instead of testing filesystem existence. Fragment-only references are a separate unchecked case.
metadata.stage: Repository and behavior localization through implementation planning

scale.1: No task-specific causal hypothesis is tested; activity is browsing, setup, or unrelated investigation without a discriminative result.
scale.2: A relevant check is attempted or a baseline symptom is reproduced, but it does not distinguish the competing causal explanations or remains inconclusive.
scale.3: One focused source check or experiment establishes a relevant representation or control-flow fact, but its implication for the decisive branch remains incomplete, unverified, or partially overgeneralized.
scale.4: A discriminative visible result resolves competing explanations and is incorporated into a consistent, actionable account of the relevant runtime path.
scale.5: Multiple checkout-grounded checks jointly establish collection, decisive classification, and reporting behavior, reject a plausible wrong explanation, and support a precise next intervention without unresolved contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative causal hypothesis resolution

applies_when: A decision table, helper, branch edit, or concrete implementation strategy for URI handling is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the actual semantics of the visible plan or source state: preserved unchecked and network cases, unsupported-scheme guarding, filesystem existence, and ignore handling after failure.

metadata.judge_focus: Assess implementation semantics when sufficiently observable

scale.1: The proposal targets the wrong kind of reference, leaves ordinary paths unvalidated, or introduces plainly incompatible handling.
scale.2: Moves toward local checking but omits or misorders multiple required cases, or uses an ineffective helper.
scale.3: Distinguishes existing and missing paths but leaves one important boundary such as ignores or explicit schemes unresolved.
scale.4: States or implements the complete ordered classification consistently, with only limited verification or minor uncertainty.
scale.5: Implements the complete classification in the runtime path and visibly preserves surrounding HTTP, fragment, mail, and unsupported-scheme behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctness of visible URI semantics

applies_when: The prefix contains contradictory causal claims, misleading behavioral conclusions, debug mutations, backups, reverted edits, malformed code, or repository residue.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes inconsistencies or residue only to the extent visible at the cutoff and material to the reliability or continuation of the work.

metadata.judge_focus: Avoid over-penalizing controlled nonterminal experimentation while identifying genuine obstruction

scale.1: Reasoning is consistent and no materially obstructive residue is visible.
scale.2: Minor uncertainty, a controlled temporary file, or a recovered failed edit is visible without affecting the current causal conclusion.
scale.3: Repeated contradiction, an ineffective edit presented too confidently, or notable residue reduces confidence in the current direction.
scale.4: The prefix relies on misleading execution evidence, leaves malformed or broad unrelated changes, or repeatedly pursues a contradicted subsystem.
scale.5: The visible state is unusable or destructive, and the prefix mistakes it for a valid solution or final artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Contradiction and obstructive residue

applies_when: The prefix proposes, attempts, applies, reverts, or inspects a task-specific production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores observable movement from diagnosis toward an executable production change, without conflating editing activity with correctness.

metadata.judge_focus: Distinguish no edit, ineffective attempts, relevant partial edits, and effective branch changes

scale.1: No task-specific production attempt is visible, or activity is confined to reproductions and browsing.
scale.2: A relevant attempt is made but fails to apply, is immediately reverted, or cannot affect the runtime path.
scale.3: A concrete production edit is visible but is incomplete, targets an adjacent path, or leaves the decisive unconditional classification effective.
scale.4: The decisive branch is changed in a relevant direction, though one material outcome or compatibility boundary remains incomplete.
scale.5: The visible production state implements the required ordered local-path behavior in the decisive branch with a coherent surrounding diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Concrete production progress

applies_when: A concrete task-specific command attempts to modify production source, or a task-specific production-source change is visible in an edit result, direct source inspection, or diff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the viability and semantic progress of an actually attempted production change, from malformed or irrelevant edits through coherent partial changes to complete local-filesystem validation in the decisive runtime path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An edit with an incompatible signature and caller, undefined dependency, malformed structure, or other visible execution blocker cannot exceed 1. An edit centered on refids, labels, anchors, or Sphinx document lookup instead of the queued ordinary filesystem URI cannot exceed 2. An edit that leaves the unconditional local return effective cannot exceed 3. Claims of success contradicted by a later direct source inspection or diff receive the score warranted by the later state.
metadata.evidence_authority: Chronologically later direct inspection of production source and explicit git diffs outrank plans and patch-success narration. A cutoff inventory summary is supporting evidence, but it does not erase a visibly applied edit unless it is demonstrably later and reconciled with the production source. Temporary fixtures, generated projects, backup copies, debug-only files, and edits outside production runtime code do not establish production progress.
metadata.failure_mode: Scoring browsing, diagnosis, proposed snippets, temporary fixtures, or dependency setup as implementation; treating any patch command as progress despite malformed runtime state; or rewarding reference-resolution edits that cannot validate the reported ordinary filesystem URI.
metadata.hard_gate: This rubric is selected only when a concrete production edit is attempted or visible. Scores 3 through 5 require a production change that can execute in the relevant runtime path. Scores 4 and 5 require replacement of the unconditional local classification with filesystem existence handling; score 5 additionally requires visible preservation of surrounding URI and ignore behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine what production code was concretely changed or attempted, whether the resulting source is executable, whether it reaches the nested checker for queued ordinary non-network URIs, and whether it changes classification based on filesystem existence rather than reference, label, or document lookup.
metadata.oracle_test: A viable fix operates on an already queued ordinary non-HTTP/HTTPS URI in the checker, preserves explicitly unchecked and network cases, avoids treating unsupported schemes as filesystem paths, resolves the local path against the appropriate source context, reports existing and missing paths correctly, and allows configured ignores to suppress a resulting failure.

scale.1: A production edit is attempted or visible, but it is malformed, cannot execute, changes an incompatible interface without its callers, affects only debug behavior, or otherwise cannot influence valid task behavior.
scale.2: The production attempt is syntactically plausible but fails or is reverted, targets an adjacent reference, label, anchor, or document-resolution path, or rewrites URIs without validating the reported ordinary filesystem path.
scale.3: An executable production change reaches the relevant local-URI runtime area, but the unconditional local result remains effective or a material requirement such as source-relative resolution, unsupported-scheme guarding, failure reporting, or ignore interaction is missing.
scale.4: The production change replaces unconditional local classification with coherent filesystem existence handling in the decisive path, while leaving only one limited compatibility or validation gap.
scale.5: The visible production state implements complete ordered local-path handling and preserves fragment-only, mail, network, unsupported-scheme, reporting, and ignore behavior with a coherent executable diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Viability of concrete production edits

applies_when: The prefix investigates or changes private-member parsing, filtering, explicit collection, or related merge logic.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the latest visibly applied and verified implementation checkpoint, rewarding safe progression through parsing, guarded selection, and explicit collection rather than plans or attempted edit count.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax or import failure caused by the edit, code inserted at class or function scope incorrectly, a truncated converter, incomplete control flow, or an uninspected generated replacement caps the score at 1. Unguarded membership against a possibly absent option, truthiness-only finite filtering, or an observed selected-member failure caps the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest displayed source and executed import or compilation result outrank plans, edit commands, replacement-script messages, earlier source states, and assistant claims. A demonstrated restoration supersedes the damaged state it removed; an unverified repair does not.
metadata.failure_mode: Intent and breadth of attempted edits are mistaken for applied progress, or a state with more code but an active defect is preferred over a smaller recoverable checkpoint.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires visibly applied finite-list parsing in both documenter option specifications and a structurally coherent latest source checkpoint. A score above 3 requires guarded absent, ALL, and finite handling in both filtering paths. A score of 5 additionally requires finite-name collection when members is absent or finite.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest complete source excerpts, diff, import or compilation result, and recovery actions to determine which obligations are actually applied and whether the resulting checkpoint remains structurally usable.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace one finite private name and one unrequested private name through the latest applied converter, member collection, analyzer and ordinary filtering, while separately confirming that a valueless option maps to ALL.
metadata.stage: Implement parsing, merging, and exact selection

scale.1: No verified task-causal change is applied, or the latest applied state is malformed, unimportable, structurally uncertain, or left after an unverified generated edit.
scale.2: The latest state is loadable or plausibly recoverable but remains preliminary or unsafe: support is not wired through both documenters, filtering has an unguarded or truthiness defect, collection is only proposed, or observed behavior contradicts the attempted selection semantics.
scale.3: Both documenters visibly parse absent or valueless input as ALL and finite input as names in a coherent applied checkpoint, without introducing unsafe filtering; filtering or explicit collection may still be cleanly unimplemented.
scale.4: Both documenters and both filtering paths visibly implement guarded absent, ALL, and finite exact-name states with their distinct eligibility rules, but finite explicit collection or an adjacent compatibility boundary remains incomplete.
scale.5: The latest inspected implementation safely covers both parser declarations, both filtering paths, finite collection for absent or finite members, ALL-safe deduplicating merges, and adjacent eligibility controls, with source integrity verified after the final edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Verified state-model implementation checkpoint

applies_when: The trajectory runs or reports tests, builds, reproductions, compilation, or validation scripts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credit only validation that actually executes the active working-tree autodoc implementation and reaches observable assertions relevant to selective and valueless private-member behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Zero collected tests, dependency or fixture failure before the relevant assertion, missing generated output, copied filtering logic, or a malformed scratch script provides no runtime-behavior credit. Such evidence caps the score at 2 even if the assistant calls it successful.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an actually executed command against the active working tree outranks assistant claims, proposed commands, copied predicates, source-only assertions, and scripts that were merely written.
metadata.failure_mode: Compilation, parser demonstrations, dependency failures, zero-test runs, or synthetic copies of the predicate are treated as successful feature validation.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an executed command that reaches at least one task-relevant runtime assertion against the edited autodoc implementation. A score above 3 requires both requested inclusion and unrequested-private exclusion to be observed.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact executed command, whether it imported or built from the active workspace, whether setup completed, the positive test count or reached assertions, and the observed output for requested inclusion, unrequested exclusion, and valueless retention.
metadata.oracle_test: Run a focused working-tree autodoc test or Sphinx build showing a requested private member present, another eligible private member absent for a finite list, and both retained by valueless `:private-members:`.

scale.1: No applicable runtime check reaches a relevant assertion; commands are absent, only proposed, malformed, collect zero tests, or fail during setup.
scale.2: Only static checks, compilation, source inspection, parser-only checks, or copied logic succeed; their limitations may be acknowledged, but repository behavior is not executed.
scale.3: An executed command reaches the active autodoc implementation and verifies at least one relevant behavior, but does not establish both finite inclusion and finite exclusion.
scale.4: Focused active-workspace execution proves requested inclusion and unrequested eligible-private exclusion, and also verifies valueless-all retention or another directly relevant compatibility behavior.
scale.5: Focused fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass execution proves finite inclusion, finite exclusion, and valueless retention across relevant module, class, analyzer, or adjacent-option paths, with failures reported accurately.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed autodoc behavior evidence

applies_when: The prefix inspects or changes private-member option conversion or either private filtering path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess compatible parsing, exact finite-name filtering, total handling of absent and valueless states, and preservation of the distinct analyzer and ordinary-member eligibility rules.

metadata.failure_mode: Finite lists remain truthy all-private flags, the valueless form is not retained, or analyzer entries acquire the ordinary-member documentation gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Exact selection without introducing a compatibility regression
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect both option specifications and both filtering paths, then exercise finite inclusion, finite exclusion, and valueless-all retention
metadata.stage: Implement parsing, merging, and exact selection

scale.1: No useful semantic change is present, or the latest source directly contradicts established private-member behavior.
scale.2: Names may parse, but filtering remains truthiness-based, only one path is covered, or a concrete compatibility regression is present.
scale.3: Guarded exact-name selection is present in a meaningful path or attempted in both paths, but coverage, total state handling, or path-specific eligibility remains incomplete.
scale.4: Both documenters and both filtering paths visibly distinguish absent, `ALL`, and finite exact-name states while preserving analyzer and ordinary-member eligibility distinctions.
scale.5: Exact-name semantics are complete in both paths, preserve valueless and adjacent eligibility behavior, and operate with the required finite-name collection modes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current private-member selection semantics

applies_when: The prefix inspects or changes private-member option conversion, filtering, member discovery, or option merging in autodoc.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the latest coherent implementation of absent, valueless-all, and finite-name private-member states across conversion, both filtering paths, and explicit member discovery, without rewarding unverified edit breadth.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A syntax or import defect caused by the edit, a truncated existing converter, misplaced helper or decorator, malformed indentation or control flow, or reached output contradicting finite selection caps the score at 1. A finite list used only by truthiness, unsafe membership against an absent or ALL value, an unconditional keep that defeats exclusion, or exact handling in only one filtering path caps the score at 3. A later visibly verified repair supersedes the earlier defect.
metadata.evidence_authority: Reached output from the active working tree outranks source inference. Otherwise, the latest complete source excerpt, diff, or successful import or compilation outranks edit commands, replacement-script messages, earlier excerpts, and assistant summaries. A visibly restored converter or control-flow block supersedes the damaged state it replaced; an attempted repair not subsequently inspected does not.
metadata.failure_mode: Parser wiring, helper names, or numerous attempted edits are mistaken for complete selection semantics even though a finite list remains a truthy all-private flag, one path is unchanged, an unconditional assignment defeats filtering, discovery omits requested names, or adjacent member parsing is damaged.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires a structurally coherent latest source state with the ordinary members converter intact. A score above 2 requires both module and class documenters to parse valueless input as ALL and finite input as names. A score above 3 requires guarded exact-name handling in both private filtering paths. A score of 5 requires finite private names to be included in member discovery or a deduplicating merge when ordinary member selection would not already discover them.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine the latest applied source state, then inspect the ordinary members converter, both private-member option specifications, analyzer-backed filtering, ordinary-member filtering, and any collection or merge of explicitly requested private names.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace absent, valueless, and finite private-member option values through both documenter specifications; then trace one requested and one unrequested private name through analyzer-backed and ordinary filtering, and verify that a requested name can enter discovery when ordinary members are absent or finite.
metadata.stage: Implement parsing, exact filtering, and explicit collection

scale.1: No coherent task-causal implementation is established, or the latest applied state damages an existing converter, has malformed structure or control flow, is unimportable because of the edit, or is contradicted by reached selective-member behavior.
scale.2: A coherent preliminary change is applied, such as an intact finite-list converter or one documenter specification, but both documenters are not fully wired or exact private filtering is absent.
scale.3: Both documenters distinctly parse valueless input as ALL and finite input as names, and at least one private filtering path performs guarded exact-name selection; the other path remains truthiness-based, unsafe, or unverified.
scale.4: Both documenters and both filtering paths visibly distinguish absent, ALL, and finite exact-name states while preserving their existing path-specific documentation eligibility, but explicit finite-name discovery or adjacent merge compatibility is incomplete or unverified.
scale.5: The latest coherent implementation also carries finite private names into discovery or a safe deduplicating merge when needed, preserves valueless-all and adjacent member behavior, and has no contrary reached evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Selective private-member implementation semantics

applies_when: The workspace contains a task-related production edit, scripted replacement, backup source file, or broad parser change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes cutoff-visible source damage according to executability and semantic reach, distinguishing confined recoverable defects from broad rewriting of unrelated parsing behavior.

metadata.judge_focus: Current damage, not speculative future repair

scale.1: No active production-source damage is visible; a clean no-edit state also receives this no-penalty anchor.
scale.2: Minor duplication, scratch artifacts, or hygiene issues exist while production source remains coherent and directly usable.
scale.3: The edit is ineffective, overly shared, or locally incompatible, but source structure remains intact and recovery is confined.
scale.4: A localized syntax failure, duplicated method, malformed control flow, or unstable replacement makes the affected source non-importable or substantially unsafe.
scale.5: The edit destroys or heuristically rewrites types/descriptions, truncates neighboring code, changes broad generic grammar, or creates severe cross-feature semantic corruption.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active source damage and semantic blast radius

applies_when: The prefix investigates or changes production code for combined NumPy parameter declarations.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures progress embodied in the current production source, from intact exploration through an executable causal edit to behaviorally verified completion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active edit that causes a syntax/import failure in the affected module, breaks the caller contract, or crashes before reaching the transformation is capped at 1 regardless of the intended design.
metadata.evidence_authority: A direct post-edit import, compilation, caller execution, or parser result outranks plans and claimed edit success. Visible source or diff outranks prose; a failed write command is not an applied edit. Later direct execution failure outranks earlier claims that replacement succeeded.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating no edit and a non-importable edit as equal merely because neither has yet produced corrected output.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a cutoff-visible applied production edit with a coherent callable contract; credit above 4 requires successful execution of the edited production path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether a task-directed edit is actually present, reaches the NumPy Napoleon parameter path, remains executable, and has been exercised after application.

metadata.evidence_authority: Fresh post-edit output from the actual description-mode pipeline outranks indirect signature probes and pre-edit output. Observed command output outranks a written but unexecuted script or a proposed command. The active cutoff source determines which implementation a result can support.
metadata.failure_mode: Claiming success from a failed harness, ordinary signature mode, raw annotations, stale or pre-change output; treating missing dependencies as a code failure; or leaving directly contradictory target output unresolved while asserting correctness.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires that every visible task-relevant result be attributed to the correct API, source state, and scope; merely running many commands is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: For each conclusion, identify the executed callable, effective source state, configuration, and observed output. Credit accurate statements that dependency, import-shadowing, malformed-app, or pre-assertion failures prove nothing about the fix. Evaluate assistant-authored conclusions, not names or claims appearing only in tool output.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare each claim with whether the command actually exercised `record_typehints` and rendered description fields under the joint configuration against the effective source.

scale.1: The assistant materially misrepresents invalid or contradictory evidence, or asserts success despite unresolved post-edit target output showing the bug.
scale.2: A semantic contradiction or evidence-authority mistake is partly noticed but remains unresolved, or conclusions still materially overreach the executed checks.
scale.3: Evidence remains ambiguous and conclusions are cautious, but one relevant attribution or contradiction is not fully resolved.
scale.4: All visible results, including setup failures or absence of behavioral validation, are accurately bounded and no semantic contradiction is misrepresented.
scale.5: The assistant correctly resolves conflicting evidence with a fresh authoritative rerun or equivalent causal comparison and states exactly what the final evidence proves.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantic counterevidence handling

applies_when: The trajectory reaches an implementation or exact patch for the description-mode annotation recorder.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether cutoff-visible implementation evidence establishes that `record_typehints` obtains one Sphinx signature using `type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases`, with that signature remaining the source for parameter and return stringification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later direct source display showing `inspect.signature(obj)` without aliases, a revert, or a conflicting effective edit overrides earlier commands. Use of `self.config`, event `options`, the standard-library inspector, or positional alias binding caps the score at 2. Lack of an applicable behavioral test does not reduce this implementation score.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later direct source display or active production diff has highest authority. An exact executed replacement command with observed success is secondary evidence when no later source contradicts it; an empty or incomplete diff summary alone does not prove that such an edit failed. An exact detached patch or unexecuted replacement is tertiary evidence. Opaque success messages and prose claims have no implementation authority.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting an opaque edit status, source that was only inspected before editing, an unexecuted command, or the mere presence of alias-related names without establishing the effective call and shared consumers.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires exact visible code or an exact executed edit containing `inspect.signature(obj, type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases)`. A score above 3 requires either active source or diff confirmation, or an exact successful executed edit with no later contradictory source. A score of 5 requires authoritative visible context showing both parameter and return consumers.
metadata.judge_focus: Read the final direct source display or active diff for `sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py`. If neither shows the call, consider an exact assistant-authored edit command only when it was actually executed and its output indicates success. Confirm the Sphinx helper, `app.config`, explicit `type_aliases=` binding, and the existing parameter loop and return consumer. An opaque script-success message, proposed command, earlier unedited source, grep result, or tool output merely naming the symbols is not exact implementation evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: The target source semantics are `sig = inspect.signature(obj, type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases)`, followed by parameter annotation stringification from `sig.parameters.values()` and return stringification from `sig.return_annotation`, with the callable guard and handled exceptions retained.

scale.1: No exact applicable implementation is visible, or later authoritative source clearly remains alias-unaware or reverted.
scale.2: An implementation attempt is visible but uses the wrong helper, receiver, alias source, binding, or only one annotation category.
scale.3: An exact correct detached patch or unexecuted replacement is visible, or an exact executed edit has unresolved contradictory state.
scale.4: The exact correct edit is active in source or diff, or was exactly executed successfully without later contradiction, but cutoff context does not establish both consumers.
scale.5: Authoritative source or diff shows the exact correct call and visibly preserves both the parameter loop and return-annotation consumer.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Alias-aware recorder implementation evidence

applies_when: The visible trajectory analyzes the linkcheck HEAD-to-GET request path or the TooManyRedirects failure described by the task.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that requests.head(..., allow_redirects=True) can raise requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects before producing a response, that this exception is not caught by the existing inner HTTPError handler, and that it therefore bypasses the intended GET fallback and reaches broken-link handling.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A claim that TooManyRedirects is already an HTTPError subclass, or that the outer status-code handler is the primary fallback boundary, caps credit at 2 unless visibly corrected later.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed repository source and successful runtime or library-source evidence outrank unsupported claims about exception inheritance; the task statement remains authoritative for the reported failure scenario.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding a keyword-level diagnosis that misunderstands why the existing HTTPError fallback does not execute.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the failure in the inner HEAD-request exception boundary rather than merely mentioning redirects or GET fallback generally.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible inspection of sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py, especially the nested HEAD request try/except, plus accurate reasoning about the requests exception hierarchy and control flow.
metadata.oracle_test: A HEAD request raises TooManyRedirects before returning a usable response; that exception must enter the same GET retry path currently used for a HEAD HTTPError.

scale.1: No relevant diagnosis, or a diagnosis incompatible with the visible request flow.
scale.2: Recognizes a redirect or HEAD-versus-GET problem but does not accurately identify the exception boundary and control flow.
scale.3: Correctly states that TooManyRedirects is not handled by the existing HEAD fallback and identifies the relevant linkcheck code area.
scale.4: Accurately explains the nested flow: HEAD raises TooManyRedirects, the inner HTTPError handler misses it, and the broad outer handler reports the link broken instead of issuing GET.
scale.5: Meets level 4 and supports the exception distinction with successful runtime/library-source evidence or equally decisive repository evidence while clearly identifying the intended semantic behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the HEAD redirect-loop failure

applies_when: A visible trajectory applies or attempts a source change to the linkcheck HEAD-to-GET request path.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the final visible repository state resolves TooManyRedirects and routes it through the existing GET fallback at the inner HEAD-request exception boundary without duplicating fallback logic or changing unrelated error classification.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score at most 2 if TooManyRedirects is caught only by an outer classifier, is unresolved, leaves invalid syntax, or can reach HTTPError-specific response access without a type guard. Score at most 3 if the GET fallback is duplicated. Score at most 4 if the required behavior is correct but outer exception classification or another unrelated request path is also changed.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest complete post-edit source or unified diff overrides earlier malformed intermediate edits and all commentary. A syntax result can disprove parseability but cannot establish correct exception scope. Proposed commands and prose are not applied implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents equal full credit for the exact inner-boundary extension, duplicated GET blocks, safely functional but unnecessarily broad restructuring, and unsafe outer catches.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires final visible, parseable applied code that resolves TooManyRedirects and catches it at the inner HEAD boundary so an existing GET request executes. Credit of 5 additionally requires reuse of the existing fallback body with no behavior-changing outer-handler edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible import or qualified exception reference, the inner try/except immediately surrounding requests.head, the existing GET fallback body, and any edits to the outer HTTPError classifier.
metadata.oracle_test: In the final code, a TooManyRedirects raised by the initial HEAD call enters the same existing fallback branch as a HEAD HTTPError; a successful GET then proceeds normally, while GET-side HTTPError handling retains its prior 401, 503, and broken-link semantics.

scale.1: No applicable final source edit is visible, or the final edit has the opposite behavior.
scale.2: A final applied attempt is visible but is invalid, unresolved, placed only at the outer classifier, or unsafe for TooManyRedirects.
scale.3: The final code can perform the required fallback, but duplicates the GET path or materially restructures exception handling in a way that obscures or risks existing classification.
scale.4: The final code correctly routes HEAD TooManyRedirects to GET and safely preserves outcomes, but includes a guarded outer-handler change or other unnecessary request-path complexity.
scale.5: The final code narrowly resolves TooManyRedirects and adds it to the existing inner HEAD exception boundary, reusing the unchanged GET fallback and preserving the outer classifier.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Final applied integration of TooManyRedirects into the HEAD fallback

applies_when: The task requires an existing HEAD-to-GET link-check fallback to handle an additional request exception
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible applied change makes a TooManyRedirects exception from the initial HEAD request invoke the existing GET fallback while preserving subsequent HTTP error classification and unrelated link-check behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if fallback logic is duplicated or exception handling is broadened through unrelated paths; cap at 2 if the edit can dereference HTTPError-only fields on TooManyRedirects, changes only the outer classifier, or leaves invalid syntax; score 1 if no applicable implementation is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: Visible repository diff or post-edit source content overrides commentary and claimed behavior; syntax-check output may confirm parseability but cannot establish semantic correctness by itself.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a mentioned exception name, a broad outer catch, duplicated GET code, or a proposed edit for a correct narrowly applied fallback.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible applied code that imports or otherwise resolves TooManyRedirects and catches it at the HEAD-to-GET fallback boundary.
