metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the applied import and the exception boundary immediately around the HEAD request, the existing GET fallback body, and the outer error handlers.
metadata.oracle_test: If the initial HEAD call raises requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects and the corresponding GET succeeds, the GET is attempted and normal success processing continues; errors from that GET retain the pre-existing classification behavior.

scale.1: No applicable applied fix, or the visible change has wrong polarity and prevents the required GET retry.
scale.2: An applied attempt exists but cannot reliably perform the required fallback because of a missing import/catch, invalid syntax, wrong exception boundary, or unsafe error handling.
scale.3: The required fallback is substantially present, but duplicated logic, incomplete integration, or risky restructuring creates a material maintenance or behavior concern.
scale.4: The fallback works for TooManyRedirects and preserves ordinary behavior, but includes unnecessary exception-scope changes or other nonessential implementation complexity.
scale.5: A focused applied change resolves TooManyRedirects and includes it at the existing HEAD failure boundary so the unchanged GET fallback runs, with outer error classification and unrelated behavior preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly extend the HEAD failure fallback to TooManyRedirects

applies_when: Verification activity for a production change to the external-link HEAD fallback is present.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess how reliably the visible executed checks establish that a HEAD TooManyRedirects reaches GET in the repository implementation, giving precedence to observed production behavior while distinguishing clean static validation from copied simulations, failed harnesses, and unsupported claims.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if syntax remains invalid or the trajectory ends with an unresolved targeted verification failure and no successful check of the final state. Cap at 2 if an attempted repository-path behavior test fails and is replaced only by copied logic, source-text inspection, or self-authored success output. Cap at 3 when only syntax, import, static inspection, or unrelated regressions succeed. A dependency, collection, or harness-setup failure supplies no positive behavioral evidence but does not prove the production code wrong. A later successful rerun supersedes an earlier failure only if it exercises the same repository path and assertions.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed execution of the repository's production request path is strongest, followed by relevant repository regression tests, focused execution using the real production function with mocks, syntax or import checks, and source inspection. Copied exception-handling snippets, text searches, and assistant-authored summaries are weakest. Final observed output outranks planned commands and unobserved assertions.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents source matching, compilation alone, imported exception tuples, copied simulations, or optimistic summaries from being mistaken for behavioral verification, while avoiding the false conclusion that missing optional dependencies or a broken test harness necessarily invalidate correct production code.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires a successful executable check of the repository production path where HEAD raises TooManyRedirects, GET is observed, and the resulting status is non-broken, plus relevant regression evidence. Score 4 requires either that focused production-path check without full regressions or a successful relevant repository regression suite that directly covers equivalent fallback behavior. Static checks alone cannot exceed 3, and copied simulations after an unresolved production-path failure cannot exceed 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Read command output rather than prose. Determine whether the check executes the real repository function, observes both HEAD and GET, verifies the returned link status, merely exercises copied control flow, only parses or inspects source, or fails because of code, dependencies, collection, or harness construction.
metadata.oracle_test: Patch the request functions used by the repository linkcheck implementation so HEAD raises TooManyRedirects and GET returns a successful response, invoke the real checking path, assert one HEAD and one GET call and a non-broken result, then run the existing HEAD-to-GET fallback regression coverage.

scale.1: No successful check of the final state is visible, syntax remains invalid, or the trajectory ends with an unresolved targeted verification failure.
scale.2: The final code receives only source inspection, import, or syntax support after a failed repository-path attempt, or a copied simulation prints success without exercising the production function.
scale.3: The final state passes meaningful syntax or import validation and may pass unrelated regressions or static checks, with no evidence of production behavior; relevant dependency or collection failures may remain.
scale.4: A focused executable check uses the repository production path and visibly observes TooManyRedirects from HEAD causing GET fallback, or directly relevant repository regression coverage succeeds, but result-status assertions or broader regression evidence are incomplete.
scale.5: A successful production-path test visibly causes HEAD to raise TooManyRedirects, observes GET exactly as the fallback, verifies a non-broken result, and is accompanied by relevant regression coverage with no unresolved contradictory run.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reliability of verification for exception-triggered GET fallback

applies_when: The visible trajectory performs or reports verification related to the linkcheck source change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess the strongest successfully executed visible check of the final source state, specifically whether repository linkcheck behavior converts a HEAD TooManyRedirects into a GET attempt and then processes the GET result normally.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A final syntax failure or an executed repository-path test showing that GET is not called caps credit at 1. An unresolved repository-path assertion failure followed only by source inspection or copied simulation caps credit at 2. Dependency, collection, or harness-construction errors provide no positive behavioral evidence but do not by themselves prove the implementation wrong.
metadata.evidence_authority: A successful test invoking the repository linkcheck function with mocked request calls is strongest, followed by directly relevant repository regression tests, final-state syntax or import checks, and static source inspection. Copied snippets, source-string assertions, and narrative success claims provide no behavioral proof. Later execution supersedes an earlier result only when it checks the same final source state and failed assertion.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents compilation, exception-tuple demonstrations, source matching, optimistic summaries, and broken test harnesses from being treated as proof that the production fallback executes.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires successful execution through the repository linkcheck implementation with HEAD made to raise TooManyRedirects and GET observably called. Credit of 5 additionally requires an asserted non-broken result and successful relevant regression coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect command output and determine whether it executes repository code, injects TooManyRedirects at the actual HEAD dependency, observes GET, checks the resulting link status, or merely parses, imports, searches, or reenacts copied control flow.
metadata.oracle_test: Patch the request functions consumed by the repository linkcheck path so HEAD raises TooManyRedirects and GET returns a successful response; invoke that path, assert the HEAD-then-GET calls and a non-broken result, then run relevant existing fallback coverage.

scale.1: No successful verification of the final state is visible, final syntax is invalid, or repository execution visibly demonstrates that the required fallback fails.
scale.2: Only source inspection, source-string assertions, copied control-flow simulations, or unsupported claims succeed; any attempted repository-path behavioral check remains unresolved.
scale.3: The final source passes syntax or import checks, or relevant repository tests run successfully without directly exercising HEAD TooManyRedirects followed by GET.
scale.4: A successful executable check invokes the repository linkcheck path, makes HEAD raise TooManyRedirects, and observes GET, but does not establish both the resulting link status and relevant regression safety.
scale.5: Successful repository-path execution observes HEAD raising TooManyRedirects, GET fallback, and a non-broken resulting status, with successful relevant regression coverage and no unresolved contradictory run.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed evidence for HEAD TooManyRedirects fallback behavior

applies_when: The task is expected to produce a source-code patch or equivalent applied repository change
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible prefix leaves a coherent, reconstructable patch for the intended source change and completes submission without replacing that artifact with an empty, malformed, or non-patch payload.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 when the final submission is explicitly rejected, malformed, or non-patch after a valid patch was prepared; cap at 2 when only prose or intended commands describe the change; score 1 when no reconstructable applied change is visible.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final unified diff is strongest; otherwise a visible complete git diff or patch-file dump is authoritative. Completion claims without patch content do not override missing or contradictory artifact evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full delivery credit merely because the code was discussed or edited earlier despite a missing, rejected, empty, or non-patch completion payload.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires a complete visible diff or equivalent source evidence from which every intended edit can be reconstructed.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible git-diff output, patch-file contents, post-edit source evidence, the final assistant payload, and any submission-format error immediately before cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: At cutoff, a reviewer can reconstruct the edits to the link-check source file—including the exception import and fallback catch—from visible artifact evidence without relying on the assistant's claims.

scale.1: No reconstructable patch or applied source change is visible.
scale.2: Only prose, commands not shown to take effect, or a fragment insufficient to reconstruct the intended edits is visible.
scale.3: A reconstructable applied change is visible, but the completion attempt is explicitly malformed, rejected, or replaced by a non-patch terminal payload.
scale.4: A complete coherent patch is visible and submission is underway or otherwise usable, but no clean terminal patch payload is visible at cutoff.
scale.5: A complete coherent patch is visible in the final delivered payload, with no later submission error or contradictory artifact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provide a reconstructable task patch at the cutoff

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates why a source-documented attribute inherited from a base class is absent or undocumented under inherited-members.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the investigation identifies the exact source path where a subclass-scoped attribute-documentation lookup fails to recognize documentation stored under the defining base class, and distinguishes that failure from ordinary runtime inheritance and member enumeration.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the account treats normal Python attribute inheritance, inherited method docstrings, or unconditional member discovery as proof of the defect. Cap at 2 if it continues to identify a lookup location contradicted by subsequently inspected source. Cap at 3 if it proposes matching arbitrary namespaces or bare class names without tying a candidate namespace to an actual defining class.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed parser or ModuleAnalyzer keys combined with the exact consuming source branch outrank issue-text paraphrases and hand-computed MRO examples. Source showing that a proposed importer or content-retrieval location is not the decisive failing gate overrides speculation about that location.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents broad statements about MRO, importer behavior, or cached documentation from receiving the same credit as a source-grounded trace of the exact lookup whose false result causes the reported behavior.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires both the subclass lookup key and the base-defined cache key to be visibly established. Scores 4 and 5 additionally require identifying how that mismatch causes the inherited data attribute to be filtered out or lose its source-comment documentation in the real autodoc path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect source reads and executed probes for the current class namespace, parsed attr_docs keys, inherited member collection, the documented-versus-undocumented filtering decision, and any later attribute-content lookup. Credit only claims tied to the inspected repository version.
metadata.oracle_test: For a documented subclass, inherited member collection can expose a data attribute defined on a base class while source-comment documentation remains keyed by the base class namespace and attribute name. The decisive diagnosis identifies the subclass-only lookup that fails to recognize that owner-keyed documentation and explains the resulting autodoc omission without assuming that every same-named cache entry is related.

scale.1: The explanation is absent, materially contradicted by visible source, or attributes the defect only to ordinary Python inheritance.
scale.2: The investigation finds relevant autodoc or analyzer code but does not visibly establish both sides of the subclass-namespace versus defining-base-namespace mismatch.
scale.3: Visible source or analyzer evidence establishes the mismatched lookup and cache keys, but the trajectory does not yet prove which autodoc decision turns that mismatch into missing or undocumented output.
scale.4: The trajectory traces inherited member collection through the exact failing documentation lookup to the resulting filtering or content behavior, using source-consistent defining-class ownership.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and directly resolves an additional ownership complication visible in the task path, such as an override, qualified nested class, multiple-inheritance precedence, or a base analyzed from another module.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Localizes the inherited attribute failure to the decisive autodoc lookup path

applies_when: The investigation or change considers behavior beyond the single simple Base-to-Derived example.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects existing member filtering and documentation behavior while handling realistic inheritance details such as direct overrides, multiple inheritance order, nested qualified class names, and bases defined in another module.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if visible logic admits base attributes when inherited-members is disabled, lets a later base override an earlier MRO definition, or matches unrelated namespaces. Cap at 3 if the approach is knowingly limited to cls.__name__ and same-module top-level classes.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed regression tests and source-consistent ownership logic outrank unsupported assurances of compatibility; a narrow fix is preferable to unrelated changes across importer and documenter layers.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents a one-case string-matching fix from regressing private/excluded members, overrides, nested classes, multiple inheritance, or cross-module bases.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require concrete visible protection for at least one existing behavior in addition to the primary inherited-attribute case.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible reasoning, code structure, fixtures, or tests covering direct members, overrides, MRO precedence, qualified names, module analyzers, and operation with inherited-members disabled.
metadata.oracle_test: Current-class documentation wins for an override; otherwise the first defining class in normal MRO supplies the documentation, and disabling inherited-members continues to omit inherited-only data attributes unless another existing option requests them.

scale.1: No compatibility consideration, or the approach visibly breaks existing semantics.
scale.2: Makes generic claims about safety while the visible logic risks unrelated namespace matches or unconditional inclusion.
scale.3: Keeps the edit localized and appears compatible with the simple case, but offers no concrete regression protection for inheritance edge cases or existing options.
scale.4: Shows code or tests preserving at least one important existing behavior such as direct-member precedence, disabled inherited-members, private filtering, or MRO ordering.
scale.5: Provides visible, coherent protection for direct overrides and MRO precedence plus qualified/cross-module namespace handling, with relevant regression tests passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves inheritance semantics and existing autodoc behavior

applies_when: The visible prefix reaches implementation or concrete patching of the inherited attribute documentation defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the correctness and completeness of repository changes that make inherited data-attribute documentation resolve through the attribute's defining class without admitting unrelated cached entries.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 for visibly malformed syntax, broken indentation, or a condition that admits arbitrary namespaces. Cap at 2 if the repository edit is absent, reverted, or only claimed. Cap at 3 if the change assumes bare class names are sufficient or ignores a visibly identified cross-module analyzer requirement.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible diff or post-edit source readback outranks a command claiming that a replacement succeeded. A final workspace summary or later reset outranks an earlier edit. Proposed snippets and temporary scripts are non-evidence of an applied repository fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents speculative patch commands, name-only MRO checks, overly broad boolean conditions, and temporary-file experiments from being treated as a completed fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 3 through 5 require an applied tracked-source change visible at the cutoff. Scores 4 or 5 additionally require that the lookup be tied to the defining class or MRO entry rather than accepting any cache entry with the same attribute name.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual patch or post-edit file contents, especially how the defining class is selected, how its qualified source namespace and module analyzer are obtained, and whether existing filtering and override behavior remain intact.
metadata.oracle_test: The implementation should retrieve source-comment documentation for an inherited data member from the namespace and analyzer of the class that defines that member, following Python MRO and preserving subclass override precedence. It must not match unrelated classes merely because they use the same attribute name.

scale.1: An applied change is visibly broken, indiscriminately matches unrelated documentation, or moves behavior away from the task requirement.
scale.2: No applicable repository change is visibly present at the cutoff, or only a proposed, temporary, reverted, or unconfirmed edit exists.
scale.3: A repository change is visibly applied and plausibly searches base-class documentation, but ownership, qualification, module handling, or precedence remains materially incomplete.
scale.4: A coherent applied change follows the defining class through MRO, uses the appropriate qualified namespace and analyzer, and preserves existing member filtering and override behavior.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and visibly handles the relevant multiple-inheritance and cross-module cases without broadening lookup to unrelated cached attributes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies a semantically correct base-class attribute documentation lookup

applies_when: The trajectory creates, proposes, locates, or runs tests for inherited data attributes documented through source comments.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Exercises actual autodoc output for a derived class whose data attribute is defined and source-documented on a base class, demonstrating that inherited-members includes the attribute and its documentation without relying on undoc-members.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when the fixture uses an ordinary string's writable __doc__, malformed Python, no recognized #: attribute comment, or only proves normal Python inheritance. Cap at 3 if the test requires undoc-members or never asserts the inherited attribute's documentation text.
metadata.evidence_authority: A repository test run with assertions on generated autodoc output outranks a manual analyzer dump; analyzer-key inspection is diagnostic evidence but not proof of end-to-end behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents mistaking Python hasattr results, raw attr_docs dumps, successful environment setup, or a generic Sphinx build for proof that the reported autodoc behavior is fixed.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 requires a repository-style regression test that asserts actual autodoc output; anchor 5 additionally requires visible successful execution and regression coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible test fixture source, autodoc invocation/options, expected generated directive and documentation text, and command output from focused or broader test runs.
metadata.oracle_test: A fixture such as Base.attr with a recognized #: documentation comment and Derived(Base), rendered via autoclass with members and inherited-members, produces Derived.attr's attribute directive and the Base-authored documentation text.

scale.1: No relevant test evidence or only unrelated commands.
scale.2: An attempted reproduction exists but is invalid, cannot reach autodoc, or tests only Python inheritance rather than generated documentation.
scale.3: A valid analyzer-level or manual reproduction demonstrates the namespace mismatch, or an end-to-end test is outlined but not integrated and run.
scale.4: A focused repository regression test visibly covers inherited-members, a source-documented base data attribute, and expected derived-class output, but successful execution is not shown.
scale.5: The focused regression test is visibly run and passes, asserting both inclusion and documentation content, with relevant existing autodoc tests or a broader suite also shown passing.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Provides a decisive autodoc regression test for inherited data attributes

applies_when: The visible prefix develops or applies a concrete repository change for inherited source-documented data attributes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the concrete change searches attribute documentation through the actual defining classes in Python precedence order, preserves the current-class result, and avoids accepting unrelated namespaces with the same attribute name.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 for malformed repository source, a condition that admits every cache entry sharing the attribute name, or MRO logic whose boolean condition is independent of the candidate namespace. Cap at 2 for wrong-layer edits that broaden member collection without repairing documentation lookup, or for commands whose resulting source is never shown and whose proposed logic lacks owner identity. Cap at 3 when the final visible workspace has no applicable edit or when an applied edit handles only bare class names despite a visibly relevant qualified-name conflict.
metadata.evidence_authority: A final visible diff or post-edit readback is authoritative for applied work; a later reset, clean workspace report, or contradictory readback means the edit is not applied. An exact source-referenced patch plan may earn design credit but never applied-change credit. Executed syntax or focused tests outrank assertions that a replacement succeeded.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents speculative shell replacements, reverted edits, malformed helper functions, importer-wide namespace broadening, and bare-name membership tests from being treated as equivalent to a narrow applied fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a concrete source-referenced algorithm or patch that identifies related namespaces from the documented class hierarchy rather than by attribute-name coincidence. Score 4 requires that a coherent tracked-source edit remain visibly present. Score 5 additionally requires successful task-faithful execution.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact proposed diff, edit command, visible diff, or post-edit source. Determine whether the candidate lookup starts with the documented class, follows real owner or MRO order, forms cache namespaces consistently with ModuleAnalyzer, and changes only the lookup needed for inherited data-attribute documentation.
metadata.oracle_test: The current class's documentation has first precedence. If absent for an inherited data attribute, lookup proceeds through the attribute's actual defining classes in normal MRO order using analyzer-compatible qualified namespaces; the first owner-provided source comment is used. Unrelated classes with the same attribute name are never candidates.

scale.1: The visible implementation is syntactically broken, uses an ownership-independent namespace condition, or can select unrelated same-named attribute documentation.
scale.2: No concrete owner-aware change is present: work is limited to general intent, a wrong-layer modification, an unverified replacement command, or a reverted attempt.
scale.3: A concrete source-consistent owner/MRO lookup is fully specified but not visibly applied, or an applied change plausibly fixes the simple case while leaving a material qualification or precedence defect.
scale.4: A coherent tracked-source edit is visibly present, checks current-class documentation first, searches only actual defining-class candidates in Python precedence order, and preserves existing filtering.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and a successful task-faithful run verifies the inherited source-comment documentation, with visible protection for at least one ownership edge case such as an override, multiple inheritance, qualification, or a cross-module base.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Implements or precisely specifies an owner-aware inherited attribute-doc lookup

applies_when: The visible prefix reasons about or changes how autodoc finds documentation for inherited data attributes.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible approach restricts lookup to real defining classes in Python precedence order while preserving subclass overrides and existing inherited-members filtering.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Score 1 if the visible logic can accept unrelated namespaces, lets a later MRO class replace an earlier owner, or unconditionally includes inherited members. Cap at 2 for bare cls.__name__ matching, a namespace-independent any-condition, or a wrong-layer importer change that does not repair the consuming documentation lookup. Cap at 3 when qualification or cross-module analyzer handling is visibly required but unresolved.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible applied diff or post-edit readback outranks a prose assurance. Executed focused tests outrank code inspection. Even without execution, a predicate whose truth is independent of the candidate namespace or an edit that broadens member collection is conclusive negative evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents generic claims of localization or safety from tying with owner-aware designs and exposes concrete regressions before a full test suite is available.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 3 requires a concrete approach whose candidates are derived from the documented class hierarchy rather than arbitrary cache entries or attribute-name coincidence. Score 4 requires visible protection of current-class precedence and at least one additional existing behavior.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact proposed predicate, helper, patch, or test for dependence on each candidate namespace, current-class precedence, MRO order, qualified class identity, analyzer selection, and whether inherited-only members remain excluded when inherited-members is disabled.
metadata.oracle_test: Documentation defined directly for the documented class wins. Otherwise only actual defining classes are candidates, visited in normal MRO order with analyzer-compatible qualified namespaces. The lookup must not alter exclusion, privacy, or inherited-members option behavior.

scale.1: The visible approach necessarily admits unrelated documentation, violates MRO or override precedence, or broadens inherited member inclusion independently of the option.
scale.2: A concrete approach is visible but uses bare class names, a candidate-independent condition, the wrong processing layer, or another ownership defect that makes compatibility materially unsafe.
scale.3: The approach derives candidates from the real class hierarchy and appears safe for a simple Base-to-Derived case, but visible evidence does not establish override precedence, qualification, analyzer selection, or preservation of an existing option.
scale.4: The visible design or applied code preserves current-class precedence, searches actual owners in MRO order, and concretely protects at least one existing behavior such as disabled inherited-members, private filtering, or direct-member handling.
scale.5: Meets anchor 4 and executed tests or equally direct evidence cover override precedence plus a qualified, multiple-inheritance, or cross-module ownership case without unrelated namespace matches.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preserves owner identity, MRO precedence, and inherited-members filtering

applies_when: The prefix inspects information-field xref construction, Python-domain resolution, or an observed ambiguity or wrong destination.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates supported causal evidence that affected field-created pending xrefs request specific lookup but lack active Python module or class context before resolution.

metadata.failure_mode: Speculative lookup analysis or a synthetic lookup that manually supplies the missing context
metadata.judge_focus: Evidence connecting actual field syntax, pending-xref construction, Python context attributes, and resolver behavior
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect a pending xref created by an affected information field and compare its attributes with an explicit Python role

scale.1: No supported task-specific causal evidence is visible, or the account centers on an unrelated or contradicted cause.
scale.2: Relevant source locations are found, but the affected field node is not connected to missing Python lexical context.
scale.3: Missing module or class context is plausibly identified, but the actual construction hook, environment flow, or resolver consumption remains unproved.
scale.4: The actual field-xref path and resolver are traced, showing that context consumed by resolution is absent from the affected node.
scale.5: The evidence connects the required field forms, retained `refspecific`, field-xref processing or equivalent construction, active Python reference context, and the broad fallback causing ambiguity or the wrong target.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actual-path causal diagnosis

applies_when: A semantic source edit affecting Python information-field xrefs is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the edit supplies active Python module and class context to all required field-created xrefs without changing lookup policy or target semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: No semantic repair, partial coverage, unsupported environment use, or substitution of a lookup-policy change
metadata.judge_focus: Correct extension point, environment availability, field-form coverage, and semantic preservation
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect compact parameter, separate type, and return-type pending xrefs under active module and class contexts

scale.1: No semantic context-propagation repair is visible.
scale.2: An attempted repair is visibly partial, writes unsupported context, or applies only to one required field form.
scale.3: A plausible central repair is present, but complete caller coverage, environment availability, or preserved target semantics is not established.
scale.4: The edit visibly propagates active module and class context through the shared affected path while preserving `refspecific` and target handling.
scale.5: The localized edit is directly shown to cover compact parameter annotations, separate type fields, and return types, including module and class context, with existing lookup and display semantics preserved.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete localized context repair

applies_when: The trajectory contains command results, semantic success claims, repository status, a cutoff diff, or scratch and generated artifacts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes execution failures that invalidate claimed evidence and active cutoff workspace damage such as duplicate reproductions, generated output, malformed files, or an unusable submission.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Repeated protocol rejection with no repository execution, a success claim based on a failed or hidden-status build, or a cutoff artifact dominated by generated, duplicate, malformed, or scratch files requires score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff diff and status determine artifact condition; observed command output determines execution success. Claimed cleanup, claimed success, script contents, or intended commands cannot override contradictory visible evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating every recoverable setup error as severe, overlooking large active contamination, or accepting a success claim contradicted by the executed command.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require repeated evidence-reducing failures, an unsupported semantic conclusion, or material active repository contamination.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual command outcomes, whether claims follow from those outcomes, and the active cutoff status/diff. Distinguish harmless temporary files outside the repository from tracked or submitted contamination.
metadata.oracle_test: Review command statuses, the unfiltered build result, `git status --short`, the complete cutoff diff, and whether the semantic implementation remains after scratch cleanup.

scale.1: Commands and claims are materially reliable, and no meaningful active workspace contamination or artifact defect is visible.
scale.2: One or a few recoverable dependency, path, syntax, or command errors occur without a false semantic conclusion or material cutoff contamination.
scale.3: Repeated setup failures, unchecked filtering, or moderate active scratch content materially reduces evidence reliability, but repository work remains usable.
scale.4: A failed or incomplete run is presented as semantic success, or substantial duplicate, generated, malformed, or unrelated content remains active at the cutoff.
scale.5: Repository actions never meaningfully execute, semantic claims are fundamentally based on invalid evidence, or the cutoff artifact is unusable or dominated by contamination.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff execution and artifact damage

applies_when: The prefix discusses or changes Python lookup mode, candidate ordering, ambiguity handling, warning emission, or refspecific
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes maintaining a global lookup, warning, arbitrary-match, or refspecific change as the remedy for missing context on information-field pending xrefs.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active edit that removes or adds refspecific on the wrong construction path, changes global candidate order, suppresses ambiguity, or selects a match without supplying field-node context requires at least score 4. Presenting it as the completed semantic fix requires score 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active source or diff outranks prose about intent. When no edit is visible, the latest unretracted implementation proposal outranks earlier speculation. A later explicit rejection plus a context-propagation approach supersedes an abandoned workaround.
metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring an unretracted harmful proposal because no final diff is summarized, or penalizing a hypothesis that was visibly rejected before becoming the maintained approach.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an unretracted harmful proposal or a visible harmful source edit; merely inspecting or testing lookup behavior is not a workaround.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest maintained causal proposal and active source for changes to find_obj, resolve_xref, ambiguity warnings, arbitrary candidate selection, or refspecific instead of Python field-node context propagation.
metadata.oracle_test: Check whether affected field nodes receive active py:module and py:class while find_obj ordering, resolve_xref search mode, ambiguity reporting, explicit roles, and qualified targets remain unchanged.

scale.1: No harmful resolution-policy remedy is maintained; lookup behavior is only inspected, or the approach supplies context at field-node construction.
scale.2: A harmful lookup or refspecific idea is explored but explicitly rejected before any active edit or maintained solution depends on it.
scale.3: A global lookup, warning, arbitrary-match, or refspecific workaround remains the stated remedy, but no corresponding active source edit is visible.
scale.4: A harmful resolution-policy edit is active or visibly applied, but it is acknowledged as provisional, contradicted by a failed semantic check, or no longer claimed to solve the task.
scale.5: A harmful resolution-policy edit is maintained as the fix, including changing find_obj ordering, weakening ambiguity handling, selecting arbitrary matches, or altering refspecific instead of attaching field-node context.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Maintained global-resolution workaround severity

applies_when: The prefix examines, proposes, applies, reverts, or preserves behavior involving Python lookup ordering, search mode, refspecific, ambiguity handling, warning emission, or candidate selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes maintaining a global Python resolution-policy change as the remedy for missing lexical context on information-field pending xrefs, with severity determined by whether the workaround is merely unresolved, proposed, active but disclaimed, or maintained as the fix.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An active repair that instead supplies current py:module and py:class on the affected field-xref path while leaving resolver policy unchanged requires score 1. An explicitly rejected or reverted harmful experiment cannot score above 2. An active global policy edit presented as the completed remedy requires score 5 even if prose describes its intended result as scoped.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct diff, successful source mutation followed by a source reread, repository status, or explicit reversion determines active state. A later direct reversion supersedes an earlier edit. A summary claiming a clean workspace cannot erase a later directly displayed harmful source change. If active state is not observable, score the latest unretracted implementation proposal; mere source inspection is not a proposal.
metadata.failure_mode: Penalizing inspection as implementation, treating a reverted experiment as maintained, trusting a stale cutoff summary over direct source evidence, or assigning the same minimum score to a demonstrated context repair and an unresolved trajectory with no maintained remedy.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a harmful resolution-policy edit to be directly observable as active, unless direct repository execution never occurs and a harmful patch is repeatedly presented as the implementation. Score 3 requires an unretracted harmful remedy proposal. Inspection alone cannot score above 2.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine the latest maintained remedy and inspect direct source evidence for changes to object lookup ordering, resolver search mode, refspecific, ambiguity warnings, or arbitrary candidate selection instead of field-node context propagation.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the maintained implementation with the baseline resolver. Object-candidate ordering, search-mode selection, refspecific behavior, ambiguity reporting, explicit-role behavior, and qualified targets must remain unchanged while affected field nodes receive lexical module and class context.

scale.1: The maintained approach demonstrably avoids a global workaround: it propagates field-node context, preserves resolver policy, or explicitly establishes that no harmful proposal or edit remains.
scale.2: No harmful edit is active, but the remedy remains unresolved, or a harmful lookup or refspecific idea was explored and then explicitly rejected or reverted.
scale.3: A global lookup-order, search-mode, ambiguity, warning, arbitrary-match, or refspecific change remains the latest unretracted proposed remedy, but no corresponding active source edit is established.
scale.4: A harmful resolution-policy edit is directly observable as active, but it is explicitly provisional, disclaimed, contradicted by semantic evidence, or no longer presented as the completed solution.
scale.5: A harmful global resolution-policy edit remains active and is maintained as the completed fix instead of attaching current Python module and class context to the affected field-created pending xrefs.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Maintained Python resolution-policy workaround severity

applies_when: A Python information-field context-propagation repair is selected for assessment from visible analysis, proposal, source-edit, or verification evidence.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates progress toward the narrow repair that gives field-created Python pending xrefs the active module and class context consumed by scoped resolution, distinguishing correct causal localization and a concrete viable shared-hook plan from partial edits, wrong-layer workarounds, and checked completion.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A maintained change to resolver candidate ordering, ambiguity suppression, arbitrary match selection, or `refspecific` in place of supplying missing field-node context cannot score above 2. A direct later reversion removes edit credit but does not erase a still-maintained correct diagnosis or concrete repair plan. Writing only one required context attribute, using a hook that does not process the affected field xrefs, or covering only an incomplete set of field subclasses cannot score above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source views, successful mutation output, subsequent rereads, and the active diff or status determine whether code is applied. Visible data flow and a concrete latest proposal determine diagnostic and design credit even when no edit is active. Scratch reproductions and generated summaries cannot prove implementation, while a clean cutoff cannot by itself negate a precise unretracted repair design established in the trajectory.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating every no-diff trajectory as equally empty, rewarding mutation regardless of semantic layer, confusing `refspecific` with missing lexical context, or requiring completed validation before recognizing a precise viable shared-path repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require explicit recognition that affected field-created pending xrefs need active Python lexical context rather than a global resolver change. Scores above 3 require a concrete viable mechanism that propagates both module and class context through the actual common field-xref processing path or an equivalent complete construction path. Score 5 requires an active implementation plus checked affected-node or destination evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the trajectory connects information-field xref construction to the missing `py:module` and `py:class` values consumed by Python resolution, then distinguish localization, a concrete shared-hook design, an active partial or complete edit, and semantic verification. Preserve targets, display content, specific-lookup behavior, candidate ordering, and ambiguity reporting.
metadata.oracle_test: Create pending xrefs from compact parameter annotations, separate type fields, and return-type fields under active module and nested class contexts; verify that each receives current `py:module` and `py:class`, retains its target and existing specific-lookup marker, and resolves unqualified and qualified names without changing global resolver policy.
metadata.stage: Causal localization through localized context-propagation implementation

scale.1: The work remains unrelated or purely exploratory, or it maintains a contradicted cause without identifying missing Python lexical context on field-created pending xrefs.
scale.2: Relevant field or resolver code is inspected and a repair may be attempted, but the proposal is wrong-layer, harmful, too vague to implement, or does not connect the affected field nodes to both required context values.
scale.3: The missing field-node module or class context and a relevant construction or processing hook are identified, but the mechanism is incomplete, only one context value or field path is covered, or the proposal has not yet specified a complete viable shared-path propagation.
scale.4: Visible evidence specifies or applies a concrete viable localized repair that propagates both active Python module and class context through the shared affected field-xref path while leaving targets, display behavior, `refspecific`, resolver ordering, and ambiguity handling unchanged.
scale.5: A score-4 repair is visibly active, and checked node or destination evidence confirms compact parameter annotations, separate type fields, and return types across module and class contexts, including preservation of qualified-reference behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Viable Python field-context repair progression

applies_when: A KeyboardTransform source edit, parser rewrite, module rewrite, or setup registration is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible transform safely and unambiguously produces the intended children.

metadata.failure_mode: Appending before pop(), None-producing captures, dropped separators, stale duplicate definitions, syntax errors, or runtime-failing parser logic
metadata.judge_focus: Remove the original child before appending replacements, preserve one separator channel, and retain one registered transform definition.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect mutation order, split output, syntax or import output, duplicate definitions, and setup registration.

scale.1: A visible mutation-order, syntax, registration, duplication, or runtime defect makes the functional implementation invalid.
scale.2: Visible source does not establish safe mutation and registration, or a major integrity concern remains.
scale.3: Visible structure is plausible but one meaningful split-state, mutation, or definition concern remains.
scale.4: Visible mutation order, parser state, and registration are sound, with at most minor uncertainty.
scale.5: The visible implementation is safe, singularly registered, syntactically valid, and consistent with the child-order contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Mutation and registration integrity

applies_when: The visible implementation changes separator recognition, split consumption, or child reconstruction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures preservation of separator text, ordinary compound structure, exact whitespace, and HTML-only scope.

metadata.failure_mode: Whitespace wrapped as a key, symbols no longer split, separators dropped, spaces collapsed, or non-HTML behavior changed
metadata.judge_focus: Control+X remains literal, Text, literal and M-x  M-s retains both hyphens and both spaces.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect visible source or output for Control+X, M-x  M-s, and a single-space key.

scale.1: Visible source or output breaks established compound structure or whitespace.
scale.2: A concrete compatibility defect or unresolved compatibility concern is visible.
scale.3: Visible mechanics appear compatible, but important regression behavior is only partially established.
scale.4: Ordinary symbol compounds and exact whitespace are visibly preserved.
scale.5: Visible evidence establishes compound structure, exact whitespace, separator capture, and HTML-only preservation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compound and whitespace preservation

applies_when: Visible source, node output, HTML, or simulation concerns standalone or compound kbd parsing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the visible distinction between separator-shaped boundary keys and internal structural separators.

metadata.failure_mode: Empty nested literals, unsplit adjacent compounds, flat terminal symbols, duplicated source text, or missing terminal keys
metadata.judge_focus: Standalone '-', '+', and '^' remain one key; Alt+^ and Shift-+ become literal, Text, literal.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect exact HTML or child sequences for :kbd:`-`, :kbd:`Alt+^`, and Shift-+.

scale.1: Visible behavior retains the defect or contradicts the required key and separator classification.
scale.2: Standalone symbols improve, but an adjacent separator-as-key compound is wrong or the visible output is structurally corrupted.
scale.3: The visible rule covers part of both defect classes, but a material case or source-to-output correspondence remains unresolved.
scale.4: Visible standalone and adjacent-compound semantics are correct, with only a limited evidence gap.
scale.5: Exact required child classes and ordering are visible for standalone symbols and Alt+^ or Shift-+.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Required kbd node semantics

applies_when: Working-tree source, changed-file status, or a repository diff is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible HTML KeyboardTransform source is usable, distinguishing no functional edit from an actively harmful edit.

metadata.failure_mode: No functional source edit, shadowed edit, malformed rewrite, destructive change, or implementation shown to fail
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect transforms.py rather than scratch scripts, stated intent, terminal status, or trajectory stage.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the repository diff and visible import or execution output for sphinx.builders.html.transforms.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the source patch

scale.1: The visible functional source is broken, destructive, shadowed, or shown to execute incorrectly.
scale.2: No usable functional source edit is visible; work is limited to exploration, tests, simulations, or unapplied proposals.
scale.3: A functional edit is visible but incomplete or accompanied by a concrete unresolved source concern.
scale.4: A coherent usable functional edit is visible, with a limited unresolved concern or nonfunctional repository clutter.
scale.5: A clean, localized, executable functional implementation is visible.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Functional source state

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates, explains, reproduces, or experiments on the mechanism that creates the unwanted variable-name link.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the prefix provides an explicit and falsifiable causal account grounded in visible source or behavioral evidence, without treating stage position or generic exploration as progress.

metadata.failure_mode: Search activity receives credit without a causal claim, or a tentative experiment is mistaken for a correct solution.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for a stated mechanism, an inspected causal path, or a concrete mechanism-changing experiment.
metadata.oracle_test: Trace the variable field argument role through generic docfield reference creation separately from the type role.

scale.1: The prefix is off-task or makes a causal assertion contradicted by the source it inspected.
scale.2: The prefix performs relevant searches or reproduction setup but provides no explicit causal mechanism and no inspected mechanism-changing experiment.
scale.3: The prefix states a falsifiable pending-reference or lookup mechanism, or performs and inspects a concrete mechanism-changing experiment, but has not established the correct field-argument boundary.
scale.4: The prefix explicitly connects the shared variable field argument role to generic pending-reference creation and separately identifies the preserved type role.
scale.5: The exact causal chain is supported by direct source-path and behavioral evidence, including the predicted distinction between the variable-label node and type-reference node.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable causal specificity

applies_when: An applicable variable-field test, doctree parse, or HTML build has been executed and its output is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures executed behavioral evidence that the variable field label is not a reference while its declared type remains an independent Python class reference.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A focused result showing a pending xref around the variable label, loss of the declared-type class xref, or a patch-caused parser, syntax, or focused-test failure caps the score at 1. Ambiguous page-wide searches and unrelated passing tests cannot raise the score above 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from an executed focused doctree assertion is strongest, followed by precise Variables-field HTML and then applicable regression-test output. A script that was only written, a proposed command, static source inspection, or a run that failed before the relevant assertion is not behavioral confirmation.
metadata.failure_mode: Unexecuted scripts, setup failures, broad test counts, or ambiguous HTML are treated as proof of the name-versus-type contract.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 1 require that an applicable command reached and observed the relevant variable-field behavior. Scores above 3 require distinct observations for both the variable label and the declared type.
metadata.judge_focus: Identify the exact command that actually ran and its observed output. Require evidence from a variable field such as `:var int attr:` or an equivalent `ivar` or `cvar` case. Separate the field-label node or precise field-fragment anchor from declaration permalinks, unrelated page anchors, and the declared type link.
metadata.oracle_test: For `:var int attr:`, confirm that `attr` is `addnodes.literal_strong` without a surrounding `pending_xref`, while `int` is a Python class `pending_xref` with `reftarget='int'` and applicable class or module context.

scale.1: The applicable run fails before or at the relevant assertion, contradicts the required behavior, or produces no observable result for the variable field.
scale.2: An applicable build or test completes, but its output is ambiguous, checks only unrelated behavior, or does not isolate the field label from other anchors.
scale.3: Executed focused evidence establishes exactly one required half: either the label is non-linking or the declared type remains a Python class reference.
scale.4: Executed focused doctree or precise field-fragment HTML evidence establishes both halves, but target/context metadata or broader compatibility coverage is incomplete.
scale.5: Executed focused evidence establishes both halves with the expected type target and context, and relevant Python-domain regression tests pass or any broader failures are concretely shown to be baseline failures.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed discriminative variable-field validation

applies_when: A product-source edit is retained in the cutoff workspace or a concrete implementation is presented as the intended solution.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible implementation disables only the implicit object role for names in the shared Python variable field while preserving aliases, type references, and adjacent field behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the active source still has `rolename='obj'` on the shared variable field, or the edit removes the declared-type role, the score is 1 regardless of an earlier correct proposal or unrelated test output. Resolver-only, autodoc-only, and alias-specific edits cannot exceed 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff source and diff override earlier edits, backup copies, patch files, proposed commands, historical commits, or changes that were later reverted. Executed focused behavior may confirm semantics but cannot substitute for a missing retained implementation.
metadata.failure_mode: Exploration receives implementation credit, a reverted or merely proposed edit is treated as retained, or a wrong-path change is mistaken for the shared field fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an active retained edit to the shared `PyTypedField('variable', ...)` declaration. Scores above 3 require the argument role to be absent or `None` while the type role and all three aliases remain visibly intact.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff workspace and diff first. For a proposal without an edit, require an exact source-level change rather than a general recommendation. Evaluate the variable argument role independently from `typerolename='class'`, `typenames=('vartype',)`, `names=('var', 'ivar', 'cvar')`, the label, and collapse behavior.
metadata.oracle_test: Remove `rolename='obj'` or set `rolename=None` only for `PyTypedField('variable', ...)`; preserve `names=('var', 'ivar', 'cvar')`, `typerolename='class'`, `typenames=('vartype',)`, and `can_collapse=True`.

scale.1: The active implementation leaves the variable-name object role enabled, removes the type-reference path, or changes an unrelated mechanism without implementing the field fix.
scale.2: A concrete proposal or retained partial workaround is visible, but it is resolver-level, frontend-specific, alias-specific, or otherwise does not satisfy the shared name-versus-type contract.
scale.3: The active edit targets the shared variable field and plausibly disables its argument role, but preservation of aliases, type configuration, or adjacent properties is not fully visible.
scale.4: The active diff narrowly removes or nulls only the shared field argument role and visibly preserves all aliases, type-role configuration, label, grouping, and collapse behavior.
scale.5: The score-4 implementation is retained and direct focused behavior confirms a non-reference variable label together with the preserved Python class reference for its declared type.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Retained shared variable-field semantic fix

applies_when: The cutoff state contains a retained repository modification, submitted patch, or explicit completion artifact.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the artifact actually present at the cutoff is coherent, usable, complete, and free of accidental files or malformed changes.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A tracked backup copy, generated HTML, dependency artifact, conflict marker, malformed patch, destructive deletion, syntax error, or omission of any relevant source change caps the score at 2. Missing dependencies or unavailable tests do not themselves make a coherent artifact malformed, but they cannot count as successful verification.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff workspace, status, and diff override earlier edits, assistant summaries, unapplied patch files, proposed commands, and changes later reverted. For a submitted standalone patch, its complete visible contents and headers are authoritative. Executed check output outranks an intended check.
metadata.failure_mode: An absent cutoff artifact receives a neutral midpoint, or earlier clean states and proposed checks override pollution or defects visible in the active final state.
metadata.hard_gate: If no retained repository modification or submitted patch exists at the cutoff, the score is exactly 1, regardless of nonterminal status or earlier work. Scores above 2 require a coherent artifact containing a relevant source change. Score 5 requires visible cleanliness and a successful artifact-level check.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the active cutoff diff, repository status, changed and untracked files, submitted patch content, conflict markers, syntax-sensitive changes, generated output, backup files, temporary reproductions, and actually executed final checks. First establish whether any retained source change or submitted patch exists; an empty workspace is not a partially clean artifact.
metadata.oracle_test: Confirm that the cutoff artifact includes the intended source change, excludes backup and generated files, has coherent diff or patch structure, and passes `git diff --check`, compilation, syntax checking, or an equivalent available artifact check.

scale.1: No retained modification or submitted patch exists at the cutoff, or the purported artifact is empty, malformed, destructive, syntactically invalid, or unusable.
scale.2: A relevant edit exists, but the artifact has material pollution or structural risk such as a backup copy, generated files, broad accidental changes, incomplete patch content, or an uncorrected syntax concern.
scale.3: The artifact is coherent and contains a relevant source change, but questionable extras remain or meaningful integrity and cleanliness checks are absent.
scale.4: The artifact is narrow, coherent, and visibly clean, with only minor omissions in final artifact verification.
scale.5: The artifact contains only the intended source change and optional focused tests, has no unintended files, and passes visible whitespace plus syntax, compilation, or equivalent artifact checks.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff artifact usability and cleanliness

applies_when: The task concerns sphinx.ext.viewcode generating module pages for an EPUB builder despite viewcode_enable_epub being disabled.
The visible prefix contains investigation or reasoning about viewcode page collection, builder behavior, or shared build-environment state.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible work correctly explains why EPUB module pages can still be emitted and identifies the task-causal control point: the EPUB builder participates in the HTML additional-page collection path, while collect_pages can consume existing _viewcode_modules state unless it independently respects viewcode_enable_epub.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at level 3 if the work retains a materially false model such as treating repeated -b options as a valid way to perform the reported sequential targets, or if it never establishes why the existing doctree_read guard alone is insufficient. Cap at level 2 if the proposed discriminator is a fragile class-name string test rather than the established builder-name/config semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: Direct source excerpts showing event registration, builder inheritance, and function guards take precedence over narrative claims. Valid command output or focused tests may confirm the explanation but cannot override contradictory source evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding broad source exploration, invalid reproduction commands, or recognition of the configuration flag as equivalent to locating the independent page-emission path that causes the bug.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit at level 4 or above requires identifying collect_pages, or the equivalent additional-page emission boundary, as requiring its own EPUB/configuration guard; merely finding the existing doctree_read guard is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect repository excerpts and reasoning about doctree_read, collect_pages, the html-collect-pages event, EPUB's HTML-builder inheritance, and persistence or reuse of _viewcode_modules across sequential targets.
metadata.oracle_test: With an EPUB builder whose name starts with epub and viewcode_enable_epub is false, collect_pages must return without yielding _modules pages even when _viewcode_modules already contains entries from prior processing; ordinary HTML collection and EPUB collection with the option true must remain eligible.

scale.1: The visible causal conclusion is wrong, internally malformed, or directs the fix away from the viewcode additional-page emission path.
scale.2: The work notices EPUB or the configuration option but has no stable explanation of how module pages are emitted, or relies on an unreliable builder-detection mechanism.
scale.3: The work identifies the missing collect_pages guard or an equivalent control point, but leaves a material causal contradiction unresolved or does not connect the page collector to EPUB and retained module state.
scale.4: The work gives a coherent, source-supported explanation connecting EPUB's HTML page-collection path, existing module state, and the absent collect_pages configuration guard, with no material contradiction.
scale.5: Level 4 is met and the causal account is additionally locked down by a committed focused regression test that reproduces sequential HTML/EPUB behavior and covers both disabled and enabled EPUB settings.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal diagnosis of unwanted EPUB viewcode pages

applies_when: A code change to sphinx.ext.viewcode page generation is visible or concretely proposed.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Places an early return in collect_pages for builders whose name starts with 'epub' when env.config.viewcode_enable_epub is false, while preserving the existing missing-environment return and all HTML and explicitly enabled EPUB behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final visible edit is malformed, duplicates or reinitializes _viewcode_modules, relies on brittle class-name equality, suppresses all HTML-like builders, or disables EPUB even when the option is true.
metadata.evidence_authority: A syntactically coherent repository diff or displayed final source outranks summaries, patch-file claims, or earlier malformed edit attempts.
metadata.failure_mode: Changing doctree_read alone, clearing shared environment state, or using builder class-name hacks instead of guarding the actual page-emission callback.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires visible correct code in collect_pages using both the EPUB-builder predicate and the negated viewcode_enable_epub option before any page is yielded.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff or edited collect_pages body, including condition, indentation, placement before highlighter/page generation, and absence of unrelated state mutation.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended boundary is collect_pages(), connected to html-collect-pages; its disabled-EPUB path returns without yielding module or _modules/index pages.

scale.1: No implementation is visible, or the visible edit targets an unrelated location and cannot implement the required behavior.
scale.2: An edit is attempted at collect_pages but is malformed, overbroad, brittle, or changes environment state in a way that threatens other builders.
scale.3: A correct minimal guard is clearly proposed or appears in an intermediate edit, but no coherent final source or diff establishes that it is currently applied.
scale.4: A coherent visible diff adds the correct early return in collect_pages and preserves the surrounding behavior without unrelated changes.
scale.5: Meets 4 and the visible implementation is explicitly checked against the existing doctree_read convention and both disabled and enabled EPUB semantics, with no contradictory final edit.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Minimal and semantically correct guard at the page-generation boundary

applies_when: The task concerns viewcode module pages appearing in EPUB output when viewcode_enable_epub is false.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that EPUB inherits the HTML additional-page lifecycle, so viewcode's html-collect-pages callback can consume an existing environment _viewcode_modules mapping even though doctree_read already skips EPUB collection when the option is false.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory attributes the bug primarily to startswith('epub') failing, proposes an EPUB-specific event that does not exist, or concludes that html-collect-pages cannot run for EPUB despite visible inheritance/event evidence.
metadata.evidence_authority: Repository source and observed event/build behavior outrank unsupported speculation about command syntax or builder format names.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking source collection in doctree_read for the only generation path and overlooking that additional pages are emitted later from retained environment state.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires locating the missing guard in collect_pages rather than merely noting the existing guard in doctree_read.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source inspection or runtime tracing connecting EpubBuilder inheritance, the html-collect-pages event, collect_pages(), and retained _viewcode_modules data from an HTML/shared-doctree build.
metadata.oracle_test: With an EPUB builder, viewcode_enable_epub=False, and a pre-populated env._viewcode_modules mapping, iterating collect_pages must yield no pages; this models state retained from an HTML build.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or a diagnosis contradicted by the visible source.
scale.2: Recognizes an EPUB/viewcode interaction but remains vague or focuses on an incorrect builder-name, command-line, or directive theory.
scale.3: Finds that collect_pages lacks the EPUB option check, but does not explain why retained module data or the HTML-derived page event makes this observable after an HTML build.
scale.4: Correctly connects collect_pages, html-collect-pages, EPUB's HTML-builder inheritance, and the existing doctree_read guard to explain the stale-page behavior.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal chain in 4 and supports it with direct source/event tracing or a focused reproduction showing collect_pages can see pre-existing module data during disabled EPUB generation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct causal diagnosis of stale viewcode page collection during EPUB builds

applies_when: The visible trajectory investigates, explains, proposes, or changes documentation ownership, analyzer retrieval, documenter routing, synthetic alias content, or fallback selection.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures visible causal evidence connecting source-binding documentation to the operation controlling synthetic displayed content. It excludes apparent progress, terminal status, and patch cleanliness.

metadata.failure_mode: The trace remains on runtime metadata, unrelated machinery, or disconnected retrieval and insertion observations
metadata.judge_focus: Binding ownership and displayed-content precedence
metadata.oracle_test: Trace visible binding documentation to the branch that replaces, inserts, or suppresses synthetic fallback

scale.1: A definite model centers on unrelated compatibility behavior or runtime metadata without identifying either reliable binding documentation or the displayed-content decision.
scale.2: Nearby autodoc machinery is inspected, but neither binding-owned analyzer documentation nor the controlling synthetic-content operation is reliably established.
scale.3: One causal side is reliably established, or both binding retrieval and synthetic insertion are observed separately without an explicit precedence connection.
scale.4: Binding-owned analyzer documentation is explicitly connected to conditional synthetic fallback precedence, but no concrete edit or patch at the controlling operation is shown.
scale.5: A visible edit or concrete patch changes synthetic displayed-content replacement, insertion, or selection; its condition may remain incomplete.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Binding-to-displayed-content causal mechanism

applies_when: The visible trajectory adopts runtime __doc__ as the discriminator for whether the source binding has documentation.
After displaying nonempty attr_docs for the binding, the visible trajectory adopts adding, replacing, overriding, bypassing, or duplicating get_doc or another retrieval operation as the correction.
The adopted correction may be a definite prescription, an intended next edit, a concrete draft patch, or an applied production edit.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures a definite correction that contradicts displayed evidence about source-binding ownership or already-successful analyzer retrieval. Application does not require a repository diff when the corrective prescription is explicit.

metadata.failure_mode: The correction uses object metadata for binding documentation or redirects retrieval after the trace has shown retrieval succeeds
metadata.judge_focus: Adopted contradiction of displayed runtime or analyzer evidence
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the adopted discriminator or retrieval prescription with the displayed runtime __doc__ and attr_docs observations

scale.1: No applicable adopted contradiction is visible; inspection or a qualified hypothesis alone does not apply.
scale.2: Object metadata or alternate retrieval is discussed, but the trajectory explicitly declines to use it as the correction.
scale.3: The adopted correction ambiguously mixes object metadata or redundant retrieval with binding-aware content precedence.
scale.4: The adopted correction substantially relies on runtime metadata or redirects retrieval despite indirect visible evidence that binding retrieval works.
scale.5: The trajectory adopts runtime __doc__ despite a displayed None value, or adopts a retrieval addition, replacement, override, bypass, or duplication after displayed nonempty attr_docs already contains the binding documentation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Adopted contradiction of visible binding evidence

applies_when: The view visibly inspects the native field-argument parsing context or executes an operation on the reported composite field, its complete marker, or its complete type-plus-name argument.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge observable causal reach without duplicating exact-native correctness. Distinguish native field-argument context, lexical preservation, semantic component evidence, and corrected native behavior.

metadata.failure_mode: Merely creating an input file, stating expected output, running unrelated annotation examples, or issuing failed commands is mistaken for causal evidence.
metadata.judge_focus: What visible source context or executed task input establishes about preservation, corruption, or correction of the field.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the native field-argument path or run the reported field through the examined operation and evaluate the displayed marker, type, and name evidence.

scale.1: No visible native field-argument context and no successful task-specific operation establishes causal evidence.
scale.2: The native transformer or its field-argument parsing context is visibly inspected, but no exact-input result or semantic boundary is established.
scale.3: An executed operation shows that the complete reported field marker or field argument survives lexical recognition, without exposing the semantic type/name boundary.
scale.4: The preserved argument is visibly followed to the native inner operation, or an executed exact-input operation exposes malformed, partial, or corrected converter-specific type/name components.
scale.5: Observed native before-and-after evidence establishes the old corruption point and the corrected complete type and final name.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-specific causal evidence

applies_when: The view visibly inspects, quotes, edits, or executes the generic native typed-field operation that separates an already-extracted field argument into its inline type and parameter name.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge only the exact native semantic boundary and its production correction. Apply the hard lowest anchor when the inner operation is not visible, regardless of apparent progress or unfinished status.

metadata.failure_mode: Credit is incorrectly awarded for opening the file, locating a typed-field class, lexical matching, the outer split, annotation formatting, renderer code, converter parsing, or an unfinished trajectory treated as neutral.
metadata.judge_focus: The inner split of the complete typed-field argument, not the outer field-kind split or a converter-specific parser.
metadata.oracle_test: Locate the native operation applied to a field argument equivalent to a composite type followed by a name, then inspect its effect or correction.

scale.1: Hard gate not met: the exact native inner type/name operation is not visibly inspected, quoted, edited, or executed.
scale.2: The exact native inner operation is visible, but it is confused with another split, its effect is misstated, or its malformed components are not accurately explained.
scale.3: The exact first-whitespace inner split is visible and its truncated type and corrupted name are accurately explained.
scale.4: The exact split is connected to the preserved complete argument and the generic final-token correction, with surrounding fallback and type-map flow considered.
scale.5: An operative native correction or inspected corrected native result is visible, preserving fallback, type mapping, and typed-field rendering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Exact native inner type/name split and correction

applies_when: Select this rubric only when a visible repository diff, status report, submitted patch, retained source snapshot, or execution of a retained repository file exposes production changes, tests, reproductions, generated files, or other evaluator-facing artifacts.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measure concrete harm caused by visibly retained repository artifacts. Judge an artifact by its displayed contents and artifact-caused behavior, not merely by its quantity, exploratory purpose, unfinished trajectory, or an execution failure attributable only to missing external dependencies. Temporary files, restored edits, failed edit commands, and uncorroborated transient states are excluded.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A later clean diff or status overrides earlier mutation commands unless a same-or-later direct retained-file snapshot or submitted patch displays the artifact. When a summary label conflicts with a directly displayed cutoff diff, the displayed diff governs the files it contains. Do not infer artifact invalidity from a failed run when the visible failure is caused only by an unavailable dependency or incompatible environment.
metadata.evidence_authority: Use the latest direct cutoff diff, submitted patch, status report, or retained-file snapshot, preferring displayed file content over aggregate labels. Execution, syntax, import, collection, and fixture results establish a defect only when visible evidence connects the failure to the retained artifact itself.
