reference_golden_rubrics.title: Latest quaternion formula semantics

applies_when: A terminal response, patch, diff, repository summary, or current workspace state is visible at the cutoff.
The visible state permits determining whether a source change is available to the evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the cutoff exposes an applicable, syntactically usable source change to the target implementation, independently of whether that change has the correct quaternion semantics.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed hunks, conflict markers, syntax damage, destructive replacement, a later reversion, or an explicit final response that omits the changed source cap the score at 4 or worse. A summary label alone cannot contradict visibly complete patch content.
metadata.evidence_authority: Actual visible patch contents and the latest visible tracked diff outrank summary classifications such as terminal payload format or changed-file counts. At a terminal cutoff, an applicable diff in the final response outranks a conflicting label that calls it non-patch; absent final patch content, the terminal response controls delivery. At a nonterminal cutoff, the latest tracked workspace state controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Trusting payload-format metadata over visible diff contents, treating successful diagnostics as delivered source, or assigning the same failure level to transient applied work and complete absence of an implementation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 1 through 3 require a complete applicable diff in the terminal response or a current tracked target-file edit at a genuinely nonterminal cutoff. A proposed formula, test output, temporary script, or earlier edit later omitted from a terminal response cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual final response for patch content and, at a nonterminal cutoff, the latest tracked workspace diff; distinguish usable target-file changes from earlier command output, detached diagnostic files, prose proposals, and absent edits.
metadata.oracle_test: The evaluator can apply or directly inspect a syntactically valid change to `sympy/algebras/quaternion.py`; mathematical correctness of the changed expression is outside this delivery rubric.
metadata.stage: Assess the evaluator-facing artifact at the visible cutoff

scale.1: A clean, complete target-file patch is present in the terminal response, or the cutoff is nonterminal and the latest tracked workspace contains an applicable target-file edit; no material artifact defect is visible.
scale.2: The same applicable evaluator-facing source change is present, with only harmless warnings, formatting noise, or untracked diagnostic files.
scale.3: An applicable evaluator-facing target-file change is present, but unrelated tracked edits, redundant hunks, or material review ambiguity accompany it without making it malformed.
scale.4: No applicable source correction is evaluator-facing at the cutoff, but a syntactically plausible target-file edit is visibly shown only in earlier command output, a detached file, a transient workspace state, or an incomplete terminal diff.
scale.5: No applicable target-file correction is visible anywhere, or the only exposed artifact is malformed, conflict-ridden, syntax-invalid, stale after a visible reversion, or destructive.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evaluator-facing source correction availability

applies_when: The prefix has edited, reverted, stashed, displayed, generated, or submitted repository content.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the visible quality of the effective current or submitted source artifact, including whether the tested fix remains present.

metadata.failure_mode: Restored baseline with unresolved target, empty or test-only state, stale stash, malformed source, debug instrumentation, or non-applicable patch.
metadata.judge_focus: Presence of the intended source fix, syntactic coherence, current repository state, applicability, and agreement with the tested implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the current `sympy/core/mod.py` diff, repository status, importability, diff headers, and whether the tested edit remains present.
metadata.stage: Review repository state and prepare the final artifact

scale.1: No effective source fix is current, the fix was reverted or lost, or the affected source is malformed or debug-corrupted.
scale.2: A source change is visible but incomplete, stale, inconsistent with the tested state, or subject to a serious unresolved repository-state concern.
scale.3: A coherent current source edit is visible and importable, but applicability, cleanup, or agreement with complete validation is not established.
scale.4: The visible diff is focused, coherent, and agrees with successful validation, with only minor artifact-review gaps.
scale.5: A clean applicable evaluator-facing diff contains the tested source fix, has valid syntax and headers, and excludes unrelated tracked changes.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective source artifact

applies_when: The prefix makes correctness claims from tests, printouts, substitutions, baseline comparisons, or expected expressions.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible validation distinguishes the intended fix from unsafe alternatives using correct assumptions and expectations independent of the patched evaluator.

metadata.failure_mode: Happy-path-only printouts, mismatched assumptions, finite substitutions used as symbolic proof, self-referential expectations, or unsupported dismissal of failures.
metadata.judge_focus: Exact assertions, intended symbol identity, independent structural expectations, focused existing tests, and accurate infrastructure triage.
metadata.oracle_test: Use direct assertions with reused integer symbols, the existing test or unmodified tree for structural expectations, and exact reruns for claimed regressions.
metadata.stage: Run discriminative validation and recover from regressions

scale.1: Validation is absent, internally invalid, or visibly contradicts the claimed result.
scale.2: Only the headline or nondiscriminative printouts are checked, or a material test-harness error remains unresolved.
scale.3: The target and some related behavior are checked correctly, but important boundaries or independent oracles are missing.
scale.4: Issue behavior and at least one discriminative boundary are directly checked with correct assumptions and a sound oracle.
scale.5: All issue cases and key compatibility boundaries are asserted with independent expectations, and any infrastructure or baseline differences are accurately isolated.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discriminative validation and oracle quality

applies_when: The trajectory contains a candidate implementation, malformed edit, recursion, compatibility failure, or corrective repository operation.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible exploration produces a coherent current implementation and whether demonstrated failures are causally corrected and retested.

metadata.failure_mode: Ignoring a demonstrated failure, repeatedly restoring the same unsafe rewrite, or claiming recovery without a corrective edit and exact rerun.
metadata.judge_focus: Observable movement from an unsafe or malformed attempt to a narrower coherent implementation, using the exact observed failure as the recovery oracle.
metadata.oracle_test: After a visible recursion, float, or structural failure, inspect the corrective source diff and rerun the same expression together with the target.
metadata.stage: Implement and refine safe coefficient normalization

scale.1: A demonstrated regression or malformed edit is ignored, misattributed, or retained without meaningful diagnosis.
scale.2: The exact failure is identified, but no corrective source change and successful exact rerun are visible.
scale.3: The work reaches a coherent candidate without an unresolved demonstrated failure, or safely reverts a bad attempt but has not completed a replacement.
scale.4: A causal corrective edit is visible and the target or the exact prior failure is successfully rerun.
scale.5: The unsafe mechanism is correctly explained, replaced with a narrower implementation, and both the target and every previously failing compatibility probe visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal refinement and recovery

applies_when: The prefix contains an execution, assertion, test result, or behavioral comparison concerning the affected Mod evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether validation supports a reliable accept-or-reject judgment about the latest applied Mod implementation, using sound oracles and discriminative affected cases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A post-edit recursion, wrong focused existing-test result, wrong divisible-product result, or wrong nonintegral-quotient result from the current candidate caps the score at 2 until the candidate is changed and that exact failure is rerun successfully. Merely diagnosing or disputing the failure does not remove the cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Post-edit exact assertions and focused existing tests outrank print-only comparisons and prose. Results from an older implementation become stale after an edit, revert, stash restoration, or checkout. An expected expression produced by the same patched evaluator, finite substitutions, and an intended future rerun are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding high validation credit because a broad test discovered an unresolved regression, accepting self-referential expectations, using stale pre-edit output, or treating concrete substitutions as proof of symbolic normalization.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a valid post-edit execution of `Mod(3*i, 2) == Mod(i, 2)` using the same integer symbol on both sides. Scores above 3 require at least one independently expected affected boundary beyond the headline.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect checks executed after the latest source-changing operation: the integer-symbol target, divisible coefficient behavior, nonintegral symbolic quotient behavior, symbolic-factor termination, and float or modulus-one compatibility.
metadata.oracle_test: Use direct structural assertions for `Mod(3*i, 2) == Mod(i, 2)`, `Mod(8*i, 4) == 0`, `Mod(8*i/j, 4) == 4*Mod(2*i/j, 1)`, and `(3*i*x) % (2*i*y) == i*Mod(3*x, 2*y)`. Use the existing unmodified test expectation for `(x - 3.3) % 1` or another float/modulus-one boundary.

scale.1: No valid post-edit target check is visible, the latest target execution fails or cannot run, or the claimed check uses incompatible assumptions or an invalid oracle.
scale.2: The target passes after the latest edit but the current candidate has a directly demonstrated unresolved affected contradiction; alternatively, only ambiguous printouts or self-referential comparisons are available.
scale.3: The target passes after the latest edit with a sound direct comparison and no current contradiction, but no independently expected discriminative boundary is established.
scale.4: The target and at least one independently expected affected boundary pass in the same current candidate, with no unresolved contradiction, but termination or a key coefficient or compatibility class remains unchecked.
scale.5: The current candidate passes the target, divisible and nonintegral coefficient cases, symbolic-factor termination, and a float or modulus-one compatibility boundary using exact independent expectations.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Decision-reliable current-candidate validation

applies_when: The prefix visibly edits, restores, displays, or submits repository content relevant to the Mod evaluator.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the coherence and readiness of the evaluator-facing source change that is visibly applied at the cutoff, rather than proposed or stale work.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A current malformed evaluator file, debug instrumentation in production source, reverted evaluator fix, or directly demonstrated regression retained by the current source caps credit at 2. A source edit after a failure makes the old execution stale but does not establish that the failure is repaired.
metadata.evidence_authority: A later checkout, restore, stash operation, overwrite, or displayed source supersedes earlier diffs and executions. Direct file displays, `git diff`, and command observations outrank prose and generated patch text. Summary fields do not erase a visibly applied edit unless a later repository operation or file display shows it absent.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting an unexecuted patch proposal, treating untracked debugging utilities as the fix, relying on stale pre-revert output, trusting an empty summary over visible current source, or awarding readiness to malformed or debug-corrupted production code.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a coherent evaluator-facing source edit visibly applied in `sympy/core/mod.py`; helper scripts, test-only edits, patch text, or a described future edit do not satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible contents or diff of `sympy/core/mod.py`, syntax and indentation, residual debugging, repository operations affecting that file, and agreement between the applied source and post-edit executions.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest applied Mul-branch logic with the intended coefficient-normalization behavior, verify importability or syntax when executed, inspect the current evaluator diff, and confirm that any claimed tested implementation is the same source state.
metadata.stage: Maintain and review the current implementation

scale.1: No evaluator-facing fix is currently applied, it was visibly reverted or lost, or the current evaluator source is malformed or debug-corrupted.
scale.2: An evaluator edit is applied but is incomplete, internally inconsistent, retains a directly demonstrated regression, or cannot be matched to an executable coherent implementation.
scale.3: A coherent importable evaluator edit is visibly current and the target behavior is consistent with it, but repository cleanliness, focused scope, or artifact-to-validation agreement remains materially unverified.
scale.4: The current evaluator diff is focused and coherent, agrees with successful post-edit target validation, and has no visible retained contradiction; only minor cleanup or artifact-review evidence is missing.
scale.5: A clean, applicable, evaluator-facing diff contains the validated fix, has coherent syntax and headers, excludes debug or unrelated tracked changes, and agrees with successful discriminative post-edit validation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current applied Mod evaluator artifact

applies_when: A production edit, source inspection, import result, or nonempty behavior is visible by the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize production damage distinct from the empty-result choice. Relevant defects include changing established identity or absorbing-element declarations, altering live unary or nonempty processing, leaving duplicated or malformed shared logic, or causing an import or behavioral regression.

metadata.failure_mode: Established declarations or shared live behavior are damaged independently of whether the empty result is correct.
metadata.judge_focus: Damage outside the localized empty-call semantic choice
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the effective production source, declaration values, module import, and visible unary or nonempty behavior.

scale.1: No distinct production-integrity defect is visible; the edit is localized or the source remains behaviorally intact.
scale.2: Minor live production noise is visible, but import, declarations, and demonstrated nonempty behavior remain intact.
scale.3: Additional shared production changes, duplicated or unreachable code, or a limited demonstrated regression creates a material but recoverable concern.
scale.4: Live shared processing is materially altered, a serious structural defect remains, or multiple nonempty behaviors are put at visible risk.
scale.5: Established identity or absorbing-element declarations are changed, production is unimportable, core nonempty behavior is demonstrably broken, or destructive source damage remains.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of production invariants

applies_when: The visible trajectory inspects, edits, executes, tests, or claims behavior for either zero-argument extrema call.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Score the effective applied behavior of both empty calls: `Min()` must return canonical `S.Infinity` and `Max()` must return canonical `S.NegativeInfinity`, without changing the established `identity` or `zero` declarations or damaging the shared constructor.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest visible state changes either established `identity` or `zero` declaration, leaves malformed or unimportable shared constructor logic, or if later effective source contradicts earlier passing execution. Recovered edits do not cap credit after restoration is visibly established.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible effective production source and post-edit execution outrank earlier tests, comments, expected-value labels, success banners, and implementation-derived oracles. A later source edit supersedes runtime evidence obtained before that edit. Separate literal comparisons to `S.Infinity` and `S.NegativeInfinity` are strongest.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting stale execution or an identity-based-looking branch after declarations were mutated, or treating reversed `cls.zero` results as correct because a custom script labels them successful.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an applied production implementation that yields both required mappings while preserving `Max.identity = S.NegativeInfinity`, `Min.identity = S.Infinity`, `Max.zero = S.Infinity`, `Min.zero = S.NegativeInfinity`, and the live nonempty constructor path.
metadata.judge_focus: The latest effective `MinMaxBase.__new__` branch, both class-level `identity` and `zero` declarations, and separate observable results for `Min()` and `Max()`.
metadata.oracle_test: Independently establish `Min() == S.Infinity` and `Max() == S.NegativeInfinity`; `cls.identity` is the valid shared source, whereas `cls.zero` produces the reversed pair.

scale.1: The latest effective state mutates an established `identity` or `zero` declaration, leaves the shared constructor malformed or unimportable, or is contradicted by a later source edit, regardless of earlier passing output.
scale.2: Declarations and shared nonempty processing remain intact, but neither required result is established: both calls retain the exception, return the reversed pair, are otherwise wrong, or no production implementation is applied.
scale.3: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and exactly one required call is established while the other is wrong or unresolved.
scale.4: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and effective applied source unambiguously yields both required canonical results, but no post-edit evidence independently executes or discriminates both calls.
scale.5: Declarations and shared processing remain intact, and post-edit execution or literal independent assertions establish `Min() == S.Infinity` and `Max() == S.NegativeInfinity` separately.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective empty-extrema semantics and identity integrity

applies_when: Visible production source, import execution, or unary or nonempty Min/Max behavior is available by the cutoff.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Credit preservation of established `Min` and `Max` declarations, importability, and shared unary and nonempty constructor behavior while implementing or investigating the zero-argument case.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 if the latest effective state changes any established `zero` or `identity` declaration, is unimportable, or visibly breaks core unary or nonempty behavior. Cap at 2 if live shared processing contains unrecovered duplicated, unreachable, or structurally malformed logic even without a demonstrated runtime failure. A visibly restored latest state removes an earlier cap.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible effective production source outranks earlier source views, explanations, generated patch files, and test labels. Post-edit import or nonempty execution can establish behavior only for the source state that produced it; a later production edit supersedes earlier execution. Repository status or a final diff outranks claims that a temporary edit was restored.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding declaration mutation or shared-constructor damage because it happens to produce a desired empty-call output, or numerically ranking more severe damage above a localized intact edit.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require the established declarations to remain `Max.zero = S.Infinity`, `Max.identity = S.NegativeInfinity`, `Min.zero = S.NegativeInfinity`, and `Min.identity = S.Infinity`, with no visible malformed shared constructor path.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest effective production diff or source for declaration mutations, malformed or duplicated constructor logic, and visible regressions in import, unary calls, or nonempty calls; do not score whether the two empty results themselves have the requested polarity here.
metadata.oracle_test: Compare the latest production source with the original declarations and shared `MinMaxBase.__new__` flow, then use any source-state-matched import and unary or nonempty executions to determine whether behavior outside the zero-argument result remains intact.
metadata.stage: Apply a localized production change without collateral regressions

scale.1: The latest state mutates an established `zero` or `identity` declaration, is unimportable, demonstrably breaks core unary or nonempty behavior, or retains destructive production damage.
scale.2: Declarations are not visibly mutated and no core regression is demonstrated, but unrecovered malformed, duplicated, unreachable, or broadly invasive shared production logic creates a serious integrity defect.
scale.3: Production remains importable and declarations remain intact, but a material nonempty risk, limited demonstrated regression, or substantial unnecessary shared-code disturbance remains.
scale.4: Declarations and demonstrated unary or nonempty behavior remain intact; only minor live production noise or an unverified localized compatibility concern remains.
scale.5: The latest effective production change is localized to the empty-call handling or leaves production untouched, preserves all established declarations and shared processing, and shows no distinct import, unary, or nonempty regression.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production integrity outside the empty-call result

applies_when: The visible trajectory includes an attempted production edit to `Add._eval_is_zero`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest visible repository state contains a coherent, executable production change whose behavior was exercised against that same state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest method is syntactically or structurally damaged, if the tested edit was reverted or superseded, or if broad classification changes lack visible preservation of existing real-term branches. Cap at 3 if the current execution gives either definitive Boolean result for the reported unsimplified Add.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest inspected source and execution from the edited checkout override earlier successful runs, edit-script success messages, intentions, and results from code later restored or overwritten. A final focused diff is strongest source-state evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a replacement-script success message, an earlier transient run, or extensive reasoning as evidence that the latest repository contains an effective executable correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires visible evidence that a production edit is currently present and either its complete relevant context is coherent or that edited source subsequently imports and executes.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest complete `sympy/core/add.py` state, whether the edit is structurally coherent, and whether a subsequent command executes that exact state; distinguish applied work from proposed, reverted, or superseded work.
metadata.oracle_test: Execute the edited checkout on `e = -2*I + (1 + I)**2` and require `e.is_zero is None`; source inspection should show the all-known-zero path remains before the conservative handling and the real-term classification branches remain intact.
metadata.stage: Implement and validate the focused core correction

scale.1: No effective production correction is present, or the latest production method is visibly malformed, truncated, or replaced by a test-only or scratch artifact.
scale.2: A correction is proposed or an edit command runs, but the current production state is unverified, reverted, superseded, or visibly broad enough that source coherence is unresolved.
scale.3: A coherent current production edit is visibly exercised from the edited checkout, but the reported unsimplified Add still receives a definitive Boolean result or task-specific semantic validation is otherwise contradictory.
scale.4: A coherent current production edit is exercised and the reported unsimplified Add visibly returns exactly `None`, but final source-state inspection or representative preservation evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: The latest focused production diff is coherent and executable, the edited checkout visibly returns exactly `None` for the reported unsimplified Add, and current checks preserve both proven-zero and proven-nonzero behavior without contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Effective and executable Add correction

applies_when: The visible trajectory analyzes why `Add._eval_is_zero` misclassifies sums containing imaginary terms.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest reasoning correctly connects imaginary-term classification, the absence of a meaningful real subtotal, and the need to return unknown rather than infer a Boolean result for the complete Add.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest reasoning treats `self.func(*nz) == 0` as proof that the complete imaginary Add is zero, endorses either definitive result for the reported unsimplified expression, or rejects a visible `None` result as incomplete. Cap at 3 when the correct reasoning applies only to a reverted or unverified edit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest explicit conclusion and the latest source-directed action override earlier tentative diagnoses. Direct current behavior may confirm that the reasoning was applied, but output alone does not prove causal understanding.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding high causal credit for mentioning cancellation while the latest conclusion still infers `True` or `False` from the empty constructed subtotal.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the conservative conclusion to guide the current edit or a checked next action; merely observing `nz == []`, cancellation, or a failed overbroad experiment is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for a causal trace from imaginary arguments not supplying a known nonzero real subtotal, through the empty `nz` state, to the conclusion that the complete sum may cancel and therefore requires `None`.
metadata.oracle_test: The empty collected real subtotal is an identity created by `self.func(*[])`; it contains no evidence that the omitted imaginary addends cancel. After preserving the all-known-zero return, this state must remain undecidable for the reported Add.
metadata.stage: Derive the conservative Add decision rule

scale.1: The latest diagnosis targets the wrong mechanism, denies possible cancellation, or endorses a definitive answer from the empty subtotal without recognizing the evidentiary gap.
scale.2: The empty collection or imaginary cancellation is noticed, but the latest reasoning remains contradictory, treats the empty subtotal as proof, or rejects the required conservative result.
scale.3: The trajectory correctly concludes that the empty subtotal cannot decide the complete Add, but the conclusion remains diagnostic, applies only to a reverted attempt, or has not guided a verifiable current action.
scale.4: The conservative causal rule guides the current edit or checked action and the reported expression visibly returns `None`, though the distinction from all preserved definitive paths is not fully demonstrated.
scale.5: The trajectory precisely traces classification to the empty real subtotal, preserves the earlier all-known-zero proof, distinguishes safe nonzero deductions, and uses those distinctions to produce and verify the conservative current behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal control-flow understanding of unknown zero

applies_when: The prefix shows execution, reasoning, or a source change affecting `Add._eval_is_zero`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest visible behavior avoids a wrong definitive answer for the unsimplified complex Add while retaining observable proven-zero and proven-nonzero deductions.

metadata.failure_mode: The reported expression remains `False`, becomes an unsound `True`, or nearby established deductions visibly regress.
metadata.judge_focus: The exact tri-valued result and visible preservation behavior, not whether a command merely completed.
metadata.oracle_test: `e = -2*I + (1 + I)**2; assert e.is_zero is None`, together with visible checks that a proven zero remains `True` and explicit nonzero cases remain `False`.

scale.1: The latest visible behavior gives a wrong definitive result and the prefix endorses or retains that result as its solution.
scale.2: The bug is reproduced or discussed, but current behavior remains wrong and no coherent conservative correction is present.
scale.3: A plausible conservative correction is present or the exact expression returns `None`, but preservation is unverified or the edit visibly affects a broader state.
scale.4: The exact expression visibly returns `None`, and representative proven-zero and proven-nonzero cases remain correct.
scale.5: The latest coherent source isolates the undecidable state, the exact identity assertion passes, and visible preservation checks cover both definitive Boolean outcomes without contradiction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Observable tri-valued semantic safety

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains task-relevant work at the Implement the core Add correction stage.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates visible evidence that the implementation honors the tri-valued assumptions contract for the reported complex Add and the general empty-real-subtotal case.

metadata.failure_mode: The expression returns `False`, or the correction unsafely returns `True` for arbitrary all-imaginary Adds.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether multiple imaginary addends that may cancel produce unknown rather than an incorrect definitive result.
metadata.oracle_test: `e = -2*I + (1 + I)**2; assert e.is_zero is None`

scale.1: Visible behavior preserves the wrong `False`, returns an unsound `True`, or changes unrelated logic without addressing the unsafe state.
scale.2: The issue is recognized but the proposed rule remains ambiguous, special-cased, or visibly overbroad.
scale.3: A plausible conservative source edit is present, but the exact regression is not checked and edge semantics remain uncertain.
scale.4: The core edit clearly handles empty `nz` conservatively and direct evidence shows the reported expression returns `None`.
scale.5: The reported expression returns exactly `None`, the rule is general and conservative, and visible checks preserve both proven-zero and proven-nonzero Add behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Conservative Add zero semantics

applies_when: The visible trajectory attempts, applies, reverts, or validates a production change affecting `Add._eval_is_zero`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rates whether the latest visible repository state contains a focused, structurally sound production intervention that improves the unsafe complex-Add decision without introducing a demonstrated semantic regression.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Assign at most 1 when a current production intervention is visibly malformed, makes the reported expression return either definitive Boolean, or demonstrably regresses an established zero or nonzero case. Assign at most 2 when the attempted edit was reverted, superseded, confined to scratch code, or supported only by an edit-command success message. Assign at most 3 when the exact `None` result is not visibly linked to the latest source state.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest focused diff or complete source inspection establishes the current production state. A subsequent execution from that checkout establishes its behavior. Later restores, stashes, overwrites, or source inspections supersede earlier runs. Scratch files, replacement-script messages, intended edits, explanations, and executions performed before the latest edit are not evidence that the current production state works.
metadata.failure_mode: Ranking an executed but semantically harmful or structurally damaged edit above a safe trajectory with no current production change, or crediting behavior from an edit that was later reverted or overwritten.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 2 requires a currently present, coherent production edit confirmed by source inspection or successful import after the edit. Credit above 3 requires same-state execution showing `e.is_zero is None` for the reported unsimplified expression.
metadata.judge_focus: Determine whether a production edit is present in the latest visible state, whether it preserves the surrounding real-term and all-known-zero branches, and whether execution from that same state returns unknown for the reported unsimplified Add.
metadata.oracle_test: In the edited checkout, `e = -2*I + (1 + I)**2` must satisfy `e.is_zero is None`. The method must retain its prior proof for an Add whose arguments are all known zero and must not lose justified `False` deductions for representative explicit nonzero Adds.
metadata.stage: Apply and validate the focused Add correction

scale.1: A current production intervention is present but is visibly malformed, overbroad, or contradicted by a wrong definitive result for the reported Add or by a demonstrated regression.
scale.2: No effective production intervention is present in the latest state: work is diagnostic or proposed only, the edit was reverted or superseded, or an edit command ran without reliable current-source confirmation.
scale.3: A focused and structurally coherent production edit is visibly present and importable or source-confirmed, but the reported expression has not been executed against that same state or its required `None` result remains unverified.
scale.4: A coherent current production edit is linked to execution showing exactly `None` for the reported unsimplified Add, with no visible contradiction, but preservation of both definitive Boolean paths is incomplete.
scale.5: The latest focused diff is coherent and current, same-state execution shows exactly `None` for the reported Add, and visible checks preserve representative proven-zero and proven-nonzero behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Integrity of the current Add production intervention

applies_when: The task requires posify replacement symbols to preserve finiteness or other existing symbol assumptions
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the visible cutoff state contains a coherent implementation that creates positive replacement symbols while preserving compatible original assumptions through normal symbol construction, rather than by mutating an already-created symbol's internal assumption state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Directly writing, unioning, or assigning facts into a constructed symbol's private _assumptions knowledge base caps the score at 1. An observed syntax/runtime failure or failure of the finite-preservation example against the latest applied implementation caps it at 2. If no task source change remains applied at cutoff, the score is capped at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file contents or unified diff at the cutoff outrank earlier edits, test runs, plans, and narrative claims. Tests count only for the implementation that was present when they ran. A later stash, revert, overwrite, or corruption supersedes earlier successful evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents crediting extensive testing of an unsafe private-state mutation, tests that predate the final edit, a stashed or reverted patch, or a constructor call that loses or conflicts with the original assumptions.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a task-relevant source change still applied at the cutoff and use of constructor-level or another consistency-preserving assumptions mechanism. Score 5 additionally requires successful targeted verification against the final implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible posify source or patch, then tests run against that exact state. Check whether assumptions are supplied when the replacement Dummy is constructed, whether positive=True takes precedence without duplicate or contradictory inputs, and whether the original posify behavior remains intact.
metadata.oracle_test: For a symbol such as Symbol('x', finite=True) whose positivity is unknown, posify must return a positive replacement whose is_finite is True and whose assumption closure is internally consistent. Compatible assumptions such as integer, rational, even, odd, or prime should be retained generically when present; symbols already known positive or non-positive must retain existing posify replacement behavior.

scale.1: An applied attempt mutates the replacement symbol's private assumption knowledge base after construction, or otherwise bypasses assumption consistency.
scale.2: A task-relevant implementation is applied, but the latest visible evidence demonstrates that it is malformed, raises an error, or still fails the finite-preservation behavior.
scale.3: A concrete and plausible consistency-preserving repair was developed, and may have been tested, but no task-relevant source change remains applied at the cutoff.
scale.4: An applied implementation transfers assumptions through replacement-symbol construction or an equivalent consistency-preserving mechanism and plausibly fixes finiteness, but verification against the final state is incomplete or leaves unresolved compatibility concerns.
scale.5: The final applied implementation consistently constructs positive replacements while preserving compatible assumptions, and targeted tests against that state confirm finiteness preservation plus existing posify behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied, assumption-consistent preservation in posify

applies_when: A visible implementation or concrete implementation attempt changes how posify creates positive replacement symbols
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the cutoff-visible posify implementation transfers the original symbol's compatible known assumptions generally through replacement-symbol construction, gives positive=True unambiguous precedence, and avoids private assumption-state mutation.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Direct assignment, update, or union into a constructed symbol's private _assumptions knowledge base fixes the score at 1. If no task source change remains applied at cutoff, cap at 2. A duplicate-keyword error, contradictory constructor inputs, failure of the finite=True example, or a selective assumption whitelist caps an applied attempt at 3. Absence of a focused checked-in regression test caps an otherwise correct implementation at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible file contents or unified diff outrank earlier edits, temporary scripts, test output, and narrative claims. Runtime results apply only to the source state that produced them. A later revert, stash, overwrite, or malformed edit supersedes earlier successful verification.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents rewarding passing examples produced by unsafe private-state mutation, treating reverted work as currently implemented, overlooking duplicate positive arguments, or mistaking a finite-only whitelist for a general assumption-preserving repair.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a task-relevant source change still applied at cutoff and a valid general constructor-level or equivalently consistency-preserving transfer mechanism. Score 5 additionally requires a focused checked-in regression test and successful targeted verification against the final applied state.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest visible source or unified diff at the non-iterable replacement site. Determine whether assumptions are passed into Dummy construction, whether positive is removed or overridden without duplicate keywords, whether both true and false known facts are handled generally, and whether that exact implementation remains applied at cutoff.
metadata.oracle_test: For Symbol('x', finite=True) with unknown positivity, posify must construct a positive Dummy whose is_finite is True and whose assumption closure is consistent. The mechanism should retain compatible known assumptions generically, including false facts where relevant, while deliberately overriding only positivity and preserving established behavior for symbols already known positive or non-positive.

scale.1: No concrete task repair was developed, or the latest applied attempt writes, updates, or unions facts into the replacement symbol's private _assumptions state.
scale.2: A concrete consistency-preserving repair was developed or tested, but no task-relevant source change remains applied at the cutoff.
scale.3: A task-relevant source change remains applied, but it is visibly malformed, fails the reported finite case, supplies contradictory or duplicate constructor inputs, or preserves only a selected assumption whitelist.
scale.4: A valid applied implementation generally transfers compatible known assumptions through construction with safe positive precedence, but lacks a focused checked-in regression test or final-state targeted verification.
scale.5: A clean general constructor-level implementation remains applied, safely overrides positivity while retaining compatible true and false facts, and a focused checked-in regression test plus targeted final-state verification confirm the reported case and existing posify behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Safe and general assumption transfer in the current posify implementation

applies_when: A visible implementation or concrete implementation plan changes how posify constructs replacement Dummy symbols.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The replacement Dummy is made positive while preserving the original symbol's compatible known assumptions generally, rather than handling only a narrow list, and does so through valid constructor inputs without duplicate keywords or unsafe mutation of internal assumption state.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible implementation raises a duplicate-keyword or inconsistent-assumptions error on the reported case; cap at 3 for a selective finite/integer/rational whitelist or direct post-construction mutation of _assumptions; cap at 4 if the general merge is correct but no regression test is added.
metadata.evidence_authority: A visible final diff and runtime behavior outrank prose claims; constructor exceptions or contradictory assumption errors outrank an assertion that the merge is safe.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a passing finite-only example for a general fix, copying positive twice, discarding false assumptions, or mutating the private fact database after construction.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires concrete code that both forces positive=True and carries original assumptions into the newly constructed Dummy without duplicate positive keyword arguments.
metadata.judge_focus: The visible diff or exact proposed code at the non-iterable replacement construction in posify, including merge precedence, filtering or overriding of positive, and treatment of true and false known facts.
metadata.oracle_test: The semantic operation is equivalent to constructing Dummy(s.name, **merged_assumptions), where the original symbol's known assumption facts are retained and positive is deliberately set to True with unambiguous precedence.

scale.1: No relevant implementation, or the implementation leaves the positive-only Dummy behavior unchanged.
scale.2: Attempts preservation but visible code is invalid, contradictory, corrupts the function, or fails the reported finite=True case.
scale.3: Preserves only selected named assumptions, mutates private assumption storage after construction, or otherwise fixes the example without a general constructor-level merge.
scale.4: Uses a valid general merge that preserves original known assumptions and overrides positive safely at the correct replacement site, but lacks a checked-in regression test or leaves a minor maintainability concern.
scale.5: Implements the general constructor-level merge cleanly and minimally, with explicit safe precedence for positive and a focused checked-in regression test covering the lost assumption behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Semantically correct assumption-preserving replacement

applies_when: A concrete edit or submitted patch changes how posify constructs positive replacement symbols
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the latest visible implementation safely and generally transfers compatible known assumptions through replacement-symbol construction, deliberately resolves facts affected by forcing positivity, remains present at the cutoff, and is delivered in the required patch form when the trajectory has terminated.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Direct post-construction assignment, update, or union into a replacement symbol's private assumption knowledge base fixes the score at 1. A malformed implementation, observed constructor exception, or failure of the reported finite case caps the score at 1. An explicit revert or a terminal response that omits the required patch despite an earlier edit caps the score at 2. A selective named-assumption whitelist, duplicate positivity keyword, or visible unresolved conflict between forced positivity and copied facts caps the score at 3. Absence of a focused checked-in regression test caps an otherwise complete repair at 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: At a nonterminal cutoff, the latest visible source read, exact edit, or repository diff may establish that a change is currently applied; lack of a terminal artifact alone does not negate it. For a terminated trajectory, the required final patch payload is authoritative for delivery, and a terminal prose-only or otherwise non-patch response cannot be rescued by an earlier diff. A later stash, revert, overwrite, clean diff, corruption, or source read supersedes earlier edits and test results. Runtime evidence validates only the source state that produced it.
metadata.failure_mode: Prevents tying a safely filtered current edit with an unfiltered or conflict-prone constructor call merely because both trajectories are nonterminal, prevents an earlier working diff from rescuing an unusable terminal submission, and prevents temporary passing checks from validating reverted or different source.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a task-relevant implementation shown as currently applied at a nonterminal cutoff or delivered as the required patch at a terminal cutoff, a general constructor-level or equivalently consistency-preserving transfer, unambiguous positivity precedence, no visible unresolved conflicting facts, and successful targeted verification against matching source. Score 5 additionally requires a focused checked-in regression test.
metadata.judge_focus: First classify the cutoff correctly: inspect the latest source evidence for a nonterminal trajectory, but inspect the delivered final payload for a terminated trajectory. Then check whether assumption transfer is general, whether positivity is supplied exactly once or overrides a copied mapping safely, whether positivity-sensitive facts are filtered or otherwise proven consistent, and whether tests ran against that same implementation.
metadata.oracle_test: For a symbol with finite=True and unknown positivity, posify must return a positive replacement whose is_finite is True and whose assumption closure is consistent. Compatible known true and false assumptions should transfer generically through construction, while facts incompatible with forced positivity must not be forwarded as contradictions. Symbols already known positive or non-positive and iterable posify behavior must remain unchanged.
metadata.stage: implementation persistence, safety, verification, and delivery

scale.1: The latest implementation mutates private assumption state after construction, is malformed, raises an assumption error, or fails the reported finite-preservation behavior.
scale.2: A viable repair appeared earlier, but it was explicitly removed, no task-relevant edit is visible at cutoff, or a terminated trajectory fails to deliver the required patch and ends with a non-patch response.
scale.3: A concrete repair remains visible or is delivered and fixes finiteness, but it is selectively whitelisted, has ambiguous or duplicate positivity precedence, leaves a visible positivity-related consistency concern unresolved, or lacks matching-state verification.
scale.4: The current nonterminal source or delivered terminal patch generally transfers compatible assumptions through construction, resolves positivity precedence without visible conflicts, and matching targeted verification confirms finiteness and established posify behavior, but no focused checked-in regression test is present.
scale.5: A clean current or properly delivered constructor-level implementation safely preserves compatible assumptions with explicit positivity precedence, and a focused checked-in regression test plus matching-state targeted verification confirm the reported case and established posify behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Currently applied, conflict-safe assumption transfer and delivery

Constructor mutation is non-evidence for this rubric and belongs to the constructor-specific rubric.
metadata.evidence_authority: A post-edit execution of `Symbol(..., even=True).is_finite` has highest authority; visible task-source edits and generated diffs are next; stated intentions and unexecuted proposals are lowest. Predicate-query success cannot override a core-property result that remains `None`.
metadata.failure_mode: The trajectory applies or persists with a predicate-side or evaluator-side fix as though it controlled the reported core property, despite stronger visible source or execution evidence to the contrary.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a visible operative edit to a noncontrolling mechanism. Searches, file inspection, or discussion alone cannot exceed score 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether other-layer inspection remains exploratory or becomes an applied attempted fix for Symbol `.is_finite`, and whether the trajectory responds to a post-edit target probe
metadata.oracle_test: For the reported API, the controlling semantic reference is the legacy core FactRules closure in `sympy/core/assumptions.py`; `ask.py`, `ask_generated.py`, predicate handlers, and static number-class attributes may be separately relevant but do not by themselves change `Symbol(...).is_finite`.
metadata.stage: Reproduce the symptom and identify both inference engines

scale.1: The trajectory reaches and recognizes the controlling core FactRules closure; other assumptions layers are only inspected for their separate synchronization role, or no noncontrolling pursuit occurs.
scale.2: A noncontrolling mechanism is briefly suspected or proposed, but no operative edit is made and the trajectory then reaches or correctly redirects toward the core FactRules closure.
scale.3: Investigation remains substantially focused on noncontrolling mechanisms through the cutoff, but no operative noncontrolling fix is applied to task source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Integrity and validation of assumptions-rule edits

applies_when: The prefix applies or displays a concrete source edit intended to preserve an unused explicit array argument.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible source intervention preserves shape-derived dimensions at the actual redundant-input construction point while avoiding scalar, ordering, expression, and backend regressions.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the edited branch is not entered by an unused explicit argument, cap at 2. If active post-edit evidence still shows `dimensions=None`, `double x`, or the original array-conversion failure, cap at 2. Artificial dependencies, unconditional pointer conversion, argument removal, or invalid bounds force score 1.
metadata.evidence_authority: The operative diff or displayed post-edit source outranks a proposed patch in prose. Post-edit routine metadata and generated declarations outrank visual plausibility. If displayed source and a later target check conflict, the later target check controls.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding an edit merely because it was applied, overlooking that it modifies expression-derived discovery, iterates over an unavailable shape, assigns dimensions to scalars, or remains contradicted by the active target check.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require a visible source intervention in routine construction. Scores above 3 require the intervention to affect the explicit missing-entry path and derive dimensions from a reliably shaped object. Score 5 requires discriminative validation of the target and scalar control.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the actual edited hunk, the branch reached by an expression-unused explicit argument, the source of shape information, the dimension bounds, and guards that leave ordinary scalars unchanged.
metadata.oracle_test: The operative change should create the unused `MatrixSymbol('x', 2, 1)` input with dimensions equivalent to `[(S.Zero, 1), (S.Zero, 0)]`, yielding pointer handling while leaving an unused `Symbol` scalar and leaving the constant body independent of `x`.

scale.1: The intervention is semantically wrong or unsafe: it fakes expression dependence, removes the argument, pointer-types scalars, uses invalid bounds, or breaks construction.
scale.2: A source edit is visible but it targets an unreachable or insufficient path, or active target evidence shows that it remains ineffective.
scale.3: The edit reaches routine construction and plausibly preserves array metadata, but its shape guard, bounds, or effect on the exact fallback is incomplete or unverified.
scale.4: The operative edit correctly handles the explicit missing-entry path with direct shape-derived inclusive bounds and preserves ordinary scalar behavior by construction.
scale.5: The semantically correct, narrowly scoped edit is additionally verified by corrected target dimensions or pointer ABI, successful exact array behavior, and an unchanged scalar control.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operative metadata-fix semantics and safety

applies_when: The prefix investigates routine construction or proposes where dimensions should be recovered.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the investigation reaches an actionable source mechanism without allowing static causal detail to overwhelm stronger experimental evidence.

metadata.failure_mode: Wrapper-only diagnosis, expression-only recovery, artificial dependencies, or incorrect bounds
metadata.judge_focus: Explicit argument construction, absence from expression discovery, and direct shaped-symbol provenance

scale.1: The proposed cause is unrelated or relies on an artificial expression dependency.
scale.2: The investigation recognizes a scalar-versus-array problem but remains centered on wrapper symptoms or datatype speculation.
scale.3: Missing dimensions are localized to routine argument construction, though the exact fallback or shape source remains incomplete.
scale.4: The explicit unused-argument path is identified and expression-only discovery is recognized as insufficient.
scale.5: The source path and direct shaped-symbol provenance are established with the existing zero-based inclusive-bound convention.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actionable source localization and shape provenance

applies_when: The trajectory inspects routine argument metadata or generated native and Cython declarations for the unused MatrixSymbol case.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures concrete artifact evidence that missing or restored routine dimensions propagate to scalar or pointer declarations for the same unused-array case.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If active generated C still declares `double x`, corrected-ABI credit is forbidden regardless of intended code. If metadata and declarations come from different or unresolved cases, cap at 3. Merely reading `get_prototype` or `_prototype_arg` caps at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: Artifacts generated or printed by an executed command from the active checkout outrank inferred declarations and prose. The active post-edit artifacts outrank pre-edit artifacts when assessing correction; runtime output does not substitute for missing metadata or declaration evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring artifacts from source logic, combining unrelated runs, treating a runtime exception as metadata evidence, or claiming pointer correction while the active generated declaration remains scalar.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require direct observation of either `InputArgument.dimensions` or a generated scalar-versus-pointer declaration for the target case. Scores above 3 require both metadata and a generated native declaration tied to that case.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect actual printed routine arguments and actual generated C, header, or `.pyx` contents. Match artifacts to the same constant-expression `MatrixSymbol('x', 2, 1)` case. Source logic saying dimensions control pointers is contextual evidence only, not proof of a generated declaration.
metadata.oracle_test: For the unused matrix, observe dimensions equivalent to `[(0, 1), (0, 0)]` and generated `double *x`; pre-fix evidence may instead show `dimensions=None` and `double x`. The constant body should remain unchanged.

scale.1: No reliable target-case metadata or generated declaration is observed.
scale.2: Only pointer-selection source logic or another indirect artifact is inspected.
scale.3: Either target-case routine dimensions or a target-case generated scalar/pointer declaration is directly observed.
scale.4: Target-case routine metadata and generated native declaration are both directly observed and consistently connected; wrapper declaration evidence may also be present.
scale.5: Post-edit target metadata has the correct two inclusive dimensions, native and Cython declarations consistently use pointer/array handling, and the constant body remains independent of `x`.

Absence of both a current repository diff and a usable evaluator-facing patch caps an otherwise correct transient edit at 3. applies_when: A source edit to `_TR56` is visible.
Regression tests or direct real-power checks have been run.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards evidence that the new eligibility guard does not alter supported real-power transformations or existing negative-power early returns.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Preservation of established Fu transformations

applies_when: The visible prefix diagnoses or modifies `_TR56` exponent handling.
A targeted sine or cosine power can reach the Fu transformation callback.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards an applied local eligibility exit that prevents unsuitable exponents from reaching every ordered, parity, division, and power-decomposition operation in `_TR56`.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 3 if an unsuitable exponent can continue to equality, modulo, floor-division, or `perfect_power` logic, even when literal or mixed complex examples happen to pass. Cap at 2 if the check occurs after an unsafe operation, special-cases a representation, or changes global comparison semantics.
metadata.evidence_authority: The applied source diff and its control flow outrank prose claims and passing examples. A test of `I` proves only that execution did not fail for that input; it does not prove branch-wide containment. When source is unavailable, explicit control-flow reasoning is weaker evidence than an applied edit.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating suppression of `<` and `>` for the reported imaginary unit as equivalent to preventing the same unsuitable exponent from entering the rest of the transformation branch.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visible branch-wide early return for ineligible exponents that dominates all downstream exponent processing; guarding individual comparisons or catching their exceptions cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the visible `_TR56` callback for one return path placed after the targeted `Pow` check and before `< 0`, `> max`, `%`, `//`, and `perfect_power` processing.
metadata.oracle_test: Within `_TR56._f`, the semantic reference is an early return after `rv.is_Pow and rv.base.func == f` and before all exponent processing; the strongest form is equivalent to `if not rv.exp.is_real: return rv`, which rejects both `False` and `None` realness on `rv.exp`.

scale.1: No applicable containment is present, or the final edit leaves the original unsafe comparison reachable without a relevant guard.
scale.2: The issue is only diagnosed, handled by a literal special case, checked after unsafe processing, or addressed through broad/global semantics rather than an applied local eligibility boundary.
scale.3: An applied local change suppresses one or both ordered comparisons, sign checks, or comparison exceptions, but no early return dominates all later exponent processing.
scale.4: An applied early return dominates every downstream exponent operation, but its eligibility predicate is imperfect, such as admitting unknown realness or unnecessarily requiring integer exponents.

metadata.evidence_authority: A passing rerun after correction, a pre-edit run reproducing the same failure, or a visible repository-native expected-failure designation outranks prose attribution. Raw failing output outranks an unsupported claim that failures are pre-existing. Focused regression success establishes the reported case only and does not erase contradictory compatibility evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a nonzero or failing validation result as successful based only on assertion, while relying on focused happy-path output to conceal unresolved compatibility evidence.

scale.4: One or more post-edit failures are declared harmless or expected without visible baseline, expected-failure, or successful-rerun authority, and compatibility or overall test success is nevertheless claimed.
scale.5: Visible authoritative evidence ties a failure to the edit, or a syntax, import, recursion, affected-path, or compatibility failure is ignored or directly contradicted by a claim that validation passed.

scale.5: The narrow faithful boundary fallback is visibly active, the reported as_set path succeeds after the edit, and no unresolved semantic, exception-scope, import, or structural contradiction remains.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A fixed or altered predicate, reversed symbol and condition, non-real base set, unreachable branch, unconditional fallback, broad exception handler, or replacement of the normal solver path caps at 3. Multiple fundamental defects cap at 2.

scale.2: The candidate fundamentally misrepresents the set or boundary, such as using multiple wrong constructor components, an unreachable location, or an unconditional solver replacement.
scale.3: The candidate is relevant but has one material contract defect, such as a wrong predicate, argument order, domain, edit layer, exception scope, or bypassed normal path.
scale.4: The candidate has the faithful symbol, original relation, real domain, retained normal solver call, and NotImplementedError-only fallback, but is merely proposed, reverted, or has a minor unresolved scope/import uncertainty.

metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible source inspection or active diff determines whether an implementation is active. Successful edit-command output proves only that an attempt ran. Later restores, failed replacements, stashes, and source inspections override earlier activation claims. A successful reported as_set execution proves that the active path was reached but does not by itself prove contract fidelity.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating an active but flawed implementation as equivalent to import-only setup or an unapplied proposal, or inferring activation solely from an edit command whose replacement did not take effect.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires visible evidence that a production edit in Relational._eval_as_set or its exact conversion boundary became active. A score above 3 requires an active, structurally callable implementation that retains the existing solver call and adds an exception-driven fallback. A score of 5 requires successful post-edit execution of the reported as_set call.

scale.1: Only reproduction, browsing, diagnosis, or unrelated investigation is visible; no concrete production-edit attempt targets the relational conversion boundary.
scale.2: A target fix is described, prepared, or executed as a command, but the latest visible state does not establish an active production edit at the relational boundary, or the work remains at the wrong layer or import-only setup.

scale.5: A structurally callable relational-boundary implementation is visibly active and the reported as_set path is successfully executed after the edit, with no visible activation, import, syntax, shadowing, or method-structure blocker.

metadata.judge_focus: Retained executable source rather than plans, scratch simulations, or superseded candidates
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect the retained production diff, parse or import the edited module, and execute the relevant public API against that source.

scale.1: A submitted artifact has no production implementation, or retained production source is unusable and has no coherent evaluable change.
scale.2: A production edit exists but is incomplete, malformed, wrong-layer, overly broad, or blocked by an unresolved deterministic failure.
scale.3: A coherent production edit is visibly present and inspectable, but retained-state behavior is only partially established.

applies_when: The trajectory investigates, changes, or executes expression-level square-free factorization of a univariate polynomial.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the retained expression-level square-free route emits one multiplied square-free base for each multiplicity in a univariate polynomial, rather than preserving separate same-multiplicity factors merely because the input was written as a product.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Explicitly requiring irreducible splitting, adding multiplicities, or treating ordering alone as the discrepancy scores 1. Editing only an already-correct low-level routine or proposing indiscriminate irreducible post-processing caps the score at 2 unless retained public execution directly demonstrates the required result. A visible adjacent API or test regression caps an otherwise correct implementation at 4; it does not negate an exact demonstrated correction within this univariate semantic scope.
metadata.evidence_authority: Successful public API execution after the latest visible production edit is strongest, followed by retained production source and direct comparison with the formal polynomial or expanded-input route. Pre-edit runs, scratch simulations, proposed patches, and explanations alone cannot establish corrected behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: The expression route remains sensitive to input structure, same-multiplicity bases remain split, ordinary irreducible factorization is substituted for square-free decomposition, or a broad grouping change introduces an observed adjacent regression.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 and 5 require a visible retained production edit and a successful post-edit public expression-level execution that returns one multiplicity-three quadratic base for the issue input. Diagnosis without that execution cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Exact current public output for factored expression input, agreement with the formal polynomial route, and preservation of square-free rather than irreducible semantics
metadata.oracle_test: On the factored issue expression, public square-free listing must contain the quadratic product of the two multiplicity-three linear bases as one entry with multiplicity three, alongside the multiplicity-one and multiplicity-two entries. The supplied expanded comparison must retain one linear base at multiplicity one and one quadratic base at multiplicity two, and multiplying the reported powers by the coefficient must reconstruct each input.

scale.1: The trajectory endorses separate same-multiplicity entries, irreducible splitting, multiplicity addition, or an ordering-only remedy.
scale.2: It recognizes the desired grouped result but targets only an already-correct low-level route, proposes irreducible post-processing, or retains a malformed or plainly inapplicable change.
scale.3: It correctly demonstrates the expression-versus-formal route discrepancy or retains a plausible focused edit, but no successful post-edit public execution proves the correction.
scale.4: Retained production source and post-edit public execution produce the required single multiplicity-three quadratic base, but reconstruction, the supplied comparison, formal-route agreement, or adjacent compatibility remains incomplete or an adjacent regression is visible.
scale.5: The retained correction produces the exact grouped issue result, preserves the supplied expanded comparison, agrees with the formal polynomial route, reconstructs both inputs, and passes an adjacent univariate same-multiplicity case without a relevant regression.

A syntax/import failure in the latest source, a public result still showing the reported split behavior, or a deterministic reconstruction failure caps the score at 2. Tests run only before the latest edit cannot support scores above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed edit commands and resulting file contents or diffs outrank summary-level changed-file fields. A post-edit public execution against the repository outranks edit claims. A later checkout, replacement, or edit supersedes earlier source and tests.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating plans, generated patch scripts, scratch simulations, edit-success messages, pre-edit tests, or superseded source as an applied working implementation.

metadata.judge_focus: Chronological production-file edits, later rewrites or checkouts, visible final source or diff, syntax/import status, and public API behavior executed after the latest edit

scale.1: No production edit is visibly applied in the retained chronology, or every visible production edit is later restored or superseded without a replacement.
scale.2: A production edit is applied, but the latest visible state is malformed, wrong-layer, indiscriminately broad, or followed by an unresolved deterministic failure.
scale.3: A focused production edit is visibly retained and structurally plausible, but execution after the latest edit does not establish the required public behavior.
scale.4: The latest focused edit imports or executes and the public issue case visibly returns the required grouped factor, with only limited retained-state validation beyond that case.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applied and retained production correction

applies_when: A production change affecting Subs LaTeX parenthesization is active or has been attempted in the cutoff workspace.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the active production implementation unconditionally places exact scalable parentheses around the rendered body of every `Subs` inside the evaluation bar, including additive and multiplicative bodies.

metadata.contradiction_rule: No active production edit, a reverted edit, or malformed active Python forces score 1. An active generic `_needs_mul_brackets` change that wraps the complete Subs notation, or an ineffective call that receives already-rendered text, caps the score at 2. Conditional wrapping, plain parentheses, spaces inside `\left(` or `\right)`, or visible omission for `x*y` caps the score at 3. A latest applicable output from the active source overrides contrary assumptions about what the code should emit.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active production source at cutoff is primary. A later restoration or checkout overrides an earlier edit. A latest command executed from that active source may contradict an optimistic source interpretation. Viewed source, proposed patches, helper scripts, untracked backups, failed edit commands, and reverted implementations are non-evidence for an active fix.
metadata.failure_mode: Absent or reverted production change, wrong parenthesization boundary, ineffective rendered-text helper use, conditional body selection, non-scalable delimiters, or exact-spacing defects.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an active production edit. A score above 2 requires the edit to affect the Subs body inside the evaluation bar. A score above 3 requires source logic that applies to every Subs body without a precedence, Add, sign, first-character, coefficient, or surrounding-Mul condition. A score of 5 requires the visible active source to conclusively encode the exact inner `\left(%s\right)` form.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A displayed exception or expression unequal to the exact no-space oracle forces score 1. If that boundary succeeds, a displayed marker leak, genuinely wrong marker-path result, or effective source that unconditionally activates marker state without replacement caps the score at 2. A nonempty fabricated marker that can collide on a no-replacement path caps the score at 3 unless displayed evidence rules out the reachable collision. These caps outweigh passing examples and confident prose.

Effective source outranks a few passing examples when it proves an unavoidable false marker transition, including the fact that `'' in s` is always true. A focused `test_kernS` result or causally complete source may establish an unprinted boundary. A label such as `FAIL`, or a comparison against an ordinarily evaluated SymPy expression, is not contradictory when the displayed `kernS` result itself has the required preserved form.
metadata.failure_mode: Crediting sampled outputs despite an unconditional empty-sentinel marker state, treating misleading comparison prose as a real marker-path failure, accepting marker leakage because execution did not raise, or awarding full credit when only one behavior family is established.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 5 requires evidence for both behavior families and no contradictory effective source state. Any unconditional marker state on the no-space path prevents a score above 2.
metadata.judge_focus: First inspect the exact returned expression. Then inspect a genuine space-containing parenthesized result or the effective source transition that governs marker insertion and cleanup. Check specifically whether the no-space path leaves `hit` false; do not infer correctness solely from the reported example returning successfully.
metadata.oracle_test: The no-space boundary is `kernS("(2*x)/(x-1)") == 2*x/(x-1)`. Marker-path references include `kernS('2*(x + y)') == 2*(x + y)` and `kernS('-(x + 1)') == -(x + 1)`, with no generated marker retained and no marker-dependent cleanup activated when no replacement occurred.

scale.3: The exact boundary succeeds and no direct marker-path failure is shown, but the source fabricates a collision-prone nonempty marker on a no-replacement path, or the available evidence remains too incomplete to establish marker-path preservation.
