reference_golden_rubrics.title: Established kernS boundary behavior

applies_when: The active cutoff workspace contains a runtime change to quantum multiplication recognition, fallback construction, or operation priority.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures algebraic compatibility damage caused by the active multiplication change, excluding the target expressions merely remaining unsimplified.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A narrow Dagger or Operator predicate with an ordinary Mul or Expr fallback cannot receive a regression score merely because compatibility tests were omitted. Passing the two target cases does not override an observed non-target regression. Circular-import or syntax failures alone belong to implementation viability and do not establish an algebraic overreach score above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Completed behavioral output from the active cutoff source has priority. Otherwise use the active runtime diff only to identify breadth or unsafe dispatch risk. Ignore proposed edits, scratch patches, direct method simulations that do not match Python expression dispatch, tool-output names, and experiments later reverted.
metadata.failure_mode: Universal identity elimination, discarded non-identity factors, broken canonicalization, ordinary Operator regression, recursion, or broad operation-priority corruption.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a completed execution showing an established non-target behavior broken by the active source. An active broad predicate or global dispatch change without such an observed failure can score at most 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect active predicates and non-identity fallbacks, followed by completed executions against that same active source. Relevant regressions include eliminating IdentityOperator beside generic scalars or symbols, dropping factors from ordinary Dagger products, changing repeated-Dagger canonicalization, breaking ordinary Operator identity behavior, or causing arithmetic recursion. Failure to simplify either target orientation is not itself a compatibility regression.
metadata.oracle_test: Dagger(O) * O remains a product; Dagger(O) * Dagger(O) equals Dagger(O)**2; O * I and I * O equal O; I * I remains IdentityOperator; 3 * I and I * Symbol('x') remain Mul.

scale.1: No active algebraic compatibility flaw is visible, or no compatibility-affecting runtime edit remains.
scale.2: A localized active-source ambiguity exists, but the recognized operand class remains narrow and no established non-target behavior is shown broken.
scale.3: The active source uses a materially broad predicate or dispatch mechanism, such as arbitrary adjoint duck typing or global priority changes, but no established non-target failure is observed.
scale.4: One established non-target multiplication behavior is visibly broken by execution against the active source.
scale.5: Multiple established behaviors are visibly broken, or active arithmetic dispatch loses factors, broadly eliminates IdentityOperator, or recurses.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active algebraic compatibility regression

applies_when: A rollout prefix reaches runtime source editing or concrete patch design for Dagger and IdentityOperator multiplication.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how far the active runtime change has progressed toward a narrow, effective two-sided repair without relying on a consumed reflected operation or altering ordinary multiplication.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if active Operator.__mul__ treats a Dagger operand as though it were an identity, if an unconditional branch drops non-identity factors, or if the only reverse-order solution is Dagger.__rmul__ and completed execution after that active edit shows IdentityOperator.__mul__ consumes the operation first. A clean direct-handler edit with an ordinary fallback may score 3 while a localized invocation or class-resolution discrepancy is still being diagnosed, but not if the branch is visibly malformed or abandoned.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest visible runtime file contents or diff determine which edits are active. Completed executions against those contents determine whether a purported path is effective. A later applied edit supersedes earlier output only for the path it changed and remains unverified until rerun. Ignore proposed snippets, scratch files, edits visibly reverted, direct method simulations that bypass expression dispatch, and generic workspace summaries that predate or omit later displayed source edits.
metadata.failure_mode: No applied runtime repair, factor-dropping Operator logic, one-sided implementation, ineffective reflected dispatch, malformed method placement, unsafe circular import, or missing ordinary fallback.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 1 requires an applied runtime source branch. A score above 3 requires active direct handling for both operand orders: Dagger-side handling for a right IdentityOperator and IdentityOperator-side recognition of a right Dagger. A score of 5 additionally requires narrow predicates, an ordinary Mul or Expr fallback, and cycle-safe dependency handling.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest active implementations handling Dagger(O) * I and I * Dagger(O), their non-identity fallbacks, and whether each branch is located on the method Python actually reaches. Distinguish an unresolved direct-handler invocation problem from a design that knowingly relies on an unreachable reflected method.
metadata.oracle_test: Dagger(Operator('O')) * IdentityOperator() is handled by Dagger-side multiplication; IdentityOperator() * Dagger(Operator('O')) is handled by IdentityOperator.__mul__; other Dagger products retain normal symbolic multiplication.
metadata.stage: Implement and stabilize the runtime change

scale.1: No active runtime source branch addresses either required operand order.
scale.2: Active work is harmful, malformed, or known ineffective: it corrupts ordinary multiplication, places the repair only on a consumed reflected path, or leaves no trustworthy direct target branch.
scale.3: Exactly one operand order has a narrow direct-handler implementation with an ordinary fallback, or one such clean branch is applied while a localized invocation discrepancy is actively isolated; the other order has no effective direct handler.
scale.4: Both operand orders have active direct-handler branches, but a localized structural concern remains, such as an unsafe dependency direction, ambiguous fallback, materially broad predicate, or visible unresolved contradiction.
scale.5: Both operand orders have narrow active direct-handler branches, ordinary non-identity fallback is preserved, and dependency handling is visibly cycle-safe with no active source contradiction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the active diagnosis claims that adding only Dagger.__rmul__ repairs Dagger(O) * I after normal execution shows Expr.__mul__ already returns Mul, or if it treats Operator.__mul__ as the method reached by a Dagger object. Dagger(O) * I is decided by Dagger's direct or inherited __mul__; I * Dagger(O) is decided by IdentityOperator.__mul__. A concrete result from the left operand prevents reliance on the right operand's reflected method.

applies_when: The visible trajectory contains an edit or concrete implementation of representative-record removal in `PermutationGroup.minimal_blocks()`.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible implementation removes obsolete minimal-block records without index shifting or positional misalignment among `blocks`, `num_blocks`, and `rep_blocks`, while preserving the surrounding containment and candidate-insertion logic.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A bounds-based skip, exception suppression, forward deletion from shifting lists, update of fewer than all three collections, dead cleanup guard, active value-based cleanup that can remove unselected records, altered containment polarity, removed guarded append, or visibly wrong subgroup order prevents scores above 2. Lack of exact behavioral validation alone does not reduce a visibly complete causal implementation below 4.
metadata.evidence_authority: Judge the latest coherent source excerpt or submitted diff. A later checkout, replacement, or corruption supersedes earlier code and claims. Tests support only the source state they visibly follow. A remaining value-based expression is not itself contradictory if its selector is provably empty or the code establishes that it cannot remove any record beyond the positions already selected; an active selector capable of separate or extra removal is contradictory.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a non-crashing workaround or an incomplete source excerpt for synchronized removal, while also rejecting equivalent descending positional deletion or harmless inert cleanup solely because it is not expressed as three identical list comprehensions.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require a visibly applied, general positional implementation. It may either finish comparisons before mutating the lists or traverse positions strictly downward, but it must remove corresponding entries from all three parallel collections without shifting any position that remains to be inspected. Scores 4 or 5 also require preservation of both containment tests, cleanup accumulated before an early break, and `minimal and num_block not in num_blocks`.
metadata.judge_focus: Accept either collection of original removal positions followed by synchronized filtering or descending deletion, or a strictly descending traversal that synchronously deletes the current position from all three collections. Verify that every selected record is removed from all three collections, no unselected record can be removed, cleanup selected before a later candidate-rejection break still occurs, both containment branches remain intact, and the guarded candidate append is preserved.
metadata.oracle_test: Under the same source state, established `minimal_blocks()` checks retain their expected block systems, and the Sylow 2-subgroups returned for `DihedralGroup(18)` and `DihedralGroup(50)` both have order 4.
metadata.stage: Implement the causal minimal-block record-removal repair

scale.5: The score-4 implementation is visible, both reported cases are directly checked to return subgroup order 4 for that source state, and focused minimal-block or Sylow regression tests pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Numeric-zero compatibility and fallback retention

applies_when: The prefix contains claims or direct evidence about the cause or correction of the Float-versus-Boolean equality asymmetry.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether visible evidence converges on the premature zero-Float falsiness return in `Float.__eq__` and turns that diagnosis into a valid, localized correction plan or applied change.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible result still returns `True` and is claimed as fixed, the intended result remains `True`, or the latest source contradicts the asserted correction. Cap at 3 when an edit is only claimed without source, diff, or post-edit behavioral confirmation.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest direct source views, diffs, and runtime results outrank assistant summaries and earlier hypotheses. A later corrected explanation supersedes exploratory mistakes. An edit-success message alone does not prove that source changed.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating extensive exploration, a correct isolated observation, or an unverified edit message as equivalent to a settled causal account with an executable local correction.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require an explicit valid correction plan or visible applied change in `Float.__eq__` after sympification; merely locating or explaining the branch cannot exceed 3.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the latest settled account connects `_sympify(other)`, the premature `if not self: return not other`, falsy `BooleanFalse`, and a correction that gives Boolean rejection precedence without replacing specialized numeric dispatch.
metadata.oracle_test: After `_sympify(other)`, Boolean operands must be rejected before any `not other` equality result; NumberSymbol, Float, Rational, general Number, `SympifyError`, and `NotImplemented` behavior must remain available.
metadata.stage: Trace and correct Float equality control flow

scale.1: The latest settled account preserves the wrong `True` target, changes the wrong equality layer, or proposes truthiness-based Boolean/numeric conflation.
scale.2: The asymmetry is reproduced or relevant code is explored, but the active cause remains wrong, contradictory, or unresolved and no valid local correction is specified.
scale.3: The correct premature `Float.__eq__` branch and Boolean interaction are accurately explained, but no explicit valid correction is proposed or applied.
scale.4: A concrete valid post-sympification Boolean-before-falsiness correction is proposed or visibly applied, with no material contradiction, but source or behavioral verification is incomplete.
scale.5: Visible source or diff confirms the localized correction, and direct post-edit evidence confirms the discriminator while preservation evidence supports the surrounding numeric dispatch.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Settled causal diagnosis and actionable Float equality correction

applies_when: A source view, worktree summary, production diff, edit command, revert, helper file, or unchanged repository state is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the latest observable worktree remains importable and confines any production change to the necessary `Float.__eq__` Boolean-before-falsiness correction without deleting fallback logic, altering another equality method, or relying on helper files as the repair.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 1 when the latest visible production state deletes or corrupts a required equality fallback, modifies another equality method through a broad replacement, is malformed or non-importable, or intentionally introduces a core semantic regression. Cap at 2 when conflicting or duplicate production logic remains. Untracked diagnostic helpers do not prove a production fix and cannot override a hazardous diff.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest direct diff, source view, repository status, and import result outrank edit-success messages, assistant summaries, focused runtime output, and earlier transient states. A later verified revert or correction supersedes an earlier harmful edit. If a textual replacement matched multiple methods, the resulting diff determines scope.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a passing focused check or an edit-success message as proof of safety while the latest diff contains fallback deletion, a second equality-method change, duplicate logic, or malformed production code.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require direct evidence of the latest worktree state, such as a diff, source view, status summary, or verified unchanged state. Passing helper scripts or runtime checks alone cannot establish safe production scope.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the latest production diff and complete affected method regions for cross-method replacements, deleted or duplicated fallback branches, malformed syntax, unrelated files, and whether the actual repair resides in production source.
metadata.oracle_test: Only `Float.__eq__` should give a sympified `Boolean` rejection precedence over `if not self: return not other`; the generic zero fallback and the Rational, NumberSymbol, Float, Number, SympifyError, and NotImplemented paths must remain structurally available.
metadata.stage: Assess production scope and regression risk at the visible cutoff

scale.1: The latest production state is destructive or invalid: it contains a broad cross-method replacement, deletion or corruption of a required fallback, a change to another equality method, malformed/non-importable code, or an intentional semantic regression.
scale.2: The latest production state is localized but still materially unsafe, with conflicting or duplicate guards, an incomplete recovery, or another unresolved production defect that can affect equality behavior.
scale.3: Production safety is unresolved: an edit was claimed or attempted without a confirming latest source/diff view, or visible scope information is insufficient to rule out material collateral changes.
scale.4: The latest state shows a narrow, apparently safe `Float.__eq__` correction with required surrounding branches retained, but complete method scope, importability, or cleanup evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: The latest state is directly verified as unchanged or as a clean, importable, narrowly scoped `Float.__eq__` correction, with no unrelated production edits and all required fallback and specialized dispatch branches intact.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Causal and semantic fit

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates or changes behavior related to the reported PolynomialError.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how precisely visible evidence localizes the leaked PolynomialError to optional common-factor extraction at G = gcd(p, q) in Mod.eval, independently of whether the final recovery has already been implemented.

metadata.contradiction_rule: An applied edit that does not import or parse, or post-edit execution that still fails before demonstrating the claimed path, caps the score at 2. A usable recovery confined to a hyperbolic or assumptions caller caps the score at 3. Changing polynomial validation, caller recovery quality, and fallback continuation do not erase an otherwise proven localization, but they prevent anchor 5.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed traceback and inspected source take precedence over assistant summaries. An observed Mod.eval frame at G = gcd(p, q) outranks isolated reconstructed expressions. Applied source and its execution determine whether a claimed caller workaround is usable.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating exact causal localization with patch completion, or awarding exact-localization credit from the exception text alone without connecting it to the Mod.eval gcd frame.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 4 or 5 requires visible source or traceback evidence identifying G = gcd(p, q) in Mod.eval as the operation from which PolynomialError escapes; merely mentioning modulo, Piecewise, polynomial conversion, or gcd elsewhere is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the exact cold-cache traceback, the cited Mod.eval source, and any observed p and q operands; distinguish localization of the throwing operation from correctness or completeness of the proposed patch.
metadata.oracle_test: The task-specific causal reference is reconstruction during substitution leading through a hyperbolic assumptions query to Mod evaluation, where optional G = gcd(p, q) invokes unsupported polynomial conversion for a Piecewise-containing operand.
metadata.stage: Trace the assumptions query to the optional Mod simplification

scale.1: No visible evidence connects the failure to modulo evaluation or polynomial gcd processing.
scale.2: Evidence reaches modulo or unsupported polynomial conversion but does not establish the G = gcd(p, q) frame in Mod.eval; also use this anchor when the attempted edit is visibly unimportable or its claimed diagnosis cannot execute.
scale.3: The exact Mod.eval gcd path is encountered, but the selected usable recovery remains confined to a triggering caller or expression-shape check, so the investigation treats the generic operation as incidental rather than the causal boundary.
scale.4: Source or traceback evidence establishes G = gcd(p, q) in Mod.eval as the exception-producing generic operation, but the proposed handling is absent, incomplete, or shifted into gcd or polynomial-conversion machinery without proving conservative Mod continuation.
scale.5: Source or traceback evidence establishes the exact Mod.eval gcd operation and explicitly classifies it as optional common-factor extraction whose unsupported failure provides no modulo result and should be skipped conservatively at that boundary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Traceback-backed localization of the generic failure

applies_when: A source edit or concrete code-level correction is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible source state implements a meaningful generic Mod correction with defined conservative control flow.

metadata.failure_mode: No semantic source edit, caller-only edit, malformed Mod code, undefined G, premature return, or fabricated result
metadata.judge_focus: Generic location, executable control flow, defined fallback state, and continuation through later Mod logic
metadata.oracle_test: Unsupported gcd extraction leaves p and q unchanged, records no extracted common factor, and proceeds through the remainder of Mod.eval
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow conservative fallback in Mod.eval

scale.1: No generic Mod source correction is present, or the visible source edit is confined to a triggering caller.
scale.2: Mod.eval is edited, but the change is malformed, ineffective for the observed operand, or leaves fallback state or control flow unsafe.
scale.3: A meaningful generic Mod fallback exists but uses expression-shape detection, premature return, or an unnecessarily broad exception boundary.
scale.4: An executable exception-based Mod fallback records no extracted gcd and continues later evaluation, with only limited precision or protected-region concerns.
scale.5: The source cleanly catches the precise unsupported-polynomial exception at optional gcd extraction, preserves operands, and continues all later Mod logic.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Generic Mod correction completeness

applies_when: The prefix applies a guard, exception handler, fallback, or result-selection change intended to avoid the failure.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the concrete recovery is precise, capability-driven, and mathematically conservative.

metadata.failure_mode: Bare or broad catch, Piecewise syntax policy, disabled assumptions, undefined state, or fabricated modulo value
metadata.judge_focus: Precise exception type, absence of syntax policy, conservative fallback state, and preservation of unrelated failures
metadata.oracle_test: Only PolynomialError is suppressed and failure means solely that no common gcd was extracted
metadata.stage: Implement a narrow conservative fallback in Mod.eval

scale.1: No concrete recovery exists, or the recovery is malformed, fabricates a result, or broadly corrupts relevant semantics.
scale.2: The recovery is conservative in intent but relies on Piecewise-shape detection, broad exceptions, or premature evaluation bypass.
scale.3: The recovery catches PolynomialError narrowly but is placed in a triggering caller or otherwise leaves generic Mod exposed.
scale.4: The recovery is capability-driven and narrowly catches PolynomialError at generic gcd processing, with only a minor boundary concern.
scale.5: The recovery precisely protects optional gcd extraction and its immediate reduction, uses a no-common-factor fallback, and preserves all later evaluation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Recovery precision and semantic safety

applies_when: A production-source correction and execution intended to validate it are visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether execution performed after an observable generic Mod correction demonstrates first-call recovery of the reported substitution and preservation of representative modulo behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the relevant post-edit run fails to import or parse, raises before completing substitution, or still exposes PolynomialError, the score is 1. If no relevant command follows the edit, the score is 2. Warm-cache-only success, a reduced trigger, or execution whose relation to the edited source is not observable cannot exceed 2. A later unrelated test-script error does not erase an earlier completed qualifying run.
metadata.evidence_authority: Chronologically post-edit command output is authoritative. A fresh process or explicit cache clear before expression construction outranks repeated-process success. Displayed source or an exact applied edit command must connect the execution to a generic Mod correction; pre-edit runs, expected-result comments, and diagnostic scripts do not validate it.
metadata.failure_mode: Using pre-edit reproduction, second-call cache behavior, source inspection without execution, reduced hyperbolic cases, or broad smoke output as proof of a validated generic recovery.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchor 3 or higher requires both an observable generic Mod.eval recovery and a subsequent successful first-call execution of the full real-symbol expression containing Piecewise, division, the hyperbolic function, the outer function, and subs({1: 1.0}) in a fresh process or after an explicit cache clear. Caller-only edits and reduced expressions cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Establish command chronology, confirm that the tested process used the edited production source, check the full trigger shape and first-call cache state, and then inspect variant and ordinary Mod regression coverage.
metadata.oracle_test: Using the edited production source, the first cold-cache substitution on the full reported expression completes without PolynomialError, while ordinary Mod common-factor simplification still produces its normal symbolic simplification and unrelated exceptions are not broadly swallowed.

scale.1: No usable qualifying post-edit execution exists, or the relevant post-edit command fails before completing the full cold-cache substitution.
scale.2: A production edit is followed only by source inspection, no relevant execution, warm-cache success, an indirect or reduced trigger, or execution not observably tied to a generic Mod correction.
scale.3: After an observable generic Mod correction, the full reported expression succeeds on its first fresh-cache substitution, but no relevant variant or ordinary Mod regression is executed.
scale.4: The full cold-cache reproducer succeeds after the generic correction, and post-edit execution also covers at least one relevant Piecewise or hyperbolic variant and one ordinary Mod common-factor simplification.
scale.5: The evidence for anchor 4 is present and a focused repository regression test covering the failure is added or executed successfully, with no visible regression in the exercised generic Mod behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed validation of the generic recovery

applies_when: The visible prefix selects or compares at least one concrete code-level repair location for the PolynomialError.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the visible repair direction places conservative failure handling at optional common-factor extraction in Mod.eval rather than encoding Piecewise policy or suppressing the failure in a triggering caller.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removing polynomial validation, teaching polynomial generators to accept Piecewise without mathematical support, fabricating a modulo value, or disabling assumptions caps the score at 1. An applied but unusable implementation caps the score at 2 even if its intended boundary was correct.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied source outranks patch text, which outranks a concrete code-level plan, which outranks general discussion. Executed evidence that a selected boundary cannot import or cannot reach the reported path overrides claims that it is suitable.
metadata.failure_mode: Conflating the deepest throwing function with the appropriate recovery boundary, or rewarding a caller workaround because it happens to avoid the supplied expression.
metadata.hard_gate: Anchors 4 and 5 require explicit selection of Mod.eval's optional gcd-based common-factor extraction as the recovery boundary and an explicit conservative no-extraction fallback; merely naming Mod, gcd, Piecewise, or PolynomialError is insufficient.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect the stated or applied repair location, the operation it protects, the proposed fallback state, and whether later Mod.eval processing is intended to continue.
metadata.oracle_test: Unsupported polynomial conversion during gcd means only that Mod.eval cannot perform its optional common-factor optimization; it does not supply a modulo result and does not justify changing gcd, Piecewise validation, or hyperbolic assumptions.
metadata.stage: Choose the code boundary and fallback semantics

scale.1: No concrete repair boundary is selected, or the selected direction weakens polynomial validation, fabricates a result, or otherwise contradicts the failure semantics.
scale.2: The selected recovery is tied to a hyperbolic, assumptions, substitution, or Piecewise-shaped caller and therefore leaves equivalent generic Mod inputs exposed.
scale.3: The selected direction is generic but handles the failure inside gcd or polynomial conversion, catches unrelated failures broadly, or proposes an early Mod return that skips later evaluation.
scale.4: The direction explicitly selects optional gcd extraction in Mod.eval and proposes preserving operands with no extracted factor before continuing, but the exception type, protected region, or concrete control flow is incomplete.
scale.5: The direction precisely selects the optional common-factor block in Mod.eval, narrowly treats PolynomialError as no extracted gcd, preserves p and q, and continues the remaining Mod.eval logic.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Selection of the conservative repair boundary

applies_when: The inspected work proposes, applies, displays, or submits a source change for the ImageSet and S.Reals intersection defect.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards visible availability of an applicable source artifact containing the causal handler change, rather than merely proposed edits or transient mutation claims.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the visible artifact omits the handler source change, is malformed or truncated, contains conflict markers, or is test-only. Cap at 3 if source mutation is demonstrated but no complete applicable changed source or diff is available for inspection.
metadata.evidence_authority: A complete displayed git diff, patch, or repository-visible changed source is authoritative over prose claims, planned replacement commands, summaries, and scratch scripts. Execution earns artifact credit only when the applied source state is also visible; a final diff displayed after execution establishes continuity unless an intervening mutation is shown.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating a proposed replacement, transient editing command, successful reproduction, or passing output as equivalent to an inspectable source patch.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires a complete applicable source diff or equivalent inspectable changed source at the cutoff; proposed code, a reported successful replacement, or output from an undisplayed mutation cannot satisfy this gate.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect whether the cutoff contains a complete source diff or equivalent repository-visible change for the localized ImageSet/S.Reals handler and whether execution is attributable to that same visible state.
metadata.oracle_test: The artifact must visibly modify the localized ImageSet/S.Reals intersection path and be sufficient for an evaluator to apply or inspect the causal source change.
metadata.stage: Review and finalize the evaluator-facing artifact

scale.1: No source modification is proposed, applied, or displayed.
scale.2: A source change is proposed or partially shown, but application is not established or the visible artifact is incomplete, malformed, or test-only.
scale.3: A relevant source mutation is visibly applied or executed in the working session, but no complete applicable diff or equivalent changed source is available at the cutoff.
scale.4: A complete applicable localized source artifact is visible, but execution against that same state is not established.
scale.5: A complete applicable localized source artifact is visible, and cutoff-visible execution directly supports the primary corrected behavior on that source state.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Inspectable applied source artifact

applies_when: The inspected work reasons about, traces, proposes a change to, or edits the ImageSet intersection with S.Reals.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards observable causal evidence that the handler must retain parameters where the imaginary part is zero instead of removing those parameters.

metadata.failure_mode: Endorsing the Complement, changing only tuple presentation, applying an unrelated subset workaround, or naming roots without settling the set operation.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the retain-zero diagnosis is expressed as a precise operation, focused edit, or executed equivalent transformation.
metadata.oracle_test: The candidate operation retains zero-imaginary parameters and yields the required finite real intersection with the reported nonmember excluded.
metadata.stage: Implement conservative zero-set and pole filtering

scale.1: The inspected reasoning endorses removal of zero-imaginary parameters or supplies no relevant causal account.
scale.2: The handler or roots are identified, but retain-versus-remove polarity remains absent, incorrect, or contradictory.
scale.3: The zero-imaginary parameters are correctly described as admissible, but no precise candidate operation, handler edit, or executed equivalent transformation is shown.
scale.4: A precise operation, focused handler edit, or executed equivalent transformation visibly retains the zero-imaginary parameters.
scale.5: A generic localized implementation visibly produces the required primary set and membership behavior through the correct filtered parameter domain.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Operational retain-zero correction

applies_when: The inspected work discusses or manipulates the parameter base domain, multiple roots, unresolved equations, real-part mapping, or denominator zeros.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards observable implementation of the complete parameter-domain equation rather than a repair limited to the reported polynomial.

metadata.failure_mode: Tuple-wrapped roots, fixed integer fallback, discarded unresolved conditions, retained poles, or raw parameter output.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether each inspected set operation uses the correct expression and polarity.
metadata.oracle_test: Intersect the supplied base domain with zeros of the imaginary numerator, subtract zeros of denominators of the full expression, preserve unresolved equations, and apply the real-part lambda.
metadata.stage: Implement conservative zero-set and pole filtering

scale.1: No inspected candidate operation establishes any secondary domain obligation.
scale.2: An inspected candidate operation establishes one obligation: separate roots, supplied-domain filtering, unresolved-condition preservation, real-part mapping, or pole subtraction.
scale.3: Inspected candidate operations establish multiple obligations, but at least one material part of the domain contract remains absent or incorrect.
scale.4: The complete domain equation is visibly implemented with the correct expressions and operation polarity.
scale.5: The complete domain equation is implemented and visibly verified on base-domain, unresolved-equation, nonidentity-mapping, and pole-sensitive cases.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete filtered-domain contract

applies_when: The inspected work runs a reproduction, production trace, candidate set transformation, modified handler, or semantic assertion.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards command outputs that directly establish the claimed cause or corrected set semantics.

metadata.failure_mode: Only pre-correction reproduction, diagnostics omitting production statements, failing scripts, or conclusions unsupported by output.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether execution reaches the actual corrected operation without relying on an inaccurate branch transcription.
metadata.oracle_test: An exact handler trace respects back-substitution order, or an executed candidate operation demonstrates the corrected filtered domain.

scale.1: No reliable execution supports the claimed cause.
scale.2: Execution reliably reproduces the failure and localizes the handler but does not execute a corrected operation.
scale.3: An exact production trace, focused source mutation, or equivalent corrected parameter transformation is visibly executed.
scale.4: The corrected primary behavior and at least one discriminative secondary behavior are visibly executed.
scale.5: The primary, base-domain, unresolved-equation, mapping, and pole-sensitive checks visibly pass on the candidate source.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executable causal evidence

applies_when: The visible prefix investigates the nested-fraction behavior, expression structure, ordinary string rendering, or a related source correction.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures how reliably the trajectory uses visible structural and semantic evidence to distinguish the preserved nested reciprocal tree from its ambiguous ordinary string rendering and localize the defect to StrPrinter denominator grouping.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest causal position still targets LaTeX grammar, convert_frac evaluation, or ANTLR generation as the defect, or if the trajectory uses a mathematically different expression such as division by c**2 as the expected oracle. A later explicit correction supported by structural evidence removes that cap. Malformed or merely proposed edits receive no implementation credit.
metadata.evidence_authority: Latest explicit assistant-authored causal conclusion wins over earlier speculation. Executed srepr or args and the parser-independent Mul/Pow reproduction outrank ambiguous str output and simplification alone. Latest visible file contents or diff determine whether a correction was actually applied; proposed edits and intermediate commands are not implementations.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating ambiguous text as a malformed parse, counting simplification as proof of faithful rendering, crediting raw source listings as authored diagnosis, or accepting parser evaluation changes that erase the structure to be printed.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an explicit assistant-authored conclusion, supported by visible structural evidence or a parser-independent reproduction, that the reciprocal-of-reciprocal tree is preserved and ordinary string rendering is defective. A score above 3 additionally requires tracing StrPrinter._print_Mul denominator extraction and the existing guarded parenthesization path. A score of 5 requires a visible effective localized source edit.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect executed srepr, args, direct unevaluated Mul/Pow probes, exact displayed strings, assistant-authored causal conclusions, and any visible source inspection or edit. Distinguish evidence that the tree is mathematically intended from a mere simplification result, and distinguish inspecting _print_Mul from only naming StrPrinter.
metadata.oracle_test: The intended tree contains an outer inverse whose base is the complete inner reciprocal; for example, Mul(x, Pow(1/y, -1, evaluate=False), evaluate=False) must retain that structure and should be rendered by StrPrinter as x/(1/y). The relevant source mechanism is _print_Mul extracting the negative-Pow base into its denominator list while the existing guarded pow_paren handling covers suitable Mul bases but misses Pow bases.
metadata.stage: Reproduce, classify, and localize the defect

scale.1: No executed structural or semantic evidence advances classification; investigation remains setup-oriented, grammar-oriented, or causally unsupported.
scale.2: Executed evidence provides a useful partial distinction—such as mathematical equivalence, nested-Pow clues, args inspection, or a representation concern—but the latest diagnosis remains unresolved, parser-directed, semantically contradictory, or unsupported as a printer conclusion.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly and consistently concludes, from visible structural evidence or the direct unevaluated reproduction, that the reciprocal tree is preserved and ordinary string rendering is the defect, but does not trace the exact _print_Mul grouping mechanism.
scale.4: In addition to the supported printer diagnosis, the trajectory traces negative-Pow denominator extraction in _print_Mul and explains that the reciprocal Pow base is missed by the existing guarded Mul-only parenthesization path; no effective correction is yet visible.
scale.5: The complete level-4 causal account is accompanied by a visible, syntactically valid, localized source correction that extends the relevant denominator-parenthesization behavior to the reciprocal Pow case without evaluating the structure away.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Evidence-grounded tree-versus-rendering localization

applies_when: The cutoff state exposes an active repository diff, changed-file summary, or tracked file contents.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures task-causal evaluator risk from harmful changes still present in the active cutoff workspace, especially parser evaluation rewrites, generated-ANTLR modification, malformed core source, and invalid tracked artifacts.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Removal or reversion shown by later cutoff evidence cancels the corresponding penalty. Conversely, successful mathematical output does not excuse an active change that evaluates away the required reciprocal structure or corrupts generated artifacts.
metadata.evidence_authority: The latest visible git diff and cutoff file contents override earlier edit commands, assistant claims, and intermediate source listings. An empty or clean cutoff diff establishes that earlier experiments are no longer active.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring damage from discussion or intermediate commands rather than the active diff, or treating all scratch files and absent implementations as equivalent to semantic source corruption.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires an active tracked change with task-causal compatibility or evaluator risk. Missing implementation, unfinished status, and an unchanged repository are not damage.
metadata.judge_focus: Use only changes visibly active at cutoff. Distinguish tracked core-source or generated-file damage from harmless exploratory scripts, dependency installation outside the repository, proposed edits, failed commands that changed nothing, and edits later reverted.
metadata.oracle_test: The active workspace must not replace convert_frac's unevaluated Mul/Pow construction with ordinary division or simplification, alter serialized ANTLR payloads, leave malformed Python in core files, or track a failed download containing only an error body.

scale.1: No harmful active tracked change is visible; the workspace is clean or contains only the intended localized printer/test work.
scale.2: Only minor tracked exploratory clutter is active, such as valid task-related scripts, with no parser semantic rewrite, generated-file change, malformed artifact, or core compatibility risk.
scale.3: A broad or poorly justified active source change creates concrete compatibility risk, but no required structure is visibly erased and core source remains syntactically usable.
scale.4: A material wrong-layer or invalid artifact remains active, such as evaluating or simplifying convert_frac, replacing its unevaluated construction with ordinary division, or tracking a failed-download placeholder.
scale.5: Severe active damage is visible: malformed core Python, conflict markers, corrupted or manually version-edited generated ANTLR data, truncated core files, or another change that prevents reliable evaluation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Task-causal damage in the active cutoff workspace

applies_when: The trajectory attempts to validate behavior through commands, assertions, or focused tests.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures observed results from actually executed checks of the exact direct printer regression, the reported LaTeX output, and nearby established string-printer compatibility.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A visible failure of the exact assertion or a source-caused failure in test_Mul/test_str.py caps the score at 2 until a later rerun visibly passes. Environment failure before reaching the assertion supplies no positive or negative result for that assertion.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed command output from the cutoff trajectory overrides claims that a test passed. Repository test results outrank custom-script summaries when they exercise the same behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Counting simplify/equality checks, hand-built evaluated expressions, written-only scripts, or pre-assertion dependency failures as successful regression validation.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores above 2 require an actually executed exact check of either the direct x/(1/y) oracle or the complete reported LaTeX string. Scores above 3 require both the direct oracle and a passing focused printer test.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands that were actually executed and their observed output. Require complete-string comparisons where claimed. A script merely written, a proposed command, a manual construction that does not exercise the changed path, or a run failing before the relevant assertion is non-evidence.
metadata.oracle_test: assert str(Mul(x, Pow(1/y, -1, evaluate=False), evaluate=False)) == 'x/(1/y)'; additionally compare the reported parse_latex result to '((a**3 + b)/c)/(1/(c**2))'.

scale.1: No applicable check reaches its assertion or output comparison; only proposed commands, written-only scripts, setup failures, or unrelated tests are visible.
scale.2: Executed checks are limited to simplification, mathematical equality, numeric substitution, substring heuristics, or manual simulations that do not establish the exact required string.
scale.3: An executed exact check visibly passes for either the direct x/(1/y) expression or the complete reported LaTeX output, but not both and without a passing focused printer test.
scale.4: The exact direct x/(1/y) check passes and test_Mul or sympy/printing/tests/test_str.py visibly passes; the reported parse output may be unavailable because of an external parser dependency.
scale.5: The exact direct assertion, complete reported LaTeX string, focused printer suite, and relevant nearby compatibility checks such as x/y, 1/x, or the issue-14160 case all visibly pass.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed exact regression and compatibility validation

applies_when: The trajectory contains causal reasoning about whether the defect originates in parsing, expression construction, or printing.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the assistant explicitly concludes that the nested reciprocal tree is preserved and explains that ambiguous text is caused by StrPrinter._print_Mul extracting a Pow base without the grouping already afforded to suitable Mul bases.

metadata.contradiction_rule: If the assistant's latest causal conclusion still identifies convert_frac, LaTeX grammar, or ANTLR generation as the target defect without recognizing the preserved tree and printer failure, cap the score at 2.
metadata.evidence_authority: The assistant's explicit reasoning is authoritative for diagnosis; tool output can support but cannot substitute for the conclusion. Later explicit corrections override earlier speculation unless the assistant subsequently reverts to the contradicted parser diagnosis.
metadata.failure_mode: Inferring a malformed parse tree from the ambiguous displayed string or treating raw tool output as an authored printer diagnosis.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores of 3 or higher require an explicit assistant-authored conclusion that the internal reciprocal-of-reciprocal structure is preserved and the defect is in ordinary string rendering rather than fraction grammar or conversion.
metadata.judge_focus: Credit only assistant-authored causal conclusions supported by visible structural inspection or a parser-independent reproduction. Names appearing solely in grep output, source listings, tracebacks, or handbook text are not authored diagnosis.
metadata.oracle_test: Use srepr, args, or the direct Mul(x, Pow(1/y, -1, evaluate=False), evaluate=False) case to connect the preserved tree to StrPrinter._print_Mul and its Mul-only pow_paren condition.

scale.1: No relevant authored causal conclusion is present, or the assistant concludes that grammar, ANTLR, or convert_frac constructed the wrong mathematics without recognizing a printer defect.
scale.2: The assistant mentions a possible display or grouping issue but remains causally unresolved or continues to endorse a conflicting parser-side explanation.
scale.3: The assistant explicitly concludes that the nested reciprocal structure is preserved and that ordinary string rendering, rather than parsing, is defective.
scale.4: In addition to the level-3 conclusion, the assistant explains that _print_Mul extracts the outer negative power's base into the denominator and that this base is itself a Pow whose rendering contains division.
scale.5: The assistant gives the complete causal account: structural evidence or the direct reproduction, denominator extraction in _print_Mul, the existing guarded Mul-only pow_paren behavior, why Pow is missed, and why parser evaluation or simplification is not an equivalent fix.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Assistant-authored tree-versus-rendering diagnosis

applies_when: The trajectory investigates or changes the integer total-degree branch of itermonomials
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether visible work applies a source change that restores the inclusive integer total-degree interval and establishes its correctness through coherent post-edit execution of the reported case and relevant adjacent behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 when a valid post-edit execution with matching inputs demonstrates omitted in-range terms, included out-of-range terms, or a compatibility regression and no later valid correction resolves it. Cap at 3 when the reported case passes but later visible reasoning leaves material uncertainty about interval, boundary, list-bound, or commutativity behavior without a valid corrected rerun. Invalid scripts do not prove a source defect, but an unresolved conclusion drawn from them prevents scores above 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: Applied repository edits or exact patch text outrank proposed code. Post-edit execution with matching symbols and bounds outranks predictions. Direct membership, set equality, and valid polynomial total-degree checks outrank informal counts. Completed relevant tests outrank spot checks. Import failures, malformed calculations, sorting errors, ordinary symbols mislabeled as noncommutative, and zero discovered tests do not establish implementation behavior.
metadata.failure_mode: Awarding full credit after only the issue reproduction, dismissing later semantic uncertainty merely because its script was flawed, treating setup failures as regressions, or crediting an unexecuted implementation idea as an applied fix.
metadata.hard_gate: Score 4 requires a visibly applied source change or exact patch plus a valid post-edit reproduction showing required mixed degree-3 terms. Score 5 additionally requires at least two distinct, valid adjacent checks, or a completed relevant suite plus one valid adjacent check; all material later semantic concerns must be reconciled.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect visible source edits or exact patch content, the post-edit three-variable exact-degree reproduction, and valid adjacent checks for unequal bounds, omitted minimums, zero or empty boundaries, list-valued bounds, existing tests, or genuinely noncommutative symbols. Also inspect whether later failures or incompatible claims are resolved.
metadata.oracle_test: For integer bounds, every and only monomials whose exponent sum lies in the inclusive interval must be returned. Three commutative variables at bounds 3 and 3 yield exactly 10 monomials: three cubes, six 2+1 mixed terms, and the product of all three variables. Omitted minimums include degree zero, list bounds remain componentwise, and genuine noncommutative inputs preserve word order.

scale.1: No correct source-level direction for inclusive integer total-degree behavior is established, or the visible direction applies per-variable rather than total-degree semantics.
scale.2: Relevant implementation work exists, but valid post-edit evidence demonstrates an unresolved semantic failure or compatibility regression.
scale.3: The causal fix is correctly identified but not visibly applied and reproduced; alternatively, the reported case passes after an applied change but later material semantic uncertainty remains unresolved.
scale.4: A semantically appropriate source change is visibly applied and a valid post-edit reproduction shows the required mixed exact-degree terms, with no valid unresolved failure, but adjacent verification is limited to at most one distinct valid mode.
scale.5: The applied change passes a valid complete reported-case check and is supported by multiple distinct adjacent checks, or by a completed relevant suite plus an adjacent check, with all material visible contradictions reconciled.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Applies a total-degree fix and establishes coherent post-edit correctness

applies_when: The trajectory reasons about or tests integer min_degrees behavior in itermonomials
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Assess whether the trajectory uses mathematically correct expected monomial sets, counts, degree calculations, and symbol assumptions when deciding whether the implementation satisfies the documented inclusive total-degree range.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the latest visible reasoning calls a mathematically correct result a failure, accepts an output outside the requested total-degree interval, omits valid mixed terms from its oracle, or claims a noncommutative test while visibly constructing ordinary commutative symbols. Cap at 3 when such an error is explicitly corrected but validation remains incomplete.
metadata.evidence_authority: The documented integer-versus-list semantics and direct symbolic membership or degree checks outrank informal expected counts and prose claims. Later corrected calculations outrank earlier arithmetic mistakes. Tool output only supports a conclusion when the tested symbols and bounds match the claimed case.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewarding a trajectory merely because it ran tests, even though its expected count, degree computation, or commutativity premise was wrong.
metadata.hard_gate: Scores 4 or 5 require at least one correct task-specific oracle check involving a mixed monomial or a correct complete count/set for an integer total-degree interval.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect explicit expected sets or counts, total-degree calculations, commutativity assumptions, and the trajectory's interpretation of observed outputs. For n commutative variables, exact degree d has binomial(n+d-1, d) monomials; an inclusive range sums those counts. Integer bounds constrain total degree, while list bounds constrain each variable separately.
metadata.oracle_test: For three commutative variables with min_degree=max_degree=3, the result is exactly the 10 exponent triples summing to 3, including all pure cubes, six 2+1 mixed terms, and x1*x2*x3. More generally, integer bounds mean min_degree <= sum of exponents <= max_degree.

scale.1: Uses an incorrect interpretation of integer min_degrees or provides no usable semantic oracle.
scale.2: Attempts relevant validation, but the latest visible interpretation contains a material oracle error or accepts/rejects outputs on an invalid premise.
scale.3: States the correct total-degree rule and avoids material false conclusions, but checks only the reported symptom or leaves expected membership/counts materially incomplete.
scale.4: Correctly validates the reported mixed degree-3 terms and at least one additional bound or symbol case, with no unresolved oracle contradiction.
scale.5: Uses a complete, correct oracle for the reported case and representative interval, default, edge, or commutativity cases, and consistently interprets all visible results against it.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correctly interprets degree-range validation against the monomial oracle

applies_when: The cutoff contains compatibility analysis, regression checks, or test-suite execution related to itermonomials.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Protects existing behavior outside the reported example, including omitted min_degrees, zero and empty-variable boundaries, list-valued componentwise bounds, and noncommutative variables.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if a relevant existing test or compatibility assertion fails and remains unresolved. A unittest invocation reporting zero tests provides no positive credit and cannot override failures.
metadata.evidence_authority: A completed relevant test-suite run and explicit assertions outrank informal claims; a zero-tests result is not test-suite evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: Assumes that passing only the issue example proves compatibility, mistakes zero discovered tests for a passing suite, or uses commutative sorting failures as evidence about noncommutative generation.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires at least one successful automated existing-suite run or several successful targeted compatibility checks spanning more than the reported commutative exact-degree case.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible successful checks of existing SymPy tests or targeted assertions for default, list-valued, edge, and noncommutative modes.
metadata.oracle_test: Representative invariants include itermonomials([x,y],2) == {1,x,y,x**2,x*y,y**2}; list bounds [2,4] and [1,2] retain componentwise semantics and six results; min_degree greater than max_degree yields no results; noncommutative products preserve order.

scale.1: No compatibility evidence is present, or visible regressions are ignored.
scale.2: Only superficial checks are attempted, relevant checks fail, or the reported suite executes zero tests.
scale.3: Some default or edge behavior is successfully checked, but major modes such as list-valued or noncommutative inputs remain unaddressed.
scale.4: Several relevant compatibility modes pass, or the focused existing monomials test module passes after the change.
scale.5: The focused existing suite passes and targeted checks additionally cover default/zero behavior, unequal integer bounds, list-valued componentwise bounds, and noncommutative ordering.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Compatibility and regression protection across itermonomials modes

applies_when: The cutoff contains conflicting counts, outputs, assertions, or interpretations about the candidate fix.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Recognizes and resolves semantic contradictions before concluding that the fix is correct, separating test-script mistakes from genuine implementation failures.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the final reasoning declares success despite unresolved out-of-range monomials, failed assertions, incorrect combinatorial expectations, or known noncommutative regressions.
metadata.evidence_authority: A corrected rerun with valid assertions outranks an earlier faulty script; unresolved implementation output outranks later unsupported claims of success.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards persistence or a final patch despite visible evidence that the implementation is still wrong, or penalizes correct behavior because the trajectory's expected set or degree calculator is faulty.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires the trajectory to identify the source of each material contradiction and show corrected evidence or revert/repair the implicated implementation.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible follow-up after wrong counts, unexpected lower-degree terms, failed assertions, malformed expected sets, or noncommutative test problems.
metadata.oracle_test: The exact degree-3 count in three variables is 10, and x2*x3**2 is valid because its exponent sum is 3; constants have polynomial total degree 0 even if an ad hoc as_powers_dict sum mishandles S.One.

scale.1: Material contradictory evidence is present and ignored or explained incorrectly.
scale.2: Contradictions are noticed but remain unresolved when the trajectory concludes or changes direction.
scale.3: The trajectory plausibly diagnoses a contradiction but provides incomplete corrected evidence.
scale.4: Each material contradiction is correctly classified as a script/expectation problem or implementation defect and followed by an appropriate correction.
scale.5: The reconciliation is complete and disciplined: faulty checks are corrected, genuine defects are repaired or reverted, and final semantic evidence is internally consistent with the documented contract.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Resolution of contradictory semantic evidence

applies_when: The cutoff contains analysis of integer-valued max_degrees and min_degrees in itermonomials.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Identifies that the integer-degree branch must filter on the sum of exponents (total degree), while the defective logic compares min_degree with the largest individual exponent and therefore drops mixed monomials.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 if the trajectory continues to claim that combinations_with_replacement itself cannot produce mixed degree-3 terms, that S.One padding is inherently the defect, or that the list-valued degree branch has the same semantics without resolving that claim.
metadata.evidence_authority: Directly quoted implementation and reproduced outputs outrank unsupported explanations; the documented total-degree contract is the semantic authority.
metadata.failure_mode: Rewards reproducing the symptom without understanding why mixed terms are rejected, or confuses total-degree bounds with componentwise list bounds.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 3 requires explicitly distinguishing total degree (sum of exponents) from maximum per-variable exponent.
metadata.judge_focus: Visible source analysis connecting max(powers.values()) to the omission of mixed terms such as x1*x2**2 and x1*x2*x3.
metadata.oracle_test: For three commutative variables and max_degrees=min_degrees=3, exponent tuples must satisfy e1+e2+e3=3, yielding 10 monomials, not only the three pure cubes.

scale.1: No task-causal diagnosis, or the stated diagnosis is incompatible with the documented total-degree contract.
scale.2: Recognizes that min_degrees is involved but gives only a vague or materially confused explanation.
scale.3: Locates the integer total-degree branch and the suspicious exponent check, but does not precisely explain max-versus-sum semantics.
scale.4: Correctly explains that max(powers.values()) tests an individual exponent rather than total degree and links this to missing mixed monomials.
scale.5: Provides the complete causal account for both commutative and noncommutative paths, explains the role of S.One padding or equivalent degree generation, and distinguishes the integer total-degree API from list-valued componentwise bounds.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct diagnosis of the total-degree filtering defect

applies_when: A task-specific production edit, concrete replacement, or explicit decision about the required grouping form is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the cutoff-visible work has converged on and consistently preserves the exact secondquant complete-atom grouping contract, rather than remaining unapplied, implementing an incompatible grouping form, or explicitly disputing its own retained correction.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Malformed or destructive active source forces score 1. An explicit later claim that required standalone outer braces are unnecessary, coupled with investigation or preparation of an incompatible conditional or generic replacement, caps the score at 2 even if an earlier active edit happened to emit the oracle form. Partial superscript grouping, escaped visible braces, or visible parentheses caps the score at 3.
metadata.evidence_authority: The active cutoff production source and public-printer output establish what is implemented. Later explicit technical statements about whether that exact form is required establish whether the resolution remains internally consistent. Mere exploration, questions, or missing validation do not contradict an active correct edit; only a clear rejection of the required form or a concrete incompatible replacement direction does.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge treats an earlier correct output as settled despite a later explicit repudiation of its required form, or treats any applied grouping attempt as equivalent to exact invisible complete-atom grouping.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 3 requires an active renderer or executed active-workspace output using literal complete-atom outer braces such as `{b^\dagger_{i}}`. A score of 5 additionally requires no later explicit rejection of that exact compatibility form.
metadata.judge_focus: Compare the active task-specific renderer state with the latest explicit technical interpretation of the required output. Look for consistent acceptance of literal invisible outer braces around the complete creator atom, not merely any attempted grouping or an earlier correct intermediate result.
metadata.oracle_test: The resolved contract is that object-specific secondquant renderers emit `{b^\dagger_{i}}` and `{a^\dagger_{p}}`, so an outer power yields `{b^\dagger_{0}}^{2}` without changing generic Pow behavior or substituting visible delimiters.

scale.1: The active production source is malformed, destructive, or unable to render the relevant expression.
scale.2: The work remains diagnosis-only with no concrete active correction, or an earlier exact correction is explicitly rejected at cutoff in favor of an incompatible mechanism or output contract.
scale.3: A concrete task-specific edit is active, but it uses an incompatible form such as dagger-only grouping, escaped visible braces, visible parentheses, or another non-oracle grouping.
scale.4: Literal complete-atom outer-brace grouping is active and accepted, but retained-source or active-workspace evidence is incomplete for one creator category.
scale.5: The active task-specific implementation and latest visible technical stance consistently preserve literal complete-atom outer-brace grouping for both bosonic and fermionic creators, with no contradictory replacement direction.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Resolved adherence to the exact grouping contract

applies_when: Production editing, deterministic replacement logic, a retained diff, or repository recovery is visible.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures whether the correct source change is retained or concretely represented by a correctly escaped, target-verified edit against an intact source file.

metadata.failure_mode: Only intent exists, replacement matched nothing, source is malformed, or the retained production edit implements the wrong grouping.
metadata.judge_focus: Applied return strings, exact replacement targets, no-op detection, and retained source state.
metadata.oracle_test: Inspect affected return strings, match counts, source size, and the focused diff.

scale.1: The retained production edit is malformed or destructive, or the proposed edit cannot apply as written.
scale.2: There is diagnosis or an incorrect production edit, but no correct implementation-ready source change.
scale.3: A correct exact edit is concretely specified with valid escaping and target locations, but is not retained in production source.
scale.4: A correct narrow creator implementation is retained, or an intact restored source has a verified deterministic correction ready to apply.
scale.5: All required renderer changes are retained in production source and verified through source inspection or a focused diff.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Production realization and edit correctness

applies_when: The trajectory runs or discusses tests, assertion scripts, or public-printer checks for the secondquant LaTeX change.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Measures the breadth of applicable validation that actually executes against the active workspace, covering corrected creator and tensor outputs plus preserved annihilator and generic Dagger behavior.

metadata.contradiction_rule: A zero-test run, import failure, syntax error, or command failure before the relevant assertion supplies no positive validation. A visibly failed intended assertion cannot be reported as passing; obsolete old-string failures may be excluded only when actual output is shown to match the new contract.
metadata.evidence_authority: Observed output from commands executed after the latest active production edit is authoritative. Earlier runs, runs against subsequently changed source, comments in scripts, and hand-written expected strings without comparison are non-evidence.
metadata.failure_mode: The judge rewards the existence of test scripts, successful process status with zero tests, printed claims such as 'all tests passed', or outputs generated before the final edit.
metadata.hard_gate: A score above 2 requires execution to reach a corrected-output check against the active workspace. A score above 3 requires multiple applicable changed-output checks, not just reproduction of the original defect.
metadata.judge_focus: Inspect commands that actually ran and their observed output. Give strongest credit to explicit equality assertions or named collected tests. A script merely written, a proposed command, a private-method failure, or a runner reporting zero executed tests is not validation.
metadata.oracle_test: Executed checks for powered Bd and exact bosonic Commutator; standalone Bd and Fd; AntiSymmetricTensor; fermionic Commutator and NO; unchanged B, F, and quantum `Dagger(x)`.
metadata.stage: Validate exact outputs and classify regressions

scale.1: No applicable public-printer check or assertion executes successfully after the relevant active edit; only scripts, failed commands, private-method errors, or zero-test results are visible.
scale.2: An executed command only reproduces the original malformed output or checks one unrelated/preserved value without exercising corrected behavior.
scale.3: At least one corrected public-printer target executes against the active workspace, but exact assertion evidence or broader changed-output coverage is absent.
scale.4: Executed assertions or equivalent exact comparisons cover the powered creator and several creator/composed outputs, with only tensor or preserved-behavior coverage missing.
scale.5: Nonzero executed assertions or collected tests cover all changed creator, tensor, Commutator, and NO outputs and also verify unchanged annihilator and generic Dagger behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Executed secondquant compatibility validation

applies_when: The prefix has reproduced malformed Python for a negated Mod expression and inspected at least one printer or precedence implementation point.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the cutoff-visible evidence coherently connects the symbolic expression shape, shared negative-coefficient handling, infix Mod emission, and Python parsing that changes the expression's meaning.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 4 if any required link is only inferred rather than displayed. Cap at 3 while the current reasoning says modulo binds more tightly than unary minus, calls -x % y semantically correct for -Mod(x, y), conflates Mod(-x, y) with -Mod(x, y), or relies on coincidental numeric equality, unless that claim is explicitly corrected and abandoned.
metadata.evidence_authority: Executed generated source, runtime or bytecode output, and directly displayed repository source outrank commentary. A later explicit correction and abandonment outranks an earlier exploratory mistake; merely displaying correct output does not silently retract a conflicting latest explanation.
metadata.failure_mode: Mistaking a collection of relevant inspections for a completed causal explanation, or overlooking an unresolved precedence or arithmetic contradiction at the cutoff.
metadata.hard_gate: Credit above 4 requires direct visible evidence for the symbolic Mul shape, the active shared sign-extraction behavior, the emitted infix expression, and the correct Python parse distinction, all supporting the current conclusion.
metadata.judge_focus: A current, source-backed chain from Mul(-1, Mod(...)) through CodePrinter sign extraction and PythonCodePrinter infix emission to Python parsing as (-x) % y rather than -(x % y).
metadata.oracle_test: For symbolic -Mod(x, y), the active path must be consistent with Mul(-1, Mod(x, y)); sign extraction emits a textual leading minus; _print_Mod emits x % y; Python parses -x % y as (-x) % y; therefore semantics require grouping equivalent to -(x % y).
metadata.stage: Localize the shared printer and precedence mechanisms

scale.1: No correct current causal chain is established; the explanation remains on namespaces, symbolic Mod evaluation, or another unrelated cause.
scale.2: Malformed source and its numeric consequence are correctly reproduced, but the active source mechanism producing the grouping is not established.
scale.3: One active implementation link—such as infix Mod emission or negative-coefficient sign extraction—is directly shown and correctly interpreted, but the chain to the other link and Python parsing is incomplete.
scale.4: The symbolic shape, active printer behavior, and parse consequence are substantially connected, but at least one required link is indirect, or a secondary unresolved contradiction prevents a fully stable handoff.
scale.5: Direct visible evidence forms a complete, current, contradiction-free chain from Mul(-1, Mod(...)) through shared sign extraction and infix Mod emission to Python's (-x) % y parse and the required -(x % y) grouping.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Cutoff-stable negated-Mod causal chain

applies_when: The prefix contains expected values, interpretations of output, failed commands, environment changes, or claims about the cause.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes only defects that remain material at the cutoff or support the latest conclusion. Corrected exploratory mistakes and environment-dependent default-module differences should receive little or no penalty.

metadata.failure_mode: Uncorrected false oracle, contradictory final interpretation, unexecuted probe presented as proof, or disruptive repository modification
metadata.judge_focus: Whether unresolved defects contaminate the current conclusion
metadata.oracle_test: Recompute the latest stated oracle and verify that the cited command or source inspection actually supports the claim

scale.1: The latest conclusion is supported by coherent source or runtime evidence; any earlier mistakes are corrected and abandoned.
scale.2: Minor command or import failures occur, but the current technical conclusion remains well supported.
scale.3: Repeated weak probes or an unresolved secondary inconsistency reduces confidence without determining the diagnosis.
scale.4: A false oracle, contradictory interpretation, inactive-path claim, or failed probe materially supports the current conclusion.
scale.5: The trajectory is dominated by unresolved false arithmetic, claims contradicted by displayed evidence, destructive environment changes, or probes that never established the asserted behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Current evidence integrity

applies_when: The prefix inspects generated source, lambdify printer selection, printer inheritance, _print_Mod, _print_Mul, or precedence handling.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the highest technical milestone visibly established on the executable modules=[] printing path. This is the primary ordering rubric for exploratory prefixes.

metadata.failure_mode: Remaining on namespace selection, symbolic evaluation, or an inactive printer
metadata.judge_focus: Verified causal milestone at the rollout cutoff
metadata.oracle_test: Trace the selected executable printer to infix Mod emission, shared multiplication handling, sign extraction, and precedence lookup

scale.1: The prefix remains on module namespaces, symbolic Mod evaluation, or an unrelated printer and does not explain the malformed executable source.
scale.2: Malformed executable source is reproduced or the Python printer is suspected, but the active inheritance or multiplication path is not established.
scale.3: The active executable printer and either shared multiplication/sign extraction or Mod precedence are verified.
scale.4: Both shared sign extraction and Mod's effective precedence are inspected, with the need for separate negative and multiplicative handling substantially established.
scale.5: The prefix derives the complete two-boundary model at active integration points, including a unary-minus level between multiplication and exponentiation.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Active-path causal progress

applies_when: The prefix proposes a concrete repair or visibly edits repository source.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores whether the latest visible repair state addresses the established cause at an active boundary rather than merely formatting one example.

metadata.failure_mode: Inactive edit, namespace workaround, one-sided repair, or unconditional wrapping
metadata.judge_focus: Completeness and activity of the proposed or applied repair
metadata.oracle_test: Check for both Mod multiplication precedence and scoped negative-factor handling, with standalone Mod and exponentiation preserved

scale.1: The proposal or edit targets module selection, symbolic evaluation, an inactive path, or otherwise does not address the printer cause.
scale.2: A one-case formatting workaround is proposed, such as unconditional wrapping, without preserving neighboring contracts.
scale.3: One required precedence mechanism is concretely proposed or implemented at an active location, while the complementary mechanism is absent.
scale.4: Both mechanisms are concretely located or edited with plausible scope, but compatibility evidence is incomplete.
scale.5: A complete active repair is visible and preserves standalone Mod, multiplied and negative Mod grouping, and the exponentiation boundary.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Actionable repair state

applies_when: The prefix investigates generated Python for an expression containing Mod or inspects the Python printer path used to emit that expression.
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Scores the highest cutoff-visible milestone localizing how an outer symbolic multiplication or negation is composed with infix Mod output on the executable Python-printing path.

metadata.contradiction_rule: Cap at 2 while the current account attributes the malformed grouping to namespaces, symbolic Mod evaluation, or argument rewriting despite visible infix output. Cap at 3 if either displayed implementation boundary is not connected to the concrete printer that emitted the source. Cap at 4 if printer selection is indirect but concrete-printer execution and method ownership otherwise establish the path.
